entries.zh: 於是汝貴、玉昆軍南門外大同江，志超部將江自康軍北門外小山，寶貴任城守。
entries.en: Rugui and Yukun took position on the Datong River south of the southern gate; Ye Zhichao's subordinate Jiang Zikang held the hill north of the northern gate; and Baogui was charged with defending the city itself.
entries.literal: Thereupon Rugui's and Yukun's troops were on the Datong River south of the southern gate; Ye Zhichao's subordinate Jiang Zikang's troops on the hill north of the northern gate; Baogui was charged with holding the city.

entries.zh: 未止舍，日軍猝至，寶貴與丰紳阿擊卻之。
entries.en: They had scarcely made camp when Japanese troops struck without warning; Baogui and Fengshen'e drove them back.
entries.literal: Before they had even settled in camp, Japanese troops suddenly arrived; Baogui and Fengshen'e beat them back.

entries.zh: 敵退龍岡，分道來攻，又敗之。
entries.en: The enemy fell back to Longgang and attacked along several routes; they were beaten again.
entries.literal: The enemy withdrew to Longgang and attacked by separate routes; they were defeated again.

entries.zh: 志超乃聚全軍為嬰城計。
entries.en: Ye Zhichao then drew the whole army together to hold the city behind its walls.
entries.literal: Ye Zhichao then gathered the entire army to plan a purely defensive holding of the city.

entries.zh: 論曰：中東之戰，陸軍皆遁，寶貴獨死平壤；
entries.en: The historian comments: In the war with Japan, the land armies all fled, but Baogui alone died at Pyongyang;
entries.literal: The historian comments: In the China–Japan War, the land armies all fled, but Baogui alone died at Pyongyang;

entries.zh: 海軍皆降，世昌獨死東溝。
entries.en: the navy all surrendered, but Shichang alone died at Dadonggou.
entries.literal: the navy all surrendered, but Shichang alone died at Dadonggou.

entries.zh: 中外傳其壯節，並稱「雙忠」。
entries.en: Their heroic deaths were celebrated far and wide, and the two were paired as the "Two Loyal Ones."
entries.literal: Within and beyond the realm their heroic deaths were told, and they were jointly called the "Two Loyal Ones."

entries.zh: 及日兵入奉，永山獨死鳳城，敵遂長驅進矣。
entries.en: When Japanese troops entered Fengtian, Yong Shan alone died at Fengcheng, and the enemy drove on unchecked.
entries.literal: When Japanese troops entered Fengtian, Yong Shan alone died at Fengcheng, and the enemy then drove deep inland.

entries.zh: 旅、大既失，威海勢孤，步蟾、宗騫皆先後誓死。
entries.en: After Lüshun and Dalian fell, Weihai was cut off; Buchan and Zongqian each in turn swore to die for the cause.
entries.literal: After Lüshun and Dalian were lost, Weihai stood isolated; Buchan and Zongqian each in turn swore to die.

entries.zh: 士氣如此，豈遂不可一戰？
entries.en: With spirit like this in the ranks, could they really not have fought once more?
entries.literal: With morale such as this, could they truly not have fought one more battle?

entries.zh: 此主兵者之責。
entries.en: That failure lay with those who commanded the armies.
entries.literal: This was the responsibility of those who commanded the armies.

entries.zh: 五人雖敗，猶有榮焉！
entries.en: Though these five men were defeated, they died with honor!
entries.literal: Though these five men were defeated, they still had honor!

entries.zh: 列傳二百四十七
entries.en: Biography 247
entries.literal: Biographies, number two hundred forty-seven.

entries.zh: 唐景崧劉永福唐景崧，字維卿，廣西灌陽人。
entries.en: Tang Jingsong and Liu Yongfu. Tang Jingsong, whose courtesy name was Weiqing, came from Guanyang in Guangxi.
entries.literal: Tang Jingsong, Liu Yongfu. Tang Jingsong, courtesy name Weiqing, was a native of Guanyang in Guangxi.

entries.zh: 同治四年進士，選庶吉士，改吏部主事。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of the Tongzhi reign, entered the Hanlin Academy as a junior compiler, and was later appointed a director in the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tongzhi he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a junior compiler in the Hanlin Academy, and was transferred to serve as a director in the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 光緒八年，法越事起，自請出關招致劉永福，廷旨交岑毓英差序。
entries.en: When the Franco-Vietnamese conflict broke out in the eighth year of Guangxu, he volunteered to go beyond the border to recruit Liu Yongfu, and the court entrusted the assignment to Cen Yuying.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Guangxu the Franco-Vietnamese affair arose; he volunteered to cross the border to win over Liu Yongfu, and the court ordered Cen Yuying to arrange the matter.

entries.zh: 景崧先至粵，謁曾國荃，韙其議，資之入越。
entries.en: Jingsong went first to Guangdong and visited Zeng Guoquan, who endorsed his plan and funded his mission into Vietnam.
entries.literal: Jingsong went first to Guangdong, called on Zeng Guoquan, who approved his plan and supplied funds for his entry into Vietnam.

entries.zh: 明年，抵保勝，見永福，為陳三策，謂：「據保勝十州，傳檄而定諸省，請命中國，假以名號，事成則王，此上策也；
entries.en: The following year he reached Baosheng and met Yongfu, presenting three strategies: "Seize the ten districts around Baosheng, proclaim your authority to bring the provinces into line, and ask China for a formal title—success would make you king. That is the best course;
entries.literal: The next year he reached Baosheng, met Yongfu, and set forth three plans, saying: "Hold the ten prefectures around Baosheng, issue proclamations to bring the provinces to submission, ask China to grant a title—if successful you become king; this is the best plan;

entries.zh: 次則提全師擊河內，中國必助之餉；
entries.en: next, march your full force against Hanoi, with China certain to supply your rations;
entries.literal: next, lead the whole army to strike Hanoi, and China will certainly supply provisions;

entries.zh: 若坐守保勝，事敗而投中國，策之下也。」
entries.en: if you merely hold Baosheng, fail, and then throw yourself on China, that is the worst course."
entries.literal: if you merely sit and guard Baosheng, fail, and then submit to China, that is the worst plan."

entries.zh: 永福從中策。
entries.en: Yongfu chose the middle course.
entries.literal: Yongfu adopted the middle plan.

entries.zh: 戰紙橋，敵潰，為作檄文佈告內外，檄出，遠近爭響應。
entries.en: At Paper Bridge the enemy was routed. Jingsong drafted a proclamation for circulation at home and abroad, and once it went out, supporters rallied from far and near.
entries.literal: They fought at Paper Bridge; the enemy was routed. He drafted a proclamation for circulation at home and abroad; once it was issued, responses poured in from far and near.

entries.zh: 越嗣君為法脅，莫能自振，景崧乘間勸內附。
entries.en: The Vietnamese heir was bullied by France and could not recover his authority; Jingsong seized the moment to urge bringing Vietnam under Chinese protection.
entries.literal: The Vietnamese heir was coerced by France and could not recover himself; Jingsong seized the opportunity to urge submission to China.

entries.zh: 永福意猶豫，景崧曰：「子能存亡繼絕，即所以報故主也。
entries.en: Yongfu still hesitated. Jingsong told him: "If you can save a dying state and restore a broken line, that is how you repay your former sovereign.
entries.literal: Yongfu was still hesitant. Jingsong said: "If you can preserve what is perishing and continue what is cut off, that is how you repay your former lord.

entries.zh: 且阮福時已薨，無背主嫌。」
entries.en: Besides, Nguyen Phuc Thi is already dead, so you cannot be accused of betraying your lord."
entries.literal: Moreover, Nguyen Phuc Thi is already dead, so there is no taint of betraying one's lord."

entries.zh: 永福意稍動，於是廣招戎幕謀大舉。
entries.en: Yongfu was somewhat swayed, and he then recruited military advisers on a broad scale to plan a major offensive.
entries.literal: Yongfu's mind was somewhat moved, and he then widely recruited military advisers to plan a major campaign.

entries.zh: 上念景崧勞，賞四品銜。
entries.en: The emperor, mindful of Jingsong's service, granted him a fourth-rank title.
entries.literal: The emperor, mindful of Jingsong's labors, rewarded him with a fourth-rank title.

entries.zh: 九年，法人要議越事，岑毓英力言土寇可驅，永福斷不宜逐，上韙之，命永福相機規河內，並濟以餉。
entries.en: In the ninth year the French demanded negotiations on Vietnam; Cen Yuying argued strongly that local bandits could be driven off and Yongfu must by no means be expelled; the emperor approved and ordered Yongfu to seize the opportunity to plan against Hanoi while supplying his rations.
entries.literal: In the ninth year the French demanded negotiations on Vietnam; Cen Yuying strongly argued that local bandits could be driven off and Yongfu must by no means be expelled; the emperor approved and ordered Yongfu to seize the opportunity to plan against Hanoi and also supplied provisions.

entries.zh: 十年，毓英次嘉喻關，永福往謁，毓英極優禮之，編其軍為十二營。
entries.en: In the tenth year Yuying was stationed at Jiayuguan; Yongfu went to call on him; Yuying treated him with the utmost courtesy and organized his army into twelve battalions.
entries.literal: In the tenth year Yuying was stationed at Jiayuguan; Yongfu went to call on him; Yuying treated him with the utmost courtesy and organized his army into twelve battalions.

entries.zh: 法人聞之，改道犯北寧。
entries.en: When the French heard of this, they changed course and attacked Bac Ninh.
entries.literal: When the French heard of this, they changed course and attacked Bac Ninh.

entries.zh: 永福馳援，迳永祥金，英、法教民梗阻，擊卻之。
entries.en: Yongfu hurried to the relief, went straight through Yongxiangjin, drove off British and French missionary converts who blocked the way.
entries.literal: Yongfu hurried to the relief, went straight through Yongxiangjin; British and French missionary converts blocked the way and he drove them off.

entries.zh: 比至，粵軍已大潰，永福奪還扶朗、猛球砲台。
entries.en: By the time he arrived the Guangdong army had already been routed; Yongfu recaptured the batteries at Phu Lang Thuong and Mong Cau.
entries.literal: By the time he arrived the Guangdong army had already been routed; Yongfu recaptured the batteries at Phu Lang Thuong and Mong Cau.

entries.zh: 俄北寧失，力不支，再還興化。
entries.en: Soon Bac Ninh fell; unable to hold, he returned again to Xinghua.
entries.literal: Soon Bac Ninh fell; unable to hold, he returned again to Xinghua.

entries.zh: 復以糧運艱阻，改壁文盤洲大灘，候進止。
entries.en: Again, because grain transport was difficult, he shifted his camp to Wenpanzhou Datan and awaited orders.
entries.literal: Again, because grain transport was difficult, he shifted his camp to Wenpanzhou Datan and awaited orders to advance or halt.

entries.zh: 毓英奏言：「永福為越官守越地，分所應為，若畀以職，將來邊徼海澨，皆可驅策。」
entries.en: Yuying memorialized: "As a Vietnamese official Yongfu guards Vietnamese territory—this is his proper duty; if he is given office, in future the borderlands and seacoasts can all be driven by him."
entries.literal: Yuying memorialized: "Yongfu as a Vietnamese official guards Vietnamese territory—this is what he ought to do; if he is given office, in future the borderlands and seacoasts can all be driven by him."

entries.zh: 於是擢提督，賞花翎。
entries.en: He was then promoted to provincial commander and awarded the peacock feather.
entries.literal: He was then promoted to provincial commander and awarded the peacock feather.

entries.zh: 而李鴻章堅持和議，猶責其騷動。
entries.en: But Li Hongzhang insisted on peace talks and still blamed him for stirring up trouble.
entries.literal: But Li Hongzhang insisted on peace talks and still blamed him for stirring up trouble.

entries.zh: 已，和局中變，上令永福軍先進。
entries.en: Soon the peace negotiations broke down; the emperor ordered Yongfu's army to advance first.
entries.literal: Soon the peace negotiations changed; the emperor ordered Yongfu's army to advance first.

entries.zh: 法人擾宣光，永福窖地雷待之，連日隱卒以誘敵，不敢出。
entries.en: The French harassed Tuyen Quang; Yongfu buried land mines to await them, for days concealed his troops to lure the enemy, and they did not dare come out.
entries.literal: The French harassed Tuyen Quang; Yongfu buried land mines to await them, for days concealed his troops to lure the enemy, and they did not dare come out.

entries.zh: 复徙營偪城，三戰皆利。
entries.en: He moved camp again to press the city, and won all three engagements.
entries.literal: Again he moved camp to press the city; three battles were all victorious.

entries.zh: 敵援至，毓英遣水師溯河而上，永福夾流截擊，奪其船二十馀艘，斬馘數十級，法人愕走。
entries.en: When enemy reinforcements arrived, Yuying sent the river fleet upstream; Yongfu struck from both sides of the stream, captured more than twenty boats, beheaded dozens of the enemy, and the French fled in astonishment.
entries.literal: When enemy reinforcements arrived, Yuying sent the river fleet upstream; Yongfu attacked from both sides of the stream, captured more than twenty of their boats, beheaded dozens, and the French fled in astonishment.

entries.zh: 踰月，法艦入同章，毓英遣將分伏河東西，永福居中策應，兩岸轟擊，敗之，復以全力扼河道。
entries.en: After more than a month French warships entered Tongzhang; Yuying sent generals to ambush both banks while Yongfu coordinated from the center; both shores opened fire and defeated them, then sealed the river channel with full force.
entries.literal: After more than a month French warships entered Tongzhang; Yuying sent generals to lie in ambush on both banks of the river; Yongfu coordinated from the center; both shores blasted away and defeated them, then again blocked the river channel with full force.

entries.zh: 十一年，法軍攻左域，守忠失同章不守，諸軍敗挫，永福退浪泊。
entries.en: In the eleventh year the French attacked Zuoyu; Shouzhong lost Tongzhang and could not hold it; the allied armies were beaten back, and Yongfu withdrew to Langbo.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year the French attacked Zuoyu; Shouzhong lost Tongzhang and could not hold it; the armies were defeated; Yongfu withdrew to Langbo.

entries.zh: 停戰詔已下未至，猶大捷臨洮。
entries.en: The ceasefire edict had been issued but had not yet arrived; he still won a great victory at Lin Tao.
entries.literal: The ceasefire edict had been issued but not yet arrived; he still won a great victory at Lin Tao.

entries.zh: 論勝宣、臨功，賜號依博德恩巴圖魯。
entries.en: For victories at Tuyen Quang and Lin Tao he was granted the title Yibode'en Batulu.
entries.literal: In recognition of victories at Tuyen Quang and Lin Tao he was granted the title Yibode'en Batulu.

entries.zh: 和議成，法人要逐如故。
entries.en: When peace was concluded, the French still demanded his expulsion as before.
entries.literal: When peace was concluded, the French still demanded expulsion as before.

entries.zh: 張之洞令永福駐思欽，不肯行。
entries.en: Zhang Zhidong ordered Yongfu to garrison Sixin, but he refused to go.
entries.literal: Zhang Zhidong ordered Yongfu to garrison Sixin; he refused to go.

entries.zh: 景崧危詞脅之，乃勉歸於粵，授南澳鎮總兵。
entries.en: Jingsong threatened him with alarming words; he then reluctantly returned to Guangdong and was appointed commander of the Nan'ao garrison.
entries.literal: Jingsong threatened him with alarming words; he then reluctantly returned to Guangdong and was appointed commander of Nan'ao garrison.

entries.zh: 割台議起，主事邱逢甲建議自主，台民爭讚之。
entries.en: When the plan to cede Taiwan arose, the director Qiu Fengjia proposed self-rule, and the people of Taiwan vied in praising the idea.
entries.literal: When the plan to cede Taiwan arose, the director Qiu Fengjia proposed self-rule, and the people of Taiwan vied in praising it.

entries.zh: 乃建「民國」，設議院，推景崧為總統。
entries.en: They then established a "Republic," set up a parliament, and elected Jingsong president.
entries.literal: They then established a "Republic," set up a parliament, and elected Jingsong president.

entries.zh: 和議成，抗疏援贖遼先例，請免割，不報，命內渡。
entries.en: When the peace treaty was concluded, he submitted a memorial citing the precedent of redeeming Liaodong and asked that Taiwan be spared; there was no reply, and he was ordered to cross to the mainland.
entries.literal: When the peace treaty was concluded, he submitted a memorial citing the precedent of redeeming Liaodong and asked that the cession be waived; there was no reply, and he was ordered to cross to the mainland.

entries.zh: 台民憤，乃決自主，制藍旗，上印綬於景崧，鼓吹前導，紳民數千人詣撫署。
entries.en: The people of Taiwan were indignant and resolved on self-rule; they made a blue flag, presented the seal and sash to Jingsong with music leading the way, and several thousand gentry and commoners came to the governor's yamen.
entries.literal: The people of Taiwan were indignant and resolved on self-rule; they made a blue flag, presented the seal and sash to Jingsong with music leading the way, and several thousand gentry and commoners came to the governor's yamen.

entries.zh: 景崧朝服出，望闕謝罪，旋北面受任，大哭而入。
entries.en: Jingsong came out in court dress, faced toward the imperial palace and begged forgiveness, then turned north to accept office and went inside weeping.
entries.literal: Jingsong came out in court dress, faced the imperial palace and begged forgiveness, then turned north to accept office and went inside weeping.

entries.zh: 電告中外，有「遙奉正朔，永作屏籓」語，置內部、外部、軍部以下各大臣。
entries.en: He telegraphed China and foreign countries with the phrase "afar we follow the imperial calendar, forever a protective screen," and appointed grand ministers for internal affairs, foreign affairs, military affairs, and the rest.
entries.literal: He telegraphed China and foreign countries with the phrase "afar we follow the imperial calendar, forever a protective screen," and appointed grand ministers for internal affairs, foreign affairs, military affairs, and the rest.

entries.zh: 命陳季同介法人求各國承認，無應者。
entries.en: He ordered Chen Jitong to act through the French to seek recognition from the various powers, but none responded.
entries.literal: He ordered Chen Jitong to act through the French to seek recognition from the various powers; none responded.

entries.zh: 無何，日軍攻基隆，分統李文忠敗潰。
entries.en: Before long the Japanese attacked Keelung, and the deputy commander Li Wenzong was routed.
entries.literal: Before long the Japanese attacked Keelung; the deputy commander Li Wenzong was routed.

entries.zh: 景崧命黃義德頓八堵，遽馳歸，詭言獅球嶺已失，八堵不能軍，且日人懸金六十萬購總統頭，故還防內亂，景崧不敢詰也。
entries.en: Jingsong ordered Huang Yide to hold Badu, but Yide hurried back and falsely claimed Shiziuling had fallen, that Badu could not be held, and that the Japanese had posted six hundred thousand in gold for the president's head, so he had returned to guard against internal disorder; Jingsong did not dare question him.
entries.literal: Jingsong ordered Huang Yide to hold Badu, but Yide hurried back and falsely claimed Shiziuling had fallen, that Badu could not be held, and that the Japanese had posted six hundred thousand in gold for the president's head, so he returned to guard against internal disorder; Jingsong did not dare question him.

entries.zh: 是夜，義德所部譁變。
entries.en: That night Yide's troops mutinied.
entries.literal: That night Yide's troops mutinied in uproar.

entries.zh: 平旦，日軍果占獅球嶺，潰兵爭入城，城中大驚擾亂，客勇、土勇互仇殺，屍遍地。
entries.en: At dawn the Japanese indeed took Shiziuling; routed troops scrambled into the city, throwing it into panic; mercenary troops and native militia killed one another until corpses littered the streets.
entries.literal: At dawn the Japanese indeed took Shiziuling; routed troops scrambled into the city, and the city was thrown into great alarm and disorder; mercenary troops and native militia killed one another, corpses littered the ground.

entries.zh: 總統府火發，景崧微服挈子遁，附英輪至廈門，時立國方七日也。
entries.en: Fire broke out at the presidential residence; Jingsong slipped away in plain clothes with his son aboard a British steamer to Xiamen—the republic had lasted only seven days.
entries.literal: Fire broke out at the presidential residence; Jingsong slipped away in plain clothes with his son, took a British steamer to Xiamen—the republic had stood only seven days.

entries.zh: 二十八年，卒。
entries.en: He died in the twenty-eighth year of Guangxu.
entries.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died.

entries.zh: 列傳二百五十
entries.en: Biographies 250
entries.literal: Biographies 250

entries.zh: 李端棻 徐致靖 子仁鑄 陳寶箴 黃遵憲 曾鉌 楊深秀 楊銳 劉光第 譚嗣同 唐才常 林旭 康廣仁 李端棻，字苾園，貴州貴筑人。
entries.en: Li Duanfen, Xu Zhijing, his son Renzhu, Chen Baozhen, Huang Zunxian, Zeng He, Yang Shenxiu, Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Tang Caichang, Lin Xu, and Kang Guangren. Li Duanfen, whose courtesy name was Biyuan, came from Guizhu in Guizhou.
entries.literal: Li Duanfen, Xu Zhijing, son Renzhu, Chen Baozhen, Huang Zunxian, Zeng He, Yang Shenxiu, Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Tang Caichang, Lin Xu, and Kang Guangren. Li Duanfen, courtesy name Biyuan, was a native of Guizhu in Guizhou.

entries.zh: 同治二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，為大學士倭仁、尚書羅敦衍所器。
entries.en: In Tongzhi 2 he took his jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin as a junior compiler, was appointed a compiler, and won the regard of Grand Secretary Woren and Minister Luo Dunyan.
entries.literal: In Tongzhi year two he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a junior compiler, appointed compiler, and was valued by Grand Secretary Woren and Minister Luo Dunyan.

entries.zh: 十年，出督雲南學政。
entries.en: In year ten he was sent out as Educational Commissioner of Yunnan.
entries.literal: In year ten, he was sent out as Educational Commissioner of Yunnan.

entries.zh: 值回寇亂後，荒服道亙，前使者試未遍，端棻始一一按臨，文化漸振。
entries.en: This was after the Muslim uprising, when frontier routes were still broken and the previous commissioner had not been able to hold examinations throughout the province. Duanfen toured each district in person, and learning gradually revived.
entries.literal: This was after the Muslim uprising, when frontier routes were still broken and the previous commissioner had not been able to hold examinations throughout the province. Duanfen now toured each district in person, and culture and learning gradually revived.

entries.zh: 光緒五年，轉御史，以叔父朝儀官京尹，迴避，改故官。
entries.en: In Guangxu 5 he was made a censor, but when his uncle Chaoyi served as metropolitan magistrate of Beijing, he withdrew under the kinship rule and resumed his former office.
entries.literal: In Guangxu year five he was transferred to censor, but because his uncle Chaoyi held office as metropolitan magistrate of Beijing, he withdrew under the avoidance rule and returned to his former office.

entries.zh: 累擢內閣學士。
entries.en: He rose step by step to junior grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to junior grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

entries.zh: 十八年，遷刑部侍郎。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year he was moved to vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.

entries.zh: 越六年，調倉場。
entries.en: Six years later he was reassigned to oversee the grain depots.
entries.literal: Six years later he was transferred to the grain depots.

entries.zh: 前後迭司文柄，四為鄉試考官，一為會試副總裁，喜獎拔士類。
entries.en: On several occasions he held charge of the civil examinations, serving four times as provincial examiner and once as associate chief examiner for the metropolitan examination, and he took pleasure in recognizing and advancing promising scholars.
entries.literal: Before and after he repeatedly held control of literary examinations: four times as examiner for the provincial examinations and once as associate chief examiner for the metropolitan examination; he delighted in rewarding and promoting men of talent.

entries.zh: 典試廣東，賞梁啟超才，以從妹妻之，自是頗納啟超議，娓娓道東西邦制度。
entries.en: While conducting examinations in Guangdong he admired Liang Qichao's ability, married a younger female cousin to him, and thereafter often took Liang's counsel, speaking at length about the political systems of East and West.
entries.literal: While conducting examinations in Guangdong he admired Liang Qichao's ability and married a younger female cousin to him; thereafter he often accepted Qichao's counsel and spoke at length about the institutions of Eastern and Western countries.

entries.zh: 維時康有為上書請變法，兼及興學。
entries.en: About this time Kang Youwei submitted memorials calling for reform and for the expansion of education.
entries.literal: At this time Kang Youwei submitted memorials requesting reform, also touching on the promotion of schools.

entries.zh: 二十二年，端棻遂疏請立京師大學，凡各省府、州、縣遍設學堂，分齋講習；
entries.en: In year twenty-two Duanfen memorialized to establish a national university in the capital and schools in every province, prefecture, department, and county, with separate halls for study;
entries.literal: In year twenty-two, Duanfen then memorialized requesting the establishment of a capital university, and that schools be set up throughout every province, prefecture, department, and county, with halls divided for instruction and practice;

entries.zh: 並建藏書樓、儀器院、譯書局，廣立報館，選派遊歷生。
entries.en: and to set up libraries, instrument halls, and translation bureaus, to open newspapers widely, and to select students to travel abroad for study.
entries.literal: and also to build libraries, instrument halls, and translation bureaus, to establish newspapers widely, and to select and send students abroad for observation.

entries.zh: 二十四年，密薦康有為及譚嗣同堪大用。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year he secretly recommended Kang Youwei and Tan Sitong as men capable of high responsibility.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he secretly recommended Kang Youwei and Tan Sitong as fit for great employment.

entries.zh: 又以各衙門則例，語涉紛歧，疏請刪訂，上尤善之，詔趣各長官定限期革前敝。
entries.en: He further observed that the regulatory precedents of the various offices were inconsistent in wording and asked that they be revised; the emperor was especially pleased and ordered each department head to fix a deadline for removing old abuses.
entries.literal: He also noted that the regulations of the various yamens were worded in conflicting ways and memorialized requesting their revision; the emperor especially approved this and ordered each chief official to set a deadline for abolishing former abuses.

entries.zh: 擢禮部尚書。
entries.en: He was promoted to minister of the Ministry of Rites.
entries.literal: He was promoted to minister of the Ministry of Rites.

entries.zh: 未幾，有為等敗，端棻自疏檢舉，詔褫職，戍新疆。
entries.en: Before long Kang Youwei's party fell; Duanfen submitted a memorial denouncing himself, and an edict removed him from office and banished him to Xinjiang.
entries.literal: Before long Kang Youwei and his associates were ruined; Duanfen memorialized accusing himself, and an edict stripped him of office and sent him into exile in Xinjiang.

entries.zh: 中道遘疾，留甘州。
entries.en: He fell ill en route and was held at Ganzhou.
entries.literal: On the way he fell ill and was detained at Ganzhou.

entries.zh: 二十七年，赦歸，主講貴州經世學堂。
entries.en: In the twenty-seventh year he was amnestied and went home, where he lectured at the Guizhou Jingshi Academy.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was pardoned and returned home, where he served as lecturer at the Guizhou Jingshi Academy.

entries.zh: 三十三年，卒。
entries.en: In the thirty-third year he died.
entries.literal: In the thirty-third year he died.

entries.zh: 宣統元年，從雲南、貴州京朝官請，復官。
entries.en: In the first year of Xuantong, at the petition of Yunnan and Guizhou officials in Beijing, his former office was restored.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xuantong, at the request of officials from Yunnan and Guizhou in the capital, his former office was restored.

entries.zh: 徐致靖，字子靜，江蘇宜興人，寄籍宛平。
entries.en: Xu Zhijing, whose courtesy name was Zijing, came from Yixing in Jiangsu and was registered at Wanping.
entries.literal: Xu Zhijing, courtesy name Zijing, was a native of Yixing in Jiangsu, with registered domicile at Wanping.

entries.zh: 光緒二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
entries.en: In Guangxu 2 he took his jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin as a junior compiler, and was appointed a compiler.
entries.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a junior compiler, and appointed compiler.

entries.zh: 累遷侍讀學士。
entries.en: He rose in stages to reader-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to reader-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy.

entries.zh: 父憂服闋，二十三年，起故官。
entries.en: After completing mourning for his father, in the twenty-third year he was recalled to his former office.
entries.literal: When his mourning for his father was completed, in the twenty-third year he was recalled to his former post.

entries.zh: 致靖嘗憂外患日迫，思所以為獻納計。
entries.en: Zhijing had long been troubled by the daily tightening of foreign pressure and pondered how he might advise the throne.
entries.literal: Zhijing had long been troubled by foreign pressure growing daily more urgent and pondered how he might offer advice to the throne.

entries.zh: 子仁鑄，時以編修督湘學，倡新學，書告致靖舉康有為。
entries.en: His son Renzhu, then a compiler serving as Hunan's educational commissioner, promoted the new learning and wrote urging Zhijing to recommend Kang Youwei.
entries.literal: His son Renzhu, then a compiler serving as educational commissioner of Hunan, promoted the new learning and wrote telling Zhijing to recommend Kang Youwei.

entries.zh: 致靖遂上言：「國是未定，請申乾斷示從違。」
entries.en: Zhijing then memorialized: "The nation's course is still unsettled; I ask that Your Majesty's own judgment be made explicit, showing what is to be adopted and what rejected."
entries.literal: Zhijing then memorialized: "The nation's course is still unsettled; I request that Your Majesty's own judgment be made explicit, showing what is to be adopted and what rejected."

entries.zh: 藉以覘上意。
entries.en: In this way he hoped to discern the emperor's intentions.
entries.literal: Thus he sought to gauge the emperor's mind.

entries.zh: 未幾，詔果求通才，於是致靖奏有為堪大用，並及梁啟超、黃遵憲等。
entries.en: Soon an edict did call for broadly talented men; Zhijing then reported that Kang Youwei was fit for high office, and also named Liang Qichao, Huang Zunxian, and others.
entries.literal: Before long an edict indeed called for men of broad ability; Zhijing then memorialized that Youwei was fit for great employment, and also named Liang Qichao, Huang Zunxian, and others.

entries.zh: 又連上書請廢製藝，改試策論，省冗官，酌置散卿。
entries.en: He also sent a series of memorials asking to abolish the eight-legged essay, test policy essays instead, cut redundant offices, and appoint honorary grand secretaries as appropriate.
entries.literal: He also submitted successive memorials requesting the abolition of the examination essay, replacement by policy discourse, reduction of superfluous offices, and the considered establishment of honorary grand secretaries.

entries.zh: 復以邊患棘，宜練重兵，力荐袁世凱主軍事。
entries.en: He further urged that with border crises pressing, large forces should be drilled, and strongly recommended Yuan Shikai to direct military affairs.
entries.literal: He further urged that with border troubles urgent, heavy forces should be trained, and strongly recommended Yuan Shikai to direct military affairs.

entries.zh: 上皆然其言，敕依行。
entries.en: The emperor approved all his proposals and ordered them implemented.
entries.literal: The emperor approved all his proposals and ordered them carried out.

entries.zh: 罷斥禮部尚書許應騤等阻遏言路，遂命致靖權右侍郎。
entries.en: Minister of Rites Xu Yingkui and others who had obstructed memorials to the throne were removed, and Zhijing was appointed acting right vice minister.
entries.literal: Minister of Rites Xu Yingkui and others who had obstructed the channels of remonstrance were removed, and Zhijing was appointed acting right vice minister.

entries.zh: 二十四年八月，太后復出訓政，參預新政諸臣皆獲罪。
entries.en: In the eighth month of the twenty-fourth year the empress dowager resumed control of government, and every official who had joined the reform movement was punished.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-fourth year the empress dowager resumed regency, and all the officials who had taken part in the new policies were punished.

entries.zh: 致靖褫職坐系，尋定永遠監禁，仁鑄亦罷官。
entries.en: Zhijing was stripped of rank and imprisoned; he was soon sentenced to lifelong detention, and Renzhu was dismissed from office as well.
entries.literal: Zhijing was stripped of office and imprisoned; soon he was sentenced to lifelong detention, and Renzhu was also dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 庚子，聯軍陷京師，致靖始出獄待罪，詔赦免。
entries.en: In the gengzi year, when the allied armies occupied Beijing, Zhijing was released from prison to await sentence, and an edict granted him amnesty.
entries.literal: In the gengzi year, when the allied armies occupied the capital, Zhijing was first released from prison to await sentence, and an edict granted him amnesty.

entries.zh: 卒，年七十五。
entries.en: He died at the age of seventy-five.
entries.literal: He died at the age of seventy-five.

entries.zh: 陳寶箴，字右銘，江西義寧人。
entries.en: Chen Baozhen, courtesy name Youming, was from Yining in Jiangxi.
entries.literal: Chen Baozhen, courtesy name Youming, was from Yining in Jiangxi.

entries.zh: 少負志節，詩文皆有法度，為曾國籓所器。
entries.en: From youth he showed strong character; his poetry and prose were disciplined, and Zeng Guofan valued him.
entries.literal: From youth he showed strong character; his poetry and prose were disciplined, and Zeng Guofan valued him.

entries.zh: 以舉人隨父偉琳治鄉團，禦粵寇。
entries.en: While still a provincial graduate, he followed his father Weilin in managing local militia against the Guangdong rebels.
entries.literal: While still a provincial graduate, he followed his father Weilin in managing local militia against the Guangdong rebels.

entries.zh: 已而走湖南，參易佩紳戎幕，軍來鳳、龍山間。
entries.en: He then went to Hunan, entered Yi Peishen’s military staff, and campaigned between Laifeng and Longshan.
entries.literal: He then went to Hunan, entered Yi Peishen’s military staff, and campaigned between Laifeng and Longshan.

entries.zh: 石達開來犯，軍飢疲，走永順募糧，糧至不絕，守益堅，寇稍稍引去。
entries.en: When Shi Dakai attacked, the troops were hungry and exhausted; Baozhen went to Yongshun to raise grain, supplies kept coming, the defense held firmer, and the rebels gradually withdrew.
entries.literal: When Shi Dakai attacked, the troops were hungry and exhausted; Baozhen went to Yongshun to raise grain, supplies kept coming, the defense held firmer, and the rebels gradually withdrew.

entries.zh: 寶箴之江西，為席寶田畫策殲寇洪福瑱，事寧，敘知府，超授河北道。
entries.en: When Baozhen went to Jiangxi, he planned for Xi Baotian the destruction of the rebel Hong Fuzhen; when matters were pacified, he was recommended as prefect and promoted out of turn to intendant of Hebei Circuit.
entries.literal: When Baozhen went to Jiangxi, he planned for Xi Baotian the destruction of the rebel Hong Fuzhen; when matters were pacified, he was recommended as prefect and promoted out of turn to intendant of Hebei Circuit.

entries.zh: 創致用精舍，遴選三州學子，延名師教之。
entries.en: He founded the Zhiyong Jingshe Academy, selected students from three prefectures, and invited distinguished teachers to instruct them.
entries.literal: He founded the Zhiyong Jingshe Academy, selected students from three prefectures, and invited distinguished teachers to instruct them.

entries.zh: 遷浙江按察使，坐事免。
entries.en: He was transferred to be judicial commissioner of Zhejiang but was removed because of an affair.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be judicial commissioner of Zhejiang but was removed because of an affair.

entries.zh: 湖南巡撫王文韶薦其才，光緒十六年，召入都，除湖北按察使，署布政使。
entries.en: Hunan governor Wang Wenshao recommended his ability; in Guangxu 16 he was summoned to the capital, appointed judicial commissioner of Hubei, and made acting provincial administration commissioner.
entries.literal: Hunan governor Wang Wenshao recommended his ability; in Guangxu 16 he was summoned to the capital, appointed judicial commissioner of Hubei, and made acting provincial administration commissioner.

entries.zh: 二十年，擢直隸布政使，入對，時中東戰亟，見上形容憂悴，請日讀聖祖御纂周易，以期變不失常。
entries.en: In Guangxu 20 he was promoted to provincial administration commissioner of Zhili. When received in audience, with the Sino-Japanese war pressing and seeing the emperor’s worn and anxious appearance, he requested that the emperor read daily the Kangxi Emperor’s imperially compiled Zhouyi, hoping that amid change he would not lose constancy.
entries.literal: In Guangxu 20 he was promoted to provincial administration commissioner of Zhili. When received in audience, with the Sino-Japanese war pressing and seeing the emperor’s worn and anxious appearance, he requested that the emperor read daily the Kangxi Emperor’s imperially compiled Zhouyi, hoping that amid change he would not lose constancy.

entries.zh: 他所陳奏語甚多，並稱旨。
entries.en: His other memorials were many, and all met with the emperor's approval.
entries.literal: His other memorial statements were numerous, and all pleased the emperor.

entries.zh: 上以為忠，命治糈台，專摺奏事。
entries.en: The emperor judged him loyal and put him in charge of the grain depots with authority to submit memorials directly.
entries.literal: The emperor regarded him as loyal and ordered him to manage the grain depots and submit memorials on his own authority.

entries.zh: 馬關和約成，泣曰：「殆不國矣！」
entries.en: When the Treaty of Shimonoseki was signed, he wept and said, "The dynasty is all but finished!"
entries.literal: When the Treaty of Shimonoseki was concluded, he wept and said: "The state is nearly lost!"

entries.zh: 明年，以榮祿薦，擢湖南巡撫。
entries.en: The following year, on Ronglu's recommendation, he was made Governor of Hunan.
entries.literal: The next year, on Ronglu's recommendation, he was promoted to Governor of Hunan.

entries.zh: 撫幕有任驎者，植黨私利，至即重治之。
entries.en: A man named Ren Lin in the governor's staff had built a clique for private gain; Baozhen punished him severely as soon as he took office.
entries.literal: In the governor's secretariat there was Ren Lin, who formed a faction for private profit; as soon as Baozhen arrived he punished him severely.

entries.zh: 直隸布政使王廉為關說，據以上聞，廉獲譴。
entries.en: Zhili treasurer Wang Lian pleaded on Ren's behalf; Baozhen reported the matter upward, and Wang was censured.
entries.literal: Zhili Provincial Treasurer Wang Lian interceded for him; Baozhen reported the facts to the throne, and Lian was punished.

entries.zh: 覆按史念祖被劾事，盡暴其任用非人狀，念祖遂褫職。
entries.en: He reviewed the impeachment of Shi Nianzu, fully exposing how Nianzu had appointed unfit men, and Nianzu was dismissed.
entries.literal: He reinvestigated the case in which Shi Nianzu had been impeached, fully exposing how Nianzu had employed unworthy men, and Nianzu was stripped of office.

entries.zh: 繇是有伉直聲。
entries.en: From this he gained a reputation for uncompromising integrity.
entries.literal: From this he gained a reputation for stern uprightness.

entries.zh: 湘俗故闇僿，寶箴思以一隅致富強，為東南倡，先後設電信，置小輪，建製造槍彈廠，又立保衛局、南學會、時務學堂。
entries.en: Hunan had long been backward and insular; Baozhen hoped to make the province a model of wealth and strength for the southeast. He set up telegraph lines, introduced steam launches, built an arms and ammunition factory, and founded a Public Security Bureau, the Southern Study Society, and the Current Affairs Academy.
entries.literal: Hunan customs were formerly benighted and obstructed; Baozhen wished to make one corner rich and strong and be a leader for the southeast. In succession he set up telegraph lines, introduced steam launches, built a factory for manufacturing firearms and ammunition, and also established a Public Security Bureau, the Southern Study Society, and the Current Affairs Academy.

entries.zh: 延梁啟超主湘學，湘俗大變。
entries.en: He invited Liang Qichao to lead Hunan's schools, and local attitudes changed dramatically.
entries.literal: He invited Liang Qichao to direct Hunan learning, and local custom changed greatly.

entries.zh: 又疏請釐正學術及練兵、籌款諸大端，上皆嘉納，敕令持定見，毋為浮言動，並特旨褒勵之。
entries.en: He also memorialized on reforming scholarship, drilling troops, and raising revenue; the emperor approved everything, told him to stand by his convictions and ignore loose talk, and issued a special edict of praise.
entries.literal: He also memorialized requesting correction of scholarship and the major tasks of drilling troops and raising funds; the emperor approved all and ordered him to hold firm views and not be moved by loose talk, and also issued a special edict praising him.

entries.zh: 是時張之洞負盛名，司道咸屏息以伺。
entries.en: At this time Zhang Zhidong enjoyed great fame, and the provincial officials all held their breath and watched him.
entries.literal: At this time Zhang Zhidong enjoyed great fame, and the provincial officials all held their breath and watched him.

entries.zh: 寶箴初綰鄂籓，遇事不合，獨與爭無私撓，之洞雖不懌，無如何也。
entries.en: When Baozhen first took charge of Hubei’s provincial administration, whenever matters did not accord, he alone argued with Zhang without private compromise; though Zhidong was displeased, there was nothing he could do.
entries.literal: When Baozhen first took charge of Hubei’s provincial administration, whenever matters did not accord, he alone argued with Zhang without private compromise; though Zhidong was displeased, there was nothing he could do.

entries.zh: 久之，兩人深相結，凡條上新政皆聯銜，而鄂撫譚繼洵反不與。
entries.en: In time the two became deeply allied; every memorial setting out new policies bore both their names, while Hubei governor Tan Jixun, by contrast, did not participate.
entries.literal: In time the two became deeply allied; every memorial setting out new policies bore both their names, while Hubei governor Tan Jixun, by contrast, did not participate.

entries.zh: 會康有為言事數見效。
entries.en: At that time Kang Youwei’s policy proposals had repeatedly shown results.
entries.literal: At that time Kang Youwei’s policy proposals had repeatedly shown results.

entries.zh: 寶箴素慕曾、胡薦士，因上言楊銳、劉光第、譚嗣同、林旭佐新政。
entries.en: Baozhen had long admired how Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi recommended men, and therefore memorialized that Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, and Lin Xu should assist the new policies.
entries.literal: Baozhen had long admired how Zeng Guofan and Hu Linyi recommended men, and therefore memorialized that Yang Rui, Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, and Lin Xu should assist the new policies.

entries.zh: 上方詔求通變才，遽擢京卿，參新政，於是四人上書論時事無顧忌。
entries.en: The emperor had just called for adaptable talent; the four were suddenly raised to high office in the capital to join the reforms, and from then on they spoke on public affairs without restraint.
entries.literal: The emperor had just issued an edict seeking men of adaptable talent; the four were abruptly promoted to grand secretaries in the capital to take part in the new policies, and thereafter they memorialized on current affairs without reserve.

entries.zh: 寶箴又言四人雖才，恐資望輕，視事過易，原得厚重大臣如之洞者領之。
entries.en: Baozhen also said that though the four were able, their standing was slight and they might treat office too lightly; he asked that a senior figure such as Zhang Zhidong supervise them.
entries.literal: Baozhen also said that though the four were talented, he feared their standing was light and they would treat office too easily; he wished to have a weighty senior minister such as Zhidong lead them.

entries.zh: 疏上而太后已出訓政，誅四京卿，罪及舉主，寶箴去官，其子主事三立亦革職，並毀湘學所著學約、界說、劄記、答問諸書。
entries.en: By the time the memorial arrived the empress dowager had resumed power; the four capital officials were executed, blame fell on their recommender, Baozhen was dismissed, his son Sanli was stripped of office, and the Hunan school's Xueyue, Jieshuo, Zhaji, and Dawen were destroyed.
entries.literal: By the time the memorial arrived, the Empress Dowager had already issued instructions and resumed government; the four capital officials were executed, blame extended to their recommender, Baozhen left office, his son Sanli, a ministry secretary, was also dismissed, and the Hunan school's works Xueyue, Jieshuo, Zhaji, and Dawen were destroyed.

entries.zh: 初，寧鄉已革道員周漢，以張揭帖攻西教為總督所治。
entries.en: Earlier the dismissed intendant Zhou Han of Ningxiang had been punished by the governor-general for posting anti-Christian placards.
entries.literal: Earlier, Zhou Han, a dismissed intendant from Ningxiang, had been punished by the governor-general for posting placards attacking the Western religion.

entries.zh: 寶箴至，漢復刊帖傳布，寶箴令毀之，漢毆毀帖者，寶箴怒，下之獄。
entries.en: When Baozhen arrived, Zhou Han printed placards again; Baozhen ordered them destroyed, Zhou Han beat those who tore them down, and Baozhen had him jailed in anger.
entries.literal: When Baozhen arrived, Han again printed placards and circulated them. Baozhen ordered them destroyed; Han beat those who destroyed the placards, and Baozhen angrily had him jailed.

entries.zh: 舊黨恨次骨，然喜新之士，亦以此翕然稱之。
entries.en: The conservative faction hated him bitterly, yet reform-minded men united in praise for the same act.
entries.literal: The old faction hated him to the marrow, yet men who favored the new learning also united in praising him for this.

entries.zh: 既去，諸所營構便於民者，雖效益已著，皆廢毀無一存雲。
entries.en: After he left, every institution he had built for the people, though already proving useful, was abolished until nothing remained.
entries.literal: After he left, all the institutions he had built for the people's benefit, though their good effects were already evident, were abolished and destroyed until not one remained.

entries.zh: 卒，年七十。
entries.en: He died at the age of seventy.
entries.literal: He died at the age of seventy.

entries.zh: 黃遵憲，字公度，嘉應州人。
entries.en: Huang Zunxian, whose courtesy name was Gongdu, came from Jiaying Prefecture.
entries.literal: Huang Zunxian, courtesy name Gongdu, was a native of Jiaying Prefecture.

entries.zh: 以舉人入貲為道員。
entries.en: As a provincial graduate he bought appointment as a circuit intendant.
entries.literal: As a provincial graduate he purchased appointment as a circuit intendant.

entries.zh: 充使日參贊，著日本國誌上之朝。
entries.en: He served as attaché on the mission to Japan and submitted his Record of Japan to the court.
entries.literal: He served as counsellor on the mission to Japan and submitted his Riben guozhi to the court.

entries.zh: 旋移舊金山總領事。
entries.en: He was soon made consul-general at San Francisco.
entries.literal: He was soon transferred to be consul-general at San Francisco.

entries.zh: 美吏嘗藉口衛生，逮華僑滿獄。
entries.en: American officials once used public health as a pretext to arrest Chinese residents until the prisons were packed.
entries.literal: American officials once used sanitation as a pretext to arrest Chinese residents until the prisons were full.

entries.zh: 徑詣獄中，令從者度其容積，曰：「此處衛生顧右於僑居邪？」
entries.en: Zunxian went straight to the jail and had his attendants measure its space, saying, "Is sanitation really better here than where the Chinese live?"
entries.literal: Zunxian went straight to the prison and ordered his attendants to measure its capacity, saying: "Is sanitation here really better cared for than in the Chinese quarter?"

entries.zh: 吏謝，遽釋之。
entries.en: The officials apologized and released them immediately.
entries.literal: The American officials apologized and released them at once.

entries.zh: 歷湖南長寶鹽法道，署按察使。
entries.en: He served as salt controller of Hunan's Changbao Circuit and acted as judicial commissioner.
entries.literal: He served as salt controller of Hunan's Changbao Circuit and acted as judicial commissioner.

entries.zh: 時寶箴為巡撫，行新政，遵憲首倡民治於眾曰：「亦自治其身，自治其鄉而已。
entries.en: Chen Baozhen was then governor and pursuing reforms; Zunxian first preached popular self-government to the people, saying: "It means governing yourself and governing your own township.
entries.literal: Baozhen was then governor and carrying out new policies; Zunxian first advocated people's self-government before the public, saying: "It means governing yourself and governing your own township.

entries.zh: 由一鄉推之一縣、一府、一省，以迄全國，可以成共和之郅治，臻大同之盛軌。」
entries.en: Extend that from one township to a county, a prefecture, a province, and then the whole country, and you can reach the ideal of republican government and the great harmony of the Datong age."
entries.literal: From one township extend it to one county, one prefecture, one province, and then to the whole country, and one may attain the highest government of a republic and reach the great path of universal harmony."

entries.zh: 於是略仿西國巡警之制，設保衛局，凡與民利民瘼相麗，而為一方民力能舉者，悉屬之，領以民望，而官輔其不及焉。
entries.en: He then roughly copied the Western police system and set up a Public Security Bureau; everything touching local welfare that the people could manage was placed under respected local leaders, with officials helping where needed.
entries.literal: Thereupon, roughly imitating the Western police patrol system, he established the Public Security Bureau; all matters touching the people's benefit and hardship that the local people had strength to undertake were placed under it, led by men of local standing, while officials assisted where they fell short.

entries.zh: 尋解職，奉出使日本之命，未行而黨禍起，遂罷歸。
entries.en: He soon left office and was ordered to Japan as envoy, but before he could depart the reform purge began and he went home.
entries.literal: Soon he left office and received orders to go as envoy to Japan, but before he departed the factional disaster broke out and he returned home dismissed.

entries.zh: 著有人境廬詩草等。
entries.en: He wrote works including Renjinglu Shicao and others.
entries.literal: His writings include Renjinglu Shicao and others.

entries.zh: 曾鉌，字懷清，喜塔臘氏，滿洲正白旗人。
entries.en: Zeng He, whose courtesy name was Huaiqing, of the Hitara clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
entries.literal: Zeng He, courtesy name Huaiqing, of the Hitara clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

entries.zh: 父慶昀，寧夏將軍。
entries.en: His father Qingyun was General of Ningxia.
entries.literal: His father Qingyun was General of Ningxia.

entries.zh: 以任子為工部主事，累遷郎中，充軍機章京，轉御史。
entries.en: By hereditary privilege he entered the Ministry of Works as a director, rose to bureau director, served on the Grand Council staff, and became a censor.
entries.literal: By hereditary privilege he became a director in the Ministry of Works, was promoted in succession to bureau director, served as a clerk in the Grand Council, and was transferred to censor.

entries.zh: 光緒九年，出為陝西督糧道。
entries.en: In Guangxu 9 he was sent out as grain transport commissioner of Shaanxi.
entries.literal: In Guangxu year nine, he was sent out as grain transport commissioner of Shaanxi.

entries.zh: 西、同各屬農民納糧例繳省倉，道塗艱遠，多弊竇，設法清釐之，民稱便。
entries.en: In the Xi'an and Tongzhou circuits peasants normally paid grain tax to the provincial granary; the routes were long and corrupt. He reformed the system, and the people welcomed the change.
entries.literal: In Xi'an, Tongzhou, and their subordinate districts, peasants normally paid grain tax to the provincial granary; the routes were long and difficult and there were many abuses. He devised methods to clarify and regulate it, and the people found it convenient.

entries.zh: 三輔士風樸僿，藝事苦窳，延長安柏景偉、咸陽劉光蕡主關中書院，督課實學，士論翕然。
entries.en: Scholarship in the Sanfu region was plain and narrow, and literary work was poor; he brought Bo Jingwei of Chang'an and Liu Guangfen of Xianyang to head the Guanzhong Academy, stressed practical studies, and scholars rallied to him.
entries.literal: The scholarly culture of the Sanfu region was plain and narrow, and literary work was poor; he invited Bo Jingwei of Chang'an and Liu Guangfen of Xianyang to head the Guanzhong Academy, supervised instruction in practical learning, and scholarly opinion rallied to him.

entries.zh: 又設蠶桑局，聘織師教以煮湅織染法，歲出絲帛埒齊、豫。
entries.en: He also set up a sericulture bureau, hired weavers to teach reeling, weaving, and dyeing, and each year produced silk output rivaling Shandong and Henan.
entries.literal: He also established a sericulture bureau, hired weaving masters to teach boiling, reeling, weaving, and dyeing methods, and each year produced silk and cloth rivaling Qi and Yu.

entries.zh: 十三年，遷按察使。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year he was made judicial commissioner.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to judicial commissioner.

entries.zh: 明年，母憂解職。
entries.en: The next year he left office to mourn his mother.
entries.literal: The next year, on his mother's death, he left office for mourning.

entries.zh: 服除，起故官，俄遷甘肅布政使。
entries.en: When mourning ended he returned to office and was soon made Treasurer of Gansu.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he returned to his former office and was soon promoted to Provincial Treasurer of Gansu.

entries.zh: 二十四年，調直隸，迴避，留本任。
entries.en: In year twenty-four he was transferred to Zhili but stayed in Gansu on account of the avoidance rule.
entries.literal: In year twenty-four, he was transferred to Zhili, but because of the avoidance rule he remained in his original post.

entries.zh: 擢湖北巡撫，慨然曰：「時艱至此，猶可拘成法不變耶？」
entries.en: He was made Governor of Hubei and said with feeling, "Times are this desperate; can we still cling to old rules and refuse to change?"
entries.literal: He was promoted to Governor of Hubei and said with feeling: "Times are this difficult; can we still be bound by fixed rules and not change?"

entries.zh: 於是假陝甘總督印上陳補官、掣籤、度支、訟獄四事，宜變通成例，厚植國本。
entries.en: He then used the Shaanxi-Gansu governor-general's seal to memorialize on filling offices, drawing lots for posts, revenue, and litigation, urging flexible change to strengthen the state.
entries.literal: He then used the Shaanxi-Gansu governor-general's seal to memorialize on four matters--filling offices, drawing lots for posts, revenue, and litigation--saying that precedents should be adapted to strengthen the foundations of the state.

entries.zh: 侍讀學士貽穀、光祿寺少卿張仲炘彈其亂政，詔褫職。
entries.en: Reader-in-waiting Yigu and Guanglu Temple Vice Minister Zhang Zhongxin impeached him for subverting government, and he was dismissed by edict.
entries.literal: Reader-in-waiting Yigu and Guanglu Temple Vice Minister Zhang Zhongxin impeached him for disordering government, and an edict stripped him of office.

entries.zh: 始，曾鉌官京朝，家綦貧，僦居陋室。
entries.en: When Zeng He first served in Beijing his family was very poor and he lived in rented quarters.
entries.literal: At first, when Zeng He served in capital offices, his family was extremely poor and rented a humble room.

entries.zh: 及任外台，孜孜民事，不顧問有無。
entries.en: Once he held office in the provinces, he devoted himself tirelessly to the people's affairs, heedless of his own comfort.
entries.literal: When he came to hold a provincial appointment, he worked diligently at the people's affairs, without regard to whether he himself had enough or not.

entries.zh: 既閒廢，出入皆徒步，民恆歲醵金濟之。
entries.en: After his dismissal he went everywhere on foot; the people of Shaanxi regularly collected money each year to support him.
entries.literal: After he was dismissed and idle, he went in and out everywhere on foot; the people of Shaanxi regularly pooled money each year to assist him.

entries.zh: 後益困，至敝衣鬻卜都市。
entries.en: His circumstances worsened until he wore threadbare clothes and sold divination in the city markets.
entries.literal: Later his straits grew worse, until he wore tattered clothes and sold divination in the capital markets.

entries.zh: 未幾，卒。
entries.en: Before long he died.
entries.literal: Before long, he died.

entries.zh: 宣統改元，總督端方為奏復原官。
entries.en: At the Xuantong change of reign era, Governor-General Duanfang memorialized to restore his former rank.
entries.literal: When Xuantong became the reign title, Governor-General Duanfang memorialized to restore his original office.

entries.zh: 楊深秀，字儀村，本名毓秀，山西聞喜人。
entries.en: Yang Shenxiu, whose courtesy name was Yicun and whose original name was Yuxiu, came from Wenxi in Shanxi.
entries.literal: Yang Shenxiu, courtesy name Yicun, originally named Yuxiu, was a native of Wenxi in Shanxi.

entries.zh: 少穎敏，諳中西算術。
entries.en: As a youth he was sharp and quick-witted, and thoroughly versed in Chinese and Western mathematics.
entries.literal: As a youth he was sharp and quick-witted and thoroughly versed in Chinese and Western mathematics.

entries.zh: 同治初，以舉人入貲為刑部員外郎。
entries.en: Early in the Tongzhi reign, as a provincial graduate he bought appointment as an assistant department director in the Ministry of Punishments.
entries.literal: Early in Tongzhi, as a provincial graduate he bought appointment as an assistant department director in the Ministry of Punishments.

entries.zh: 假歸，值晉大饑，閻敬銘銜命籌賑，深秀條上改革差徭法，困少蘇。
entries.en: While on leave he encountered the great famine in Shanxi; Yan Jingming, charged with organizing relief, received Shenxiu's detailed plan to reform corvée and labor levies, and the people's distress was somewhat relieved.
entries.literal: While on leave he returned home and encountered the great famine in Shanxi; Yan Jingming had been ordered to plan relief, and Shenxiu submitted a detailed plan to reform corvée and labor levies, so the people in distress somewhat revived.

entries.zh: 十五年，成進士，就本官遷郎中，轉御史。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year of Guangxu he took his jinshi degree, was promoted within his existing office to department director, and then transferred to censor.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year of Guangxu he passed the jinshi examination, was transferred in his original post to department director, and then to censor.

entries.zh: 嘗言：「時勢危迫，不革舊無以圖新，不變法無以圖存。」
entries.en: He once said, "The times are perilously urgent: without overturning the old there is no way to plan the new, and without changing the laws there is no way to plan for survival."
entries.literal: He once said: "The times are perilously urgent; without reforming the old there is no means to plan the new, and without changing the laws there is no means to plan survival."

entries.zh: 二十四年，俄人脅割旅順、大連灣。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year, Russia coerced China into ceding Lüshun and Dalian Bay.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, the Russians coerced the cession of Lüshun and Dalian Bay.

entries.zh: 深秀力請聯英、日拒之，詞甚切直。
entries.en: Shenxiu urgently petitioned that China ally with Britain and Japan to resist, in language that was forceful and blunt.
entries.literal: Shenxiu urgently petitioned to ally with Britain and Japan in resisting them, his language very forceful and direct.

entries.zh: 時朝廷銳意行新政，而大臣恆多異議。
entries.en: The court was then eager to enact new policies, but senior ministers constantly raised objections.
entries.literal: At the time the court was keen to carry out new policies, but senior ministers often had many objections.

entries.zh: 深秀乃與徐致靖先後疏請定國是，又以取士之法未善，請參酌宋、元、明舊制，釐正文體，下其議於禮部，尚書許應騤心非之，未奏也。
entries.en: Shenxiu and Xu Zhijing then submitted successive memorials asking that the national course be fixed; finding the method of selecting talent inadequate, Shenxiu urged that the old systems of Song, Yuan, and Ming be consulted, literary forms standardized, and the matter referred to the Ministry of Rites, but Minister Xu Yingkui privately disapproved and never forwarded the proposal.
entries.literal: Shenxiu and Xu Zhijing then submitted successive memorials requesting that the national course be fixed. He also found the method of selecting talent inadequate and asked that the old systems of Song, Yuan, and Ming be consulted, that literary forms be standardized, and that the matter be referred to the Ministry of Rites. Minister Xu Yingkui privately disapproved and did not memorialize.

entries.zh: 會議經濟特科務減額，於是深秀合宋伯魯彈其阻撓。
entries.en: When the economic special examination came up for discussion with efforts to cut its quota, Shenxiu joined Song Bolu in impeaching Xu Yingkui for obstruction.
entries.literal: When the economic special examination was discussed and efforts were made to reduce its quota, Shenxiu joined Song Bolu in impeaching him for obstruction.

entries.zh: 上令應騤自陳，奏上，劾康有為夤緣要津，請罷斥，詞連深秀，上不之詰也。
entries.en: The Emperor ordered Xu Yingkui to explain himself; in his reply Xu impeached Kang Youwei for currying favor at key posts and asked that he be dismissed, implicating Shenxiu in the wording, but the Emperor did not pursue Shenxiu.
entries.literal: The Emperor ordered Yingkui to explain himself. In the submitted memorial, he impeached Kang Youwei for currying favor at key posts and asked that he be dismissed; the wording implicated Shenxiu, but the Emperor did not pursue him.

entries.zh: 御史文悌劾深秀傳布有為所立保國會，並暴有為交通內外狀，德宗責以代人報復，反獲咎。
entries.en: Censor Wenti impeached Shenxiu for disseminating the Baoguo Society founded by Kang Youwei and exposed Youwei's dealings inside and outside the court; Emperor Dezong rebuked Wenti for retaliating on another's behalf, and Wenti himself was punished.
entries.literal: Censor Wenti impeached Shenxiu for disseminating the Baoguo Society founded by Youwei and also exposed Youwei's dealings inside and outside the court. Dezong rebuked him for retaliating on another's behalf, and he instead incurred blame.

entries.zh: 深秀益感奮，連上書請設譯書局，派王公遊歷各國，並定遊學日本章程，皆報可。
entries.en: Shenxiu was all the more stirred to action, and in a series of memorials asked that a Translation Bureau be established, that princes and nobles be sent to tour foreign countries, and that regulations for study in Japan be drawn up; all were approved.
entries.literal: Shenxiu was all the more stirred to action, and in successive memorials requested the establishment of a Translation Bureau, the dispatch of princes and dukes to tour the various countries, and the fixing of regulations for study in Japan; all were approved.

entries.zh: 又請試庶官，日番二十人，料簡貞實，而汰其庸愚罷老不諳時務者，繇是廷臣益側目。
entries.en: He also proposed testing ordinary officials twenty at a time each day, selecting the upright and sincere while weeding out the mediocre, foolish, and aged who did not understand current affairs; from this the court ministers looked upon him with growing hostility.
entries.literal: He also asked to test ordinary officials, twenty per day in rotation, to select the upright and sincere and eliminate the mediocre, foolish, worn out, and aged who did not understand current affairs; from this court ministers looked upon him with ever greater resentment.

entries.zh: 湖南巡撫陳寶箴圖治甚急，中蜚語，深秀為剖辨之，上以特旨褒寶箴，寶箴乃得行其志。
entries.en: Hunan Governor Chen Baozhen was pressing hard for reform when slander spread against him; Shenxiu defended him in a memorial, and the Emperor issued a special edict praising Baozhen, who was then able to carry out his plans.
entries.literal: Hunan Governor Chen Baozhen pressed urgently for reform but was struck by slanderous talk; Shenxiu analyzed and defended him, and the Emperor issued a special edict praising Baozhen, so Baozhen was able to carry out his plans.

entries.zh: 八月，政變，舉朝惴惴，懼大誅至，獨深秀抗疏請太后歸政。
entries.en: In the eighth month the coup occurred; the whole court trembled, fearing mass executions, yet Shenxiu alone submitted a bold memorial asking the Empress Dowager to restore power to the Emperor.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, the coup occurred; the whole court trembled, fearing a great purge would come, but Shenxiu alone submitted a forceful memorial asking the Empress Dowager to return government to the Emperor.

entries.zh: 方疏未上時，其子黻田苦口諫止，深秀厲聲叱之退。
entries.en: Before the memorial could be submitted, his son Futian pleaded desperately with him to desist; Shenxiu sharply rebuked him and ordered him away.
entries.literal: Before the memorial was submitted, his son Futian pleaded earnestly to stop him, but Shenxiu sharply rebuked him and sent him away.

entries.zh: 俄被逮，論棄市。
entries.en: Soon he was arrested and condemned to execution in the marketplace.
entries.literal: Soon he was arrested and sentenced to execution in the marketplace.

entries.zh: 深秀性鯁直，嘗面折人過，以此叢忌。
entries.en: Shenxiu was blunt and upright by nature, often rebuking others to their faces over their faults, and for this he accumulated many enemies.
entries.literal: Shenxiu was blunt and upright by nature and often corrected people's faults to their faces, thereby accumulating resentment.

entries.zh: 官臺諫十閱月，封事二十餘上，稿不具存，惟獄中詩三章流傳於世。
entries.en: In ten months on the censorate he submitted more than twenty sealed memorials; the drafts are not fully preserved—only three poems written in prison survive.
entries.literal: In ten months as a remonstrance official on the censorate, he submitted more than twenty sealed memorials; the drafts are not fully preserved—only three poems from prison circulate in the world.

entries.zh: 著有虛聲堂稿、聞喜縣新志。
entries.en: He authored Xushengtang gao and Wenxi xian xinzhi.
entries.literal: His works include Xushengtang gao and Wenxi xian xinzhi.

entries.zh: 楊銳，字叔嶠，四川綿竹人。
entries.en: Yang Rui, whose courtesy name was Shuqiao, came from Mianzhu in Sichuan.
entries.literal: Yang Rui, courtesy name Shuqiao, was a native of Mianzhu, Sichuan.

entries.zh: 少俊慧，督學張之洞奇其才，招入幕。
entries.en: As a youth he was brilliant and quick-witted; Educational Commissioner Zhang Zhidong was struck by his talent and brought him onto his staff.
entries.literal: In youth he was handsome and clever; Educational Commissioner Zhang Zhidong marveled at his talent and recruited him into his staff.

entries.zh: 肄業尊經書院，年最少，嘗冠其曹。
entries.en: He studied at the Zunjing Academy; though the youngest in his cohort, he often ranked first among his peers.
entries.literal: He studied at the Zunjing Academy; though the youngest in years, he often led his class.

entries.zh: 優貢朝考得知縣。
entries.en: Selected as an outstanding tribute student, he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed district magistrate.
entries.literal: As an outstanding tribute student he passed the metropolitan tribute examination and was appointed district magistrate.

entries.zh: 之洞督兩廣，從赴粵。
entries.en: When Zhidong became governor-general of the Two Guang, Yang Rui accompanied him to Guangdong.
entries.literal: When Zhidong became governor-general of the Two Guang, Yang Rui accompanied him to Guangdong.

entries.zh: 光緒十一年，舉順天鄉試，考取內閣中書。
entries.en: In Guangxu 11 he passed the Shuntian provincial examination and was selected as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
entries.literal: In Guangxu 11 he passed the Shuntian provincial examination and was selected as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

entries.zh: 二十四年，之洞薦應經濟特科。
entries.en: In Guangxu 24, Zhidong recommended him for the special economics examination.
entries.literal: In Guangxu 24, Zhidong recommended him for the special economics examination.

entries.zh: 又以陳寶箴薦，與劉光第、譚嗣同、林旭並加四品卿，充軍機章京，參新政。
entries.en: Again through Chen Baozhen’s recommendation, he, together with Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, and Lin Xu, was given fourth-rank ministerial title, appointed a Grand Council secretary, and took part in the new policies.
entries.literal: Again through Chen Baozhen’s recommendation, he, together with Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, and Lin Xu, was given fourth-rank ministerial title, appointed a Grand Council secretary, and took part in the new policies.

entries.zh: 召見，銳面陳興學、練兵為救亡策，稱旨。
entries.en: When summoned for audience, Rui stated directly that promoting education and drilling troops were strategies for saving the nation, and this pleased the throne.
entries.literal: When summoned for audience, Rui stated directly that promoting education and drilling troops were strategies for saving the nation, and this pleased the throne.

entries.zh: 七月，禮部主事王照上封事，尚書許應騤等格不奏。
entries.en: In the seventh month, Ministry of Rites secretary Wang Zhao submitted a sealed memorial, but Minister Xu Yingkui and others blocked it and did not present it.
entries.literal: In the seventh month, Ministry of Rites secretary Wang Zhao submitted a sealed memorial, but Minister Xu Yingkui and others blocked it and did not present it.

entries.zh: 上聞，震怒，盡褫尚書侍郎六人革職，朝臣皆不自安。
entries.en: When the Emperor learned of this he was furious and dismissed all six ministers and vice ministers; the court was thrown into unease.
entries.literal: When the Emperor learned of it, he was furious and stripped all six ministers and vice ministers of their posts; court officials were all ill at ease.

entries.zh: 上手詔密諭云：「近日朕仰觀聖母意旨，不欲退此老耄昏庸大臣而進英勇通達之人，亦不欲將法盡變。
entries.en: The Emperor personally sent Rui a secret hand-edict: "Of late I have observed the Empress Dowager's intent—she does not wish to remove these aged and incompetent ministers in favor of bold and capable men, nor does she wish to change the laws entirely.
entries.literal: The Emperor personally issued a secret hand-edict to Rui, saying: "Recently I have looked up to observe the Empress Dowager's intent: she does not wish to remove these aged, senile, and incompetent ministers and advance brave and penetrating men, nor does she wish to change the laws entirely.

entries.zh: 朕豈不知積弱不振，非力行新政不可？
entries.en: Do I not know that China has long been weak and enfeebled, and that only vigorous new policies can save it?
entries.literal: Do I not know that China has long been weak and failing, and that vigorous new policies are indispensable?

entries.zh: 然此時不惟朕權力所不及，若強行之，朕位且不能保。
entries.en: Yet at this moment my power does not reach that far; if I force the matter, I cannot even keep my throne.
entries.literal: Yet at this time not only is my power insufficient; if I force matters, I cannot even keep my throne.

entries.zh: 爾與劉光弟、譚嗣同、林旭等詳悉籌議，必如何而後能進用英達，使新政及時舉行，又不致少拂聖意，即具奏，候朕審擇，不勝焦慮之至！」
entries.en: You, together with Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Lin Xu, and the others, must deliberate carefully on how to advance able men so that the new policies may proceed in good time without the least offense to the Empress Dowager's wishes. Memorialize at once for my review. My anxiety is beyond words!"
entries.literal: You, together with Liu Guangdi, Tan Sitong, Lin Xu, and the others, must deliberate carefully on how able men can be advanced so the new policies may be carried out in time without even slightly offending Her Majesty's wishes; submit a memorial at once for my review. My anxiety is beyond measure!"

entries.zh: 銳復奏言：「太后親挈大位授之皇上，皇上宜以孝先天下，遇事將順。
entries.en: Rui memorialized in reply: "The Empress Dowager personally invested the throne in Your Majesty; Your Majesty should put filial piety before all else and accommodate her wishes in every matter.
entries.literal: Rui again memorialized: "The Empress Dowager personally took the great position and gave it to Your Majesty; Your Majesty should put filial piety before all under Heaven and accommodate her in every matter.

entries.zh: 變法宜有次第，進退大臣不宜太驟。」
entries.en: Reform should proceed step by step; the advancement and dismissal of ministers should not be too sudden."
entries.literal: Reform should proceed in due order; advancing and dismissing ministers should not be too abrupt.

entries.zh: 上是之。
entries.en: The Emperor approved.
entries.literal: The Emperor approved this.

entries.zh: 已而太后再訓政，諸言新政者皆予重誅。
entries.en: Before long the Empress Dowager resumed regency, and all who had advocated the new policies were severely punished.
entries.literal: Before long the Empress Dowager again assumed regency; all who spoke for the new policies were given severe punishment.

entries.zh: 銳既下獄，自揣實無罪，謂即訊不難白，次日，遽詔與光第等同棄市。
entries.en: Once imprisoned, Rui believed himself innocent and thought he could easily clear his name under interrogation, but the next day an edict suddenly ordered him executed in the marketplace together with Guangdi and the others.
entries.literal: Once Rui had been imprisoned, he judged himself truly innocent and thought that if interrogated he could easily make it clear. The next day, however, an edict suddenly ordered him executed in the marketplace together with Guangdi and the others.

entries.zh: 宣統改元，銳子慶昶繳手詔於都察院，請代奏，始傳於世。
entries.en: At the Xuantong change of reign era, Rui's son Qingchang submitted the hand-edict to the Censorate and asked that it be forwarded to the throne; only then did it become known to the world.
entries.literal: When Xuantong became the reign title, Rui's son Qingchang submitted the hand-edict to the Censorate and requested that it memorialize on his behalf; only then did it circulate in the world.

entries.zh: 劉光第，字裴村，四川富順人。
entries.en: Liu Guangdi, whose courtesy name was Peicun, came from Fushun in Sichuan.
entries.literal: Liu Guangdi, courtesy name Peicun, was a native of Fushun in Sichuan.

entries.zh: 光緒九年進士，授刑部主事。
entries.en: In Guangxu 9 he took his jinshi degree and was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
entries.literal: In Guangxu year nine he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed ministry secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.

entries.zh: 治事精嚴，因讞獄忤長官​​，遂退而閉戶勤學，絕跡不詣署。
entries.en: He handled business with exacting rigor; when a criminal case brought him into conflict with his superior, he withdrew, shut his doors to study, and stopped going to the office altogether.
entries.literal: In handling affairs he was meticulous and strict; because of a criminal case he offended his superior, whereupon he withdrew, closed his doors, and studied diligently, cutting off all visits to the yamen.

entries.zh: 家素貧，而性廉介，非舊交，雖禮饋弗受。
entries.en: His family had always been poor, but he was incorruptible by nature and would accept no courtesy gift from anyone who was not an old friend.
entries.literal: His family had long been poor, yet his nature was upright and incorruptible; unless they were old friends, he would not accept gifts even of courtesy.

entries.zh: 獨與楊銳善。
entries.en: Yang Rui alone numbered among his close friends.
entries.literal: He was on good terms with Yang Rui alone.

entries.zh: 通周官、禮及大小戴禮記。
entries.en: He was deeply versed in the Offices of Zhou, the Rites, and both recensions of the Record of Rites.
entries.literal: He was versed in the Offices of Zhou, the Rites, and the Record of Rites of the Elder and Younger Dai.

entries.zh: 其應召也，亦以陳寶箴薦，然非其素志，將具疏辭，川人官京朝者力勸之。
entries.en: He answered the summons on Chen Baozhen's recommendation too, though it was not what he had wanted; he was preparing a memorial to decline when Sichuan colleagues in the capital pressed him hard to accept.
entries.literal: When he answered the summons, it was also on Chen Baozhen's recommendation; yet this was not his original intent, and he was about to prepare a memorial declining, but Sichuan officials serving in the capital strongly urged him on.

entries.zh: 一日，召見，力陳時危民困，外患日迫，亟宜虛懷圖治，上稱善。
entries.en: One day he was received in audience and spoke urgently of national peril, popular distress, and the daily tightening of foreign pressure, urging the emperor to govern with an open mind; the emperor was pleased.
entries.literal: One day he was summoned for audience and forcefully stated that the times were perilous, the people distressed, and foreign danger pressing daily; the throne should urgently open its mind and plan good government—the emperor approved.

entries.zh: 惟時言路宏啟，臣民奏事日數百計，竟日批答，簽識可否，以待上裁。
entries.en: Memorial channels were then wide open, with hundreds of submissions arriving daily; Guangdi spent entire days drafting replies and marking what should stand or fall, all for the emperor's final ruling.
entries.literal: At that time the channels of remonstrance were broadly opened; memorials from officials and commoners numbered hundreds each day; Guangdi spent the whole day drafting responses, marking approval or rejection, awaiting the emperor's final decision.

entries.zh: 退語所親曰：「吾終不任此，行當亟假歸矣！」
entries.en: Afterward he told those close to him, “I cannot bear this responsibility to the end; I mean to ask leave and go home at once!”
entries.literal: Afterward he told those close to him, “I cannot bear this responsibility to the end; I mean to ask leave and go home at once!”

entries.zh: 未一月而禍作，光第自投獄。
entries.en: Less than a month later the disaster broke out, and Guangdi surrendered himself to prison.
entries.literal: Less than a month later disaster broke out, and Guangdi surrendered himself to prison.

entries.zh: 臨刑，協辦大學士剛毅監斬，光第詫曰：「未訊而誅，何哉？」
entries.en: At the execution, Associate Grand Secretary Gangyi supervised the beheading, and Guangdi cried out in astonishment, "To execute a man without trial--why?"
entries.literal: At the execution, Associate Grand Secretary Gangyi supervised the beheading, and Guangdi cried out in astonishment: "To execute a man without trial--why?"

entries.zh: 令跪聽旨，光第不可，曰：「祖制，雖盜賊，臨刑呼冤，當復訊。
entries.en: He was ordered to kneel and hear the edict; Guangdi refused, saying, "By ancestral law, even a thief who cries injustice at execution must be interrogated again.
entries.literal: He was ordered to kneel and hear the edict, but Guangdi refused, saying: "By ancestral law, even a thief who cries injustice at execution must be interrogated again.

entries.zh: 吾輩縱不足惜，如國體何！」
entries.en: Even if we are not worth sparing, what of the dignity of the state!”
entries.literal: Even if we are not worth sparing, what of the dignity of the state!”

entries.zh: 剛毅默不應，再詢之，曰：「吾奉命監刑耳，他何知？」
entries.en: Gangyi was silent and did not answer. When questioned again, he replied, "I am only here under orders to supervise the execution; what else would I know?"
entries.literal: Gangyi was silent and did not answer. When questioned again, he said: "I am only here under orders to supervise the execution; what else would I know?"

entries.zh: 獄卒強之跪，光第崛立自如。
entries.en: The jailers tried to force him to his knees, but Guangdi stood straight and unmoved.
entries.literal: The jailers tried to force him to kneel, but Guangdi stood upright and unmoved.

entries.zh: 楊銳呼曰：「裴村，跪！
entries.en: Yang Rui called out, "Peicun, kneel!
entries.literal: Yang Rui called out: "Peicun, kneel!

entries.zh: 跪！
entries.en: Kneel!
entries.literal: Kneel!

entries.zh: 遵旨而已。」
entries.en: It is only to obey the edict."
entries.literal: It is only to obey the edict."

entries.zh: 乃跪就戮。
entries.en: Then he knelt and went to his death.
entries.literal: Then he knelt and submitted to execution.

entries.zh: 著有介白堂詩文集。
entries.en: He wrote Jiebaitang shiwenji.
entries.literal: His writings include Jiebaitang shiwenji.

entries.zh: 譚嗣同，字復生，湖南瀏陽人。
entries.en: Tan Sitong, whose courtesy name was Fusheng, came from Liuyang in Hunan.
entries.literal: Tan Sitong, courtesy name Fusheng, was a native of Liuyang in Hunan.

entries.zh: 父繼洵，湖北巡撫。
entries.en: His father Tan Jixun was Governor of Hubei.
entries.literal: His father Jixun was Governor of Hubei.

entries.zh: 少倜儻有大志，文為奇肆。
entries.en: From youth he was spirited and ambitious, and his prose was bold and unrestrained.
entries.literal: From youth he was free-spirited and had great ambition; his writing was bold and unconventional.

entries.zh: 其學以日新為主，視倫常舊說若無足措意者。
entries.en: He took daily renewal as the heart of his learning and treated conventional morality and inherited doctrine as hardly worth notice.
entries.literal: His learning took daily renewal as its principle; he regarded conventional morality and old doctrines as scarcely worth a thought.

entries.zh: 繼洵素謹飭，以是頗見惡。
entries.en: Jixun was stern and proper by nature, and for this Sitong was much disliked by him.
entries.literal: Jixun was stern and proper by nature, and for this Sitong was much disliked by him.

entries.zh: 嗣同乃遊新疆劉錦棠幕，以同知入貲為知府，銓江蘇。
entries.en: Sitong then served on Liu Jintang’s staff in Xinjiang, purchased appointment as a prefect through the rank of subprefect, and was assigned to Jiangsu.
entries.literal: Sitong then served on Liu Jintang’s staff in Xinjiang, purchased appointment as a prefect through the rank of subprefect, and was assigned to Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 陳寶箴撫湖南，嗣同還鄉佐新政。
entries.en: When Chen Baozhen governed Hunan, Sitong returned home to assist the new policies.
entries.literal: When Chen Baozhen governed Hunan, Sitong returned home to assist the new policies.

entries.zh: 梁啟超倡辦南學會，嗣同為之長。
entries.en: Liang Qichao initiated the Southern Study Society, and Sitong served as its head.
entries.literal: Liang Qichao initiated the Southern Study Society, and Sitong served as its head.

entries.zh: 屆會期，集者恆數百人，聞嗣同慷慨論時事，多感動。
entries.en: At meeting times, several hundred people regularly gathered, and many were moved when they heard Sitong speak passionately about current affairs.
entries.literal: At meeting times, several hundred people regularly gathered, and many were moved when they heard Sitong speak passionately about current affairs.

entries.zh: 光緒二十四年，召入都，奏對稱旨，擢四品卿、軍機章京。
entries.en: In Guangxu 24 he was summoned to the capital; his audience replies pleased the throne, and he was promoted to fourth-rank ministerial title and Grand Council secretary.
