entries.literal: In Guangxu 24 he was summoned to the capital; his audience replies pleased the throne, and he was promoted to fourth-rank ministerial title and Grand Council secretary.

entries.zh: 四人雖同被命，每召對，嗣同建議獨多。
entries.en: Although the four men received the same appointment, at each audience Sitong alone offered especially many proposals.
entries.literal: Although the four men received the same appointment, at each audience Sitong alone offered especially many proposals.

entries.zh: 上欲開懋勤殿，設顧問官，令嗣同擬旨，必載明前朝故事，將親詣頤和園請命太后。
entries.en: The emperor wished to open Maoqin Hall and establish advisory officials; he ordered Sitong to draft the edict, requiring it to set out former-dynasty precedents clearly, and planned personally to go to the Summer Palace to request the empress dowager’s approval.
entries.literal: The emperor wished to open Maoqin Hall and establish advisory officials; he ordered Sitong to draft the edict, requiring it to set out former-dynasty precedents clearly, and planned personally to go to the Summer Palace to request the empress dowager’s approval.

entries.zh: 嗣同退謂人曰：「今乃知上絕無權也！」
entries.en: Sitong withdrew and told others, “Now I know the emperor has absolutely no power!”
entries.literal: Sitong withdrew and told others, “Now I know the emperor has absolutely no power!”

entries.zh: 時榮祿督畿輔，袁世凱以監司練兵天津。
entries.en: At the time Ronglu governed the metropolitan region, and Yuan Shikai, as a surveillance commissioner, trained troops at Tianjin.
entries.literal: At the time Ronglu governed the metropolitan region, and Yuan Shikai, as a surveillance commissioner, trained troops at Tianjin.

entries.zh: 詔擢世凱侍郎，召入覲。
entries.en: An edict promoted Shikai to vice minister and summoned him for audience.
entries.literal: An edict promoted Shikai to vice minister and summoned him for audience.

entries.zh: 嗣同嘗夜詣世凱有所議。
entries.en: Sitong once went at night to Shikai to discuss something.
entries.literal: Sitong once went at night to Shikai to discuss something.

entries.zh: 明日，世凱返天津。
entries.en: The next day Shikai returned to Tianjin.
entries.literal: The next day Shikai returned to Tianjin.

entries.zh: 越晨，太后自頤和園還宮，收政權。
entries.en: The following morning, the empress dowager returned from the Summer Palace to the palace and took back political power.
entries.literal: The following morning, the empress dowager returned from the Summer Palace to the palace and took back political power.

entries.zh: 啟超避匿日本使館，嗣同往見之，勸嗣同東遊。
entries.en: Qichao took refuge in the Japanese legation. Sitong went to see him, and Qichao urged Sitong to travel east.
entries.literal: Qichao took refuge in the Japanese legation. Sitong went to see him, and Qichao urged Sitong to travel east.

entries.zh: 嗣同曰：「不有行者，無以圖將來；
entries.en: Sitong said, “Without someone who goes on living, there is no way to plan for the future;
entries.literal: Sitong said, “Without someone who goes on living, there is no way to plan for the future;

entries.zh: 不有死者，無以酬聖主。」
entries.en: without someone who dies, there is no way to repay a devoted sovereign."
entries.literal: without one who dies, there is no way to repay the sagely sovereign."

entries.zh: 卒不去。
entries.en: In the end he refused to go.
entries.literal: In the end he did not leave.

entries.zh: 未幾，斬於市。
entries.en: Before long he was executed in the marketplace.
entries.literal: Before long he was beheaded in the marketplace.

entries.zh: 著有仁學及莽蒼蒼齋詩集等。
entries.en: He wrote Renxue and Mangcangcangzhai shiji, among other works.
entries.literal: He wrote Renxue and Mangcangcangzhai shiji, among other works.

entries.zh: 唐才常，字佛塵。
entries.en: Tang Caichang, courtesy name Fochen.
entries.literal: Tang Caichang, courtesy name Fochen.

entries.zh: 少與嗣同齊名，稱「瀏陽二生」，兩湖學堂高材生也。
entries.en: From youth he was equally famous with Sitong, and they were called “the Two Students of Liuyang”; he was an outstanding student of the Lianghu Academy.
entries.literal: From youth he was equally famous with Sitong, and they were called “the Two Students of Liuyang”; he was an outstanding student of the Lianghu Academy.

entries.zh: 聞嗣同死，憂憤，屢有所謀，每言及德宗，常泣下。
entries.en: Hearing of Sitong’s death, he was grieved and indignant and repeatedly made plans; whenever he spoke of Emperor Dezong, he would often weep.
entries.literal: Hearing of Sitong’s death, he was grieved and indignant and repeatedly made plans; whenever he spoke of Emperor Dezong, he would often weep.

entries.zh: 二十六年，兩宮出狩，才常陰結富有會謀舉事，號勤王，將攻武、漢。
entries.en: In Guangxu 26, when the two palaces went out on progress, Caichang secretly organized the Fuyou Society and planned to rise, calling it loyal rescue of the throne, intending to attack Wuchang and Hankou.
entries.literal: In Guangxu 26, when the two palaces went out on progress, Caichang secretly organized the Fuyou Society and planned to rise, calling it loyal rescue of the throne, intending to attack Wuchang and Hankou.

entries.zh: 被獲，慷慨言無所隱，請就死，遂殺之。
entries.en: Captured, he spoke without concealment and asked only to die; he was killed.
entries.literal: He was captured; speaking boldly he concealed nothing, asked to die, and was executed.

entries.zh: 林旭，字暾谷，福建侯官人。
entries.en: Lin Xu, whose courtesy name was Tangu, came from Houguan in Fujian.
entries.literal: Lin Xu, courtesy name Tangu, was a native of Houguan in Fujian.

entries.zh: 年十九，舉本省鄉試第一。
entries.en: At nineteen he topped the provincial examinations in Fujian.
entries.literal: At nineteen he placed first in the provincial examination of his province.

entries.zh: 後試禮部，值構釁，糾同試者上書論時事，不報。
entries.en: He later took the metropolitan examination; when war broke out with Japan, he joined fellow candidates in a memorial on public affairs, but the court did not reply.
entries.literal: Later he sat for the Ministry of Rites examination; when the Sino-Japanese conflict broke out, he joined fellow candidates in memorializing on current affairs, but received no response.

entries.zh: 入貲為內閣中書。
entries.en: He bought appointment as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
entries.literal: He purchased appointment as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

entries.zh: 時康有為倡言變法，先於京師立粵學會，以振厲士氣，而蜀學、浙學、陝學、閩學諸會繼之。
entries.en: When Kang Youwei began calling for reform, he first founded the Guangdong Study Society in the capital to stir scholarly morale; the Sichuan, Zhejiang, Shaanxi, and Fujian societies followed.
entries.literal: At that time Kang Youwei advocated reform; he first established the Guangdong Study Society in the capital to rouse scholarly morale, and the Sichuan, Zhejiang, Shaanxi, and Fujian study societies followed.

entries.zh: 旭為閩學會領袖，又充保國會會員。
entries.en: Xu led the Fujian Study Society and also joined the Baoguo Society.
entries.literal: Xu was leader of the Fujian Study Society and also served as a member of the Society for the Preservation of the Nation.

entries.zh: 榮祿先為福州將軍，雅好閩士，及至天津，延旭入幕。
entries.en: Ronglu, formerly General of Fuzhou, had long favored Fujian scholars; when he went to Tianjin he brought Xu onto his staff.
entries.literal: Ronglu had earlier been General of Fuzhou and had long favored Fujian scholars; when he reached Tianjin he took Xu into his staff.

entries.zh: 俄以奏保人才召見，操土語，上不盡解。
entries.en: Soon he was summoned on memorial recommendation; he spoke in his local dialect and the emperor could not fully follow him.
entries.literal: Soon, on memorial recommendation as talent, Xu was summoned for audience; he spoke in his local dialect and the emperor did not fully understand.

entries.zh: 退繕摺，上稱善，遂命與譚嗣同等同參機務，詔諭多旭起草。
entries.en: He then revised his memorial, which the Emperor praised, and was ordered to join Tan Sitong and the others in confidential duties; many edicts were drafted by Xu.
entries.literal: He withdrew and drafted a memorial; the Emperor praised it, then ordered him to join Tan Sitong and the others in participating in confidential affairs, and many edicts were drafted by Xu.

entries.zh: 及變起，同戮於市，年二十有四。
entries.en: When the coup came he was executed in the marketplace with the others, aged twenty-four.
entries.literal: When the coup broke out he was executed in the marketplace together with the others, at the age of twenty-four.

entries.zh: 著有晚翠軒詩集。
entries.en: He wrote Wancuixuan shiji.
entries.literal: His writings include Wancuixuan shiji.

entries.zh: 妻沈葆楨孫女，聞變，仰藥不死，以毀卒。
entries.en: His wife was Shen Baozhen's granddaughter; on hearing the news she took poison but survived, and died of grief.
entries.literal: His wife was a granddaughter of Shen Baozhen; when she heard of the disaster she took poison but did not die, and died of grief.

entries.zh: 康廣仁，名有溥，以字行，有為弟。
entries.en: Kang Guangren, whose personal name was Youpu and who went by his courtesy name, was Kang Youwei's younger brother.
entries.literal: Kang Guangren, personal name Youpu, styled by his courtesy name, was Kang Youwei's younger brother.

entries.zh: 少從兄學。
entries.en: From youth he studied under his brother.
entries.literal: From youth he studied under his elder brother.

entries.zh: 有為上書請改革，廣仁謂當先變科舉，庶人才可出。
entries.en: When Youwei memorialized for reform, Guangren urged that the examinations be changed first so talent could emerge.
entries.literal: When Youwei memorialized requesting reform, Guangren said that the examinations should be changed first, so that talent might emerge.

entries.zh: 其後罷鄉會試、製藝，而歲科試未變，廣仁激勵言官抗疏論之，得旨俞允。
entries.en: After the provincial and metropolitan examinations and the eight-legged essay were abolished, the annual local tests remained unchanged; Guangren pressed censors to memorialize boldly, and the Emperor approved.
entries.literal: After the provincial and metropolitan examinations and the eight-legged essay were abolished, the annual and triennial examinations had not yet changed. Guangren stirred the censors to submit forceful memorials on the matter, and obtained an approving edict.

entries.zh: 於是廣仁語有為：「今科舉既廢，宜且南歸興學專教育，俟養成多數有用才，數年後乃可云改革也。」
entries.en: Guangren then told Youwei, "With the examinations gone, you should go south and devote yourself to education, train many useful men, and only after several years speak of reform again."
entries.literal: Guangren then told Youwei: "Now that the examinations have been abolished, you should for the moment return south, promote schools, and devote yourself to education. Wait until a large number of useful talents have been trained; only after several years can reform be spoken of."

entries.zh: 有為不忍去。
entries.en: Youwei could not bring himself to leave.
entries.literal: Youwei could not bear to leave.

entries.zh: 及初聞變，廣仁復趣有為歸。
entries.en: When news of the coup first came, Guangren again urged Youwei to flee.
entries.literal: When he first heard of the coup, Guangren again urged Youwei to leave.

entries.zh: 有為走，廣仁被逮。
entries.en: Youwei escaped; Guangren was arrested.
entries.literal: Youwei fled, and Guangren was arrested.

entries.zh: 在獄言笑自若，臨刑猶言曰：「中國自強之機在此矣！」
entries.en: In prison he was calm and even cheerful; at the block he still said, "China's chance to strengthen itself lies in this!"
entries.literal: In prison he talked and laughed as usual; at his execution he still said: "China's opportunity to strengthen itself lies here!"

entries.zh: 論曰：戊戌變法，德宗發憤圖強，用端棻等言，召用新進。
entries.en: The commentator says: In the Wuxu reforms Emperor Dezong, determined to strengthen the state, took the advice of Li Duanfen and others and called in new men.
entries.literal: The commentary says: In the Wuxu reforms, Dezong roused himself to pursue strength, adopted the words of Duanfen and the others, and summoned new men for employment.

entries.zh: 百日維新，中外震仰，黨爭遽起，激成政變。
entries.en: For a hundred days the reforms awed China and the world, but factional struggle erupted and provoked the coup.
entries.literal: For a hundred days the reforms made China and foreign countries tremble and look up in admiration, but factional struggle suddenly arose and provoked the coup.

entries.zh: 銳、光第、嗣同、旭及深秀、廣仁同日被禍，世稱「六君子」，皆悲其志。
entries.en: Rui, Guangdi, Sitong, Xu, Shenxiu, and Guangren were executed on the same day; the world called them the "Six Gentlemen," and all mourned their purpose.
entries.literal: Rui, Guangdi, Sitong, Xu, Shenxiu, and Guangren suffered disaster on the same day; the world called them the "Six Gentlemen," and all mourned their purpose.

entries.zh: 內爭不已，牽及外交。
entries.en: Internal strife continued and entangled foreign relations.
entries.literal: Internal strife did not cease, and foreign relations were drawn into it.

entries.zh: 其後遂釀庚子排外之亂，終致危亡。
entries.en: This led to the Boxer uprising of 1900 and, in the end, ruin.
entries.literal: Thereafter the Boxer uprising of 1900 was brewed, and in the end the dynasty was brought to ruin.

entries.zh: 此亦代興衰一大關鍵也。
entries.en: This was a great turning point in the fate of the Qing dynasty.
entries.literal: This too was a great turning point in the rise and fall of the Qing.

entries.zh: 徐桐 剛毅 趙舒翹 啟秀 英年 裕祿 毓賢。
entries.en: Xu Tong; Gang Yi; Zhao Shuqiao; Qi Xiu; Ying Nian; Yu Lu; Yu Xian.
entries.literal: Xu Tong, Gang Yi, Zhao Shuqiao, Qi Xiu, Ying Nian, Yu Lu, Yu Xian.

entries.zh: 徐桐，字蔭軒，漢軍正藍旗人，尚書澤醇子。
entries.en: Xu Tong, whose style was Yinxuan, came from the Plain Blue Banner of the Han Chinese Banners; his father was Minister Ze Chun.
entries.literal: Xu Tong, styled Yinxuan, was a man of the Plain Blue Banner of the Han Chinese Banners and son of Minister Ze Chun.

entries.zh: 道光三十年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
entries.en: In 1850 he took his jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
entries.literal: In the thirtieth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin, and appointed compiler.

entries.zh: 坐修改中卷干磨勘，罷職。
entries.en: He was dismissed after altering an examination middle scroll and being caught in a review.
entries.literal: Because he altered the middle scroll in an examination and was caught in a review, he was dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 咸豐十年，特賞檢討，協修文宗實錄。
entries.en: In 1860 he was specially made a reviser and helped compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Wenzong.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng he was specially granted the post of reviser and helped compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Wenzong.

entries.zh: 同治初，命在上書房行走，奉懿旨番講治平寶鑑，入直弘德殿，累遷侍講學士。
entries.en: Early in the Tongzhi reign he served in the Upper Study Halls, lectured on the Mirror of Governance and Tranquility by empress-dowager order, entered duty at Hongde Hall, and rose to expositor of the Hanlin Academy.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi he was ordered to serve in the Upper Study Halls, received an empress-dowager edict to lecture on the Mirror of Governance and Tranquility, entered duty at Hongde Hall, and was promoted step by step to expositor of the Hanlin Academy.

entries.zh: 先後疏請習政事、勤修省，成大學衍義體要以進。
entries.en: He repeatedly urged study of government and diligent self-examination, and presented his Essentials of the Great Learning in Outline.
entries.literal: He repeatedly memorialized to study state affairs and practice diligent self-examination, and completed the Essentials of the Great Learning in Outline to present.

entries.zh: 數擢至禮部侍郎。
entries.en: He was promoted several times to Vice Minister of Rites.
entries.literal: He was promoted several times to Vice Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 念外人麕集京師，和議難恃，宜壹意修攘圖自強；
entries.en: Seeing foreigners massed in the capital and treaties unreliable, he argued the court should focus on defense and self-strengthening;
entries.literal: Reflecting that foreigners thronged the capital and peace negotiations could not be relied on, he held that one should concentrate on strengthening defenses and plotting self-strengthening;

entries.zh: 因條上簡才能、結民心、裕度支、修邊備四策。
entries.en: he proposed four policies: appointing capable men, winning popular support, strengthening finances, and repairing frontier defenses.
entries.literal: he therefore itemized four policies: selecting talent, binding popular hearts, expanding revenue, and repairing frontier defenses.

entries.zh: 光緒初，授禮部尚書，加太子少保。
entries.en: Early in the Guangxu reign he became Minister of Rites with the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu he was appointed Minister of Rites and given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 主事吳可讀請豫定大統，以屍諫，桐與翁同龢等謂其未悉本朝家法：「當申明列聖不建儲彝訓，俾知他日紹膺大寶之元良，即為承繼穆宗之聖子。
entries.en: When Principal Clerk Wu Kedu petitioned to settle the succession in advance and died remonstrating, Xu Tong and Weng Tonghe argued he misunderstood dynastic law: "The ancestral rule against naming an heir in advance should be reaffirmed, so all would know the heir who one day receives the throne is the son who succeeds Emperor Muzong.
entries.literal: Principal Clerk Wu Kedu requested that the succession be settled in advance and remonstrated with his corpse; Xu Tong and Weng Tonghe and others said he did not understand the house law of the dynasty: "The instruction of successive sages not to establish an heir in advance ought to be declared, so that people may know the heir apparent who will one day receive the great treasure is the sage son who will succeed Emperor Muzong.

entries.zh: 揆諸前諭則合，準諸家法則符。」
entries.en: That accords with prior edicts and with house law."
entries.literal: Measured against earlier edicts it accords; judged by house law it conforms."

entries.zh: 疏入，詔存毓慶宮備覽。
entries.en: The memorial was filed and the throne ordered it kept in the Palace of Accumulated Celebration for reference.
entries.literal: When the memorial entered, an edict ordered it kept in the Palace of Accumulated Celebration for reference.

entries.zh: 曰運貨迳至漢口；
entries.en: allowing cargo to pass through to Hankou;
entries.literal: namely, transporting goods straight through to Hankou;

entries.zh: 曰行船直入伯都訥。
entries.en: and permitting vessels to navigate directly to Berdunier.
entries.literal: namely, permitting ships to sail directly into Berdunier.

entries.zh: 六年，廷議徇俄人請，將赦崇厚罪，桐力持不可，謂：「揆度機要在樞廷，折衝俎豆在總署，講信修睦在使臣。
entries.en: In 1880, when the court debated yielding to Russian pressure and pardoning Chonghou, Xu Tong stood firm against it, arguing: "Strategic judgment rests with the Grand Council; negotiation at the council table rests with the Zongli Yamen; building trust and good relations rests with the envoys.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, when the court considered acceding to the Russians' request and were about to pardon Chonghou's crime, [Xu] Tong firmly insisted it could not be done, saying: "Weighing strategy belongs in the Grand Council; parrying at the council table belongs in the Zongli Yamen; cultivating trust and harmony belongs to the envoys.

entries.zh: 赦之而彼就範，猶裨國事；
entries.en: If a pardon brings them to terms, it may still serve the state;
entries.literal: If one pardons him and the other side then submits, it may still benefit state affairs;

entries.zh: 若釁端仍不能弭，反失刑政大權。
entries.en: but if hostilities cannot be settled, we forfeit the crown's authority over punishment and law.
entries.literal: but if trouble cannot still be quelled, one instead loses the great authority of penal administration.

entries.zh: 推原禍始，宜肅國憲。」
entries.en: The root of the disaster should be traced to strict enforcement of national law."
entries.literal: Tracing the origin of the calamity, the state constitution ought to be upheld."

entries.zh: 又言：「今日用人之道，秉忠持正者為上，宅心樸實者次之。
entries.en: He added: "In appointing officials today, men who are loyal and upright should come first; men of plain and honest character should come next.
entries.literal: He also said: "The way to employ men today: those who uphold loyalty and rectitude rank first; those whose hearts are plain and honest rank next.

entries.zh: 若以機權靈警，諳曉各國語言文字，遽目為通才，而責以鉅任，未有不僨且蹶者！」
entries.en: To treat men merely because they are quick-witted and fluent in foreign tongues and scripts as universal talents fit for weighty office is to invite certain ruin."
entries.literal: If one suddenly regards men who are sharp in maneuver, clever and alert, and versed in the languages and scripts of the various nations as versatile talents and charges them with great responsibilities, there has never been a case where they did not collapse in failure!"

entries.zh: 不報。
entries.en: His advice went unheeded.
entries.literal: There was no response.

entries.zh: 歷充翰林院掌院學士、上書房總師傅。
entries.en: He rose to be chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and grand tutor in the Upper Study Halls.
entries.literal: He successively served as Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and Grand Tutor of the Upper Study Halls.

entries.zh: 十五年，以吏部尚書協辦大學士，晉太子太保。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year (1889) he was appointed Minister of Personnel with concurrent duty as assistant grand secretary, then promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year, as Minister of Personnel he served as Assistant Grand Secretary, and was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 二十二年，拜體仁閣大學士。
entries.en: In the twenty-second year (1896) he was made grand secretary of the Hall of Embodied Benevolence.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Embodied Benevolence.

entries.zh: 桐崇宋儒說，守舊，惡西學如仇。
entries.en: Xu Tong revered Song Neo-Confucianism, clung to the old ways, and hated Western learning like a mortal foe.
entries.literal: Xu Tong revered Song Neo-Confucian doctrine, clung to the old ways, and hated Western learning as he would an enemy.

entries.zh: 門人言新政者，屏不令入謁。
entries.en: He barred disciples who advocated reform from his audience.
entries.literal: Disciples who spoke of new policies he barred and would not receive in audience.

entries.zh: 二十四年政變後，太后以其耆臣碩望，頗優禮，朝請令近侍扶掖以寵之。
entries.en: After the 1898 coup the Empress Dowager favored this venerable statesman, ordering attendants to support him at court.
entries.literal: After the coup of the twenty-fourth year the Empress Dowager, because he was an aged minister of great reputation, treated him with especial favor and ordered attendants to support him at court as a mark of grace.

entries.zh: 有豫師者，字錫之，內務府漢軍。
entries.en: Yu Shi, whose style was Xizhi, served in the Imperial Household Department as a member of the Han Chinese Banner.
entries.literal: There was Yu Shi, styled Xizhi, of the Han Chinese Banner in the Imperial Household Department.

entries.zh: 進士。
entries.en: He held the jinshi degree.
entries.literal: A jinshi degree holder.

entries.zh: 官至烏魯木齊都統，以講學為桐所傾服。
entries.en: He eventually became commander-in-chief at Urumqi, and Xu Tong looked up to him as a scholar.
entries.literal: He rose to commandant-general at Urumqi; Xu Tong admired him for his scholarship.

entries.zh: 方太后議廢帝，立端王載漪子溥儁為「大阿哥」，桐主之甚力，實皆豫師本謀也。
entries.en: During the debate over deposing the emperor and elevating Prince Duan's son Pujun as "Great Heir Apparent," Xu Tong pushed hard for it—the scheme was Yu Shi's in essence.
entries.literal: When the Empress Dowager debated deposing the emperor and installing Prince Duan's son Pujun as "Great Heir Apparent," Xu Tong strongly advocated it; in truth all these plots originated with Yu Shi.

entries.zh: 既而桐被命照料，益親載漪。
entries.en: Once Xu Tong was charged with supervising the boy, he grew even closer to Prince Duan.
entries.literal: When Xu Tong was thereafter ordered to oversee [the heir], he became still closer to Prince Duan.

entries.zh: 各國不慊載漪等所為，漪恚甚，圖報復。
entries.en: The foreign powers were displeased with what Prince Duan and his circle had done; furious, he sought revenge.
entries.literal: The foreign powers were displeased with what Prince Duan and his circle had done; furious, he sought revenge.

entries.zh: 二十六年，義和拳起釁仇外，載漪大喜，導之入都。
entries.en: In 1900, when the Boxers stirred up hatred of foreigners, Prince Duan was delighted and ushered them into Beijing.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when the Boxers rose and turned hostility outward, [Prince Duan] was greatly pleased and guided them into the capital.

entries.zh: 桐謂：「中國當自此強矣！」
entries.en: Xu Tong declared: "From this day China will grow strong!"
entries.literal: Xu Tong said: "China shall henceforth be strong!"

entries.zh: 至且親迓之。
entries.en: He even went out in person to welcome them.
entries.literal: He would even go out in person to welcome them.

entries.zh: 然及其亂時，仍被劫掠。
entries.en: Yet when the chaos broke out, he was looted like everyone else.
entries.literal: Yet during the disorder he was still plundered.

entries.zh: 袁昶、許景澄之死，舉國稱冤，而桐則曰：「是死且有餘辜！」
entries.en: When Yuan Chang and Xu Jingcheng were executed, the nation called it a miscarriage of justice; Xu Tong said: "They deserved worse than death!"
entries.literal: At the deaths of Yuan Chang and Xu Jingcheng the whole country called it injustice, but Xu Tong said: "Even in death they still had guilt to spare!"

entries.zh: 時其子監刑，揚揚頗自得。
entries.en: His son Chengyu oversaw the executions, swaggering with evident satisfaction.
entries.literal: At the time his son Chengyu supervised the execution, looking quite pleased with himself.

entries.zh: 啟秀端謹有風操，為徐桐所賞。
entries.en: Qi Xiu was upright and principled, and Xu Tong held him in high regard.
entries.literal: Qi Xiu was upright, careful, and possessed moral integrity; Xu Tong admired him.

entries.zh: 自政變後，桐最被盻遇，欲引參機務，乃舉啟秀自代。
entries.en: After the 1898 coup Xu Tong was the Empress Dowager's favorite; wanting a proxy in policy, he recommended Qi Xiu to take his place.
entries.literal: After the political coup Xu Tong was most favored; wishing to draw him into state affairs, he recommended Qi Xiu to replace himself.

entries.zh: 已而拳亂作，董福祥攻使館不下，啟秀薦五台僧禦敵，頗附和之。
entries.en: When the Boxer rising erupted and Dong Fuxiang failed to overrun the legations, Qi Xiu recommended a Wutai monk to fight the foreigners and lent his support.
entries.literal: Soon the Boxer disturbance broke out; Dong Fuxiang could not take the legations; Qi Xiu recommended a monk of Wutai to repel the enemy and largely went along with the plan.

entries.zh: 逮兩宮狩西安，啟秀以母病弗克從。
entries.en: When the court fled to Xi'an, Qi Xiu stayed behind because his mother was ill.
entries.literal: When the two palaces went on tour to Xi'an, Qi Xiu could not follow because his mother was ill.

entries.zh: 日本軍拘啟秀及徐承煜嚴守之，承煜，桐子也。
entries.en: Japanese troops seized Qi Xiu and Xu Chengyu and held them under close guard; Chengyu was Xu Tong's son.
entries.literal: The Japanese army detained Qi Xiu and Xu Chengyu and kept them under strict guard; Chengyu was Xu Tong's son.

entries.zh: 朝旨褫職，而各國猶言罪魁不可縱。
entries.en: The court stripped them of rank, but the powers insisted the chief culprits must not go unpunished.
entries.literal: An imperial order stripped them of office, yet the various nations still said the chief culprits could not be spared.

entries.zh: 明年，正法命下，日軍官置酒為餞，席次，傳詔旨，啟秀神色自若，曰：​​「即此已邀聖恩矣！」
entries.en: The following year the execution order came down. A Japanese officer gave him a farewell feast; when the edict was read, Qi Xiu remained composed and said: "Even this is already imperial favor!"
entries.literal: The next year the order for lawful execution was issued; a Japanese officer set out wine as a farewell; at the banquet, when the edict was announced, Qi Xiu's expression was calm as he said: "Even this already invites imperial grace!"

entries.zh: 肅衣冠赴菜市。
entries.en: He dressed in full court robes and walked to the execution ground at Caishikou.
entries.literal: He put on formal dress and hat and went to the Vegetable Market.

entries.zh: 啟秀宅近日本權領地，日官與語，當善芘其家，第曰：「厚意可感。」
entries.en: His home lay near the Japanese concession; a Japanese official promised to protect his family. Qi Xiu replied only: "Your kindness moves me."
entries.literal: Qi Xiu's residence was near the Japanese concession; a Japanese official spoke with him, saying his family would be well protected; he only said: "Your generous intent is deeply felt."

entries.zh: 他無復言，遂就戮。
entries.en: He said nothing more and went to his death.
entries.literal: He said nothing more and then submitted to execution.

entries.zh: 承煜，字楠士。
entries.en: Chengyu, whose style was Nanshi.
entries.literal: Chengyu, styled Nanshi.

entries.zh: 拔貢。
entries.en: He had entered by senior licentiate recommendation.
entries.literal: A senior licentiate by recommendation.

entries.zh: 以戶部小京官晉遷郎中，累官刑部左侍郎。
entries.en: He rose from a junior post in the Ministry of Revenue to director and eventually Left Vice Minister of Justice.
entries.literal: Starting as a junior secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, he was promoted step by step to director, and eventually rose to Left Vice Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 已，聯軍入，桐倉皇失措，承煜請曰：「父芘拳匪，外人至，必不免，失大臣體。
entries.en: When the allied armies entered Beijing, Xu Tong panicked. Chengyu urged him: "Father sheltered the Boxers; when the foreigners arrive you cannot escape without disgracing your rank.
entries.literal: Before long the allied armies entered; Xu Tong was flustered and at a loss, and Chengyu urged: "Father sheltered the Boxer bandits; when foreigners arrive you cannot escape and will lose the dignity of a great minister.

entries.zh: 盍殉國？
entries.en: Why not die for the state?
entries.literal: Why not die for the state?

entries.zh: 兒當從侍地下耳！」
entries.en: Your son will follow you to the grave!"
entries.literal: Your son will follow and attend you in the grave!"

entries.zh: 桐乃投繯死，年八十有二矣。
entries.en: Xu Tong hanged himself at the age of eighty-two.
entries.literal: Xu Tong then hanged himself; he was eighty-two.

entries.zh: 而承煜遂亡走，為日軍所拘，置之順天府尹署，與啟秀俱明年正月正法。
entries.en: Chengyu fled but was seized by Japanese troops and held at the Shuntian prefect's yamen; he and Qi Xiu were executed the following first month.
entries.literal: Chengyu then fled, was seized by the Japanese army, and was placed in the yamen of the prefect of Shuntian; he and Qi Xiu were both executed by lawful punishment in the first month of the following year.

entries.zh: 命下，日軍官置酒為餞，傳詔旨，承煜色變，口呼冤，痛詆西人不已。
entries.en: When the order came, a Japanese officer offered wine and read the edict; Chengyu turned pale, cried injustice, and bitterly denounced the Westerners.
entries.literal: When the order came down, a Japanese officer set out wine to send him off and transmitted the edict; Chengyu changed color, cried out his innocence, and bitterly denounced Westerners without cease.

entries.zh: 翼日，備輿送至菜市，監刑官出席禮之，已昏不知人矣，尋就戮。
entries.en: The next day he was taken to Caishikou; the execution officer saluted him, but he was already unconscious when he was killed.
entries.literal: The next day a carriage was prepared to send him to Caishikou; the supervising execution officer came out to salute him, but he was already unconscious; soon he was put to death.

entries.zh: 和議成，褫桐職，奪卹典，旋論棄市，以先死議免。
entries.en: After peace was made Xu Tong's offices and mourning honors were revoked; public execution was debated but waived because he had already died.
entries.literal: When peace was concluded Xu Tong's offices were stripped and mourning honors revoked; soon decapitation and public display were debated, but because he had died first the sentence was waived.

entries.zh: 時擅訂約，下群臣議，乃條摘其不可行者：曰、各城定界；
entries.en: When Chonghou took it upon himself to negotiate the Russian treaty, the matter was laid before the full court. Xu Tong listed the terms that could not be accepted: delimiting the cities of Ili and Tarbagatai;
entries.literal: At that time Chonghou had arbitrarily concluded a treaty with Russia; when it was referred to the court for discussion among all officials, [Xu Tong] itemized what could not be accepted: namely, fixing boundaries for the cities of Ili and Tarbagatai;

entries.zh: 曰新疆、蒙古通商；
entries.en: opening trade in Xinjiang and Mongolia;
entries.literal: namely, opening trade in Xinjiang and Mongolia;

entries.zh: 論曰：戊戌政變後，廢立議起，患外人為梗，遂欲仇之，而庚子拳匪之亂乘機作矣。
entries.en: The historian comments: After the coup of 1898, the struggle over deposing the emperor revived; seeing foreigners as the obstacle, the court turned toward hostility, and the Boxer rising of 1900 erupted in that moment.
entries.literal: The commentator says: After the coup of 1898, debate over deposing the emperor and installing an heir arose; fearing foreigners as an obstruction, they wished to make them enemies, and the Boxer disturbance of 1900 seized the opportunity to break out.

entries.zh: 太后信其術，思倚以鋤敵而立威。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager believed in their magic and hoped to lean on them to destroy enemies and assert her power.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager believed their arts and thought to rely on them to cut down enemies and establish authority.

entries.zh: 王公貴人各為其私，群奉意旨不敢違，大亂遂成。
entries.en: Princes and grandees each pursued private ends; all followed her will without dissent, and catastrophe followed.
entries.literal: Princes, dukes, and nobles each pursued private ends; all followed her intent and dared not disobey, and great disorder was thus accomplished.

entries.zh: 及事敗，各國議懲首禍，徐桐等皆不能免。
entries.en: When the cause collapsed, the powers demanded the ringleaders be punished, and Xu Tong and his circle could not escape.
entries.literal: When matters failed, the various nations discussed punishing the chief instigators, and Xu Tong and the others could none of them escape.

entries.zh: 逢君之惡，孽由自作。
entries.en: They had indulged the ruler's worst impulses; the ruin was of their own making.
entries.literal: They indulged the ruler's wickedness; the calamity was of their own making.

entries.zh: 然刑賞聽命於人，何以立國哉？
entries.en: Yet when punishments and rewards are dictated by foreign powers, what foundation remains for the state?
entries.literal: Yet when punishment and reward obey others' commands, how can a state be established?

entries.zh: 列傳二百五十二
entries.en: Biographies 252
entries.literal: Biographies 252

entries.zh: 二十六年，拳禍起。
entries.en: In Guangxu 26 the Boxer disaster broke out.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer calamity arose.

entries.zh: 先是上以行新政為中外所推，而儲嗣久虛。
entries.en: The emperor had lately won praise at home and abroad for reform, but the succession had stood vacant for years.
entries.literal: Earlier the Emperor had been praised at home and abroad for carrying out new policies, yet the heir had long remained unsettled.

entries.zh: 載漪既用事，陰謀廢立，慮外人為梗，聞拳民有神勇，仇西教，欲倚以集事，召入京，遂縱恣不可制。
entries.en: Once Zaiyi was in charge he plotted deposition and enthronement in secret, fearing foreign interference; told the Boxers were supernaturally brave and hated Christianity, he meant to use them to carry out his plan, called them to Beijing, and they soon could not be restrained.
entries.literal: Once Zaiyi held power he plotted in secret to depose and enthrone, fearing foreigners would obstruct him; hearing that Boxers had divine valor and hated Western religion, he wished to rely on them to accomplish his design, summoned them to the capital, and they then ran riot beyond control.

entries.zh: 用儀請嚴禁遏，不聽。
entries.en: Yongyi urged stern prohibition and suppression, but no one listened.
entries.literal: Yongyi requested strict prohibition and suppression, but was not heeded.

entries.zh: 俄戕德使克林德，用儀駭曰：「禍始此矣！」
entries.en: Soon the German minister von Ketteler was murdered; Yongyi cried in alarm, "The calamity starts here!"
entries.literal: Before long the German minister Klemens von Ketteler was killed; Yongyi said in alarm: "Disaster begins here!"

entries.zh: 言於慶親王奕劻，厚歛之。
entries.en: He told Prince Qing Yikuang, who raised a heavy sum of money.
entries.literal: He spoke to Prince Qing Yikuang, who collected funds in large amounts.

entries.zh: 各國兵艦至津沽，詔廷臣集議和戰。
entries.en: Foreign warships reached Taku; the throne ordered ministers to meet and debate war or peace.
entries.literal: Warships of the various powers reached Taku; an edict ordered court ministers to assemble and debate peace and war.

entries.zh: 用儀、景澄、昶及尚書立山、內閣學士聯元並言：「奸民不可縱，外为不可啟。」
entries.en: Yongyi, Jingcheng, Chang, Minister Li Shan, and Hanlin Bachelor Lian Yuan jointly declared, "Riotous mobs must not be indulged, and foreign conflict must not be started."
entries.literal: Yongyi, Jingcheng, Chang, and Minister Li Shan and Hanlin Bachelor Lian Yuan all said together: "Wicked commoners must not be indulged; foreign trouble must not be provoked."

entries.zh: 而載漪等主戰甚力，在廷大臣率依違不決。
entries.en: But Zaiyi and his party argued fiercely for war, and most ministers at court vacillated without a decision.
entries.literal: Yet Zaiyi and others pressed for war with great force, and ministers at court mostly wavered and could not decide.

entries.zh: 用儀以太后命詣使館議緩兵，當事者益目為奸邪。
entries.en: Sent by the Empress Dowager to the legations to negotiate a pause in fighting, Yongyi was seen by the war party as all the more treacherous.
entries.literal: Yongyi, on the Empress Dowager's order, went to the legations to negotiate a truce; those in charge regarded him all the more as a traitor.

entries.zh: 膠州事起，下詔求言，昶條列時政二萬餘言，以：「德突據膠灣，其禍急而小；
entries.en: After the Jiaozhou crisis the throne sought advice; Chang submitted more than twenty thousand characters, arguing, "Germany's seizure of Jiaozhou was urgent but small;
entries.literal: When the Jiaozhou affair arose the throne called for memorials; Chang set forth more than twenty thousand characters on current policy, saying: "Germany's sudden seizure of Jiaozhou is a calamity urgent yet small;

entries.zh: 俄自西北至東北，與我壤地相錯，蒙喀四十八部將折入異域，其禍紆而大。
entries.en: Russia from the northwest to the northeast shares intertwined territory with us; the forty-eight Mongol and Khalkha banners will be folded into foreign lands—the calamity is winding yet great.
entries.literal: Russia from the northwest to the northeast shares intertwined territory with us; the forty-eight Mongol and Khalkha banners will be folded into foreign lands—the calamity is winding yet great.

entries.zh: 宜及今預練勁旅，痛革吉、奉華靡風習。
entries.en: We ought even now to train crack troops beforehand and thoroughly reform the extravagant habits of Jilin and Fengtian.
entries.literal: We ought even now to train crack troops beforehand and thoroughly reform the extravagant habits of Jilin and Fengtian.

entries.zh: 自頃兵力不能議戰，要不可不議守。
entries.en: Lately our military strength cannot sustain debate on war, yet we absolutely cannot fail to debate defense.
entries.literal: Lately our military strength cannot sustain debate on war, yet we absolutely cannot fail to debate defense.

entries.zh: 我朝八旗初制，文武不分途，京外不分途，人皆兵，官皆將，故人才盛，國勢強。
entries.en: Under the original Eight Banner system civil and military, capital and province were one; every man was a soldier and every officer a commander, so talent abounded and the state was strong.
entries.literal: Our dynasty's original Eight Banner system made no distinction between civil and military tracks, nor between capital and provinces; every man was a soldier and every official a general; therefore talent flourished and national strength was great.

entries.zh: 承平日久，文法繁密，諸臣救過之不暇，於是相率為鄉愿，而舉國之人才靡矣！
entries.en: Long peace bred intricate regulations; officials scrambled only to avoid blame, fell into timid conformity, and national talent withered.
entries.literal: After long peace the code grew intricate; ministers had no leisure beyond correcting faults; they therefore followed one another in timid conformity, and the nation's talent withered!

entries.zh: 金田洪、楊之亂，其始一小民耳，猶窮全國之力僅而克之，況諸國互肆蠶食之心，有不乘吾敝而攻吾之短者哉？
entries.en: The Taiping revolt began with ordinary villagers yet nearly exhausted the empire; with many powers eager to devour us, who would not strike when we were weak?
entries.literal: The Hong and Yang rebellion of Jintian began with a single commoner, yet the empire's full strength barely overcame it; how much more when many states all harbor designs of nibbling us—will there not be those who seize our weakness and strike our flaws?

entries.zh: 夫敵國外患，為殷憂啟聖之資。
entries.en: Foreign enemies and external troubles are resources by which deep anxiety awakens sagely rule.
entries.literal: Foreign enemies and external troubles are resources by which deep anxiety awakens sagely rule.

entries.zh: 苟得其人，毋拘以文法，則理財、練兵、防海、交鄰之策，可次第就理。」
entries.en: Given the right men, unbound by red tape, finance, armies, coast defense, and diplomacy could be put in order one by one."
entries.literal: If the right men are obtained and not bound by written regulations, then policies for finance, training troops, coastal defense, and foreign relations can be set in order step by step."

entries.zh: 上親書其綱要於冊，下中外大臣議行。
entries.en: The emperor copied its main points into a booklet and circulated them to ministers at home and abroad for action.
entries.literal: The Emperor personally copied its main points into a booklet and sent it down to Chinese and foreign ministers for discussion and implementation.

entries.zh: 二十四年，遷陝西按察使，未到官，擢江寧布政使，調直隸。
entries.en: In year 24 he was named Shaanxi judicial commissioner, then promoted to Jiangning financial commissioner and moved to Zhili before taking the first post.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to Shaanxi judicial commissioner; before taking office he was promoted to Jiangning financial commissioner and transferred to Zhili.

entries.zh: 未幾，內召，以三品京堂在總理衙門行走，授光祿寺卿，轉太常寺卿。
entries.en: Soon recalled to Beijing, he served at the Yamen as a third-rank capital official, became Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then Director of Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: Before long he was summoned to the capital; as a third-rank capital official he served at the Zongli Yamen, was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 時財用匱，議整釐稅。
entries.en: Finances were depleted and officials debated reorganizing the likin tax.
entries.literal: At that time finances were depleted and there was debate on reorganizing the likin tax.

entries.zh: 昶極言釐金名病商，實病民，不可議增。
entries.en: Chang insisted likin nominally hurt merchants but really hurt the people and must not be raised.
entries.literal: Chang strongly argued that likin by name harms merchants but in fact harms the people, and must not be increased.

entries.zh: 義和團起山東，屠戮外國教士。
entries.en: The Boxer movement rose in Shandong and massacred foreign missionaries.
entries.literal: The Boxers arose in Shandong and slaughtered foreign missionaries.

entries.zh: 昶與許景澄相善，廷詢時，陳奏皆谒慨，上執景澄手而泣。
entries.en: Close to Xu Jingcheng, Chang spoke as bluntly as he at court audiences; the emperor took Jingcheng's hand and wept.
entries.literal: Chang was on good terms with Xu Jingcheng; when questioned at court their statements were all forthright; the Emperor grasped Jingcheng's hand and wept.

entries.zh: 昶連上二疏，力言奸民不可縱，使臣不宜殺，皆不報。
entries.en: Chang sent two memorials in succession urging that rioters not be indulged and envoys not be killed; neither was answered.
entries.literal: Chang submitted two memorials in succession, strongly stating that wicked commoners must not be indulged and envoys must not be killed; none received response.

entries.zh: 復與景澄合上第三疏，嚴劾釀亂大臣，未及奏，已被禍，疏稿為世稱誦。
entries.en: He and Jingcheng drafted a third memorial impeaching the ministers who brewed the crisis; before it reached the throne he was dead, yet the draft became famous.
entries.literal: He again joined Jingcheng in submitting a third memorial, sternly impeaching the ministers who brewed the disorder; before it could be presented he had already met disaster; the draft was praised by the world.

entries.zh: 追諡忠節，江南人祠之蕪湖。
entries.en: Posthumously titled Zhongjie, Loyal and Upright, he was enshrined at Wuhu by Jiangnan gentry.
entries.literal: He was posthumously given the title Zhongjie; people of Jiangnan enshrined him at Wuhu.

entries.zh: 許景澄，字竹篔，嘉興人。
entries.en: Xu Jingcheng, whose courtesy name was Zhuyun, came from Jiaxing.
entries.literal: Xu Jingcheng, courtesy name Zhuyun, was a native of Jiaxing.

entries.zh: 同治七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
entries.en: In Tongzhi 7 he became a metropolitan graduate, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was made an editor.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Tongzhi he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed an editor.

entries.zh: 明習時事，大學士文祥以使才薦。
entries.en: Well versed in current affairs, he was recommended by Grand Secretary Wenxiang for talent in foreign service.
entries.literal: He was well versed in current affairs; Grand Secretary Wenxiang recommended him for diplomatic talent.

entries.zh: 光緒六年，詔使日本，遭父憂，未行。
entries.en: In Guangxu 6 he was ordered envoy to Japan, but his father died and he never went.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu he was ordered to serve as envoy to Japan but met his father's death and did not go.

entries.zh: 服闋，補侍講。
entries.en: After mourning he was appointed supervising reader.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he was made a supervising reader.

entries.zh: 法越之役，條上籌備事宜，上褒納。
entries.en: During the Sino-French War he laid out preparedness measures in a memorial, which the throne praised and adopted.
entries.literal: During the Sino-French War he submitted in detail plans for preparedness; the Emperor praised and accepted them.

entries.zh: 十年，出使法德意和奧五國大臣，兼攝比國使務。
entries.en: In year 10 he became minister to France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, and Austria, and concurrently to Belgium.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he served as minister to France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, and Austria, and concurrently handled Belgian affairs.

entries.zh: 時海軍初創，從德國購造鐵艦，未就。
entries.en: The navy had just been created; ironclads ordered from Germany were still unfinished.
entries.literal: At that time the navy was newly founded; ironclads were being purchased from Germany but were not yet completed.

entries.zh: 景澄躬歷船廠，鉤稽輯上外國師船表。
entries.en: Jingcheng inspected the yards himself, verified the figures, and submitted a register of foreign warships and instructors.
entries.literal: Jingcheng personally visited the shipyards, investigated and compiled, and submitted a table of foreign warships and instructors.

entries.zh: 又言海軍宜定屯埠膠州灣，設鐵甲尓船大沽口。
entries.en: He also urged fixing the fleet's base at Jiaozhou Bay and posting ironclads at Dagu.
entries.literal: He also said the navy ought to fix its base at Jiaozhou Bay and station ironclads at the Dagu mouth.

entries.zh: 轉侍讀，母憂歸。
entries.en: Made reader-in-waiting, he then left office to mourn his mother.
entries.literal: He was transferred to reader-in-waiting and returned home on his mother's death.

entries.zh: 景澄、昶先被害，用儀知不免，意氣自如。
entries.en: Jingcheng and Chang were executed first; Yongyi knew his end was near yet kept his bearing calm.
entries.literal: Jingcheng and Chang were killed first; Yongyi knew he could not escape yet remained composed in spirit.

entries.zh: 七月既望，遽發拳匪捕之於家，擁至莊王邸。
entries.en: On the sixteenth day of the seventh month Boxers suddenly arrested him at home and marched him to Prince Zhuang's residence.
entries.literal: On the full moon of the seventh month Boxers suddenly seized him at his home and escorted him to Prince Zhuang's mansion.

entries.zh: 用儀不置辯，第曰：「天降奇禍，死固分耳！」
entries.en: Yongyi made no defense and only said, "Heaven has sent this extraordinary disaster; to die is only my due!"
entries.literal: Yongyi offered no defense and only said: "Heaven sends this strange calamity; death is my allotted share!"

entries.zh: 遂與立山、聯元同棄市。
entries.en: He was then publicly executed together with Li Shan and Lian Yuan.
entries.literal: He was then executed in the marketplace together with Li Shan and Lian Yuan.

entries.zh: 越三日，聯軍入京，而兩宮西狩。
entries.en: Three days later the allied forces entered Beijing as the two courts fled west.
entries.literal: Three days later the allied armies entered the capital while the two sovereigns fled west.

entries.zh: 十二月，詔湔雪，復故官。
entries.en: In the twelfth month an edict rehabilitated them and restored their former ranks.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month an edict cleared their names and restored their former offices.

entries.zh: 宣統元年，追諡忠愍。
entries.en: In Xuantong 1 he received the posthumous title Zhongmin, Loyal and Suffering.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xuantong he was posthumously given the title Zhongmin.

entries.zh: 浙人祠之西湖，與景澄、昶並稱「三忠」。
entries.en: Zhejiang gentry built him a shrine at West Lake; with Jingcheng and Chang he was known as one of the "Three Loyal Ones."
entries.literal: Men of Zhejiang enshrined him at West Lake; together with Jingcheng and Chang they were called the "Three Loyal Ones."

entries.zh: 聯元，字仙蘅，崔佳氏，滿洲鑲紅旗人。
entries.en: Lian Yuan, courtesy name Xianheng, of the Cuijia clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner.
entries.literal: Lian Yuan, courtesy name Xianheng, of the Cuijia clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner.

entries.zh: 同治七年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討，累遷侍講。
entries.en: In Tongzhi 7 he became a metropolitan graduate and Hanlin bachelor, was made reviser, and rose to supervising reader.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Tongzhi he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, was appointed reviser, and was promoted in succession to supervising reader.

entries.zh: 大考，左遷中允，再陟侍講。
entries.en: After a poor grand examination he was demoted to junior expositor, then promoted again to supervising reader.
entries.literal: In the grand examination he was demoted to junior expositor and again rose to supervising reader.

entries.zh: 以京察，出知安徽太平府，調安慶。
entries.en: On a capital inspection he became prefect of Taiping in Anhui, then was moved to Anqing.
entries.literal: Through the capital inspection he went out as prefect of Taiping in Anhui and was transferred to Anqing.

entries.zh: 兩薦卓異，署滁和道，遷廣東惠潮嘉道。
entries.en: Twice rated outstanding, he served as acting intendant on the Chuzhou-He circuit and then as intendant of Huizhou, Chaozhou, and Jiazhou in Guangdong.
entries.literal: Twice recommended as outstanding, he acted as intendant of Chuzhou and He prefectures and was transferred to intendant of Huizhou, Chaozhou, and Jiazhou in Guangdong.

entries.zh: 汕頭者，通商要衢也，奸人倚英領事為民暴，聯元裁以法，良善獲安。
entries.en: At Shantou, a vital treaty port, ruffians sheltered behind the British consul to prey on the people until Lian Yuan punished them by law and the law-abiding were safe.
entries.literal: Shantou was a key port for foreign trade; wicked men relied on the British consul to tyrannize the people; Lian Yuan judged them by law and the good obtained peace.

entries.zh: 二十四年，擢安徽按察使，入覲，改三品京堂，在總理衙門行走。
entries.en: In year 24 he became Anhui judicial commissioner; after audience he was made a third-rank capital official at the Zongli Yamen.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was promoted to Anhui judicial commissioner; on entering audience he was made a third-rank capital official serving at the Zongli Yamen.

entries.zh: 又明年，補內閣學士。
entries.en: The following year he was appointed Hanlin bachelor.
entries.literal: The next year he was appointed Hanlin bachelor.

entries.zh: 拳民仇西教，載漪、剛毅助之，勢益橫，日夜圍攻使館，不能下。
entries.en: Boxers hated Christianity; backed by Zaiyi and Gang Yi they grew bolder, besieging the legations day and night without success.
entries.literal: The Boxers hated Western religion; Zaiyi and Gang Yi supported them; their power grew all the more overbearing; day and night they besieged the legations but could not take them.

entries.zh: 大臣負清望者徐桐、崇綺，皆謂：「民氣可用。」
entries.en: Respected ministers Xu Tong and Chongqi both declared, "The people's spirit can be harnessed."
entries.literal: Ministers of high repute, Xu Tong and Chongqi, all said: "Popular spirit can be used."

entries.zh: 聯元與崇綺爭論帝前，謂：「民氣可用，匪氣不可用。」
entries.en: Before the emperor Lian Yuan argued with Chongqi: "Popular spirit may be used, but bandit spirit must not."
entries.literal: Lian Yuan debated with Chongqi before the Emperor, saying: "Popular spirit can be used; bandit spirit cannot be used."

entries.zh: 聯軍既陷大沽，載漪等猶壹意主戰。
entries.en: Even after the allies captured Dagu, Zaiyi and his party still insisted on war.
entries.literal: After the allied armies had taken Dagu, Zaiyi and others still single-mindedly favored war.

entries.zh: 聯元謂：「甲午之役，一日本且不能勝，況八強國乎？
entries.en: Lian Yuan said, "In the Sino-Japanese War we could not beat Japan alone—what chance against eight great powers?
entries.literal: Lian Yuan said: "In the war of Jiawu, China could not even defeat Japan alone—how much less eight great powers?

entries.zh: 儻戰而敗，如宗廟何？」
entries.en: If we fight and lose, what becomes of the ancestral shrines?"
entries.literal: If we fight and are defeated, what of the ancestral temples?"

entries.zh: 載漪斥其言不祥，七月十七日，斬西市。
entries.en: Zaiyi called his words unlucky; on the seventeenth of the seventh month he was beheaded at the West Market.
entries.literal: Zaiyi denounced his words as ill-omened; on the seventeenth day of the seventh month he was beheaded at the West Market.

entries.zh: 昭雪後，予諡文直。
entries.en: After rehabilitation he received the posthumous title Wenzhi, Cultured and Upright.
entries.literal: After rehabilitation he was given the posthumous title Wenzhi.

entries.zh: 順天府奏請立山、聯元合祠宣武門外，而聯元祖居寶坻，更於其地建專祠焉。
entries.en: Shuntian requested a joint shrine to Li Shan and Lian Yuan outside Xuanwu Gate; because Lian Yuan's family came from Baodi, a separate shrine was built there as well.
entries.literal: Shuntian prefecture memorialized requesting a joint shrine for Li Shan and Lian Yuan outside Xuanwu Gate; because Lian Yuan's ancestral home was in Baodi, a separate shrine was also built there.

entries.zh: 徐用儀，字筱雲，浙江海鹽人。
entries.en: Xu Yongyi, whose courtesy name was Xiaoyun, came from Haiyan in Zhejiang.
entries.literal: Xu Yongyi, courtesy name Xiaoyun, was a native of Haiyan in Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 由副貢生入貲為主事，官刑部。
entries.en: Having bought office as a deputy tribute graduate, he entered service as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.
entries.literal: Through the office purchased by deputy tribute graduates he became a principal secretary and served in the Ministry of Punishments.

entries.zh: 咸豐九年，舉順天鄉試．同治初，充軍機章京，兼直總理各國事務衙門。
entries.en: In Xianfeng 9 he passed the Shuntian provincial examination; early in Tongzhi he became a Grand Council clerk and also served at the Zongli Yamen.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Xianfeng he passed the provincial examination in Shuntian; at the beginning of the Tongzhi reign he served as a Grand Council clerk and concurrently attended the Zongli Yamen.

entries.zh: 累遷鴻臚寺少卿，以憂歸。
entries.en: He rose step by step to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then left office to mourn a parent.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and returned home on bereavement leave.

entries.zh: 光緒三年，起太僕寺少卿，遷大理寺卿，直軍機如故。
entries.en: In Guangxu 3 he was recalled as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, then made President of the Court of Judicial Review while still attending the Grand Council.
entries.literal: In the third year of Guangxu he was recalled as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and transferred to President of the Court of Judicial Review, continuing to attend the Grand Council as before.

entries.zh: 擢工部侍郎，始罷直。
entries.en: Promoted to Vice Minister of Works, he at last gave up his regular seat on the Council.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Works and only then ceased regular attendance at the Council.

entries.zh: 旋充總理衙門大臣，歷兵部、吏部侍郎，授軍機大臣。
entries.en: He soon became a Zongli Yamen minister, served as vice minister of War and of Personnel in turn, and was appointed to the Grand Council.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he served as a Zongli Yamen minister, passed through the vice ministries of War and Personnel, and was appointed a Grand Council minister.

entries.zh: 二十年，加太子少保。
entries.en: In year 20 of the reign he received the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 日朝搆为，舉朝爭議和戰，樞臣孫毓汶被劾罷，翁同龢繼入，主戰益力。
entries.en: When Japan provoked conflict, the court split over peace and war; Grand Councillor Sun Yuwen was impeached out of office, and Weng Tonghe took his place and argued for war even harder.
entries.literal: Japan stirred up trouble; the whole court debated peace and war; Grand Councillor Sun Yuwen was impeached and dismissed; Weng Tonghe succeeded him and pressed for war all the more.

entries.zh: 用儀論事與同龢忤，遂出樞廷，並解總署事。
entries.en: Because Yongyi's policy views clashed with Weng Tonghe's, he was expelled from the Grand Council and stripped of his Yamen post as well.
entries.literal: Yongyi's views on affairs clashed with Tonghe's, and he was therefore removed from the Council and also relieved of his Zongli Yamen duties.

entries.zh: 二十四年，皇太后再訓政，復直總署，迺密薦太常寺卿袁昶。
entries.en: In Guangxu 24, after the Empress Dowager resumed rule, he returned to the Yamen and privately recommended Yuan Chang of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the Empress Dowager resumed personal rule; he again attended the Yamen and thereupon secretly recommended Yuan Chang, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 會許景澄奉使還，被命同入署。
entries.en: About then Xu Jingcheng came back from abroad and was ordered to join the Yamen with him.
entries.literal: At that time Xu Jingcheng returned from a diplomatic mission and was ordered to enter the Yamen together with him.

entries.zh: 李秉衡王廷相聶士成羅榮光壽山族孫瑞昌鳳翔崇玉等
entries.en: Li Bingheng, Wang Tingxiang, Nie Shicheng, Luo Rongguang, and Shoushan's kinsmen Ruichang, Fengxiang, Chongyu, and others
entries.literal: Li Bingheng, Wang Tingxiang, Nie Shicheng, Luo Rongguang, and the clansmen of Shoushan: Ruichang, Fengxiang, Chongyu, and others

entries.zh: 壽山，字眉峰，袁氏，漢軍正白旗人，黑龍江駐防，吉林將軍富明阿子。
entries.en: Shoushan, styled Meifeng, of the Yuan clan, was a Plain White Bannerman garrisoned in Heilongjiang and son of Fuming'a, governor-general of Jilin.
entries.literal: Shoushan, styled Meifeng, of the Yuan clan, was a Bannerman of the Plain White, garrisoned in Heilongjiang, and son of Fuming'a, military governor of Jilin.

entries.zh: 以父任為員外郎，兼襲騎都尉世職，遷郎中。
entries.en: Through his father's position he became an outer-court secretary, also inherited the hereditary post of Commandant of Cavalry, and rose to director.
entries.literal: Through his father's office he became an outer-court secretary, also inherited the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry, and was promoted to director.

entries.zh: 光緒二十年，日軍犯奉天，自請赴前敵，充步隊統領。
entries.en: In 1894, when the Japanese invaded Fengtian, he volunteered for the front as commander of the infantry.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year of Guangxu, when the Japanese invaded Fengtian, he volunteered for the front as commander of the infantry.

entries.zh: 弟永山領馬隊，數與日軍戰，复草河嶺，克連山關，進薄鳳凰城。
entries.en: His younger brother Yongshan led the cavalry; they fought the Japanese repeatedly, recovered Caoling, took Lianshan Pass, and pressed toward Fengcheng.
entries.literal: His younger brother Yongshan led the cavalry; they fought the Japanese repeatedly, recovered Caoling, took Lianshan Pass, and pressed close to Fengcheng.

entries.zh: 敵援至，永山歿於陣，壽山被重創。
entries.en: When enemy reinforcements arrived Yongshan fell in battle and Shoushan was badly wounded.
entries.literal: When enemy reinforcements arrived Yongshan died in battle and Shoushan was severely wounded.

entries.zh: 以敢戰，兼領鎮邊軍馬隊。
entries.en: For his bold fighting he was also given command of the Frontier Defense Army's cavalry.
entries.literal: For his bold fighting he was also given command of the cavalry of the Frontier Defense Army.

entries.zh: 逾歲，降敕褒嘉。
entries.en: A year later the throne issued an edict of praise.
entries.literal: A year later an imperial edict praised him.

entries.zh: 官軍既克海城，壽山領七十騎詣遼南诇敵勢，遇之湯岡子，搏戰，槍彈入右腹，貫左臀出，戰愈猛，敵稍卻，馳還壁，血縷縷滿衣袴。
entries.en: After the army recovered Haicheng, Shoushan led seventy horsemen to scout the enemy in southern Liaoning; at Tangangzi they fought; a bullet entered his right side and passed out his left hip; he fought all the harder; the enemy fell back slightly; he rode back to camp with blood soaking his clothes.
entries.literal: After government troops recovered Haicheng, Shoushan led seventy horsemen to scout the enemy in southern Liaoning; at Tangangzi they met the enemy in battle; a bullet entered his right abdomen and passed out through his left hip; he fought all the fiercer; the enemy gave ground slightly; he galloped back to camp, blood streaming down his clothes.

entries.zh: 上嘉其勇，遷知府，賞花翎。
entries.en: The court praised his courage; he was promoted to prefect and granted the peacock feather.
entries.literal: The throne praised his courage; he was promoted to prefect and granted the peacock feather.

entries.zh: 二十三年，調充鎮邊軍左路統領，徙駐黑龍江城。
entries.en: In 1897 he was made commander of the left wing of the Frontier Defense Army and moved his headquarters to Heilongjiang City.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year he was appointed commander of the left wing of the Frontier Defense Army and moved his headquarters to Heilongjiang City.

entries.zh: 越二年，除知開封遺缺知府，未之官，值東北邊防亟，超改黑龍江副都統。
entries.en: Two years later he was named to the vacant prefecture of Kaifeng but did not take office; with the northeastern frontier in crisis he was promoted out of turn to deputy lieutenant-general of Heilongjiang.
entries.literal: Two years later he was appointed to the vacant prefecture of Kaifeng but did not take office; with the northeastern frontier urgent, he was promoted out of turn to deputy lieutenant-general of Heilongjiang.

entries.zh: 明年春，入覲，垂詢邊情甚悉，命佐將軍恩澤治軍。
entries.en: The next spring he had an audience; the throne questioned him closely on border affairs and ordered him to assist General Enze in commanding the army.
entries.literal: The next spring he had an audience; the throne inquired minutely about border conditions and ordered him to assist General Enze in commanding the troops.

entries.zh: 疏請增募十五營，調諳邊事者十餘人，躬詣上海購軍械，自長崎、海參崴、伯利循海歸，潛度形勢，備戰守。
entries.en: He asked to recruit fifteen more battalions, called in more than ten men who knew the frontier, went himself to Shanghai to buy arms, returned by sea via Nagasaki, Vladivostok, and Khabarovsk, secretly surveyed the terrain, and prepared for defense.
entries.literal: He memorialized to recruit fifteen additional battalions, summoned more than ten men versed in frontier affairs, went in person to Shanghai to buy arms, returned by sea via Nagasaki, Vladivostok, and Khabarovsk, secretly surveyed the terrain, and prepared for war and defense.

entries.zh: 新軍成，而恩澤卒於任，朝命代之。
entries.en: When the new army was ready Enze died in office and the court ordered Shoushan to succeed him.
entries.literal: When the new army was ready Enze died in office and the court ordered Shoushan to replace him.

entries.zh: 既蒞事，鏟姦弊，明賞罰，圖要塞；
entries.en: Once in office he rooted out corruption, made rewards and punishments clear, and planned fortifications;
entries.literal: Once in charge he rooted out corruption, made rewards and punishments clear, and planned strongpoints;

entries.zh: 手訂行陣操法，頒之各將領，使番上，授以方略；
entries.en: he personally drafted field-drill regulations and issued them to every commander, requiring rotation on duty and teaching strategy;
entries.literal: he personally drafted drill regulations for field formations and issued them to every commander, requiring them to take turns on duty and teaching them strategy;

entries.zh: 雖末弁亦接見，籍記備器使。
entries.en: even junior officers he received in audience and recorded what equipment each could provide.
entries.literal: even junior officers he received and recorded what equipment each could supply.

entries.zh: 二十六年夏，拳亂作，俄軍數千聲為保護哈爾濱鐵軌，紛集海蘭泡，乞假道。
entries.en: In the summer of 1900 the Boxer uprising broke out; several thousand Russian troops, claiming to protect the Harbin railway, gathered at Blagoveshchensk and asked to pass through.
entries.literal: In the summer of the twenty-sixth year the Boxer turmoil broke out; several thousand Russian troops, claiming to protect the Harbin railway, gathered at Hailanpao and asked passage.

entries.zh: 壽山曰：「敵偪我都，我假敵道，如大義何！」
entries.en: Shoushan said: "The enemy threatens our territory; if we let the enemy march through, what becomes of duty!"
entries.literal: Shoushan said: "The enemy presses on our capital; if we grant the enemy passage, what becomes of righteousness!"

entries.zh: 拒之。
entries.en: He refused.
entries.literal: He refused.

entries.zh: 遂檄愛琿副都統鳳翔禦北路，呼倫貝爾副都統依興阿禦西路，通肯副都統慶祺禦東路，令各嚴戒備毋浪戰；
entries.en: He ordered Deputy Lieutenant-General Fengxiang of Aihui to hold the northern route, Yixing'a of Hulunbuir the west, and Qingqi of Tongken the east, telling each to stand on guard and not fight recklessly;
entries.literal: He then ordered Deputy Lieutenant-General Fengxiang of Aihui to guard the northern route, Deputy Lieutenant-General Yixing'a of Hulunbuir the western route, and Deputy Lieutenant-General Qingqi of Tongken the eastern route, instructing each to hold strict guard and not fight recklessly;

entries.zh: 並牒俄勿進兵，願負保路責。
entries.en: he also notified the Russians not to advance, offering to bear full responsibility for protecting the railway.
entries.literal: and also notified the Russians not to advance, offering to bear full responsibility for protecting the railway.

entries.zh: 而俄軍已分道進，重以鐵路土工可十餘萬索值，倡罷工，揚言與俄為難。
entries.en: But Russian columns were already advancing on several roads; more than a hundred thousand railway laborers demanded wages, struck work, and openly threatened Russia.
entries.literal: But the Russian armies had already advanced on several roads; more than a hundred thousand railway laborers demanded back pay, called a strike, and openly threatened trouble with Russia.

entries.zh: 壽山亟下令軍中曰：「保鐵路，護難民，全睦誼，違者殺無赦！」
entries.en: Shoushan urgently ordered the army: "Protect the railway, shelter refugees, preserve good relations—violators shall be executed without mercy!"
entries.literal: Shoushan urgently ordered the army: "Protect the railway, shelter refugees, preserve friendly relations—whoever violates this shall be killed without mercy!"

entries.zh: 復使統領吉祥約富拉爾基監工蓋爾肖甫入城，俾釋疑懼，而蓋爾肖甫乃擊殺工人宵遁。
entries.en: He also sent Commander Jixiang with Giershov at Fularji to supervise work and enter the city to ease fears, but Giershov killed workers by night and fled.
entries.literal: He also sent Commander Jixiang with Giershov at Fularji to supervise the work and enter the city to ease suspicion, but Giershov killed workers by night and fled.

entries.zh: 壽山猶強為容忍也，慎導俄民出境，籍錄其財物備還，然俄軍不為止，入寇愛琿及黑河屯，華人被迫赴水者，屍蔽江下。
entries.en: Shoushan still forced forbearance, carefully escorting Russian civilians out and recording their goods for return, yet the Russians did not stop; they invaded Aihui and Heihe Tun; Chinese driven into the river left the water choked with corpses downstream.
entries.literal: Shoushan still forced himself to endure, carefully escorting Russian civilians out of the country and recording their property for return, yet the Russian army did not stop; it invaded Aihui and Heihe Tun; Chinese forced into the river left corpses covering the current downstream.

entries.zh: 三姓、呼倫貝爾又紛紛告警，壽山亟電吉林將軍長順會攻哈爾濱，然猶囑其語俄總監工，謂若罷兵，願以全家質。
entries.en: Sanxing and Hulunbuir also sent alarms; Shoushan wired Jilin Governor Chang Shun to attack Harbin jointly, yet still told the Russian chief engineer that if they halted he would pledge his whole family.
entries.literal: Alarm came from Sanxing and Hulunbuir as well; Shoushan urgently wired the Jilin governor Chang Shun to join in attacking Harbin, yet still told the Russian chief engineer that if they halted he would stake his whole family as guarantee.

entries.zh: 當是時，諸路軍皆潰敗，北路統領崇玉，營官德春、瑞昌，西路統領保全，東路營官保林，並陷陣死，於是俄遂偪齊齊哈爾省城。
entries.en: By then every column had been broken; on the north Commander Chongyu and camp officers Dechun and Ruichang, on the west Commander Baoquan, on the east camp officer Baolin—all fell; the Russians then pressed on Qiqihar.
entries.literal: At that time every route's army was broken; on the northern route Commander Chongyu, camp officers Dechun and Ruichang, on the western route Commander Baoquan, on the eastern route camp officer Baolin—all fell in battle; the Russians then pressed on Qiqihar.

entries.zh: 既而聞聯軍媾和，乃遣同知程德全往商和議，而自守「軍覆則死」之義，命妻及子婦先裁，手繕遺疏，猶惓惓於墾政，並致書俄將領囑勿戕民。
entries.en: When word came that the allied powers had made peace, he sent Subprefect Cheng Dequan to negotiate, while he upheld the rule of "a defeated commander must die"; he had his wife and daughters-in-law killed first, wrote his final memorial still urging land reclamation, and wrote the Russian commanders begging them not to harm civilians.
entries.literal: When word came that the allied powers had made peace, he sent Subprefect Cheng Dequan to negotiate, while he himself upheld the principle of "when the army is destroyed the commander must die"; he ordered his wife and daughters-in-law cut down first, wrote his final memorial still urging land reclamation, and wrote the Russian commanders asking them not to harm the people.

entries.zh: 閱日，具衣冠，飲金，臥柩中，不死；
entries.en: A day later, in full dress, he drank poison and lay in his coffin, but did not die;
entries.literal: A day later, dressed in full regalia, he drank gold and lay in his coffin, but did not die;

entries.zh: 呼其屬下材官擊以槍，不忍，手顫機動，彈出中左脅，猶不死；
entries.en: he called his armorer to shoot him; the man could not bear to, his hand shook, the trigger slipped, the bullet struck his left side, yet he still lived;
entries.literal: he called his armorer to shoot him; the man could not bear to, his hand shook and the trigger slipped; the bullet struck his left ribs but he still did not die;

entries.zh: 更呼材官擊小腹，仍不死；
entries.en: he called again for a shot in the lower belly; still he lived;
entries.literal: he called again for a shot in the lower abdomen; still he did not die;

entries.zh: 呼益厲，又擊之，氣始絕。
entries.en: he shouted all the fiercer; they shot again, and only then did he die.
entries.literal: he shouted all the fiercer; they shot again, and only then did his breath stop.

entries.zh: 先是詔責其開邊釁，部議奪職。
entries.en: Earlier an edict had blamed him for provoking border trouble and the Board had voted to strip his rank.
entries.literal: Earlier an edict had blamed him for provoking border trouble and the Board voted to strip his office.

entries.zh: 後以總督徐世昌請復官，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，附祀富明阿祠。
entries.en: Later, at Governor-General Xu Shichang's request, his rank was restored; he was granted hereditary offices and given a place in sacrifice at Fuming'a's shrine.
entries.literal: Later, on Governor-General Xu Shichang's request, his office was restored; he was granted the hereditary offices of Commandant of Cavalry and Cloud Cavalry Captain, and given a place in sacrifice at Fuming'a's shrine.

entries.zh: 鳳翔，字集庭，漢軍鑲黃旗人，吉林駐防。
entries.en: Fengxiang, styled Jiting, was a Bordered Yellow Bannerman garrisoned in Jilin.
entries.literal: Fengxiang, styled Jiting, was a Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow, garrisoned in Jilin.

entries.zh: 累官協領。
entries.en: He rose step by step to assistant commandant.
entries.literal: He rose by stages to assistant commandant.

entries.zh: 光緒二十一年，中日事起，將軍長順赴奉督師，鳳翔任餽運，給食不乏。
entries.en: In 1895, when war broke out between China and Japan, General Chang Shun went to Fengtian to command; Fengxiang handled transport and food never ran short.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year of Guangxu, when trouble broke out between China and Japan, General Chang Shun went to Fengtian to command the army; Fengxiang handled transport and provisions never ran short.

entries.zh: 尋擢愛琿副都統。
entries.en: Soon he was promoted to deputy lieutenant-general of Aihui.
entries.literal: Soon he was promoted to deputy lieutenant-general of Aihui.

entries.zh: 二十六年，俄將固畢乃脫爾來假道，壽山令愛琿戒備。
entries.en: In 1900 the Russian general Gubinadel came asking passage; Shoushan ordered Aihui to stand on guard.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Russian general Gubinadel came asking passage; Shoushan ordered Aihui to stand on guard.

entries.zh: 俄軍已自黑龍江下駛，翼日，俄官廓米薩爾名闊利士密德者，浮軍艦至，鳳翔遣軍拒之三道溝。
entries.en: Russian troops had already sailed down the Amur; the next day the Russian officer Komissarov arrived with gunboats; Fengxiang sent troops to meet him at Sandao Gou.
entries.literal: Russian troops had already sailed down the Amur; the next day the Russian officer Komissarov, called Kolishimide, arrived with gunboats; Fengxiang sent troops to resist him at Sandao Gou.

entries.zh: 闊利士密德來謁，申前請，弗允，赬怒去，令舟師擊我，而我師已先發，殲其軍官二，闊利士密德被重創，奔還海蘭泡，旋卒。
entries.en: Komissarov came to call and repeated the request; it was refused; he left in anger and ordered his fleet to attack, but our troops had already fired, killing two officers; Komissarov was badly wounded, fled to Blagoveshchensk, and soon died.
entries.literal: Komissarov came to call and repeated the request; it was refused; he left flushed with anger and ordered his fleet to attack us, but our troops had already opened fire, killing two of their officers; Komissarov was badly wounded, fled back to Hailanpao, and soon died.

entries.zh: 於是黑河軍與海蘭泡俄軍相轟擊者數日。
entries.en: For days thereafter the Heihe army and the Russians at Blagoveshchensk exchanged fire.
entries.literal: Thereafter the Heihe army and the Russians at Hailanpao exchanged fire for several days.

entries.zh: 鳳翔令統領王仲良率騎旅三百渡江擊之，始小挫，繼獲大勝。
entries.en: Fengxiang ordered Commander Wang Zhongliang to lead three hundred cavalry across the river; at first they met a small setback, then a great victory.
entries.literal: Fengxiang ordered Commander Wang Zhongliang to lead three hundred cavalry across the river to attack; at first they met a small setback, then won a great victory.

entries.zh: 俄軍緣江遁，師往馳之，會其軍艦泊江岸，載歸。
entries.en: The Russians fled along the river; our forces pursued and towed back their gunboats moored on the bank.
entries.literal: The Russian army fled along the river; our forces pursued; finding their gunboats moored on the bank, they towed them back.

entries.zh: 閱二日，又渡江來，擊卻之。
entries.en: Two days later they crossed again; we drove them back.
entries.literal: Two days later they crossed the river again; we beat them back.

entries.zh: 遲明，又率步旅六千自五道河濟，右路統領崇玉望見之，其軍皆樹我幟，衣我衣，意為漠河護礦兵也，弗敢擊，既登岸始覺，而勢已不可遏，我師敗績，崇玉殞於陣，愛琿陷。
entries.en: At dawn six thousand infantry crossed from Wudao River; Commander Chongyu on the right saw them flying our banners in our uniforms and thought them the Mohe mineral guard; he dared not fire until they had landed; by then it was too late; our army was routed, Chongyu fell, and Aihui was lost.
entries.literal: At dawn they led six thousand infantry across from Wudao River; Commander Chongyu on the right wing saw them; their troops all flew our banners and wore our uniforms; he thought them the Mohe mineral-guard troops and dared not attack; only after they landed did he realize it, but the momentum could not be stopped; our army was defeated, Chongyu fell in battle, and Aihui was lost.

entries.zh: 壽山聞之，亟令鳳翔回援，弗及。
entries.en: When Shoushan heard, he urgently ordered Fengxiang back, but too late.
entries.literal: When Shoushan heard, he urgently ordered Fengxiang to return to aid him, but it was too late.

entries.zh: 鳳翔駐兜溝子，去愛琿七十里。
entries.en: Fengxiang held Dougouzi, seventy li from Aihui.
entries.literal: Fengxiang encamped at Dougouzi, seventy li from Aihui.

entries.zh: 踰月，俄軍復至，槍彈雨下，鳳翔以戰為守，相持累日。
entries.en: A month later the Russians returned; bullets fell like rain; Fengxiang fought to hold and the standoff lasted many days.
entries.literal: A month later the Russians came again; bullets fell like rain; Fengxiang fought to hold his ground and the standoff lasted many days.

entries.zh: 黑龍江行軍故無棚帳，戰罷露宿，眾苦寒，以是軍有怨聲，鳳翔慮譁潰，復以地勢平衍難扼守，乃請壽山結陣徐退，抵內興安嶺軍焉，去兜溝子又百六十里。
entries.en: The Heilongjiang troops had no tents and slept in the open after battle; the cold bred discontent; Fengxiang feared mutiny; the ground was too open to hold; he asked Shoushan to withdraw in order to the Inner Xing'an camp, another hundred sixty li beyond Dougouzi.
entries.literal: Heilongjiang field armies had no tents; after battle they slept in the open; the men suffered bitter cold, and discontent arose; Fengxiang feared mutiny; the ground was also too flat to defend; he asked Shoushan to withdraw in good order to the Inner Xing'an Range army, another hundred sixty li beyond Dougouzi.

entries.zh: 未幾，俄軍爭上嶺，勢洶洶，師失利，仍扼嶺拒之。
entries.en: Soon the Russians pressed up the ridge in force; our troops were beaten but still held the pass.
entries.literal: Before long the Russians pressed up the ridge in force; our troops met defeat but still held the pass against them.

entries.zh: 敵攻益亟，鳳翔悉甲出，令曰：「有後者斬！」
entries.en: As the attack intensified Fengxiang sent out his whole force with the order: "Whoever retreats shall be beheaded!"
entries.literal: As the enemy pressed harder Fengxiang sent out his entire force with the order: "Whoever falls back shall be beheaded!"

entries.zh: 而自赴前敵督懾。
entries.en: He himself went to the front to command.
entries.literal: He himself went to the front to oversee.

entries.zh: 有材官稍卻，立使飛騎斬之。
entries.en: When an armorer gave ground slightly he sent a mounted courier to behead him at once.
entries.literal: When an armorer fell back slightly he immediately sent a flying courier to behead him.

entries.zh: 材官懼，大呼陷陣，俄軍少卻，復進，遂大敗，署北路翼長恆玉斷一臂，俄將卒死傷無算。
entries.en: The men in fear shouted and charged; the Russians fell back, advanced again, and were routed; Acting Northern Wing Commander Hengyu lost an arm, and countless Russians were killed or wounded.
entries.literal: The armorers in fear shouted and charged the line; the Russians fell back slightly, then advanced again, and were utterly defeated; Acting Northern Wing Commander Hengyu lost an arm, and countless Russian officers and men were killed or wounded.

entries.zh: 鳳翔戰既酣，右臂左足兩受彈傷，墜馬者三，輒复躍上，鏖戰不少休，既還，嘔血數升而死。
entries.en: Fengxiang fought with all his might; his right arm and left foot were shot; three times he fell from his horse and leaped back up; he would not stop; after returning to camp he vomited blood and died.
entries.literal: Fengxiang fought with utmost fury; his right arm and left foot were both shot; three times he fell from his horse and leaped back up; he fought without pause; after returning he vomited several pints of blood and died.

entries.zh: 事聞，優恤如製。
entries.en: When word reached court, posthumous honors were granted by regulation.
entries.literal: When word reached the throne, special posthumous benefits were granted according to regulation.

entries.zh: 論曰：秉衡清忠自矢，受命危難，大節凜然，此不能以成敗論也。
entries.en: The commentators say: Bingheng held fast to integrity and took up duty in crisis; his great constancy commands respect—this cannot be judged by success or failure alone.
entries.literal: The commentators say: Bingheng kept his integrity and devoted himself to duty in peril; his great integrity was awe-inspiring—this cannot be judged by success or failure alone.

entries.zh: 聯軍之佔津、海也，長驅而入，唯士成阻之；
entries.en: When the allied armies held Tianjin and the coast they advanced at will; only Shicheng stood in their way;
entries.literal: When the allied armies occupied Tianjin and the coast they marched in at will; only Shicheng blocked them;

entries.zh: 俄兵之侵龍江也，乘隙以進，唯壽山拒之：固知必不能敵，誓以一死報耳。
entries.en: When the Russians invaded the Amur country they pressed through every gap; only Shoushan stood against them—knowing he could not win, yet sworn to repay his duty with his life.
entries.literal: When Russian troops invaded the Amur region they advanced through every opening; only Shoushan resisted them: he knew full well he could not prevail, yet vowed to repay the state with his death.

entries.zh: 榮光爭大沽，鳳翔守愛琿，雖已無救於大局，而至死不屈，外人亦為之奪氣，何其壯哉！
