entries.en: Rongguang fought at Dagu and Fengxiang held Aihui; though neither could alter the larger outcome, both died unbowed, and even the foreigners were struck with awe—how splendid their courage!
entries.literal: Rongguang fought for Dagu and Fengxiang held Aihui; though they could not save the larger situation, to the end they did not yield, and even foreigners were awed by them—how magnificent!

entries.zh: 列傳二百五十四
entries.en: Biographies 254
entries.literal: Biographies 254

entries.zh: 光緒二年，充會試副考官，補鑲黃旗漢軍副都統。
entries.en: In 1876 he served as associate examiner for the metropolitan examinations and was appointed deputy lieutenant-general of the Han Bordered Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: In the second year of Guangxu, he served as associate examiner for the metropolitan examinations and was appointed to fill the post of deputy lieutenant-general of the Han Bordered Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 會河南旱，大吏匿不報，為言官所劾。
entries.en: When Henan suffered drought, provincial officials concealed the disaster and failed to report it, drawing impeachment from the censorate.
entries.literal: It happened that Henan suffered drought; high officials concealed it and did not report it, and they were impeached by censorial officials.

entries.zh: 上命偕侍郎邵亨豫按問，廉得實，巡撫李慶翔以下皆獲罪。
entries.en: The emperor ordered him to investigate jointly with Vice Minister Shao Hengyu; they uncovered the truth, and Governor Li Qingxiang and his subordinates were all punished.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered him to go with Vice Minister Shao Hengyu to investigate; the truth was obtained with integrity, and Governor Li Qingxiang and those below him were all punished.

entries.zh: 四年，吉林駐防侍衛倭興額被盜誣控，詔與侍郎馮譽驥往讞，尋命崇綺署將軍專治之。
entries.en: In 1878, Wo Xing'e, a bodyguard stationed in Jilin, was falsely accused of theft; Chong Qi was sent with Vice Minister Feng Yuji to try the case, and soon afterward was ordered to act as general and take exclusive charge of it.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, the garrison guard of Jilin, Bodyguard Wo Xing'e, was falsely accused of theft; an edict ordered him to go with Vice Minister Feng Yuji to judge the case, and soon Chong Qi was ordered to act as general and handle it exclusively.

entries.zh: 倭興額控如故，事下侍郎志和覈覆，得誣告狀，崇綺自劾，被宥。
entries.en: Wo Xing'e's accusation stood unchanged until Vice Minister Zhi He reviewed the case and confirmed it was a false charge; Chong Qi submitted a self-impeachment and was pardoned.
entries.literal: Wo Xing'e's accusation remained as before; the matter was sent down to Vice Minister Zhi He for re-examination, and a false-accusation case was established; Chong Qi impeached himself and was pardoned.

entries.zh: 五年，出為熱河都統。
entries.en: In 1879 he was appointed commander-in-chief of Rehe.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, he went out as commander-in-chief of Rehe.

entries.zh: 御史孔憲疏稱其忠直，宜留輔，不許。
entries.en: Censor Kong Xian memorialized praising his loyalty and urging that he be kept at court to assist the throne, but the request was denied.
entries.literal: Censor Kong Xian memorialized saying he was loyal and upright and ought to be retained to assist, but this was not permitted.

entries.zh: 七年，調盛京將軍。
entries.en: In 1881 he was transferred to general of Mukden.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, he was transferred to be general of Mukden.

entries.zh: 中法構釁，疏言：「我國士夫多懵外勢，請自今慎選使才，令其考察彼國政治利弊，圖其山川夷險，隨時奏聞。」
entries.en: When the Sino-French conflict broke out, he memorialized: 'Our scholars are largely ignorant of foreign conditions. Henceforth, please carefully select capable envoys and charge them to investigate those countries' political strengths and weaknesses, map their terrain and strategic features, and report back regularly.'
entries.literal: When China and France came into conflict, he memorialized: 'The gentlemen of our country are largely ignorant of foreign conditions; from now on please carefully select men of talent for missions, and order them to investigate the political advantages and disadvantages of those countries, map their mountains and rivers and their difficult and easy terrain, and report at all times.'

entries.zh: 又言：「名將必知地利而後可行師，廟堂必知地利而後可馭將。
entries.en: He also wrote: 'A great general must know the terrain before he can march; the court must know the terrain before it can command generals.
entries.literal: He also said: 'A famous general must know the advantages of terrain before he can march troops; the court must know the advantages of terrain before it can command generals.

entries.zh: 今宜北起盛京，南踰嶺廣，合台、瓊為一氣。
entries.en: Maps should run from Mukden in the north through Lingnan and Guangdong in the south, uniting Taiwan and Hainan into a single strategic picture.
entries.literal: Now it is fitting to begin in the north at Mukden, cross south beyond the Lingnan and Guangdong regions, and unite Taiwan and Hainan as one continuous whole.

entries.zh: 復自滇、粵邊外訖越南全境，分繪兩圖，更令諸疆臣各繪所轄地圖，上測緯度，下準方斜，俾知相距里數，為軍事之用。」
entries.en: From beyond the Yunnan and Guangdong frontiers through all of Vietnam, two separate maps should be drawn; frontier officials should each map their jurisdictions with latitude above and bearings below, so distances in li may be known for military planning.'
entries.literal: Again, from beyond the borders of Yunnan and Guangdong through the whole territory of Vietnam, draw two separate maps; further order each frontier official to draw a map of his jurisdiction, measuring latitude above and fixing bearings below, so that the distance in li between places may be known, for use in military affairs.'

entries.zh: 上韙其議。
entries.en: The emperor approved his proposal.
entries.literal: The emperor approved his proposal.

entries.zh: 宗室壽富，字伯茀，隸正藍旗，侍讀寶廷子。
entries.en: The imperial clansman Shou Fu, style name Bofu, was registered in the Plain Blue Banner and was the son of Reader Bao Ting.
entries.literal: The imperial clansman Shou Fu, style name Bofu, was registered in the Plain Blue Banner, son of the reader Bao Ting.

entries.zh: 泛覽群籍，尤諳周官、禮、太史公書，旁逮外國史，通算術，工古文詩詞。
entries.en: He read widely, was especially versed in the Offices of Zhou, the Rites, and Sima Qian's Records, also studied foreign histories, mastered mathematics, and excelled in classical prose and poetry.
entries.literal: He ranged widely through all books, was especially versed in the Offices of Zhou, the Rites, and the Grand Historian's Records, also reached to foreign histories, mastered mathematics, and was skilled in ancient-style prose and poetry.

entries.zh: 光緒十四年，成進士，選庶吉士。
entries.en: In 1888 he passed the examinations and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year of Guangxu he became a jinshi and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.

entries.zh: 嘗憤國勢不張，八旗人才日衰，箸勸八旗官士文，立知恥會，大旨警頑傲，勵以自強。
entries.en: Angered by the dynasty's weakness and the daily decline of Eight Banner talent, he wrote urging banner officials and gentry to study, founded a Society for Knowing Shame, and sought to warn against stubborn arrogance and encourage self-strengthening.
entries.literal: He once resented that the nation's power did not expand and that Eight Banner talent daily declined; he wrote urging the Eight Banner officials and gentry to study, established a Society for Knowing Shame, the main purpose being to warn against stubborn arrogance and encourage self-strengthening.

entries.zh: 浙江巡撫廖壽豐疏薦壽富才學堪大用，命赴日本考政治。
entries.en: Zhejiang Governor Liao Shoufeng memorialized recommending Shou Fu for high office; the court ordered him to Japan to study its political system.
entries.literal: Zhejiang Governor Liao Shoufeng memorialized recommending Shou Fu's talent and learning as fit for great employment; he was ordered to go to Japan to investigate politics.

entries.zh: 既還，箸日本風土志四卷獻上，召見，痛陳中國積弊及所宜興宜革者，漏三下始退，上器之。
entries.en: On his return he presented a four-volume Record of Japanese Customs, was summoned to audience, and spoke at length on China's accumulated abuses and what should be promoted or reformed; he did not withdraw until the third watch, and the emperor valued him highly.
entries.literal: After he returned, he wrote a four-volume Record of Japanese Customs and presented it; he was summoned for audience, bitterly stated China's accumulated abuses and what ought to be promoted and reformed, and did not withdraw until the third watch; the emperor valued him.

entries.zh: 政變作，遂杜門。
entries.en: After the coup of 1898 he shut himself indoors and refused visitors.
entries.literal: When the political coup occurred, he then shut his doors.

entries.zh: 九年，謝病歸。
entries.en: In 1883 he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.

entries.zh: 旋授戶部尚書，再調戶部，复乞休。
entries.en: He was soon appointed minister of Revenue, then transferred back to that same ministry, and again petitioned to retire.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed minister of the Revenue ministry, was again transferred to the Revenue ministry, and again begged to retire.

entries.zh: 初，穆宗崩，孝哲皇后以身殉，崇綺不自安，故再引疾。
entries.en: After Emperor Muzong died and Empress Xiaozhe followed him in death, Chong Qi felt ill at ease at court and therefore pleaded illness a second time.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Muzong died, Empress Xiaozhe followed him in death; Chong Qi did not feel secure, and therefore again pleaded illness.

entries.zh: 二十六年，立溥俊為「大阿哥」，嗣穆宗。
entries.en: In 1900, Pu Jun was installed as the 'Great Heir Apparent' to succeed Emperor Muzong.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, Pu Jun was established as the 'Great Heir Apparent' to succeed Muzong.

entries.zh: 乃起崇綺於家，俾署翰林院掌院學士，傅溥俊。
entries.en: Chong Qi was then recalled from retirement and appointed acting chancellor of the Hanlin Academy to tutor Pu Jun.
entries.literal: Thereupon Chong Qi was summoned from retirement at home and made to act as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, to tutor Pu Jun.

entries.zh: 於是崇綺再出，與徐桐比而言廢立，甚得太后寵，恩眷與桐埒。
entries.en: Chong Qi thus returned to power; like Xu Tong he spoke openly of deposing and installing rulers, won the empress dowager's deep favor, and received imperial grace equal to Tong's.
entries.literal: Thus Chong Qi came forth again; he and Xu Tong were alike in speaking of deposing and establishing rulers, and he won the empress dowager's great favor; imperial grace and favor were equal to Tong's.

entries.zh: 義和團起，朝貴崇奉者十之七八，而崇綺亦信仰之。
entries.en: When the Boxer movement arose, seven or eight out of ten court grandees embraced it, and Chong Qi was among the believers.
entries.literal: When the Boxers arose, seven or eight tenths of the court nobility revered them, and Chong Qi also believed in them.

entries.zh: 事敗，隨榮祿走保定，居蓮池書院，自縊死。
entries.en: When the movement collapsed, he fled with Rong Lu to Baoding, took lodging at the Lotus Pond Academy, and hanged himself.
entries.literal: When affairs failed, he followed Rong Lu in fleeing to Baoding, lodged at the Lotus Pond Academy, and hanged himself.

entries.zh: 榮祿以聞，賜奠醊，入祀昭忠祠，諡文節。
entries.en: Rong Lu reported his death; the court granted libation offerings, enshrined him in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty, and gave him the posthumous title Wenjie.
entries.literal: Rong Lu reported it; libation offerings were bestowed, he was entered for worship in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty, and given the posthumous title Wenjie.

entries.zh: 列傳二百五十五
entries.en: Biography 255
entries.literal: Biographies 255

entries.zh: 十年，署天津海關道。
entries.en: In the tenth year (1884) he acted as Tianjin customs daotai.
entries.literal: In the tenth year, he served as acting Tianjin customs daotai.

entries.zh: 會法越搆釁，海防急。
entries.en: War broke out between France and Vietnam, and coastal defense suddenly grew urgent.
entries.literal: When France and Vietnam clashed, coastal defense became urgent.

entries.zh: 迺移金州礦貲治蘇、浙、閩、粵電綫，便軍事，而部議指爲含混，科以降級調用。
entries.en: He diverted Jinzhou mining funds to build telegraph lines in Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, and Guangdong for military use; the ministry found his accounts unclear and ordered him demoted and transferred.
entries.literal: He then shifted Jinzho mining capital to establish telegraph lines in Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, and Guangdong for military convenience, but the ministry judged his report vague and imposed demotion and transfer.

entries.zh: 左宗棠爲言於上，事下南洋大臣曾國荃等，上其績狀，始改留任。
entries.en: Zuo Zongtang pleaded his case at court; the matter went to Nanyang minister Zeng Guoquan and others, who reported his record, and he was allowed to stay in office.
entries.literal: Zuo Zongtang spoke for him to the throne; the matter was referred to Nanyang Grand Secretary Zeng Guoquan and others, who reported his merits, and he was finally allowed to retain his post.

entries.zh: 十二年，授山東登萊青道。
entries.en: In the twelfth year (1886) he was appointed intendant of the Deng-Lai-Qing circuit in Shandong.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year, he was appointed Shandong Deng-Lai-Qing circuit intendant.

entries.zh: 法領事林椿詣煙臺與訂越南北圻綫約，朝旨既報可矣，而張之洞執言不可行。
entries.en: The French consul Lin Chun came to Yantai to sign a Tonkin cable agreement; the court had approved it, but Zhang Zhidong insisted it must not proceed.
entries.literal: The French consul Lin Chun came to Yantai to conclude the Tonkin-North Vietnam line agreement; the imperial rescript had already approved it, but Zhang Zhidong insisted it could not be carried out.

entries.zh: 宣懷曰：「今琿春、海蘭泡欲接俄綫，俄方有挾求。
entries.en: Xuanhuai said: "Hunchun and Hailanpao now seek to link with Russian lines, and Russia will use that as leverage.
entries.literal: Xuanhuai said: "Now Hunchun and Hailanpao wish to connect with Russian lines, and the Russian side has leverage for demands.

entries.zh: 法既許接綫，彼必易就範。
entries.en: If France is allowed to connect its line, the Russians will be easier to bring to terms.
entries.literal: If France is allowed to connect lines, they will surely be easier to bring within bounds.

entries.zh: 且英、丹皆與約，奚拒法！」
entries.en: Britain and Denmark have both signed similar agreements—why refuse France alone?"
entries.literal: Moreover Britain and Denmark have both made agreements—why reject France!"

entries.zh: 總署然之。
entries.en: The Zongli Yamen accepted his view.
entries.literal: The Zongli Yamen agreed with this.

entries.zh: 果不數年而俄約成。
entries.en: Within a few years the agreement with Russia was indeed concluded.
entries.literal: Indeed within a few years the Russian agreement was concluded.

entries.zh: 十八年，除眞。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year (1892) he received confirmation in his substantive post.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was confirmed in substantive appointment.

entries.zh: 滬上織布局廠災，宣懷籌設華盛總廠，復任彌漢冶鐵廠虧耗。
entries.en: After fire destroyed the Shanghai weaving mill, Xuanhuai organized the Huasheng General Mill and again shouldered the Hanyang Ironworks' deficits.
entries.literal: When the Shanghai weaving mill was destroyed by fire, Xuanhuai planned the Huasheng General Mill and also took charge of covering losses at the Hanyang Ironworks.

entries.zh: 於是之洞賞其才，與王文韶交薦之，遂擢四品京堂，督辦鐵路總公司。
entries.en: Zhang Zhidong then admired his ability; he and Wang Wenshao recommended him jointly, and he was raised to fourth-rank capital official and superintendent of the Railway Company.
entries.literal: Thereupon Zhidong admired his talent; he and Wang Wenshao jointly recommended him, and he was promoted to fourth-rank capital official and superintendent of the Railway Company.

entries.zh: 入覲，奏言築路與練兵、理財、育才互爲用，並請開銀行，設達成館，稱旨，補太常寺少卿。
entries.en: At audience he argued that railways, troop training, finance, and education reinforced one another, and asked to open a bank and a Dacheng Hall; the throne was pleased and he was made vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: On audience with the throne he memorialized that railway-building, troop training, financial management, and nurturing talent were mutually reinforcing, and also requested opening a bank and establishing a Dacheng Hall; the emperor was pleased and he was made vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 與比訂貸款草約。
entries.en: He signed a draft loan agreement with Belgium.
entries.literal: He concluded a draft loan agreement with Belgium.

entries.zh: 二十四年，詔趣造粵漢路。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year (1898) an edict ordered the Canton–Hankou Railway built without delay.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, an edict urged rapid construction of the Canton-Hankou Railway.

entries.zh: 宣懷建議貸美款歸自辦，具改歸商辦本末以上；
entries.en: Xuanhuai proposed an American loan to bring the line back under Chinese management and submitted a full account of reverting it to merchant operation;
entries.literal: Xuanhuai proposed borrowing American funds to return the line to self-management and submitted a full account of changing it to merchant management;

entries.zh: 而言者盛毀其所爲遲滯，被訶責。
entries.en: but critics loudly attacked his slowness, and he was rebuked.
entries.literal: but critics widely denounced his delays and he was rebuked.

entries.zh: 宣懷具報曲折，上乃慰而勉之。
entries.en: Xuanhuai reported the full circumstances; the throne consoled him and urged him on.
entries.literal: Xuanhuai submitted a detailed report of the circumstances, and the throne consoled and encouraged him.

entries.zh: 宣懷自請解職，仍留京會議洋貨稅則。
entries.en: Xuanhuai asked to be relieved of his post but stayed in the capital to negotiate foreign-goods tariffs.
entries.literal: Xuanhuai requested to resign his post but remained in the capital to confer on foreign goods tariff schedules.

entries.zh: 已而徐桐劾兩局有中飽，適剛毅按事南下，銜命察覆。
entries.en: Soon Xu Tong accused both bureaus of skimming funds; Gangyi was then investigating in the south and was ordered to review the case.
entries.literal: Before long Xu Tong memorialized that both bureaus had embezzlement at the middle level; Gangyi happened to be investigating affairs in the south and was ordered to inspect and report.

entries.zh: 宣懷具以實對，奏上，被溫旨。
entries.en: Xuanhuai answered with the full facts; when his report reached the throne he received a warm edict in reply.
entries.literal: Xuanhuai answered fully with the facts; when the memorial was submitted he received a gracious edict.

entries.zh: 瑞澂，字莘儒，滿洲正黃旗人，大學士琦善孫，將軍恭鏜子。
entries.en: Rui Cheng, whose style name was Xinru, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner, grandson of Grand Secretary Qishan and son of General Gongtang.
entries.literal: Rui Cheng, style name Xinru, was a Plain Yellow Banner Manchu, grandson of Grand Secretary Qishan and son of General Gongtang.

entries.zh: 以貢生官刑部筆帖式，遷主事，調升戶部員外郎。
entries.en: Entering office as a tribute student, he served as a Ministry of Justice clerk, rose to chief secretary, and was transferred to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.
entries.literal: As a tribute student he served as a Ministry of Justice clerk, was promoted to chief secretary, and transferred to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.

entries.zh: 出為九江道，有治聲，移上海道。
entries.en: Posted as Jiujiang daotai, he won a name for good government and was transferred to Shanghai.
entries.literal: He went out as Jiujiang daotai, gained a reputation for good governance, and was moved to Shanghai daotai.

entries.zh: 滬地交涉繁，瑞澂應付縝密，頗負持正名。
entries.en: Shanghai's foreign dealings were complex; Rui Cheng handled them with care and earned a reputation for standing firm.
entries.literal: Shanghai dealings were complex; Rui Cheng responded meticulously and bore a reputation for uprightness.

entries.zh: 尤顓意警政，建總局，廓分區，設學堂，練馬巡，中外交誦其能。
entries.en: He gave special attention to policing: he built a central bureau, mapped districts, founded schools, and trained mounted patrols—praised alike by Chinese and foreigners.
entries.literal: He especially focused on police administration, established a general bureau, divided districts, set up schools, trained mounted patrols—Chinese and foreigners alike praised his ability.

entries.zh: 光緒三十三年，授江西按察使，遷江蘇布政使。
entries.en: In the thirty-third year of Guangxu (1907) he was made Jiangxi judicial commissioner and then Jiangsu administration commissioner.
entries.literal: In the thirty-third year of Guangxu he was appointed Jiangxi judicial commissioner and transferred to Jiangsu administration commissioner.

entries.zh: 時江、浙梟匪蠢動，出沒滬、杭孔道，釀成巨案。
entries.en: Bandit leaders in Jiangsu and Zhejiang were stirring, raiding the Shanghai–Hangzhou corridor and spawning major cases.
entries.literal: At the time Jiang-Zhe bandit chiefs stirred, appearing along the Shanghai-Hangzhou routes and brewing major cases.

entries.zh: 侍郎沈家本建議辦清鄉，朝命瑞澂主蘇、松、太、杭、嘉、湖捕務，六屬文武受節度。
entries.en: Vice Minister Shen Jiaben proposed rural pacification; the court put Rui Cheng in charge of pursuit in Suzhou, Songjiang, Taicang, Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou, with civil and military officials of the six districts under his command.
entries.literal: Vice Minister Shen Jiaben proposed rural pacification; the court ordered Rui Cheng to direct capture affairs in Su, Song, Tai, Hang, Jia, and Hu—the six prefectures' civil and military officials under his command.

entries.zh: 瑞澂添募水師，購置兵輪，仿各國海軍制，編成聯隊。
entries.en: Rui Cheng recruited additional river troops, bought gunboats, modeled foreign naval organization, and formed a combined flotilla.
entries.literal: Rui Cheng added river forces, purchased gunboats, imitated foreign naval organization, and formed a flotilla.

entries.zh: 擒獲巨魁夏竹、林聲為，匪徒斂跡。
entries.en: He captured the ringleaders Xia Zhu and Lin Shengwei, and the bandits fell quiet.
entries.literal: He captured the great chiefs Xia Zhu and Lin Shengwei, and bandits subsided.

entries.zh: 盛宣懷，字杏蓀，江蘇武進人。
entries.en: Sheng Xuanhuai, whose style name was Xingsun, came from Wujin in Jiangsu.
entries.literal: Sheng Xuanhuai, style name Xingsun, was a native of Wujin in Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 以諸生納貲爲主事，改官直隸州知州，累至道員。
entries.en: Having entered office by purchase as a licentiate, he served as a secretary, was later reassigned to prefect of Zhili Subprefecture, and eventually rose to the rank of circuit intendant.
entries.literal: As a licentiate he purchased appointment as a secretary, was reassigned as prefect of Zhili Subprefecture, and rose through successive ranks to circuit intendant.

entries.zh: 嘗贊置輪船招商局，開採湖北煤鐵礦，李鴻章頗信任之。
entries.en: He had helped set up the China Merchants' Steam Navigation Company and develop Hubei's coal and iron mines, and Li Hongzhang placed great confidence in him.
entries.literal: He once assisted in establishing the China Merchants' Steam Navigation Company and in opening Hubei's coal and iron mines; Li Hongzhang trusted him greatly.

entries.zh: 英商擅築鐵軌，首滬逕寶山訖吳淞，上海道數阻，弗聽。
entries.en: British merchants had laid railway track on their own from Shanghai via Baoshan to Wusong; the Shanghai daotai tried repeatedly to stop them, but they paid no heed.
entries.literal: British merchants built railway tracks on their own authority from Shanghai through Baoshan to Wusong; the Shanghai daotai repeatedly obstructed them but they would not listen.

entries.zh: 宣懷與英官梅輝立折辯，償銀二十八萬有奇，始歸於我。
entries.en: Xuanhuai argued the case with the British official Mei Huili, paid compensation of more than 280,000 taels, and only then did the line come back under Chinese control.
entries.literal: Xuanhuai debated with the British official Mei Huili, paid more than 280,000 taels in compensation, and only then did it revert to our side.

entries.zh: 光緒五年，署天津道。
entries.en: In the fifth year of the Guangxu reign (1879), he acted as Tianjin daotai.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu, he served as acting Tianjin daotai.

entries.zh: 時鴻章督畿輔，方嚮新政，以鐵路、電報事專屬宣懷。
entries.en: Li Hongzhang was then supervising Zhili and pushing new policies; he entrusted railway and telegraph affairs entirely to Xuanhuai.
entries.literal: At the time Hongzhang was supervising Zhili, was turning toward new policies, and placed railway and telegraph affairs exclusively in Xuanhuai's hands.

entries.zh: 宣懷以英、丹所設水陸綫漸侵內地，迺集貲設津滬陸綫，建電報學堂，並援萬國公例與爭，始克嚴定條款。
entries.en: Seeing British and Danish land and submarine lines gradually pressing inland, he raised capital for a Tianjin–Shanghai land line, founded a telegraph school, and invoked international law in dispute—only then were the terms firmly fixed.
entries.literal: Because the land and sea lines set up by Britain and Denmark were gradually encroaching on the interior, he raised funds to establish the Tianjin-Shanghai land line, founded a telegraph school, and appealed to international public law in disputes, only then securing strict provisions.

entries.zh: 會訂水綫相接合同，於是與輪船招商同爲商辦兩大局。
entries.en: Once contracts were signed to link the submarine cables, telegraphy and the China Merchants' line stood as the two great merchant-run enterprises of the age.
entries.literal: When a contract was concluded for connecting the submarine lines, these together with the China Merchants' Steam Navigation Company became the two great merchant-managed undertakings.

entries.zh: 八年，英、法、德、美議立萬國電報公司，增造自滬至香港水綫，壟利權。
entries.en: In the eighth year (1882), Britain, France, Germany, and the United States proposed a Universal Telegraph Company and extra Shanghai–Hong Kong cables to corner the profits.
entries.literal: In the eighth year, Britain, France, Germany, and the United States discussed establishing a Universal Telegraph Company and building additional submarine lines from Shanghai to Hong Kong to monopolize profit rights.

entries.zh: 宣懷復勸集華商自設緣海各口陸綫，以絕覬覦。
entries.en: Xuanhuai again urged Chinese merchants to fund land lines at coastal ports, so as to forestall foreign encroachment.
entries.literal: Xuanhuai again urged gathering Chinese merchants to set up land lines at coastal ports to cut off covetous designs.

entries.zh: 武昌兵變，官軍既克漢陽，武昌旦夕下。
entries.en: After the Wuchang mutiny, imperial troops took Hanyang and Wuchang seemed about to fall.
entries.literal: When the Wuchang mutiny broke out, government troops had already taken Hanyang and Wuchang would fall within days.

entries.zh: 而新內閣又成立，總理大臣袁世凱議修和息戰禍，取隆裕太后懿旨，頒示天下，改建國體，於是遜位詔下矣。
entries.en: A new cabinet was formed; Prime Minister Yuan Shikai sought peace to end the war, secured an edict from Empress Dowager Longyu, and proclaimed a change of polity to the empire—and so the abdication decree came down.
entries.literal: Then a new cabinet was formed; Prime Minister Yuan Shikai proposed peace to end the calamity of war, obtained an edict from Empress Dowager Longyu, and promulgated it throughout the realm to change the form of state—and thus the abdication edict was issued.

entries.zh: 潤庠以老瞶辭授讀差，奉懿旨仍照料毓慶宮，給月俸如故，授太保。
entries.en: Runxiang resigned his tutoring post on grounds of age and failing sight; by edict he was still to oversee the Yuqing Palace at his former salary and was made Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: Runxiang, citing age and dim sight, resigned his tutoring post; by imperial edict he was still to oversee the Yuqing Palace, his monthly salary continued as before, and he was appointed Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 越二年，病卒，年七十五，贈太傅，諡文端。
entries.en: Two years later he died of illness at seventy-five; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the posthumous name Wenduan.
entries.literal: Two years later he died of illness, aged seventy-five; he was posthumously appointed Grand Tutor with the posthumous name Wenduan.

entries.zh: 宣統改元，以疾乞休。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Xuantong reign he asked to retire on grounds of illness.
entries.literal: At the change of reign to Xuantong, he requested retirement on grounds of illness.

entries.zh: 三年，復起原官，仍兼總管內務府大臣。
entries.en: In the third year he was recalled to his former posts and again served as Grand Minister of the Internal Affairs Office.
entries.literal: In the third year he was recalled to his former post and still concurrently served as Grand Minister of the Internal Affairs Office.

entries.zh: 及議遜位，世續首讚之。
entries.en: When abdication was discussed, Shi Xu was the first to endorse it.
entries.literal: When abdication was discussed, Shi Xu was first to endorse it.

entries.zh: 太后令磋商優待條件，授太保。
entries.en: The empress dowager ordered negotiations on favorable terms for the abdication and appointed him Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: The empress dowager ordered negotiation of favorable treatment terms and appointed him Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 接修崇陵工程，加太傅。
entries.en: He took charge of repairs to the Chongling Mausoleum and was promoted to Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: He took charge of repairing the Chongling Mausoleum project and was promoted to Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 丁巳復辟，懼禍及，力阻之。
entries.en: During the 1917 restoration he feared he would be implicated and strongly opposed it.
entries.literal: At the 1917 restoration he feared disaster would reach him and strenuously opposed it.

entries.zh: 事變亟，入宿衛，並以殮服自隨。
entries.en: When events turned urgent he entered the palace as night guard and carried burial garments with him.
entries.literal: When events turned urgent, he entered to stand night guard and brought burial garments with him.

entries.zh: 頻年以經費拮据，支持尤苦，纂修德宗實錄，始終其事，及書成，已病不能起矣。
entries.en: Funds were tight year after year and the burden was especially heavy; he saw the Veritable Records of Guangxu through from start to finish, and when the work was done he was too ill to rise.
entries.literal: Year after year with funds tight, support was especially hard; he edited the Veritable Records of Dezong from start to finish, and when the book was finished he was already too ill to rise.

entries.zh: 辛酉年，卒，年六十九。
entries.en: He died in the xinyou year, aged sixty-nine.
entries.literal: In the xinyou year he died, aged sixty-nine.

entries.zh: 贈太師，諡文端。
entries.en: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous name Wenduan.
entries.literal: He was posthumously appointed Grand Preceptor with the posthumous name Wenduan.

entries.zh: 及武昌事起，再入都，用直隸總督陳夔龍薦，以三品京堂候補。
entries.en: When the Wuchang affair broke out, he entered the capital again; on Zhili Governor Chen Kuilong's recommendation he was made a third-rank Beijing official awaiting appointment.
entries.literal: When the Wuchang affair broke out, he entered the capital again; on Zhili Governor Chen Kuilong's recommendation he was made a third-rank Beijing official awaiting appointment.

entries.zh: 旋奉廣東宣慰使之命，粵中已大亂，道梗不得達，遂病嘔血。
entries.en: Soon he received appointment as Guangdong pacification commissioner; Guangdong was already in great disorder, the roads were blocked and he could not reach it, and he fell ill vomiting blood.
entries.literal: Soon he received appointment as Guangdong pacification commissioner; Guangdong was already in great disorder, the roads blocked and he could not reach it, and he fell ill vomiting blood.

entries.zh: 兩至梁格莊叩謁景皇帝暫安之殿，露宿寢殿旁，瞻仰流涕。
entries.en: Twice he went to Lianggezhuang to kowtow before the hall where the Guangxu Emperor temporarily resided, sleeping in the open beside the sleeping hall and gazing up in tears.
entries.literal: Twice he went to Lianggezhuang to kowtow and pay respects at the hall where the Guangxu Emperor temporarily resided, sleeping in the open beside the sleeping hall, gazing up in tears.

entries.zh: 及孝定景皇后升遐，奉安崇陵，恭送如禮，自原留守陵寢，遂命管理崇陵種樹事。
entries.en: When Empress Dowager Xiaoding Jing passed away and was interred at Chongling, he escorted her with full rites; having asked to remain and guard the mausoleum, he was ordered to manage tree-planting at Chongling.
entries.literal: When Empress Dowager Xiaoding Jing passed away and was interred at Chongling, he escorted her with full rites; having himself requested to remain and guard the mausoleum, he was ordered to manage tree-planting at Chongling.

entries.zh: 旋命在毓慶宮行走。
entries.en: Soon he was ordered to serve at the Yuqing Palace.
entries.literal: Soon he was ordered to serve at the Yuqing Palace.

entries.zh: 丁巳復辟，已臥病，強起周旋。
entries.en: At the 1917 restoration he was already bedridden, yet forced himself up to attend to affairs.
entries.literal: At the 1917 restoration he was already bedridden, yet forced himself up to attend to affairs.

entries.zh: 事變憂甚，逾年卒，諡文忠。
entries.en: Deeply grieved by the turn of events, he died the following year and was given the posthumous name Wenzhong.
entries.literal: Deeply grieved by the turn of events, he died the following year, posthumous name Wenzhong.

entries.zh: 拳禍起，兩宮西幸，鼎芬首倡呈進方物之議。
entries.en: When the Boxer calamity broke out and the Empress Dowager and the Emperor fled west, Dingfen was first to propose presenting local tribute products.
entries.literal: When the Boxer calamity arose and the two empress dowagers fled west, Dingfen was first to propose presenting local tribute products.

entries.zh: 初以端方薦，起用直隸州知州；
entries.en: At first, on Duanfang's recommendation, he was recalled as prefect of a Zhili subprefecture;
entries.literal: At first, on Duanfang's recommendation, he was recalled as prefect of a Zhili subprefecture;

entries.zh: 之洞再薦，詔赴行在所，用知府，發湖北，署武昌，補漢陽。
entries.en: Zhidong recommended him again; he was ordered to the imperial retinue, appointed prefect, sent to Hubei, acted as prefect of Wuchang, and was then appointed to Hanyang.
entries.literal: Zhidong recommended him again; he was ordered to proceed to the imperial retinue, appointed prefect, sent to Hubei, acted as prefect of Wuchang, and was then appointed to Hanyang.

entries.zh: 擢安襄鄖荊道、按察使，署布政使。
entries.en: He was promoted to the An-Xiang-Yun-Jing circuit, made surveillance commissioner, and acted as provincial treasurer.
entries.literal: He was promoted to the An-Xiang-Yun-Jing circuit, appointed surveillance commissioner, and acted as provincial treasurer.

entries.zh: 奏請化除滿、漢界限。
entries.en: He memorialized asking that Manchu-Han distinctions be abolished.
entries.literal: He memorialized requesting the abolition of Manchu-Han distinctions.

entries.zh: 三十二年，入覲，面劾慶親王奕劻通賕賄，請月給銀三萬兩以養其廉。
entries.en: In the thirty-second year he came to court and impeached Prince Qing Yikuang to his face for pervasive bribery, asking that he be given a monthly stipend of thirty thousand taels of silver to preserve his integrity.
entries.literal: In the thirty-second year he attended audience at court and in person impeached Prince Qing Yikuang for pervasive bribery, requesting a monthly stipend of thirty thousand taels of silver to preserve his integrity.

entries.zh: 又劾直隸總督袁世凱「權謀邁眾，城府阻深，能諂人又能用人，自得奕劻之助，其權威遂為我朝二百年來滿、漢疆臣所未有，引用私黨，佈滿要津。
entries.en: He also impeached Zhili Governor-General Yuan Shikai: "His schemes surpass all others, his mind is deep and obstructive; he knows how to flatter and how to use men; with Yikuang's backing his authority exceeds anything a Manchu or Han frontier minister has held in our dynasty's two hundred years, and he fills key posts with his private faction.
entries.literal: He also impeached Zhili Governor-General Yuan Shikai: "His schemes surpass the multitude, his mind is deep and obstructive; he can flatter men and also employ men; since gaining Yikuang's help, his authority has become what no Manchu or Han frontier minister in our dynasty's two hundred years has possessed; he fills key posts with his private faction.

entries.zh: 我皇太后、皇上或未盡知，臣但有一日之官，即盡一日之心。
entries.en: Our empress dowager and emperor may not fully know; yet as long as I hold office for a day, I will give my whole heart for that day.
entries.literal: Our empress dowager and emperor may not fully know; as long as this subject holds office for a day, he will give his heart for a day.

entries.zh: 言盡有淚，淚盡有血。
entries.en: When his words ran out, there were tears; when his tears ran out, there was blood.
entries.literal: When words were exhausted there were tears; when tears were exhausted there was blood.

entries.zh: 奕劻、世凱若仍不悛，臣當隨時奏劾，以報天恩」。
entries.en: If Yikuang and Shikai still do not repent, I shall memorialize impeachment whenever the occasion arises, to repay heaven's grace."
entries.literal: If Yikuang and Shikai still do not repent, this subject will memorialize impeachment at any time, to repay heaven's grace."

entries.zh: 詔訶責，引疾乞退。
entries.en: An edict rebuked him; he cited illness and begged to retire.
entries.literal: An edict rebuked him; he cited illness and begged to retire.

entries.zh: 兩宮升遐，奔赴哭臨，越日即行，時之洞在樞垣，不一往謁也。
entries.en: When the Empress Dowager and the Emperor passed away, he rushed to attend the mourning rites and left the next day; Zhidong was then in the Grand Council, yet Dingfen did not once go to pay his respects.
entries.literal: When the two empress dowagers passed away, he rushed to attend mourning rites and departed the next day; at the time Zhidong was in the Grand Council, yet he did not once go to pay respects.

entries.zh: 明年，聞之洞喪，親送葬南皮。
entries.en: The next year, on hearing of Zhidong's death, he personally escorted the funeral to Nanpi.
entries.literal: The next year, hearing of Zhidong's death, he personally escorted the funeral to Nanpi.

entries.zh: 世續，字伯軒，索勒豁金氏，隸內務府滿洲正黃旗。
entries.en: Shi Xu, whose courtesy name was Boxuan, belonged to the Suoluhojin clan and was registered with the Internal Affairs Office in the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Shi Xu, courtesy name Boxuan, of the Suoluhojin clan, was registered with the Internal Affairs Office in the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 光緒元年舉人，以議敘主事歷內務府郎中，擢武備院卿，授內閣學士。
entries.en: He passed the provincial examination in the first year of Guangxu, rose through the Internal Affairs Office from clerk to director, was promoted to Director of the Armory, and became a Grand Secretariat academician.
entries.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he passed the provincial examination as juren; by merit he rose from clerk to director in the Internal Affairs Office, was promoted to Director of the Armory, and appointed Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

entries.zh: 二十二年，為總管內務府大臣，兼工部侍郎。
entries.en: In the twenty-second year he was made Grand Minister of the Internal Affairs Office and concurrently Vice Minister of Works.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year he became Grand Minister of the Internal Affairs Office and concurrently Vice Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 二十六年，各國聯軍入京，兩宮西狩，適遭父喪，命留京辦事。
entries.en: In the twenty-sixth year, when the allied powers entered Beijing and the Empress Dowager and the Emperor fled west, he was mourning his father and was ordered to stay in the capital to manage affairs.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when the allied armies of various nations entered Beijing and the two empress dowagers fled west, he happened to be mourning his father and was ordered to remain in the capital to handle affairs.

entries.zh: 即日縗墨詣聯軍請保護宮廷​​，日為宮中備飲饌，並保壇廟。
entries.en: That same day, still in mourning dress, he went to the allied commanders to seek protection for the palace, supplied the court with food daily, and guarded the altars and temples.
entries.literal: That very day, wearing mourning garb, he went to the allied forces to request protection for the palace, daily provisioned food and drink for the court, and protected the altars and temples.

entries.zh: 晉理籓院尚書，調禮部。
entries.en: He was promoted to Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs and then transferred to the Ministry of Rites.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs and transferred to the Ministry of Rites.

entries.zh: 兩宮回鑾，賞黃馬褂，轉吏部，兼都統。
entries.en: When the Empress Dowager and the Emperor returned, he was given the yellow riding jacket, moved to the Ministry of Personnel, and also served as banner general.
entries.literal: When the two empress dowagers returned, he was awarded the yellow riding jacket, transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and served concurrently as banner general.

entries.zh: 內務府三旗甲米向歸吏胥代領折價，名曰「米折」，所得甚微。
entries.en: Grain stipends for the three Internal Affairs banners had long been collected by clerks at cut rates under the name "rice conversion," leaving the recipients very little.
entries.literal: The grain stipends for the three banners under the Internal Affairs Office had long been collected for them by clerks at discounted rates under the name "rice conversion," yielding very little.

entries.zh: 世續商之倉場，飭旗丁自領，眾感實惠。
entries.en: Shi Xu arranged with the granary that banner soldiers collect their grain in person, to everyone's real benefit.
entries.literal: Shi Xu negotiated with the granary office and ordered banner soldiers to collect in person; the people were grateful for the real benefit.

entries.zh: 纂呈四書圖說，特旨褒嘉。
entries.en: He compiled and presented Illustrated Explanations of the Four Books and received special imperial praise.
entries.literal: He compiled and presented Illustrated Explanations of the Four Books and received special imperial commendation.

entries.zh: 三十年，以吏部尚書協辦大學士，尋授體仁閣大學士。
entries.en: In the thirtieth year, as Minister of Personnel he became Associate Grand Secretary and soon Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Brilliance.
entries.literal: In the thirtieth year, as Minister of Personnel he was made Associate Grand Secretary, and soon received appointment as Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Brilliance.

entries.zh: 三十二年，命為軍機大臣。
entries.en: In the thirty-second year he was appointed to the Grand Council.
entries.literal: In the thirty-second year he was appointed Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 歷轉文華殿大學士，充憲政編查館參預政務大臣。
entries.en: He was later transferred to Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall and served as a minister with responsibility for government affairs on the Constitutional Research Commission.
entries.literal: He was transferred in succession to Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall and served as Minister with responsibility for government affairs under the Constitutional Research Office.

entries.zh: 念八旗生計日艱，奏設工藝廠，俾習工藝贍身家。
entries.en: Seeing banner livelihoods grow harder by the day, he memorialized to open craft workshops so bannermen could learn trades to support their families.
entries.literal: Concerned that banner livelihoods were growing daily more strained, he memorialized to establish craft workshops so they could learn trades to support their families.

entries.zh: 德宗崩，議繼體，世續獨言國事艱危，宜立長君，不能用。
entries.en: When Emperor Guangxu died and succession was debated, Shi Xu alone urged that in such peril an older ruler should be chosen; his advice was rejected.
entries.literal: When Emperor Dezong died and succession was debated, Shi Xu alone argued that with the state in peril an elder ruler should be installed; his view was not adopted.

entries.zh: 陸潤庠，字鳳石，江蘇元和人。
entries.en: Lu Runxiang, whose courtesy name was Fengshi, came from Yuanhe in Jiangsu.
entries.literal: Lu Runxiang, courtesy name Fengshi, was a native of Yuanhe district in Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 父懋修，精醫，見藝術傳。
entries.en: His father Maoxiu was an accomplished physician; he is treated in the Biography of Arts and Techniques.
entries.literal: His father Maoxiu was skilled in medicine; see the Biography of Arts and Techniques.

entries.zh: 潤庠，同治十三年一甲一名進士，授修撰。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year of the Tongzhi reign, Runxiang took first place in the top tier of the jinshi examination and was made a Hanlin Compiler.
entries.literal: Runxiang, in the thirteenth year of Tongzhi, placed first in the first class of metropolitan graduates and was appointed Hanlin Compiler.

entries.zh: 光緒初，屢典試事，湖南、陝西皆再至。
entries.en: In the early Guangxu years he was repeatedly appointed chief examiner, serving twice each in Hunan and Shaanxi.
entries.literal: Early in Guangxu he repeatedly served as chief examiner; he went twice each to Hunan and Shaanxi.

entries.zh: 入直南書房，洊擢侍讀。
entries.en: He was posted to the Southern Library and in time was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting.
entries.literal: He entered service in the Southern Library and was promoted in due course to Reader-in-Waiting.

entries.zh: 出督山東學政。
entries.en: He was dispatched as educational commissioner of Shandong.
entries.literal: He was sent out as educational commissioner of Shandong.

entries.zh: 父憂服闋，再遷祭酒，典試江西。
entries.en: After completing mourning for his father, he was again made Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and presided over the examinations in Jiangxi.
entries.literal: When his father's mourning period ended, he was again promoted to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and served as chief examiner in Jiangxi.

entries.zh: 以母疾乞養歸。
entries.en: When his mother fell ill, he asked leave to care for her and went home.
entries.literal: On account of his mother's illness he requested leave to nurse her and returned home.

entries.zh: 二十四年，起補祭酒，擢內閣學士，署工部侍郎。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year he was recalled as Chancellor, promoted to Grand Secretariat academician, and acted as Vice Minister of Works.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was recalled to fill the post of Chancellor, promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat, and served concurrently as Vice Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 兩宮西巡，奔赴行在，授禮部侍郎，充經筵講官。
entries.en: When the Empress Dowager and the Emperor fled west, he hurried to join the court in exile, was named Vice Minister of Rites, and became a lecturer at the imperial classics lecture.
entries.literal: When the Empress Dowager and the Emperor toured westward, he rushed to the imperial retinue, was appointed Vice Minister of Rites, and served as lecturer at the classics lecture.

entries.zh: 擢左都御史，管理醫局，典順天鄉試，充會試副總裁，署工部尚書。
entries.en: He was raised to Left Censor-in-Chief, put in charge of the Medical Bureau, presided over the Shuntian provincial exams, served as deputy chief examiner for the metropolitan finals, and acted as Minister of Works.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief, managed the Medical Bureau, presided over the Shuntian provincial examination, served as associate chief examiner for the palace examination, and acted as Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 又代陳典學事宜，略言：「伏讀雍正三年世宗憲皇帝諭：'帝王禦宇膺圖，咸資典學。'
entries.en: He also submitted a memorial on classical learning on another's behalf, stating in brief: "I have read with reverence the edict of the Xian Emperor Shizong in the third year of Yongzheng: 'When an emperor takes the realm and receives the mandate, he must rely on classical learning.'
entries.literal: He also memorialized on matters of classical learning on another's behalf, stating in brief: "Having read reverently the edict of the Xian Emperor Shizong in the third year of Yongzheng: 'When emperors hold the realm and receive the mandate, all rely on classical learning.'

entries.zh: 我聖祖仁皇帝天亶聰明，而好古敏求，六十餘年孜孜不倦。
entries.en: Our Sage Ancestor the Benevolent Emperor was gifted with heaven's intelligence, yet loved antiquity and sought learning with keen diligence—for more than sixty years he never flagged.
entries.literal: Our Sage Ancestor the Benevolent Emperor was heaven-endowed with intelligence, yet loved antiquity and pursued learning keenly, for more than sixty years never slackening.

entries.zh: 又喜慶二十四年仁宗睿皇帝：'帝王之學，在於貫徹天人，明體達用，以見諸施行，與經生尋章索句者不同。'
entries.en: And in the twenty-fourth year of Jiaqing, the Sage Emperor Renzong said: 'The emperor's learning must unite Heaven and man, grasp principle and put it to use, and be seen in what is actually done—it is not the same as scholars who hunt through chapters for isolated lines.'
entries.literal: And in the twenty-fourth year of Jiaqing, the Sage Emperor Renzong said: 'The emperor's learning lies in penetrating Heaven and man, clarifying principle and achieving practical use, making it visible in conduct—different from classicists who hunt passages and seek phrases.'

entries.zh: 仰見列聖相承，重視典學之至意。
entries.en: Thus one sees, with reverence, how successive sage emperors handed down their deepest intent to honor classical learning.
entries.literal: One sees reverently how successive sages inherited one another's utmost intent to value classical learning.

entries.zh: 我皇上睿哲性成，聰明天縱，衝齡踐祚，洪業肇基，當此春秋典學之時，實為聖敬日躋之始，伏維監國攝政王薰陶德性，輔養聖躬，慎選侍從，左右將護，亦既淵衝翕受，法戒靡遺。
entries.en: Our Emperor is wise and sagacious by nature, bright with heaven's gift; he ascended the throne in tender years, the great enterprise only just begun. At this season of youth and classical study, it is truly the beginning of daily ascent in sagely reverence. The regent prince overseeing the realm has shaped his moral nature, nurtured the imperial person, chosen attendants with care, and guarded him on every side—the young emperor has already absorbed it all, and no lesson or warning has been spared.
entries.literal: Our Emperor is by nature wise and sagacious, heaven-talented and bright; ascending the throne at a tender age, with the great enterprise newly begun, at this time of spring years and classical learning it is truly the beginning of daily advance in sagely reverence; I consider that the regent prince overseeing the realm has nurtured his moral nature, assisted in raising the imperial person, carefully chosen attendants, and guarded him on every side—already the deep child has received it all, and no lesson or warning has been lost.

entries.zh: 唯是皇上一念之張弛，系萬機之治忽；
entries.en: Yet a single moment's slackening or tightening in the emperor's mind bears upon whether the myriad affairs of state flourish or fail;
entries.literal: Only the emperor's single thought of looseness or tautness ties to the rise or neglect of the myriad affairs of state;

entries.zh: 一朝之規制，系薄海之觀瞻。
entries.en: a court's institutions bear upon how all beneath the seas regard the throne.
entries.literal: a court's institutions tie to the gaze of all within the seas.

entries.zh: 有不得不慎之又慎者，謹為我皇上詳晰陳之：一，請崇聖學。
entries.en: Some things must be guarded with redoubled care; I respectfully set them out in detail for Our Emperor: First, I ask that sagely learning be exalted.
entries.literal: There are matters where one cannot but be ever more cautious; respectfully for Our Emperor I state them in detail: First, please exalt sagely learning.

entries.zh: 易端蒙養，禮重師教，書述遜敏，詩頌緝熙，聖學精微，非尋常科學範圍之所能及。
entries.en: The Changes begins with early nurture, the Rites honors the teacher's instruction, the Documents speaks of humility and quickness, the Odes praises bright harmony—sagely learning is subtle and profound, beyond the reach of ordinary branches of study.
entries.literal: The Changes begins with early nurture, the Rites honors the teacher's instruction, the Documents describes humility and quickness, the Odes praises bright harmony—sagely learning is subtle and fine, beyond what ordinary branches of learning can reach.

entries.zh: 宋儒有言'帝王之學，與儒生異尚'，與我仁宗睿皇帝典學之諭用意正符。
entries.en: Song scholars said that 'the emperor's learning pursues a different end from that of the Confucian scholar'—words that match exactly the intent of Our Sage Emperor Renzong's edict on classical learning.
entries.literal: Song scholars said, 'The emperor's learning differs in aim from that of the Confucian scholar,' which matches exactly the intent of Our Sage Emperor Renzong's edict on classical learning.

entries.zh: 今我皇上典學之初，應定教學科目，自應會通今古，融貫中西，不可拘於舊例。
entries.en: Now, at the outset of Our Emperor's classical studies, the curriculum ought to be set: it should unite past and present and draw together Chinese and Western learning, and not be confined to old precedent.
entries.literal: Now at the beginning of Our Emperor's classical studies, the subjects of instruction ought to be fixed; they should naturally unite past and present and integrate Chinese and Western learning, and must not be bound by old precedent.

entries.zh: 伏乞簡派儒臣，詳細籌訂，鑑成憲，酌時宜，毋徒陳進講之空文，毋虛循延英之故事，庶足以開張聖聽，裨益亶聰，以立聖學聖治之基。
entries.en: I humbly ask that learned officials be chosen and sent to draw up the plan in detail, taking established precedent as mirror and present needs as measure—neither submitting empty memorials about lectures nor going through the hollow motions of the old Yanying Hall ritual—so that the imperial ear may be opened, heaven's gift sharpened, and the foundation laid for sagely learning and sagely rule.
entries.literal: Humbly begging that Confucian officials be selected and dispatched to plan in detail, taking past statutes as mirror and weighing present needs, neither offering empty memorials of lectures submitted nor hollowly following the old story of the Yanying Hall, so that the imperial ear may be opened and heaven-endowed intelligence enriched, laying the foundation for sagely learning and sagely rule.

entries.zh: 一，請擇賢傅。
entries.en: Second, I ask that worthy tutors be chosen.
entries.literal: Second, please select worthy tutors.

entries.zh: 舊制師傅向以大臣選充，期於老成典型，成就君德，然或入官從政，講學非其所長。
entries.en: Under the old system tutors were usually drawn from among grand ministers, in the hope that seasoned exemplars would complete the ruler's virtue; yet some were men of office and politics, for whom lecturing was not their strength.
entries.literal: Under the old system tutors were generally chosen from among grand ministers, with the hope that mature exemplars would complete the ruler's virtue; yet some entered office and engaged in politics, and lecturing was not their strength.

entries.zh: 老師大儒，潛德隱而勿耀，而教育精深，尤非研究有素，不能取益。
entries.en: Old masters and great scholars keep their hidden virtue from display, yet their teaching runs deep—only those who have long pursued the subject can truly profit from them.
entries.literal: Old masters and great scholars, their hidden virtue concealed and not displayed, yet profound in teaching—benefit cannot be gained unless one has long studied the matter.

entries.zh: 擬請敕下內外大臣，各舉所知，勿拘資格，略仿乾隆十四年詔舉經學人員成例，擇其品端學粹、教育卓著成績者，請旨召用，隆以師傅之任，分門講教，而仍派大臣總司其成，俾專日講於經筵，不必更勞以職事。
entries.en: I propose that ministers at court and in the provinces be ordered each to recommend men they know, without regard to formal qualifications, following roughly the precedent of Qianlong's fourteenth-year edict summoning specialists in classical learning; those of upright character, pure scholarship, and proven teaching merit should be summoned by imperial command, raised to the rank of tutor, and assigned to teach by subject, while a grand minister is still appointed to oversee the whole, so that they may lecture daily at the classics lecture without being further burdened with official duties.
entries.literal: It is proposed to request an order to ministers within and without, each to recommend those they know without being bound by qualifications, roughly following the precedent of the fourteenth year of Qianlong's edict summoning specialists in classical learning; choosing those of upright character, pure learning, and outstanding teaching achievement, begging the throne to summon and employ them, elevating them to the post of tutor, assigning them to teach by subject, while still dispatching a grand minister to oversee the whole, so that they may devote themselves daily to the classics lecture without being further burdened with official duties.

entries.zh: 其任彌專，其責彌重，其效彌速，使天下曉然於尊師崇儒之意，庶儒林有所矜式，而聖德日進高明矣。
entries.en: The more dedicated the post, the heavier the responsibility, the swifter the result—so that all under Heaven may plainly see the intent to honor teachers and exalt Confucian learning; then the scholarly community will have a model to revere, and sagely virtue will daily rise to greater heights.
entries.literal: The more dedicated the post, the heavier the responsibility, the swifter the effect—so that all under Heaven clearly understand the intent to honor teachers and exalt Confucian learning; then the Confucian community will have a model to admire, and sagely virtue will daily advance to greater heights.

entries.zh: 一，請肅​​規制。
entries.en: Third, I ask that regulations be tightened.
entries.literal: Third, please tighten regulations.

entries.zh: 古者聖王教冑，必選端方正直、道術博聞之士，與之居處，是以習與智長，化與心成。
entries.en: In antiquity, when sage kings instructed the heir, they chose men upright and learned in the Way to dwell with him—so that habit grew with wisdom and transformation took root in the heart.
entries.literal: In antiquity when sage kings taught the heir, they always chose men upright and straight, broad in the Way and learned, to dwell with him—thus habit grew with wisdom, and transformation was completed in the heart.

entries.zh: 我皇上毓德方新，始基宜固，舊制選派內監伴讀，似不足以肅學製而廣箴規。
entries.en: Our Emperor's moral cultivation has only just begun, and the foundation ought to be made firm; the old practice of assigning eunuchs as reading companions seems insufficient to give the school system proper gravity or to broaden the scope of admonition.
entries.literal: Our Emperor's moral cultivation is newly begun and the foundation ought to be firm; the old system of selecting eunuchs as reading companions seems insufficient to tighten the school system and broaden admonition.

entries.zh: 擬請改選王公大臣之賢子弟昕夕侍從，斅學相長，並參考學校制度，建設講堂，陳列圖書彝器，觀摩肄習，以收敬業樂群之效。
entries.en: I propose instead that worthy sons of princes, dukes, and grand ministers be chosen to attend morning and evening, learning from one another; and, drawing on school institutions, that lecture halls be built, books and ritual vessels displayed, and study observed and practiced together, to achieve reverent devotion to learning and delight in good company.
entries.literal: It is proposed to request instead the selection of worthy sons of princes, dukes, and grand ministers to attend morning and evening, learning from one another; also, with reference to school institutions, to build lecture halls, display books and ritual vessels, and observe and practice together, to achieve the effect of reverent devotion to study and delight in good company.

entries.zh: 以上三事，僅舉大綱。
entries.en: These three matters set forth only the main outline.
entries.literal: The three matters above merely set forth the main outline.

entries.zh: 我皇上今日之言動起居，罔有勿敬，即異日之立政敷教，罔有勿臧，此尤根本之至計，不可不謹之於漸，而慎之於始者也。
entries.en: Our Emperor's words, conduct, and daily life today are without anything irreverent; likewise, when he later establishes policy and spreads instruction, nothing will be amiss—this above all is the root plan, which must be guarded from the first and watched from the very beginning.
entries.literal: Our Emperor's words, conduct, and daily life today are without anything un-reverent; likewise his future establishment of policy and spreading of instruction will be without anything un-good—this above all is the root plan, which cannot but be guarded gradually and cautioned at the beginning.

entries.zh: 伏念朝廷廣勵人才，振興教育，侁侁學子，爭自濯磨，皇上典學伊始，益宜宏茲遠謨，以慰天下士民之望。」
entries.en: Reflecting that the court broadly encourages talent and revives education, and eager students everywhere strive to refine themselves, at the very outset of the emperor's classical studies it is all the more fitting to expand this far-reaching design and satisfy the hopes of scholars and common people throughout the realm."
entries.literal: Reflecting that the court broadly encourages talent and revives education, and eager students everywhere strive to polish themselves, at the very outset of the emperor's classical studies it is all the more fitting to expand this far-reaching design, to satisfy the hopes of scholars and people throughout the realm."

entries.zh: 世凱卒，各省有所謀，群集徐州，推勳主盟。
entries.en: After Yuan's death, as provincial leaders began scheming in various directions, they assembled at Xuzhou and made Zhang Xun their chief.
entries.literal: After Yuan Shikai died, when the provinces were plotting various schemes, they gathered at Xuzhou and chose Zhang Xun to lead the alliance.

entries.zh: 勳於是提兵北上，叩謁宮門，遂復闢。
entries.en: Zhang then marched north with his troops, paid homage at the palace gates, and effected the restoration of the monarchy.
entries.literal: Zhang Xun thereupon led his army north, knelt at the palace gate seeking audience, and thus restored the throne.

entries.zh: 連下詔令，首頒复政諭云：「朕不幸以沖齡繼承大業，煢煢在疚，未堪多難。
entries.en: A series of edicts followed, opening with a proclamation on the restoration of rule: "Having inherited the vast inheritance in my minority, I stand solitary and stricken, scarcely fit to weather further disasters.
entries.literal: Edicts were issued in succession; the first was the restoration proclamation, which read: "We unfortunately inherited the great enterprise in tender years, alone and burdened with cares, unable to bear many calamities.

entries.zh: 辛亥變起，我孝定景皇后至德深仁，不忍生民塗炭，毅然以祖宗創垂之重，億兆生靈之命，付託前閣臣袁世凱，設臨時政府，推讓政權，公諸天下，冀以息爭弭亂，民得安居。
entries.en: When the Xinhai revolution broke out, Empress Dowager Xiaoding, in her deep virtue and compassion, could not bear to see the people brought to ruin. She resolutely entrusted the ancestral enterprise and the fate of the multitudes to the former grand councillor Yuan Shikai, set up a provisional government, and yielded power to the nation, hoping to still contention and restore peace so the people could live securely.
entries.literal: The Xinhai uprising arose; Our Empress Dowager Xiaoding, of surpassing virtue and profound benevolence, could not bear to see the people suffer ravage; she resolutely entrusted the heavy legacy left by our ancestors and the lives of hundreds of millions to the former Grand Councillor Yuan Shikai, established a provisional government, and yielded political power to the world, hoping thereby to quell strife and end chaos so the people might live in peace.

entries.zh: 乃國體自改共和以來，紛爭無已，迭起干戈，強劫暴斂，賄賂公行，歲入增至四萬萬而仍患不足，外債增出十餘萬萬而有加無已。
entries.en: Yet since the nation adopted republican government, conflict has never ceased, wars have broken out again and again, armed robbery and violent exactions have spread, bribery runs unchecked, annual revenue has climbed to four hundred million yuan yet still falls short, and foreign debt has swollen by more than a billion with no limit in sight.
entries.literal: Yet since the state changed to a republic, strife has been unceasing, wars have arisen in succession, armed robbery and violent exactions prevail, bribery is openly practiced, annual revenue has risen to four hundred million yet still proves insufficient, and foreign debt has increased by more than a billion with no end in sight.

entries.zh: 海內囂然，喪其樂生之氣，使我孝定景皇后不得已遜政恤民之舉，轉以重苦吾民。
entries.en: The realm has grown turbulent, and the people's will to live in peace has been broken; the very act by which Empress Dowager Xiaoding reluctantly abdicated to spare the people has instead deepened their affliction.
entries.literal: Within the seas all is clamorous; the people's will to live in peace is lost; the act by which Our Empress Dowager Xiaoding reluctantly yielded rule to spare the people has instead redoubled their suffering.

entries.zh: 此誠我孝定景皇后初衷所不及料，在天之靈，惻痛難安；
entries.en: This was truly beyond what Empress Dowager Xiaoding could have foreseen in her original intent; her spirit in Heaven must ache with unbearable sorrow;
entries.literal: This was truly beyond what Our Empress Dowager Xiaoding's original intent could foresee; her spirit in Heaven must ache with unbearable sorrow;

entries.zh: 而朕深居宮禁，日夜禱天，徬徨飲泣，不知所出者也。
entries.en: while I, deep within the palace confines, pray to Heaven day and night, wander in distress and weep, and know not what course to take.
entries.literal: while We, deep within the palace confines, pray to Heaven day and night, wander in distress and weep, and know not what course to take.

entries.zh: 今者復以黨爭激成兵禍，天下洶洶，久莫能定，共和解體，補救已窮。
entries.en: Now party strife has again ignited military disaster; the realm has been in turmoil for so long that order cannot be restored; the republic has disintegrated, and every remedy has been exhausted.
entries.literal: Now party strife has again stirred up military disaster; the realm is in turmoil and long unable to settle; the republic has disintegrated and remedies are exhausted.

entries.zh: 據張勛等以『國本動搖，人心思舊，合詞奏請復闢，以拯生靈』，各等語。
entries.en: According to Zhang Xun and others, who jointly memorialized that "the foundation of the state is shaken, the people's hearts yearn for the old order, and we beg restoration of the throne to save the people," and similar statements.
entries.literal: According to Zhang Xun and others, who jointly memorialized that "the foundation of the state is shaken, the people's hearts yearn for the old order, and we beg restoration of the throne to save the living," and similar words.

entries.zh: 覽奏，情詞懇切，實深痛懼。
entries.en: On reading the memorial, I found its language earnest and was deeply pained and fearful.
entries.literal: On reading the memorial, its language is earnest and We are deeply pained and fearful.

entries.zh: 既不敢以天下存亡之大責，遂輕任於眇躬；
entries.en: I dare not lightly take upon my slight person the great responsibility for the survival of the realm;
entries.literal: We dare not lightly take upon Our slight person the great responsibility for the survival of the realm;

entries.zh: 又不忍以一姓禍福之讏言，置兆民於不顧。
entries.en: yet I cannot bear, on account of words concerning the fortune of one house, to abandon the millions of the people.
entries.literal: yet We cannot bear, on account of words concerning the fortune of one surname, to abandon the millions of the people.

entries.zh: 權衡重輕，天人交迫，不得已允如所奏，於宣統九年1917年五月十三日臨朝聽政，收回大權，與民更始。
entries.en: Weighing what matters most, pressed by Heaven and men alike, I have no choice but to grant the request as memorialized; on the thirteenth day of the fifth month in the ninth year of Xuantong (1917) I shall attend court and resume rule, reclaim supreme authority, and make a new beginning with the people.
entries.literal: Weighing what is heavy and light, pressed by Heaven and men alike, We have no choice but to grant the request as memorialized; on the thirteenth day of the fifth month in the ninth year of Xuantong (1917) We shall attend court and resume rule, reclaim great authority, and make a new beginning with the people.

entries.zh: 自今以往，以綱常名教為精神之憲法，以禮義廉恥收潰決之人心。
entries.en: From this time forward, let the bonds of human relations and moral teaching serve as the spiritual constitution, and let propriety, righteousness, integrity, and shame gather up the dissolving hearts of the people.
entries.literal: From this time forward, let the bonds of human relations and moral teaching serve as the spiritual constitution, and let propriety, righteousness, integrity, and shame gather up the dissolving hearts of the people.

entries.zh: 上下以至誠相感，不徒恃法守為維繫之資；
entries.en: Above and below shall be moved by utmost sincerity toward one another, and shall not rely solely on observance of law as the means of cohesion;
entries.literal: Above and below shall be moved by utmost sincerity toward one another, and shall not rely solely on observance of law as the means of cohesion;

entries.zh: 政令以懲毖為心，不得以國本為嘗試之具。
entries.en: government orders shall take correction and discipline as their aim, and the foundation of the state must not be treated as an instrument for experiment.
entries.literal: government orders shall take correction and discipline as their aim, and the foundation of the state must not be treated as an instrument for experiment.

entries.zh: 況當此萬象虛耗，元氣垂竭，存亡絕續之交，朕臨深履薄，固不敢有樂為君，稍有縱逸。
entries.en: Moreover, at this moment when all things are drained hollow and vital force is near exhaustion, at the juncture between survival and extinction, I stand over the abyss and tread on thin ice; I truly dare not take pleasure in being ruler or indulge in the slightest laxity.
entries.literal: Moreover, at this moment when all things are drained hollow and vital force is near exhaustion, at the juncture between survival and extinction, We stand over the abyss and tread on thin ice; We truly dare not take pleasure in being ruler or indulge in the slightest laxity.

entries.zh: 爾大小臣工，尤當精白乃心，滌除舊染，息息以民瘼為念。
entries.en: You ministers great and small must especially purify your hearts, wash away old stains, and at every breath keep the people's afflictions in mind.
entries.literal: You ministers great and small must especially purify your hearts, wash away old stains, and at every breath keep the people's afflictions in mind.

entries.zh: 為民生留一分元氣，即為國家延一息命脈，庶幾危亡可救，感召天庥。
entries.en: To preserve for the people's livelihood one portion of vital force is to extend for the state one breath of its life-thread; then perhaps ruin may be averted and Heaven's blessing be drawn down.
entries.literal: To preserve for the people's livelihood one portion of vital force is to extend for the state one breath of its life-thread; then perhaps ruin may be saved and Heaven's blessing be drawn down.

entries.zh: 所有興復初政亟應興革諸大端，條舉如下：*欽遵德宗景皇帝諭旨，大權統於朝廷，庶政公諸輿論，定為大清帝國君主立憲政體。
entries.en: All major points urgently to be enacted or reformed at the beginning of restored rule are listed as follows: In reverent obedience to the edict of Emperor Guangxu, supreme authority shall be unified in the court and ordinary administration referred to public opinion; the form of government is fixed as a constitutional monarchy of the Great Qing Empire.
entries.literal: All major points urgently to be enacted or reformed at the beginning of restored rule are listed as follows: * In reverent obedience to the edict of Emperor Dezong Jing, supreme authority shall be unified in the court and ordinary administration referred to public opinion; the form of government is fixed as a constitutional monarchy of the Great Qing Empire.

entries.zh: *皇室經費，仍照所定每年四百萬元數目，按年撥用，不得絲毫增加。
entries.en: Imperial household expenses shall still follow the fixed annual sum of four million yuan, disbursed year by year, and must not be increased in the slightest.
entries.literal: * Imperial household expenses shall still follow the fixed annual sum of four million yuan, disbursed year by year, and must not be increased in the slightest.

entries.zh: *懍遵本朝祖制，親貴不得乾預政事。
entries.en: In reverent observance of this dynasty's ancestral institutions, members of the imperial clan and nobility must not interfere in government affairs.
entries.literal: * In reverent observance of this dynasty's ancestral institutions, members of the imperial clan and nobility must not interfere in government affairs.

entries.zh: *實行融化滿、漢畛域，所有以前一切滿、蒙官缺已經裁撤者，概不復設。
entries.en: Manchu and Han boundaries shall be dissolved in practice; all Manchu and Mongol official posts previously abolished shall in no case be re-established.
entries.literal: * Manchu and Han boundaries shall be dissolved in practice; all Manchu and Mongol official posts previously abolished shall in no case be re-established.

entries.zh: 至通婚易俗等事，並著所司條議具奏。
entries.en: As for matters such as intermarriage and changing customs, the responsible offices are also ordered to draft detailed proposals and memorialize.
entries.literal: As for matters such as intermarriage and changing customs, the responsible offices are also ordered to draft detailed proposals and memorialize.

entries.zh: *自宣統九年五月本日以前，凡與東西各國正式簽定條約，及已付債款合同，一律繼續有效。
entries.en: All treaties formally concluded with Eastern and Western countries before this day in the fifth month of the ninth year of Xuantong, and all debt contracts already paid, shall remain in force without exception.
entries.literal: * All treaties formally concluded with Eastern and Western countries before this day in the fifth month of the ninth year of Xuantong, and all debt contracts already paid, shall remain in force without exception.

entries.zh: *民國所行印花稅一項，應即廢止，以紓民困；
entries.en: The stamp tax instituted by the Republic shall be abolished at once to relieve the people's hardship;
entries.literal: * The stamp tax instituted by the Republic shall be abolished at once to relieve the people's hardship;

entries.zh: 其餘苛細雜捐，並著各省督撫查明，奏請分別裁撤。
entries.en: other harsh and petty miscellaneous levies are also to be investigated by the governors of each province and memorialized for separate abolition.
entries.literal: other harsh and petty miscellaneous levies are also to be investigated by the governors of each province and memorialized for separate abolition.

entries.zh: *民國刑律不適國情，應即廢除，暫以宣統初年頒定現行刑律為準。
entries.en: The criminal code of the Republic does not suit national conditions and shall be abolished at once; for the present the current criminal code promulgated in the early Xuantong period shall serve as the standard.
entries.literal: * The criminal code of the Republic does not suit national conditions and shall be abolished at once; for the present the current criminal code promulgated in the early Xuantong period shall serve as the standard.

entries.zh: *禁除黨派惡習，其從前政治罪犯，概予赦免；
entries.en: Party faction and its evil practices are forbidden; all former political offenders are granted amnesty in general;
entries.literal: * Party faction and its evil practices are forbidden; all former political offenders are granted amnesty in general;

entries.zh: 儻有自棄於民而擾亂治安者，朕不敢赦。
entries.en: if any abandon themselves before the people and disturb public order, I dare not pardon them.
entries.literal: if any abandon themselves before the people and disturb public order, We dare not pardon them.

entries.zh: *凡我臣民，無論已否剪髮，應遵照宣統三年九月諭旨，悉聽其便。
entries.en: All my subjects, whether or not they have cut their hair, shall follow the edict of the ninth month of the third year of Xuantong and be left entirely to their own choice.
entries.literal: * All Our subjects, whether or not they have cut their hair, shall follow the edict of the ninth month of the third year of Xuantong and be left entirely to their own choice.

entries.zh: 先後命官以勳及陳寶琛、劉廷琛等為內閣議政大臣，次則內閣閣丞萬繩栻、胡嗣瑗，大學士為瞿鴻禨、升允，顧問大臣趙爾巽、陳夔龍、張英麟、馮煦等，各部尚書梁敦彥、張鎮芳、雷震春、沈曾植、勞乃宣等，侍郎李經邁、李瑞清、陳曾壽、王乃徵、陳毅、顧瑗等，丞參辜湯生、章梫、黎湛枝、梁用弧等，都御史張曾敡，副都御史胡思敬、溫肅；
entries.en: Offices were appointed in succession: Zhang Xun and Chen Baochen, Liu Tingchen, and others as cabinet deliberative ministers; next, cabinet vice directors Wan Shengqi and Hu Siyuan; grand secretaries Qu Hongji and Sheng Yun; advisory ministers Zhao Erxun, Chen Kuilong, Zhang Yinglin, Feng Xu, and others; ministers of the various boards Liang Dunyan, Zhang Zhenfang, Lei Zhenchun, Shen Zengzhi, Lao Naixuan, and others; vice ministers Li Jingmai, Li Ruiqing, Chen Zengshou, Wang Naizheng, Chen Yi, Gu Yuan, and others; assistant councillors Gu Tangsheng, Zhang Qin, Li Zhanzhi, Liang Yonghu, and others; censor-in-chief Zhang Ceng'e; vice censor-in-chief Hu Sijing and Wen Su;
entries.literal: Offices were appointed in succession: Zhang Xun and Chen Baochen, Liu Tingchen, and others as cabinet deliberative ministers; next, cabinet vice directors Wan Shengqi and Hu Siyuan; grand secretaries Qu Hongji and Sheng Yun; advisory ministers Zhao Erxun, Chen Kuilong, Zhang Yinglin, Feng Xu, and others; ministers of the various boards Liang Dunyan, Zhang Zhenfang, Lei Zhenchun, Shen Zengzhi, Lao Naixuan, and others; vice ministers Li Jingmai, Li Ruiqing, Chen Zengshou, Wang Naizheng, Chen Yi, Gu Yuan, and others; assistant councillors Gu Tangsheng, Zhang Kun, Li Zhanzhi, Liang Yonghu, and others; censor-in-chief Zhang Ceng'e; vice censor-in-chief Hu Sijing and Wen Su;

entries.zh: 並召鄭孝胥、吳慶坻、趙啟霖及陳邦瑞、硃益籓等均來京。
entries.en: Zheng Xiaoxu, Wu Qingdi, Zhao Qilin, Chen Bangrui, Zhu Yifan, and others were also summoned to the capital.
entries.literal: Zheng Xiaoxu, Wu Qingdi, Zhao Qilin, Chen Bangrui, Zhu Yifan, and others were also summoned to the capital.

entries.zh: 又以勳兼直隸總督、北洋大臣，仍留京。
entries.en: Zhang Xun was also made concurrent governor-general of Zhili and Beiyang minister, yet remained in the capital.
entries.literal: Zhang Xun was also made concurrent governor-general of Zhili and Beiyang minister, yet remained in the capital.

entries.zh: 各省督、撫、提、鎮，皆就現任者改之。
entries.en: The governors, provincial governors, military governors, and commanders of each province were all reassigned from among those currently in office.
entries.literal: The governors, provincial governors, military governors, and commanders of each province were all reassigned from among those currently in office.

entries.zh: 命下，各省多不應，而馬廠師起，稱討逆軍，傳檄討勳，勳自請罷斥。
entries.en: When the orders were issued, most provinces did not respond; then the army at Machang rose, styled itself the army to suppress rebellion, and issued a proclamation against Zhang Xun; Zhang asked to be dismissed.
entries.literal: When the orders were issued, most provinces did not respond; then Duan Qirui's army rose at Mafang, styled itself the army to suppress rebellion, and issued a proclamation against Zhang Xun; Zhang Xun asked to be dismissed.

entries.zh: 及攻都城，勳與戰，以兵寡不支，荷蘭公使以車迎入使館​​。
entries.en: When they attacked the capital, Zhang fought them; his forces were too few to hold; the Dutch minister received him in a carriage into the legation.
entries.literal: When they attacked the capital, Zhang Xun fought them; his forces were few and could not hold; the Dutch minister received him in a carriage into the legation.

entries.zh: 旋赴津，居久之，卒，年七十，諡忠武。
entries.en: He soon went to Tianjin, lived there a long while, and died at the age of seventy; his posthumous title was Zhongwu.
entries.literal: He soon went to Tianjin, lived there a long while, and died at the age of seventy; his posthumous title was Zhongwu.

entries.zh: 勳亢爽好客，待士卒有恩，所部數万人，無一斷髮者，世指為「辮子軍」。
entries.en: Zhang was bold and open, hospitable to guests, and gracious to his soldiers; among his command of tens of thousands, not one had cut his queue, and the world called them the "Queue Army."
entries.literal: Zhang Xun was bold and open, hospitable to guests, and gracious to his soldiers; among his command of tens of thousands, not one had cut his queue, and the world called them the "Queue Army."

entries.zh: 臨戰，盡納家屬妻妾子女別室，不聽避，蓋自懟負國，誓骨肉俱殉。
entries.en: On the eve of battle he gathered all his household—wives, concubines, and children—into separate quarters and would not let them flee, for he blamed himself for failing the state and swore that flesh and blood would perish together.
entries.literal: On the eve of battle he gathered all his household—wives, concubines, and children—into separate quarters and would not let them flee, for he blamed himself for failing the state and swore that flesh and blood would perish together.

entries.zh: 及事亟，外人破戶劫之始脫云。
entries.en: When matters grew desperate, foreigners broke in and plundered the house before they escaped.
entries.literal: When matters grew desperate, foreigners broke in and plundered the house before they escaped.

entries.zh: 康有為，字廣廈，號更生，原名祖詒，廣東南海人。
entries.en: Kang Youwei, whose style name was Guangxia and sobriquet Gengsheng, was originally named Zuyi and came from Nanhai in Guangdong.
entries.literal: Kang Youwei, style name Guangxia, sobriquet Gengsheng, original name Zuyi, was a native of Nanhai in Guangdong.

entries.zh: 光緒二十一年進士，用工部主事。
entries.en: In the twenty-first year of Guangxu, a jinshi, he served as a secretary in the Ministry of Works.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year of Guangxu, a jinshi, he served as a secretary in the Ministry of Works.

entries.zh: 少從硃次琦遊，博通經史，好公羊家言，言孔子改制，倡以孔子紀年，尊孔保教，先聚徒講學。
entries.en: In youth he studied under Zhu Ciqi, mastered the classics and histories broadly, favored the Gongyang school, spoke of Confucius's institutional reforms, advocated dating by Confucius's era, honored Confucius and protected the teaching, and first gathered disciples to lecture.
entries.literal: In youth he followed Zhu Ciqian in study, mastered the classics and histories broadly, favored the Gongyang school, spoke of Confucius's institutional reforms, advocated dating by Confucius's era, honored Confucius and protected the teaching, and first gathered disciples to lecture.

entries.zh: 入都上萬言書，議變法，給事中餘聯沅劾以惑世誣民，非聖無法，請焚所著書。
entries.en: On entering the capital he submitted a ten-thousand-word memorial advocating reform; the supervising secretary Yu Lianyuan memorialized against him for deluding the age and deceiving the people, for rejecting the sage and lacking law, and requested that his writings be burned.
entries.literal: On entering the capital he submitted a ten-thousand-word memorial advocating reform; the supervising secretary Yu Lianyuan memorialized against him for deluding the age and deceiving the people, for rejecting the sage and lacking law, and requested that his writings be burned.

entries.zh: 中日議款，有為集各省公車上書，請拒和、遷都、變法，格不達。
