entries.en: When the Sino-Japanese peace terms were negotiated, Kang gathered provincial examination candidates to submit a joint memorial requesting rejection of peace, transfer of the capital, and reform; it did not reach the throne.
entries.literal: When the Sino-Japanese peace terms were negotiated, Kang gathered provincial examination candidates to submit a joint memorial requesting rejection of peace, transfer of the capital, and reform; it did not reach the throne.

entries.zh: 复獨上書，由都察院代遞，上覽而善之，命錄存備省覽。
entries.en: He again submitted a memorial alone, forwarded through the Censorate; the emperor read it and approved, ordering it copied and kept for reference.
entries.literal: He again submitted a memorial alone, forwarded through the Censorate; the emperor read it and approved, ordering it copied and kept for reference.

entries.zh: 再請誓群臣以定國是，開制度局​​以議新制，別設法律等局以行新政，均下總署議。
entries.en: He again requested that the ministers swear an oath to fix the national policy, open a Bureau of Institutions to discuss new systems, and separately establish bureaus for law and the like to carry out new policies; all were referred to the Zongli Yamen for deliberation.
entries.literal: He again requested that the ministers swear an oath to fix the national policy, open a Bureau of Institutions to discuss new systems, and separately establish bureaus for law and the like to carry out new policies; all were referred to the Zongli Yamen for deliberation.

entries.zh: 上雖親政，遇事仍承太后意旨，久感外侮，思變法圖強，用有為言，三月維新，中外震仰。
entries.en: Although the emperor personally ruled, in affairs he still followed the empress dowager's intent; long feeling foreign humiliation, he thought to reform and strengthen the state, adopted Kang's words, and for three months carried out the Hundred Days' Reform, astonishing court and country alike.
entries.literal: Although the emperor personally ruled, in affairs he still followed the empress dowager's intent; long feeling foreign humiliation, he thought to reform and strengthen the state, adopted Kang's words, and for three months carried out the Hundred Days' Reform, astonishing court and country alike.

entries.zh: 唯新進驟起，機事不密，遂致害成。
entries.en: Only the newly risen advanced too swiftly, affairs were not kept secret, and disaster was thereby brought to completion.
entries.literal: Only the newly risen advanced too swiftly, affairs were not kept secret, and disaster was thereby brought to completion.

entries.zh: 時傳將以兵圍頤和園劫太后，人心惶惑。
entries.en: At the time it was rumored that troops would surround the Summer Palace to seize the empress dowager, and hearts were alarmed and unsettled.
entries.literal: At the time it was rumored that troops would surround the Summer Palace to seize the empress dowager, and hearts were alarmed and unsettled.

entries.zh: 上硃諭銳等籌議調和，有「朕位且不能保」之語，語具銳傳。
entries.en: The emperor issued an vermilion rescript to Yang Rui and others to plan reconciliation; it contained the words "even my throne cannot be preserved," which are recorded in Yang's biography.
entries.literal: The emperor issued an vermilion rescript to Yang Rui and others to plan reconciliation; it contained the words "even Our throne cannot be preserved," which are recorded in Yang's biography.

entries.zh: 於是太后复垂簾，盡罷新政。
entries.en: Thereupon the empress dowager again ruled from behind the curtain and abolished all the new policies.
entries.literal: Thereupon the empress dowager again ruled from behind the curtain and abolished all the new policies.

entries.zh: 以有為結黨營私，莠言亂政，褫職逮捕。
entries.en: Kang was charged with forming factions for private gain and wicked words disturbing government; his office was stripped and he was ordered arrested.
entries.literal: Kang was charged with forming factions for private gain and wicked words disturbing government; his office was stripped and he was ordered arrested.

entries.zh: 有為先走免，逮其弟廣仁及楊銳等下獄，並處斬。
entries.en: Kang fled first and escaped; his younger brother Guangren and Yang Rui and others were seized and imprisoned, and all were executed.
entries.literal: Kang fled first and escaped; his younger brother Guangren and Yang Rui and others were seized and imprisoned, and all were executed.

entries.zh: 復以有為大逆不道，構煽陰謀，頒硃諭宣示，並籍其家，懸賞購捕。
entries.en: He was again charged with great treason and fomenting secret plots; a vermilion rescript was promulgated, his household goods were confiscated, and a reward was posted for his capture.
entries.literal: He was again charged with great treason and fomenting secret plots; a vermilion rescript was promulgated, his household goods were confiscated, and a reward was posted for his capture.

entries.zh: 有為已星夜出都航海南下，英國兵艦迎至吳淞。
entries.en: Kang had already fled the capital by night and sailed south by sea; a British warship received him at Wusong.
entries.literal: Kang had already fled the capital by night and sailed south by sea; a British warship received him at Wusong.

entries.zh: 時傳上已幽廢，且被弒，有為草遺言，誓以身殉，將蹈海。
entries.en: At the time it was rumored that the emperor had been secretly deposed and even assassinated; Kang drafted a final testament, swore to die for him, and was about to cast himself into the sea.
entries.literal: At the time it was rumored that the emperor had been secretly deposed and even assassinated; Kang drafted a final testament, swore to die for him, and was about to cast himself into the sea.

entries.zh: 英人告以訛傳，有為始脫走，亡命日本，流轉南洋，遍遊歐、美各國。
entries.en: The English told him it was a false rumor; Kang then escaped, fled to Japan, wandered through the Southern Seas, and traveled throughout Europe and America.
entries.literal: The English told him it was a false rumor; Kang then escaped, fled to Japan, wandered through the Southern Seas, and traveled throughout Europe and America.

entries.zh: 所至以尊皇保國相號召，設會辦報，集貲謀再舉，屢遇艱險不少阻。
entries.en: Wherever he went he rallied people under the banner of honoring the emperor and protecting the state, established societies and ran newspapers, gathered funds to plan another rising, and met many dangers without slackening.
entries.literal: Wherever he went he rallied people under the banner of honoring the emperor and protecting the state, established societies and ran newspapers, gathered funds to plan another rising, and met many dangers without slackening.

entries.zh: 嘗結富有會，起事江漢，皆為官兵破獲，誅其黨。
entries.en: He once formed the Wealthy Society and raised a revolt in the Jianghan region; all were broken up by government troops and his partisans executed.
entries.literal: He once formed the Wealthy Society and raised a revolt in the Jianghan region; all were broken up by government troops and his partisans executed.

entries.zh: 連詔大索，毀所著書，閱其報章者並罪之。
entries.en: The court issued successive edicts ordering a nationwide hunt; his books were destroyed, and even readers of his newspapers were punished.
entries.literal: Edicts were issued in succession ordering a great search; his writings were destroyed, and those who read his newspapers were also punished.

entries.zh: 初，太后議廢帝，稱病徵醫，久閉瀛台，旦夕不測。
entries.en: At first the empress dowager considered deposing the emperor. Physicians were summoned on the pretext of illness; he was long confined on the Ocean Terrace, with his fate uncertain day by day.
entries.literal: At first the empress dowager discussed deposing the emperor; she summoned doctors on the pretext of illness; he was long confined on the Ocean Terrace, his fate uncertain from day to day.

entries.zh: 有為聞之，首發其謀，清議爭阻，外人亦起責言，兩江總督劉坤一言「君臣之分已定，中外之口難防」，始罷廢立。
entries.en: When Kang heard of it he was the first to expose the plot. Qing faction memorialists disputed and blocked it, foreigners also protested, and Liangjiang governor-general Liu Kunyi said, "The bond between sovereign and minister is already settled; opinion at home and abroad cannot be silenced." Only then was the plan to depose him abandoned.
entries.literal: Kang heard of it and was first to expose the plot; Qing faction memorialists disputed and blocked it; foreigners also raised reproaches; Liangjiang governor-general Liu Kunyi said, "The distinction between ruler and minister is already fixed; the mouths at home and abroad are hard to seal," and only then was deposition abandoned.

entries.zh: 拳匪起，以滅洋人、殺新黨為號，太后思用以立威，遂肇大亂，凡與有為往還者，輒以康黨得奇禍。
entries.en: The Boxers rose under the banner of destroying foreigners and killing reformers. The empress dowager hoped to use them to assert her authority, and great chaos followed. Anyone who had dealt with Kang was labeled a Kang partisan and met extraordinary punishment.
entries.literal: The Boxers rose, taking as their banner the extermination of foreigners and the killing of the New Party; the empress dowager thought to use them to establish prestige, and thus great chaos began; all who had dealings with Kang were charged as Kang faction and met extraordinary calamity.

entries.zh: 二十四年，有為立保國會於京師，尚書李端棻，學士徐致靖、張百熙，給事中高燮曾等，先後疏薦有為才，至是始召對。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year Kang established the Society to Protect the State in the capital; Minister Li Duanfen, Academicians Xu Zhijing and Zhang Baixi, Supervising Secretary Gao Xiezeng, and others successively memorialized recommending Kang's talent; only then was he summoned for audience.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Kang established the Society to Protect the State in the capital; Minister Li Duanfen, Academicians Xu Zhijing and Zhang Baixi, Supervising Secretary Gao Xiezeng, and others successively memorialized recommending Kang's talent; only then was he summoned for audience.

entries.zh: 有為極陳：「四夷交侵，覆亡無日，非維新變舊，不能自強。
entries.en: Kang stated urgently: "The four barbarians press in on every side; ruin may come any day; without renewing the old order we cannot make ourselves strong.
entries.literal: Kang stated urgently: "The four barbarians press in on every side; ruin may come any day; without renewing the old order we cannot make ourselves strong.

entries.zh: 變法須統籌全局而行之，遍及用人行政。」
entries.en: Reform must be carried out with the whole situation planned as one, extending to personnel and administration alike."
entries.literal: Reform must be carried out with the whole situation planned as one, extending to personnel and administration alike."

entries.zh: 上歎曰：「奈掣肘何？」
entries.en: The emperor sighed and said: "But what can be done about those who hold me back?"
entries.literal: The emperor sighed and said: "But what can be done about those who hold me back?"

entries.zh: 有為曰：「就皇上現有之權，行可變之事，扼要以圖，亦足救國。
entries.en: Kang said: "With the authority Your Majesty already possesses, carry out what can be changed, seize the essentials and plan accordingly, and that too is enough to save the state.
entries.literal: Kang said: "With the authority Your Majesty already possesses, carry out what can be changed, seize the essentials and plan accordingly, and that too is enough to save the state.

entries.zh: 唯大臣守舊，當廣召小臣，破格擢用；
entries.en: Since the great ministers cling to the old ways, Your Majesty should broadly summon junior officials and promote them beyond precedent;
entries.literal: Since the great ministers cling to the old ways, Your Majesty should broadly summon junior officials and promote them beyond precedent;

entries.zh: 並請下哀痛之詔，收拾人心。」
entries.en: and also issue an edict of heartfelt grief to gather up the people's hearts."
entries.literal: and also issue an edict of heartfelt grief to gather up the people's hearts."

entries.zh: 上皆韙之。
entries.en: The emperor approved all of this.
entries.literal: The emperor approved all of this.

entries.zh: 自辰入，至日昃始退，命在總理衙門章京上行走，特許專擢言事。
entries.en: He entered at the hour of chen and did not withdraw until the sun declined; he was ordered to serve on detached duty as a secretary at the Zongli Yamen and specially permitted to memorialize on his own authority.
entries.literal: He entered at the hour of chen and did not withdraw until the sun declined; he was ordered to serve on detached duty as a secretary at the Zongli Yamen and specially permitted to memorialize on his own authority.

entries.zh: 旋召侍讀楊銳、中書林旭、主事劉光第、知府譚嗣同參預新政。
entries.en: Soon the Hanlin reader Yang Rui, Secretariat drafter Lin Xu, secretary Liu Guangdi, and prefect Tan Sitong were summoned to take part in the new policies.
entries.literal: Soon the Hanlin reader Yang Rui, Secretariat drafter Lin Xu, secretary Liu Guangdi, and prefect Tan Sitong were summoned to take part in the new policies.

entries.zh: 有為連條議以進，於是詔定科舉新章，罷四書文，改試策論，立京師大學堂、譯書局，興農學，獎新書新器，改各省書院為學校，許士民上書言事，諭變法。
entries.en: Kang submitted proposals item by item; thereupon edicts fixed new examination regulations, abolished essays on the Four Books, changed the test to policy essays, established the Imperial University at the capital and a Translation Bureau, promoted agricultural studies, rewarded new books and new devices, converted provincial academies into schools, permitted scholars and commoners to submit memorials, and proclaimed reform.
entries.literal: Kang submitted proposals item by item; thereupon edicts fixed new examination regulations, abolished essays on the Four Books, changed the test to policy essays, established the Imperial University at the capital and a Translation Bureau, promoted agricultural studies, rewarded new books and new devices, converted provincial academies into schools, permitted scholars and commoners to submit memorials, and proclaimed reform.

entries.zh: 裁詹事府、通政司，大理、光祿、太僕、鴻臚諸寺，及各省與總督同城之巡撫，河道總督，糧道、鹽道，並議開懋勤殿，定制度，改元易服，南巡遷都。
entries.en: The Directorate of Education, the Office of Transmission, the Court of Judicature and Revision, the Court of Imperial Entertainments, the Court of the Imperial Stud, the Court of State Ceremonial, and other offices were abolished, along with provincial governors who shared a city with a governor-general, the Grand Canal director-general, grain transport intendant, and salt intendant; it was also proposed to open the Hall of Diligent Government, fix institutions, change the reign title and alter dress, and tour south to transfer the capital.
entries.literal: The Directorate of Education, the Office of Transmission, the Court of Judicature and Revision, the Court of Imperial Entertainments, the Court of the Imperial Stud, the Court of State Ceremonial, and other offices were abolished, along with provincial governors who shared a city with a governor-general, the Grand Canal director-general, grain transport intendant, and salt intendant; it was also proposed to open the Hall of Diligent Government, fix institutions, change the reign title and alter dress, and tour south to transfer the capital.

entries.zh: 未及行，以抑格言路，首違詔旨，盡奪禮部尚書、侍郎職。
entries.en: Before these could be carried out, for obstructing the memorial route and being the first to violate the edict, all ministers and vice ministers of the Ministry of Rites were stripped of office.
entries.literal: Before these could be carried out, for obstructing the memorial route and being the first to violate the edict, all ministers and vice ministers of the Ministry of Rites were stripped of office.

entries.zh: 舊臣疑懼，群起指責有為，御史文悌复痛劾之。
entries.en: Old officials grew suspicious and fearful; they rose together to denounce Kang; Censor Wen Ti again memorialized bitterly against him.
entries.literal: Old officials grew suspicious and fearful; they rose together to denounce Kang; Censor Wen Ti again memorialized bitterly against him.

entries.zh: 上先命有​​為督辦官報，复促出京。
entries.en: The emperor first ordered Kang to supervise the official gazette, then urged him to leave the capital.
entries.literal: The emperor first ordered Kang to supervise the official gazette, then urged him to leave the capital.

entries.zh: 論曰：光、宣兩朝，世變迭起，中國可謂多故矣。
entries.en: The commentator says: Under the Guangxu and Xuantong emperors, upheavals followed one upon another; China may truly be said to have known troubled times.
entries.literal: The commentator says: In the Guangxu and Xuantong reigns, worldly changes arose in succession; China may be said to have had many troubles.

entries.zh: 其事皆分見於紀、傳。
entries.en: These events are all treated separately in the annals and biographies.
entries.literal: These matters are all treated separately in annals and biographies.

entries.zh: 斷代為史，辛亥以後，例不能詳。
entries.en: In a dynastic history, events after Xinhai cannot by rule be treated in full detail.
entries.literal: When history is divided by dynasty, after Xinhai the rule cannot treat matters in detail.

entries.zh: 唯丁巳復辟，甲子移官，實為遜位後兩大案，而勳與有為又與清室相終始，亦不可遂沒其人。
entries.en: Only the dingsi restoration of 1917 and the jiazi palace removal of 1924 were truly the two great cases after abdication. Zhang Xun and Kang Youwei were bound up with the Qing house from first to last, and their lives likewise cannot simply be erased from the record.
entries.literal: Only the dingsi restoration and the jiazi removal of the palace were in truth the two great cases after abdication; Zhang Xun and Kang Youwei moreover shared the Qing house's beginning and end, and their persons likewise cannot simply be erased.

entries.zh: 明末三王及諸遺臣，史皆勿諱，今仿其體，並詳著於篇，庶幾考有清一代之本末者，有所鑑焉。
entries.en: Historians did not conceal the three Ming princes of the late dynasty or their loyalist followers; following that precedent, both men are set forth here in detail, so that those who study the rise and fall of the Qing may find something to reflect upon.
entries.literal: The three princes of the late Ming and the various loyalist subjects are not concealed in history; now following that form, both are set forth in detail in this chapter, so that those who examine the beginning and end of the Qing may have something to reflect upon.

entries.zh: :張彪，字虎臣，山西榆次人。
entries.en: Zhang Biao, whose style name was Huchen, came from Yuci in Shanxi.
entries.literal: Zhang Biao, style name Huchen, was a native of Yuci in Shanxi.

entries.zh: 以武生歸撫標，巡撫張之洞器賞之，擢外委，隨調粵、鄂至兩江。
entries.en: As a military licentiate he joined the Hunan garrison. Governor Zhang Zhidong took notice of him and promoted him to outer deputy; with successive transfers he served in Guangdong, Hubei, and the lower Yangtze region.
entries.literal: As a military licentiate he joined the Hunan garrison banner; Governor Zhang Zhidong valued and appreciated him, promoted him to outer deputy, and with transfers served in Guangdong, Hubei, and Liangjiang.

entries.zh: 時新練陸軍，充管帶，監修江陰江防砲台。
entries.en: When the new army was being trained he served as battalion commander and supervised construction of the Jiangyin Yangtze defense batteries.
entries.literal: When the new army was being trained he served as battalion commander and supervised repair of the Jiangyin Yangtze defense batteries.

entries.zh: 復還湖北，充護軍管帶。
entries.en: He returned to Hubei and served as battalion commander of the guard army.
entries.literal: He returned again to Hubei and served as battalion commander of the guard army.

entries.zh: 光緒二十三年，奏派赴日本考查軍政，歸，督修漢口後湖堤工，創漢陽兵工廠。
entries.en: In the twenty-third year of Guangxu he was sent to Japan to study military administration. On his return he supervised the Hankou rear-lake embankment project and founded the Hanyang arsenal.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year of Guangxu he was memorialized and dispatched to Japan to investigate military administration; on return he supervised repair of the Hankou rear-lake embankment works and founded the Hanyang arsenal.

entries.zh: 累保副將，賞壯勇巴圖魯勇號，兼常備軍鎮統，授松潘總兵，留充陸軍第八軍鎮統制官。
entries.en: Through repeated commendations he rose to vice general, was granted the valiant title Batulu, commanded a standing army brigade, was appointed commander at Songpan, and retained as commander of the Eighth Army Division.
entries.literal: Through repeated commendations he rose to vice general, was awarded the valiant title Batulu, concurrently commanded a standing army brigade, was appointed commander at Songpan, and retained as commander of the Eighth Army Division of the army.

entries.zh: 南北新軍會操於彰德，賞花翎；
entries.en: When northern and southern new armies held joint maneuvers at Zhangde, he was awarded the peacock feather;
entries.literal: Northern and southern new armies held joint maneuvers at Zhangde; he was awarded the peacock feather;

entries.zh: 再會操太湖，更勇號曰奇穆欽。
entries.en: at a second maneuver on Lake Tai his valiant title was changed to Qimuchin.
entries.literal: at a second maneuver at Taihu his valiant title was changed to Qimuchin.

entries.zh: 宣統二年，擢湖北提督，加陸軍副都統。
entries.en: In the second year of Xuantong he was promoted to military governor of Hubei and given the additional rank of vice commander of the army.
entries.literal: In the second year of Xuantong he was promoted to Hubei military governor and given the additional rank of vice commander of the army.

entries.zh: 三年，新軍變，總督瑞澂棄城走，彪率衛隊巷戰，自夜至日午，不能支，退召水師。
entries.en: In the third year the New Army mutinied. Governor Ruicheng abandoned the city and fled. Biao led his guard in street fighting from night until noon, could not hold, and withdrew to summon the naval forces.
entries.literal: In the third year the New Army mutinied; Governor Ruicheng abandoned the city and fled; Biao led his guard in street fighting from night until noon, could not hold, withdrew and summoned the naval forces.

entries.zh: 瑞澂劾以構變潛逃，詔革職，圖後效。
entries.en: Ruicheng accused him of fomenting the mutiny and fleeing in secret. An edict stripped his office while reserving hope for future merit.
entries.literal: Ruicheng memorialized against him for fomenting the mutiny and fleeing in secret; an edict stripped his office while reserving hope for future merit.

entries.zh: 复充湘豫鄂援軍總司令，率殘軍保漢口。
entries.en: He again served as commander-in-chief of the Hunan-Henan-Hubei relief army, leading remnant forces to defend Hankou.
entries.literal: He again served as commander-in-chief of the Hunan-Henan-Hubei relief army, leading remnant forces to hold Hankou.

entries.zh: 禁衛軍及北洋軍南下，督隊先驅，屢有克捷。
entries.en: When the Imperial Guard and Beiyang armies marched south, he led the vanguard and won repeated victories.
entries.literal: The Imperial Guard and Beiyang armies marched south; he directed the vanguard and repeatedly won victories.

entries.zh: 既复漢陽，還原官。
entries.en: After Hanyang was recovered, his original office was restored.
entries.literal: After Hanyang was recovered, his original office was restored.

entries.zh: 官軍請改共和，要彪署名，力欲之，遂稱病去。
entries.en: When the government army sought to adopt a republic and demanded Biao's signature, he firmly refused and resigned on grounds of illness.
entries.literal: The government army requested conversion to a republic and demanded Biao's signature; he strenuously refused and thereupon pleaded illness and resigned.

entries.zh: 東渡日本，歸寓津，築張園自隱。
entries.en: He went to Japan, then returned to Tianjin, where he built Zhang Garden and lived in seclusion.
entries.literal: He crossed east to Japan, returned to lodge at Tianjin, and built Zhang Garden to live in seclusion.

entries.zh: 乙丑，迎蹕駐園，供張服用，夙夜唯勤。
entries.en: In the yichou year he received the imperial procession at his garden, supplied furnishings and provisions, and served diligently from dawn to dusk.
entries.literal: In the yichou year he received the imperial procession lodging at the garden, supplied furnishings and provisions, and from dawn to dusk was diligent alone.

entries.zh: 丁卯秋，病篤，見駕臨視，已不能起，強啟目含淚而逝，年六十八。
entries.en: In the autumn of dingmao his illness grew grave. The emperor came in person to visit, but he could no longer rise. He forced his eyes open, tears streaming, and died at the age of sixty-eight.
entries.literal: In the autumn of dingmao his illness grew grave; the emperor came in person to visit; he could no longer rise; he forced his eyes open, tears in them, and died at the age of sixty-eight.

entries.zh: 張勛，字少軒，江西奉新人。
entries.en: Zhang Xun, whose style name was Shaoxuan, came from Fengxin in Jiangxi.
entries.literal: Zhang Xun, style name Shaoxuan, was a native of Fengxin in Jiangxi.

entries.zh: 少孤貧。
entries.en: He lost his parents early and grew up in poverty.
entries.literal: In youth he was orphaned and poor.

entries.zh: 投效廣西軍，預法越之戰，累保至參將。
entries.en: He joined the Guangxi forces, fought in the Sino-French War, and was repeatedly promoted until he reached the rank of colonel.
entries.literal: He enlisted in the Guangxi army, took part in the Sino-French War, and through repeated commendations rose to the rank of colonel.

entries.zh: 日韓釁啟，隨毅軍防守奉天。
entries.en: When the conflict between Japan and Korea erupted, he served with the Yiji Army in the defense of Fengtian.
entries.literal: When trouble broke out between Japan and Korea, he followed the Yiji Army to defend Fengtian.

entries.zh: 袁世凱練兵小站，充管帶。
entries.en: When Yuan Shikai raised his new army at Xiaozhan, Zhang served as a battalion commander.
entries.literal: When Yuan Shikai trained troops at Xiaozhan, he served as a battalion commander.

entries.zh: 拳匪亂作，統巡防營防剿，敘功擢副將，賞壯勇巴圖魯。
entries.en: During the Boxer rebellion he led defensive battalions in pacification campaigns and, his achievements recorded, was promoted to vice general and granted the title Valiant Batulu.
entries.literal: When the Boxer uprising broke out, he commanded garrison defense battalions in suppression operations; for his merit he was promoted to vice general and awarded the title Valiant Batulu.

entries.zh: 兩宮回鑾，隨扈至京，諭留宿衛，授建昌鎮總兵，擢雲南提督，改甘肅，皆不赴。
entries.en: When the court returned to Beijing, Zhang escorted the imperial party and was told to remain on palace guard duty. He was named commander at Jianchang, then offered the posts of military governor of Yunnan and Gansu in turn, but he declined them all.
entries.literal: When the two palaces returned to the capital, he escorted them to Beijing; he was ordered to remain on palace guard duty, appointed commander at Jianchang, promoted to Yunnan provincial military governor, then reassigned to Gansu—he accepted none of these posts.

entries.zh: 日俄戰後，調奉天，充行營翼長，節制三省防軍，賞黃馬褂。
entries.en: After the Russo-Japanese War he was posted to Fengtian as deputy chief of the field headquarters with authority over the defense forces of three provinces, and was granted a yellow riding jacket.
entries.literal: After the Russo-Japanese War he was transferred to Fengtian, served as deputy chief of the field headquarters, controlled the defense forces of three provinces, and was awarded a yellow jacket.

entries.zh: 旋命總統江防各軍，駐浦口，調江南提督。
entries.en: He was soon placed in command of all Yangtze river defense forces, headquartered at Pukou, and appointed military governor of Jiangnan.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to command all Yangtze defense forces, stationed at Pukou, and transferred to Jiangnan military governor.

entries.zh: 孔廕植，字對寰，孔子六十五代孫，世居曲阜。
entries.en: Kong Yinzhi, whose style was Duihuan, was a sixty-fifth-generation descendant of Confucius and came from a family that had long lived in Qufu.
entries.literal: Kong Yinzhi, style name Duihuan, was a sixty-fifth-generation descendant of Confucius whose family had long resided in Qufu.

entries.zh: 明天啟初，襲封衍聖公。
entries.en: Early in the Ming Tianqi reign, he inherited the dukedom of Yansheng.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign of the Ming, he inherited the title Duke Yansheng.

entries.zh: 清順治元年，世祖定鼎京師，山東巡撫方大猷疏言開國之初，首宜尊崇先聖。
entries.en: In the first year of Shunzhi, after the Founding Emperor had fixed the capital at Beijing, Shandong governor Fang Dayou submitted a memorial arguing that at the founding of a dynasty the ancient sage ought to be honored first.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi of the Qing, when the Founding Emperor established the capital at Beijing, the Shandong provincial governor Fang Dayou memorialized that at the opening of a dynasty one should first honor the ancient sage.

entries.zh: 下禮部議，衍聖公爵及其官屬，悉循明舊制。
entries.en: The case was sent to the Ministry of Rites, which ruled that the Duke Yansheng and his entire staff should continue under the Ming arrangements unchanged.
entries.literal: The matter was referred to the Ministry of Rites for deliberation; the Duke Yansheng and all his subordinate officials were to follow entirely the former Ming regulations.

entries.zh: 廕植朝京師，遣官迎勞。
entries.en: When Yinzhi traveled to the capital, the court sent officials to welcome him and attend to his comfort.
entries.literal: When Yinzhi came to the capital, officials were dispatched to welcome and comfort him.

entries.zh: 入朝，班列大學士上，賜宴，恩禮有加。
entries.en: At court he was placed in the procession above the grand secretaries, given a banquet, and treated with exceptional courtesy.
entries.literal: On entering court he was ranked above the grand secretaries, was granted a banquet, and received added favor and ceremony.

entries.zh: 四年，卒，遣山東布政使致祭。
entries.en: He died in the fourth year, and the Shandong provincial administration commissioner was dispatched to offer sacrifice on his behalf.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he died; the Shandong provincial administration commissioner was sent to perform the sacrifice.

entries.zh: 子興燮襲。
entries.en: His son Xing Xie succeeded to the title.
entries.literal: His son Xing Xie succeeded.

entries.zh: 毓圻，字鐘在。
entries.en: Yu Qi, whose style was Zhongzai.
entries.literal: Yu Qi, style name Zhongzai.

entries.zh: 方幼，年十一，朝京師。
entries.en: Still a child, he went to the capital at the age of eleven.
entries.literal: While still young, at age eleven, he came to the capital.

entries.zh: 聖祖召見瀛台，禮度如成人，奏對稱旨。
entries.en: The Kangxi Emperor received him at Yingtai; he conducted himself with the poise of a grown man, and everything he said in audience pleased the throne.
entries.literal: The Holy Ancestor summoned him to an audience at Yingtai; his deportment was like that of an adult, and his replies to the throne accorded with the Emperor's intent.

entries.zh: 越二年，上幸學，召毓圻陪祀，太皇太后召入見，賜坐，問家世，具以對，賜茶及克食。
entries.en: Two years later, when the Emperor attended the Imperial Academy rites, Yu Qi was called to assist at the sacrifice. The Grand Empress Dowager summoned him in, gave him a seat, and asked about his lineage; he answered at length, and she granted him tea and provisions for the road.
entries.literal: Two years later, when the Emperor visited the Imperial Academy, Yu Qi was summoned to assist at the sacrifice; the Grand Empress Dowager summoned him in for an audience, granted him a seat, inquired about his family history, and he answered in full detail; she bestowed tea and traveling provisions.

entries.zh: 辭出，命內臣送至宮門外，傳諭從官善輔翼之。
entries.en: As he withdrew, she ordered palace eunuchs to escort him to the outer gate and sent word that his attendants should guide and support him carefully.
entries.literal: When he took leave to withdraw, she ordered inner attendants to escort him to the palace gate; an edict was transmitted instructing his attendants to guide and support him well.

entries.zh: 上御殿，毓圻從諸大臣朝參，及退，命自御道行，逡巡辭，上敦諭之，乃趨出。
entries.en: When the Emperor held audience, Yu Qi joined the senior ministers in obeisance; as they withdrew, the Emperor told him to use the imperial path. He hesitated and demurred, but the Emperor pressed him firmly, and he then hurried out.
entries.literal: When the Emperor held court, Yu Qi followed the great ministers in paying homage; when they retired, the Emperor ordered him to walk by the imperial roadway; hesitating, he declined, but the Emperor urged him earnestly, whereupon he hastened out.

entries.zh: 加太子少師。
entries.en: He was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 二十三年，上東巡，釋奠孔子廟，留曲柄黃蓋。
entries.en: In the twenty-third year the Emperor toured the east, offered libation at the Temple of Confucius, and left behind a curved-handled yellow imperial canopy as a mark of honor.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year the Emperor made an eastern tour, performed the libation sacrifice at the Temple of Confucius, and left behind a curved-handled yellow canopy.

entries.zh: 謁林，週覽遺跡，每事問，毓圻謹以對。
entries.en: He visited the Kong Forest and went through the historic sites, questioning him on each point; Yu Qi answered with scrupulous care.
entries.literal: He visited the Kong Forest, surveyed the historic sites all around, and questioned him on every matter; Yu Qi answered with care.

entries.zh: 因請擴林地，置守衛，除租賦，設百戶，官秩視衛守備，皆許之。
entries.en: He then asked to enlarge the forest estate, post guards, lift rent and tax obligations, and establish a corps of a hundred households with rank equivalent to a garrison commandant; the Emperor approved every request.
entries.literal: Thereupon he requested expansion of the forest grounds, establishment of guards, exemption from rent and tax, and the setting up of a hundred households, with official rank equal to a garrison commandant; all were granted.

entries.zh: 毓圻輯幸魯盛典以進，復奏請重修孔子廟，白巡撫及河道總督，免縣人河工應役。
entries.en: Yu Qi edited the account of the imperial visit to Lu and presented it to the throne. He also memorialized for the rebuilding of the Confucius temple, secured the support of the provincial governor and the Grand Canal director-general, and obtained exemption for the people of the county from river-labor corvée.
entries.literal: Yu Qi compiled the record of the Emperor's visit to Lu and presented it; he also memorialized requesting reconstruction of the Temple of Confucius, informed the provincial governor and the Grand Canal director-general, and secured exemption for county people from corvée on river works.

entries.zh: 雍正元年，世宗命追封先聖五代王爵。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongzheng, the Yongzheng Emperor ordered that five generations of the ancient sage be ennobled posthumously as kings.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng the Shizong Emperor ordered posthumous ennoblement of the ancient sage's five generations as kings.

entries.zh: 十月，毓圻詣闕謝，疾作，上命醫診視，賜參餌。
entries.en: In the tenth month Yu Qi came to court to offer thanks; he fell ill, and the Emperor ordered physicians to attend him and sent ginseng as medicine.
entries.literal: In the tenth month Yu Qi came to court to give thanks; illness seized him; the Emperor ordered physicians to examine him and bestowed ginseng medicine.

entries.zh: 十一月，卒於京師，上遣內大臣奠茶酒。
entries.en: In the eleventh month he died in the capital; the Emperor sent an inner grand minister to offer libations of tea and wine.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month he died in the capital; the Emperor dispatched an inner grand minister to offer libations of tea and wine.

entries.zh: 喪歸，命皇三子及莊親王允祿臨奠，行人護行，賜葬，諡恭愨。
entries.en: When his coffin returned home, the Emperor ordered the third imperial son and Prince Zhuang Yunlu to attend the mourning, sent officials to escort the procession, granted state burial, and gave him the posthumous title Gongque.
entries.literal: When the coffin returned home, the Emperor ordered the third imperial son and Prince Zhuang Yunlu to attend the mourning rites, officials to escort the procession, granted burial honors, and conferred the posthumous title Gongque.

entries.zh: 毓圻工書，愛蘭，自號曰蘭堂。
entries.en: Yu Qi was accomplished in calligraphy, loved orchids, and took the sobriquet Orchid Hall.
entries.literal: Yu Qi was skilled at calligraphy, loved orchids, and styled himself the Orchid Hall.

entries.zh: 子傳鐸襲。
entries.en: His son Chuan Duo succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Chuan Duo succeeded.

entries.zh: 廣棨，字京立。
entries.en: Guang Qi, whose style was Jingli.
entries.literal: Guang Qi, style name Jingli.

entries.zh: 雍正初，授二品冠服，襲爵。
entries.en: Early in the Yongzheng reign he was granted second-rank court dress and inherited the title.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng he was granted second-rank court dress and succeeded to the title.

entries.zh: 以孔林工竟，率族人詣闕謝。
entries.en: When the Kong Forest project was finished, he led the clan to court to offer thanks.
entries.literal: Because work on the Kong Forest had been completed, he led the clan to court to give thanks.

entries.zh: 上御圓明園正大光明殿，召入對，命坐賜茶，諭曰：「汝為先聖後，當存聖賢心，行聖賢事，秉禮守義，以驕奢為戒。
entries.en: The Emperor received him in the Hall of Rectitude and Brightness at the Old Summer Palace, summoned him for audience, had him seated, and granted tea. He instructed him: "As a descendant of the ancient sage, you must keep the sages' heart, do the sages' deeds, hold to ritual and righteousness, and guard against pride and luxury.
entries.literal: The Emperor held audience in the Hall of Rectitude and Brightness in the Old Summer Palace, summoned him for an interview, ordered him to be seated and granted tea, and instructed him, saying: "You are a descendant of the ancient sage; you should keep the heart of the sages, perform the deeds of the sages, uphold ritual and guard righteousness, and take pride and extravagance as your warning.

entries.zh: 汝年方少，尤宜勤學讀書，敦品勵行，與汝族人相勸戒，相砥礪，為端人正士。」
entries.en: You are still very young, and should study and read all the more diligently, cultivate your character, encourage one another among your kinsmen, and become upright, principled men."
entries.literal: You are still very young; you should all the more study diligently and read books, cultivate character and encourage conduct, and with your clansmen admonish and restrain one another, polish one another, and become upright gentlemen."

entries.zh: 廣棨頓首謝。
entries.en: Guang Qi kowtowed in thanks.
entries.literal: Guang Qi bowed his head in thanks.

entries.zh: 賜松花江石硯及錦幣，賜宴，遣歸。
entries.en: He was given a Songhua River inkstone and brocade silks, entertained at banquet, and sent home.
entries.literal: He was granted an inkstone of Songhua River stone and brocade silks, given a banquet, and sent home.

entries.zh: 十三年，世宗崩，入臨。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year the Yongzheng Emperor died, and he came to the capital to mourn.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year the Shizong died; he entered the capital to mourn.

entries.zh: 高宗復召入對，以覃恩贈父繼濩如其爵。
entries.en: The Qianlong Emperor summoned him again for audience and, under a general amnesty, posthumously ennobled his father Jihuo to the same rank as his own title.
entries.literal: The Gaozong Emperor again summoned him for an audience; because of a general amnesty his father Jihuo was posthumously ennobled to the same rank as his own title.

entries.zh: 乾隆三年，上幸學，召廣棨陪祀。
entries.en: In the third year of Qianlong the Emperor visited the Imperial Academy and summoned Guang Qi to assist at the sacrifice.
entries.literal: In the third year of Qianlong the Emperor visited the Imperial Academy and summoned Guang Qi to assist at the sacrifice.

entries.zh: 獻親耕耤田頌、視學大禮慶成賦。
entries.en: He presented an ode on the Emperor's ceremonial plowing of the sacred field and a fu celebrating the completion of the imperial school visit.
entries.literal: He presented an ode on the Emperor's plowing of the sacred field and a fu on the completion of the great ceremony of the imperial school visit.

entries.zh: 四年，朝京師，祝上萬壽。
entries.en: In the fourth year he came to the capital to congratulate the Emperor on his longevity.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he came to the capital to congratulate the Emperor on his birthday.

entries.zh: 會舉經筵，令侍班，因奏請著為令。
entries.en: When the classics lecture was convened, he was ordered to attend in the lecturing corps and memorialized that the practice be made permanent.
entries.literal: When the classics lecture was held, he was ordered to attend in the lecturing corps; he thereupon memorialized requesting that this be made a standing regulation.

entries.zh: 六年，疏劾曲阜知縣毓琚不職，毓琚亦訐廣棨居鄉不法，下巡撫按治，上原廣棨而譴毓琚。
entries.en: In the sixth year he memorialized against Qufu magistrate Yu Ju for dereliction of duty. Yu Ju in turn accused Guang Qi of misconduct at home. The case was sent to the provincial governor for investigation; the Emperor excused Guang Qi and punished Yu Ju.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he memorialized impeaching Qufu magistrate Yu Ju for malfeasance; Yu Ju also denounced Guang Qi for unlawful conduct in his home district; the matter was sent to the governor for investigation; the Emperor excused Guang Qi and censured Yu Ju.

entries.zh: 八年，卒。
entries.en: He died in the eighth year.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he died.

entries.zh: 子昭煥襲。
entries.en: His son Zhao Huan succeeded.
entries.literal: His son Zhao Huan succeeded.

entries.zh: 傳鐸，字振路。
entries.en: Chuan Duo, whose style was Zhenlu.
entries.literal: Chuan Duo, style name Zhenlu.

entries.zh: 康熙間賜二品冠服，襲爵後一年，世宗幸學，召傳鐸陪祀。
entries.en: During the Kangxi reign he was granted second-rank court dress. One year after inheriting the title, when the Yongzheng Emperor visited the Imperial Academy, Chuan Duo was summoned to assist at the sacrifice.
entries.literal: During the Kangxi reign he was granted second-rank court dress; one year after succeeding to the title, when the Shizong visited the Imperial Academy, Chuan Duo was summoned to assist at the sacrifice.

entries.zh: 傳鐸老，病足，命其子繼溥代行禮。
entries.en: Chuan Duo was elderly and lame; the Emperor ordered his son Jibo to perform the rites on his behalf.
entries.literal: Chuan Duo was old and afflicted in the feet; the Emperor ordered his son Jibo to perform the rites in his stead.

entries.zh: 六月，孔子廟災，傳鐸用明弘治間故事，率族人素服三日哭，疏引咎，上遣侍郎王景曾祭告。
entries.en: In the sixth month the Temple of Confucius caught fire. Chuan Duo followed the Ming Hongzhi precedent, led the clan in mourning dress for three days of weeping, and submitted a self-reproach memorial; the Emperor sent Vice Minister Wang Jingceng to announce the sacrifice.
entries.literal: In the sixth month the Temple of Confucius suffered a fire; Chuan Duo followed the precedent of the Hongzhi reign of the Ming, led the clan in plain dress for three days of weeping, and submitted a memorial taking blame upon himself; the Emperor dispatched Vice Minister Wang Jingceng to perform the sacrificial announcement.

entries.zh: 並傳旨慰問。
entries.en: An edict of consolation was sent as well.
entries.literal: An edict of consolation was also transmitted.

entries.zh: 尋發帑重建，命侍郎留保會巡撫岳濬、前巡撫陳世倌庀工役，而以傳鐸董其事。
entries.en: Soon afterward imperial funds were released for rebuilding; the Emperor ordered Vice Minister Liubao to work with Governor Yue Jun and former governor Chen Shichang in organizing the labor, while Chuan Duo supervised the project.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter funds were issued from the treasury for reconstruction; the Emperor ordered Vice Minister Liubao to join with Governor Yue Jun and former governor Chen Shichang to arrange the labor, while Chuan Duo was put in overall charge.

entries.zh: 詔詢傳鐸，有當增設者言無隱。
entries.en: An edict asked Chuan Duo to speak frankly of anything that ought to be added.
entries.literal: An edict inquired of Chuan Duo, saying that whatever ought to be added he should speak of without concealment.

entries.zh: 因請增設樂器庫直房，上許之。
entries.en: He then asked for a direct office attached to the musical-instrument repository, and the Emperor approved.
entries.literal: He thereupon requested addition of a straight office for the musical-instrument storehouse; the Emperor approved.

entries.zh: 八年，廟成。
entries.en: In the eighth year the temple was finished.
entries.literal: In the eighth year the temple was completed.

entries.zh: 九年，上命修孔林，仍與世倌監理，疾作乞休，上允之。
entries.en: In the ninth year the Emperor ordered repairs to the Kong Forest; Chuan Duo continued to supervise the work with Chen Shichang. When illness set in he asked to retire, and the Emperor allowed it.
entries.literal: In the ninth year the Emperor ordered repair of the Kong Forest; he still supervised the work together with Shichang; when illness came on he begged to retire, and the Emperor granted it.

entries.zh: 子繼濩前卒，命以孫廣棨襲。
entries.en: His son Jihuo had died earlier, so the Emperor ordered his grandson Guang Qi to succeed.
entries.literal: His son Jihuo had died earlier; the Emperor ordered that his grandson Guang Qi succeed.

entries.zh: 十年，孔林工竟，復開館輯闕里盛典。
entries.en: In the tenth year work on the Kong Forest was completed, and the academy was reopened to compile the ceremonial records of Queli.
entries.literal: In the tenth year work on the Kong Forest was finished; the academy was reopened to compile the Queli ceremonies.

entries.zh: 十三年，卒，賜祭葬。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year he died, and state sacrifice and burial were granted.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he died; state sacrifice and burial were granted.

entries.zh: 傳鐸工詩詞，有集。
entries.en: Chuan Duo was skilled in poetry and song lyrics and left a collection of writings.
entries.literal: Chuan Duo was skilled in poetry and lyrics and left a collection of writings.

entries.zh: 昭煥，字顯明，十三年正月，上東巡，釋奠孔子廟，禦詩禮堂。
entries.en: Zhao Huan, whose style was Xianming. In the first month of the thirteenth year the Emperor toured the east, offered libation at the Temple of Confucius, and visited the Hall of Poetry and Rites.
entries.literal: Zhao Huan, style name Xianming; in the first month of the thirteenth year the Emperor made an eastern tour, performed the libation sacrifice at the Temple of Confucius, and visited the Hall of Poetry and Rites.

entries.zh: 昭煥方幼，命其族人舉人繼汾等進講。
entries.en: Zhao Huan was still a child, so the Emperor ordered his kinsman, presented scholar Jifen, and others to lecture in his place.
entries.literal: Zhao Huan was still young; the Emperor ordered his kinsman, the presented scholar Jifen, and others to advance and lecture.

entries.zh: 是日並謁林，還，复留曲柄黃蓋。
entries.en: That same day he also visited the Kong Forest; on his return he again left a curved-handled yellow canopy.
entries.literal: That same day he also visited the forest; on returning he again left behind a curved-handled yellow canopy.

entries.zh: 賜昭煥宴，賚書籍、文綺、貂幣，官繼汾中書，族人有官者皆進秩。
entries.en: He gave Zhao Huan a banquet and bestowed books, brocades, and sable gifts. Jifen was appointed to the Central Secretariat, and every clansman in office received a promotion.
entries.literal: He granted Zhao Huan a banquet and bestowed books, patterned silks, and sable gifts; Jifen was appointed Central Secretariat official, and every clansman who held office was promoted in rank.

entries.zh: 親制孔子廟碑，勒石大成門外。
entries.en: The Emperor personally composed the temple stele and had it engraved in stone outside the Gate of Great Accomplishment.
entries.literal: The Emperor personally composed the stele for the Temple of Confucius and had it carved in stone outside the Gate of Great Accomplishment.

entries.zh: 二十一年，昭煥疏言：「皇莊戶丁蒙恩免役，歷來地方官額外雜派，每事調劑非易，請酌留五十戶，餘改歸民籍，交地方官編審應役。」
entries.en: In the twenty-first year Zhao Huan memorialized: "The estate households have been graciously exempted from corvée, yet local officials have long imposed extra levies on them, making every adjustment difficult. I ask that fifty households be kept, while the rest be returned to the common register and assigned corvée by the local magistrate."
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year Zhao Huan memorialized, saying: "The householders of the official estate have received the grace of exemption from corvée, yet over the years local officials have imposed extra miscellaneous levies, and it is not easy to adjust every matter; I request that fifty households be retained as appropriate, while the rest be transferred to commoner registration and handed to local officials for compilation and corvée assignment."

entries.zh: 上諭曰：「昭煥疏言皇莊，此必沿前代舊習，然亦止應稱官莊。
entries.en: The Emperor said: "Zhao Huan writes of an 'imperial estate'—no doubt an old habit from earlier dynasties—but he should have called it only the official estate.
entries.literal: The Emperor instructed, saying: "In Zhao Huan's memorial he speaks of an imperial estate; this must be a habit carried over from earlier dynasties, yet he should only have called it the official estate.

entries.zh: 子不云乎：'甚矣由之行詐，無臣而為有臣。
entries.en: Did not the Master say, 'How excessive was You in his deceit—having no minister yet acting as if he had one'?
entries.literal: Did not the Master say: 'How excessive was the conduct of You in his deceit—having no minister yet acting as though he had one?

entries.zh: '昭煥可謂不能讀其祖書矣。
entries.en: Zhao Huan plainly has not read his ancestor's books.
entries.literal: Zhao Huan can be said not to have read his ancestor's books.

entries.zh: 此時丁銀已停徵，地方官安得更令百姓應役？
entries.en: By then the poll tax in silver had already been stopped; how could local officials still press the common people into corvée?
entries.literal: At this time the poll tax in silver had already ceased to be collected; how could local officials further make the common people perform corvée?

entries.zh: 且取役何事？
entries.en: And for what work was corvée needed in the first place?
entries.literal: Moreover, for what purpose was corvée to be taken?

entries.zh: 若為朕東巡修道，則皆發帑僱役，初未累百姓。
entries.en: If it was for repairing roads on my eastern tour, all labor was hired from the treasury and never fell on the people at all.
entries.literal: If it was for repairing roads on my eastern tour, all labor was hired with funds from the treasury and had never burdened the people from the start.

entries.zh: 朕展謁先師，衍聖公督令廟戶除道清產，理所應爾，豈當轉庇廟戶，並發帑僱役亦不肯應耶？」
entries.en: When I visited the ancient teacher, it was only fitting that the Duke Yansheng should have the temple households clear the roads and clean the grounds. How could he instead shield those households, refusing even labor paid from the treasury?"
entries.literal: When I paid my respects to the ancient teacher, it was only right that the Duke Yansheng should supervise the temple households in clearing the roads and cleaning the grounds; how could he turn instead to shield the temple households, so that even hired labor from the treasury they would not supply?"

entries.zh: 下吏議，當奪爵，上命寬之。
entries.en: The officials recommended stripping his title, but the Emperor ordered leniency.
entries.literal: The officials deliberated and ruled that his title should be stripped; the Emperor ordered leniency.

entries.zh: 以昭煥年少，歸咎繼汾及其兄繼涑，皆譴黜。
entries.en: Because Zhao Huan was young, blame fell on Jifen and his elder brother Jisu; both were censured and dismissed.
entries.literal: Because Zhao Huan was young, blame was assigned to Jifen and his elder brother Jisu; both were punished and dismissed.

entries.zh: 三月，上東巡，釋奠孔子廟，謁林。
entries.en: In the third month the Emperor toured the east, offered libation at the Temple of Confucius, and visited the Kong Forest.
entries.literal: In the third month the Emperor made an eastern tour, performed the libation sacrifice at the Temple of Confucius, and visited the forest.

entries.zh: 二十二年，上奉皇太后東巡釋奠。
entries.en: In the twenty-second year the Emperor, with the Empress Dowager, toured the east and offered libation.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year the Emperor, accompanying the Empress Dowager, toured the east and performed the libation sacrifice.

entries.zh: 三十六年，復東巡釋奠。
entries.en: In the thirty-sixth year he again toured the east and offered libation.
entries.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he again toured the east and performed the libation sacrifice.

entries.zh: 既還京師，出內府所藏週銅器木鼎、亞尊、犧尊、伯彝、冊卣、蟠夔敦、寶簠、夔鳳豆、饕餮甗、四足鬲，凡十事，置廟庭。
entries.en: After returning to the capital, he took from the inner palace ten Zhou bronzes—the wooden ding, ya zun, sacrificial zun, Bo yi, ce you, coiled kui dun, precious gui, kui-phoenix dou, taotie yan, and four-legged li—and set them in the temple courtyard.
entries.literal: After returning to the capital, he brought out from the inner palace ten Zhou bronze vessels—the wooden ding, the ya vessel, the sacrificial zun, the Bo yi, the ce you, the coiled kui dun, the precious gui, the kui-phoenix dou, the taotie yan, and the four-legged li—and placed them in the temple court.

entries.zh: 四十一年，兩金川平。
entries.en: In the forty-first year the two Jinchuan campaigns were pacified.
entries.literal: In the forty-first year the two Jinchuan campaigns were pacified.

entries.zh: 三月，复奉皇太后東巡釋奠，告成功。
entries.en: In the third month he again accompanied the Empress Dowager on an eastern tour to offer libation and announce the victory.
entries.literal: In the third month he again accompanied the Empress Dowager on an eastern tour to perform the libation sacrifice and announce the victory.

entries.zh: 次日，謁林。
entries.en: The following day he visited the Kong Forest.
entries.literal: The next day he visited the forest.

entries.zh: 四十八年，昭煥卒，子憲培襲。
entries.en: In the forty-eighth year Zhao Huan died; his son Xian Pei succeeded.
entries.literal: In the forty-eighth year Zhao Huan died; his son Xian Pei succeeded.

entries.zh: 當唐末五季，以文宣公兼曲阜令。
entries.en: From the late Tang through the Five Dynasties, the Duke of Wenxuan had also served concurrently as magistrate of Qufu.
entries.literal: At the end of Tang and through the Five Dynasties, the Duke of Wenxuan also held the post of Qufu magistrate.

entries.zh: 宋用孔氏支子，明至清初因之。
entries.en: The Song appointed a collateral branch of the Kong house, and the Ming through early Qing kept the same arrangement.
entries.literal: The Song employed a collateral line of the Kong clan, and the Ming through early Qing followed the same practice.

entries.zh: 自毓琚與廣棨互訐坐罷官，廷議以衍聖公諮送易涉私，孔氏子領鄉縣，所隸皆親屬，審斷亦未能悉公，擬更前例。
entries.en: After Yu Ju and Guang Qi impeached each other and lost their posts, the court argued that when the Duke Yansheng forwarded nominations private favor was too easily involved, and that when a Kong clansman governed the county with kinsmen as subordinates judgments could hardly be fully impartial; they therefore proposed altering the old practice.
entries.literal: After Yu Ju and Guang Qi denounced each other and were dismissed from office, court discussion held that when the Duke Yansheng forwarded nominations it was easy to involve private interest; when a Kong clansman headed the district and subordinates were all kin, judgments too could not be wholly impartial—so they proposed changing the former precedent.

entries.zh: 御史衛廷璞疏言宜仍舊貫，鴻臚寺卿林令旭又請以衢州孔氏子孫為曲阜知縣，下廷臣議，用廷璞言，仍令衍聖公諮送，巡撫考試題補。
entries.en: Censor Wei Tingpu memorialized that the old custom should stand; Director of the Court of State Ceremonies Lin Lingxu also asked that a descendant of the Quzhou Kong line be made Qufu magistrate. The case went to the full court, which followed Tingpu: the Duke Yansheng would still forward names, and the provincial governor would examine candidates and fill the post by imperial appointment.
entries.literal: Censor Wei Tingpu memorialized that the old practice should be kept; Director of the Court of State Ceremonial Lin Lingxu also asked that a descendant of the Quzhou Kong line serve as Qufu magistrate. The matter was referred to the court for deliberation; Tingpu's view was adopted, and the Duke Yansheng was still to forward nominations while the provincial governor examined candidates and filled the post by imperial appointment.

entries.zh: 後十餘年，巡撫白鍾山奏請改題缺。
entries.en: More than ten years later, Governor Bai Zhongshan memorialized to make the magistracy an ordinary provincial post.
entries.literal: More than ten years later, Governor Bai Zhongshan memorialized requesting that the post be changed to a regular provincial appointment.

entries.zh: 上諭曰：「闕里毓聖之鄉，唐、宋以來，率以聖裔領縣事。
entries.en: The Emperor said: "Queli is the village that nurtured the sage; since Tang and Song, sage-descendants have usually held the county office.
entries.literal: The Emperor instructed: "Queli is the village that nurtured the sage; since Tang and Song times the sage's descendants have generally held the district office.

entries.zh: 大宗主鬯，爵列上公。
entries.en: The main line presides over the libation wine, and its rank stands among the highest dukes.
entries.literal: The great lineage presides over the sacrificial libation; its rank stands among the highest dukes.

entries.zh: 而知縣以民事為職，奉法令，則以裁制傷恩；
entries.en: Yet a magistrate's charge is the people's affairs: enforce the law, and kinship is hurt by restraint;
entries.literal: Yet the magistrate's duty is the people's affairs; if he upholds the law, kinship is wounded by restraint;

entries.zh: 厚族黨，則以偏私廢事；
entries.en: favor the clan, and public duty is lost to partiality;
entries.literal: if he favors clansmen, public duty is abandoned through partiality;

entries.zh: 非古易地而官之道，當如鍾山議。
entries.en: that is not the ancient principle of changing offices with the land. Bai Zhongshan's proposal should be adopted.
entries.literal: this is not the ancient way of exchanging offices by place—Bai Zhongshan's proposal should be followed.

entries.zh: 仍別設世襲六品官，選孔氏子充補。」
entries.en: A separate hereditary sixth-rank post should still be set up, filled by choosing Kong clansmen."
entries.literal: A separate hereditary sixth-rank office should still be established, filled by selection from Kong clansmen."

entries.zh: 列傳二百七十
entries.en: Biographies 270
entries.literal: Biographies 270

entries.zh: 同死者，為駐防副都統長喜，前鋒協領英登布，佐領隆福，防禦貴順、額特赫，前鋒校佛印，驍騎校伊勒哈畚、根順、該杭阿及調浙助防之守備張淮泗，千總李廷貴，把總王榮、馬致榮、孫登霄，外委馬成功、硃朝貴。
entries.en: Those who fell with him included garrison deputy lieutenant-general Chang Xi, vanguard company commander Ying Dengbu, assistant commandant Long Fu, defenders Gui Shun and Etehe, vanguard corporal Foyin, brave-rider corporals Yilehaben, Genshun, and Gaihang'a, garrison commander Zhang Huaisi sent to reinforce Zhejiang, major Li Tinggui, captains Wang Rong, Ma Zhirong, and Sun Dengxiao, and staff officers Ma Chenggong and Zhu Chaogui.
entries.literal: Those who died with him were garrison deputy lieutenant-general Chang Xi, vanguard company commander Ying Dengbu, assistant commandant Long Fu, defenders Gui Shun and Etehe, vanguard corporal Foyin, brave-rider corporals Yilehaben, Genshun, and Gaihang'a, and garrison commander Zhang Huaisi sent from elsewhere to aid Zhejiang's defense, major Li Tinggui, captains Wang Rong, Ma Zhirong, and Sun Dengxiao, and staff officers Ma Chenggong and Zhu Chaogui.

entries.zh: 而伊勒哈畚尤慘，伏觀山射夷，殪甚眾，被執，磔死。
entries.en: Yilehaben's fate was especially grim: he lay in ambush on Guanshan and shot down many of the enemy, but was taken prisoner and put to death by dismemberment.
entries.literal: Yilehaben's end was especially cruel: lying in ambush on Guanshan he shot the foreigners and killed very many; captured, he was dismembered to death.

entries.zh: 子仁厚，襲職，殉粵寇。
entries.en: His son Renhou inherited his office and later fell fighting the Taiping rebels.
entries.literal: His son Renhou inherited the post and died fighting the Taiping rebels.

entries.zh: 韋逢甲，山東​​齊河人。
entries.en: Wei Fengjia was a native of Qihe in Shandong.
entries.literal: Wei Fengjia was a native of Qihe in Shandong.

entries.zh: 道光十六年進士，用知縣，發浙江，累權宣平、馀杭、浦江等縣。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi examination in the sixteenth year of Daoguang (1836), was appointed a county magistrate, posted to Zhejiang, and served in turn as acting magistrate of Xuanping, Yuhang, Pujiang, and other counties.
entries.literal: A jinshi of the sixteenth year of Daoguang, he was appointed magistrate, assigned to Zhejiang, and repeatedly served in acting capacity at Xuanping, Yuhang, Pujiang, and other counties.

entries.zh: 英吉利既再擾寧波洋面，將寇吳淞，先以弋船三十艘進攻乍浦。
entries.en: After Britain again harassed the Ningbo coast and prepared to strike at Wusong, it first sent thirty light gunboats against Zhapu.
entries.literal: Britain having again disturbed the Ningbo coast and intending to threaten Wusong, first sent thirty light gunboats to attack Zhapu.

entries.zh: 時逢甲以督鑄大砲，由鎮海赴乍浦設防，就權同知。
entries.en: Fengjia was then supervising the casting of heavy cannon; he went from Zhenhai to Zhapu to organize the defense and was appointed acting subprefect.
entries.literal: At the time Fengjia was supervising the casting of great guns; he went from Zhenhai to Zhapu to set up defenses and was given acting subprefect.

entries.zh: 四月，敵遽由東光山上陸，屯兵皆潰。
entries.en: In the fourth month the enemy landed unexpectedly from Dongguang Hill and the garrison troops scattered in rout.
entries.literal: In the fourth month the enemy suddenly landed from Dongguang Hill and the encamped troops all broke.

entries.zh: 逢甲帶鄉團禦於西行汛，死之。
entries.en: Fengjia led the local militia to hold the western outpost and was killed.
entries.literal: Fengjia led local militia to defend at the western outpost and died there.

entries.zh: 麥廷章，廣東鶴山人。
entries.en: Mai Tingzhang was a native of Heshan in Guangdong.
entries.literal: Mai Tingzhang was a native of Heshan in Guangdong.

entries.zh: 道光十二年，以外委隨剿連州瑤匪功，屢遷至游擊。
entries.en: In the twelfth year of Daoguang (1832), as a staff officer he took part in suppressing the Yao rebels of Lianzhou and rose by repeated promotion to battalion commander.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Daoguang, as a staff officer he followed the campaign against the Yao bandits of Lianzhou and was repeatedly promoted to battalion commander.

entries.zh: 林則徐查辦英吉利躉船鴉片，檄廷章率舟師駐九龍山巡防。
entries.en: When Lin Zexu was investigating British opium hulks, he ordered Tingzhang to take the fleet to Jiulongshan on coastal patrol.
entries.literal: When Lin Zexu investigated British opium receiving ships, he ordered Tingzhang to lead the naval force to garrison Jiulongshan on patrol.

entries.zh: 英酋遞書辯論，開導不服，遽開砲，廷章以大砲應之，毀雙桅敵船。
entries.en: The British commander exchanged letters in dispute; when persuasion failed he opened fire without warning; Tingzhang replied with heavy guns and sank a two-masted enemy vessel.
entries.literal: The British chief sent letters to argue; persuasion failed and he suddenly opened fire; Tingzhang answered with great guns and destroyed a two-masted enemy ship.

entries.zh: 又潛約土密兵船助攻，复擊卻之。
entries.en: He also secretly coordinated with local and foreign merchant vessels for a joint attack and drove them off once more.
entries.literal: He also secretly arranged for native and foreign merchant ships to join the attack, and again beat them off.

entries.zh: 英人既陷浙定海，遂溯大洋至天津乞和，朝命直隸總督琦善馳粵與議，海防遽懈。
entries.en: After the British captured Dinghai in Zhejiang they sailed north to Tianjin to seek peace; the court sent Zhili governor-general Qishan to Guangdong to negotiate, and coastal defenses were abruptly let down.
entries.literal: After the English had taken Dinghai in Zhejiang they sailed the great ocean to Tianjin to sue for peace; the court ordered Zhili governor-general Qishan to hurry to Guangdong to negotiate, and coastal defense was suddenly relaxed.

entries.zh: 二十年十二月，敵乘不備，突進占大角、沙角，廷章時佐提督關天培防守靖遠砲台。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of the twentieth year (1840) the enemy struck while defenses were slack and seized Dajiao and Shajiao; Tingzhang was then assisting Commander Guan Tianpei at Jingyuan battery.
entries.literal: Twelfth month of the twentieth year, the enemy took advantage of unpreparedness and suddenly advanced to occupy Dajiao and Shajiao; Tingzhang was then assisting commander Guan Tianpei in defending Jingyuan battery.

entries.zh: 明年二月，敵船擁入三門口，斷防禦椿練。
entries.en: In the second month of the following year enemy ships forced their way into Sanmenkou and severed the defensive boom chains.
entries.literal: Second month of the next year, enemy ships crowded into Sanmenkou and cut the defensive boom chains.

entries.zh: 南風作，復以大隊圍橫檔、永安，截我軍援道，進犯虎門。
entries.en: When the south wind rose they sent a large fleet to surround Hengdang and Yong'an, cut off our relief routes, and pressed on against Humen.
entries.literal: When the south wind rose they again used a large force to surround Hengdang and Yong'an, cut our army's relief routes, and advanced against Humen.

entries.zh: 廷章奮勇御之，力竭死。
entries.en: Tingzhang fought them with all his strength until he was spent and fell.
entries.literal: Tingzhang fought them bravely to the end and died from exhaustion of strength.

entries.zh: 時旅順先陷，海軍掃地，黃海諸要隘皆失守，將士多死事，以奏報有缺，不得書。
entries.en: Lüshun had already fallen, the navy was destroyed, and the Yellow Sea defenses were lost; many officers and men died for their country, but incomplete memorials kept most of them out of the record.
entries.literal: At the time Lüshun had fallen first, the navy was swept away, all strategic passes on the Yellow Sea were lost, and many officers and soldiers died for their duty; because memorial reports were incomplete, they could not be recorded.

entries.zh: 其見奏報者，三等侍衛永山，在鳳凰城戰歿；
entries.en: Among those named in memorials were third-rank bodyguard Yongshan, killed at Fenghuangcheng;
entries.literal: Among those appearing in memorial reports: third-rank bodyguard Yongshan died in battle at Fenghuangcheng;

entries.zh: 游擊李世鴻、副將李仁黨與提督楊壽山分守蓋平，禦敵大將乃木軍，戰最烈，同時以力盡陣亡。
entries.en: battalion commander Li Shihong and brigade commander Li Rendang, who with commander Yang Shoushan held Gaiping against General Nogi's army in the fiercest fighting, and all fell when their strength was spent.
entries.literal: battalion commander Li Shihong and brigade commander Li Rendang, with commander Yang Shoushan, jointly held Gaiping, resisted the enemy's great general Nogi Maresuke's army, fought most fiercely, and at the same time, strength exhausted, died on the field.

entries.zh: 步蟾、宗騫自有傳。
entries.en: Buchan and Zongqian have separate biographies.
entries.literal: Buchan and Zongqian have their own biographies.

entries.zh: 列傳二百八十一
entries.en: Biographies 281
entries.literal: Biographies 281

entries.zh: 宗室奕功，歷官奉宸苑卿，至御前侍衛。
entries.en: The imperial clansman Yigong served in turn as Director of the Imperial Parks and eventually as an imperial bodyguard in attendance.
entries.literal: Imperial clansman Yigong successively served as Director of the Imperial Parks and rose to imperial bodyguard before the throne.

entries.zh: 光緒二十六年，拳匪肇禍，各國聯軍破京都，德宗奉孝欽顯皇后西狩，奕功以世受國恩，未能隨扈，引火自焚。
entries.en: In Guangxu 26 the Boxer uprising erupted, the allied armies of the foreign powers took the capital, and Emperor Guangxu escorted Empress Dowager Cixi west in flight. Yigong, who had long enjoyed the dynasty's favor, was unable to join the imperial flight and burned himself to death.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Guangxu the Boxers began the calamity; the allied armies of the powers broke the capital; Emperor Dezong escorted Empress Dowager Xiaoqinxian west on tour; Yigong, having received the state's grace through generations, could not follow the imperial retinue, and set himself afire.

entries.zh: 妻祥佳氏、子載捷等，闔家投井殉節。
entries.en: His wife Lady Xiangjia, his son Zaijie, and the entire household cast themselves into a well and perished in loyalty.
entries.literal: His wife, Lady Xiangjia, his son Zaijie, and the rest of the household threw themselves into a well and died for their integrity.

entries.zh: 先後被難者，宗室有奉恩將軍札隆阿，子樸誠等；
entries.en: Among those who perished in the turmoil were, from the imperial clan, Enfeoffed General Zhalong'a and his son Pucheng, among others;
entries.literal: Among those who met calamity in succession, of the imperial clan there were Enfeoffed General Zhalong'a and his son Pucheng and others;

entries.zh: 奉恩將軍緝禦，子培善，孫存德、存厚等；
entries.en: Enfeoffed General Jiyu, his son Peishan, and his grandsons Cunde and Cunhou, among others;
entries.literal: Enfeoffed General Jiyu, his son Peishan, his grandsons Cunde and Cunhou and others;

entries.zh: 文舉人恩煦，子繼勳、懋勳，從子啟勳、世勳等；
entries.en: the licentiate Enxu, his sons Jixun and Maoxun, and his nephews Qixun and Shixun, among others;
entries.literal: the licentiate in letters Enxu, his sons Jixun and Maoxun, his nephews Qixun and Shixun and others;

entries.zh: 掌江西道監察御史德籓，戶部員外郎恩斝，戶部主事謹善，宗人府經歷訥欽，頭等侍衛德潤，帶隊官鈺璋，及奕鑫、載袍、恕誠、聯德、恩溥、鬆達、善章、國文、松根、景璋、承惠、和桂、鳳喜、吉辰、海明，覺羅有清廉、年瑞、德潤、榮綿。
entries.en: Supervising Censor Defan of the Jiangxi circuit, Vice Director Enjia of the Ministry of Revenue, Secretary Jinshan of the same ministry, Imperial Clan Court clerk Neqin, first-rank bodyguard Derun, detachment officer Yuzhang, and Yixin, Zaipao, Shucheng, Liande, Enpu, Songda, Shanzhang, Guowen, Songgen, Jingzhang, Chenghui, He Gui, Fengxi, Jichen, and Haiming; among the Aisin Gioro lineage were Qinglian, Nianrui, Derun, and Rongmian.
entries.literal: the supervising censor in charge of the Jiangxi circuit Defan, the Ministry of Revenue vice director Enjia, the Ministry of Revenue secretary Jinshan, the Imperial Clan Court clerk Neqin, first-rank bodyguard Derun, detachment officer Yuzhang, and Yixin, Zaipao, Shucheng, Liande, Enpu, Songda, Shanzhang, Guowen, Songgen, Jingzhang, Chenghui, He Gui, Fengxi, Jichen, and Haiming; among the Aisin Gioro were Qinglian, Nianrui, Derun, and Rongmian.

entries.zh: 馬鍾祺，字維春，隸漢軍鑲黃旗。
entries.en: Ma Zhongqi, styled Weichun, belonged to the Hanjun Bordered Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Ma Zhongqi, style Weichun, was of the Hanjun Bordered Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 少為諸生，以襲一等子，例不得與試，授三等侍衛，擢二等，有文武才。
entries.en: In his youth he was a licentiate; having inherited a first-class viscountcy he was barred by regulation from the examinations, was appointed a third-rank bodyguard, was promoted to the second rank, and possessed both literary and military ability.
entries.literal: In youth he was a licentiate; by inheriting a first-class viscountcy he was by regulation barred from examinations, was appointed a third-rank bodyguard, was promoted to the second rank, and had both civil and military talent.

entries.zh: 初服膺陸、王之學，繼參以程、硃、張、呂，不主一家。
entries.en: He first embraced the learning of Lu Xiangshan and Wang Yangming, then drew also on Cheng Yi, Zhu Xi, Zhang Zai, and Lü Dalin, and did not commit himself to any one school alone.
entries.literal: At first he adhered to the learning of Lu and Wang, then blended in Cheng, Zhu, Zhang, and Lü, and did not adhere to a single school.

entries.zh: 為人伉爽有奇氣，慕孫白谷之為人，好與朝野賢士遊，與語或不合，輒哦詩亂之，以此得狂名。
entries.en: He was forthright and spirited, admired the character of Sun Baigu, loved the company of worthy men in and out of office, and when talk did not suit him would break into verse to disrupt it, for which he gained a reputation as a eccentric.
entries.literal: As a man he was bold and open with a singular spirit; he admired the character of Sun Baigu, loved to associate with worthy men in court and country, and when conversation did not agree would chant poetry to disrupt it, and for this gained a reputation for eccentricity.

entries.zh: 光緒二十年，日本爭朝鮮，廷議出師，鍾祺上書請自效，遂從戎奉天。
entries.en: In Guangxu 20, when Japan pressed its claim over Korea and the court debated dispatching troops, Zhongqi submitted a memorial offering his service and went to war in Fengtian.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year of Guangxu Japan contended over Korea; the court debated sending troops; Zhongqi memorialized offering himself and accordingly took the field at Fengtian.

entries.zh: 盛京將軍依克唐阿器之，使統鎮邊馬隊。
entries.en: Shengjing General Yiketang'a recognized his talent and put him in command of the border cavalry.
entries.literal: Shengjing general Yiketang'a valued his ability and had him command the border cavalry.

entries.zh: 會和議定，遂歸。
entries.en: When peace was concluded he returned home.
entries.literal: When peace was settled he returned.

entries.zh: 二十五年，李秉衡奉旨巡視長江，親訪於家，疏請從行。
entries.en: In the twenty-fifth year Li Bingheng was ordered to inspect the Yangzi, called on him at home, and memorialized the throne to take him along.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Li Bingheng was ordered to inspect the Yangzi and visited him at home in person, memorializing to have him accompany him.

entries.zh: 拳匪禍作，冒鋒火而北，秉衡殉難，鍾祺護其喪歸。
entries.en: When the Boxer disaster erupted he braved the fighting to go north; after Bingheng died in service Zhongqi escorted his coffin home.
entries.literal: When the Boxer calamity arose he braved gunfire to go north; Bingheng died for the state and Zhongqi escorted his coffin home.

entries.zh: 歸三日，京師破，鍾祺自縊死。
entries.en: Three days after his return the capital fell, and Zhongqi hanged himself.
entries.literal: Three days after his return the capital fell, and Zhongqi hanged himself.

entries.zh: 著五倫大義、馬氏日記若干卷。
entries.en: He left several volumes, including The Great Meaning of the Five Relationships and the Ma Family Diary.
entries.literal: He authored several volumes of The Great Meaning of the Five Relationships and the Ma Family Diary.

entries.zh: 列傳二百八十二
entries.en: Biographies 282
entries.literal: Biographies 282

entries.zh: 蔣衡，改名振生，字湘帆，晚號拙老人。
entries.en: Jiang Heng, who later changed his name to Zhensheng, had the courtesy name Xiangfan and in his later years took the sobriquet Zhuolaoren, 'the Clumsy Old Man.'
entries.literal: Jiang Heng, who changed his name to Zhensheng, style name Xiangfan, late sobriquet Zhuolaoren.

entries.zh: 與澍同里。
entries.en: He came from the same home district as Wang Shu.
entries.literal: He was from the same district as Shu.

entries.zh: 鍵戶十二年，寫十三經。
entries.en: He shut himself indoors for twelve years and copied out the entire Thirteen Classics in his own hand.
entries.literal: He barred his door for twelve years and wrote out the Thirteen Classics.

entries.zh: 乾隆中，進上，高宗命刻石國學，授衡國子監學正，終不出。
entries.en: During the Qianlong reign he presented his work to the throne; the Qianlong Emperor ordered it cut in stone at the Imperial Academy and appointed Heng director of studies at the Directorate of Education, yet he never left home to serve.
entries.literal: In the Qianlong reign he presented it to the throne; the Gaozong Emperor ordered it carved in stone at the Imperial Academy and appointed Heng director of studies at the Directorate of Education, but he never took office.

entries.zh: 衡早歲好遊，足跡半海內，觀碑關中，獲晉、唐以來名跡，臨摹三百餘種，曰拙存堂臨古帖。
entries.en: In his youth Heng loved to travel and ranged over half the empire; in Guanzhong he studied steles and acquired celebrated works from the Jin and Tang dynasties onward, producing more than three hundred copies collected as the Zhuocuntang Copies of Ancient Rubbings.
entries.literal: Heng in his early years loved travel; his footsteps covered half the realm. Viewing steles in Guanzhong he obtained famous traces from Jin and Tang onward, copied more than three hundred kinds, and called them Zhuocuntang Copies of Ancient Rubbings.

entries.zh: 晚與澍相期斫勝，每臨一書，相從質證。
entries.en: In later life he and Wang Shu made a practice of testing each other's skill: whenever one copied a classic work, the other would join him to critique and verify the result.
entries.literal: In his later years he and Shu arranged to compare their skill; whenever either copied a work, the other would follow along to verify it.

entries.zh: 子驥，孫和，並以書世其家。
entries.en: His son Jiang Ji and grandson Jiang He both carried on the family's reputation in calligraphy.
entries.literal: His son Ji and grandson He both handed down calligraphy through their family.

entries.zh: 王文治，字禹卿，江蘇丹徒人。
entries.en: Wang Wenzhi, courtesy name Yuqing, was a native of Dantu in Jiangsu.
entries.literal: Wang Wenzhi, style name Yuqing, a man of Dantu in Jiangsu.

entries.zh: 生有夙慧，十二歲能詩，即工書。
entries.en: He was gifted from childhood: at twelve he could write poetry and was already accomplished in calligraphy.
entries.literal: Born with innate intelligence, at twelve he could compose poetry and was already skilled in calligraphy.

entries.zh: 長游京師，從翰林院侍讀全魁使琉球，文字播於海外。
entries.en: As a young man he traveled to the capital and accompanied the Hanlin reader Quan Kui on a mission to Ryukyu, where his writing won renown overseas.
entries.literal: When grown he traveled to the capital; he followed Hanlin reader Quan Kui on a mission to Ryukyu, and his writing spread beyond the seas.

entries.zh: 乾隆三十五年，成一甲三名進士，授翰林院編修。
entries.en: In the thirty-fifth year of Qianlong he placed third in the first rank of jinshi graduates and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.
entries.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Qianlong he placed third among the first-rank jinshi and was appointed Hanlin compiler.

entries.zh: 逾三年，大考第一，擢侍讀。
entries.en: Three years later he ranked first in the grand examination and was promoted to Hanlin reader.
entries.literal: After more than three years, in the grand examination he ranked first and was promoted to reader.

entries.zh: 出為雲南臨安知府，因事鐫級，乞病歸。
entries.en: He was posted as prefect of Lin'an in Yunnan, but after an incident his rank was reduced; he pleaded illness and returned home.
entries.literal: He went out as prefect of Lin'an in Yunnan; because of an affair his rank was reduced, and he requested leave on grounds of illness and returned home.

entries.zh: 後當復官，厭吏事，遂不出，往來吳、越間，主講杭州、鎮江書院。
entries.en: When he was later eligible for reinstatement he had grown weary of official business and declined to serve, traveling between the Wu and Yue regions while lecturing at academies in Hangzhou and Zhenjiang.
entries.literal: Later he was due to be restored to office, but he was weary of administrative affairs and so did not emerge; he traveled between Wu and Yue and lectured at academies in Hangzhou and Zhenjiang.

entries.zh: 高宗南巡，至錢塘僧寺，見文治書碑，大賞愛之。
entries.en: On a southern tour the Qianlong Emperor visited a Buddhist temple in Qiantang, saw a stele inscribed by Wenzhi, and was deeply impressed.
entries.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor made a southern tour and came to a Buddhist temple in Qiantang, he saw a stele inscribed by Wenzhi and greatly admired it.

entries.zh: 內廷有以告，招之出者，亦不應。
entries.en: Word reached the inner court, and although he was summoned to serve, he would not answer the call.
entries.literal: Someone in the inner court reported this; those who summoned him to come forth received no response.

entries.zh: 梁同書，字元穎，晚號山舟，浙江錢塘人，大學士詩正子。
entries.en: Liang Tongshu, courtesy name Yuanying, who in later life took the sobriquet Shanzhou, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang and the son of the Grand Secretary Liang Shizheng.
entries.literal: Liang Tongshu, style name Yuanying, late sobriquet Shanzhou, a man of Qiantang in Zhejiang, son of Grand Secretary Shizheng.

entries.zh: 乾隆十七年，會試未第，高宗特賜與殿試，入翰林，大考，擢侍講。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year of Qianlong he failed the metropolitan examination, but the Qianlong Emperor specially allowed him to take the palace examination; he entered the Hanlin Academy and, after the grand examination, was promoted to expositor.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year of Qianlong he failed the metropolitan examination; the Gaozong Emperor specially granted him participation in the palace examination. He entered the Hanlin, and in the grand examination was promoted to expositor.

entries.zh: 淡於榮利，未老，因疾不出。
entries.en: Indifferent to rank and gain, he withdrew from office while still comparatively young, pleading illness.
entries.literal: Indifferent to glory and profit, before he was old he ceased to emerge on account of illness.

entries.zh: 晚年重宴鹿鳴，加侍講學士銜。
entries.en: In his later years he was again honored at the Luming banquet for senior graduates and granted the additional title of Hanlin expositor.
entries.literal: In his later years he was again feasted at the Luming banquet and given the additional title of expositor of the Hanlin Academy.

entries.zh: 卒，年九十三。
entries.en: He died at the age of ninety-three.
entries.literal: He died at the age of ninety-three.

entries.zh: 好書出天性，十二歲能為擘窠大字。
entries.en: His love of calligraphy was inborn; at twelve he could write large decorative characters.
entries.literal: His love of calligraphy came from innate nature; at twelve he could write large characters in boke style.

entries.zh: 初法顏、柳，中年用米法，七十後乃變化。
entries.en: He began by studying Yan Zhenqing and Liu Gongquan; in midlife he adopted Mi Fu's manner; only after seventy did his style fully mature into something his own.
entries.literal: At first he followed Yan and Liu; in middle age he used Mi's method; only after seventy did he transform.

entries.zh: 名滿天下，求書者紙日數束，日本、琉球皆重之。
entries.en: His fame filled the world; patrons sent him several bundles of paper each day seeking his writing, and collectors in Japan and Ryukyu prized his work highly.
entries.literal: His fame filled the world; those who sought his writing sent several bundles of paper daily; Japan and Ryukyu all prized him.

entries.zh: 好石鼓文，李斯嶧山碑、泰山刻石，漢開母石闕，燉煌太守碑，吳蘇建國山碑，皇像天發神讖碑，唐李陽冰城隍廟碑、三墳記，每種臨摹各百本。
