entries.en: In the twenty-fifth year Cao Pi of Wei took the imperial title and changed the era name to Huangchu.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Wei Emperor Wen assumed honored title; changed the year to Huangchu.

entries.zh: 或傳聞漢帝見害，先主乃發喪制服，追諡曰孝愍皇帝。
entries.en: Rumors spread that the Han emperor had been murdered; Liu Bei then went into mourning and posthumously titled him Emperor Xiaomin.
entries.literal: Some heard rumor the Han emperor was seen harmed; the Former Lord then issued mourning and donned mourning garments; posthumously titled Filial Compassionate Emperor.

entries.zh: 是後在所並言眾瑞，日月相屬，故議郎陽泉侯劉豹、青衣侯向舉、偏將軍張裔、黃權、大司馬屬殷純、益州別駕從事趙莋、治中從事楊洪、從事祭酒何宗、議曹從事杜瓊、勸學從事張爽、尹默、譙周等上言：
entries.en: Thenceforth every district reported omens in endless succession; Gentleman-adviser Liu Bao, marquis of Yangquan, Xiang Ju, marquis of Qingyi, Major General Zhang Yi, Huang Quan, Yin Chun of the grand marshal’s staff, chief clerk Zhao Zha, headquarters clerk Yang Hong, libationer He Zong, Du Qiong of the consult bureau, Zhang Shuang, Yin Mo, Qiao Zhou, and others memorialized:
entries.literal: After this in places together spoke many auspices, sun and moon linked in succession; therefore Gentleman-adviser village marquis of Yangquan Liu Bao, village marquis of Qingyi Xiang Ju, major general Zhang Yi, Huang Quan, Grand Marshal’s subordinate Yin Chun, Yizhou chief clerk Zhao Zha, headquarters clerk Yang Hong, clerk libationer He Zong, consult bureau clerk Du Qiong, encourage-learning clerk Zhang Shuang, Yin Mo, Qiao Zhou and others upward spoke:

entries.zh: 先主 劉備
entries.en: The Former Lord: Liu Bei.
entries.literal: The Former Lord Liu Bei.

entries.zh: 建興元年夏，臧柯太守朱褒擁郡反。
entries.en: That summer of 223, Zhu Bao, prefect of Zangke, rose in revolt and took the commandery for himself.
entries.literal: In the summer of the first year of Jianxing, Zhu Bao, the Administrator of Zangke, seized the commandery and rebelled.

entries.zh: 〈《魏氏春秋》曰：初，益州從事常房行部，聞褒將有異志，收其主簿案問，殺之。
entries.en: 〈The Wei Annals of Spring and Autumn record that earlier, Yizhou staff officer Chang Fang, on circuit duty, heard Zhu Bao was turning disloyal; he arrested Zhu's chief clerk for questioning and had him executed.
entries.literal: 〈The Wei shi chunqiu states: At first, Chang Fang, an aide in Yizhou, was making an inspection tour of his circuit; hearing that Bao was about to harbor disloyal intent, he seized Bao's chief clerk, interrogated him under investigation, and killed him.

entries.zh: 褒怒，攻殺房，誣以謀反。
entries.en: Zhu Bao struck back: he killed Chang Fang and then framed him for treason.
entries.literal: Bao was angry; he attacked and killed Fang, and slandered him with a charge of plotting rebellion.

entries.zh: 諸葛亮誅房諸子，徙其四弟於越雋，欲以安之。
entries.en: Zhuge Liang put Chang Fang's sons to death, banished four of his younger brothers to Yuexi, and meant the gesture as a conciliatory signal.
entries.literal: Zhuge Liang executed Fang's sons and relocated his four younger brothers to Yuexi, intending thereby to pacify the situation.

entries.zh: 褒猶不悛改，遂以郡叛應雍闓。
entries.en: Zhu Bao refused to mend his ways and soon threw in his lot with Yong Kai, rebelling at the head of the commandery.
entries.literal: Bao still did not reform; thereupon with the commandery he rebelled in response to Yong Kai.

entries.zh: 臣松之案：以為房為褒所誣，執政所宜澄察，安有妄殺不辜以悅姦慝？
entries.en: Pei Songzhi argues that Chang Fang was framed by Zhu Bao and that the court should have sorted truth from falsehood instead of executing innocents to appease a traitor.
entries.literal: Your subject Songzhi submits: I consider that Fang was slandered by Bao; those in power ought to have clarified and investigated—how could there be wanton killing of the guiltless in order to please the wicked?

entries.zh: 斯殆妄矣！〉
entries.en: That account is almost certainly wrong.〉
entries.literal: This is probably false!〉

entries.zh: 先是，益州郡有大姓雍闓反，流太守張裔於吳，據郡不賓，越巂夷王高定亦背叛。
entries.en: Even before that, the great clan leader Yong Kai had risen in Yizhou commandery, shipped Prefect Zhang Yi off to Wu, refused allegiance while holding the territory, and Gao Ding, king of the Yuexi tribes, had joined the revolt.
entries.literal: Before this, in Yizhou commandery the magnate Yong Kai rebelled, banished the Administrator Zhang Yi to Wu, held the commandery and did not submit, and the Yuexi Yi king Gao Ding also rebelled.

entries.zh: 是歲，立皇后張氏。
entries.en: The same year he took Lady Zhang as empress.
entries.literal: That year, an empress surnamed Zhang was established.

entries.zh: 遣尚書
entries.en: The court dispatched a Director of the Secretariat
entries.literal: A Director of the Secretariat was dispatched

entries.en: The transmitted text inserts the character lang, marking him as a Gentleman of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: (The text supplies the character Gentleman [lang] in the office title.)

entries.zh: 鄧芝固好於吳，吳王孫權與蜀和親使聘，是歲通好。
entries.en: Deng Zhi was dispatched to shore up ties with Wu; Sun Quan of Wu and Shu exchanged marriage overtures and embassies, and that year the two courts formally made peace.
entries.literal: Deng Zhi to consolidate friendship with Wu; the King of Wu Sun Quan with Shu made peace by marriage and exchanged envoys; that year they opened friendly relations.

entries.zh: 八年秋，魏使司馬懿由西城，張郺由子午，曹真由斜谷，
entries.en: In the autumn of 230 Wei launched a three-pronged move on Hanzhong: Sima Yi through Xicheng, Zhang He through the Ziwu defile, and Cao Zhen up the Xie Valley,
entries.literal: In the autumn of the eighth year, Wei sent Sima Yi by Xicheng, Zhang He by Ziwu, and Cao Zhen by Xie Valley,

entries.zh: 〈斜，余奢反。〉
entries.en: 〈Commentary gloss: the graph xie is read with the yu-she fanqie.〉
entries.literal: 〈Xie: read with the fanqie initial yu and final she.〉

entries.zh: 欲攻漢中。
entries.en: intending to overrun Hanzhong.
entries.literal: intending to attack Hanzhong.

entries.zh: 丞相亮待之於城固、赤坂，大雨道絕，真等皆還。
entries.en: Zhuge Liang blocked them at Chenggu and Chipo; torrential rains washed out the roads, and Cao Zhen's columns had to turn back.
entries.literal: Chancellor Liang awaited them at Chenggu and Chipo; great rain cut off the roads, and Zhen and the others all returned.

entries.zh: 是歲，魏延破魏雍州剌史郭淮於陽溪。
entries.en: The same year Wei Yan routed Yongzhou inspector Guo Huai for Wei at Yangxi.
entries.literal: That year, Wei Yan defeated Wei's Inspector of Yongzhou Guo Huai at Yangxi.

entries.zh: 徙魯王永為甘陵王，梁王理為安平王，皆以魯、梁在吳分界故也。
entries.en: Prince Yong of Lu was redesignated prince of Ganling and Prince Li of Liang became prince of Pingan, since Lu and Liang lay in territory allotted to Wu.
entries.literal: The Prince of Lu Yong was moved to be Prince of Ganling, and the Prince of Liang Li was moved to be Prince of Pingan—both because Lu and Liang lay on Wu's side of the partition.

entries.zh: 九年春二月，亮復出軍圍祁山，始以木牛運。
entries.en: In the second month of 231 Zhuge Liang marched on Qishan again, this time supplying the army with his wooden-ox carts.
entries.literal: In the spring, second month, of the ninth year, Liang again went out with the army and besieged Qishan, for the first time using the wooden ox to transport.

entries.zh: 魏司馬懿、張郺救祁山。
entries.en: Sima Yi and Zhang He of Wei raced to lift the siege at Qishan.
entries.literal: Wei's Sima Yi and Zhang He relieved Qishan.

entries.zh: 夏六月，亮糧盡退軍，郺追至青封，與亮交戰，被箭死。
entries.en: By the sixth month Zhuge Liang had exhausted his grain and fell back; Zhang He pressed him to Qingfeng, joined battle, and was killed by an arrow.
entries.literal: In the summer, sixth month, when Liang's provisions were exhausted he withdrew the army; He pursued to Qingfeng, fought with Liang, and was hit by an arrow and died.

entries.zh: 秋八月，都護李嚴廢徙梓潼郡。
entries.en: That August Li Yan was stripped of office and exiled to Zitong.
entries.literal: In the autumn, eighth month, Chief Controller Li Yan was dismissed and banished to Zitong commandery.

entries.zh: 〈《漢晉春秋》曰：冬十月，江陽至江州有鳥從江南飛渡江北，不能達，墮水死者以千數。〉
entries.en: 〈The Han–Jin Annals of Spring and Autumn record that in the tenth month flocks tried to fly from the south bank of the Yangzi toward Jiangzhou; thousands dropped into the river and drowned.〉
entries.literal: 〈The Han Jin chunqiu states: In the winter, tenth month, from Jiangyang to Jiangzhou there were birds flying from south of the Yangzi to cross north of the Yangzi; unable to reach, they fell into the water and died by the thousands.〉

entries.zh: 景耀元年，姜維還成都。
entries.en: In 258 Jiang Wei was back in Chengdu.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jingyao, Jiang Wei returned to Chengdu.

entries.zh: 史官言景星見，於是大赦，改年。
entries.en: Court astronomers reported an auspicious jing star; the throne ordered a general amnesty and adopted the reign title Jingyao.
entries.literal: The scribes reported that a jing star appeared; thereupon a great amnesty was proclaimed and the year was changed.

entries.zh: 宦人黃皓始專政。
entries.en: The eunuch Huang Hao began to dominate the court.
entries.literal: The eunuch Huang Hao for the first time monopolized government.

entries.zh: 吳大將軍孫琳廢其主亮，立琅邪王休。
entries.en: In Wu, Grand General Sun Lin deposed Sun Liang and set Sun Xiu, prince of Langye, on the throne.
entries.literal: Wu Grand General Sun Lin deposed his ruler Liang and established the Prince of Langye Xiu.

entries.zh: 三年秋九月，追諡故將軍關羽、張飛、馬超、龐統、黃忠。
entries.en: That ninth month of 260 posthumous honors were conferred on Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, Ma Chao, Pang Tong, and Huang Zhong.
entries.literal: In the autumn, ninth month, of the third year, posthumous titles were granted to the former generals Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, Ma Chao, Pang Tong, and Huang Zhong.

entries.zh: 六年夏，魏大興徒從眾，命征西將軍鄧艾、鎮西將軍鍾會、雍州剌史諸葛緒數道並攻。
entries.en: That summer of 263 Wei mobilized a huge host and ordered Deng Ai, Zhong Hui, and Yongzhou inspector Zhuge Xu to advance on several columns.
entries.literal: In the summer of the sixth year, Wei on a great scale raised transport-follower masses, ordering General Who Conquers the West Deng Ai, General Who Guards the West Zhong Hui, and Inspector of Yongzhou Zhuge Xu on several routes jointly to attack.

entries.zh: 於是遣左右車騎將軍張翼、廖化、輔國大將軍董厥等拒之。
entries.en: Shu sent Zhang Yi and Liao Hua, generals of chariots and cavalry left and right, and Dong Jue, assistant grand general for state support, to hold the line.
entries.literal: Thereupon he dispatched the Left and Right Generals of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang Yi, Liao Hua, Assistant State General Dong Jue, and others to resist them.

entries.zh: 大赦。
entries.en: A general amnesty was declared.
entries.literal: A great amnesty was proclaimed.

entries.zh: 改元為炎興。
entries.en: The era name was changed to Yanxing.
entries.literal: The reign title was changed to Yanxing.

entries.zh: 冬，鄧艾破衛將軍諸葛瞻於綿竹。
entries.en: That winter Deng Ai shattered Zhuge Zhan, guard general, at Mianzhu.
entries.literal: In winter, Deng Ai defeated Guard General Zhuge Zhan at Mianzhu.

entries.zh: 用光祿大夫譙周策，降於艾，奉書曰：
entries.en: On the advice of Qiao Zhou, grandee of the imperial household, he capitulated to Deng Ai and sent this letter:
entries.literal: Employing the plan of Imperial Household Grandee Qiao Zhou, he surrendered to Ai and presented a letter saying:

entries.zh: 限分江、漢，遇值深遠，階緣蜀土，斗絕一隅，干運犯冒，漸苒歷載，遂與京畿攸隔萬里。
entries.en: The Yangzi and Han have long cut us off from the heartland; fate set us on this remote plateau of Shu, a pocket realm hemmed by mountains. Year after year we have pressed our luck, until we stand ten thousand li from the imperial precincts.
entries.literal: Limited and partitioned by the Yangzi and Han, encountering circumstances deep and remote, ascending by steps onto Shu soil, isolated in a single corner, interfering with fortune and offending risk, gradually dragging through years, thereupon with the capital region was separated by ten thousand li.

entries.zh: 每惟黃初中，文皇帝命虎牙將軍鮮于輔，宣溫密之詔，申三好之恩，開示門戶，大義炳然，而否德闇弱，竊貪遣緒，俯仰累紀，未率大教。
entries.en: I still recall how in the Huangchu era Emperor Wen of Wei sent General Xianyu Fu with a gracious, confidential message offering peace on three counts and holding the door open to us. The moral case was luminous, yet I—small in virtue and dull of wit—clung to my father's legacy, bobbing through the years without answering that higher teaching.
entries.literal: Whenever I reflect on the Huangchu period, Emperor Wen ordered General Who Bares the Teeth Xianyu Fu to proclaim a warm and secret edict, extend the grace of threefold friendship, open and show the gate and door—great righteousness blazed bright—yet my deficient virtue is dim and weak; I secretly covet the thread left by those who departed; bowing and lifting my head through accumulated years, I have not followed the great instruction.

entries.zh: 天威既震，人鬼歸能之數，怖駭王師，神武所次，敢不革面，順以從命！
entries.en: Now that heavenly majesty has struck and every sign—human and spectral—points to submission, I tremble before your invincible host. Wherever it halts, how could I refuse to turn about and obey?
entries.literal: Heaven's might having shaken, the reckoning by which men and spirits submit to capability, fearing and trembling at the royal army, wherever divine martiality halts—how dare I not change face and comply with the command!

entries.zh: 輒敕群帥投戈釋甲，官府帑藏一無所毀。
entries.en: I have ordered every commander to stack arms and shed armor; no government office or state store is to be touched.
entries.literal: I immediately ordered the host of commanders to cast aside spears and strip armor; official bureaus and treasury stores are not to be harmed in the slightest.

entries.zh: 百姓布野，餘糧棲畝，以俟後來之惠，全元元之命。
entries.en: The people remain in their fields; grain still stands in the furrows, waiting for your mercy so their humble lives may be spared.
entries.literal: The hundred surnames are spread across the wilds; surplus grain lodges in the fields, in order to await later kindness, and preserve the lives of the multitude.

entries.zh: 伏惟大魏布德施化，宰輔伊、周，含覆藏疾。
entries.en: Great Wei spreads civilizing virtue; its ministers rival the ancient worthies Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou; its mercy covers even the flawed.
entries.literal: I humbly consider that Great Wei spreads virtue and applies transformation; its ministers are like Yi and Zhou; it covers and conceals even sickness.

entries.zh: 謹遣私署侍中張紹、光祿大夫譙周、駙馬都尉鄧良奉繼印綬，請命告誠，敬輸忠款，存亡敕賜，惟所裁之。
entries.en: I therefore send my acting palace attendant Zhang Shao, grandee of the household Qiao Zhou, and chief groom Deng Liang with the seals of state to beg for terms and declare our good faith. Life or death rests in your judgment alone.
entries.literal: I respectfully dispatch my privately appointed Palace Attendant Zhang Shao, Imperial Household Grandee Qiao Zhou, and Chief of the Capitals Grooms Deng Liang to present the seals and cords of succession, request a mandate and declare sincerity, respectfully offer loyal sincerity; as to life or death, command and grant—let it be as you decide.

entries.zh: 輿櫬在近，不復縷陳。
entries.en: My coffin awaits me just outside the wall; I need not belabor the point.
entries.literal: The bier-cart is near at hand; I will not again enumerate in detail.

entries.zh: 後主 劉禪
entries.en: The Later Lord: Liu Shan.
entries.literal: The Later Lord, Liu Shan.

entries.zh: 皇思夫人履行脩仁，淑慎其身。
entries.en: The late Lady of Imperial Remembrance lived with integrity and kindness, modest and guarded in deportment.
entries.literal: The Lady of Imperial Remembrance practiced conduct and cultivated benevolence, chaste and careful in her person.

entries.zh: 大行皇帝昔在上將，嬪妃作合，載育聖躬，大命不融。
entries.en: When our late sovereign was still a field commander, she joined him in wedlock and bore his heir, though heaven cut that union short.
entries.literal: The late emperor, in former days as a general, was matched with a consort who bore and nurtured his sacred person, yet the great mandate did not endure.

entries.zh: 大行皇帝存時，篤義垂恩，念皇思夫人神柩在遠飄颻，特遣使者奉迎。
entries.en: In his lifetime he never forgot her: learning her coffin still wandered far from the capital, he sent envoys to escort it home.
entries.literal: While the late emperor lived he was deeply dutiful and showed favor, remembering that the Lady of Imperial Remembrance’s spirit coffin drifted far away, and specially dispatched envoys to welcome it.

entries.zh: 會大行皇帝崩，今皇思夫人神柩以到，又梓宮在道，園陵將成，安厝有期。
entries.en: He has since died, yet her catafalque has now reached us while his own bier is still en route and the imperial tombs near completion, so both burials may soon be ordered.
entries.literal: It happened that the late emperor died; now the Lady of Imperial Remembrance’s spirit coffin has arrived, and moreover the catalpa coffin is on the road, the mausoleum park nearly complete, and the date for laying her to rest is set.

entries.zh: 臣輒與太常臣賴恭等議：《禮記》曰：『立愛自親始，教民孝也；
entries.en: I have consulted Minister Lai Gong and others. The Book of Rites teaches, 'Teach love by starting with one’s parents—thus the people learn filial piety;
entries.literal: Your servant has rashly deliberated with Minister of Ceremonies Lai Gong and others: the Record of Rites says, 'Establish love beginning with kin—this teaches the people filial piety;

entries.zh: 立敬自長始，教民順也。』
entries.en: teach respect by starting with one’s elders—thus the people learn deference.'
entries.literal: establish reverence beginning with elders—this teaches the people obedience.'

entries.zh: 不忘其親，所由生也。
entries.en: To forget not those who gave you life is the root of all moral feeling.
entries.literal: Not forgetting one’s kin is the source from which life proceeds.

entries.zh: 春秋之義，母以子貴。
entries.en: The Spring and Autumn canon holds that a mother’s rank rises with her son’s.
entries.literal: By the principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals, the mother is honored because of her son.

entries.zh: 昔高皇帝追尊太上昭靈夫人為昭靈皇后，孝和皇帝改葬其母梁貴人，尊號曰恭懷皇后，孝愍皇帝亦改葬其母王夫人，尊號曰靈懷皇后。
entries.en: Gaozu of Han raised his mother to Empress Zhaoling; He-di reinterred Lady Liang as Empress Gonghuai; Min-di did the same for Lady Wang as Empress Linghuai.
entries.literal: In antiquity the High Emperor posthumously honored the Grand Supreme Lady Zhao Ling as Empress Zhao Ling; Emperor Xiaohe reburied his mother the Honored Lady Liang with the title Empress Gonghuai; Emperor Xiaomin likewise reburied his mother Lady Wang with the title Empress Linghuai.

entries.zh: 今皇思夫人宜有尊號，以慰寒泉之思，輒與恭等案諡法，宜曰昭烈皇后。
entries.en: She therefore deserves a throne name that may comfort the living. We have weighed the statutes of posthumous honor and propose Empress Zhaolie.
entries.literal: Now the Lady of Imperial Remembrance ought to receive an exalted title to console thoughts from the cold spring; your servant has rashly with Gong and others examined the posthumous-title code—she should be called Empress Zhaolie.

entries.zh: 詩曰：『谷則異室，死則同穴。』
entries.en: The Classic of Poetry says, ‘We dwelt apart in life; we lie together in death.’
entries.literal: The Odes say, ‘In life we dwelt in different chambers; in death we share one grave.’

entries.zh: 〈《禮》云：上古無合葬，中古後因時方有。〉
entries.en: Commentary: The Rites note that joint burial was unknown in earliest ages and became practice only in later ages.〉
entries.literal: 〈The Rites states: In high antiquity there was no joint burial; from middle antiquity onward it arose with the times.〉

entries.zh: 故昭烈皇后宜與大行皇帝合葬，臣請太尉告宗廟，布露天下，具禮儀別奏。
entries.en: We therefore ask that she be laid beside the late emperor, that the grand commandant report this to the shrines of state, that an edict proclaim it to the realm, and that the detailed rites be submitted in a further memorial.
entries.literal: Therefore Empress Zhaolie ought to be buried with the late emperor; your servant requests the Grand Commandant announce this in the ancestral temples, publish it throughout the realm, and separately memorialize the full ritual observances.

entries.zh: 先主穆皇后，陳留人也。
entries.en: Lady Mu, empress of Liu Bei, came from Chenliu.
entries.literal: Empress Mu of the First Lord was a native of Chenliu.

entries.zh: 兄吳壹，少孤，壹父素與劉焉有舊，是以舉家隨焉入蜀。
entries.en: Her brother Wu Yi was orphaned young. Their father had been close to Liu Yan, so the whole family followed Yan into Shu.
entries.literal: Her elder brother was Wu Yi; orphaned young, Yi's father had long been on familiar terms with Liu Yan, and on that account the whole family followed Yan into Shu.

entries.zh: 焉有異志，而聞善相者相后當大貴。
entries.en: Liu Yan nurtured separate ambitions, and word came that a physiognomist had foretold the girl would rise to great rank.
entries.literal: Yan harbored separate ambitions, and it was heard that a skilled physiognomist predicted the empress would attain great honor.

entries.zh: 焉時將子瑁自隨，遂為瑁納后。
entries.en: Liu Yan then had his son Mao marry her.
entries.literal: At the time Yan took his son Mao with him; thereupon he had Mao take the empress in marriage.

entries.zh: 瑁死，后寡居。
entries.en: When Mao died she remained a widow.
entries.literal: Mao died; the empress lived in widowhood.

entries.zh: 先主既定益州，而孫夫人還吳，《漢晉春秋》云：先主入益州，吳遣迎孫夫人。
entries.en: Once Liu Bei held Yizhou, Lady Sun went back to Wu. The Spring and Autumn of Han and Jin says Wu sent to fetch her when Liu Bei entered Yizhou.
entries.literal: After the First Lord had settled Yizhou, Lady Sun returned to Wu. The Spring and Autumn of Han and Jin states: When the First Lord entered Yizhou, Wu sent to welcome Lady Sun.

entries.zh: 夫人欲將太子歸吳，諸葛亮使趙雲勒兵斷江留太子，乃得止。
entries.en: She meant to take the crown prince with her, but Zhuge Liang had Zhao Yun seal the river and keep the boy—only then was she stopped.
entries.literal: The lady wished to take the crown prince back to Wu; Zhuge Liang had Zhao Yun draw up troops and block the river to keep the crown prince—only then was it stopped.

entries.zh: 群下勸先主聘后，先主疑與瑁同族，法正進曰：「論其親疏，何與晉文之於子圉乎？」
entries.en: His court urged Liu Bei to wed her, but he worried she was kin to Mao. Fa Zheng argued: "By closeness of kin, how does this resemble Duke Wen of Jin and Zi Yu?"
entries.literal: The assembly urged the First Lord to take the empress as bride; the First Lord suspected she was of the same clan as Mao. Fa Zheng advanced and said, "As to degrees of kinship, how does this compare with Duke Wen of Jin and Zi Yu?"

entries.zh: 於是納后為夫人。
entries.en: He then took her as consort.
entries.literal: Thereupon he took the empress in as his lady.

entries.zh: 習鑿齒曰：夫婚姻，人倫之始，王化之本，匹夫猶不可以無禮，而況人君乎？
entries.en: Xi Zaochi wrote: Marriage begins human order and grounds royal civilizing rule; even commoners must observe ritual—how much more a sovereign?
entries.literal: Xi Zaochi said: Marriage is the beginning of human relations and the root of royal transformation; even common men cannot lack ritual—how much more a ruler?

entries.zh: 晉文廢禮行權，以濟其業，故子犯曰，有求於人，必先從之，將奪其國，何有於妻，非無故而違禮教者也。
entries.en: Duke Wen of Jin set ritual aside and used expedient power to save his cause; hence Zi Fan said that when one needs others one must first yield, and when one is about to seize a state what care is there for a wife?—that was not capricious breach of ritual.
entries.literal: Duke Wen of Jin set ritual aside and exercised expedient power to save his enterprise; hence Zi Fan said: when one has need of others, one must first yield to them; about to seize their state, what care for a wife?—this was not violating ritual teaching without cause.

entries.zh: 今先主無權事之偪，而引前失以為譬，非導其君以堯、舜之道者。
entries.en: Liu Bei faced no such coercion, yet Fa Zheng cited an old lapse as precedent—this was not guiding a ruler along the path of Yao and Shun.
entries.literal: Now the First Lord had no coercion of expedient affairs, yet cited a past fault as precedent—this is not guiding one's lord by the Way of Yao and Shun.

entries.zh: 先主從之，過矣。
entries.en: Liu Bei took the advice—a mistake, in Xi Zaochi's view.
entries.literal: The First Lord followed it—an error.

entries.zh: 建安二十四年，立為漢中王后。
entries.en: In Jian'an 24 she was made queen of Hanzhong.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Jian'an she was established as queen of Hanzhong.

entries.zh: 章武元年夏五月，策曰：「朕承天命，奉至尊，臨萬國。
entries.en: In the fifth month of Zhangwu 1 an edict ran: "I receive Heaven's mandate, hold supreme dignity, and rule the myriad states.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of summer in the first year of Zhangwu the patent read, "We receive Heaven's mandate, hold the supreme dignity, and face the myriad states.

entries.zh: 今以后為皇后，遣使持節丞相亮授璽綬，承宗廟，母天下，皇后其敬之哉！」
entries.en: I now make the empress queen, send envoys with the imperial baton for Chancellor Zhuge Liang to confer her seals and cords, that she may receive the ancestral shrines and mother the realm—revere this charge, O empress!"
entries.literal: Now We make the empress queen, dispatch envoys bearing the tally for Chancellor Liang to confer seals and ribbons, to receive the ancestral temples and mother the realm—may the empress revere this charge!"

entries.zh: 建興元年223年五月，後主即位，尊后為皇太后，稱長樂宮。
entries.en: In the fifth month of Jianxing 1 (223 CE) Liu Shan succeeded and raised her to empress dowager of Changle Palace.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Jianxing (223 CE) the Later Lord ascended the throne and honored the empress as empress dowager, with her residence called Changle Palace.

entries.zh: 壹官至車騎將軍，封縣侯。
entries.en: Wu Yi rose to general of chariots and cavalry and received a district marquisate.
entries.literal: Yi rose to General of Chariots and Cavalry and was enfeoffed as a district marquis.

entries.zh: 延熙八年，后薨，合葬惠陵。
entries.en: In Yanxi 8 she died and was interred with Liu Bei at Huiling.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Yanxi the empress died and was buried with the First Lord at Huiling.

entries.zh: 孫盛《蜀世譜》曰：壹孫喬，沒李雄中三十年，不為雄屈也。
entries.en: Sun Sheng's Shu genealogy notes that Wu Yi's grandson Qiao, held among Li Xiong's forces for thirty years, never bowed to Xiong.
entries.literal: Sun Sheng's Genealogy of Shu states: Yi's grandson Qiao, captured among Li Xiong's forces for thirty years, would not submit to Xiong.

entries.zh: 後主太子璿，字文衡。
entries.en: Liu Xuan, styled Wenheng, was Liu Shan’s heir apparent.
entries.literal: Crown Prince Xuan of the Later Lord, courtesy Wenheng.

entries.zh: 母王貴人，本敬哀張皇后侍人也。
entries.en: His mother was Lady Wang, once a maid to Empress Jing’ai of the Zhang clan.
entries.literal: His mother was Honored Lady Wang, originally a handmaid of Empress Jing’ai née Zhang.

entries.zh: 延熙元年正月策曰：「在昔帝王，繼體立嗣，副貳國統，古今常道。
entries.en: Yanxi 1 opened with an edict: “Since antiquity sovereigns have named heirs to carry on the flesh and serve as second to the throne—
entries.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yanxi the patent said, "Of old emperors and kings, continuing the body and establishing the heir, appointing a deputy for the state’s succession, has been the constant way from ancient to present.

entries.zh: 今以璿為皇太子，昭顯祖宗之威，命使行丞相事左將軍朗持節授印緩。
entries.en: We therefore invest Liu Xuan as crown prince so the ancestors’ awe may shine abroad, and We dispatch Lang, left general acting as chancellor, with the imperial baton to present his seals and cords.
entries.literal: Now We make Xuan crown prince, to manifest the majesty of the ancestors; We order Lang, acting as chancellor and general of the left, to bear the tally and confer seals and ribbons.

entries.zh: 其勉脩茂質，祗恪道義，諮詢典禮，敬友師傅，斟酌眾善，翼成爾德，可不務脩以自勗哉！」
entries.en: Cultivate excellence in yourself, hold fast to duty and the moral law, study the rites, honor your teachers, sift good counsel from many voices, and so grow into virtue—how could you not strive to improve and press yourself forward?”
entries.literal: Strive to cultivate a rich nature, reverently keep to the Way and its duties, consult the canons of ritual, respectfully befriend your tutors, weigh the counsel of many good men, and thereby wing your virtue—can you fail to labor at cultivation and urge yourself onward!"

entries.zh: 時年十五。
entries.en: He was fifteen sui at the time.
entries.literal: At that time he was fifteen.

entries.zh: 景耀六年冬，蜀亡。
entries.en: In the winter of Jingyao 6 the state of Shu was extinguished.
entries.literal: In the winter of the sixth year of Jingyao Shu fell.

entries.zh: 咸熙元年正月，鍾會作亂於成都，璿為亂兵所害。
entries.en: In the first month of Xianxi 1 Zhong Hui mutinied at Chengdu, and Liu Xuan was cut down by the riotous soldiery.
entries.literal: In the first month of the first year of Xianxi Zhong Hui raised rebellion in Chengdu, and Xuan was killed by mutinous troops.

entries.zh: 〈孫盛《蜀世譜》曰：璿弟，瑤、琮、瓚、諶、恂、璩六人。
entries.en: 〈Sun Sheng’s Shu genealogy lists six younger brothers: Yao, Cong, Zan, Chen, Xun, and Qu.
entries.literal: 〈Sun Sheng’s Genealogy of Shu states: Xuan had younger brothers Yao, Cong, Zan, Chen, Xun, and Qu—six men.

entries.zh: 蜀敗，諶自殺，餘皆內徙。
entries.en: When Shu collapsed Chen took his own life; the others were deported to the interior.
entries.literal: When Shu fell, Chen committed suicide; the rest were moved inward.

entries.zh: 值永嘉大亂，子孫絕滅。
entries.en: The Yongjia upheavals wiped out their posterity.
entries.literal: They encountered the great turmoil of Yongjia, and descendants were cut off.

entries.zh: 唯永孫玄奔蜀，李雄偽署安樂公以嗣禪後。
entries.en: Only Liu Yong’s grandson Liu Xuan escaped back into Shu, where Li Xiong named him duke of Anle in mock succession to Liu Shan.
entries.literal: Only Yong’s grandson Xuan fled to Shu, and Li Xiong falsely installed him as duke of Anle to continue the line after Shan.

entries.zh: 永和三年討李勢，盛參戎行，見玄於成都也。〉
entries.en: In Yonghe 3, during the expedition against Li Shi, Sun Sheng himself saw Liu Xuan in Chengdu.〉
entries.literal: In the third year of Yonghe, when Li Shi was campaigned against, Sheng took part in the army and saw Xuan at Chengdu.〉

entries.zh: 後主張皇后，前后敬哀之妹也。
entries.en: Liu Shan's Empress Zhang was the younger sister of Empress Jing'ai.
entries.literal: Empress Zhang of the Later Lord was the younger sister of the former Empress Jing'ai.

entries.zh: 建興十五年237年，入為貴人。
entries.en: In Jianxing 15 (237 CE) she entered the palace as an honored lady.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year of Jianxing (237 CE) she entered the palace as an honored lady.

entries.zh: 延熙元年238年春正月，策曰：「朕統承大業，君臨天下，奉郊廟社稷。
entries.en: In the first month of Yanxi 1 (238 CE) an edict ran: "I inherit the great enterprise, rule the realm, and serve the suburban altars and state shrines.
entries.literal: In the first month of spring in the first year of Yanxi (238 CE) the patent read, "We inherit the great enterprise, face the realm, and serve the suburban altars and state shrines.

entries.zh: 今以貴人為皇后，使行丞相事左將軍向朗持節授璽綬。
entries.en: I now make the honored lady empress and dispatch Xiang Lang, left general acting as chancellor, with the imperial baton to present her seals and cords.
entries.literal: Now We make the honored lady empress, and order Xiang Lang, left general acting as chancellor, to bear the tally and confer seals and ribbons.

entries.zh: 勉脩中饋，恪肅禋祀，皇后其敬之哉！」
entries.en: Cultivate the inner household and reverently keep the state sacrifices—revere this charge, O empress!"
entries.literal: Strive to cultivate inner household duties and reverently keep sacrificial rites—may the empress revere this charge!"

entries.zh: 咸熙元年，隨後主遷於洛陽。
entries.en: In Xianxi 1 she followed Liu Shan to Luoyang.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xianxi she followed the Later Lord in removal to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 《漢晉春秋》曰：魏以蜀宮人賜諸將之無妻者，李昭儀曰：「我不能二三屈辱。」
entries.en: The Spring and Autumn of Han and Jin says Wei gave Shu palace women to generals without wives. Lady Li, the Zhaoyi, said, "I cannot endure repeated humiliation."
entries.literal: The Spring and Autumn of Han and Jin states: Wei gave Shu palace women to generals without wives; Lady Li the Zhaoyi said, "I cannot endure repeated humiliation."

entries.zh: 乃自殺。
entries.en: She then took her own life.
entries.literal: Thereupon she killed herself.

entries.zh: 劉永字公壽，先主子，後主庶弟也。
entries.en: Liu Yong, styled Gongshou, was Liu Bei's son and Liu Shan's younger half-brother.
entries.literal: Liu Yong, courtesy Gongshou, was a son of the First Lord and a younger half-brother of the Later Lord.

entries.zh: 章武元年六月，使司徒靖立永為魯王，策曰：「小子永，受茲青土。
entries.en: In the sixth month of Zhangwu 1 Liu Bei ordered Xu Jing, minister of education, to enfeoff Liu Yong as prince of Lu. The edict ran: "Young Liu Yong, receive this azure soil.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Zhangwu the emperor ordered Minister of Education Xu Jing to invest Yong as Prince of Lu; the patent read, "Young Yong, receive this azure soil.

entries.zh: 朕承天序，繼統大業，遵脩稽古，建爾國家，封於東土，奄有龜蒙，世為籓輔。
entries.en: I carry on Heaven's line, continue the great enterprise, observe antiquity, establish your state, enfeoff you in the east, embrace Gui and Meng, and make you a feudal shield for generations.
entries.literal: We inherit Heaven's sequence, continue the great enterprise, observe and restore antiquity, establish your state and house, enfeoff you in the eastern lands, embrace Gui and Meng, and make you a feudal bulwark for generations.

entries.zh: 嗚呼，恭朕之詔！
entries.en: Revere this charge of mine!
entries.literal: Alas, revere Our edict!

entries.zh: 惟彼魯邦，一變適道，風化存焉。
entries.en: Lu, once transformed, was fit for the Way; civilizing rule endures there.
entries.literal: That state of Lu, once transformed, was fit for the Way; civilizing transformation abides there.

entries.zh: 人之好德，世茲懿美。
entries.en: Its people's love of virtue is a lasting excellence.
entries.literal: Men's love of virtue there is ever this excellent beauty.

entries.zh: 王其秉心率禮，綏爾士民，是饗是宜，其戒之哉！」
entries.en: Hold your heart to ritual, pacify your officers and people, receive what is fitting—revere this charge, my prince!"
entries.literal: May you, my prince, hold your heart and lead by ritual, pacify your officers and people, receive and keep what is fitting—revere this charge!"

entries.zh: 建興八年230年，改封為甘陵王。
entries.en: In Jianxing 8 (230 CE) his title was changed to prince of Ganling.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Jianxing (230 CE) his fief was changed to Prince of Ganling.

entries.zh: 初，永憎宦人黃皓，皓既信任用事，譖構永於後主，後主稍疏外永，至不得朝見者十餘年。
entries.en: Liu Yong hated the eunuch Huang Hao. Once Huang Hao gained power he slandered Liu Yong to Liu Shan, who gradually kept him at arm's length until for more than ten years he could not attend court.
entries.literal: At first Yong detested the eunuch Huang Hao; once Hao gained trust and wielded power he slandered Yong to the Later Lord, and the Later Lord gradually kept Yong at a distance until for more than ten years he could not attend court audiences.

entries.zh: 咸熙元年，永東遷洛陽，拜奉車都尉，封為鄉侯。
entries.en: In Xianxi 1 Liu Yong went east to Luoyang, became commandant of the imperial carriage, and received a village marquisate.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xianxi Yong moved east to Luoyang, was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Carriage, and enfeoffed as a village marquis.

entries.zh: 劉理字奉孝，亦後主庶弟也，與永異母。
entries.en: Liu Li, styled Fengxiao, was another younger half-brother of Liu Shan, not born to the same mother as Liu Yong.
entries.literal: Liu Li, courtesy Fengxiao, was also a younger half-brother of the Later Lord by a different mother from Yong.

entries.zh: 章武元年六月，使司徒靖立理為梁王，策曰：「小子理，朕統承漢序，祗順天命，遵脩典秩，建爾於東，為漢籓輔。
entries.en: In the sixth month of Zhangwu 1 Liu Bei ordered Xu Jing, minister of education, to enfeoff Liu Li as prince of Liang. The edict ran: “Young Liu Li, I carry on Han’s line, bow to heaven’s charge, and uphold the statutes; I therefore enfeoff you in the east as a feudal shield of the house of Han.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Zhangwu the emperor ordered Minister of Education Xu Jing to invest Li as Prince of Liang; the patent read, "Young Li, We inherit the sequence of Han, reverently obey Heaven’s mandate, observe canonical order, and establish you in the east as a feudal bulwark of Han.

entries.zh: 惟彼梁土，畿甸之邦，民狎教化，易導以禮。
entries.en: Liang lies within the royal domain; its people are used to civilizing rule and readily led by ritual.
entries.literal: That land of Liang is a domain within the capital region; the people are intimate with instruction and easily guided by ritual.

entries.zh: 往悉乃心，懷保黎庶，以永爾國，王其敬之哉！」
entries.en: Go with a whole heart, shelter the common folk, and so long preserve your state—revere this charge, my prince!”
entries.literal: Go forth with all your heart, cherish and protect the black-haired masses, and thereby perpetuate your state—may you, my prince, revere these words!"

entries.zh: 建興八年，改封理為安平王。
entries.en: In Jianxing 8 his title was changed to prince of Anping.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Jianxing Li’s fief was changed to Prince of Anping.

entries.zh: 延熙七年卒，諡曰悼王。
entries.en: He died in Yanxi 7 and received the posthumous epithet Prince Dao (Lamented).
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Yanxi he died; his posthumous title was Prince Dao.

entries.zh: 子哀王胤嗣，十九年卒。
entries.en: His son Yin, prince Ai, succeeded and died in the nineteenth year.
entries.literal: His son Prince Ai Yin succeeded; in the nineteenth year he died.

entries.zh: 子殤王承嗣，二十年卒。
entries.en: Cheng, prince Shang, followed and died in the twentieth year.
entries.literal: His son Prince Shang Cheng succeeded; in the twentieth year he died.

entries.zh: 景耀四年詔曰：「安平王，先帝所命。
entries.en: Jingyao 4 brought an edict: “The prince of Anping was enfeoffed by the late sovereign.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Jingyao an edict said, "The Prince of Anping was enfeoffed by the late emperor.

entries.zh: 三世早夭，國嗣頹絕，朕用傷悼。
entries.en: Three heirs in a row have perished young, leaving the fief without an heir, and We mourn that break.
entries.literal: Three generations have died young in succession, and the line of succession has broken off; We are thereby grieved.

entries.zh: 其以武邑侯輯襲王位。」
entries.en: We therefore order Ji, marquis of Wuyi, to inherit the princedom.”
entries.literal: Let Marquis of Wuyi Ji succeed to the princedom."

entries.zh: 輯，理子也，咸熙元年，東遷洛陽，拜奉車都尉，封鄉侯。
entries.en: Ji was Liu Li’s son. In Xianxi 1 he went east to Luoyang, became commandant of the imperial carriage, and received a village marquisate.
entries.literal: Ji was Li’s son; in the first year of Xianxi he moved east to Luoyang, was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Carriage, and enfeoffed as village marquis.

entries.zh: 先主甘皇后
entries.en: Lady Gan, consort of Liu Bei (styled the First Lord)
entries.literal: Empress Gan of the First Lord

entries.zh: 先主自葭萌還攻劉璋，召諸葛亮。
entries.en: The First Lord marched back from Jiameng against Liu Zhang and called up Zhuge Liang.
entries.literal: The First Lord returned from Jiameng to attack Liu Zhang and summoned Zhuge Liang.

entries.zh: 亮率雲與張飛等俱溯江西上，平定郡縣。
entries.en: Zhuge Liang took Zhao Yun, Zhang Fei, and the rest up the river westward, reducing counties as they went.
entries.literal: Liang led Yun together with Zhang Fei and others alike upriver west, pacifying commanderies and districts.

entries.zh: 至江州，分遣雲從外水上江陽，與亮會於成都。
entries.en: At Jiangzhou he detached Zhao Yun up the outer water route to Jiangyang to rendezvous with Zhuge Liang at Chengdu.
entries.literal: Reaching Jiangzhou, he separately dispatched Yun from the outer waters up to Jiangyang to meet Liang at Chengdu.

entries.zh: 成都既定，以雲為翊軍將軍。
entries.en: Once Chengdu was secure, he named Zhao Yun General Who Aids the Army.
entries.literal: When Chengdu was settled, he made Yun General Who Aids the Army.

entries.zh: 雲別傳曰：益州既定，時議欲以成都中屋舍及城外園地桑田分賜諸將。
entries.en: The Zhao Yun biezhuan records that after Yizhou was pacified, some proposed dividing Chengdu houses and suburban gardens and mulberry fields among the generals.
entries.literal: The Zhao Yun biezhuan states: When Yizhou was settled, at the time there was discussion of wanting to divide and grant to the various generals the houses within Chengdu and the garden lands and mulberry fields outside the walls.

entries.zh: 雲駮之曰：「霍去病以匈奴未滅，無用家為，令國賊非但匈奴，未可求安也。
entries.en: Zhao Yun objected: "Huo Qubing said that while the Xiongnu still lived, a man had no business building a home; our state's foe is not the Xiongnu alone—we cannot settle into comfort yet.
entries.literal: Yun rebutted, saying, "Huo Qubing, because the Xiongnu were not yet destroyed, had no use for a home; now the state's enemy is not only the Xiongnu—one cannot seek ease.

entries.zh: 須天下都定，各反桑梓，歸耕本土，乃其宜耳。
entries.en: Only when the realm is wholly at peace should each man return home and till his own fields—that is the proper course.
entries.literal: Only when all under Heaven is fully settled should each return to his native place and go back to farm his homeland—that is fitting.

entries.zh: 益州人民，初罹兵革，田宅皆可歸還，今安居複業，然後可役調，得其歡心。」
entries.en: The people of Yizhou have only just endured war; their fields and homes should be restored. Let them settle and resume their livelihoods first—only then levy service and taxes and win their goodwill."
entries.literal: The people of Yizhou had just suffered war; fields and dwellings can all be returned; now let them settle and resume their occupations, and only then can levies and corvée be imposed to win their hearts."

entries.zh: 先主即從之。
entries.en: The First Lord accepted the advice at once.
entries.literal: The First Lord at once followed this advice.

entries.zh: 夏侯淵敗，曹公爭漢中地，運米北山下，數千萬囊。
entries.en: After Xiahou Yuan's defeat, Lord Cao fought for Hanzhong and hauled grain in tens of millions of sacks to the foot of North Mountain.
entries.literal: Xiahou Yuan was defeated; Lord Cao contested Hanzhong territory and transported grain to the foot of North Mountain—tens of millions of sacks.

entries.zh: 黃忠以為可取，雲兵隨忠取米。
entries.en: Huang Zhong judged the stores ripe for the taking, and Zhao Yun's men went with him to seize the grain.
entries.literal: Huang Zhong thought it could be taken; Yun's troops followed Zhong to seize the grain.

entries.zh: 忠過期不還，雲將數十騎輕行出圍，迎視忠等。
entries.en: When Huang Zhong failed to return on time, Zhao Yun took a few dozen horsemen on a swift ride out of camp to find him.
entries.literal: When Zhong passed the deadline and did not return, Yun led several dozen horsemen on a light sortie out of the encampment to meet and look in on Zhong and the others.

entries.zh: 值曹公揚兵大出，雲為公前鋒所擊，方戰，其大眾至，勢偪，遂前突其陳，且鬥且卻。
entries.en: Lord Cao marched out in strength; Zhao Yun collided with the vanguard and, as the main host closed in, drove into the enemy line while fighting his way back.
entries.literal: He encountered Lord Cao raising troops and coming out in force; Yun was struck by the Lord's vanguard. As he was fighting, the enemy's main force arrived; the situation pressed hard, so he charged forward into their formation, fighting as he retreated.

entries.zh: 公軍散，已復合，雲陷敵，還趣圍。
entries.en: The Wei ranks broke, then re-formed; Zhao Yun was trapped among the enemy and wheeled back toward his camp.
entries.literal: The Lord's army scattered, then rallied again; Yun was cut off among the enemy and turned back toward the encampment.

entries.zh: 將張著被創，雲復馳馬還營迎著。
entries.en: General Zhang Zhu was wounded, and Zhao Yun galloped back into camp to bring him out.
entries.literal: General Zhang Zhu was wounded; Yun again galloped back to camp to receive Zhu.

entries.zh: 公軍追至圍，此時沔陽長張翼在雲圍內，翼欲閉門拒守，而雲入營，更大開門，偃旗息鼓。
entries.en: Wei troops pressed to the stockade. Zhang Yi, magistrate of Mianyang, was inside and meant to shut the gates; Zhao Yun entered, threw the gates wide, lowered the banners, and silenced the drums.
entries.literal: The Lord's army pursued to the encampment. At that time Zhang Yi, magistrate of Mianyang, was inside Yun's encampment and wished to close the gate and hold in defense; but Yun entered the camp and instead opened the gate wide, lowered the banners, and silenced the drums.

entries.zh: 公軍疑雲有伏兵，引去。
entries.en: The Wei army suspected an ambush and withdrew.
entries.literal: The Lord's army suspected Yun had ambush troops and withdrew.

entries.zh: 雲雷鼓震天，惟以戎弩於後射公軍，公軍驚駭，自相蹂踐，墮漢水中死者甚多。
entries.en: Zhao Yun rolled the drums to heaven and raked the retreating Wei ranks with crossbows from the rear; panic broke their lines, and many drowned in the Han River.
entries.literal: Yun thundered the drums to shake heaven and with crossbows alone shot at the Lord's army from behind; the Lord's army was shocked and terrified, trampled one another, and many fell into the Han River and died.

entries.zh: 先主明旦自來至雲營圍視昨戰處，曰：「子龍一身都是膽也。」
entries.en: The next morning the First Lord came in person to Zhao Yun's camp to see the field of battle and said, "Zilong is courage from head to foot."
entries.literal: The next morning the First Lord came in person to Yun's encampment to view yesterday's battlefield and said, "Zilong's whole body is courage."

entries.zh: 作樂飲宴至暝，軍中號雲為虎威將軍。
entries.en: There was music and feasting until dusk, and the army styled Zhao Yun General Who Displays Tiger Might.
entries.literal: Music was made and a banquet held until dusk; in the army Yun was styled General Who Displays Tiger Might.

entries.zh: 孫權襲荊州，先主大怒，欲討權。
entries.en: When Sun Quan seized Jing Province, the First Lord was furious and meant to march against him.
entries.literal: Sun Quan raided Jing Province; the First Lord was greatly enraged and wished to campaign against Quan.

entries.zh: 雲諫曰：「國賊是曹操，非孫權也，且先滅魏，則吳自服。
entries.en: Zhao Yun remonstrated: "The state's enemy is Cao Cao, not Sun Quan. Destroy Wei first and Wu will submit of itself.
entries.literal: Yun remonstrated, saying, "The state's enemy is Cao Cao, not Sun Quan; moreover, if Wei is destroyed first, then Wu will submit of itself.

entries.zh: 操身雖斃，子丕篡盜，當因眾心，早圖關中，居河、渭上流以討凶逆，關東義士必裹糧策馬以迎王師。
entries.en: Though Cao Cao is dead, his son Pi has usurped the throne. Seize the people's will, take Guanzhong early, hold the upper He and Wei, and march against the traitors—the righteous east of the Pass will saddle up with grain to welcome the royal army.
entries.literal: Though Cao's person has perished, his son Pi usurped and stole the throne; one should follow the people's hearts, plan early for Guanzhong, hold the upper reaches of the He and Wei rivers to campaign against the traitors, and the righteous men east of the Pass will surely wrap grain and spur their horses to welcome the royal army.

entries.zh: 不應置魏，先與吳戰；
entries.en: Do not set Wei aside to fight Wu first;
entries.literal: One should not set Wei aside and fight Wu first;

entries.zh: 兵勢一交，不得卒解。」
entries.en: once arms are joined, the war cannot quickly be ended."
entries.literal: once military momentum is joined, it cannot be quickly resolved."

entries.zh: 先主不聽，遂東征，留雲督江州。
entries.en: The First Lord would not listen and marched east, leaving Zhao Yun to oversee Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: The First Lord did not heed this and thereupon campaigned east, leaving Yun to oversee Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 先主失利於秭歸，雲進兵至永安，吳軍已退。
entries.en: After the First Lord's defeat at Zigui, Zhao Yun advanced to Yong'an and found the Wu army already gone.
entries.literal: The First Lord met defeat at Zigui; Yun advanced to Yong'an and the Wu army had already withdrawn.

entries.zh: 建興元年，為中護軍、征南將軍，封永昌亭侯，遷鎮東將軍。
entries.en: In Jianxing 1 (223) he became central protector of the army and general who conquers the south, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongchang precinct, and rose to general who guards the east.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianxing he became Central Protector of the Army and General Who Conquers the South, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongchang precinct, and was transferred to General Who Guards the East.

entries.zh: 五年，隨諸葛亮駐漢中。
entries.en: In the fifth year he followed Zhuge Liang to garrison Hanzhong.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he followed Zhuge Liang in garrisoning Hanzhong.

entries.zh: 明年，亮出軍，揚聲由斜谷道，曹真遣大眾當之。
entries.en: The next year Zhuge Liang marched out, loudly declaring the Xie Valley route; Cao Zhen sent a great host to meet him.
entries.literal: The next year Liang marched out, publicly declaring he would take the Xie Valley route; Cao Zhen sent a large force to oppose him.

entries.zh: 亮令雲與鄧芝往拒，而身攻祁山。
entries.en: Zhuge Liang sent Zhao Yun and Deng Zhi to hold the line while he struck Qishan himself.
entries.literal: Liang ordered Yun and Deng Zhi to go resist while he himself attacked Mount Qi.

entries.zh: 雲、芝兵弱敵強，失利於箕谷，然斂眾固守，不至大敗。
entries.en: Zhao Yun and Deng Zhi were outmatched and lost at Jigu, yet gathered their men, held firm, and escaped catastrophe.
entries.literal: Yun and Zhi's troops were weak and the enemy strong; they met defeat at Jigu, yet gathered the force and held firm without suffering great defeat.

entries.zh: 軍退，貶為鎮軍將軍。
entries.en: After the withdrawal he was demoted to general who guards the army.
entries.literal: When the army withdrew, he was demoted to General Who Guards the Army.

entries.zh: 雲別傳曰：亮曰：「街亭軍退，兵將不復相錄，箕穀軍退，兵將初不相失，何故？」
entries.en: The Zhao Yun biezhuan records Zhuge Liang saying, "At Jieting the army broke and officers and men could not find one another; at Jigu the army withdrew yet officers and men never lost one another—why?"
entries.literal: The Zhao Yun biezhuan states: Liang said, "When the Jieting army withdrew, soldiers and generals could no longer find one another; when the Jigu army withdrew, soldiers and generals at first did not lose one another—why?"

entries.zh: 芝答曰：「雲身自斷後，軍資什物，略無所棄，兵將無緣相失。」
entries.en: Deng Zhi answered, "Zhao Yun covered the retreat himself; stores and gear were scarcely abandoned—officers and men had no chance to lose one another."
entries.literal: Zhi answered, "Yun personally covered the retreat; army supplies and goods were almost nothing abandoned—soldiers and generals had no occasion to lose one another."

entries.zh: 雲有軍資餘絹，亮使分賜將士，雲曰：「軍事無利，何為有賜？
entries.en: Zhao Yun still held surplus army silk; Zhuge Liang had it divided among the officers and soldiers. Zhao Yun said, "The campaign brought no gain—why grant gifts?
entries.literal: Yun had surplus silk from army supplies; Liang had it divided and granted to officers and soldiers. Yun said, "The military campaign brought no gain—why should there be gifts?

entries.zh: 其物請悉入赤岸府庫，須十月為冬賜。」
entries.en: Put it all in the Chian treasury and hold it for the winter grant in the tenth month."
entries.literal: Please put all these goods into the Chian office storehouses and wait until the tenth month for the winter grant."

entries.zh: 亮大善之。
entries.en: Zhuge Liang greatly approved.
entries.literal: Liang greatly approved of this.

entries.zh: 關羽字雲長，本字長生，河東解人也。
entries.en: Guan Yu, styled Yunzhang—his original style was Changsheng—came from Jie in Hedong.
entries.literal: Guan Yu, courtesy name Yunzhang, originally courtesy name Changsheng, was a native of Jie in Hedong.

entries.zh: 亡命奔涿郡。
entries.en: He fled the law and made his way to Zhuo commandery.
entries.literal: He fled as an outlaw and ran to Zhuo commandery.

entries.zh: 先主於鄉里合徒眾，而羽與張飛為之禦侮。
entries.en: While the First Lord was raising a band of men in his home country, Guan Yu and Zhang Fei stood as his shield against abuse and attack.
entries.literal: When the First Lord gathered followers in his home district, Yu together with Zhang Fei defended him from insult and harm.

entries.zh: 先主為平原相，以羽、飛為別部司馬，分統部曲。
entries.en: Once the First Lord was appointed Administrator of Pingyuan, he made Guan Yu and Zhang Fei Separate Command Majors, splitting the command of their forces between them.
entries.literal: When the First Lord became Administrator of Pingyuan, he appointed Yu and Fei as Separate Command Majors, each commanding a division of troops.

entries.zh: 先主與二人寢則同床，恩若兄弟。
entries.en: The First Lord slept on the same couch with the two of them, and the affection among them was like that of brothers.
entries.literal: The First Lord with the two of them, when sleeping, shared one bed; their kindness was like that of brothers.

entries.zh: 而稠人廣坐，侍立終日，隨先主周旋，不避艱險。
entries.en: Even in thronged halls and before large assemblies they would stand attendance the whole day through, attending the First Lord wherever he went, never shrinking from hardship or peril.
entries.literal: Yet in crowded places and at public gatherings they stood in attendance all day, following the First Lord in his comings and goings, not shunning hardship or danger.

entries.zh: 〈蜀記曰：曹公與劉備圍呂布於下邳，關羽啟公，布使秦宜祿行求救，乞娶其妻，公許之。
entries.en: 〈The Shu Ji records that when Lord Cao and Liu Bei had Lü Bu bottled up at Xiapi, Guan Yu petitioned him: Lü Bu had sent Qin Yilu out to plead for help, and Guan Yu asked leave to take Qin's wife in marriage; Lord Cao agreed.
entries.literal: 〈The Shu Ji states: Lord Cao and Liu Bei besieged Lü Bu at Xiapi. Guan Yu reported to the Lord that, when Lü Bu had Qin Yilu go out to seek rescue, he begged to marry Qin's wife, and the Lord granted it.

entries.zh: 臨破，又屢啟於公。
entries.en: When the city was on the verge of being taken, he pressed the matter again and again with Lord Cao.
entries.literal: As the city was about to fall, he repeatedly reported to the Lord.

entries.zh: 公疑其有異色，先遣迎看，因自留之，羽心不自安。
entries.en: Lord Cao suspected the woman was strikingly beautiful, sent someone ahead to fetch and inspect her, then kept her for himself—leaving Guan Yu uneasy in his mind.
entries.literal: The Lord suspected she had unusual beauty, first sent men to meet and look at her, and therefore kept her himself; Yu's heart was not at ease.

entries.zh: 此與魏氏春秋所說無異也。〉
entries.en: This matches the account given in the Wei shi chunqiu.〉
entries.literal: This is no different from what the Wei shi chunqiu says.〉

entries.zh: 先主之襲殺徐州刺史車胄，使羽守下邳城，行太守事，
entries.en: When the First Lord struck down Xu Province Inspector Che Zhou in a surprise attack, he left Guan Yu to hold Xiapi and conduct the duties of Administrator.
entries.literal: When the First Lord suddenly attacked and killed the Inspector of Xu Province, Che Zhou, he had Yu guard Xiapi city and act as Administrator.

entries.zh: 〈《魏書》云：以羽領徐州。〉
entries.en: 〈The Wei shu adds that Guan Yu was given authority over Xu Province.〉
entries.literal: 〈The Wei shu states: Yu was placed in charge of Xu Province.〉

entries.zh: 而身還小沛。
entries.en: The First Lord himself meanwhile withdrew to Xiao Pei.
entries.literal: While he himself returned to Xiao Pei.

entries.zh: 龐統字士元，襄陽人也。
entries.en: Pang Tong, whose courtesy name was Shiyuan, came from Xiangyang.
entries.literal: Pang Tong, courtesy name Shiyuan, was a man of Xiangyang.

entries.zh: 少時樸鈍，未有識者。
entries.en: As a boy he seemed dull and unremarkable, and no one yet appreciated him.
entries.literal: In youth he was plain and slow-witted; no one recognized his talent.

entries.zh: 潁川司馬徽清雅有知人鑒，統弱冠往見徽，徽採桑於樹上，坐統在樹下，共語自晝至夜。
entries.en: Sima Hui of Yingchuan was elegant and had a gift for sizing people up. When Tong came of age he paid him a visit: Hui was in a mulberry tree gathering leaves, had Tong sit below, and they conversed from dawn into the night.
entries.literal: Sima Hui of Yingchuan was refined and discerning in judging men; when Tong reached his capped years he went to visit Hui. Hui was picking mulberries in a tree and seated Tong beneath the tree; they talked from day until night.

entries.zh: 徽甚異之，稱統當南州士之冠冕，由是漸顯。
entries.en: Hui found him remarkable and said Tong would stand first among the gentlemen of the south; thereafter Tong’s name slowly spread.
entries.literal: Hui thought him extraordinary and declared that Tong would be the foremost scholar of the southern provinces; from this Tong gradually became known.

entries.zh: 〈《襄陽記》曰：諸葛孔明為臥龍，龐士元為鳳雛，司馬德操為水鏡，皆龐德公語也。
entries.en: 〈The Xiangyang Ji records that people called Zhuge Liang the Sleeping Dragon, Pang Tong the Fledgling Phoenix, and Sima Hui the Clear Mirror of Water—epithets attributed to Pang Degong.
entries.literal: 〈The Xiangyang Ji says: Zhuge Kongming was called the Crouching Dragon, Pang Shiyuan the Young Phoenix, and Sima Decao the Water Mirror—all phrases of Lord Pang Degong.

entries.zh: 德公，襄陽人。
entries.en: Pang Degong was a native of Xiangyang.
entries.literal: Degong was a man of Xiangyang.

entries.zh: 孔明每至其家，獨拜床下，德公初不令止。
entries.en: Whenever Zhuge Liang visited, he alone bowed low at the bedside; Degong did not at first tell him to rise.
entries.literal: Whenever Kongming came to his house, he alone bowed at the foot of the bed; Degong at first did not tell him to stop.

entries.zh: 德操嘗造德公，值其渡沔，上祀先人墓，德操徑入其室，呼德公妻子，使速作黍，「徐元直向雲有客當來就我與龐公譚。」
entries.en: Once Sima Hui called on Degong while Degong was away—he had crossed the Han to tend his ancestors’ graves uphill. Hui walked straight in, told Degong’s wife and children to cook millet quickly, and said, “Xu Shu mentioned that a guest would come visit me and Master Pang.”
entries.literal: Decao once went to visit Degong when Degong was crossing the Han to sacrifice at his ancestors’ tombs above; Decao went straight into his house, called to Degong’s wife and children, and had them hurry to prepare millet, saying, “Xu Yuanzhi said earlier that a guest would come to talk with me and Lord Pang.”

entries.zh: 其妻子皆羅列拜於堂下，奔走供設。
entries.en: The women lined up to bow in the hall below and bustled about laying out the meal.
entries.literal: His wife and children all lined up and bowed in the hall below, rushing about to set out provisions.

entries.zh: 須臾，德公還，直入相就，不知何者是客也。
entries.en: Soon Degong came home, walked straight in, and sat down with everyone—no one could tell who was the guest.
entries.literal: Presently Degong returned; he went straight in and joined them, not knowing which was the guest.

entries.zh: 德操年小德公十歲，兄事之，呼作龐公，故世人遂謂龐公是德公名，非也。
entries.en: Hui was ten years Degong’s junior yet honored him like an elder and called him “Lord Pang,” so folk mistook “Lord Pang” for Degong’s personal name—incorrectly.
entries.literal: Decao was ten years younger than Degong but treated him as an elder brother and addressed him as Lord Pang; hence people in the world came to think “Lord Pang” was Degong’s name—it was not.

entries.zh: 德公子山民，亦有令名，娶諸葛孔明小姊，為魏黃門吏部郎，早卒。
entries.en: Degong’s son Shanmin likewise enjoyed a good name; he married Zhuge Liang’s elder sister and served Wei as a Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates and Director of the Bureau of Appointments, but died young.
entries.literal: Degong’s son Shanmin also had a fine reputation; he married Zhuge Kongming’s elder sister and served Wei as Gentleman of the Yellow Gates and Director of the Bureau of Appointments; he died young.

entries.zh: 子渙，字世文，晉太康中為牂牁太守。
entries.en: His son Huan, courtesy name Shiwen, served as Administrator of Zangke during the Jin dynasty’s Taikang period.
entries.literal: His son Huan, courtesy name Shiwen, became Administrator of Zangke in the Taikang era of Jin.

entries.zh: 統，德公從子也，少未有識者，惟德公重之，年十八，使往見德操。
entries.en: Tong was Degong’s nephew. As a youth none praised him except Degong; at eighteen Degong sent him to meet Sima Hui.
entries.literal: Tong was Degong’s nephew; in youth no one recognized him—only Degong valued him. At eighteen Degong sent him to visit Decao.

entries.zh: 德操與語，既而嘆曰：「德公誠知人，此實盛德也。」〉
entries.en: After talking with him, Hui sighed, “Degong truly knows men—this is real moral discernment.”〉
entries.literal: Decao spoke with him and afterward sighed, saying, “Degong truly knows how to judge men; this is indeed great virtue.”〉

entries.zh: 後郡命為功曹。
entries.en: The commandery later appointed him Clerk of Merit.
entries.literal: Later the commandery appointed him Clerk of Merit.

entries.zh: 性好人倫，勤於長養。
entries.en: He delighted in appraising character and worked hard to mentor and lift others up.
entries.literal: By nature he loved to discuss human relations and labored to nurture and promote others.

entries.zh: 每所稱述，多過其才，時人怪而問之，統答曰：「當今天下大亂，雅道陵遲，善人少而惡人多。
entries.en: When he praised people he often overstated their abilities; contemporaries asked why. Tong answered, “The empire is torn apart and civility is in ruins—the virtuous are scarce and the vicious plentiful.
entries.literal: Whenever he praised someone, he often exceeded that person’s actual talents; people of the time wondered and asked him. Tong replied, “The realm is in great chaos; proper conduct has declined; good men are few and wicked many.

entries.zh: 方欲興風俗，長道業，不美其譚即聲名不足慕企，不足慕企而為善者少矣。
entries.en: I mean to revive decent habits and grow the moral vocation: unless people sound worthy in conversation, their reputations will not invite emulation—and without emulation few will choose the good.
entries.literal: I wish to improve customs and advance the Way—if I do not praise their conversation, their fame will not be worth aspiring to; if fame is not worth aspiring to, few will strive to do good.

entries.zh: 今拔十失五，猶得其半，而可以崇邁世教，使有志者自勵，不亦可乎？」
entries.en: If I recommend ten and only five measure up, I still secure half the field and can thereby lift public teaching and stir the ambitious—is that not worthwhile?”
entries.literal: Now if I promote ten and miss five, I still gain half, and can thereby elevate instruction for the age and spur those with ambition—may it not be acceptable?”

entries.zh: 吳將周瑜助先主取荊州，因領南郡太守。
entries.en: The Wu commander Zhou Yu helped Liu Bei secure Jingzhou and on that basis also served as Administrator of Nan Commandery.
entries.literal: Wu general Zhou Yu aided the Former Lord in taking Jingzhou and therefore held concurrent office as Administrator of Nan Commandery.

entries.zh: 瑜卒，統送喪至吳，吳人多聞其名。
entries.en: When Zhou Yu died, Tong accompanied the bier east to Wu, where many had already heard of him.
entries.literal: When Yu died, Tong escorted the funeral to Wu; many in Wu had heard his name.

entries.zh: 及當西還，並會昌門，陸勣、顧劭、全琮皆往。
entries.en: As he prepared to go west again, a gathering formed at Chang Gate: Lu Ji, Gu Shao, and Quan Cong all attended.
entries.literal: When he was about to return west, they all met at Chang Gate—Lu Ji, Gu Shao, and Quan Cong all went.

entries.zh: 統曰：「陸子可謂駑馬有逸足之力，顧子可謂駑牛能負重致遠也。」
entries.en: Tong remarked, “Lu Ji is like a nag that still has a burst of speed; Gu Shao is like a draft ox that can haul a heavy load a long way.”
entries.literal: Tong said, “Master Lu may be called a slow horse with the strength of a swift gallop; Master Gu may be called a slow ox able to bear heavy loads far.”

entries.zh: 〈張勃吳錄曰：或問統曰：「如所目，陸子為勝乎？」
entries.en: 〈Zhang Bo’s Record of Wu relates that someone asked Tong, “If that is so, does Lu Ji come out ahead?”
entries.literal: 〈Zhang Bo’s Wu lu says: Someone asked Tong, “By that judgment, is Master Lu the better one?”

entries.zh: 統曰：「駑馬雖精，所致一人耳。
entries.en: Tong replied, “A nag may be spirited, yet what it carries is one rider.
entries.literal: Tong said, “Though a slow horse may be keen, it carries only one person.

entries.zh: 駑牛一日行三百里，所致豈一人之重哉！」
entries.en: An ox plods three hundred li a day—what it hauls is far more than one man’s burden!”
entries.literal: A slow ox travels three hundred li in a day—what it carries is surely not the weight of one man alone!”

entries.zh: 劭就統宿，語，因問：「卿名知人，吾與卿孰愈？」
entries.en: Gu Shao lodged with Tong that night and in conversation asked, “You are celebrated as a judge of men—which of us ranks higher?”
entries.literal: Shao stayed overnight with Tong and conversed, then asked, “You are famed for knowing men—which of us two is better?”

entries.zh: 統曰：「陶冶世俗，甄綜人物，吾不及卿；
entries.en: Tong said, “In shaping popular esteem and cataloguing talent, I am not your match;
entries.literal: Tong said, “In molding common opinion and surveying men, I am not your equal;

entries.zh: 論帝王之秘策，攬倚伏之要最，吾似有一日之長。」
entries.en: in weighing the hidden policies of emperors and the turning points of fortune and ruin, I believe I have the edge.”
entries.literal: in discussing the secret strategies of emperors and kings and grasping the essentials of dependency and reversal, I seem to have the advantage for a day.”

entries.zh: 劭安其言而親之。〉
entries.en: Shao accepted this and grew intimate with him.〉
entries.literal: Shao was satisfied with these words and drew close to him.〉

entries.zh: 謂全琮曰：「卿好施慕名，有似汝南樊子昭。
entries.en: To Quan Cong he said, “You are generous and crave a good name—you remind me of Fan Zizhao of Runan.
entries.literal: To Quan Cong he said, “You love to give and seek renown—you resemble Fan Zizhao of Runan.

entries.zh: 〈蔣濟《萬機論》雲許子將褒貶不平，以拔樊子昭而抑許文休。
entries.en: 〈Jiang Ji’s Treatise on Myriad Affairs notes that Xu Shao’s praises and censures were skewed—he boosted Fan Zizhao and played down Xu Wenxiu.
entries.literal: 〈Jiang Ji’s Wan ji lun says Xu Zijiang’s praise and blame were unfair—he elevated Fan Zizhao and belittled Xu Wenxiu.

entries.zh: 劉曄曰：「子昭拔自賈豎，年至耳順，退能守靜，進能不苟。」
entries.en: Liu Ye objected that Zizhao rose from a merchant family; at sixty he could still withdraw in calm or advance without bending principle.
entries.literal: Liu Ye objected that Zizhao rose from a merchant’s son; at sixty he could retire in quiet when withdrawn and advance without compromise.

entries.zh: 濟答曰：「子昭誠自長幼完潔，然觀其臿齒牙，樹頰胲，吐脣吻，自非文休敵也。」
entries.en: Ji answered that Zizhao is modest and steady from youth to age, but look at those buck teeth, those jowls, that mouth—in looks he cannot rival Xu Wenxiu.
entries.literal: Ji answered that Zizhao is indeed clean from youth to old age, yet look at his projecting teeth, his broad cheeks, his pursed lips—he is no match for Wenxiu.

entries.zh: 胲音改。〉
entries.en: The editorial note reads the syllable as gai.〉
entries.literal: The gloss reads the syllable as gai.〉

entries.zh: 雖智力不多，亦一時之佳也。」
entries.en: His wit may be limited, yet he is still a notable man of the hour.”
entries.literal: Though his intelligence is not great, he is still a fine man of his time.”

entries.zh: 績、劭謂統曰：「使天下太平，當與卿共料四海之士。」
entries.en: Lu Ji and Gu Shao told Tong, “Should the realm ever know peace, we would rank the talent of the four quarters at your side.”
entries.literal: Ji and Shao said to Tong, “If the realm were at peace, we would survey the worthies of the four quarters with you.”

entries.zh: 深與統相結而還。
entries.en: They grew close to Tong and then took their leave.
entries.literal: They formed a deep bond with Tong and returned.

entries.zh: 十九年，進圍成都，璋蜀郡太守許靖將逾城降，事覺，不果。
entries.en: In year 19 the army closed on Chengdu; Xu Jing, prefect of Shu under Liu Zhang, tried to slip over the wall to defect but was caught and could not complete it.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year they advanced to besiege Chengdu; Xu Jing, Liu Zhang’s Administrator of Shu Commandery, attempted to climb the walls and surrender but was discovered and failed.

entries.zh: 璋以危亡在近，故不誅靖。
entries.en: With collapse imminent Liu Zhang spared Xu Jing’s life.
entries.literal: Because ruin pressed near, Liu Zhang did not execute Xu Jing.

entries.zh: 璋既稽服，先主以此薄靖不用也。
entries.en: Once Liu Zhang capitulated, Liu Bei despised Xu Jing and hesitated to use him.
entries.literal: After Liu Zhang submitted, the Former Lord thought little of Xu Jing and would not employ him.

entries.zh: 正說曰：「天下有獲虛譽而無其實者，許靖是也。
entries.en: Fa Zheng argued: “The world holds reputations without substance—Xu Jing is one.
entries.literal: Zheng urged: “The realm has men who win empty fame without substance—Xu Jing is such.

entries.zh: 然今主公始創大業，天下之人不可戶說，靖之浮稱，播流四海，若其不禮，天下之人以是謂主公為賤賢也。
entries.en: Yet as you launch your rule you cannot lecture every home; Xu Jing’s renown rings everywhere—if you dishonor him, people will call you contemptuous of talent.
entries.literal: Yet now you inaugurate a great enterprise; you cannot explain yourself household by household—Xu Jing’s inflated name circulates the realm—if you slight him, folk will say you scorn worthies.

entries.zh: 宜加敬重，以眩遠近，追昔燕王之待郭隗。」
entries.en: Elevate him to impress distant audiences, as King Zhao of Yan honored Guo Wei.”
entries.literal: Honor him to dazzle near and far, emulating the King of Yan’s treatment of Guo Wei.”

entries.zh: 先主於是乃厚待靖。
entries.en: Liu Bei accordingly welcomed Xu Jing with honor.
entries.literal: The Former Lord then treated Xu Jing generously.

entries.zh: 〈孫盛曰：夫禮賢崇德，為邦之要道，封墓式閭，先王之令軌，故必以體行英邈，高義蓋世，然後可以延視四海，振服群黎。
entries.en: 〈Sun Sheng remarks that honoring wise men anchors government; repairing graves marked sage-king usage—only transcendent virtue should command the four seas.
entries.literal: 〈Sun Sheng said: Honoring worthies and exalting virtue is the vital path of state; tending tombs and marking lanes are august precedents—therefore one must embody heroic breadth and righteousness towering above the age before swaying the realm and awing the multitude.

entries.zh: 苟非其人，道不虛行。
entries.en: Without the right person principle rings hollow.
entries.literal: If the man does not match, the Way walks empty.

entries.zh: 靖處室則友於不穆，出身則受位非所，語信則夷險易心，論識則殆為釁首，安在其可寵先而有以感致者乎？
entries.en: At home Xu Jing failed brotherly harmony; in career he took ill-fitting posts; in loyal speech he veered with fortune; in counsel he nearly sparked disaster—what merit earns awe?
entries.literal: Xu Jing was no harmonious brother at home; in office he held posts unsuited to him; in speech he shifted heart between safety and peril; in judgment he nearly became the cause of strife—wherein lies favor that moves others?

entries.zh: 若乃浮虛是崇，偷薄斯榮，則秉直仗義之士，將何以禮之？
entries.en: If puffery wins crowns, how do we salute those who stand on integrity?
entries.literal: If hollow fame is honored and petty vanity crowned, how shall straight men who cling to duty be treated?

entries.zh: 正務眩惑之術，違貴尚之風，譬之郭隗，非其倫矣。
entries.en: Fa Zheng used dazzlers’ tricks against noble taste—he is no Guo Wei.
entries.literal: Zheng pursued dazzlement’s trick and violated noble fashion—compare him to Guo Wei and he is no peer.

entries.zh: 臣松之以為郭隗非賢，猶以權計蒙寵，況文休名聲夙著，天下謂之英偉，雖末年有瑕，而事不彰徹，若不加禮，何以釋遠近之惑乎？
entries.en: Pei Songzhi answers: Guo Wei was mediocre yet duped a throne; Xu Jing’s name towered—ignore courtesy and you fuel rumor.
entries.literal: Pei Songzhi considers: Guo Wei was no sage yet won favor by stratagem—how much more Xu Jing, whose fame long marked him heroic among the realm; though flawed in old age the faults stayed hidden—without courtesy how quiet distant doubts?

entries.zh: 法正以靖方隗，未為不當，而盛以封墓式閭為難，何其迂哉！
entries.en: Fa Zheng’s analogy holds; Sun Sheng’s fuss over grave ritual is fussy pedantry.
entries.literal: For Fa Zheng to pair Xu Jing with Guo Wei was not wrong—yet Sun Sheng treats tending tombs as scandal—how pedantic!

entries.zh: 然則燕昭亦非，豈唯劉翁？
entries.en: If so, King Zhao erred too—not Liu Bei alone.
entries.literal: Then King Zhao was also wrong—not only “Lord Liu.”

entries.zh: 至於友於不穆，失由子將，尋蔣濟之論，知非文休之尤。
entries.en: Domestic discord traces to Xu Shao’s verdict—read Jiang Ji and Xu Jing’s guilt shrinks.
entries.literal: As for unhappy brotherhood, blame falls on Zijiang—refer to Jiang Ji’s essay and see Xu Jing was hardly chief culprit.

entries.zh: 盛又譏其受
entries.en: Sun Sheng also ridiculed Xu Jing’s acceptance of
entries.literal: Sun Sheng further mocked his accepting

entries.en: office—
entries.literal: (appointment)

entries.zh: 非所，將謂仕於董卓。
entries.en: implying he served Dong Zhuo.
entries.literal: to mean serving Dong Zhuo.

entries.zh: 卓初秉政，顯擢賢俊，受其策爵者森然皆是。
entries.en: When Zhuo seized government he promoted talent widely—those who accepted titles were legion.
entries.literal: When Zhuo first seized power he elevated worthies wholesale—those who took his patents filled the rolls.

entries.zh: 文休為選官。
entries.en: Xu Jing directed appointments.
entries.literal: Xu Jing served as selection officer.

entries.zh: 在卓未至之前，後遷中丞，不為超越。
entries.en: That predated Zhuo’s arrival in Luoyang; his promotion to imperial secretary followed normal course.
entries.literal: That was before Zhuo reached the capital; later he rose to Palace Assistant Clerk—no leap beyond merit.

entries.zh: 以此為貶，則荀爽、陳紀之儔皆應擯棄於世矣。〉
entries.en: Condemn him on this ground and you must exile Xun Shuang and Chen Ji as well.
entries.literal: To fault him on this would banish Xun Shuang and Chen Ji’s ilk from the age.

entries.zh: 以正為蜀郡太守、揚武將軍，外統都畿，內為謀主。
entries.en: Fa Zheng became prefect of Shu and General Who Displays Might—he governed the capital region on the outside and framed strategy at Liu Bei’s side within.
entries.literal: Zheng was appointed Administrator of Shu Commandery and General Who Displays Might—externally he commanded the metropolitan district; internally he was chief strategist.

entries.zh: 一餐之德，睚眥之怨，無不報復，擅殺毀傷己者數人。
entries.en: He repaid the slightest kindness or grudge—summarily killing several who had wronged him.
entries.literal: For a meal’s kindness or a sidelong grudge he spared no repayment—on his own authority he executed several who had injured him.

entries.zh: 或謂諸葛亮曰：「法正於蜀郡太縱橫，將軍宜啟主公，抑其威福。」
entries.en: Advisers urged Zhuge Liang: “Fa Zheng abuses his prefecture—tell our lord to rein him in.”
entries.literal: Someone told Zhuge Liang: “Fa Zheng runs riot in Shu Commandery—you should inform the sovereign and curb his power.”

entries.zh: 亮答曰：「主公之在公安也，北畏曹公之強，東憚孫權之逼，近則懼孫夫人生變於肘腋之下；
entries.en: Zhuge Liang answered: “When our lord sheltered at Gong’an he dreaded Cao Cao north, Sun Quan east, and Lady Sun plotting beside him;
entries.literal: Liang replied: “When the sovereign was at Gong’an he feared Cao Cao’s strength to the north, Sun Quan’s pressure to the east, and Lady Sun brewing trouble at his elbow;

entries.zh: 當斯之時，進退狼跋，法孝直為之輔翼，令翻然翱翔，不可復制，如何禁止法正使不得行其意邪！」
entries.en: trapped between threats Fa Xiaozhi lent wings—today he vaults free—why choke Fa Zheng’s desires?”
entries.literal: in such straits, advancing or retreating like a wolf in brush, Fa Xiaozhi gave him wings—now he soars beyond restraint—why forbid Fa Zheng his will?”

entries.zh: 初，孫權以妹妻先主，妹才捷剛猛，有諸兄之風，侍婢百餘人，皆親執刀侍立，先主每入，衷心常凜凜；
entries.en: Sun Quan had married his sister to Liu Bei: she was sharp-tempered and fierce like her brothers, and over a hundred maids stood guard with naked blades—each time Liu Bei crossed her threshold his courage nearly failed him.
entries.literal: At first Sun Quan gave his younger sister to the Former Lord in marriage; she was capable, quick, fierce, and bold, with the bearing of her elder brothers; more than a hundred maidservants all stood attendance personally bearing swords; whenever the Former Lord entered, his heart always trembled with dread.

entries.zh: 亮又知先主雅愛信正，故言如此。
entries.en: Zhuge Liang knew how fond Liu Bei was of Fa Zheng—that is why he framed his answer this way.
entries.literal: Liang also knew the Former Lord deeply trusted Zheng—hence these words.

entries.zh: 〈孫盛曰：夫威福自下，亡家害國之道，刑縱於寵，毀政亂理之源，安可以功臣而極其陵肆，嬖幸而藉其國柄者哉？
entries.en: 〈Sun Sheng argues that delegating supreme authority downward destroys dynasties, and indulgent punishment corrupts rule—no merit minister should be allowed unchecked license or favorite lackeys the imperial grip.
entries.literal: 〈Sun Sheng said: When awe and blessing rise from below it is the path to ruin house and harm state; when punishment runs loose through favor it is the root of wrecking government and disordering principle—how may merit ministers be stretched to utmost arrogance or favored favorites lent the state’s lever?

entries.zh: 故顛頡雖勤，不免違命之刑，楊干雖親，猶加亂行之戮，夫豈不愛，王憲故也。
entries.en: Thus Dian Xian earned execution despite diligence; Yang Gan died though royal kin—law, not affection, ruled the realm.
entries.literal: Hence though Dian Xian was diligent he did not escape sentence for disobeying orders; though Yang Gan was kin he still suffered execution for unruly conduct—not from lack of love, but because of royal law.

entries.zh: 諸葛氏之言，於是乎失政刑矣。〉
entries.en: In Sun Sheng’s eyes Zhuge Liang’s defense blurred the line between policy and penal justice.〉
entries.literal: Zhuge Liang’s words thus missed balance between governance and punishment.〉

entries.zh: 書非史記周圖，仲尼不采，道非虛無自然，嚴平不演。
entries.en: Confucius took nothing into the classics that was not grounded in the histories and charts of Zhou; Yan Junping expounded no Way that was not rooted in emptiness and naturalness.
entries.literal: Books that are not the historical records of Zhou charts, Zhongni did not gather; the Way that is not empty void self-so, Yan Ping did not expound.

entries.zh: 海以受淤，歲一蕩清；
entries.en: The sea accepts silt from every stream, yet each year a great tide scours it clean;
entries.literal: The sea by receiving silt, each year once washes clear;

entries.zh: 君子博識，非禮不視。
entries.en: and the gentleman may read widely, but he does not look at what is contrary to ritual.
entries.literal: the gentleman's broad knowledge, if not ritual he does not view.

entries.zh: 今戰國反覆儀、秦之術，殺人自生，亡人自存，經之所疾。
entries.en: The Intrigues teach the shifting schemes of Su Qin and Zhang Yi—killing others to save oneself, ruining others to survive. The classics condemn such things.
entries.literal: Now the Warring States turn and return the arts of Yi and Qin, kill others to live oneself, destroy others to preserve oneself; the classics abhor this.

entries.zh: 故孔子發憤作《春秋》。
entries.en: That is why Confucius, in indignation, composed the Chunqiu.
entries.literal: Therefore Kongzi in wrath composed the Spring and Autumn.

entries.zh: 大乎居正，複製《孝經》，廣陳德行。
entries.en: How great is the principle of holding to the right! He also composed the Classic of Filial Piety to set forth virtue in breadth.
entries.literal: Great is dwelling in rectitude; again he made the Classic of Filial Piety, broadly set forth virtue and conduct.

entries.zh: 杜漸防萌，預有所抑，是以老氏絕禍于未萌，豈不信邪﹗成湯大聖，睹野魚而有獵逐之失，定公賢者，見女樂而棄朝事，
entries.en: He checked evil in its first stirrings and curbed excess before it could grow—hence Laozi cuts off calamity before it buds; can you doubt it? Tang the Completer was a great sage, yet the sight of wild game led him to hunting excess; Duke Ding of Lu was a worthy ruler, yet the sight of female musicians made him neglect court business;
entries.literal: Stop gradual prevent sprouting, beforehand have what to restrain; therefore the Old Master cut off disaster before not sprouting, is it not trustworthy! Cheng Tang great sage, seeing wild fish yet had hunting pursuit's fault; Duke Ding worthy man, seeing women's music then abandoned court affairs,

entries.zh: 〈臣松之案：書傳魯定公無善可稱。
entries.en: 〈Pei Songzhi notes: the transmitted texts record no virtue in Duke Ding of Lu worth praising.
entries.literal: 〈Your subject Songzhi investigates: in documents and transmissions Duke Ding of Lu has no good worth praising.

entries.zh: 宓謂之賢者，淺學所未達也。〉
entries.en: For Qin Mi to call him a worthy shows a shallow reading of the sources.
entries.literal: Mi calling him worthy man, shallow learning has not reached.

entries.zh: 若此輩類，焉可勝陳。
entries.en: Examples of this sort could fill many pages.
entries.literal: If this sort of kind, how can they be fully arrayed.

entries.zh: 道家法曰︰‘不見所欲，使心不亂。
entries.en: The Daoist maxim runs, "Give the eye no craving and the heart will not be thrown into turmoil.
entries.literal: The Daoist law says: "Not seeing what is desired, causes the mind not to be chaotic.

entries.zh: ’是故天地貞觀，日月貞明，其直如矢，君子所覆。
entries.en: Hence Heaven and Earth hold to constancy, sun and moon shine with constancy, and the straight course flies like an arrow—such is the model the gentleman embraces."
entries.literal: Therefore Heaven and Earth are correct in viewing, sun and moon correct in brightness; their straightness like arrows; what the gentleman covers."

entries.zh: 《洪范》記災，發于言貌，何戰國之譎權乎哉﹗
entries.en: The Hong fan traces calamity to words and bearing—what have they to do with the cunning stratagems of the Warring States?
entries.literal: The Hong Fan records disasters, arising from speech and appearance; what Warring States deceitful stratagems!

entries.zh: 許靖字文休，汝南平輿人。
entries.en: Xu Jing, styled Wenxiu, came from Pingyu in Runan commandery.
entries.literal: Xu Jing, courtesy name Wenxiu, was a man of Pingyu in Runan.

entries.zh: 少與從弟劭俱知名，並有人倫臧否之稱，而私情不協。
entries.en: As a young man he and his cousin Xu Shao rose to fame together, and both were celebrated for sizing up men of the age, yet the two never got along in private.
