entries.literal: Xian returned, raided and took Wu's Wucheng, and thereupon submitted a plan to attack Wu.

entries.zh: 宪方亮严正，待士不倦，轻财好施，不治产业。
entries.en: He was upright and austere, tireless with his men, generous with his purse, and uninterested in amassing property.
entries.literal: Xian was square, bright, stern, and correct, treating gentlemen without weariness, lightening wealth and loving generosity, not managing estates.

entries.zh: 六年薨，赠安南将军，谥曰烈侯。
entries.en: He died in 270 and was posthumously named general who pacifies the south with the epithet “martial marquis.”
entries.literal: In the sixth year he died; posthumously he was awarded General Who Pacifies the South, posthumous name Marquis Lie.

entries.zh: 子袭，以凌江将军领部曲，早卒，追赠广汉太守。
entries.en: His son Luo Xi, general who crosses the river leading family troops, died young and was honored posthumously as governor of Guanghan.
entries.literal: The son Xi, as General Who Crosses the River leading retainers, died early; posthumously he was awarded Administrator of Guanghan.

entries.zh: 袭子徽，顺阳内史，永嘉五年为王如所杀。
entries.en: Luo Xi’s son Hui served as interior secretary of Shunyang and was killed by the rebel Wang Ru in 311.
entries.literal: Xi's son Hui was interior secretary of Shunyang; in the fifth year of Yongjia he was killed by Wang Ru.

entries.zh: 此作“献”，名与本传不同，未详孰是也。〉
entries.en: The excerpt uses a different character for the name than our main text; it is unclear which spelling is right.〉
entries.literal: Here the name is written with an alternate graph for xian, not matching this biography; which form is correct is unclear.〉

entries.zh: 王連字文儀，南陽人也。
entries.en: Wang Lian, styled Wenyi, was a native of Nanyang.
entries.literal: Wang Lian, courtesy name Wenyi, was a man of Nanyang.

entries.zh: 劉璋時入蜀為梓潼令。
entries.en: Under Liu Zhang he entered Shu and served as magistrate of Zitong.
entries.literal: In Liu Zhang's time he entered Shu and became magistrate of Zitong.

entries.zh: 先主起事葭萌，進軍來南，連閉城不降，先主義之，不強逼也。
entries.en: When Liu Bei rose at Jiameng and marched south, Wang Lian shut the gates and refused to yield; Liu Bei respected his stand and did not press the siege.
entries.literal: The First Sovereign raised troops at Jiameng and advanced the army coming south; Lian closed the city and would not submit; the First Sovereign deemed him righteous and did not force him.

entries.zh: 及成都既平，以連為什邡令，轉在廣都，所居有績。
entries.en: After Chengdu fell he was named magistrate of Shifang, then moved to Guangdu, and in each post he left a strong record.
entries.literal: When Chengdu was already pacified, Lian was appointed magistrate of Shifang, transferred to Guangdu, and where he dwelt there was achievement.

entries.zh: 遷司鹽校尉，較鹽鐵之利，利入甚多，有裨國用，於是簡取良才以為官屬，若呂乂、杜祺、劉干，終皆至大官，自連所拔也。
entries.en: He rose to colonel director of salt, where he tightened the salt-and-iron accounts and greatly increased revenue for the treasury. He recruited able men—Lü Yi, Du Qi, and Liu Gan among them—who all rose to high rank on his recommendation.
entries.literal: He was promoted Colonel Director of Salt, compared the profits of salt and iron, profit income was very great, benefiting state use; thereupon he selected and took fine talent to be office subordinates, such as Lü Yi, Du Qi, Liu Gan; in the end all reached high office, from Lian's raising them.

entries.zh: 遷蜀郡太守、興業將軍，領鹽府如故。
entries.en: He was promoted to governor of Shu and general who establishes enterprise while continuing to head the salt monopoly.
entries.literal: He was promoted Administrator of Shu commandery and General Who Establishes Enterprise, concurrently directing the salt office as before.

entries.zh: 建興元年，拜屯騎校尉，領丞相長史，封平陽亭侯。
entries.en: In 223 he became colonel of garrisoned cavalry, chief clerk to the chancellor, and village marquis of Pingyang.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianxing he was appointed Colonel of Garrisoned Cavalry, concurrently chief clerk to the chancellor, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingyang village.

entries.zh: 時南方諸郡不賓，諸葛亮將自征之，連諫以為「此不毛之地，疫癘之鄉，不宜以一國之望，冒險而行」。
entries.en: At the time, the southern commanderies had not submitted, and Zhuge Liang was about to lead a campaign against them in person. Wang Lian remonstrated, arguing that "this is barren country, a land of pestilence; the one on whom the whole state depends should not go there at such risk."
entries.literal: At the time the southern commanderies did not submit; Zhuge Liang was about to personally campaign against them; Lian remonstrated deeming that "this is barren land, a region of pestilence; it is not fitting that the hope of the whole state risk danger in going."

entries.zh: 亮慮諸將才不及己，意欲必往而連言輒懇至，故停留者久之。
entries.en: Zhuge Liang doubted any general could replace him, yet Wang Lian’s pleas were so earnest that the campaign was delayed for a long while.
entries.literal: Liang worried the generals' talent did not match his own, his intention wished certainly to go, but Lian's words were always earnest and thorough, therefore he halted and remained long.

entries.zh: 會連卒。
entries.en: Then Wang Lian died.
entries.literal: It happened that Lian died.

entries.zh: 子山嗣，官至江陽太守。
entries.en: His son Wang Shan inherited the title and rose to governor of Jiangyang.
entries.literal: The son Shan succeeded; his office reached Administrator of Jiangyang.

entries.zh: 朗兄子寵，先主時為牙門將。
entries.en: Xiang Lang's elder brother's son Xiang Chong served as general of the household yamen under the Former Lord.
entries.literal: Lang's elder brother's son Chong, in the Former Lord's time served as general of the household yamen.

entries.zh: 秭歸之敗，寵營特完。
entries.en: At the defeat at Zigui, Chong's camp alone remained intact.
entries.literal: At the defeat at Zigui, Chong's camp alone remained intact.

entries.zh: 建興元年223年封都亭侯，後為中部督，典宿衛兵。
entries.en: In Jianxing 1 (223) he was enfeoffed marquis of Duting; later he became supervisor of the central section and commanded the palace guard.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianxing, 223, he was enfeoffed Marquis of Duting; later he became supervisor of the central section and directed the palace guard.

entries.zh: 諸葛亮當北行，表與後主曰：「將軍向寵，性行淑均，曉暢軍事，試用於昔，先帝稱之曰能，是以眾論舉寵為督。
entries.en: When Zhuge Liang was about to march north, he memorialized the emperor: "General Xiang Chong is even-tempered and fair, and well versed in military affairs. The late emperor tested him in earlier days and praised his ability, and the court therefore recommended him as camp supervisor.
entries.literal: When Zhuge Liang was about to march north, he memorialized the Later Lord, saying: "General Xiang Chong is even and fair in nature and conduct, well versed in military affairs; tested in former days, the late Emperor praised him as capable, and so by common counsel Chong was recommended as supervisor.

entries.zh: 愚以為營中之事，悉以咨之，必能使行陳和睦，優劣得所也。」
entries.en: I believe that in camp affairs, if you consult him on everything, the ranks will stay harmonious and each man will be placed according to his worth."
entries.literal: Your servant thinks that in camp affairs, if you consult him on all, you will surely make the ranks harmonious and assign merit and fault to their proper places."

entries.zh: 遷中領軍。
entries.en: He was promoted to director of the central army.
entries.literal: He was transferred to director of the central army.

entries.zh: 延熙三年，征漢嘉蠻夷，遇害。
entries.en: In Yanxi 3 (240) he campaigned against the Hanjia tribes and was killed.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yanxi he campaigned against the Hanjia barbarians and met with harm.

entries.zh: 寵弟充，歷射聲校尉、尚書。
entries.en: Chong's younger brother Xiang Chong served as colonel of the army of loud-shouting archers and as master of writing.
entries.literal: Chong's younger brother Chong served as colonel of the army of loud-shouting archers and as master of writing.

entries.zh: 《襄阳记》曰：魏咸熙元年六月，镇西将军卫瓘至於成都，得璧玉印各一枚，文似“成信”字，魏人宣示百官，藏于相国府。
entries.en: The Xiangyang ji records that in the sixth month of Wei Xianxi 1 (264), General Who Guards the West Wei Guan reached Chengdu and found a pair of jade seals inscribed with characters resembling "completed faith"; Wei officials displayed them to the court and stored them in the chancellor's mansion.
entries.literal: The Xiangyang ji states: In the sixth month of the first year of Xianxi in Wei, General Who Guards the West Wei Guan reached Chengdu and obtained one jade seal each, the inscription resembling the characters for "completed faith"; the men of Wei displayed them to the hundred officials and stored them in the chancellor's mansion.

entries.zh: 充闻之曰：“吾闻谯周之言，先帝讳备，其训具也，后主讳禅，其训授也，如言刘已具矣，当授与人也。
entries.en: Xiang Chong said: "I have heard Qiao Zhou's remark—the Former Lord's taboo name Bei means 'complete,' and the Later Lord's taboo name Shan means 'hand over,' as though the Liu house were finished and due to be handed on.
entries.literal: Chong heard of it and said: "I have heard Qiao Zhou's words: the Former Lord's taboo name Bei, its gloss is 'complete'; the Later Lord's taboo name Shan, its gloss is 'hand over'; as if saying the Liu house is already complete and should be handed to another.

entries.zh: 今中抚军名炎，而汉年极於炎兴，瑞出成都，而藏之於相国府，此殆天意也。”
entries.en: Now the Central Pacifier is named Yan, Han's years end in Yanxing, the omen appeared at Chengdu and was stored in the chancellor's mansion—surely this is heaven's intent."
entries.literal: Now the Central Pacifier is named Yan, and the Han years end in Yanxing; the omen appeared at Chengdu yet is stored in the chancellor's mansion—this is perhaps heaven's intent.

entries.zh: 是岁，拜充为梓潼太守，明年十二月而晋武帝即尊位，炎兴於是乎徵焉。
entries.en: That year Xiang Chong was appointed governor of Zitong; in the twelfth month of the next year Emperor Wu of Jin took the throne, and Yanxing was thereby fulfilled.
entries.literal: That year Chong was appointed Administrator of Zitong; in the twelfth month of the next year Emperor Wu of Jin assumed the exalted position, and Yanxing was thereby fulfilled.

entries.zh: 孙盛曰：昔公孙自以起成都，号曰成氏，二玉之文，殆述所作乎！
entries.en: Sun Sheng said: When Gongsun Shu rose from Chengdu and styled himself the Cheng clan, the inscription on the two jades perhaps described what he had done!
entries.literal: Sun Sheng said: Formerly Gongsun [Sun] took Chengdu as his rise and styled himself the Cheng clan—the text on the two jades perhaps describes what he wrought!

entries.zh: 張裔字君嗣，蜀郡成都人也。
entries.en: Zhang Yi, styled Jinsi, was a native of Chengdu in Shu commandery.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi, courtesy name Jinsi, was a man of Chengdu in Shu commandery.

entries.zh: 治《公羊春秋》，博涉《史》、《漢》。
entries.en: He mastered the Gongyang tradition of the Spring and Autumn and read widely in the Records of the Historian and the Book of Han.
entries.literal: He studied the Gongyang commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals and broadly perused the Records and the Han.

entries.zh: 汝南許文休入蜀，謂裔干裡敏捷，是中夏鐘元常之倫也。
entries.en: Xu Jing of Runan, on entering Shu, pronounced Zhang Yi as quick and capable in office as Zhong Yao of the central plain.
entries.literal: When Xu Wenxiu of Runan entered Shu, he said Yi was keen and nimble in affairs, of the same class as Zhong Yuanchang of the central plain.

entries.zh: 劉璋時，舉孝廉，為魚復長，還州署從事，領帳下司馬。
entries.en: Under Liu Zhang he was nominated filial and incorrupt, served as magistrate of Yufu, then came back to headquarters as an aide and marshal of the guard.
entries.literal: In Liu Zhang's time he was recommended filial and incorrupt, became magistrate of Yufu, returned to the province to hold staff aide, and led marshal under the tent.

entries.zh: 張飛自荊州由墊江入，璋授裔兵，拒張飛於德陽陌下，軍敗，還成都。
entries.en: When Zhang Fei marched in from Jingzhou via Dianjiang, Liu Zhang gave Zhang Yi troops to block him on the Deyang plain; Yi was beaten and withdrew to Chengdu.
entries.literal: Zhang Fei from Jing Province entered by Dianjiang; Zhang gave Yi troops to resist Zhang Fei below the roads of Deyang; the army was defeated; he returned to Chengdu.

entries.zh: 為璋奉使詣先主，先主許以禮其君而安其人也，裔還，城門乃開。
entries.en: Zhang Yi went to Liu Bei as Liu Zhang’s envoy; Liu Bei pledged to honor Zhang’s lord and spare the people, whereupon Yi returned and the gates were opened.
entries.literal: For Zhang he carried mission to the First Sovereign; the First Sovereign promised to treat his lord with ritual and secure his people; Yi returned, and then the city gates were opened.

entries.zh: 先主以裔巴郡太守，還為司金中郎將，典作農戰之器。
entries.en: Liu Bei first made him governor of Ba, then recalled him as general of the household for metals to oversee farm tools and weapons.
entries.literal: The First Sovereign appointed Yi Administrator of Ba commandery, then returned him to be General of the Household for Metals, directing the making of agricultural and military implements.

entries.zh: 先是，益州郡殺太守正昂，耆率雍闓恩信著於南土，使命周旋，遠通孫權。
entries.en: Earlier, Yizhou commandery had slain Governor Zheng Ang; the chieftain Yong Kai, influential in the south, sent envoys and opened contact with Sun Quan.
entries.literal: Before this, Yizhou commandery killed the Administrator Zheng Ang; the elder leader Yong Kai's grace and trust were renowned in the southern land; envoys went back and forth, far communicating with Sun Quan.

entries.zh: 乃以裔為益州太守，逕往至郡。
entries.en: Zhang Yi was therefore named governor of Yizhou and went straight to his post.
entries.literal: Thereupon Yi was made Administrator of Yizhou, going straight to arrive at the commandery.

entries.zh: 闓遂趑趄不賓，假鬼教曰：「張府君如瓠壺，外雖澤而內實粗，不足殺，令縛與吳。」
entries.en: Yong Kai therefore hesitated and refused to submit. Pretending to relay a ghostly command, he said, "Administrator Zhang is like a gourd vessel: glossy on the outside but coarse within. He is not worth killing; bind him and hand him over to Wu."
entries.literal: Kai thereupon hesitated and did not submit, feigning ghost instruction saying, "Administrator Zhang is like a gourd vessel: outside although glossy yet inside truly coarse; not worth killing—order bind him and give to Wu."

entries.zh: 於是遂送裔於權。
entries.en: They then sent Zhang Yi as a captive to Sun Quan.
entries.literal: Thereupon they sent Yi to Quan.

entries.zh: 既至蜀，丞相亮以為參軍，署府事，又領益州治中從事。
entries.en: Back in Shu, Zhuge Liang made him an army adviser with charge of headquarters business and added the post of administrative aide for Yizhou.
entries.literal: Having reached Shu, Chancellor Liang made him aide-de-camp, assigned bureau affairs, and also led Yizhou administrative aide.

entries.zh: 亮出駐漢中，裔以射聲校尉領留府長史，常稱曰：「公賞不遺遠，罰不阿近，爵不可以無功取，刑不可以貴勢免，此賢愚之所以僉忘其身者也。」
entries.en: When Zhuge Liang went out to garrison Hanzhong, Zhang Yi, as Colonel of the She-sheng Archers, served concurrently as chief clerk of the rear headquarters. He often said, "The Duke's rewards do not overlook those far away, and his punishments do not favor those close to him. Rank cannot be taken without merit, and punishment cannot be escaped through noble power. This is why worthy and foolish alike forget themselves in his service."
entries.literal: When Liang went out and encamped at Hanzhong, Yi as Colonel of Archers Who Sound the Charge led chief clerk of the rear headquarters, often declaring saying, "The Duke's rewards do not omit the distant, punishments do not partial the near; noble rank may not be taken without merit, punishment may not be escaped by noble power—this is why worthy and foolish alike forget their persons."

entries.zh: 其明年，北詣亮諮事，送者數百，車乘盈路，裔還書與所親曰：「近者涉道，晝夜接客，不得寧息，人自敬丞相長史，男子張君嗣附之，疲倦欲死。」
entries.en: The next year, when he went north to consult Zhuge Liang on affairs, several hundred people saw him off and carriages filled the road. Zhang Yi later wrote to close friends, "Recently on the road I have had to receive guests day and night, with no chance for quiet rest. People honor the Chancellor's chief clerk, and Zhang Junsi, poor man, is carried along by it until he is nearly dead with fatigue."
entries.literal: The next year, going north to consult Liang on affairs, several hundred saw him off, carriages filled the road; Yi returned a letter to those close saying, "Lately traveling the road, day and night receiving guests, unable to obtain quiet rest—men themselves revere the chief clerk to the chancellor; the fellow Zhang Jinsi attached to it—weary nearly to death."

entries.zh: 其談啁流速，皆此類也。
entries.en: His witty, rapid talk was always in this vein.
entries.literal: His jesting banter was fluent and quick; all were of this kind.

entries.zh: 〈臣松之以为谈啁贵於机捷，书疏可容留意。
entries.en: 〈Pei Songzhi remarks that banter prizes quick wit while letters allow deliberation.
entries.literal: 〈Your servant Songzhi thinks jesting banter values quick wit; letters and memorials may allow careful attention.

entries.zh: 今因书疏之巧，以著谈啁之速，非其理也。〉
entries.en: To infer his conversational speed from the polish of a written note is misleading.〉
entries.literal: Now relying on the skill of letters and memorials to display jesting banter's speed is not its principle.〉

entries.zh: 少與犍為楊恭友善，恭早死，遺孤未數歲，裔迎留，與分屋而居，事恭母如母。
entries.en: In youth he had befriended Yang Gong of Qianwei; when Gong died leaving a small child, Zhang Yi took the boy in, housed him separately, and honored Gong’s mother as his own.
entries.literal: In youth he was friendly with Yang Gong of Qianwei; Gong died early, leaving an orphan not several years old; Yi welcomed and kept him, dwelling in divided houses, serving Gong's mother as mother.

entries.zh: 恭之子息長大，為之娶婦，買田宅產業，使立門戶。
entries.en: When the boy grew up, Zhang Yi found him a wife, bought land and a house, and set him up with his own household.
entries.literal: Gong's sons and heirs grew great; for them he took wives, bought fields, houses, and estates, causing them to establish households.

entries.zh: 撫恤故舊，振贍衰宗，行義甚至。
entries.en: He helped old friends and bolstered struggling kinsmen with exceptional generosity.
entries.literal: He comforted and pitied old associates, relieved and aided declining clans; conduct and righteousness reached the utmost.

entries.zh: 加輔漢將軍，領長史如故。
entries.en: He was promoted to general who assists Han while keeping the chief clerkship.
entries.literal: He was added General Who Assists Han, leading chief clerk as before.

entries.zh: 建興八年卒。
entries.en: He died in 230.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Jianxing he died.

entries.zh: 子毣嗣，
entries.en: His son Zhang Mao inherited the title,
entries.literal: The son Mao succeeded,

entries.zh: 〈毣音忙角反，见字林，曰“毣，思貌也”。〉
entries.en: 〈The commentary gives Mao’s reading (mang-jue fan) and cites the Zilin gloss “thoughtful mien.”〉
entries.literal: 〈Mao is read mang-jue fan, seen in the Zilin, stating "Mao, appearance of thought."〉

entries.zh: 歷三郡守、監軍。
entries.en: He later served as governor of three commanderies and as army supervisor.
entries.literal: He passed through three commandery governorships and army supervisor.

entries.zh: 毣郁，太子中庶子。
entries.en: Zhang Mao’s son Yu became a palace attendant to the crown prince.
entries.literal: Mao's son Yu was palace attendant to the heir.

entries.zh: 會先主薨，諸葛亮遣鄧芝使吳，亮令芝言次可從權請裔。
entries.en: When Liu Bei died, Zhuge Liang sent Deng Zhi to Wu and told him to seize an opening to ask Sun Quan for Zhang Yi’s release.
entries.literal: It happened the First Sovereign died; Zhuge Liang sent Deng Zhi on mission to Wu; Liang ordered Zhi in the course of conversation to be able to request Yi from Quan.

entries.zh: 裔自至吳數年，流徒伏匿，權未之知也，故許芝遣裔。
entries.en: Zhang Yi had spent years in Wu in obscurity, and Sun Quan had lost track of him, so he agreed to let Deng Zhi take him back.
entries.literal: From the time Yi arrived in Wu several years, drifting, hiding, Quan did not know of him, therefore permitted Zhi to send Yi.

entries.zh: 裔臨發，權乃引見。
entries.en: Just before Zhang Yi sailed, Sun Quan finally received him in audience.
entries.literal: When Yi was about to depart, Quan thereupon summoned audience.

entries.zh: 問裔曰：「蜀卓氏寡女，亡奔司馬相如，貴土風俗何以乃爾乎？」
entries.en: He asked Yi saying, "Shu's Zhuo clan's widowed daughter fled to join Sima Xiangru—how is it that your land's customs are thus?"
entries.literal: He asked Yi saying, "Shu's Zhuo clan's widowed daughter fled to join Sima Xiangru—how is it that your land's customs are thus?"

entries.zh: 裔對曰：「愚以為卓氏之寡女，猶賢於買臣之妻。」
entries.en: Yi replied saying, "Your foolish servant thinks the Zhuo clan's widowed daughter was still worthier than Mai Chen's wife."
entries.literal: Yi replied saying, "Your foolish servant thinks the Zhuo clan's widowed daughter was still worthier than Mai Chen's wife."

entries.zh: 權又謂裔曰：「君還，必用事西朝，終不作田父子閭裡也，將何以報我？」
entries.en: Sun Quan also said to Zhang Yi, "When you return, you are certain to hold power at the western court. You will not end up as a farmer living with your sons in the lanes. How will you repay me?"
entries.literal: Quan further said to Yi, "When you return, you will surely hold office in the western court; in the end you will not be a farmer father and son in the lanes—how will you repay me?"

entries.zh: 裔對曰：「裔負罪而歸，將委命有司。
entries.en: Yi replied saying, "Yi bearing guilt returns, will entrust his life to the authorities.
entries.literal: Yi replied saying, "Yi bearing guilt returns, will entrust his life to the authorities.

entries.zh: 若蒙僥倖得全首領，五十八已前父母之年也，自此已後大王之賜也。」
entries.en: If by good fortune permitted to preserve head and neck, fifty-eight and before is parents' years; from this after is the Great King's gift."
entries.literal: If by good fortune permitted to preserve head and neck, fifty-eight and before is parents' years; from this after is the Great King's gift."

entries.zh: 權言笑歡悅，有器裔之色。
entries.en: Sun Quan laughed and showed open regard for him.
entries.literal: Quan spoke and laughed, pleased and delighted, having the look of one who esteems Yi.

entries.zh: 裔出閣，深悔不能陽愚，即便就船，倍道兼行。
entries.en: Leaving the hall, Zhang Yi regretted he had not played the fool; he went straight to the boat and raced homeward at double speed.
entries.literal: Yi left the pavilion, deeply regretted being unable to feign stupidity, then immediately boarded ship, doubling roads and combining marches.

entries.zh: 權果追之，裔已入永安界數十里，追者不能及。
entries.en: Sun Quan did send pursuers, but Zhang Yi was already dozens of li inside Yong’an and they could not overtake him.
entries.literal: Quan indeed pursued him; Yi had already entered Yong'an border several tens of li; pursuers could not catch up.

entries.zh: 五年，丞相亮北住漢中，欲用張裔為留府長史，問洪何如？
entries.en: In 227, with Zhuge Liang in Hanzhong, he considered making Zhang Yi chief clerk of the rear headquarters and asked Yang Hong’s opinion.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, Chancellor Liang north lodged at Hanzhong, wished to use Zhang Yi as chief clerk of the rear headquarters, asked Hong how it was?

entries.zh: 洪對曰：「裔天姿明察，長於治劇，才誠堪之，然性不公平，恐不可專任，不如留向朗。
entries.en: Yang Hong replied, "Zhang Yi is naturally clear-sighted and perceptive, and he excels at handling difficult administration. His talent is indeed equal to the task, but his temperament is not impartial or even; I fear he cannot be entrusted with it alone. It would be better to keep Xiang Lang.
entries.literal: Hong replied saying, "Yi's heaven-given nature is clear and perceptive; he excels at governing difficult matters; talent truly suffices for it, yet his nature is not fair and even; I fear he cannot be solely entrusted—better retain Xiang Lang.

entries.zh: 朗情偽差少，裔隨從目下，效其器能，於事兩善。」
entries.en: Lang's feelings of falsehood are somewhat less; Yi following under the eye, displaying his tools and ability—on affairs both good."
entries.literal: Lang's feelings of falsehood are somewhat less; Yi following under the eye, displaying his tools and ability—on affairs both good."

entries.zh: 初，裔少與洪親善。
entries.en: Zhang Yi and Yang Hong had been close since youth.
entries.literal: At first, in youth Yi and Hong were intimate and good.

entries.zh: 裔流放在吳，洪臨裔郡，裔子郁給郡吏，微過受罰，不特原假。
entries.en: While Zhang Yi was a hostage in Wu, Yang Hong governed his old commandery; Zhang Yi’s son Yu served there and was punished for a minor fault without special leniency.
entries.literal: Yi was exiled in Wu; Hong came to Yi's commandery; Yi's son Yu supplied commandery clerks, slight fault received punishment, not especially pardoned.

entries.zh: 裔後還聞之，深以為恨，與洪情好有損。
entries.en: When Zhang Yi returned and learned of it, he nursed a deep grudge and their friendship cooled.
entries.literal: Yi later returned and heard of it, deeply took it as resentment; with Hong affection and friendship had damage.

entries.zh: 及洪見亮出，至裔許，具說所言。
entries.en: After Yang Hong’s interview with Zhuge Liang he went to Zhang Yi and repeated every word.
entries.literal: When Hong saw Liang go out, arrived at Yi's lodging, fully told what was said.

entries.zh: 裔答洪曰：「公留我了矣，明府不能止。」
entries.en: Yi answered Hong saying, "The Duke has kept me indeed; the enlightened prefect could not stop it."
entries.literal: Yi answered Hong saying, "The Duke has kept me indeed; the enlightened prefect could not stop it."

entries.zh: 時人或疑洪意自欲作長史，或疑洪知裔自嫌，不願裔處要職，典後事也。
entries.en: Some thought Yang Hong wanted the chief clerk’s post for himself; others thought he knew Zhang Yi would refuse the rear post and spoke accordingly.
entries.literal: At the time some suspected Hong's intention was himself to wish to become chief clerk, or suspected Hong knew Yi himself grudged, did not wish Yi to hold key office, directing rear affairs.

entries.zh: 後裔與司鹽校尉岑述不和，至於忿恨。
entries.en: Later Zhang Yi quarreled bitterly with Cen Shu, the colonel director of salt.
entries.literal: Later Yi and Colonel Director of Salt Cen Shu were not harmonious, reaching to resentment.

entries.zh: 亮與裔書曰：「君昔在[陌]下，營壞，吾之用心，食不知味；
entries.en: Liang wrote Yi a letter saying, "Sir, formerly below the roads [at Deyang], the camp was ruined—my heart's use, eating did not know flavor;
entries.literal: Liang wrote Yi a letter saying, "Sir, formerly below the roads [at Deyang], the camp was ruined—my heart's use, eating did not know flavor;

entries.zh: 後流洪迸南海，相為悲歎，寢不安席；
entries.en: when rumor said you had been banished to the southern seas, he had grieved with you and could not sleep at ease;
entries.literal: later when rumor had you cast into the South Sea, mutually for each other mourned and sighed, lying did not secure mat;

entries.zh: 及其來還，委付大任，同獎王室，自以為與君古之石交也。
entries.en: and after his return, when Zhuge Liang entrusted him with weighty office to help the house of Han, he had thought theirs the “stone friendship” of old.
entries.literal: and when you came back, entrusted great charge, together aided the royal house—I thought myself with you ancient stone friendship.

entries.zh: 石交之道，舉仇以相益，割骨肉以相明，猶不相謝也，況吾但委意於元儉，而君不能忍邪？」
entries.en: In a friendship firm as stone, one raises up an enemy for the other's benefit and cuts into one's own flesh and bone to make things clear, yet still there is no apology. How much less should you resent that I merely placed my confidence in Yuanjian?"
entries.literal: Stone friendship's way raises enemy to mutually benefit, cuts flesh and bone to mutually clarify, still does not decline—how much more I only entrusted intention to Yuanjian, yet you cannot endure?"

entries.zh: 論者由是明洪無私。
entries.en: Onlookers then saw that Yang Hong had acted without private motive.
entries.literal: Discussers from this clarified Hong had no selfishness.

entries.zh: 費詩字公舉，犍為南安人也。
entries.en: Fei Shi, styled Gongju, came from Nan'an in Qianwei.
entries.literal: Fei Shi, courtesy name Gongju, was a man of Nan'an in Qianwei.

entries.zh: 劉璋時為綿竹令，先主攻綿竹時，詩先舉城降。
entries.en: Under Liu Zhang he was magistrate of Mianzhu and was the first to surrender the town when Liu Bei attacked.
entries.literal: In Liu Zhang's time he was Mianzhu magistrate; when the First Sovereign attacked Mianzhu, Shi first raised the city and surrendered.

entries.zh: 成都既定，先主領益州牧，以詩為督軍從事，出為牂牁太守，還為州前部司馬。
entries.en: After Chengdu fell, Liu Bei as governor of Yizhou made him an army aide, then governor of Zangke, then brought him back as forward-division major of the province.
entries.literal: When Chengdu was already settled, the First Sovereign led Governor of Yizhou, appointing Shi aide on military affairs, sent out as Administrator of Zangke, returned as forward-division major of the province.

entries.zh: 先主為漢中王，遣詩拜關羽為前將軍，羽聞黃忠為後將軍，
entries.en: When Liu Bei became king of Hanzhong, he sent Fei Shi to present Guan Yu with appointment as general of the van. Guan Yu learned that Huang Zhong had been named general of the rear,
entries.literal: The First Sovereign became King of Hanzhong, sent Shi to invest Guan Yu as General of the Van; Yu heard Huang Zhong was General of the Rear,

entries.en: (Guan Yu)
entries.literal: (Yu)

entries.zh: 怒曰：「大丈夫終不與老兵同列！」
entries.en: angrily said, "A great man in the end will not share rank with an old soldier!"
entries.literal: angrily said, "A great man in the end will not share rank with an old soldier!"

entries.zh: 不肯受拜。
entries.en: He refused the commission.
entries.literal: He refused to accept the investiture.

entries.zh: 詩謂羽曰：「夫立王業者，所用非一。
entries.en: Shi said to Yu, "Now he who establishes kingly enterprise employs not one kind.
entries.literal: Shi said to Yu, "Now he who establishes kingly enterprise employs not one kind.

entries.zh: 昔蕭、曹與高祖少小親舊，而陳、韓亡命後主，論其班列，韓最居上，未聞蕭、曹以此為怨。
entries.en: Xiao He and Cao Shen had grown up with Gaozu, while Chen Ping and Han Xin arrived as fugitives, yet Han Xin ranked above them in court order without rousing Xiao’s or Cao’s resentment.
entries.literal: Formerly Xiao and Cao with the Supreme Ancestor from youth were intimate old friends, yet Chen and Han were fugitives who came later as lords; discussing their order of ranks, Han was highest; I have not heard Xiao and Cao on this account harbored resentment.

entries.zh: 今
entries.en: Today
entries.literal: Now

entries.zh: （漢王）
entries.en: (the king of Han)
entries.literal: (King of Han)

entries.zh: [漢中王]以一時之功隆崇於漢升，然意之輕重，寧當與君侯齊乎！
entries.en: the king of Hanzhong has honored Hansheng for one exploit, but His Majesty’s regard for you, my lord, surely still outweighs that.
entries.literal: [King of Hanzhong] by a moment's merit exalts Hansheng, yet as to the weight of favor, how could it be equal to you, lord!

entries.zh: 且王與君侯臂猶一體，同休等戚，禍福共之，愚為君侯不宜計官號之高下、爵祿之多少為意也。
entries.en: You and the king are as two arms on one body, sharing weal and woe; you should not fuss over title or pay.
entries.literal: Moreover the king and you, lord, are arms as one body, share rest and equal sorrow, fortune and misfortune together; your foolish servant thinks you, lord, ought not take to heart the height or lowness of office titles, the much or little of noble rank and stipend.

entries.zh: 僕一介之使，銜命之人，君侯不受拜，如是便還，但相為惜此舉動，恐有後悔耳！」
entries.en: I am only a single envoy, a man carrying orders. If Your Lordship will not accept investiture, I shall simply return. I merely regret this action on your behalf, fearing there will be later remorse!"
entries.literal: Your servant, a single messenger, a man bearing mandate—if you, lord, do not accept investiture, thus I will return, only mutually for you pity this movement, fearing there will be later regret!"

entries.zh: 羽大感悟，遂即受拜。
entries.en: Guan Yu was deeply moved and accepted the appointment.
entries.literal: Yu greatly was moved and awakened, thereupon at once accepted investiture.

entries.zh: 後群臣議欲推漢中王稱尊號，詩上疏曰：「殿下以曹操父子逼主篡位，故乃羈旅萬里，糾合士眾，將以討賊。
entries.en: Later the assembled ministers deliberated and wished to urge the King of Hanzhong to assume the imperial title. Shi submitted a memorial saying, "Your Highness, because Cao Cao and his son coerced the ruler and usurped the throne, wandered in exile ten thousand li, gathered officers and troops, and intended to punish the rebels.
entries.literal: Later the assembled ministers deliberated and wished to urge the King of Hanzhong to assume the exalted title. Shi submitted a memorial saying, "Your Highness, because Cao Cao and his son coerced the ruler and usurped the throne, wandered in exile ten thousand li, gathered and united officers and troops, and intended to use them to punish the rebels.

entries.zh: 今天敵未克，而先主自立，恐人心疑惑。
entries.en: The great enemy was still unbeaten, he warned, and proclaiming oneself emperor now would only unsettle popular feeling.
entries.literal: Now heaven's foe is not yet overcome, yet the First Sovereign establishes himself—I fear people's hearts will be doubtful and confused.

entries.zh: 昔高祖與楚約，先破秦者王。
entries.en: Gaozu had sworn with Chu that whoever first destroyed Qin would be king.
entries.literal: Formerly the Supreme Ancestor made covenant with Chu: whoever first broke Qin would be king.

entries.zh: 及屠咸陽，獲子嬰，猶懷推讓，況今殿下未出門庭，便欲自立邪！
entries.en: Even after taking Xianyang and capturing Ying Ziying, Gaozu had hesitated to claim the throne; how could Liu Bei, who had not yet left his own threshold, rush to declare himself?
entries.literal: When he slaughtered Xianyang, captured Ziying, still cherished yielding and declining—how much more now Your Highness has not yet gone out the gate and courtyard, then wishes to establish yourself!

entries.zh: 愚臣誠不為殿下取也。」
entries.en: Your foolish servant truly does not approve for Your Highness."
entries.literal: Your foolish servant truly does not approve for Your Highness."

entries.zh: 由是忤指，左遷部永昌從事。
entries.en: For this bluntness he was demoted to an aide in Yongchang.
entries.literal: From this he offended intent, was demoted left to department Yongchang aide.

entries.zh: 〈习凿齿曰：夫创本之君，须大定而后正己，纂统之主，俟速建以系众心，是故惠公朝虏而子圉夕立，更始尚存而光武举号，夫岂忘主徼利，社稷之故也。
entries.en: 〈Xi Zuochi observes that a founder waits until the realm is settled before taking supreme rank, while a successor must act quickly to steady hearts—hence Duke Hui of Jin was captured in the morning and his heir enthroned that evening, and Guangwu took title while Gengshi still lived; such steps served the state, not private ambition.
entries.literal: 〈Xi Zuochi states: Now the lord who founds the root must await great settling then rectify himself; the lord who continues the line waits on swift establishment to bind the multitude's hearts—therefore Duke Hui was captive at dawn and Ziyu was established at evening; Gengshi still existed yet Guangwu raised title—how could they forget the ruler and seek profit? It was for the altars of soil and grain.

entries.zh: 今先主纠合义兵，将以讨贼。
entries.en: Liu Bei had rallied a loyal host to punish the usurper.
entries.literal: Now the First Sovereign gathers righteous troops, about to use them to strike the rebels.

entries.zh: 贼强祸大，主没国丧，二祖之庙，绝而不祀，苟非亲贤，孰能绍此？
entries.en: The foe was powerful, the sovereign dead, the altars of the two Han founders untended—who but a worthy kinsman could renew the line?
entries.literal: The rebels are strong, calamity great; the ruler perished, state mourned; the two ancestors' temples are cut off and not sacrificed—if not kin and worthy, who can continue this?

entries.zh: 嗣祖配天，非咸阳之譬，杖正讨逆，何推让之有？
entries.en: To succeed the ancestors and match heaven is not the same as Gaozu’s moment at Xianyang; when one wields justice against traitors, there is no room for false modesty.
entries.literal: Heir connects ancestor matching heaven—this is not Xianyang's comparison; leaning on rectitude to strike rebellion—what yielding and declining is there?

entries.zh: 於此时也，不知速尊有德以奉大统，使民欣反正，世睹旧物，杖顺者齐心，附逆者同惧，可谓闇惑矣。
entries.en: To delay enthroning a worthy heir at such a hour, letting the people rejoice in restoration and the wicked tremble, would be folly indeed.
entries.literal: At this time, not knowing to speedily honor the virtuous to serve the great line, causing the people gladly to return to rectification, the age to behold old things, those leaning on compliance to unite hearts, those attaching to rebellion together to fear—may be called benighted and deluded.

entries.zh: 其黜降也宜哉！
entries.en: Small wonder Fei Shi was demoted!
entries.literal: His demotion was fitting!

entries.zh: 臣松之以为凿齿论议，惟此论最善。〉
entries.en: Pei Songzhi calls this the finest of Xi Zuochi’s arguments.〉
entries.literal: Your servant Songzhi thinks in Zuochi's discussions and debates, only this discussion is best.〉

entries.zh: 建興三年，隨諸葛亮南行，歸至漢陽縣，降人李鴻來詣亮，亮見鴻，時蔣琬與詩在坐。
entries.en: In 225, returning with Zhuge Liang from the southern campaign, they reached Hanyang county, where the defector Li Hong came to see Zhuge Liang; Jiang Wan and Fei Shi were present.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jianxing, he followed Zhuge Liang south; returning reached Hanyang county; surrendered man Li Hong came to visit Liang; Liang saw Hong; at the time Jiang Wan and Shi were seated.

entries.zh: 鴻曰：「聞過孟達許，適見王沖從南來，言往者達之去就，明公切齒，欲誅達妻子，賴先主不聽言。
entries.en: Li Hong said, "I heard this while passing through Meng Da's area. I happened to meet Wang Chong coming from the south, and he said that when Da changed allegiance in the past, Your Excellency ground your teeth and wanted to execute Da's wife and children, but fortunately the First Sovereign would not listen to the proposal.
entries.literal: Hong said, "I heard passing Meng Da's place, just then saw Wang Chong coming from the south, speaking of former times Da's going and coming, the enlightened lord gnashed teeth, wished to execute Da's wife and children, relied on the First Sovereign not listening to the words.

entries.zh: 達曰：『諸葛亮見顧有本末，終不爾也。』
entries.en: Meng Da had replied that Zhuge Liang’s goodwill had always been consistent and he would never do such a thing.
entries.literal: Da said, 'Zhuge Liang's regard has beginning and end; in the end will not be thus.

entries.zh: 盡不信沖言，委仰明公，無復已已。」
entries.en: He wholly did not believe Chong's words, entrusted and looked up to the enlightened lord, no more end."
entries.literal: He wholly did not believe Chong's words, entrusted and looked up to the enlightened lord, no more end."

entries.zh: 亮謂琬、詩曰：「還都當有書與子度相聞。」
entries.en: Liang said to Wan and Shi, "When returning to the capital there ought to be a letter to exchange news with Zidu."
entries.literal: Liang said to Wan and Shi, "When returning to the capital there ought to be a letter to exchange news with Zidu."

entries.zh: 詩進曰：「孟達小子，昔事振威不忠，後又背叛先主，反覆之人，何足與書邪！」
entries.en: Fei Shi said, "Meng Da is a petty man. He was disloyal when he formerly served the General Who Inspires Awe, and later he betrayed the First Sovereign as well. A man so changeable is not worth exchanging letters with!"
entries.literal: Shi advanced saying, "Meng Da the petty fellow, formerly served General Who Strikes Terror disloyally, afterward again betrayed the First Sovereign—a man of back and forth—what worth to exchange letters!"

entries.zh: 亮默然不答。
entries.en: Zhuge Liang said nothing.
entries.literal: Liang was silent and did not answer.

entries.zh: 亮欲誘達以為外援，竟與達書曰：「往年南征，歲
entries.en: Zhuge Liang wished to draw Meng Da in as an outside ally and ultimately wrote him a letter: "In former years, during the southern campaign, before the year
entries.literal: Liang wished to entice Da to be an external aid; in the end wrote Da a letter saying, "In former years on the southern campaign, before the year

entries.zh: （未及）
entries.en: (before the year had ended)
entries.literal: (not yet reached)

entries.zh: [末及]還，適與李鴻會於漢陽，承知消息，慨然永歎，以存足下平素之志，豈徒空托名榮，貴為乘離乎！
entries.en: had closed I was still on the road; I met Li Hong at Hanyang and learned your mind. I sighed long for the loyalty you have always shown—surely you do not seek empty glory while we remain apart!
entries.literal: had ended I returned, just then met Li Hong at Hanyang, received and knew your message, sighed long with feeling—thereby to preserve your foot's constant purpose—how merely empty entrusting name and glory, prized as riding estrangement!

entries.zh: 嗚呼孟子，斯實劉封侵陵足下，以傷先主待士之義。
entries.en: Alas, Meng Da—it was Liu Feng’s bullying that wronged you and violated the late emperor’s duty to his men.
entries.literal: Alas, Mengzi, this truly was Liu Feng encroaching and bullying you, thereby harming the First Sovereign's righteousness in treating gentlemen.

entries.zh: 又鴻道王沖造作虛語，云足下量度吾心，不受沖說。
entries.en: Li Hong also said Wang Chong’s story was invented, and he praised you for seeing my true intent and rejecting the lie.
entries.literal: Again Hong related that Wang Chong fabricated empty words, saying you measured my mind and did not accept Chong's tale.

entries.zh: 尋表明之言，追平生之好，依依東望，故遣有書。」
entries.en: Clarifying what was declared above, pursuing the friendship of a lifetime, lingering as I gaze east—I therefore send this letter."
entries.literal: Clarifying what was declared above, pursuing the friendship of a lifetime, lingering as I gaze east—I therefore send this letter."

entries.zh: 達得亮書，數相交通，辭欲叛魏。
entries.en: Meng Da answered repeatedly and began plotting to revolt from Wei.
entries.literal: When Da obtained Liang's letter, repeatedly exchanged communication, declared intent wishing to rebel against Wei.

entries.zh: 魏遣司馬宣王征之，即斬滅達。
entries.en: Wei sent Sima Yi against him and had him killed at once.
entries.literal: Wei sent Sima the King of Xuan to campaign against him; at once beheaded and destroyed Da.

entries.zh: 亮亦以達無款誠之心，故不救助也。
entries.en: Zhuge Liang did not send help because he judged Meng Da insincere.
entries.literal: Liang also because Da had no sincere and honest heart, therefore did not rescue and aid.

entries.zh: 蔣琬秉政，以詩為諫議大夫，卒於家。
entries.en: Under Jiang Wan’s regency Fei Shi became grandee remonstrant and died at home.
entries.literal: Jiang Wan held government, appointed Shi grandee remonstrant; he died at home.

entries.zh: 评曰：霍峻孤城不倾，王连固节不移，向朗好学不倦，张裔肤敏应机，杨洪乃心忠公，费诗率意而言，皆有可纪焉。
entries.en: The historian’s judgment: Huo Jun held a lone city; Wang Lian kept faith; Xiang Lang never tired of study; Zhang Yi was quick and resourceful; Yang Hong was utterly loyal; Fei Shi spoke his mind—all merit remembrance.
entries.literal: The appraisal states: Huo Jun's lone city did not topple; Wang Lian's firm integrity did not shift; Xiang Lang loved learning without weariness; Zhang Yi was perceptive and keen, responding to opportunity; Yang Hong's heart was loyal to the ducal; Fei Shi spoke following his mind—all had what is worth recording.

entries.zh: 以先主之广济，诸葛之准绳，诗吐直言，犹用陵迟，况庸后乎哉！
entries.en: Yet even Liu Bei’s generosity and Zhuge Liang’s fairness could not save Fei Shi from demotion for blunt speech—what hope for lesser lords thereafter?
entries.literal: Given the First Sovereign's broad succor, Zhuge's marking cord—Shi spat forth straight words, still was used declining—how much more vulgar successors!

entries.zh: 霍峻字仲邈，南郡枝江人也。
entries.en: Huo Jun, styled Zhongmiao, came from Zhijiang in Nan Commandery.
entries.literal: Huo Jun, courtesy name Zhongmiao, was a man of Zhijiang in Nan Commandery.

entries.zh: 兄篤於鄉里合部曲數百人，篤卒，荊州牧劉表令峻攝其眾。
entries.en: His older brother Huo Du had raised a few hundred local followers; after Du died, Jing governor Liu Biao put Jun in charge of that band.
entries.literal: His elder brother Huo Du in the countryside assembled several hundred retainers in a private corps; when Du died, the Governor of Jing Province, Liu Biao, ordered Jun to take command of his troops.

entries.zh: 表卒，峻率眾歸先主，先主以峻為中郎將。
entries.en: After Liu Biao’s death, Jun brought his men to Liu Bei, who made him a general of the household.
entries.literal: When Liu Biao died, Jun led the troops to submit to the First Sovereign, who appointed Jun General of the Gentlemen of the Household.

entries.zh: 先主自葭萌南還襲劉璋，留峻守葭萌城。
entries.en: Liu Bei marched south from Jiameng to attack Liu Zhang and left Huo Jun to hold the fortress there.
entries.literal: The First Sovereign returned south from Jiameng to strike Liu Zhang, leaving Jun to defend Jiameng city.

entries.zh: 張魯遣將楊帛誘峻，求共守城，峻曰：「小人頭可得，城不可得。」
entries.en: Zhang Lu’s officer Yang Bo tried to win him over for a joint defense, but Huo Jun replied, "You may have my head; you will not have this city."
entries.literal: Zhang Lu sent the general Yang Bo to entice Jun, seeking to defend the city together; Jun said, "This petty man's head may be taken, but the city cannot be taken."

entries.zh: 帛乃退去。
entries.en: Yang Bo withdrew his force.
entries.literal: Bo thereupon withdrew.

entries.zh: 後璋將扶禁、向存等帥萬餘人由閬水上，攻圍攻峻，且一年，不能下。
entries.en: Liu Zhang’s generals Fu Jin and Xiang Cun then brought over ten thousand men up the Lang River and besieged the town for the better part of a year without breaking it.
entries.literal: Later Zhang's generals Fu Jin, Xiang Cun, and others led more than ten thousand men up the Lang River, attacked, besieged, and assaulted Jun for nearly a year but could not take him.

entries.zh: 峻城中兵才數百人，伺其怠隙，選精銳出擊，大破之，即斬存首。
entries.en: Huo Jun had only a few hundred defenders. When he saw an opening, he sent picked troops out in a sortie, routed the besiegers, and took Xiang Cun’s head.
entries.literal: Jun had only several hundred soldiers in the city; watching for their slackness and gaps, he selected crack troops, sallied out, struck them a great defeat, and beheaded Cun on the spot.

entries.zh: 先主定蜀，嘉峻之功，乃分廣漢為梓潼郡，以峻為梓潼太守、裨將軍。
entries.en: Once Liu Bei had secured Shu, he singled out Huo Jun’s exploit, carved Zitong commandery out of Guanghan, and named him its governor with the rank of major general.
entries.literal: The First Sovereign settled Shu, praised Jun's merit, thereupon divided Guanghan to make Zitong Commandery, and appointed Jun Administrator of Zitong and Major General.

entries.zh: 在官三年，年四十卒，還葬成都。
entries.en: He served three years in post, died at forty, and was brought home for burial in Chengdu.
entries.literal: In office three years, at age forty he died; he was returned for burial at Chengdu.

entries.zh: 先主甚悼惜，乃詔諸葛亮曰：「峻既佳士，加有功於國，欲行爵。」
entries.en: The First Sovereign mourned him deeply and issued an edict to Zhuge Liang: "Jun was an excellent man and, moreover, had rendered merit to the state. I wish to grant him rank."
entries.literal: The First Sovereign greatly mourned and pitied him, then issued an edict to Zhuge Liang saying, "Jun is already an excellent gentleman, moreover having merit for the state; I wish to carry out enfeoffment."

entries.zh: 遂親率群僚臨會弔祭，因留宿墓上，當時榮之。
entries.en: He then led the full court to the funeral, stayed the night by the grave, and contemporaries counted it the highest honor.
entries.literal: Thereupon he personally led the host of officials to attend the assembly, mourn, and sacrifice, and on that account lodged overnight on the tomb; at the time they deemed it glorious.

entries.zh: 後領益州刺史，徙佔河南。
entries.en: He later held concurrent rank as Inspector of Yi Province and moved to reside south of the Yellow River.
entries.literal: Later he concurrently served as Inspector of Yi Province and shifted to reside south of the Yellow River [in Wei territory].

entries.zh: 大將軍司馬宣王深器之，問權曰：「蜀中有卿輩幾人？」
entries.en: Grand General Sima Yi thought highly of him and asked, “How many men like you remain in Shu?”
entries.literal: Grand General Sima Yi deeply esteemed him and asked Quan, saying: 'How many men like you, sir, are there in Shu?'

entries.zh: 權笑而答曰：「不圖明公見顧之重也！」
entries.en: Huang Quan smiled and said, “I hardly expected such attention from you.”
entries.literal: Quan smiled and replied: 'I did not expect the illustrious lord to regard me so heavily!'

entries.zh: 宣王與諸葛亮書曰：「黃公衡，快士也，每坐起歎述足下，不去口實。」
entries.en: Sima Yi wrote Zhuge Liang: “Huang Gongheng is a blunt-spoken man who speaks of you whenever he rises or sits.”
entries.literal: King Xuan wrote to Zhuge Liang, saying: 'Huang Gongheng is a forthright knight; each time he sits or rises he sighs and narrates you—words do not leave his mouth.'

entries.zh: 景初三年，蜀延熙二年，權遷車騎將軍、儀同三司。
entries.en: In 239 Wei’s third year of Jingchu and Shu’s second year of Yanxi he became general of chariots and cavalry with Three Excellencies protocol.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jingchu [239], the second year of Yanxi in Shu [239], Quan was promoted General of Chariots and Cavalry with ceremonial parity of the Three Offices.

entries.zh: 〈《蜀記》曰：魏明帝問權：「天下鼎立，當以何地為正？」
entries.en: 〈The Shu ji records that Emperor Ming of Wei asked Huang Quan which place should be considered orthodox while the realm stood like a tripod.
entries.literal: 〈The Shu Ji states: Emperor Ming of Wei asked Quan: 'The realm stands like a tripod—what place should be considered orthodox?'

entries.zh: 權對曰：「當以天文為正。
entries.en: Huang Quan answered: “Heaven’s omens decide legitimacy.
entries.literal: Quan replied: 'One should take celestial signs as orthodox.

entries.zh: 往者熒惑守心而文皇帝崩，吳、蜀二主平安，此其徵也。」〉
entries.en: When Mars lodged in the Heart and Wei’s Emperor Wen died, the rulers of Wu and Shu were untouched—that is the proof.”〉
entries.literal: Formerly Mars lodged in the Heart [constellation] and Emperor Wen died; the two lords of Wu and Shu were safe—this is its proof.'〉"

entries.zh: 明年卒，謚曰景侯。
entries.en: He died the following year with the posthumous title Marquis Jing.
entries.literal: The next year he died; his posthumous title was Marquis Jing.

entries.zh: 子邕嗣、邕無子，絕。
entries.en: His son Huang Yong inherited but died without heirs, so the marquisate lapsed.
entries.literal: His son Yong succeeded; Yong had no son—the line ended.

entries.zh: 權留蜀子祟，為尚書郎，隨衛將軍諸葛瞻拒鄧艾。
entries.en: Huang Quan’s son Huang Chong stayed in Shu as a masters-of-writing gentleman and followed Guardian General Zhuge Zhan against Deng Ai.
entries.literal: Quan left behind in Shu his son Chong, who was Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; he followed Guardian General Zhuge Zhan to resist Deng Ai.

entries.zh: 到涪縣，瞻盤桓未近，祟屢勸瞻宜速行據險，無令敵得入平地。
entries.en: At Fu County, Zhuge Zhan hesitated; Huang Chong urged him repeatedly to seize the passes before Deng Ai reached the plain.
entries.literal: When they reached Fu County, Zhan lingered and did not advance near; Chong repeatedly urged Zhan that he ought swiftly to march and seize defiles—do not allow the enemy to reach level ground.

entries.zh: 瞻猶與未納，祟至於流涕。
entries.en: Zhuge Zhan still delayed until Huang Chong wept with frustration.
entries.literal: Zhan still dallied and did not accept; Chong reached the point of shedding tears.

entries.zh: 會艾長驅而前，瞻卻戰綿竹，祟帥厲軍士，期於必死，臨陣見殺。
entries.en: Deng Ai swept forward; Zhuge Zhan fell back to Mianzhu. Huang Chong rallied the troops for a fight to the death and died in the front rank.
entries.literal: As it happened Ai drove straight forward; Zhan withdrew to fight at Mianzhu; Chong led and exhorted the soldiers, expecting certain death; facing battle he was killed.

entries.zh: 馬忠字德信，巴西閬中人也。
entries.en: Ma Zhong, styled Dexin, came from Langzhong in Ba-Xi Commandery.
entries.literal: Ma Zhong, courtesy name Dexin, was a man of Langzhong in Ba-Xi.

entries.zh: 少養外家，姓狐，名篤，後乃復姓，改名忠。
entries.en: Raised in his mother's Hu clan under the name Du, he later resumed the surname Ma and took the name Zhong.
entries.literal: In youth he was raised by his maternal family, surnamed Hu and named Du; later he restored his surname and changed his name to Zhong.

entries.zh: 為郡吏，建安末舉孝廉，除漢昌長。
entries.en: He served as a commandery clerk and, at the end of Jian'an, was recommended as filial and incorrupt and made chief of Hanchang.
entries.literal: He was a commandery clerk; at the end of the Jian'an era he was recommended as filial and incorrupt and appointed chief of Hanchang.

entries.zh: 先主東征，敗績猇亭，巴西太守閻芝發諸縣兵五千人以補遣闕，遣忠送往。
entries.en: After Liu Bei's defeat at Xiaoting, Ba-Xi administrator Yan Zhi raised five thousand county troops to fill the army's losses and sent Ma Zhong with them.
entries.literal: When the First Sovereign campaigned east and was defeated at Xiaoting, Ba-Xi Administrator Yan Zhi mobilized five thousand troops from the various counties to fill shortages and losses and sent Zhong to deliver them.

entries.zh: 先主已還永安，見忠與語，謂尚書令劉巴曰：「雖亡黃權，復得狐篤，此為世不乏賢也。」
entries.en: Liu Bei had already returned to Yong'an. After meeting Ma Zhong he told Masters-of-Writing Director Liu Ba, "Though I lost Huang Quan, I have gained Hu Du—the world never lacks talent."
entries.literal: The First Sovereign had already returned to Yong'an. Seeing Zhong and speaking with him, he said to Masters-of-Writing Director Liu Ba: "Though I have lost Huang Quan, I have again gained Hu Du—this shows the age is never short of worthy men."

entries.zh: 建興元年223年，丞相亮開府，以忠為下督。
entries.en: In Jianxing 1 Zhuge Liang opened his chancellor's bureau and named Ma Zhong lower supervisor.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianxing [223], Chancellor Liang opened his bureau and appointed Zhong lower supervisor.

entries.zh: 三年，亮入南，拜忠牂牁太守。
entries.en: In Jianxing 3, when Zhuge Liang marched south, he made Ma Zhong administrator of Zangke.
entries.literal: In the third year, when Liang entered the south, he appointed Zhong Administrator of Zangke.

entries.zh: 郡丞朱褒反。
entries.en: Assistant administrator Zhu Bao rebelled.
entries.literal: Assistant Administrator Zhu Bao rebelled.

entries.zh: 叛亂之後，忠撫育卹理，甚有威惠。
entries.en: After the rebellion Ma Zhong nursed the people back to order with both sternness and kindness.
entries.literal: After the rebellion, Zhong nurtured and comforted the people and governed them; he had great authority and grace.

entries.zh: 八年，召為丞相參軍，副長史蔣琬署留府事。
entries.en: In Jianxing 8 he was recalled as the chancellor's army adviser, assisting chief clerk Jiang Wan in running the rear headquarters.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was summoned as army adviser to the chancellor, assisting Chief Clerk Jiang Wan in administering rear headquarters affairs.

entries.zh: 又領州治中從事。
entries.en: He also served concurrently as director of the provincial headquarters staff.
entries.literal: He also concurrently served as director of the headquarters staff of the province.

entries.zh: 明年，亮出祁山，忠詣亮所，經營戌事。
entries.en: The next year, when Zhuge Liang marched to Qishan, Ma Zhong joined his headquarters to manage garrison affairs.
entries.literal: The next year, when Liang marched out to Qishan, Zhong went to Liang's headquarters and managed garrison affairs.

entries.zh: 軍還，督將軍張嶷等討汶山郡叛羌。
entries.en: After the campaign he directed Zhang Ni and others against rebel Qiang in Wenshan Commandery.
entries.literal: When the army returned, he supervised Generals Zhang Ni and others in punishing the rebel Qiang of Wenshan Commandery.

entries.zh: 十一年，南夷豪帥劉冑反，擾亂諸郡。
entries.en: In Jianxing 11 the southern chieftain Liu Zhou rebelled and threw several commanderies into turmoil.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year the southern Yi chieftain Liu Zhou rebelled and disturbed the various commanderies.

entries.zh: 徵庲降都督張冀還，以忠代冀。
entries.en: Laixiang area commander Zhang Ji was recalled and Ma Zhong replaced him.
entries.literal: Area Commander of Laixiang Zhang Ji was recalled and Zhong replaced Ji.

entries.zh: 忠遂斬冑，平南土。
entries.en: Ma Zhong beheaded Liu Zhou and pacified the south.
entries.literal: Zhong thereupon beheaded Zhou and pacified the southern lands.

entries.zh: 加忠監軍、奮威將軍，封博陽亭侯。
entries.en: He was promoted to army supervisor and general who displays might and enfeoffed as village marquis of Boyang.
entries.literal: Zhong was additionally made army supervisor and General Who Displays Might, and enfeoffed as village marquis of Boyang.

entries.zh: 初，建寧郡殺太守正昂，縛太守張裔於吳，故都督常駐平夷縣。
entries.en: Earlier Jianning had killed Administrator Zheng Ang and sent Administrator Zhang Yi bound to Wu, so area commanders had long been stationed at Pingyi County.
entries.literal: At first Jianning Commandery killed Administrator Zheng Ang and bound Administrator Zhang Yi in Wu; therefore area commanders had regularly been stationed at Pingyi County.

entries.zh: 至忠，乃移治味縣，處民夷之間。
entries.en: Under Ma Zhong the seat moved to Wei County, among Han and tribal settlements.
entries.literal: When Zhong took office, he moved the seat to Wei County, placing it among Han and tribal peoples.

entries.zh: 又越嶲郡亦久失土地，忠率將太守張嶷開复舊郡，由此就加安南將軍，進封彭鄉亭侯。
entries.en: He also led Zhang Ni to recover long-lost Yuexi territory and was promoted to general who pacifies the south and advanced to village marquis of Pengxiang.
entries.literal: Moreover Yuexi Commandery had long lost territory; Zhong led Administrator Zhang Ni to reopen and recover the old commandery; thereby he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the South and advanced to village marquis of Pengxiang.

entries.zh: 延熙五年還朝，因至漢中，見大司馬蔣琬，宣傳詔旨，加拜鎮南大將軍。
entries.en: In Yanxi 5 he returned to court, stopped at Hanzhong to see Grand Marshal Jiang Wan, delivered the imperial edict, and was promoted to grand general who guards the south.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Yanxi he returned to court, and on the way to Hanzhong he saw Grand Marshal Jiang Wan, proclaimed the imperial edict, and was additionally appointed Grand General Who Guards the South.

entries.zh: 七年春，大將軍費韋北禦魏敵，留忠成都，平尚書事。
entries.en: In the spring of Yanxi 7 Grand General Fei Yi marched north against Wei and left Ma Zhong at Chengdu to balance masters-of-writing affairs.
entries.literal: In the spring of the seventh year, Grand General Fei Yi marched north to resist Wei enemies and left Zhong at Chengdu to balance Masters-of-Writing affairs.

entries.zh: 禕還，忠乃歸南。
entries.en: When Fei Yi returned, Ma Zhong went back south.
entries.literal: When Yi returned, Zhong then returned south.

entries.zh: 十二年卒，子脩嗣。
entries.en: He died in the twelfth year [of Yanxi]; his son Ma Xiu inherited the title.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year [of Yanxi] he died; his son Xiu succeeded.

entries.zh: 脩弟恢。
entries.en: Ma Xiu's younger brother was Hui.
entries.literal: Xiu's younger brother was Hui.

entries.zh: 恢子義，晉建寧太守。
entries.en: Hui's son Yi served Jin as administrator of Jianning.
entries.literal: Hui's son Yi was Administrator of Jianning under Jin.

entries.zh: 忠為人寬濟有度量，但恢啁大笑，忿怒不形於色。
entries.en: Ma Zhong was generous and broad-minded, laughed loudly when pleased, and never let anger show.
entries.literal: Zhong as a man was generous and relieving, with breadth of measure; only when cheerful he laughed loudly, and anger did not show on his face.

entries.zh: 然處事能斷，威思並立，是以蠻夷畏而愛之。
entries.en: Yet he decided firmly, pairing authority with kindness, so the tribes both feared and loved him.
entries.literal: Yet in handling affairs he could decide; authority and kindness stood together—therefore the tribes both feared and loved him.

entries.zh: 及卒，莫不自致喪庭，流涕盡哀，為之立廟祀，迄今猶在。
entries.en: At his death tribesmen came in person to mourn, weeping fully, and built shrines to him that still stand.
entries.literal: When he died, none failed to come in person to the mourning hall, weeping with full grief; they built temples to sacrifice to him, which remain to this day.

entries.zh: 張表，時名士，清望逾忠。
entries.en: Zhang Biao was a celebrated gentleman whose repute outshone Ma Zhong's.
entries.literal: Zhang Biao was a famed gentleman of the time; his pure reputation surpassed Zhong's.

entries.zh: 閻宇宿有功幹，於事精勤。
entries.en: Yan Yu had long shown ability and handled affairs with care.
entries.literal: Yan Yu for long had merit and capability and was meticulous and diligent in affairs.

entries.zh: 繼踵在忠後，其威風稱績，皆不及忠。
entries.en: Successors who followed Ma Zhong never matched his authority or record.
entries.literal: Those who followed in Zhong's footsteps—their authority, reputation, and achievements all did not reach Zhong's.

entries.zh: 《益部耆舊傳》曰：張表，肅子也。
entries.en: The Yibu tradition says Zhang Biao was Su's son.
entries.literal: The Traditions of Former Worthies of Yibu states: Zhang Biao was the son of Su.

entries.zh: 《華陽國志》云：表，張松子，未詳。
entries.en: The Huayang guo zhi says Biao was the son of Zhang Song—this is uncertain.
entries.literal: The Huayang guo zhi says: Biao was Zhang Songzi—uncertain.

entries.zh: 閻宇字文平，南郡人也。
entries.en: Yan Yu, styled Wenping, came from Nan Commandery.
entries.literal: Yan Yu, courtesy name Wenping, was a man of Nan Commandery.

entries.zh: 王平字子均，巴西宕渠人也。
entries.en: Wang Ping, styled Zijun, came from Dangqu in Ba-Xi.
entries.literal: Wang Ping, courtesy name Zijun, was a man of Dangqu in Ba-Xi.

entries.zh: 本養外家何氏。
entries.en: He had been raised under the He surname on his mother’s side.
entries.literal: Originally he was raised by his maternal He family.

entries.zh: 後復姓王。
entries.en: He later resumed the surname Wang.
entries.literal: Later he restored the surname Wang.

entries.zh: 隨杜濩、樸胡詣洛陽，假校尉，從曹公征漢中，因降先主，拜牙門將、裨將軍。
entries.en: He went to Luoyang with Du Hu and Pu Hu as acting colonel, followed Cao Cao into Hanzhong, then defected to Liu Bei and became colonel of the standard and supporting general.
entries.literal: He followed Du Hu and Pu Hu to Luoyang; he was appointed acting Colonel; he followed Duke Cao on campaign against Hanzhong; therefore he surrendered to the First Sovereign and was appointed Colonel of the Standard and General Who Supports Might.

entries.zh: 建興六年，屬參軍馬謖先鋒。
entries.en: In 228 he served under army adviser Ma Su as vanguard.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Jianxing [228], he was attached to Army Adviser Ma Su's vanguard.

entries.zh: 謖捨水上山，舉措煩擾，平連規諫謖，謖不能用，大敗於街亭。
entries.en: Ma Su forsook the river for the heights and bungled deployment; Wang Ping argued repeatedly but was ignored, and they were routed at Jieting.
entries.literal: Su abandoned the water and went up the mountain; his measures were vexing and disturbed; Ping repeatedly remonstrated with Su; Su could not employ [his advice]; there was great defeat at Jieting.

entries.zh: 眾盡星散，惟平所領千人鳴鼓自持，魏將張郃疑其伏兵，不往逼也。
entries.en: The army fled in panic while Wang Ping’s thousand men beat drums and held line until Zhang He feared an ambush and halted.
entries.literal: The host all scattered like stars; only the thousand led by Ping beat drums and held formation; Wei general Zhang He suspected ambush and did not press forward.

entries.zh: 於是平徐徐收合諸營遺迸，率將士而還。
entries.en: Wang Ping slowly regrouped the broken camps and marched the survivors home.
entries.literal: Thereupon Ping slowly gathered the scattered remnants of the various camps and led officers and troops back.

entries.zh: 丞相亮既誅馬謖及將軍張休、李盛，奪將軍黃襲等兵。
entries.en: Zhuge Liang executed Ma Su, Zhang Xiu, and Li Sheng and cashiered Huang Xi’s command.
entries.literal: After Chancellor Liang executed Ma Su as well as Generals Zhang Xiu and Li Sheng, he stripped Generals Huang Xi and others of their troops.

entries.zh: 平特見崇顯，加拜參軍，統五部兼當營事，進位討寇將軍，封亭侯。
entries.en: Wang Ping alone was rewarded with army adviser rank, command of five tribal divisions, camp duties, promotion to general who punishes rebels, and a village marquisate.
entries.literal: Ping alone was specially honored and elevated; he was additionally appointed army adviser, commanding five divisions while concurrently handling camp affairs; he advanced in rank to General Who Punishes Rebels and was enfeoffed as village marquis.

entries.zh: 九年，亮圍祁山，平別守南圍。
entries.en: In 231, during the Qishan siege, Wang Ping held the southern perimeter.
entries.literal: In the ninth year [231], Liang besieged Qishan; Ping separately guarded the southern enclosure.

entries.zh: 魏大將軍司馬宣王攻亮，張郃攻平，平堅守不動，郃不能克。
entries.en: While Sima Yi struck Zhuge Liang, Zhang He assaulted Wang Ping’s sector but could not break his defense.
entries.literal: Wei Grand General Sima Yi attacked Liang; Zhang He attacked Ping; Ping defended firmly without moving; He could not overcome him.

entries.zh: 初，平同郡漢昌句
entries.en: Wang Ping had a fellow townsman from Hanchang surnamed Gou—
entries.literal: At first, [there was one] Gou of Hanchang in the same commandery as Ping—

entries.zh: 〈句古候反〉
entries.en: 〈Here the surname Gou is read like English "go" (the fanqie gloss gives an ancient hou reading), not like "jyu."〉
entries.literal: 〈The surname Gou is read gou (ancient hou fan cut).〉

entries.zh: 忠勇寬厚，數有戰功，功名爵位亞平，官至左將軍，封宕渠侯。
entries.en: —named Gou Fu—who was loyal, brave, generous, and substantial, repeatedly won battle merit, stood second only to Wang Ping in achievement, fame, rank, and title, rose to Left General, and was enfeoffed Marquis of Dangqu.
entries.literal: —loyal, brave, generous, and thick—several times meritorious in battle; his merit, fame, rank, and titles stood second to Ping; he reached Left General and was enfeoffed Marquis of Dangqu.

entries.zh: 〈《華陽國志》曰：後張翼、廖化並為大將軍，時人語曰：「前有王、句，後有張、廖。」〉
entries.en: 〈Chang Qu notes that when Zhang Yi and Liao Hua became grand generals, folk rhymed: “Wang and Gou led the way; Zhang and Liao followed.”〉
entries.literal: 〈The Records of Huayang states: Later Zhang Yi and Liao Hua both became Grand Generals; people of the time said: "Before there were Wang and Gou; after there are Zhang and Liao."〉

entries.zh: 在郡十五年，邦域安穆。
entries.en: Fifteen quiet years in Yuexi.
entries.literal: Fifteen years in the commandery—the domain was secure and calm.

entries.zh: 屢乞求還，乃徵詣成都。
entries.en: He begged recall until Chengdu summoned him.
entries.literal: Repeatedly begging to return, he was at last summoned to Chengdu.

entries.zh: 夷民戀慕，扶轂泣涕，過旄牛邑，邑君襁負來迎，及追尋至蜀郡界，其督相率隨嶷朝貢者百餘人。
entries.en: Tribes clung to his wheels, infants met him at Maoniu, and a hundred chiefs escorted him toward Chengdu.
entries.literal: Yi commoners clung to him, supporting his carriage hubs and weeping; passing Maoniu town the town lord carried infants to greet him; chasing all the way to Shu Commandery border, more than a hundred chiefs followed Ni to court tribute.

entries.zh: 嶷至，拜蕩寇將軍，慷慨壯烈，士人咸多貴之。
entries.en: Chengdu named him general who sweeps away bandits; literati admired his fire.
entries.literal: When Ni arrived he was appointed General Who Sweeps Away Bandits—spirited and heroic—gentlemen all esteemed him.

entries.zh: 然放蕩少禮，人亦以此譏焉，
entries.en: His blunt manners drew ridicule.
entries.literal: Yet he was unrestrained and short on ritual—people also mocked him for this.

entries.zh: 〈《益部耆舊傳》曰：時車騎將軍夏侯霸謂嶷曰：「雖與足下疏闊，然託心如舊，宜明此意。」
entries.en: 〈The Traditions of Former Worthies of Yibu states: At that time General of Chariots and Cavalry Xiahou Ba said to Zhang Ni, "Although you and I have had little contact, I entrust my heart to you as if we were old friends. You should understand this intention clearly."
entries.literal: 〈The Traditions of Former Worthies of Yibu states: At that time General of Chariots and Cavalry Xiahou Ba said to Ni: "Although with you, sir, I am distant and broad, yet my heart entrusts as of old—you ought clarify this intent."

entries.zh: 嶷答曰：「僕未知子，子未知我，大道在彼，何云託心乎！
entries.en: Zhang Ni answered coldly: "We hardly know each other—talk of hearts is premature.
entries.literal: Ni replied: "Your servant does not know you, sir; you do not know me—the great Way lies yonder—what speak of entrusting hearts!

entries.zh: 原三年之後徐陳斯言。」
entries.en: Let three years pass before such intimacy."
entries.literal: I beg after three years slowly to state these words."

entries.zh: 有識之士以為美談。〉
entries.en: Thoughtful men praised the exchange.〉
entries.literal: Men of discernment considered this fine conversation.〉

entries.zh: 是歲延熙十七年也。
entries.en: It was 254.
entries.literal: That year was the seventeenth year of Yanxi [254].

entries.zh: 魏狄道長李簡密書請降，衛將軍姜維率嶷等因簡之資以出隴西。
entries.en: Didao magistrate Li Jian plotted defection; Jiang Wei exploited it to march into Longxi with Zhang Ni.
entries.literal: Wei Didao county chief Li Jian secretly wrote requesting surrender; Guard General Jiang Wei led Ni and others using Jian's resources to issue forth into Longxi.

entries.zh: 〈《益部耆舊傳》曰：嶷風濕固疾，至都浸篤，扶杖然後能起。
entries.en: 〈Chronic rheumatism crippled him in Chengdu.
entries.literal: 〈The Traditions of Former Worthies of Yibu states: Ni's rheumatic ailment was chronic; reaching the capital it worsened—only with a staff could he rise.

entries.zh: 李簡請降，眾議狐疑，而嶷曰必然。
entries.en: Court skeptics doubted Li Jian; Zhang Ni insisted it was genuine.
entries.literal: When Li Jian sought surrender the assembly doubted; Ni said it was certain.

entries.zh: 姜維之出，時論以嶷初還，股疾不能在行中，由是嶷自乞肆力中原，致身敵庭。
entries.en: Though ill from travel he volunteered for Jiang Wei's western thrust anyway.
entries.literal: When Jiang Wei marched forth, contemporary opinion held that Ni had just returned and leg ailment kept him from the column—thereby Ni himself begged to exert strength in the Central Plains and give his body to the enemy court.

entries.zh: 臨發，辭後主曰：「臣當值聖明，受恩過量，加以疾病在身，常恐一朝隕沒，辜負榮遇。
entries.en: Before marching he told Liu Shan: “I have enjoyed imperial favor beyond merit and bear a sickly frame—I dread dying overnight and failing your trust.
entries.literal: As he was about to set out, taking leave of the Later Lord he said: 'Your servant has encountered sagely clarity and received favor beyond measure; added to that sickness afflicts my body—I constantly fear falling dead one morning and betraying this splendid encounter.

entries.zh: 天不違原，得豫戎事。
entries.en: Heaven granted my wish to join the campaign.
entries.literal: Heaven did not thwart my prayer; I was able to take part in martial affairs.

entries.zh: 若涼州克定，臣為籓表守將；
entries.en: If we secure Liangzhou I will hold the frontier for you;
entries.literal: If Liangzhou is conquered and settled, your servant will be a frontier-screen guarding commander on the outer defense;

entries.zh: 若有未捷，殺身以報。」
entries.en: if not, I give my life in repayment.”
entries.literal: If there is no victory, I will kill myself to repay.'

entries.zh: 後主慨然為之流涕。〉
entries.en: Liu Shan wept at his words.〉
entries.literal: The Later Lord sighed deeply and for him shed tears.〉

entries.zh: 既到狄道，簡悉率城中吏民出迎軍。
entries.en: At Didao, Li Jian brought the whole town out to greet Jiang Wei’s host.
entries.literal: When they reached Didao, Jian led all clerks and commoners of the city out to welcome the army.

entries.zh: 軍前與魏將徐質交鋒，嶷臨陣隕身，然其所殺傷亦過倍。
entries.en: He fought Xu Zhi at the front and died in action after inflicting more than twice his own losses.
entries.literal: Before the army he crossed blades with Wei general Xu Zhi; Ni fell in facing battle—yet those he killed and wounded were also more than double.

entries.zh: 既亡，封長子瑛西鄉侯，次子護雄襲爵。
entries.en: After he died, his eldest son Ying was enfeoffed as marquis of Xixiang and his second son Huguo inherited the noble title.
entries.literal: After his death, his eldest son Ying was enfeoffed Marquis of Xixiang; second son Huguo succeeded to the noble rank.

entries.zh: 南土越崔巂民夷聞嶷死，無不悲泣，為嶷立廟，四時水旱輒祀之。
entries.en: Southern Han and Yi of Yuexi wept at Zhang Ni’s death, built him shrines, and prayed there whenever drought or flood struck.
entries.literal: People of the southern lands—the Han and Yi of Yuexi Commandery—hearing of Ni's death, none did not weep in sorrow; they erected a temple for Ni; at the four seasons for flood or drought they always sacrificed to him.

entries.zh: 〈《益部耆舊傳》曰：余觀張嶷儀貌辭令，不能駭人，而其策略足以入算，果烈足以立威，為臣有忠誠之節，處類有亮直之風，而動必顧典，後主深崇之。
entries.en: 〈The Yibu tradition says Zhang Ni looked unremarkable yet planned brilliantly, fought fiercely, served with steadfast loyalty, stood candid among colleagues, and weighed every act against precedent—so Liu Shan revered him deeply.
entries.literal: 〈The Traditions of Former Worthies of Yibu states: I observed Zhang Ni—his bearing and speech could not startle people, yet his stratagems sufficed to enter calculation; his decisive fierceness sufficed to establish awe; as minister he had integrity of loyalty; among peers he had the wind of candid straightness; yet in action he always consulted the canon—the Later Lord deeply revered him.

entries.zh: 雖古之英士，何以遠逾哉！
entries.en: Ancient heroes would scarcely surpass him!
entries.literal: Although compared to ancient heroic gentlemen—how could they surpass him far!

entries.zh: 《蜀世譜》曰：嶷孫奕，晉梁州刺史。〉
entries.en: The Shu shifu adds that Zhang Ni’s grandson Zhang Yi became Jin’s inspector of Liangzhou.〉
entries.literal: The Shu Shifu states: Ni's grandson Yi was Liang Province Inspector of Jin.〉

entries.zh: 黃權，字公衡，巴西閬中人也。
entries.en: Huang Quan, styled Gongheng, came from Langzhong in Ba-Xi Commandery.
entries.literal: Huang Quan, courtesy name Gongheng, was a man of Langzhong in Ba-Xi.

entries.zh: 少為郡吏，州牧劉璋召為主簿。
entries.en: He began as a county clerk until Yi Province Governor Liu Zhang named him chief clerk.
entries.literal: In youth he was a county clerk; Governor Liu Zhang summoned him as chief clerk.

entries.zh: 時別駕張鬆建議，宜迎先主，使伐張魯。
entries.en: Zhang Song, Liu Zhang’s vice administrator, urged inviting Liu Bei west to attack Zhang Lu.
entries.literal: At that time Vice Administrator Zhang Song proposed that it was fitting to welcome the First Sovereign and send him to campaign against Zhang Lu.

entries.zh: 權諫曰：「左將軍有驍名，今請到，欲以部曲遇之，則不滿其心，欲以賓客禮待，則一國不容二君。
entries.en: Huang Quan objected: “The Left General is famous as a fighter. Treat him like a subordinate and he will resent it; treat him as an honored guest and two masters cannot share one realm.
entries.literal: Quan remonstrated, saying: 'The Left General has a fierce reputation; now if we invite him and wish to treat him as retainers [buqu], we will not satisfy his heart; if we wish to receive him with the rites due a guest, then one state cannot contain two lords.

entries.zh: 若容有泰山之安，則主有累卵之危。
entries.en: Your guest would stand firm as Taishan while you teeter like a stack of eggs.
entries.literal: If the guest has the security of Mount Tai, then the lord has the peril of piled eggs.

entries.zh: 可但閉境，以待河清。」
entries.en: Better seal the passes and wait until the world settles.”
entries.literal: One may simply close the borders and await the river running clear [i.e. peace in the realm].'

entries.zh: 璋不聽，竟遣使迎先生，出權為廣漢長，及先主襲取益州，將帥分下郡縣。
entries.en: Liu Zhang refused, sent an envoy to welcome Liu Bei anyway, and transferred Huang Quan out as chief of Guanghan. When Liu Bei seized Yi Province by surprise, generals and commanders spread through the commanderies and counties.
entries.literal: Zhang did not listen; in the end he dispatched an envoy to welcome the First Sovereign; he transferred Quan out to be chief of Guanghan; when the First Sovereign seized Yi Province by surprise, generals and commanders fanned out into commanderies and counties.

entries.zh: 郡縣風景附，權閉城堅守，須劉璋稽服，乃詣降先主。
entries.en: County after county yielded; Huang Quan held his walls until Liu Zhang capitulated, then opened his gates to Liu Bei.
entries.literal: Commanderies and counties submitted like wind and shadow [swiftly]; Quan closed the city and defended firmly; he waited until Liu Zhang bowed in submission, then went to surrender to the First Sovereign.

entries.zh: 先主假權偏將軍。
entries.en: Liu Bei named him acting lieutenant general.
entries.literal: The First Sovereign appointed Quan acting Lieutenant General.

entries.zh: 〈徐眾評曰：權既忠諫於主，又閉城拒守，得事君之禮。
entries.en: 〈Xu Zhong remarks that Huang Quan both warned his lord faithfully and held his city—proper conduct for a minister.
entries.literal: 〈Xu Zhong appraises: Quan both loyally remonstrated his lord and closed the city and resisted defense—he obtained the rites of serving a lord.

entries.zh: 武王下車，封比干之墓，表商容之閭，所以大顯忠賢之士，而明示所貴之旨。
entries.en: King Wu honored Bi Gan’s tomb and Shang Rong’s lane to proclaim loyalty—the standard Liu Bei should emulate.
entries.literal: When King Wu stepped down from his chariot, he enfeoffed Bi Gan's tomb and marked Shang Rong's lane—thereby greatly displaying loyal and worthy men and clearly showing the aim of what is honored.

entries.zh: 先主假權將軍，善矣，然猶薄少，未足彰忠義之高節，而大勸為善者之心。〉
entries.en: Promoting him to general was decent but too modest to honor such steadfast loyalty or inspire others.〉
entries.literal: That the First Sovereign appointed Quan general is good, yet still meager—it does not suffice to display the lofty integrity of loyalty and righteousness or greatly encourage the hearts of those who do good.〉

entries.zh: 及曹公破張魯，魯走入巴中，權進曰：「若失漢中，則三巴不振，此為割蜀之股臂也。」
entries.en: When Cao Cao drove Zhang Lu into Bazhong, Huang Quan urged: “Lose Hanzhong and the Three Ba collapse—you would sever Shu’s limbs.”
entries.literal: When Duke Cao defeated Zhang Lu, Lu fled into Ba-Zhong; Quan advanced his view, saying: 'If we lose Hanzhong, then the Three Ba will not flourish—this is cutting off Shu's thigh and arm.'

entries.zh: 於是先主以權為護軍，率諸將迎魯，魯已還南鄭，北降曹公。
entries.en: Liu Bei made Huang Quan protector of the army and marched to intercept Zhang Lu, but Zhang Lu had already doubled back to Nan Zheng and surrendered to Cao Cao.
entries.literal: Thereupon the First Sovereign appointed Quan Protector of the Army and led the various generals to welcome Lu; Lu had already returned to Nan Zheng and submitted north to Duke Cao.

entries.zh: 然卒破杜濩、樸胡，殺夏候淵，據漢中，皆權本謀也。
entries.en: Yet the victories over Du Hu and Pu Hu, the death of Xiahou Yuan, and the seizure of Hanzhong all stemmed from Huang Quan’s original plan.
entries.literal: Yet in the end [they] defeated Du Hu and Pu Hu, killed Xiahou Yuan, and occupied Hanzhong—all were Quan's original stratagem.

entries.zh: 建興元年，丞相亮開府，辟琬為東曹掾。
entries.en: In Jianxing 1 (223 CE) Chancellor Zhuge Liang opened his headquarters and appointed Jiang Wan clerk of the eastern bureau.
entries.literal: Jianxing first year, Chancellor Liang opened office, summoned Wan as eastern bureau clerk.

entries.zh: 舉茂才，琬固讓劉邕、陰化、龐延、廖淳，亮教答曰：「思惟背親捨德，以殄百姓，眾人既不隱於心，實又使遠近不解其義，是以君宜顯其功舉，以明此選之清重也。」
entries.en: Nominated as "abundant talent," Jiang Wan insisted the honor go to Liu Yong, Yin Hua, Pang Yan, or Liao Chun. Zhuge Liang answered: "If worthy men hid their light and turned their backs on the people, neither the court nor the countryside would understand—accept the nomination and show how seriously this selection is taken."
entries.literal: Recommended abundant talent—Wan firmly yielded to Liu Yong, Yin Hua, Pang Yan, Liao Chun; Liang instructed reply saying: "Thinking consider betray kin abandon virtue, thereby destroy hundred surnames—crowd already not hidden in heart; truly also cause far near not understand its meaning—therefore lord should display this merit recommendation, thereby clarify this selection's purity weight."

entries.zh: 遷為參軍。
entries.en: He was promoted to army adviser.
entries.literal: Then transferred as army adviser.

entries.zh: 五年，亮住漢中，琬與長史張裔統留府事。
entries.en: In the fifth year (227 CE) Zhuge Liang moved to Hanzhong; Jiang Wan and chief clerk Zhang Yi ran the rear headquarters.
entries.literal: Fifth year, Liang dwelt Hanzhong; Wan together with chief clerk Zhang Yi governed remaining office affairs.

entries.zh: 八年，代裔為長史，加撫軍將軍。
entries.en: In the eighth year he succeeded Zhang Yi as chief clerk and received the title general who stabilizes the army.
entries.literal: Eighth year, replaced Yi as chief clerk; added general who stabilizes the army.

entries.zh: 亮數外出，琬常足食足兵以相供給。
entries.en: Whenever Zhuge Liang marched out, Jiang Wan kept grain and weapons flowing without fail.
entries.literal: Liang repeatedly went out abroad; Wan constantly full food full weapons thereby mutually supplied.

entries.zh: 亮每言：「公琰托志忠雅，當與吾共贊王業者也。」
entries.en: Zhuge Liang often said, "Gongyan is loyal and cultivated—he is the man to help me sustain the kingly enterprise."
entries.literal: Liang each time said: "Gongyan entrusts ambition loyal refined—ought with me together assist kingly enterprise."

entries.zh: 密表後主曰：「臣若不幸，後事宜以付琬。」
entries.en: He secretly memorialized the emperor: "If I die, let Jiang Wan carry what follows."
entries.literal: Secret memorial Later Lord saying: "Your servant if unlucky—after affairs should entrust to Wan."

entries.zh: 延熙七年，魏軍次於興勢，假禕節，率眾往御之。
entries.en: In Yanxi 7 (244), when Wei halted at Xingshi, Fei Yi took the imperial baton and marched to meet them.
entries.literal: In Yanxi's seventh year Wei troops halted at Xingshi; Yi was lent credentials and led the host to oppose them.

entries.zh: 光祿大夫來敏至禕許別，求共圍棋。
entries.en: Grand Mentor Lai Min visited Fei Yi before departure and challenged him to a game of weiqi.
entries.literal: Minister Laimin came to Yi's quarters to bid farewell and requested to play weiqi together.

entries.zh: 於時羽檄交馳，人馬擐甲，嚴駕已訖。
