entries.en: Feather reports flew while troops stood harnessed and armed.
entries.literal: At that time urgent bulletins flew crisscross; men and horses donned armor—strict readiness was already finished.

entries.zh: 禕與敏留意對戲，色無厭倦。
entries.en: Fei Yi gave the board his full attention without betraying anxiety.
entries.literal: Yi and Min attended closely to the match—his expression showed no disgust or weariness.

entries.zh: 敏曰：「向聊觀試君耳!君信可人，必能辦賊者也。」
entries.en: Lai Min said: "I only tested you—you have the steel nerves needed against the enemy."
entries.literal: Min said, "Just now I idly tested you! You truly are the right man—you surely can manage the bandits."

entries.zh: 禕至，敵遂退，封成鄉侯。
entries.en: Fei Yi reached the front and the Wei army withdrew; he received the village marquisate of Cheng.
entries.literal: When Yi arrived, the enemy then withdrew; he was enfeoffed marquis of Cheng Village.

entries.zh: 〈殷基通语曰：司马懿诛曹爽，祎设甲乙论平其是非。
entries.en: < Yin Ji records that after Sima Yi killed Cao Shuang, Fei Yi wrote an A-side/B-side essay debating the deed.
entries.literal: < Yin Ji's Comprehensive Tales records: When Sima Yi executed Cao Shuang, Yi drafted an A–B debate weighing their right and wrong.

entries.zh: 甲以为曹爽兄弟凡品庸人，苟以宗子枝属，得蒙顾命之任，而骄奢僭逸，交非其人，私树朋党，谋以乱国。
entries.en: Side A: Cao Shuang’s faction were mediocre men lifted only by blood ties; they wasted power on favorites until treason loomed.
entries.literal: Side A held that Cao Shuang and his brothers were mediocre rustics—only because they were imperial kin did they receive testament authority—yet arrogance, luxury, and excess led them to trust unworthy men, build private factions, and plot to disorder the state.

entries.zh: 懿奋诛讨，一朝殄尽，此所以称其任，副士民之望也。
entries.en: Sima Yi struck decisively and cleared them in a day—matching duty and popular expectation.
entries.literal: Yi rose to punish them—in one morning they were wiped out—thereby fulfilling his charge and answering scholar-officials' hopes.

entries.zh: 乙以为懿感曹仲付己不一，岂爽与相干？
entries.en: Side B: Sima Yi nursed private resentment—Cao Shuang was not the sole culprit.
entries.literal: Side B held that Yi resented Cao Shuang for inconsistent trust—how could Shuang alone cause trouble?

entries.zh: 事势不专，以此阴成疵瑕。
entries.en: Shared authority let grudges fester unseen.
entries.literal: Power was not concentrated—thereby he secretly bred faults.

entries.zh: 初无忠告侃尔之训，一朝屠戮，攙其不意，岂大人经国笃本之事乎！
entries.en: He offered no warning, then slaughtered them overnight—hardly the steady hand of a chief minister.
entries.literal: From the first there was no earnest loyal counsel—yet in one dawn they slaughtered—catching them unaware—is that how great men anchor the state?

entries.zh: 若爽信有谋主之心，大逆已构，而发兵之日，更以芳委爽兄弟。
entries.en: If treason were real, why did he leave the emperor in Cao Shuang’s hands when mobilizing?
entries.literal: If Shuang truly harbored treason, great rebellion already framed—yet when troops marched he still entrusted Cao Fang to Shuang's brothers.

entries.zh: 懿父子从后闭门举兵，蹙而向芳，必无悉宁，忠臣为君深虑之谓乎？
entries.en: The Simas barred the palace and turned arms on the sovereign—was that loyal foresight?
entries.literal: Yi and his son closed the gates behind and raised troops—pressing toward Fang—could loyal ministers deeply counsel thus?

entries.zh: 以此推之，爽无大恶明矣。
entries.en: On this reading Cao Shuang’s guilt was hardly proven.
entries.literal: By this reasoning Shuang had no great evil—it is clear.

entries.zh: 若懿以爽奢僭，废之刑之可也，灭其尺口，被以不义，绝子丹血食，及何晏子魏之亲甥，亦与同戮，为僭滥不当矣。〉
entries.en: Executing the entire clan and collateral kin—including He Yan—went beyond justice.>
entries.literal: If Yi thought Shuang extravagant and presumptuous—depose or punish him—acceptable; but extinguishing his whole household, branding him unjust, cutting off Dan's sacrifices—and even executing He Yan, the emperor's kin—was cruel excess.>

entries.zh: 琬固讓州職，禕復領益州刺史。
entries.en: Jiang Wan declined the governorship of Yi; Fei Yi reassumed it.
entries.literal: Wan firmly yielded the provincial post; Yi again took Yi Province inspector.

entries.zh: 禕當國功名，略與琬比。
entries.en: As steward of Shu his stature rivaled Jiang Wan’s.
entries.literal: Yi holding state—merit and fame roughly matched Wan.

entries.zh: 禕别傳曰：禕雅性谦素，家不积财。
entries.en: It adds that Fei Yi lived modestly and kept little treasure.
entries.literal: The supplemental biography says: Yi was by nature humble and plain—his household did not hoard wealth.

entries.zh: 兒子皆令布衣素食，出入不从车骑，无异凡人。
entries.en: He made his sons dress like commoners and travel without escort.
entries.literal: His sons were ordered plain cloth and vegetarian diet; going out they did not follow chariots and riders—no difference from common folk.

entries.zh: 十一年，出住漢中，自琬及禕，雖自身在外，慶賞刑威，皆遙先咨斷然，後乃行。
entries.en: In Yanxi 11 (248) he moved to Hanzhong; even away from Chengdu he and Jiang Wan still settled rewards and punishments by courier before execution.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he went out to garrison Hanzhong—from Wan and Yi onward, though themselves outside, rewards, punishments, and awe were all first consulted and decided from afar, then carried out.

entries.zh: 其推任如此。
entries.en: The court trusted them that completely.
entries.literal: Such was the trust placed in them.

entries.zh: 後十四年夏，還成都，成都望氣者雲都邑無宰相位，故冬復比屯漢壽。
entries.en: Soothsayers claimed Chengdu held no seat for a chief minister, so he wintered again at Hanshou.
entries.literal: Later in the fourteenth year's summer he returned to Chengdu—Chengdu aura-readers said the capital lacked a minister's seat—therefore in winter he again camped north at Hanshou.

entries.zh: 姜維，字伯約，天水冀人也。
entries.en: Jiang Wei, courtesy name Boyue, came from Ji in Tianshui.
entries.literal: Jiang Wei, courtesy name Boyue, was a man of Ji in Tianshui.

entries.zh: 少孤，與母居，好鄭氏學。
entries.en: Orphaned young, he lived with his mother and studied Zheng Xuan’s classical scholarship.
entries.literal: In youth orphaned, he dwelt with his mother and loved Zheng Xuan's learning.

entries.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：维为人好立功名，阴养死士，不脩布衣之业。〉
entries.en: < Fu Xuan claims Jiang Wei schemed for glory and kept a retinue of fighting men.>
entries.literal: < The Fu Zi says: Wei by nature loved to establish merit and fame; secretly he nurtured braves and did not cultivate commoner's occupation.>

entries.zh: 仕郡上計掾，州闢為從事。
entries.en: He rose to county accountant and then provincial attendant.
entries.literal: He served the commandery as accounts clerk; the province summoned him as attendant clerk.

entries.zh: 以父冏昔為郡功曹，值羌、戎叛亂，身衛郡將，沒於戰場，賜維官中郎，參本郡軍事。
entries.en: His father Jiang Jiong died defending the prefect against Qiang rebels; Jiang Wei received a cadet’s rank and a place on the staff.
entries.literal: Because father Jiong long ago was commandery merit clerk—when Qiang and Rong rebelled he guarded the prefect and died on the battlefield—Wei was granted gentleman cadet and joined his commandery's military staff.

entries.zh: 建興六年，丞相諸葛亮軍向祁山，時天水太守適出案行。
entries.en: In 228 Zhuge Liang marched on Qi—Tianshui’s prefect was away on circuit.
entries.literal: In Jianxing's sixth year Chancellor Zhuge Liang's army aimed at Mount Qi—at that time Tianshui's prefect happened to be out inspecting.

entries.zh: 維及功曹梁緒、主簿尹賞、主記梁虔等從行。
entries.en: Jiang Wei rode with Liang Xu, Yin Shang, Liang Qian, and the staff.
entries.literal: Wei together with merit clerk Liang Xu, chief clerk Yin Shang, recorder Liang Qian and others followed the circuit.

entries.zh: 太守聞蜀軍垂至而諸縣響應，疑維等皆有異心，於是夜亡保上邽。
entries.en: The prefect feared collaboration with Shu and fled overnight to Shanggui.
entries.literal: The prefect heard Shu troops were near and counties were responding—suspected Wei and others all had alien hearts—thereupon fled by night to hold Shanggui.

entries.zh: 維等覺太守去，追遲，至城門，城門已閉，不納。
entries.en: They caught up too late; the city gates shut them out.
entries.literal: Wei and others noticed the prefect had gone—pursued late—reached the gate—the gate was closed—not admitted.

entries.zh: 維等相率還冀，冀亦不入維。
entries.en: They rode to Ji, but Ji refused them too.
entries.literal: Wei and others led one another back to Ji—Ji also would not admit Wei.

entries.zh: 維等乃俱詣諸葛亮。
entries.en: They went together to Zhuge Liang.
entries.literal: Wei and others then all went to Zhuge Liang.

entries.zh: 會馬謖敗於街亭。
entries.en: Ma Su had just been crushed at Jieting.
entries.literal: It happened Ma Su was defeated at Jieting.

entries.zh: 亮拔將西縣千餘家及維等還，故維遂與母相失。
entries.en: Zhuge Liang evacuated Xixian and brought Jiang Wei along—parting him from his mother.
entries.literal: Liang pulled west county thousand-plus households and Wei and others back—therefore Wei then lost contact with his mother.

entries.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：天水太守马遵将维及诸官属随雍州刺史郭淮偶自西至洛门案行，会闻亮已到祁山，淮顾遵曰：“是欲不善！”
entries.en: < The Wei Lue adds another flight from Tianshui: Ma Zun was west of Luomen with Guo Huai when news of Zhuge Liang arrived—Guo Huai cried trouble.
entries.literal: < The Wei Lue says: Tianshui prefect Ma Zun led Wei and officials following provincial governor Guo Huai on circuit west to Luomen—happened to hear Liang had reached Qi Mountain—Huai looked at Zun and said, "This cannot be good!

entries.zh: 遂驱东还上邽。
entries.en: They galloped back toward Shanggui.
entries.literal: Thereupon drove east back to Shanggui.

entries.zh: 遵念所治冀县界在西偏，又恐吏民乐乱，遂亦随淮去。
entries.en: Ma Zun feared unrest in his western districts and fled with Guo Huai.
entries.literal: Zun thought his jurisdiction Ji County lay on the west flank—also feared officials and people would delight in chaos—thereupon also followed Huai away.

entries.zh: 时维谓遵曰：“明府当还冀。”
entries.en: Jiang Wei urged Ma Zun to return and hold Ji.
entries.literal: At the time Wei said to Zun, "My lord ought to return to Ji.

entries.zh: 遵谓维等曰：“卿诸人
entries.en: Ma Zun told them, "You people—
entries.literal: Zun said to Wei and others, "You gentlemen—

entries.en: (text breaks mid-clause)
entries.literal: (return)

entries.zh: 复信，皆贼也。”
entries.en: —if you defect to the enemy you are traitors every one."
entries.literal: if you turn back again—all are bandits."

entries.zh: 各自行。
entries.en: Then each rode his separate path.
entries.literal: Each went his own way.

entries.zh: 维亦无如遵何，而家在冀，遂与郡吏上官子脩等还冀。
entries.en: Powerless to sway Ma Zun, Jiang Wei headed home to Ji with staff officer Shangguan Zixiu.
entries.literal: Wei could do nothing about Zun—but his home was in Ji—thereupon with county clerk Shangguan Zixiu and others returned to Ji.

entries.zh: 冀中吏民见维等大喜，便推令见亮。
entries.en: The people of Ji welcomed them and urged them to meet Zhuge Liang.
entries.literal: Ji officials and people seeing Wei and others greatly rejoiced—and pushed them to go see Liang.

entries.zh: 二人不获已，乃共诣亮。
entries.en: With little choice both men presented themselves to Zhuge Liang.
entries.literal: The two could not avoid it—thereupon together went to Liang.

entries.zh: 亮见，大悦。
entries.en: Zhuge Liang received them gladly.
entries.literal: Liang seeing them greatly rejoiced.

entries.zh: 未及遣迎冀中人，会亮前锋为张郃、费繇等所破，遂将维等卻缩。
entries.en: Before Ji could be secured the vanguard fell to Zhang He—Zhuge Liang had to pull Jiang Wei back.
entries.literal: Before he could dispatch to welcome Ji people—it happened Liang's vanguard was broken by Zhang He, Fei Yao and others—thereupon led Wei and others to shrink back.

entries.zh: 维不得还，遂入蜀。
entries.en: Cut off from Wei, Jiang Wei entered Shu.
entries.literal: Wei could not return—thereupon entered Shu.

entries.zh: 诸军攻冀，皆得维母妻子，亦以维本无去意，故不没其家，但系保官以延之。
entries.en: Wei besieged Ji and took his family but did not execute them, hoping to lure him back.
entries.literal: The various armies attacked Ji—all obtained Wei's mother and wife—also because Wei originally had no intent to leave—therefore did not confiscate his family—but tied them in protective custody to entice him.

entries.zh: 此语与本傳不同。
entries.en: This variant differs from the standard account.>
entries.literal: This language differs from the main biography.>

entries.zh: 亮辟維為倉曹掾，加奉義將軍，封當陽亭侯，時年二十七。
entries.en: Zhuge Liang made him Granary Clerk, General Who Upholds Righteousness, and Village Marquis of Dangyang—at twenty-seven.
entries.literal: Liang summoned Wei as granary clerk; added general who upholds righteousness; enfeoffed village marquis of Dangyang—at the time age twenty-seven.

entries.zh: 亮與留府長史張裔、參軍蔣琬書曰：「姜伯約忠勤時事，思慮精密，考其所有，永南、季常諸人不如也。
entries.en: He wrote Zhang Yi and Jiang Wan: "Jiang Wei is meticulous and loyal—Yongnan and Jichang cannot compare.
entries.literal: Liang wrote to chief clerk Zhang Yi and adviser Jiang Wan: "Jiang Boyue is loyal and diligent in affairs of the time—thought careful and fine—measuring his qualities—Yongnan and Jichang and such do not match.

entries.zh: 其人，涼州上士也。」
entries.en: He is the finest talent of the northwest."
entries.literal: This man is upper gentry of Liangzhou."

entries.zh: 又曰：「須先教中虎步兵五六千人。
entries.en: Also said: "Must first drill central tiger infantry five or six thousand.
entries.literal: Also said: "Must first drill central tiger infantry five or six thousand.

entries.zh: 姜伯約甚敏於軍事，既有膽義，深解兵意。
entries.en: He is bold in war and grasps how soldiers think.
entries.literal: Jiang Boyue is very keen in military affairs—already has courage and duty—deeply understands soldier intent.

entries.zh: 此人心存漢室而才兼於人，畢教軍事，當遣詣宮，覲見主上。」
entries.en: His heart is Han’s—once trained, bring him to audience."
entries.literal: This man's heart cherishes the House of Han while talent surpasses others—when military teaching is finished—ought send him to palace—to gaze on the lord."

entries.zh: 〈孙盛杂记曰：初，姜维诣亮，与母相失，复得母书，令求当归。
entries.en: < Sun Sheng adds that his mother wrote demanding he return.
entries.literal: < Sun Sheng's Miscellany says: At first when Jiang Wei went to Liang he lost his mother—again obtained mother's letter ordering him to seek danggui medicine.

entries.zh: 维曰：“良田百顷，不在一亩，但有远志，不在当归也。”〉
entries.en: He answered with a pun: ‘far ambition,’ not ‘return home.’
entries.literal: Wei said: "A hundred qing of fine fields are not one acre—but one has yuanzhi medicine—not danggui.

entries.zh: 後遷中監軍、征西將軍。
entries.en: He rose to Central Inspector and General Who Campaigns West.
entries.literal: Later promoted central army inspector and general who campaigns west.

entries.zh: 五年，維率眾出漢。
entries.en: In the fifth year of the Jingyao era (262) he led the army out from Hanzhong.
entries.literal: Fifth year—Wei led the host out from Han.

entries.zh: 侯和為鄧艾所破，還住沓中。
entries.en: Deng Ai scattered him at Hehe; Jiang Wei fell back to Tazhong.
entries.literal: He was defeated at Hehe by Deng Ai and withdrew to garrison Tazhong.

entries.zh: 維本羈旅托國，累年攻戰，功績不立。
entries.en: A northerner serving Shu, he campaigned endlessly with little to show for it.
entries.literal: Wei was by nature a wanderer relying on the state—year after year attacking yet merit not established.

entries.zh: 而宦官黃皓等弄權於內，右大將軍閻宇與皓協比，而皓陰欲廢維樹宇。
entries.en: Court eunuch Huang Hao meddled at court; Yan Yu curried favor with him while Huang schemed to replace Jiang Wei.
entries.literal: Yet eunuch Huang Hao and others wielded power within; General of the Right Yan Yu colluded with Hao—and Hao secretly wished to dismiss Wei and raise Yu.

entries.zh: 維亦疑之，故自危懼，不復還成都。
entries.en: Jiang Wei feared court intrigue and stayed away from Chengdu.
entries.literal: Wei also suspected this—therefore lived in peril fear—no longer returned to Chengdu.

entries.zh: 〈《华阳国志》曰；
entries.en: < The Huayang Guo Zhi relates:
entries.literal: < The Huayang Guo Zhi records:

entries.zh: 维恶黄皓恣擅，启后主欲杀之。
entries.en: Jiang Wei denounced Huang Hao’s excess and asked Liu Shan to execute him.
entries.literal: Wei detested Huang Hao's wantonness and memorialized the Later Lord wishing to kill him.

entries.zh: 后主曰：“皓趋走小臣耳，往董允切齿，吾常恨之，君何足介意！”
entries.en: Liu Shan dismissed him: "Huang Hao is a mere runner—Dong Yun hated him too, yet I kept him—why fuss?"
entries.literal: The Later Lord said, "Hao is only a running petty minister—long ago Dong Yun gnashed teeth at him—I always resented that—why should you care!"

entries.zh: 维见皓枝附叶连，惧於失言，逊辞而出。
entries.en: Seeing Huang Hao’s network, Jiang Wei held his tongue and withdrew politely.
entries.literal: Wei saw Hao's branches attached leaves connected—feared misspeaking—yielding words and departed.

entries.zh: 后主敕皓诣维陈谢。
entries.en: Liu Shan sent Huang Hao to apologize to Jiang Wei.
entries.literal: The Later Lord ordered Hao to go to Wei and declare apology.

entries.zh: 维说皓求沓中种麦，以避内逼耳。〉
entries.en: Jiang Wei asked leave to grow grain at Tazhong and escape court cabals.>
entries.literal: Wei persuaded Hao to seek wheat planting at Tazhong—to avoid inner pressure.>

entries.zh: 六年，維表後主：「聞鐘會治兵關中，欲規進取，宜並遣張翼、廖化詣督堵軍分護陽安關口、陰平橋頭，以防未然。」
entries.en: In the sixth year, Jiang Wei memorialized the Later Lord: "I hear that Zhong Hui is training troops in Guanzhong and intends to make an advance. Zhang Yi and Liao Hua should be sent at once to command blocking forces, separately guarding the Yang'an pass and the bridgehead at Yinping, so as to forestall what has not yet happened."
entries.literal: Sixth year—Wei memorialized the Later Lord: "I hear Zhong Hui trains troops in Guanzhong—intends to strike—we ought together dispatch Zhang Yi and Liao Hua to various supervisors to divide guard Yang'an pass and Yinping bridge—to guard before it happens."

entries.zh: 皓徵信鬼巫，謂敌終不自致。
entries.en: Huang Hao trusted sorcerers who swore the enemy would never march.
entries.literal: Hao trusted ghost shamans—said the enemy in the end would not come of themselves.

entries.zh: 啟後主寢其事，而群臣不知。
entries.en: Liu Shan buried the memorial; the court never heard of it.
entries.literal: He had the Later Lord sleep on the matter—and the host of ministers knew not.

entries.zh: 及鐘會將向駱谷，鄧艾將入沓中。
entries.en: When Zhong Hui entered Lu Valley and Deng Ai struck Tazhong,
entries.literal: By the time Zhong Hui was bound for Lu Valley and Deng Ai for Tazhong—

entries.zh: 然後乃遣右車騎廖化詣沓中為維援，左車騎張翼、輔國大將軍董厥等詣陽安關口以為諸圍外助。
entries.en: relief came late: Liao Hua toward Tazhong, Zhang Yi and Dong Jue toward Yang’an.
entries.literal: only then sent General of the Right Cavalry Liao Hua to Tazhong as aid to Wei—General of the Left Cavalry Zhang Yi and Defender-in-Chief Dong Jue and others to Yang'an pass as outer help for the ramparts.

entries.zh: 比至陰平，聞魏將諸葛緒向建威，故住待之。
entries.en: At Yinping he learned Zhuge Xu was aiming at Jianwei and paused.
entries.literal: Reaching Yinping—heard Wei general Zhuge Xu was heading for Jianwei—therefore halted to await.

entries.zh: 月餘，維為鄧艾所摧，還住陰平。
entries.en: A month later Deng Ai broke him and he fell back to Yinping.
entries.literal: After more than a month—Wei was crushed by Deng Ai—withdrew to Yinping.

entries.zh: 鐘會攻圍漢、樂二城，遣別將進攻關口，蔣舒開城出降，傅僉格鬥而死。
entries.en: Zhong Hui stormed Hanxing and Lecheng and sent a column at the pass—Jiang Shu surrendered while Fu Qian died fighting.
entries.literal: Zhong Hui attacked and besieged Han and Le two cities—sent a separate general to advance on the pass—Jiang Shu opened the city to surrender—Fu Qian wrestled and died.

entries.zh: 〈汉晋春秋曰：蒋舒将出降，乃诡谓傅佥曰：“今贼至不击而闭城自守，非良图也。”
entries.en: < The Han–Jin Annals: Jiang Shu meant to defect and lied to Fu Qian: "Holding the gates without fighting helps no one."
entries.literal: < The Han–Jin Annals says: Jiang Shu was about to surrender—deceitfully said to Fu Qian, "Now the bandits arrive—not striking yet closing the city to self-defend—is not a good plan."

entries.zh: 佥曰：“受命保城，惟全为功，今违命出战，若丧师负国，死无益矣。”
entries.en: Fu Qian answered: "Our orders are to hold—sortie risks defeat and dishonors the realm."
entries.literal: Qian said, "Ordered to guard the city—only completeness is merit—now disobeying order to go out—if we lose the army and betray the state—death is without benefit."

entries.zh: 舒曰：“子以保城获全为功，我以出战克敌为功，请各行其志。”
entries.en: Jiang Shu said: "You call defense victory—I call a sortie victory—do as you believe."
entries.literal: Shu said, "You take guarding the city and achieving completeness as merit—I take going out and defeating the enemy as merit—pray each walk his will."

entries.zh: 遂率众出。
entries.en: Then he marched out with his men.
entries.literal: Thereupon led the host out.

entries.zh: 佥谓其战也，至阴平，以降胡烈。
entries.en: Fu Qian thought it a real attack; Jiang Shu slipped to Yinping and surrendered to Hu Lie.
entries.literal: Qian thought he went to battle—reaching Yinping—surrendered to Hu Lie.

entries.zh: 烈乘虚袭城，佥格斗而死，魏人义之。
entries.en: Hu Lie seized the open gate; Fu Qian fought to the death and earned Wei’s respect.
entries.literal: Lie rode emptiness to raid the city—Qian wrestled and died—Wei men deemed him righteous.

entries.zh: 蜀记曰：蒋舒为武兴督，在事无称。
entries.en: The Shu Ji adds that Jiang Shu had performed poorly as Wuxing commander.
entries.literal: Shu Ji says: Jiang Shu was overseer of Wuxing—without distinction in office.

entries.zh: 蜀命人代之，因留舒助汉中守。
entries.en: Shu replaced him but kept him to help defend Hanzhong.
entries.literal: Shu ordered a man to replace him—thereupon retained Shu to assist Hanzhong defense.

entries.zh: 舒恨，故开城出降。〉
entries.en: Bitter at the snub, Jiang Shu opened the gates to the enemy.>
entries.literal: Shu resented—therefore opened the city to surrender.>

entries.zh: 會攻樂城，不能克。
entries.en: Zhong Hui failed to storm Lecheng.
entries.literal: Hui attacked Le city—could not overcome.

entries.zh: 聞關口已下，長驅而前，翼、厥甫至漢壽，維、化亦捨陰平而退。
entries.en: When the pass fell Zhong Hui drove deep; Zhang Yi and Dong Jue had only reached Hanshou while Jiang Wei and Liao Hua quit Yinping.
entries.literal: Hearing the pass had fallen—long drove forward—Yi, Jue had just reached Hanshou—Wei, Hua also abandoned Yinping and withdrew.

entries.zh: 適與翼、厥合，皆退保劍閣以拒會。
entries.en: They united at Jiange and blocked Zhong Hui.
entries.literal: Happening to join Yi, Jue—all retreated to guard Jiange to resist Hui.

entries.zh: 會與維書曰：「公侯以文武之德，懷邁世之略，功濟巴、漢、聲暢華夏，遠近莫不歸名。
entries.en: Zhong Hui wrote to Jiang Wei, saying, "You possess both civil and martial virtue and hold strategies that rise above the age. Your achievements have aided Ba and Han, and your reputation resounds through China; near and far, all acknowledge your name.
entries.literal: Hui wrote Wei a letter, saying, "Lordship with civil and martial virtue—embracing transcendent age strategy—merit bridges Ba and Han—fame rings Huaxia—far and near none do not submit name.

entries.zh: 每惟疇昔，嘗同大化，吳札、鄭喬，能喻斯好。」
entries.en: Each thinks on past days—once shared great transformation—Wu Zha, Zheng Qiao—can illustrate this friendship."
entries.literal: Each thinks on past days—once shared great transformation—Wu Zha, Zheng Qiao—can illustrate this friendship."

entries.zh: 維不答書，列營守險。
entries.en: Jiang Wei ignored the letter and manned the narrows.
entries.literal: Wei did not answer the letter—arrayed camps guarding the defile.

entries.zh: 會不能克，糧運縣遠，將議還歸。
entries.en: Zhong Hui stalled; supplies stretched thin and withdrawal loomed.
entries.literal: Hui could not overcome—grain transport hung far—generals debated returning.

entries.zh: 而鄧艾自陰平由景谷道傍入，遂破諸葛瞻於綿竹。
entries.en: Deng Ai cut through Yinping’s side valley and crushed Zhuge Zhan at Mianzhu.
entries.literal: Yet Deng Ai from Yinping by Jinggu side path slipped in—thereupon broke Zhuge Zhan at Mianzhu.

entries.zh: 後主請降於艾，艾前據成都。
entries.en: Liu Shan surrendered to Deng Ai, who marched into Chengdu.
entries.literal: The Later Lord requested surrender to Ai—Ai advanced and occupied Chengdu.

entries.zh: 維等初聞瞻破，或聞後主欲固守成都，或聞欲東入吳，或聞欲南人建寧。
entries.en: Rumors flew: Liu Shan might hold Chengdu, flee to Wu, or bolt south to Jianning.
entries.literal: Wei and others first heard Zhan broken—or heard the Later Lord wished to firm defend Chengdu—or heard wished to east enter Wu—or heard wished to south enter Jianning.

entries.zh: 於是引軍由廣漢、郪道以審虛實。
entries.en: Jiang Wei marched through Guanghan toward Qi to learn the truth.
entries.literal: Thereupon led army by Guanghan, Qishan road—to examine emptiness and substance.

entries.zh: 尋被後主敕令乃投戈放甲，詣會於涪軍前，將士鹹怒，拔刀斫石。
entries.en: Liu Shan’s order to disarm reached him at Fu; his troops wept and struck rocks with their swords.
entries.literal: Soon received Later Lord order—then cast aside weapons, loosened armor—went to Hui before Fu army—generals all angry—drew blades and hacked stone.

entries.zh: 干寶《晋纪》云：会谓维曰；
entries.en: < Gan Bao’s Jin Annals: Zhong Hui asked Jiang Wei—
entries.literal: < Gan Bao's Jin Ji records: Hui said to Wei—

entries.zh: “来何迟也？”
entries.en: "Why so late?"
entries.literal: "Why did you come so late?"

entries.zh: 维正色流涕曰：“今日见此为速矣！”
entries.en: Jiang Wei answered through tears: "To meet this moment is soon enough!"
entries.literal: Wei with stern color weeping said, "Today to see this—is already swift!"

entries.zh: 会甚奇之。〉
entries.en: Zhong Hui marveled at him.>
entries.literal: Hui greatly marveled.>

entries.zh: 蔣琬字公琰，零陵湘鄉人也。
entries.en: Jiang Wan, courtesy name Gongyan, came from Xiangxiang in Lingling Commandery.
entries.literal: Jiang Wan, courtesy name Gongyan, was a native of Xiangxiang in Lingling.

entries.zh: 弱冠與外弟泉陵劉敏懼知名。
entries.en: While still young he won local fame alongside his cousin Liu Min of Quanling.
entries.literal: While still young he won local fame alongside his cousin Liu Min of Quanling.

entries.zh: 琬以州書佐隨先主入蜀，除廣都長。
entries.en: He entered Shu as a provincial clerk under Liu Bei and was named magistrate of Guangdu.
entries.literal: Wan served as a provincial clerk and followed the Vanguard Lord into Shu; he was appointed magistrate of Guangdu.

entries.zh: 先主嘗因遊觀奄至廣都，見琬眾事不理，時又沉醉，先主大怒，將加罪戮。
entries.en: Liu Bei came to Guangdu on a tour, found Jiang Wan drunk and neglecting his duties, and was ready to execute him.
entries.literal: The Vanguard Lord once on a pleasure outing suddenly arrived at Guangdu and saw Wan leaving official business unattended and at the time also deeply drunk; the Vanguard Lord was greatly angry and was about to impose punishment and execution.

entries.zh: 軍師將軍諸葛亮請曰：「蔣琬，社稷之器，非百里之才也。
entries.en: Zhuge Liang intervened: "Jiang Wan is material for the empire, not a petty county magistrate.
entries.literal: Army commander Zhuge Liang pleaded, saying, "Jiang Wan is vessel of the altars of soil and grain—not talent for a hundred li.

entries.zh: 其為政以安民為本，不以修飾為先，願主公重加察之。」
entries.en: He rules by putting the people at ease, not by polished appearances—please look again, my lord."
entries.literal: His governing takes pacifying the people as root, not ornament as first; wish the lord examine him again carefully."

entries.zh: 先主雅敬亮，乃不加罪，倉卒但免官而已。
entries.en: Liu Bei yielded to Zhuge Liang and spared him—stripping him of office alone.
entries.literal: The Vanguard Lord always respected Liang and therefore did not add punishment; in haste he only dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 琬見推之後，夜夢有—牛頭在門前，流血滂沱，意甚惡之，呼問占夢趙直。
entries.en: After his promotion Jiang Wan dreamed of a bloody ox head at his gate and consulted Zhao Zhi about it.
entries.literal: After Wan was promoted, he dreamed at night of an ox head before the gate, bleeding profusely—his intent felt very ill; he called to ask dream-diviner Zhao Zhi.

entries.zh: 直曰：「夫見血者，事分明也。
entries.en: Zhi said, "Seeing blood means affairs are clear-cut.
entries.literal: Zhi said, "Seeing blood means affairs are clear-cut.

entries.zh: 牛角及鼻，『公』字之象，君位必當至公，大吉之征也。」
entries.en: Horns and snout sketch the word ‘duke’—you are destined for high, impartial office; most auspicious."
entries.literal: Ox horn and nose are images of the character ‘public’; your position must reach utmost fairness—a greatly auspicious sign."

entries.zh: 頃之，為什邡令。
entries.en: Soon he was appointed magistrate of Shifang.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he became magistrate of Shifang.

entries.zh: 先主為漢中王，琬人為尚書郎。
entries.en: When Liu Bei took the title King of Hanzhong, Jiang Wan became a secretary in the imperial secretariat.
entries.literal: When the Vanguard Lord became King of Hanzhong, Wan entered as gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 吳主權徐夫人，吳郡富春人也。
entries.en: Lady Xu of Sun Quan was a daughter of Fuchun in Wu commandery.
entries.literal: Lady Xu, consort of Wu ruler Quan, was a native of Fuchun in Wu commandery.

entries.zh: 祖父真，與權父堅相親，堅以妹妻真，生琨。
entries.en: Her grandfather Xu Zhen was close to Sun Jian, who married him a sister; they had Xu Kun.
entries.literal: Her grandfather Zhen was intimate with Quan's father Jian; Jian gave his younger sister in marriage to Zhen, who begot Kun.

entries.zh: 琨少仕州郡，漢末擾亂，去吏，隨堅征伐有功，拜偏將軍。
entries.en: Xu Kun began in local office, quit at the Han collapse, followed Sun Jian with distinction, and won the rank of Lieutenant General.
entries.literal: Kun in youth served the province and commandery; at the end of Han there was turmoil; he left clerical office, followed Jian on campaigns with merit, was appointed Lieutenant General.

entries.zh: 堅薨，隨孫策討樊能、於糜等於橫江，擊張英於當利口。
entries.en: After Sun Jian's death he joined Sun Ce against Fan Neng and Yu Mi at Hengjiang and Zhang Ying at Danglikou.
entries.literal: When Jian died, he followed Sun Ce to campaign against Fan Neng, Yu Mi, and others at Hengjiang, and struck Zhang Ying at Danglikou.

entries.zh: 而船少，欲駐軍更求。
entries.en: Boats were scarce; he wanted to halt and fetch more craft.
entries.literal: But boats were few; he wished to halt the army and seek more.

entries.zh: 琨母時在軍中，謂琨曰：「恐州家多發水軍來逆人，則不利矣，如何可駐邪？
entries.en: His mother, still with the host, warned him, "If the enemy throws a fleet against us, stopping here will be fatal—how can you wait?
entries.literal: Kun's mother was at that time in the army and said to Kun, "I fear the provincial authorities will send many water forces to oppose men; then it will not be advantageous—how can we halt?

entries.zh: 宜伐蘆葦以為泭，佐船渡軍。」
entries.en: Cut reeds into floats and ferry the army across on them."
entries.literal: It is fitting to cut reeds to make rafts, to assist the boats in ferrying the army."

entries.zh: 〈泭音敷。
entries.en: 〈The note gives fu as the reading.〉
entries.literal: 〈The note gives fu as the reading.〉

entries.zh: 郭璞注《方言》曰：「泭，水中簰也。」〉
entries.en: In his Fang yan commentary Guo Pu glosses the word as "fu," meaning a raft used on the water.〉
entries.literal: Guo Pu's commentary on the Fang yan states, "Fu is a raft on the water."〉

entries.zh: 琨具啟策，策即行之。
entries.en: Xu Kun laid the plan before Sun Ce, who adopted it at once.
entries.literal: Kun fully reported to Ce; Ce immediately carried it out.

entries.zh: 眾悉俱濟，遂破英，擊走笮融、劉繇，事業克定。
entries.en: The whole force crossed, broke Zhang Ying, and sent Ze Rong and Liu Yao flying—the southeast was theirs.
entries.literal: The host all crossed together; thereupon they defeated Ying, struck and drove away Ze Rong and Liu Yao, and the enterprise was settled.

entries.zh: 策表琨領丹楊太守，會吳景委廣陵來東，復為丹楊守。
entries.en: Sun Ce cited Xu Kun as acting Grand Administrator of Danyang until Wu Jing returned from Guangling and resumed that post.
entries.literal: Ce memorialized Kun to act as Grand Administrator of Danyang; it happened that Wu Jing resigned Guangling and came east, and again became Danyang defender.

entries.zh: 〈《江表傳》曰：初，袁術遣從弟胤為丹楊，策令琨討而代之。
entries.en: 〈The Jiang biao zhuan says Yuan Shu first planted his cousin in Danyang until Sun Ce sent Xu Kun to oust him.
entries.literal: 〈The Jiang biao zhuan states: At first Yuan Shu dispatched his cousin Yin as Danyang; Ce ordered Kun to campaign against him and replace him.

entries.zh: 會景還，以景前在
entries.en: When Wu Jing came back, because Jing had previously served in
entries.literal: It happened that Jing returned; because Jing previously in

entries.en: office
entries.literal: (office)

entries.zh: 丹楊，寬仁得眾，吏民所思，而琨手下兵多，策嫌其太重，且方攻伐，宜得琨眾，乃復用景，召琨還吳。〉
entries.en: Danyang with such kindness that the people missed him, while Xu Kun's following had grown unwieldy for an army on the march—so Sun Ce put Wu Jing back in charge and recalled Xu Kun to Wu.〉
entries.literal: Danyang had been kind and benevolent and won the people, whom clerks and commoners longed for, while Kun's subordinate troops were many; Ce disliked it as too weighty, and moreover was just then attacking; it was fitting to obtain Kun's host; therefore he again employed Jing, summoned Kun back to Wu.〉

entries.zh: 琨以督軍中郎將領兵，從破廬江太守李術，封廣德侯，遷平虜將軍。
entries.en: Xu Kun led troops as Supervising General of the Household, helped crush Li Shu at Lujiang, became Marquis of Guangde, and rose to General Who Pacifies Captives.
entries.literal: Kun as Supervising General of the Household led troops, followed in breaking Grand Administrator of Lujiang Li Shu, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangde, promoted to General Who Pacifies Captives.

entries.zh: 後從討黃祖，中流矢卒。
entries.en: He was killed by a stray shaft while campaigning against Huang Zu.
entries.literal: Later following the campaign against Huang Zu, in midstream he was struck by a stray arrow and died.

entries.zh: 吳主權王夫人，南陽人也。
entries.en: The Nanyang Lady Wang was another of Sun Quan's consorts.
entries.literal: Lady Wang, consort of Wu ruler Quan, was a native of Nanyang.

entries.zh: 以選人宮，嘉禾中得幸，生
entries.en: Chosen for the harem, she won favor in the Jiahe era and bore
entries.literal: By selection she entered the palace; in the Jiahe period obtained favor and gave birth to

entries.en: the child was
entries.literal: (Sun)

entries.zh: 休。
entries.en: Sun Xiu.
entries.literal: Xiu.

entries.zh: 及和為太子，和母貴重，諸姬有寵者，皆出居外。
entries.en: Once Sun He was heir, his mother's faction dominated; favored concubines were packed off to residences outside the palace.
entries.literal: When He was heir apparent, He's mother was noble and weighty; concubines who had favor all went out to dwell outside.

entries.zh: 夫人出公安，卒，因葬焉。
entries.en: Lady Wang was sent to Gong'an, where she died and was buried.
entries.literal: The lady went out to Gong'an, died, and was therefore buried there.

entries.zh: 休即位，遣使追尊曰敬懷皇后，改葬敬陵。
entries.en: When Sun Xiu took the throne he posthumously named her Empress Jinghuai and moved her grave to the Jing mausoleum complex.
entries.literal: When Xiu ascended the throne, he dispatched envoys to posthumously honor her as Empress Jinghuai, and changed burial to Jing Mausoleum.

entries.zh: 王氏無後，封同母弟文雍為亭侯。
entries.en: With no Wang heir to honor, he enfeoffed her half-brother Wang Wenyong as a precinct marquis.
entries.literal: The Wang clan had no posterity; he enfeoffed her uterine younger brother Wen Yong as precinct marquis.

entries.zh: 孫休朱夫人，朱據女，休姊公主所生也。
entries.en: Sun Xiu's consort Lady Zhu was Zhu Ju's daughter, born to Xiu's elder sister the princess.
entries.literal: Sun Xiu's Lady Zhu was the daughter of Zhu Ju, born to Xiu's elder sister the princess.

entries.zh: 臣松之以為休妻其甥，事同漢惠。
entries.en: Pei Songzhi notes that Sun Xiu married his niece—parallel to Emperor Hui of Han.
entries.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that Xiu married his niece (his sister's daughter), the case being the same as Emperor Hui of Han.

entries.zh: 荀悅譏之已當，故不復廣言。
entries.en: Xun Yue's censure was apt enough, so I say no more.
entries.literal: Xun Yue's censure was already apt; therefore I do not expand further.

entries.zh: 赤烏末，權為休納以為妃。
entries.en: Late in the Chiwu era Sun Quan betrothed her to Sun Xiu as consort.
entries.literal: At the end of Chiwu, Quan took her in marriage for Xiu to be consort.

entries.zh: 休為琅邪王，隨居丹楊。
entries.en: Sun Xiu was Prince of Langye and lived with her in Danyang.
entries.literal: Xiu was Prince of Langye and dwelt accordingly in Danyang.

entries.zh: 建興中，孫峻專政，公族皆患之。
entries.en: During Jianxing Sun Jun seized power, and every member of the imperial house feared him.
entries.literal: In the Jianxing period Sun Jun monopolized government; the imperial clan all feared it.

entries.zh: 全尚妻即峻姊。
entries.en: Quan Shang had married Jun's elder sister.
entries.literal: Quan Shang's wife was Jun's elder sister.

entries.zh: 故惟全主祐焉。
entries.en: Only Princess Quan (Sun Luban) therefore shielded Lady Zhu.
entries.literal: Therefore only the Princess of Quan protected her.

entries.zh: 初，孫和為太子時，全主譖害王夫人，欲廢太子，立魯王，朱主不聽，由是有隙。
entries.en: When Sun He was crown prince, Princess Quan slandered Lady Wang to depose the heir and elevate the Prince of Lu; Lady Zhu refused to go along, and a feud opened between them.
entries.literal: At first, when Sun He was heir apparent, the Princess of Quan slandered Lady Wang, wishing to depose the heir and establish the Prince of Lu; Lady Zhu would not listen, and from this there was a rift.

entries.zh: 五鳳中，孫儀謀殺峻，事覺被誅。
entries.en: In Wufeng Sun Yi plotted to kill Sun Jun; the plot was exposed and he was executed.
entries.literal: In the Wufeng period Sun Yi plotted to kill Jun; the affair was discovered and he was executed.

entries.zh: 全主因言朱主與儀同謀，峻枉殺朱主。
entries.en: Princess Quan then claimed Lady Zhu had conspired with Sun Yi, and Jun had Lady Zhu executed on false grounds.
entries.literal: The Princess of Quan thereupon said Lady Zhu had conspired with Yi; Jun wrongly killed Lady Zhu.

entries.zh: 休懼，遣夫人還建業，執手泣別。
entries.en: Terrified, Sun Xiu sent Lady Zhu back to Jianye, weeping as they clasped hands in farewell.
entries.literal: Xiu was afraid and sent the lady back to Jianye, clasping hands and weeping in parting.

entries.zh: 既至，峻遣還休。
entries.en: Once she reached the capital, Jun sent her back to Sun Xiu.
entries.literal: When she arrived, Jun sent her back to Xiu.

entries.zh: 太平中，孫亮知朱主為全主所害，問朱主死意？
entries.en: In Taiping Sun Liang learned Princess Quan had engineered Lady Zhu's death and questioned her about it.
entries.literal: In the Taiping period Sun Liang learned Lady Zhu had been harmed by the Princess of Quan and asked about the circumstances of Lady Zhu's death.

entries.zh: 全主懼曰：「我實不知，皆據二子熊、損所白。」
entries.en: Princess Quan, terrified, said, "I truly knew nothing—it all came from Zhu Ju's sons Xiong and Zhu Sun."
entries.literal: The Princess of Quan, afraid, said, "I truly did not know; it was all reported by Ju's two sons Xiong and Sun."

entries.zh: 亮殺熊、損。
entries.en: Sun Liang had Zhu Xiong and Zhu Sun executed.
entries.literal: Liang killed Xiong and Sun.

entries.zh: 損妻是峻妹也，孫綝益忌亮，遂廢亮，立休。
entries.en: Zhu Sun's wife was Jun's sister; Sun Chen, ever more hostile to Sun Liang, deposed him and raised Sun Xiu to the throne.
entries.literal: Zhu Sun's wife was Jun's younger sister; Sun Chen grew ever more jealous of Liang, then deposed Liang and established Xiu.

entries.zh: 永安五年262年，立夫人為皇后。
entries.en: In Yong'an 5 (262) he made Lady Zhu empress.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Yong'an (262 CE), he established the lady as empress.

entries.zh: 休卒，群臣尊夫人為皇太后，孫皓即位月餘，貶為景皇后。
entries.en: At Sun Xiu's death the court hailed her as empress dowager; a month after Sun Hao took the throne she was reduced to Empress Jing.
entries.literal: When Xiu died, the host of ministers honored the lady as empress dowager; a little more than a month after Sun Hao succeeded, she was demoted to Empress Jing.

entries.zh: 稱安定宮。
entries.en: She was given the title Palace of Anding.
entries.literal: She was styled the Palace of Anding.

entries.zh: 甘露元年265年七月，見逼薨，合葬定陵。
entries.en: In the seventh month of Ganlu 1 (265) she was driven to her death and was buried with Sun Xiu at Ding Mausoleum.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Ganlu (265 CE), she was forced and died; joint burial at Ding Mausoleum.

entries.zh: 《搜神記》曰：孫峻殺朱主，埋於石子岡。
entries.en: The Soushen ji says Sun Jun killed Lady Zhu and buried her on Shizi Hill.
entries.literal: The Soushen ji states: Sun Jun killed Lady Zhu and buried her at Shizi Hill.

entries.zh: 歸命即位，將欲改葬之。
entries.en: When Sun Hao took the throne as Lord Who Surrenders, he meant to give her a proper reburial.
entries.literal: When the Lord Who Surrenders succeeded, he was about to rebury her.

entries.zh: 塚墓相亞，不可識別，而宮人頗識主亡時所著衣服，乃使兩巫各住一處以伺其靈，使察鑑之，不得相近。
entries.en: The graves lay too close to tell apart, but palace women remembered the clothes Lady Zhu wore at death; Sun Hao posted two shamans at separate spots to watch for her spirit and identify the grave, forbidding them to compare notes.
entries.literal: Tombs and graves pressed close together and could not be distinguished; yet palace women fairly well knew the clothes the lady wore at death; therefore he sent two shamans each to dwell in one place to watch for her spirit and have them identify it, not allowing them to approach each other.

entries.zh: 久時，二人俱白：見一女人年可三十餘，上著青錦束頭，紫白袷裳，丹綈絲履，從石子岡上半岡，而以手抑膝長太息，小住須臾，進一塚上便住，徘徊良久，奄然不見。
entries.en: After a long wait both reported the same vision: a woman of about thirty in green brocade head-wrap, purple-and-white lined robe, and red silk shoes climbed halfway up Shizi Hill, pressed her knee, sighed, paused at one mound, wandered awhile, and vanished.
entries.literal: After a long while both reported: they saw a woman of perhaps thirty-odd years, wearing green brocade head-binding, purple-and-white lined robe, and red silk shoes; from halfway up Shizi Hill she came, pressing her knee with her hand and sighing long; pausing briefly, she advanced to one grave and stopped, pacing for a long while, then suddenly vanished.

entries.zh: 二人之言，不謀而同，於是開塚，衣服如之。
entries.en: Their accounts matched without collusion; they opened the grave and found the clothes just as described.
entries.literal: The two men's words matched without prior agreement; thereupon they opened the grave, and the clothes were as described.

entries.zh: 孫皓滕夫人，故太常胤之族女也。
entries.en: Sun Hao's empress Lady Teng was a kinswoman of former Grand Master of Ceremonies Teng Yin.
entries.literal: Sun Hao's Lady Teng was a clanswoman of the former Grand Master of Ceremonies Yin.

entries.zh: 胤夷滅，夫人父牧，以疏遠徙邊郡。
entries.en: After Teng Yin's clan was destroyed, her father Teng Mu was exiled to a frontier commandery as a distant kinsman.
entries.literal: When Yin was exterminated, the lady's father Mu, as a distant relation, was banished to a frontier commandery.

entries.zh: 孫休即位，大赦，得還，以牧為五官中郎。
entries.en: Sun Xiu's general amnesty let him return; Teng Mu was named a Gentleman of the Five Offices.
entries.literal: When Sun Xiu succeeded, there was a general amnesty; he was able to return, and Mu was made Gentlemen of the Five Offices.

entries.zh: 皓既封烏程侯，聘牧女為妃。
entries.en: When Sun Hao was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wucheng, he betrothed Teng Mu's daughter.
entries.literal: After Hao was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wucheng, he betrothed Mu's daughter as consort.

entries.zh: 皓即位，立為皇后，封牧高密侯，拜衛將軍，錄尚書事。
entries.en: At his accession he made her empress, enfeoffed Teng Mu as Marquis of Gaomi, and named him Guards General with oversight of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: When Hao succeeded, he established her as empress, enfeoffed Mu as Marquis of Gaomi, appointed him Guards General, and recorded Masters of Writing affairs.

entries.zh: 後朝士以牧尊戚，頗推令諫爭。
entries.en: Later courtiers, seeing Teng Mu's rank as empress kin, pressed him to remonstrate with the throne.
entries.literal: Later court gentlemen, because Mu was an honored affine, largely urged him to remonstrate.

entries.zh: 而夫人寵漸衰，皓滋不悅，皓母何恆左右之。
entries.en: As Lady Teng's favor waned Sun Hao grew angry, while his mother Lady He always sided with her.
entries.literal: But the lady's favor gradually declined; Hao grew ever more displeased; Hao's mother He constantly sided with her.

entries.zh: 又太史言，於運歷，后不可易，皓信巫覡，故得不廢，常供養昇平宮。
entries.en: Astrologers said the empress could not be changed by fate; Sun Hao trusted diviners, so she kept her title though he maintained rites at the Palace of Shengping instead.
entries.literal: Moreover the grand astrologer said that in the cycle of fate the empress could not be changed; Hao trusted shamans and sorcerers, therefore she was not deposed, and he regularly maintained offerings at the Palace of Shengping.

entries.zh: 牧見遣居蒼梧郡，雖爵位不奪，其實裔也，遂道路憂死。
entries.en: Teng Mu was sent to Cangwu; though his title remained, he was effectively exiled and died of grief on the road.
entries.literal: Mu was seen off to dwell in Cangwu Commandery; although rank was not taken away, in reality he was an exile, and on the road he died of grief.

entries.zh: 長秋官僚，備員而已，受朝賀表疏如故。
entries.en: The empress's household staff existed in name only; formal congratulations still reached her as before.
entries.literal: The Long Autumn officials were names only; receiving court congratulations and memorials continued as before.

entries.zh: 而皓內諸寵姬，佩皇后璽紱者多矣。
entries.en: Meanwhile many of Sun Hao's favorite concubines wore the empress's seal and sash.
entries.literal: Yet among Hao's favored concubines within, many wore the empress's seal and ribbon.

entries.zh: 《江表傳》曰：皓又使黃門備行州郡，科取將吏家女。
entries.en: The Jiang biao zhuan adds that Sun Hao sent eunuchs through the provinces to levy daughters of officials.
entries.literal: The Jiang biao zhuan states: Hao also sent Yellow Gate attendants through the provinces and commanderies to levy and take daughters of generals and clerks' households.

entries.zh: 其二千石大臣子女，皆當歲歲言名，年十五六一簡閱，簡閱不中，乃得出嫁。
entries.en: Ministers' daughters had to register yearly; at fifteen or sixteen they were inspected, and only those rejected could marry.
entries.literal: Daughters of ministers at the two-thousand-bushel rank all had to report their names every year; at ages fifteen or sixteen they were inspected, and only if they failed inspection could they marry out.

entries.zh: 后宮千數，而採擇無已。
entries.en: The harem held thousands of women, yet the levies never stopped.
entries.literal: The rear palace numbered in the thousands, yet selection never ceased.

entries.zh: 天紀四年，隨皓遷於洛陽。
entries.en: In Tianji 4 she followed Sun Hao into exile at Luoyang.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Tianji, she followed Hao in removal to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 吳夫人
entries.en: Lady Wu.
entries.literal: Lady Wu.

entries.zh: 鄰年九歲，代領豫章，近封都鄉侯。
entries.en: Sun Lin took Yuzhang at nine and soon received the marquisate of Dou township.
entries.literal: At age nine Lin replaced him as leader of Yuzhang and was shortly enfeoffed Marquis of Dou Township.

entries.zh: 〈吴书曰：邻字公达，雅性精敏，幼有令誉。〉
entries.en: 〈The Wu shu: Sun Lin, styled Gongda, was acute and polished and famed even as a boy.〉
entries.literal: 〈The Wu shu states: Lin’s courtesy name was Gongda; by nature he was refined, keen, and from youth had a fine reputation.〉

entries.zh: 在郡垂二十年，討平叛賊，功績修理。
entries.en: For almost twenty years in the prefecture he crushed rebels and ran an orderly administration.
entries.literal: In the commandery nearly twenty years, he suppressed and pacified rebel bandits; his achievements and administration were orderly.

entries.zh: 召還武昌，為繞帳督。
entries.en: Recalled to Wuchang, he commanded the headquarters guard.
entries.literal: He was summoned back to Wuchang and became commander of the tent guard.

entries.zh: 時太常潘浚掌荊州事，重安長陳留舒燮有罪下獄，浚嘗失燮，欲置之於法。
entries.en: Minister Pan Jun then governed Jingzhou; Shu Xie of Chenliu, magistrate of Chong’an, stood accused—Pan Jun had old grievances and meant to punish him.
entries.literal: At that time Minister of Ceremonies Pan Jun oversaw Jing Province affairs; the magistrate of Chong’an, Shu Xie of Chenliu, was guilty and imprisoned; Jun had once faulted Xie and wished to apply the law to him.

entries.zh: 論者多為有言，浚猶不釋。
entries.en: Many pleaded for Shu Xie; Pan Jun still refused to relent.
entries.literal: Though many debaters spoke on his behalf, Jun still would not release him.

entries.zh: 鄰謂浚曰："舒伯膺兄弟爭死，海內義之，以為美談，仲膺又奉國舊意。
entries.en: Sun Lin told Pan Jun: The Shu brothers once vied to die for honor—the empire admired it—and Zhongying still carries that loyalty.
entries.literal: Lin said to Jun, The Shu brothers Boying contended to die for each other—the realm praised their righteousness as a fine tale—and Zhongying moreover embodies the state’s former intentions.

entries.zh: 今君殺其子弟，若天下一統，青蓋北巡，中州士人必問仲膺繼嗣，答者雲潘承明殺燮，於事何如?"浚意即解，燮用得濟。
entries.en: If you execute his kin and the empire is someday reunited, the north will ask after Zhongying’s heir—and answering Pan Jun killed Shu Xie will shame you. Pan Jun relented and Shu Xie was spared.
entries.literal: Now if you kill his sons and nephews, should the realm unite and the imperial canopy tour north, gentlemen of the Central Plains will surely ask who succeeds Zhongying—if the answer is Pan Chengming killed Xie, how will that stand? Jun’s intent immediately loosened, and Xie obtained deliverance.

entries.zh: 〈《博物志》曰：仲膺名邵。
entries.en: 〈Bowuzhi: Zhongying’s personal name was Shao.
entries.literal: 〈The Bowuzhi states: Zhongying’s given name was Shao.

entries.zh: 初，伯膺亲友为人所杀，仲膺为报怨。
entries.en: Boying’s kin had been murdered; Zhongying took revenge.
entries.literal: At first Boying’s relatives were murdered by someone; Zhongying avenged the grievance.

entries.zh: 事觉，兄弟争死，皆得免。
entries.en: When discovered they argued over who should die; both were pardoned.
entries.literal: When the affair was discovered the brothers vied to die; both were spared.

entries.zh: 袁术时，邵为阜陵长。
entries.en: Under Yuan Shu, Shao was magistrate of Fuling.
entries.literal: During Yuan Shu’s time Shao was magistrate of Fuling.

entries.zh: 亦见江表传。〉
entries.en: The Jiangbiao zhuan records the same.〉
entries.literal: It is also seen in the Jiangbiao zhuan.〉

entries.zh: 鄰遷夏口沔中督、威遠將軍，所居任職。
entries.en: Sun Lin rose to middle-Han–Xiakou inspector and General Who Deters the Distance, performing solid service.
entries.literal: Lin was promoted inspector of Xiakou and the central Mian and General Who Deters the Distance, carrying out his duties where stationed.

entries.zh: 赤烏十二年卒。
entries.en: He died in Chiwu 12.
entries.literal: He died in the twelfth year of Chiwu.

entries.zh: 子苗嗣。
entries.en: His son Sun Miao inherited.
entries.literal: His son Miao succeeded.

entries.zh: 苗弟旅及叔父安、熙、績，皆歷列位。
entries.en: Sun Miao’s brother Sun Lü and uncles Sun An, Sun Xi, and Sun Ji all served in turn.
entries.literal: Miao’s younger brother Lü and uncles An, Xi, and Ji all held successive offices.

entries.zh: 〈吴历曰：邻又有子曰述，为武昌督，平荆州事。
entries.en: 〈The Wu li notes another son, Shu, who commanded Wuchang and Jingzhou affairs.
entries.literal: 〈The Wu li states: Lin also had a son named Shu, who was inspector of Wuchang and handled Jing Province affairs.

entries.zh: 震，无难督。
entries.en: Sun Zhen held the colonelcy Who Has No Difficulty.
entries.literal: Zhen, Colonel Who Has No Difficulty.

entries.zh: 谐，城门校尉。
entries.en: Sun Xie was colonel of the Capital Gates.
entries.literal: Xie, colonel of the Capital Gates.

entries.zh: 歆，乐乡督。
entries.en: Sun Xin commanded Lexiang.
entries.literal: Xin, inspector of Lexiang.

entries.zh: 震后御晋军，与张悌俱死。
entries.en: Sun Zhen later faced the Jin host and fell beside Zhang Ti.
entries.literal: Later Zhen opposed the Jin army and died together with Zhang Ti.

entries.zh: 贲曾孙惠，字德施。
entries.en: Sun Ben’s great-grandson Sun Hui, styled Deshi.
entries.literal: Ben’s great-grandson Hui, courtesy name Deshi.

entries.zh: 《惠别传》曰：惠好学有才智，晋永宁元年，赴齐王冏义，以功封晋兴侯，辟大司马贼曹属。
entries.en: His appendix: Sun Hui was bookish and clever; in Jin Yongning 1 he joined Prince Sima Jiong’s righteous army, earned the marquisate of Jinxing, and entered the grand marshal’s criminal bureau.
entries.literal: The Separate Biography of Hui states: Hui loved learning and had talent and judgment; in the first year of Yongning of Jin he answered Prince Qi of Qi’s call to righteousness and for merit was enfeoffed Marquis of Jinxing and summoned aide in the bandit bureau of the Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 冏骄矜僭侈，天下失望。
entries.en: Sima Jiong grew arrogant and wasteful and forfeited the empire’s trust.
entries.literal: Jiong was arrogant, presumptuous, and extravagant; the realm lost hope in him.

entries.zh: 惠献言於冏，讽以五难、四不可，劝令委让万机，归籓青岱，辞甚深切。
entries.en: Sun Hui remonstrated with the five difficulties and four impossibilities, urging him to surrender power and retire to his Shandong fief—in biting terms.
entries.literal: Hui submitted advice to Jiong, using allegories of five difficulties and four impossibilities, urging him to yield the myriad affairs of state and return to his fief on Qing and Dai—the words were trenchant indeed.

entries.zh: 冏不能纳，顷之果败。
entries.en: Sima Jiong would not listen and soon fell.
entries.literal: Jiong could not accept it; shortly afterward he indeed fell.

entries.zh: 成都王颖召为大将军参军。
entries.en: Prince Chengdu Sima Ying named him grand general’s aide.
entries.literal: Prince Chengdu Sima Ying summoned him as aide to the Grand General.

entries.zh: 是时颖将有事於长沙，以陆机为前锋都督。
entries.en: Sima Ying was preparing a Changsha campaign and made Lu Ji vanguard commander.
entries.literal: At that time Ying was about to undertake affairs at Changsha and made Lu Ji advance commander.

entries.zh: 惠与机乡里亲厚，忧其致祸，谓之曰：“子盍让都督於王粹乎？”
entries.en: Sun Hui, Lu Ji’s townsman and friend, feared ruin for him and asked: Why not give the command to Wang Cui.
entries.literal: Hui was from the same village as Ji and close to him; fearing disaster for Ji, he said to him, Why not yield the commander’s post to Wang Cui?

entries.zh: 机曰：“将谓吾避贼首鼠，更速其害。”
entries.en: Lu Ji answered: They would call me a coward—that would only hasten disaster.
entries.literal: Ji said, People would say I shrink from the enemy like a rat—that would hasten my ruin.

entries.zh: 机寻被戮，二弟云、耽亦见杀，惠甚伤恨之。
entries.en: Lu Ji was soon executed with his brothers Yun and Dan; Sun Hui mourned bitterly.
entries.literal: Ji was shortly afterward executed; his two younger brothers Yun and Dan were also killed—Hui deeply grieved for them.

entries.zh: 永兴元年，乘舆幸鄴，司空东海王越治兵下邳，惠以书干越，诡其姓名，自称南岳逸民秦祕之，勉以勤王匡世之略，辞义甚美。
entries.en: In Yongxing 1 the court moved toward Ye; Prince Donghai Sima Yue trained troops at Xiapi. Sun Hui wrote under the pseudonym Southern Mountain hermit Qin Mizhi, urging him to rescue the throne.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongxing the imperial carriage favored Ye; Minister of Works Prince Donghai Sima Yue drilled troops at Xiapi—Hui wrote to Yue under a false name, calling himself the South Mountain recluse Qin Mizhi, urging with handsome phrases the strategy of aiding the king and restoring the age.

entries.zh: 越省其书，榜题道衢，招求其人。
entries.en: Sima Yue posted the essay at crossroads and hunted for the author.
entries.literal: Yue read his letter, posted the title on the roads, and sought the man.

entries.zh: 惠乃出见，越即以为记室参军，专掌文疏，豫参谋议。
entries.en: Sun Hui revealed himself; Sima Yue made him secretary-aide for drafts and planning.
entries.literal: Hui then came forward to meet him; Yue immediately made him secretary-aide, solely in charge of documents and participating in counsel.

entries.zh: 每造书檄，越或驿马催之，应命立成，皆有辞旨。
entries.en: When Sima Yue needed edicts he sometimes sent post riders—Sun Hui composed them on demand, always elegant.
entries.literal: Whenever he drafted letters or proclamations, Yue sometimes sent relay horses to hurry him; he answered the summons on the spot and finished at once, each piece having polished rhetoric.

entries.zh: 累迁显职，后为广武将军、安丰内史。
entries.en: He climbed to high office and ended as campaigning General Who Displays Might and interior minister of Anfeng.
entries.literal: He rose through prominent posts and later became General Who Displays Might on Campaign and interior minister of Anfeng.

entries.zh: 年四十七卒。
entries.en: He died at forty-seven.
entries.literal: He died at forty-seven.

entries.zh: 惠文翰凡數十首。
entries.en: His writings ran to several dozen pieces.〉
entries.literal: Hui’s literary compositions number several tens of pieces in all.〉

entries.zh: 子泰，曹氏之甥也，為長水校尉。
entries.en: His son Sun Tai was a Cao in-law and rose to colonel of Changan waters.
entries.literal: His son Tai was the Cao clan's nephew by marriage and served as Colonel of Changan Waters.

entries.zh: 嘉禾三年，從權圍新城，中流矢死。
entries.en: In Jiahe 3 he joined Sun Quan’s siege of Xincheng and died to a stray shaft.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jiahe he followed Quan in besieging Xincheng and was struck by a stray arrow and died.

entries.zh: 泰子秀為前將軍、夏口督。
entries.en: Sun Tai’s son Sun Xiu was General of the Van and commander at Xiakou.
entries.literal: Tai's son Xiu was General of the Van and inspector of Xiakou.

entries.zh: 秀公室至親，握兵在外，皓意不能平。
entries.en: Sun Xiu was imperial kin commanding troops on the frontier—Sun Hao could not abide it.
entries.literal: Xiu was closest kin of the ducal house and held troops abroad—Hao could not stomach it.

entries.zh: 建衡二年，皓遣何定將五千人至夏口獵。
entries.en: In Jianheng 2 Sun Hao sent He Ding with five thousand men to hunt near Xiakou.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jianheng Hao sent He Ding with five thousand men to hunt at Xiakou.

entries.zh: 先是，民間歛言秀當見圖，而定遠獵，秀遂驚，夜將妻子親兵數百人奔晉。
entries.en: Rumors already said Sun Xiu would be framed; when He Ding ranged far afield on “hunt,” Sun Xiu bolted by night with family and hundreds of guards into Jin.
entries.literal: Before this, folk rumor said Xiu would be plotted against; Ding hunted far away—Xiu was alarmed and by night led wife, children, and several hundred household guards to flee to Jin.

entries.zh: 晉以秀為驃騎將軍、儀同三司，封會稽公。
entries.en: Jin named him general of agile cavalry with Three Ducal honors and duke of Kuaiji.
entries.literal: Jin appointed Xiu General of Agile Cavalry with ceremonies equal to the Three Offices and enfeoffed him Duke of Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 〈江表传曰：皓大怒，追改秀姓曰厉。
entries.en: 〈The Jiangbiao zhuan: Sun Hao was so enraged he renamed Sun Xiu “Li” retroactively.)
entries.literal: 〈《Jiangbiao zhuan》 states: Hao was furious and retroactively changed Xiu's surname to Li.

entries.zh: 干宝《晋纪》曰：秀在晋朝，初闻皓降，群臣毕贺，秀称疾不与，南向流涕曰：“昔讨逆弱冠以一校尉创业，今后主举江南而弃之，宗庙山陵，於此为墟。
entries.en: Gan Bao’s Jin ji: at the Jin court, when word came that Sun Hao had yielded, ministers rejoiced while Sun Xiu stayed away ill, faced south, and wept: “The Marshal Who Attacks Rebels began at twenty with a colonel’s commission; our last lord threw away the south—the ancestral shrines lie in dust.
entries.literal: Gan Bao's Jin Ji states: When Xiu was at the Jin court, he first heard Hao had surrendered; the ministers all congratulated—Xiu claimed illness and did not attend; facing south he wept and said, “Formerly the Marshal Who Attacks Rebels at twenty founded the realm with a colonel's rank; now the Later Lord raises Jiangnan yet casts it away—the ancestral temples and imperial tombs lie in ruins here.

entries.zh: 悠悠苍天，此何人哉！”
entries.en: O vast Heaven—what men have brought us here!”
entries.literal: Vast heaven—what manner of men are these!”

entries.zh: 朝廷美之。
entries.en: The Jin court praised him.
entries.literal: The court praised him.

entries.zh: 晋诸公赞曰：吴平，降为伏波将军，开府如故。
entries.en: (The Jin zhugong zan: after Wu fell he was demoted to general who calms the waves but kept his staff.)
entries.literal: 《Jin zhugong zan》 states: When Wu was pacified, he was reduced to General Who Calms the Waves with offices as before.

entries.zh: 永宁中卒，追赠骠骑、开府。
entries.en: He died under Yongning and was posthumously honored as agile cavalry general with full offices.
entries.literal: He died during Yongning; posthumously honored Agile Cavalry with offices.

entries.zh: 子俭，字仲节，给事中。〉
entries.en: His son Sun Jian, styled Zhongjie, served as palace attendant.〉
entries.literal: His son Jian, courtesy name Zhongjie, served as attendant within.〉

entries.zh: 韶年十七，收河餘眾，繕治京城。
entries.en: At seventeen Sun Shao rallied Sun He’s troops and rebuilt Jingcheng.
entries.literal: At age seventeen Shao gathered He's remaining host, repaired and ordered Jingcheng.

entries.zh: 起樓櫓，修器備議禦敵。
entries.en: He raised watchtowers, stocked weapons, and prepared a defense.
entries.literal: He raised towered engines, repaired implements and equipment, and laid plans to resist the enemy.

entries.zh: 權聞亂，從椒丘還，過定丹楊，引軍歸吳。
entries.en: Hearing of the revolt, Sun Quan raced back from Jiaoqiu, secured Danyang on the way, and marched for Wu.
entries.literal: When Quan heard of the disturbance he returned from Jiaoqiu, pacified Danyang en route, and led the army back to Wu.

entries.zh: 夜至京城下營，試攻驚之，兵皆乘城傳檄備警，歡聲動地，頗射外人，權使曉喻乃止。
entries.en: He camped under Jingcheng by night and feinted an assault—the garrison manned the walls, passed orders, cheered till the ground shook, and peppered the darkness with arrows until Sun Quan explained himself at dawn.
entries.literal: By night he camped below Jingcheng and probed with a trial attack to startle them—the troops all mounted the walls, passed writs and stood alert; joyous shouts shook the earth; they shot rather freely at those outside; Quan sent word of dawn before they stopped.

entries.zh: 明日見韶，甚器之。
entries.en: Next morning he met Sun Shao and was deeply impressed.
entries.literal: The next day he saw Shao and greatly esteemed him.

entries.zh: 即拜承烈校尉，統河部曲，食曲阿、丹徒二縣，自置長吏，一如河舊。
entries.en: He named him Colonel Who Upholds Fierce Resolve over Sun He’s old troops, with revenue from Qu’e and Dantu and the same right to pick county magistrates.
entries.literal: He immediately appointed him Colonel Who Upholds Fierce Resolve, commanding He's troops, subsisting on Qu’e and Dantu counties, appointing his own magistrates—exactly as He had formerly done.

entries.zh: 後為廣陵太守、偏將軍。
entries.en: Later he was Guangling prefect and General of the Left.
entries.literal: Later he became Administrator of Guangling and General of the Left.

entries.zh: 權為吳王，遷揚威將軍，封建德侯。
entries.en: When Sun Quan took the Wu kingship Sun Shao became General Who Displays Might and marquis of Jiande.
entries.literal: When Quan became King of Wu he promoted him General Who Displays Might and enfeoffed him Marquis of Jiande.

entries.zh: 權稱尊號，為鎮北將軍。
entries.en: When Sun Quan declared himself emperor Sun Shao was named General Who Guards the North.
entries.literal: When Quan assumed the imperial title he became General Who Guards the North.

entries.zh: 韶為邊將數十年，善養士卒，得其死力。
entries.en: For decades on the frontier he fed his men well and earned their lives.
entries.literal: Shao was a frontier general several decades; he was good at nurturing soldiers and won their willingness to die.

entries.zh: 常以警疆場遠斥候為務，先知動靜而為之備，故鮮有負敗。
entries.en: He lived on alert patrols, learned enemy moves early, and seldom lost.
entries.literal: He constantly took warning the borderlands and scouting far as his task; knowing enemy movements beforehand he prepared—therefore he rarely suffered defeat.

entries.zh: 青、徐、汝、沛頗來歸附，淮南濱江屯候皆徹兵遠徙，徐、泗、江、淮之地，不居者各數百里。
entries.en: People from Qing, Xu, Ru, and Pei drifted south; Wei stripped its Huai River posts—hundreds of li along Xu-Si-Jiang-Huai stood empty.
entries.literal: Qing, Xu, Ru, and Pei largely came to submit; Huainan riverbank watch posts all withdrew troops and moved far—along Xu, Si, Jiang, and Huai unsettled lands stretched several hundred li each.

entries.zh: 自權西征，還都武昌，韶不進見者十餘年。
entries.en: After Sun Quan marched west and fixed his court at Wuchang, Sun Shao stayed away from audience for more than ten years.
entries.literal: From Quan's western expedition and return capital to Wuchang, Shao did not advance to audience for over ten years.

entries.zh: 權還建業，乃得朝覲。
entries.en: Only when Sun Quan moved back to Jianye did Sun Shao appear at court.
entries.literal: When Quan returned to Jianye he was then able to pay court visit.

entries.zh: 權問青、徐諸屯要害，遠近人馬眾寡，魏將帥姓名，盡具識之，有問鹹對。
entries.en: Sun Quan quizzed him on Qing-Xu strongpoints, troop counts, distances, Wei commanders—Sun Shao answered every question from memory.
entries.literal: Quan asked about the critical points of the various garrisons in Qing and Xu, the distance and numbers of men and horses, and the names of Wei generals—he knew them all completely; whatever was asked he answered.

entries.zh: 身長八尺，儀貌都雅。
entries.en: He stood eight chi, composed and handsome.
entries.literal: His body was eight chi tall; his bearing was refined.

entries.zh: 權歡悅曰："吾久不見公禮，不圖進益乃爾。
entries.en: Sun Quan said with delight: I have missed you so long—I never guessed you had grown this sharp.
entries.literal: Quan joyfully said: I have long not seen Gongli—I did not imagine your advance could be thus.

entries.zh: "加領幽州牧、假節。
entries.en: He added him as inspector of You province with ceremonial axe and staff.
entries.literal: He additionally appointed Inspector of You Province and granted the tally of authority.

entries.zh: 赤烏四年卒。
entries.en: He died in Chiwu 4.
entries.literal: He died in the fourth year of Chiwu.

entries.zh: 子越嗣，至右將軍，越兄楷武衛大將軍、臨成侯，代越為京下督。
entries.en: His son Sun Yue inherited and rose to General of the Right; elder brother Sun Kai was grand marshal of the martial guard and marquis of Lincheng, replacing Sun Yue as capital-zone commander.
entries.literal: His son Yue succeeded; he rose to General of the Right; Yue's elder brother Kai was grand marshal of the martial guard and Marquis of Lincheng, replacing Yue as commander below the capital.

entries.zh: 楷弟異至領軍將軍，奕宗正卿，恢武陵太守。
entries.en: Sun Kai's younger brother became commanding general of the household army; a second Sun Yi headed the ministry for the imperial clan; Sun Hui was prefect of Wuling.
entries.literal: Kai's younger brother Yi rose to General Who Commands the Army; Yi became minister of the imperial clan; Hui was Administrator of Wuling.

entries.zh: 天璽元年，征楷為宮下鎮驃騎將軍。
entries.en: In Tianxi 1 Sun Kai was summoned as palace agile-cavalry general.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianxi Kai was summoned as agile-cavalry general below the palace.

entries.zh: 初永安賊施但等劫皓弟謙，襲建業，或白楷二端不即赴討者，皓數遣詰楷。
entries.en: When Yong’an rebels seized Sun Hao’s brother Sun Qian and struck Jianye, rumor said Sun Kai hesitated—Sun Hao berated him again and again.
entries.literal: At first the Yong’an bandits Shi Dan and others kidnapped Hao's younger brother Qian and raided Jianye; someone reported Kai wavered and did not immediately march to punish them—Hao repeatedly sent to rebuke Kai.

entries.zh: 楷常惶怖，而卒被召，遂將妻子親兵數百人歸晉，晉以為車騎將軍，封丹楊侯。
entries.en: Living in dread, Sun Kai bolted to Jin with family and hundreds of guards when summoned; Jin named him chariots-and-cavalry general and marquis of Danyang.
entries.literal: Kai was constantly fearful; when he was finally summoned he therefore led wife, children, and several hundred household guards to return to Jin—Jin appointed him General of Chariots and Cavalry and enfeoffed him Marquis of Danyang.

entries.zh: 〈晋诸公赞曰：吴平，降为渡辽将军，永安元年卒。
entries.en: 〈The Jin zhugong zan: after Wu fell he became general who crosses the Liao and died in Yongan 1.)
entries.literal: 〈《Jin zhugong zan》 states: When Wu was pacified he was reduced to General Who Crosses the Liao and died in the first year of Yongan.

entries.zh: 吴录曰：楷处事严整不如孙秀，而人间知名，过也。〉
entries.en: (The Wu lu says Sun Kai ran a looser ship than Sun Xiu yet was more famous—odd praise.〉
entries.literal: 《Wu lu》 states: Kai's handling of affairs was less rigorous than Sun Xiu's, yet he was better known among people—this surpassed reason.〉

entries.zh: 孫桓字叔武，河之子也。
entries.en: Sun Huan, styled Shuwo, was Sun He’s son.
entries.literal: Sun Huan, courtesy name Shuwo, was He's son.

entries.zh: 〈吴书曰：河有四子。
entries.en: 〈The Wu shu: Sun He had four sons.)
entries.literal: 〈《Wu shu》 states: He had four sons.

entries.zh: 长助，曲阿长。
entries.en: Eldest Sun Zhu, magistrate of Qu’e.
entries.literal: The eldest Zhu, magistrate of Qu’e.

entries.zh: 次谊，海盐长。
entries.en: Next Sun Yi, magistrate of Haiyan.
entries.literal: Next Yi, magistrate of Haiyan.

entries.zh: 并早卒。
entries.en: Both died young.
entries.literal: Both died early.

entries.zh: 次桓，仪容端正，器怀聪朗，博学强记，能论议应对，权常称为宗室颜渊，擢为武卫都尉。
entries.en: Sun Huan was handsome, quick-witted, learned, and eloquent—Sun Quan called him the clan’s Yan Hui and made him colonel of the martial guard.
entries.literal: Next Huan, whose bearing was correct, whose mind was bright, who studied broadly and memorized strongly, could debate and reply—Quan always called him the Zengzi of the imperial clan and promoted him colonel of the martial guard.

entries.zh: 从讨关羽於华容，诱羽餘党，得五千人，牛马器械甚众。〉
entries.en: He joined the strike on Guan Yu at Huarong, lured five thousand of his stragglers, and captured huge herds and gear.〉
entries.literal: He followed in campaigning against Guan Yu at Huarong, enticed Yu's remaining followers, gained five thousand men, and oxen, horses, and equipment were very numerous.〉

entries.zh: 年二十五，拜安東中郎將，與陸遜共拒劉備。
entries.en: At twenty-five he was General of the Household Gentlemen Who Pacifies the East beside Lu Xun against Liu Bei.
entries.literal: At age twenty-five he was appointed General of the Household Gentlemen Who Pacifies the East and together with Lu Xun resisted Liu Bei.

entries.zh: 備軍眾甚盛，彌山盈谷，桓投力奮命。
entries.en: Liu Bei’s host covered hills and dales; Sun Huan threw everything into the line.
entries.literal: Bei's army host was very strong, filling mountains and valleys; Huan devoted his strength and risked his life.

entries.zh: 與遜戮力，備遂敗走。
entries.en: He and Lu Xun strained together until Liu Bei broke and ran.
entries.literal: Together with Xun he exerted joint effort; Bei thereupon fled in defeat.

entries.zh: 桓斬上
entries.en: Sun Huan severed the Shanggui—
entries.literal: Huan cut Shang—

entries.en: ms. dou
entries.literal: (variant dou)

entries.en: ms. kui
entries.literal: (variant kui)

entries.zh: 道，截其徑要。
entries.en: —route and seized the defiles.
entries.literal: —road and intercepted the vital narrows.

entries.zh: 備逾山越險，僅乃得免，忿恚歎曰："吾昔初至京城，桓尚小兒，而今迫孤乃至此也!"桓以功拜建武將軍，封丹徒侯，下督牛港，作橫江塢，會卒。
entries.en: Liu Bei scrambled through the hills barely alive and swore: “When I first saw Jingcheng, Sun Huan was a boy—now he corners me like this!” Sun Huan earned General Who Establishes Martial Might, marquis of Dantu, command at Niugang, built the Hengjiang redoubt, then died.
entries.literal: Bei crossed mountains and passed defiles, barely escaping; angrily sighing he said: "When I first came to Jingcheng, Huan was still a small child—yet now he presses me to this!" Huan for merit was appointed General Who Establishes Martial Might, enfeoffed Marquis of Dantu, directed Niugang below, built Hengjiang rampart, and happened to die.

entries.zh: 〈吴书曰：桓弟俊，字叔英，性度恢弘，才经文武，为定武中郎将，屯戍薄落，赤乌十三年卒。
entries.en: 〈The Wu shu: younger brother Sun Jun, styled Shuying, genial and able in letters and arms—General Who Fixes Martial Might at Boluo—died Chiwu 13.)
entries.literal: 〈《Wu shu》 states: Huan's younger brother Jun, courtesy name Shuying, by nature was spacious in capacity and accomplished in civil and military arts—General Who Fixes Martial Might, garrisoning Boluo; died thirteenth year of Chiwu.

entries.zh: 长子建袭爵，平虏将军。
entries.en: Eldest Sun Jian inherited as General Who Pacifies Captives.
entries.literal: Eldest son Jian inherited the noble rank—General Who Pacifies Captives.

entries.zh: 少子慎，镇南将军。
entries.en: Younger Sun Shen became General Who Guards the South.
entries.literal: Younger son Shen, General Who Guards the South.

entries.zh: 慎子丞，字显世。
entries.en: Sun Shen’s son Sun Cheng, styled Xianshi.
entries.literal: Shen's son Cheng, courtesy name Xianshi.

entries.zh: 文士传曰：丞好学，有文章，作萤火赋行於世。
entries.en: (The Wenshi zhuan: Sun Cheng loved books and wrote the Firefly Fu.)
entries.literal: 《Wenshi zhuan》 states: Cheng loved learning and had literary skill; he composed the Rhapsody on Fireflies which circulated in the world.

entries.zh: 为黄门侍郎，与顾荣俱为侍臣。
entries.en: He was a yellow-gates gentleman alongside Gu Rong.
entries.literal: He was Gentleman of the Yellow Gates and together with Gu Rong both were attending ministers.

entries.zh: 归命世内侍多得罪尤，惟荣、丞独获全。
entries.en: When Wu yielded, most palace attendants paid with their lives—only Gu Rong and Sun Cheng survived.
entries.literal: In the generation that submitted to the decree, many inner attendants incurred blame and penalty—only Rong and Cheng alone achieved preservation.

entries.zh: 常使二人记事，丞答顾问，乃下诏曰：“自今已后，用侍郎皆当如今宗室丞、顾荣畴也。”
entries.en: The Jin ruler often consulted them and decreed: Future gentlemen-attendants must match Sun Cheng and Gu Rong.
entries.literal: He constantly had the two men keep records; Cheng answered inquiries—thereupon an edict was issued: From now on, appointed gentlemen of the attending suite should all be like the imperial-clan Cheng and Gu Rong here.

entries.zh: 吴平赴洛，为范阳涿令，甚有称绩。
entries.en: After the conquest he served as magistrate of Zhuo in Fanyang with a fine record.
entries.literal: When Wu was pacified he went to Luoyang and became magistrate of Zhuo in Fanyang—he had very praised achievements.

entries.zh: 永安中，陆机为成都王大都督，请丞为司马，与机俱被害。〉
entries.en: In Yongan Lu Ji made him staff officer on Prince Chengdu’s campaign—they died together.〉
entries.literal: During Yongan Lu Ji was grand marshal to Prince Chengdu and invited Cheng as marshal—together with Ji he met murder.〉

entries.zh: 孫靜字幼臺，堅季弟也。
entries.en: Sun Jing, styled Youtai, was the youngest of Sun Jian’s brothers.
entries.literal: Sun Jing, courtesy name Youtai, was the youngest younger brother of Sun Jian.

entries.zh: 堅始舉事，靜糾合鄉曲及宗室五六百人以為保障，眾咸附焉。
entries.en: When Sun Jian first rose in arms, Sun Jing rallied some five or six hundred local men and kinsmen as a protective force, and people flocked to him.
entries.literal: When Sun Jian first raised troops, Jing gathered five or six hundred men from the villages and the clan to serve as a safeguard, and the masses all attached themselves to him.

entries.zh: 策破劉繇，定諸縣。
entries.en: Sun Ce defeated Liu Yao and brought the counties under control.
entries.literal: Ce defeated Liu Yao and pacified the various counties.

entries.zh: 進攻會稽，遣人請靜，靜將家屬與策會於錢唐。
entries.en: He pressed the attack on Kuaiji, sent for Sun Jing, and Sun Jing brought his household to join Sun Ce at Qiantang.
entries.literal: Advancing to attack Kuaiji, he sent someone to summon Jing; Jing led his family members and met Ce at Qiantang.

entries.zh: 是時太守王朗拒策於固陵，策數渡水戰，不能克。
entries.en: The prefect Wang Lang held Sun Ce off at Guling; Sun Ce tried more than once to force a crossing and fight on the other bank but could not break through.
entries.literal: At that time the Administrator Wang Lang resisted Ce at Guling; Ce several times crossed the water to give battle but could not overcome him.

entries.zh: 靜說策曰："朗負阻城守，難可卒拔。
entries.en: Sun Jing urged Sun Ce: Wang Lang is dug in behind natural barriers; you cannot expect to storm him overnight.
entries.literal: Jing urged Ce, saying, Lang relies on natural obstacles and defends the city; he is hard to take in a hurry.

entries.zh: 查瀆南去此數十里，
entries.en: Zha Creek lies a few dozen li to the south,
entries.literal: Zha Creek is several tens of li south of here,

entries.zh: 〈查音祖加反。〉
entries.en: 〈The marginal gloss indicates that Zha takes its initial from zu and its rime from jia.〉
entries.literal: 〈Note on pronunciation: the character for Zha is read zu-jia [fanqie].〉

entries.zh: 而道之要徑也，宜從彼據其內，所謂攻其無備、出其不意者也。
entries.en: That route is the vital approach; thrust inland along it and strike where they do not expect you.
entries.literal: and it is a crucial path; you ought to advance by that route and seize what lies within—what is called striking where they are unprepared and catching them unawares.

entries.zh: 吾當自帥眾為軍前隊，破之必矣。
entries.en: I will lead the main body myself as the first wave—we will crack them for certain.
entries.literal: I shall personally lead the host as the vanguard of the army; we will surely break them.

entries.zh: "策曰："善。
entries.en: Sun Ce replied, Good.
entries.literal: Ce said, Good.

entries.zh: "乃詐令軍中曰："頃連雨水濁，兵飲之多腹痛，令促具罌缶數百口澄水。
entries.en: Then he put out a false order: The river has been silty from all this rain; men who drink it are doubled up with cramps—have them ready hundreds of jars at once to draw off clear water.
entries.literal: Then he falsely announced to the army: The rains have lately turned the water muddy; the soldiers drinking it have mostly gotten stomachaches—order them quickly to prepare several hundred jars and pots to settle the water.

entries.zh: "至昏暮，羅以然火誑朗，便分軍夜投查瀆道，襲高遷屯。
entries.en: At nightfall he lit decoy fires to fool Wang Lang, split his force, and marched up the Zha Creek track after dark to strike the camp at Gaoxian.
entries.literal: At dusk he spread fires to deceive Lang, then divided the army and by night sent them along the Zha Creek road to raid the Gaoxian camp.

entries.zh: 〈臣松之案：今永兴县有高迁桥。〉
entries.en: 〈Pei Songzhi notes that Gaoxian Bridge still stands in present-day Yongxing County.〉
entries.literal: 〈Pei Songzhi’s investigation: today in Yongxing County there is a Gaoxian Bridge.〉

entries.zh: 朗大驚。
entries.en: Wang Lang was thrown into panic.
entries.literal: Lang was greatly alarmed.

entries.zh: 遣故丹楊太守周昕等帥兵前戰。
entries.en: He dispatched the former Danyang prefect Zhou Xin and others to take the lead with their men.
entries.literal: He sent the former Danyang Administrator Zhou Xin and others to lead troops forward into battle.

entries.zh: 策破昕等，斬之，遂定會稽。
entries.en: Sun Ce routed them, killed Zhou Xin, and settled Kuaiji.
entries.literal: Ce defeated Xin and the others, beheaded them, and thereupon pacified Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：昕字大明。
entries.en: 〈According to the Kuaiji dianlu, Zhou Xin’s courtesy name was Daming.
entries.literal: 〈The Kuaiji Canon Record states: Xin’s courtesy name was Daming.

entries.zh: 少游京师，师事太傅陈蕃，博览群书，明於风角，善推灾异。
entries.en: He had studied in the capital under Grand Tutor Chen Fan, read widely, and was adept at astrological signs and reading portents.
entries.literal: In his youth he traveled to the capital and studied under Grand Tutor Chen Fan; he read widely and was skilled in “wind-angle” divination and interpreting anomalies.

entries.zh: 辟太尉府，举高第，稍迁丹杨太守。
entries.en: He entered the Grand Commandant’s service, graduated with highest honors, and rose step by step to prefect of Danyang.
entries.literal: He was summoned to the Grand Commandant’s office, ranked at the top of his cohort, and was gradually promoted to Danyang Administrator.

entries.zh: 曹公起义兵，昕前后遣兵万餘人助公征伐。
entries.en: When Cao Cao raised his coalition army, Zhou Xin repeatedly sent him upward of ten thousand men for the campaigns.
entries.literal: When Duke Cao raised the righteous army, Xin in succession sent more than ten thousand troops to assist the duke in his expeditions.

entries.zh: 袁术之在淮南也，昕恶其淫虐，绝不与通。
entries.en: While Yuan Shu occupied Huainan, Zhou Xin abhorred his cruelty and dissipation and would have nothing to do with him.
entries.literal: When Yuan Shu was in Huainan, Xin detested his debauchery and cruelty and utterly refused dealings with him.

entries.zh: 献帝春秋曰：袁术遣吴景攻昕，未拔，景乃募百姓敢从周昕者死不赦。
entries.en: The Xiandi Chunqiu records that Yuan Shu sent Wu Jing against Zhou Xin without reducing him; Wu Jing then threatened the populace that anyone who sided with Zhou Xin would die without mercy.
entries.literal: The Annals of Emperor Xian states: Yuan Shu sent Wu Jing to attack Xin but did not capture him; Jing then promised the common people that whoever dared follow Zhou Xin would be put to death without pardon.

entries.zh: 昕曰：“我则不德，百姓何罪？”
entries.en: Zhou Xin said, If I am the one at fault, what have the people done wrong?
entries.literal: Xin said, If I lack virtue, what crime have the common people committed?

entries.zh: 遂散兵，还本郡。〉
entries.en: So he sent his soldiers home and withdrew to his own commandery.
entries.literal: Thereupon he dispersed his troops and returned to his native commandery.

entries.zh: 表拜靜為奮武校尉，欲授之重任，靜戀墳墓宗族，不樂出仕，求留鎮守。
entries.en: Sun Ce recommended him as Colonel Who Inspires Martial Might and meant to give him a major post, but Sun Jing was unwilling to leave his family graves and kin and asked instead to stay and hold the territory.
entries.literal: [Sun Ce] memorialized and appointed Jing Colonel Who Inspires Martial Might, wishing to give him heavy responsibility; Jing was attached to his ancestral graves and clan and did not relish leaving office, and asked to remain to guard and hold the region.

entries.zh: 策從之。
entries.en: Sun Ce agreed.
