entries.literal: Ce granted his request.

entries.zh: 權統事，就遷昭義中郎將，終於家。
entries.en: When Sun Quan took charge, Sun Jing was promoted in place to General of the Household Gentlemen of Manifest Righteousness and ended his days at home.
entries.literal: When Quan assumed direction of affairs, [Jing] was promoted on the spot to General of the Household Gentlemen of Manifest Righteousness and died at home.

entries.zh: 有五子，皓、瑜、皎、奐、謙。
entries.en: He had five sons—Hao, Yu, Jiao, Huan, and Qian.
entries.literal: He had five sons: Hao, Yu, Jiao, Huan, and Qian.

entries.zh: 皓三子：綽、超、恭。
entries.en: Sun Hao had three sons: Chuo, Chao, and Gong.
entries.literal: Hao had three sons: Chuo, Chao, and Gong.

entries.zh: 超為偏將軍。
entries.en: Sun Chao rose to General of the Left.
entries.literal: Chao served as General of the Left.

entries.zh: 恭生峻。
entries.en: Sun Gong was the father of Sun Jun.
entries.literal: Gong fathered Jun.

entries.zh: 綽生綝。
entries.en: Sun Chuo was the father of Sun Lin.
entries.literal: Chuo fathered Lin.

entries.zh: 邵字孝則，博覽書傳，好樂人倫。
entries.en: Gu Shao, styled Xiaze, read widely and loved ethics.
entries.literal: Shao courtesy name Xiaze—read widely books and transmissions—loved delighting in human relations.

entries.zh: 少與舅陸績齊名，而陸遜、張敦、卜靜等皆亞焉。
entries.en: As a youth he rivaled uncle Lu Ji; Lu Xun, Zhang Dun, and Bu Jing stood slightly below.
entries.literal: Young together with maternal uncle Lu Ji equally famed—yet Lu Xun, Zhang Dun, Bu Jing and others all ranked below.

entries.zh: 〈吴录曰：敦字叔方，静字玄风，并吴郡人。
entries.en: 〈The Wu lu: Zhang Dun styled Shufang; Bu Jing styled Xuanfeng—both from Wu.)
entries.literal: 〈Wu lu states: Dun courtesy name Shufang—Jing courtesy name Xuanfeng—both men of Wu commandery.

entries.zh: 敦德量渊懿，清虚淡泊，又善文辞。
entries.en: Zhang Dun was deep, quiet, and literary.
entries.literal: Dun's virtue capacity deep profound—pure empty bland pale—also skilled literary phrasing.

entries.zh: 孙权为车骑将军，辟西曹掾，转主簿，出补海昬令，甚有惠化，年三十二卒。
entries.en: Sun Quan named him aide and Haihun magistrate; he died at thirty-two.
entries.literal: Sun Quan was chariots-and-cavalry general—summoned western bureau aide—transferred chief clerk—went out supplementing Haihun magistrate—had very benevolent transformation—age thirty-two died.

entries.zh: 卜静终於剡令。〉
entries.en: Bu Jing died as magistrate of Yan.〉
entries.literal: Bu Jing ended at Yan magistrate.〉

entries.zh: 自州郡庶幾及四方人士，往來相見，或言議而去，或結厚而別，風聲流聞，遠近稱之。
entries.en: Scholars everywhere sought him out and praised his name.
entries.literal: From commandery near-worthy and four quarters gentlemen—coming going mutually seeing—some spoke deliberation then left—some tied thick then parted—wind sound flowing heard—far and near praised him.

entries.zh: 權妻以策女。
entries.en: Sun Quan married him to Sun Ce's daughter.
entries.literal: Quan married him to Ce's daughter.

entries.zh: 年二十七，起家為豫章太守。
entries.en: At twenty-seven he became Yuzhang prefect.
entries.literal: Age twenty-seven—rose from house as Administrator of Yuzhang.

entries.zh: 下車祀先賢徐孺子之墓。
entries.en: On arrival he sacrificed at Xu Ruzi's grave.
entries.literal: Descending cart sacrificed to former worthy Xu Ruzi's tomb.

entries.zh: 優待其後。
entries.en: He cared for Xu's descendants.
entries.literal: Generously treated his posterity.

entries.zh: 禁其淫祀非禮之祭者。
entries.en: He banned illicit shrines.
entries.literal: Forbidden those excessive sacrifices not ritual sacrifices.

entries.zh: 小吏資質佳者，輒令就學，擇其先進，擢置右職，舉善以教，風化大行。
entries.en: He sent promising clerks to school, promoted the best, and spread decorum.
entries.literal: Petty clerks with fine capacity—always ordered attend study—selected their advanced—promoted placed right offices—raising good to teach—custom transformation greatly practiced.

entries.zh: 初，錢唐丁諝出於役伍，陽羨張秉生於庶民。
entries.en: He lifted Ding Xu from the ranks and Zhang Bing from commoners.
entries.literal: At first Qiantang Ding Xu emerged from labor ranks—Yangxian Zhang Bing born among common people.

entries.zh: 烏程吳粲、雲陽殷禮起乎微賤，邵皆拔而友之，為立聲譽。
entries.en: He befriended Wu Can and Yin Li from humble roots.
entries.literal: Wucheng Wu Can—Yunyang Yin Li rose from slight mean—Shao all pulled and befriended them—establishing fame reputation.

entries.zh: 秉遭大喪，親為制服結絰。
entries.en: When Zhang Bing mourned, Gu Shao wore hemp for him.
entries.literal: Bing encountered great mourning—personally for him made mourning garments tied headbands.

entries.zh: 邵當之豫章，發在近路，值秉疾病，時送者百數。
entries.en: Leaving for Yuzhang near home, Zhang Bing fell ill—hundreds came to see him off.
entries.literal: When Shao went to Yuzhang—departure on near road—happened Bing illness—at time senders hundred count.

entries.zh: 邵辭賓客曰："張仲節有疾，苦不能來別，恨不見之，暫還與訣，諸君少時相待。
entries.en: Gu Shao told guests: "Zhang Bing is too sick to say goodbye—I must see him—wait here briefly."
entries.literal: Shao dismissed guests saying: "Zhang Zhongjie is ill—bitterly cannot come bid farewell—regrets not seeing him—temporarily return to bid farewell—gentlemen wait a short while."

entries.zh: "其留心下士，惟善所在，皆此類也。
entries.en: He fussed over humble clients like this.
entries.literal: His mind attentive to inferiors—only where good lies—all this kind.

entries.zh: 諝至典軍中郎，秉雲陽太守，禮零陵太守，
entries.en: Ding Xu rose to colonel of the household army; Zhang Bing and Yin Li became prefects.
entries.literal: Xu reached Colonel of the Household Who Commands the Army—Bing Administrator of Yunyang—Li Administrator of Lingling—

entries.zh: 〈礼子基作通语曰：礼字德嗣，弱不好弄，潜识过人。
entries.en: 〈Yin Li's son Yin Ji wrote Tongyu: Yin Li, styled Desi, was grave even as a boy.)
entries.literal: 〈Li's son Ji authored Tongyu stating: Li courtesy name Desi—in youth did not play fondly—latent insight surpassed others.

entries.zh: 少为郡吏，年十九，守吴县丞。
entries.en: At nineteen he was assistant magistrate of Wu.
entries.literal: Young became commandery clerk—age nineteen—acting Wu county assistant.

entries.zh: 孙权为王，召除郎中。
entries.en: Sun Quan as king named him gentleman of the palace.
entries.literal: When Sun Quan became king—summoned removed Gentleman of the Palace.

entries.zh: 后与张温俱使蜀，诸葛亮甚称叹之。
entries.en: Later he joined Zhang Wen's mission to Shu and impressed Zhuge Liang.
entries.literal: Later together with Zhang Wen both went as envoy to Shu—Zhuge Liang greatly praised him.

entries.zh: 稍迁至零陵太守，卒官。
entries.en: He rose to Lingling prefect and died in harness.
entries.literal: Gradually promoted reached Lingling prefect—died in office.

entries.zh: 文士传曰：礼子基，无难督，以才学知名，著通语数十篇。
entries.en: (Wenshi zhuan: Yin Ji commanded the Feathered Forest and wrote Tongyu.)
entries.literal: Wenshi zhuan states: Li's son Ji—Colonel Who Has No Difficulty—by talent and learning became known—composed Tongyu several tens of chapters.

entries.zh: 有三子。
entries.en: He had three sons.
entries.literal: Had three sons.

entries.zh: 巨字元大，有才器，初为吴偏将军，统家部曲，城夏口，吴平后，为苍梧太守。
entries.en: Eldest Yin Ju became general and Cangwu prefect after Jin conquered Wu.
entries.literal: Ju courtesy name Yuanda—had talent and capacity—first was Wu partial general—commanding household command—fortified Xiakou—after Wu pacified—became Cangwu prefect.

entries.zh: 少子祐，字庆元，吴郡太守。〉
entries.en: Youngest Yin You was Wu prefect.〉
entries.literal: Youngest son You—courtesy name Qingyuan—Wu commandery prefect.〉

entries.zh: 粲太子少傅。
entries.en: Wu Can rose to junior tutor to the heir.
entries.literal: Can junior tutor to heir apparent.

entries.zh: 世以邵為知人。
entries.en: His generation called Gu Shao a judge of character.
entries.literal: The age considered Shao as knowing men.

entries.zh: 在郡五年，卒官，子譚、承雲。
entries.en: After five years as prefect he died; sons Gu Tan and Gu Cheng survived.
entries.literal: In commandery five years—died in office—sons Tan and Cheng cloud.

entries.zh: 譚字子默，弱冠與諸葛恪等為太子四友，從中庶子轉輔正都尉。
entries.en: Gu Tan, styled Zimo, was one of Sun Deng's four companions and became aide commandant.
entries.literal: Tan courtesy name Zimo—at capping age together with Zhuge Ke and others were heir four friends—from gentleman attendant of heir transferred aide commandant who assists rectitude.

entries.zh: 〈陆机为谭传曰：宣太子正位东宫，天子方隆训导之义，妙简俊彦，讲学左右。
entries.en: 〈Lu Ji's biography of Gu Tan: when Sun Deng took the eastern palace, the court packed his salon with talent.)
entries.literal: 〈Lu Ji for Tan biography states: When Crown Prince came correct to eastern palace—Son of Heaven just then elevated instruction and guidance meaning—subtly selected brilliant talents—studying lecturing left and right.

entries.zh: 时四方之杰毕集，太傅诸葛恪等雄奇盖众，而谭以清识绝伦，独见推重。
entries.en: Zhuge Ke dominated the heir's court, yet Gu Tan's clarity won highest esteem.
entries.literal: At that time four quarters' heroes all gathered—Grand Tutor Zhuge Ke and others heroic strange surpassing host—yet Tan by pure insight unmatched—alone seen pushed weighty.

entries.zh: 自太尉范慎、谢景、羊徽之徒，皆以秀称其名，而悉在谭下。〉
entries.en: Men like Fan Shen lauded Gu Tan above themselves.〉
entries.literal: From Grand Commandant Fan Shen, Xie Jing, Yang Hui's cohort—all by excellence praised their names—yet all ranked below Tan.〉

entries.zh: 赤烏中，代恪為左節度。
entries.en: In Chiwu he succeeded Zhuge Ke as left quartermaster.
entries.literal: In Chiwu replaced Ke as left quartermaster.

entries.zh: 〈吴书曰：谭初践官府，上疏陈事，权辍食称善，以为过於徐详。
entries.en: 〈Wu shu: Sun Quan skipped a meal praising his first memorial.)
entries.literal: 〈Wu shu states: Tan first treading official bureau—submitted memorial stating affairs—Quan stopped eating praising good—thought surpassed Xu Xiang.

entries.zh: 雅性高亮，不脩意气，或以此望之。
entries.en: His lofty cold manner drew resentment.
entries.literal: By nature lofty bright—not cultivating temperament—some therefore blamed him.

entries.zh: 然权鉴其能，见待甚隆，数蒙赏赐，特见召请。〉
entries.en: Sun Quan still favored and enriched him.〉
entries.literal: Yet Quan mirrored his ability—treatment very lofty—repeatedly received rewards—specially summoned invited.〉

entries.zh: 每省簿書，未嘗下籌，徒屈指心計，盡發疑謬，下吏以此服之。
entries.en: He audited ledgers in his head without counting rods and caught every error.
entries.literal: Whenever examining registry documents—never lowered counting rods—only bent fingers mental reckoning—fully issuing doubtful errors—subordinate clerks thereby submitted to him.

entries.zh: 加奉車都尉。
entries.en: He added chief of carriages and cavalry.
entries.literal: Added Chief of Carriages and Cavalry Commandant.

entries.zh: 薛綜為選曹尚書，固讓譚曰：“譚心精體密，貫道達微，才照人物，德允眾望，誠非愚臣所可越先。”
entries.en: Personnel chief Xue Zong ceded the post: Gu Tong exceeds me in every way.
entries.literal: Xue Zong was Selection Bureau Secretary—firmly yielding to Tan saying: "Tan mind refined body meticulous—pierces Way reaches subtle—talent illuminates men of affairs—virtue matches multitude hope—truly not what foolish minister can leap ahead."

entries.zh: 後遂代綜。
entries.en: Gu Tan took personnel.
entries.literal: Thereafter succeeded Zong.

entries.zh: 周昭者字恭遠，與韋曜、薛瑩、華核並述《吳書》，後為中書郎，坐事下獄，核表救之，孫休不聽，遂伏法雲。
entries.en: Zhou Zhao, courtesy name Gongyuan, helped Wei Yao, Xue Ying, and Hua He compile the Wu shu, later served as a palace secretariat officer, was jailed for an offense; Hua He appealed for him but Emperor Xiu of Wu refused, and Zhao was put to death.
entries.literal: Zhou Zhao styled Gongyuan—with Wei Yao, Xue Ying, Hua He together composed Wu shu—later became Palace Secretariat gentleman—sat affair lower prison—He submitted memorial rescue him—Sun Xiu not listened—thereby executed law.

entries.zh: 張昭字子布，彭城人也。
entries.en: Zhang Zhao, styled Zibu, hailed from Pengcheng.
entries.literal: Zhang Zhao, courtesy name Zibu, was a man of Pengcheng.

entries.zh: 少好學，善隸書，從白侯子安受《左氏春秋》，博覽眾書，與琅邪趙昱、東海王朗俱發名友善。
entries.en: As a youth he loved books, wrote a fine clerical hand, studied the Zuo commentary under Bai Hou Zi’an, read omnivorously, and made his name alongside Zhao Yu of Langye and Wang Lang of Donghai.
entries.literal: In youth he loved learning, was skilled at clerical script, received Zuo's Spring and Autumn from Bai Hou Zi'an, read widely among texts, and together with Zhao Yu of Langye and Wang Lang of Donghai rose to fame as friendly associates.

entries.zh: 弱冠察孝廉，不就。
entries.en: Recommended as filially pious and incorrupt at his capping, he refused appointment.
entries.literal: At the capping age he was investigated as filially pious and incorrupt but did not take office.

entries.zh: 與朗共論舊君諱事，州裡才士陳琳等皆稱善之。
entries.en: He argued with Wang Lang over taboos for former rulers; local talents such as Chen Lin praised his performance.
entries.literal: Together with Lang he debated the affair of tabooing former lords; talented men of the commandery such as Chen Lin all praised them.

entries.zh: 〈时汝南主簿应劭议宜为旧君讳，论者皆互有异同，事在《风俗通》。
entries.en: 〈Ying Shao of Runan had argued for tabooing former masters; the dispute is recorded in the Fengsu tong.)
entries.literal: 〈At that time Ying Shao, chief clerk of Runan, argued one ought taboo former lords; debaters differed from one another—the affair is in Fengsu tong.

entries.zh: 昭著论曰：“客有见大国之议，士君子之论，云起元建武已来，旧君名讳五十六人，以为后生不得协也。
entries.en: Zhang Zhao wrote a treatise, saying, “A certain visitor had examined the debates of a great state and the arguments of learned gentlemen. He said that since the Jianwu era at the beginning of the dynasty there had been fifty-six taboo names of former rulers, and that later generations could no longer use names with the same sounds.
entries.literal: Zhang Zhao wrote a treatise, saying, “A guest had seen the deliberations of a great state and the discussions of gentlemen, and said that since the Jianwu era at the beginning of the dynasty, there had been fifty-six taboo names of former rulers, and that later-born people could not use matching sounds.

entries.zh: 取乎经论，譬诸行事，义高辞丽，甚可嘉羡。
entries.en: Drawn from canonical gloss and matched to precedent, the rhetoric glows—yet something troubles me.
entries.literal: Taking from the classics and commentaries, comparing to deeds performed, the righteousness is lofty and phrases lovely—greatly to be admired.

entries.zh: 愚意褊浅，窃有疑焉。
entries.en: Forgive a shallow mind—I cannot quite agree.
entries.literal: My foolish thought is narrow and shallow—I privately harbor doubt.

entries.zh: 盖乾坤剖分，万物定形，肇有父子君臣之经。
entries.en: Once heaven and earth divided and creation took shape, the bonds of parent and child, ruler and subject, appeared.
entries.literal: In general when Heaven and Earth split apart and the myriad things fixed their forms, there began the constant pattern of father and son, lord and minister.

entries.zh: 故圣人顺天之性，制礼尚敬，在三之义，君实食之，在丧之哀，君亲临之，厚莫重焉，恩莫大焉，诚臣子所尊仰，万夫所天恃，焉得而同之哉？
entries.en: The sage fashioned ritual from heaven’s nature: lords feed us under the “three that endure”; they mourn with us—nothing outweighs that debt. How can subjects rank them with ordinary kin?
entries.literal: Therefore the sage complies with heaven's nature, institutes ritual and esteems reverence; in the duty of the three the lord truly nourishes; in mourning's grief the lord personally attends—the thickness cannot be heavier, the grace cannot be greater—truly what ministers and sons revere and myriad men rely on—how can they be equated?

entries.zh: 然亲亲有衰，尊尊有杀，故礼服上不尽高祖，下不尽玄孙。
entries.en: Yet kinship weakens by generation and mourning scales down—hence hemp stops short of the fifth grandfather above and the fifth grandson below.
entries.literal: Yet intimacy toward kin has degrees of decline; reverence toward superiors has steps of reduction—therefore mourning garments upward do not exhaust great-great-grandfather, downward do not exhaust great-great-grandchild.

entries.zh: 又传记四世而缌麻，服之穷也；
entries.en: Genealogies say after four generations one wears only thin hemp.
entries.literal: Moreover transmitted records: four generations and thin hemp—end of garments;

entries.zh: 五世袒免，降杀同姓也；
entries.en: After five generations one merely bares head and wrist—the mourning grade fades even within the clan.
entries.literal: five generations shed turban and fringe—reduced severity toward same surname;

entries.zh: 六世而亲属竭矣。
entries.en: By the sixth generation kinship ends.
entries.literal: six generations and kinship ties are exhausted.

entries.zh: 又曲礼有不逮事之义则不讳，不讳者，盖名之谓，属绝之义，不拘於协，况乃古君五十六哉！
entries.en: The Summary of Etiquette also exempts those who never served a lord from tabooing him—that ends obligation to a mere name. If distant kin need not rhyme away syllables, why taboo scores of dead kings?
entries.literal: Moreover the Summary of Etiquette has the sense that if one did not succeed to service there is no taboo—no taboo refers to personal names; meaning of severed connection is not bound by harmonizing—how much more fifty-six ancient lords!

entries.zh: 邾子会盟，季友来归，不称其名，咸书字者，是时鲁人嘉之也。
entries.en: When the Zhu ruler met allies and Jiyou came home, the classic wrote his style, not his name—Lu admired the tact.
entries.literal: The lord of Zhu at covenant assembly, Jiyou came to return—his name was not called; all were written with style—at that time the people of Lu praised it.

entries.zh: 何解臣子为君父讳乎？
entries.en: So why insist clerks taboo every syllable of old patrons?
entries.literal: How explain ministers and sons tabooing for lord and father?

entries.zh: 周穆王讳满，至定王时有王孙满者，其为大夫，是臣协君也。
entries.en: Zhou King Mu banned “Man,” yet under King Ding a minister Wangsun Man served—a subject bore the sovereign’s taboo.
entries.literal: King Mu of Zhou tabooed Man; when it reached King Ding there was Wangsun Man who was grand officer—that is a minister harmonizing with his lord.

entries.zh: 又厉王讳胡，及庄王之子名胡，其比众多。
entries.en: King Li banned “Hu,” yet Zhuang’s son was Hu—examples abound.
entries.literal: Moreover King Li tabooed Hu; and among King Zhuang's sons one was named Hu—their parallels are numerous.

entries.zh: 夫类事建议，经有明据，传有徵案，然后进攻退守，万无奔北，垂示百世，永无咎失。
entries.en: Advice must rest on canonical proof and commentary precedent—otherwise posterity laughs.
entries.literal: When grouping affairs and proposing counsel, the classics have clear proofs and the commentaries verifiable cases—then advancing attack or retreating defense never flees north in defeat; displaying for a hundred generations, never failing or missing.

entries.zh: 今应劭虽上尊旧君之名，而下无所断齐，犹归之疑云。
entries.en: Ying Shao honors old masters’ names yet sets no clear rule below—it stays muddled.
entries.literal: Now although Ying Shao upward honors former lords' names, downward he decides nothing uniform—still it returns to doubtful clouds.

entries.zh: 曲礼之篇，疑事无质，观省上下，阙义自证，文辞可为，倡而不法，将来何观？
entries.en: The Summary of Etiquette passages he cites prove nothing; pretty words without law teach nothing.
entries.literal: The Summary of Etiquette chapter—doubtful matters lack substance; observing above and below, missing righteousness proves itself—literary phrasing may be composed, advocated but not lawful—what will the future behold?

entries.zh: 言声一放，犹拾瀋也，过辞在前，悔其何追！”〉
entries.en: Once speech is released, it is like scooping up dregs; if excessive words have gone before, how can regret catch up afterward!”〉
entries.literal: Once speech is released, it is like scooping up dregs; if excessive words have gone before, how can regret catch up afterward!”〉

entries.zh: 刺史陶謙舉茂才，不應，謙以為輕己，遂見拘執。
entries.en: Prefect Tao Qian nominated him for office; when Zhang Zhao declined, Tao felt insulted and jailed him.
entries.literal: Inspector Tao Qian nominated him outstanding talent; he did not respond—Qian thought he slighted himself and thereupon had him seized.

entries.zh: 昱傾身營救，方以得免。
entries.en: Zhao Yu spent himself on bail until Zhang Zhao went free.
entries.literal: Yu threw himself into arranging rescue—only then did he obtain release.

entries.zh: 漢末大亂，徐方士民多避難揚土，昭皆南渡江。
entries.en: Late Han turmoil drove Xu refugees south—Zhang Zhao crossed with them.
entries.literal: At the end of Han great chaos arose; gentlemen and commoners of Xu region mostly fled calamity to Yang territory—Zhao all crossed the river south.

entries.zh: 孫策創業，命昭為長史、撫軍中郎將，升堂拜母，如比肩之舊，文武之事，一以委昭。
entries.en: Sun Ce named him chief clerk and general who pacifies the army, treated him like family before Lady Wu, and handed him every civil and military file.
entries.literal: When Sun Ce founded the enterprise he appointed Zhao chief clerk and General of the Household Gentlemen Who Pacifies the Army, ascended the hall to bow to his mother as with old peers shoulder to shoulder—civil and military affairs he wholly entrusted to Zhao.

entries.zh: 〈吴书曰：策得昭甚悦，谓曰：“吾方有事四方，以士人贤者上，吾於子不得轻矣。”
entries.en: 〈The Wu shu: Sun Ce rejoiced: I mean to stride the empire—among scholar-advisers I must honor you.
entries.literal: [Wu shu] states: Ce gained Zhao and was very pleased, saying to him: I am about to have affairs in the four quarters—with scholar worthies above I cannot treat you lightly.

entries.zh: 乃上为校尉，待以师友之礼。〉
entries.en: So he raised him to colonel and courted him as mentor.
entries.literal: Thereupon he promoted him to colonel and treated him with the ritual of teacher and friend.

entries.zh: 昭每得北方士大夫書疏，專歸美於昭，昭欲嘿而不宣則懼有私，宣之則恐非宜，進退不安。
entries.en: Northern letters flattered Zhang Zhao alone; silence seemed sneaky, publication awkward—he squirmed either way.
entries.literal: Whenever Zhao obtained letters from northern gentlemen-officials they exclusively attributed praise to Zhao; Zhao wished to keep silent and not announce yet feared there was partiality; announcing yet feared it was not appropriate—advancing and retreating were uneasy.

entries.zh: 策聞之，歡笑曰："昔管仲相齊，一則仲父，二則仲父，而桓公為霸者宗。
entries.en: Sun Ce laughed: Guan Zhong called Huan Gong Father twice—and Huan became hegemon.
entries.literal: When Ce heard it he laughed happily and said: Formerly Guan Zhong served Qi—first 'Father Zhong,' second 'Father Zhong,' yet Duke Huan became hegemon-in-chief.

entries.zh: 今子布賢，我能用之，其功名獨不在我乎!"，
entries.en: Zibu is worthy; if I use him well, the glory is surely mine!
entries.literal: Now Zibu is worthy—if I can employ him, will the merit and fame alone not rest with me!"

entries.zh: 初，山陰丁覽，太末徐陵，或在縣吏之中，或眾所未識，翻一見之，便與友善，終鹹顯名。
entries.en: Ding Lan of Shanyin and Xu Ling of Taimo—petty clerks or men the world had never heard of—won Yu Fan's friendship at a glance and rose to renown.
entries.literal: At first Ding Lan of Shanyin and Xu Ling of Taimo—some among county clerks, some unknown to the multitude—when Fan saw them once he befriended them, and in the end all became famous.

entries.zh: 〈《会稽典录》曰：◎览字孝连，八岁而孤，家又单微，清身立行，用意不苟，推财从弟，以义让称。
entries.en: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu notes Ding Lan, styled Xiaolian: orphaned at eight from a poor house, he kept scrupulous conduct, gave his inheritance to a cousin, and earned fame for yielding.
entries.literal: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu states: ◎ Lan, courtesy name Xiaolian, at eight sui was orphaned; his family was moreover humble; he purified himself and established conduct, his intentions never careless; he pushed wealth to a younger cousin and was praised for righteous yielding.

entries.zh: 仕郡至功曹，守始平长。
entries.en: He rose to Clerk of Merit and acting magistrate of Shiping.
entries.literal: He served the commandery up to Clerk of Merit and acted as magistrate of Shiping.

entries.zh: 为人精微絜净，门无杂宾。
entries.en: Refined, punctilious, and austere, he admitted no casual callers.
entries.literal: As a man he was refined, subtle, and cleanly austere; no miscellaneous guests crossed his gate.

entries.zh: 孙权深贵待之，未及擢用，会病卒，甚见痛惜，殊其门户。
entries.en: Sun Quan esteemed him highly but died before promoting him; Quan grieved deeply and honored his kin.
entries.literal: Sun Quan deeply prized and favored him; before he could promote him to office he died of illness; Quan greatly mourned and singled out his household for favor.

entries.zh: 览子固，字子贱，本名密，避滕密，改作固。
entries.en: His son Gu, styled Zijian—born Mi—renamed Gu to avoid Teng Mi's name.
entries.literal: Lan's son Gu, courtesy name Zijian, originally named Mi, changed to Gu to avoid Teng Mi.

entries.zh: 固在襁褓中，阚泽见而异之，曰：“此兒后必致公辅。”
entries.en: Kan Ze peered into his cradle and declared, "This boy will reach the highest councils."
entries.literal: While Gu was still in swaddling Kan Ze saw him and marveled, saying: "This child will surely rise to duke or minister."

entries.zh: 固少丧父，独与母居，家贫守约，色养致敬，族弟孤弱，与同寒温。
entries.en: Gu lost his father young and kept his mother in poverty yet filial ease; he sheltered a helpless cousin as his own.
entries.literal: Gu in youth lost his father and lived alone with his mother; the family was poor yet he kept restraint; in supporting her with gentle demeanor he showed utmost respect; a younger male cousin was orphaned and weak, and he shared cold and warmth with him.

entries.zh: 翻与固同僚书曰：“丁子贱塞渊好德，堂构克举，野无遗薪，斯之为懿，其美优矣。
entries.en: Fan wrote a fellow official: "Ding Zijian is depth and virtue embodied; he raises the family hall without leaving kindling in the field—that is true grace.
entries.literal: Fan wrote to a colleague serving with Gu: "Ding Zijian is deep as a spring and loves virtue; the hall's frame is well raised; in the wilds no stray firewood remains—such is his excellence; its beauty is supreme.

entries.zh: 令德之后，惟此君嘉耳。”
entries.en: Among sons of good stock none shines like him."
entries.literal: Among heirs of fine virtue only this gentleman is praiseworthy."

entries.zh: 历显位，孙休时固为左御史大夫，孙皓即位，迁司徒。
entries.en: He climbed to high office—Left Imperial Clerk under Sun Xiu, Minister of Education once Sun Hao ruled.
entries.literal: He rose through eminent posts; under Sun Xiu he became Left Imperial Clerk; when Sun Hao ascended the throne he advanced to Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 皓悖虐，固与陆凯、孟宗同心忧国，年七十六卒。
entries.en: When Hao turned vicious, Gu joined Lu Kai and Meng Zong in loyal anxiety; he died at seventy-six.
entries.literal: Hao was cruel and tyrannical; Gu with Lu Kai and Meng Zong shared one heart worrying for the state; he died at seventy-six sui.

entries.zh: 子弥，字钦远，仕晋，至梁州刺史。
entries.en: His son Mi, styled Qinyuan, served Jin as Inspector of Liangzhou.
entries.literal: His son Mi, courtesy name Qinyuan, served Jin and rose to Inspector of Liangzhou.

entries.zh: 孙潭，光禄大夫。
entries.en: Grandson Tan became Household Grandee.
entries.literal: Grandson Tan, Household Grandee.

entries.zh: ◎徐陵字元大，历三县长，所在著称，迁零陵太守。
entries.en: ◎ Xu Ling, styled Yuanda, distinguished himself over three magistracies and became prefect of Lingling.
entries.literal: ◎ Xu Ling, courtesy name Yuanda, served as magistrate of three counties and was renowned wherever posted; he advanced to Administrator of Lingling.

entries.zh: 时朝廷俟以列卿之位，故翻书曰：“元大受上卿之遇，叔向在晋，未若於今。”
entries.en: The court meant to give him ministerial rank; Fan wrote, "Yuanda gains honors Shuxiang never saw in Jin."
entries.literal: At the time the court awaited him with the seat of a ranked minister; therefore Fan wrote: "Yuanda receives treatment worthy of a senior minister—even Shuxiang in Jin never knew such favor today."

entries.zh: 其见重如此。
entries.en: Such was the regard he commanded.
entries.literal: Thus was he held in such esteem.

entries.zh: 陵卒，僮客土田或见侵夺，骆统为陵家讼之，求与丁览、卜清等为比，权许焉。
entries.en: After Ling died, creditors preyed on his bondservants and fields; Luo Tong sued for his family and won Sun Quan's nod to match Ding Lan's precedent.
entries.literal: When Ling died, retainers and farmland were sometimes seized; Luo Tong pleaded for Ling's household and asked that they be treated like Ding Lan, Bu Qing, and the rest—Quan approved.

entries.zh: 陵子平，字伯先，童龀知名，翻甚爱之，屡称叹焉。
entries.en: His son Ping, styled Boxian, was a prodigy Yu Fan doted on and praised aloud.
entries.literal: Ling's son Ping, courtesy name Boxian, was renowned from childhood; Fan loved him deeply and often praised him.

entries.zh: 诸葛恪为丹杨太守，讨山越，以平威重思虑，可与效力，请平为丞，稍迁武昌左部督，倾心接物，士卒皆为尽力。
entries.en: Zhuge Ke, campaigning in Danyang, valued Ping's weight of character and took him as aide, then raised him to command Wu's left wing—where Ping won every rank and file heart.
entries.literal: Zhuge Ke, as Administrator of Danyang, campaigned against the mountain Yue; deeming Ping grave in bearing and steady in counsel, fit to serve, he requested Ping as assistant magistrate; Ping was gradually promoted to Commander of the Left Wing at Wuchang, treated people with whole heart, and the soldiers all gave their utmost.

entries.zh: 初，平为恪从事，意甚薄，及恪辅政，待平益疏。
entries.en: Ke had once slighted Ping as a mere clerk; as chief minister he kept him at even greater distance.
entries.literal: At first, when Ping served Ke as an aide, Ke thought little of him; once Ke became regent he grew colder toward Ping.

entries.zh: 恪被害，子建亡走，为平部曲所得，平使遣去，别为佗军所获。
entries.en: Ke's son Jian ran into Ping's troops; Ping sent him on, only for another column to take him.
entries.literal: When Ke was assassinated, his son Jian fled and was seized by Ping's retainers; Ping ordered him released, but another unit captured him.

entries.zh: 平两妇归宗，敬奉情过乎厚。
entries.en: He showed two estranged wives a generosity warmer than ritual required.
entries.literal: Ping's two wives returned to their natal clans; he honored them with devotion deeper than ordinary duty.

entries.zh: 其行义敦笃，皆此类也。〉
entries.en: His integrity ran thick and true—every deed of this stamp.〉
entries.literal: His righteous conduct was earnest and steadfast—all of a piece with this.〉

entries.zh: 在南十餘年，年七十卒。
entries.en: He spent a dozen years in the far south and died at seventy.
entries.literal: In the south more than ten years, he died at seventy sui.

entries.zh: 〈《吴书》曰：翻虽在徙弃，心不忘国，常忧五谿宜讨，以辽东海绝，听人使来属，尚不足取，今去人财以求马，既非国利，又恐无获。
entries.en: 〈The Book of Wu says exile never dimmed Fan's patriotism—he pressed for action in Wuxi, dismissed Liaodong fealty across broken seas, and warned that trading treasure for horses helped nobody.
entries.literal: 〈The Book of Wu states: Though Fan lived in banishment his heart never left the state; he constantly urged that the five gorges of Wuxi deserved a campaign. With the Liaodong sea cut off, even hearing envoys come over to submit was hardly worth the trouble; now to squander our wealth buying horses serves neither the realm nor, he feared, would it succeed.

entries.zh: 欲谏不敢，作表以示吕岱，岱不报，为爱憎所白，复徙苍梧猛陵。
entries.en: He drafted advice for Lü Dai, heard nothing back, fell victim to slander, and was shifted deeper into Cangwu.
entries.literal: He wished to remonstrate but dared not; he drafted a memorial and showed it to Lü Dai, who gave no answer; maligned by petty likes and dislikes, Fan was transferred again to Mengling in Cangwu.

entries.zh: 《江表传》曰：后权遣将士至辽东，於海中遭风，多所没失，权悔之，乃令曰：“昔赵简子称诸君之唯唯，不如周舍之谔谔。
entries.en: The Jiangbiao zhuan tells how failed Liaodong fleets moved Quan to cite Zhao Jianzi: "flatterers cannot rival one honest Zhou She.
entries.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Later Quan dispatched officers to Liaodong; they met storms at sea and many were lost; Quan regretted it and issued an order: "Long ago Zhao Jianzi said a chorus of yes-men is no match for Zhou She's blunt speech.

entries.zh: 虞翻亮直，善於尽言，国之周舍也。
entries.en: Yu Fan's blunt candor makes him Wu's Zhou She.
entries.literal: Yu Fan is candid and straight and excels at speaking his whole mind—he is our Zhou She.

entries.zh: 前使翻在此，此役不成。”
entries.en: With Fan at court that folly would never have sailed."
entries.literal: Had Fan been there on that mission, the expedition would not have miscarried."

entries.zh: 促下问交州，翻若尚存者，给其人船，发遣还都；
entries.en: He ordered Jiaozhou questioned at once—if Fan lived, send a ship to bring him home;
entries.literal: Hasten inquiry to Jiaozhou: if Fan still lives, furnish him a boat and escort him to the capital;

entries.zh: 若以亡者，送丧还本郡，使兒子仕宦。
entries.en: if he had died, return the coffin and ennoble his sons.
entries.literal: if he has died, send his coffin to his native commandery and appoint his sons to office.

entries.zh: 会翻已终。〉
entries.en: Fan was already gone.〉
entries.literal: It happened that Fan had already passed away.〉

entries.zh: 翻有十一子。
entries.en: Yu Fan fathered eleven sons.
entries.literal: Fan had eleven sons.

entries.zh: 第四子汜最知名，永安初，從選曹朗為散騎中常侍，後為監軍使者，討扶嚴，病卒，
entries.en: Fourth-born Si stood tallest—promoted from Selection clerk to mounted attendant, then died leading troops against Fuyan.
entries.literal: The fourth son, Si, was most renowned; at the start of Yong'an he went from Gentleman of the Selection Bureau to Regular Mounted Attendant; later he became Military Supervisor Envoy on the campaign against Fuyan and died of illness.

entries.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：汜字世洪，生南海，年十六，父卒，还乡里。
entries.en: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu says Si, styled Shihong, was Nanhai-born and came home at sixteen when his father died.
entries.literal: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu states: Si, courtesy name Shihong, was born in Nanhai; at sixteen sui his father died and he returned to his native place.

entries.zh: 孙綝废幼主，迎立琅邪王休。
entries.en: Sun Lin cast the boy emperor aside for Prince Langye's Sun Xiu.
entries.literal: Sun Lin deposed the young ruler and welcomed Prince Langye Wang Xiu to succeed.

entries.zh: 休未至，綝欲入宫，图为不轨，召百官会议，皆惶怖失色，徒唯唯而已。
entries.en: Lin meant to seize the palace before Xiu arrived; the bureaucrats could only nod, pale.
entries.literal: Before Xiu arrived Lin wished to enter the palace and plot treason; he summoned the hundred officials to council—all were terrified and bloodless, uttering only yes-yes.

entries.zh: 汜对曰：“明公为国伊周，处将相之位，擅废立之威，将上安宗庙，下惠百姓，大小踊跃，自以伊霍复见。
entries.en: "Si told Lin he played Yi Yin to the realm—why panic the court by rushing the harem?
entries.literal: Si answered: "You, enlightened lord, stand as Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou for the state; you hold general and minister rank and wield power to depose and enthrone—you will pacify the ancestral shrines above and bless the hundred surnames below; great and small leap with joy, each imagining Yi Yin and Huo Guang reborn.

entries.zh: 今迎王未至，而欲入宫，如是，群下摇荡，众听疑惑，非所以永终忠孝，扬名后世也。”
entries.en: Entering the palace early would shake faith and stain his fame."
entries.literal: Now the king you welcome has not arrived yet you wish to enter the palace—in this way subordinates waver and the multitude listens in doubt—it is no way to secure loyalty and filial piety forever or lift your name for later ages."

entries.zh: 綝不怿，竟立休。
entries.en: Lin sulked yet crowned Xiu.
entries.literal: Lin was displeased but in the end enthroned Xiu.

entries.zh: 休初即位，汜与贺邵、王蕃、薛莹俱为散骑中常侍。
entries.en: Xiu kept Si, He Shao, Wang Fan, and Xue Ying as close attendants.
entries.literal: When Xiu first ascended, Si served with He Shao, Wang Fan, and Xue Ying as Regular Mounted Attendants.

entries.zh: 以讨扶严功拜交州刺史、冠军将军、餘姚侯，寻卒。〉
entries.en: Fuyan won him Jiaozhou, the Champion baton, and Yuyan marquisate—then death.〉
entries.literal: For merit in the Fuyan campaign he was appointed Inspector of Jiaozhou, Champion General, and Marquis of Yuyao; soon afterward he died.〉

entries.zh: 汜弟忠，宜都太守。
entries.en: Younger brother Zhong governed Yidu.
entries.literal: Si's younger brother Zhong was Administrator of Yidu.

entries.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：忠字世方，翻第五子。
entries.en: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu gives Zhong as Fan's fifth son, styled Shifang.
entries.literal: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu states: Zhong, courtesy name Shifang, was Fan's fifth son.

entries.zh: 贞固幹事，好识人物，造吴郡陆机於童龀之年，称上虞魏迁於无名之初，终皆远致，为著闻之士。
entries.en: Zhong spotted Lu Ji as a boy and Wei Qian before fame—both climbed high.
entries.literal: Chaste, firm, capable in affairs, skilled at recognizing men—he sought out Lu Ji of Wu commandery while still in childhood and praised Wei Qian of Shangyu before he had a name; both in the end rose far and became scholars of recorded fame.

entries.zh: 交同县王岐於孤宦之族，仕进先至宜都太守，忠乃代之。
entries.en: He bonded with clerk-born Wang Qi—Qi held Yidu first, Zhong followed.
entries.literal: He befriended Wang Qi of the same county from a clan of orphaned clerks; Wang advanced first to Administrator of Yidu, and Zhong succeeded him.

entries.zh: 晋征吴，忠与夷道监陆晏、晏弟中夏督景坚守不下，城溃被害。
entries.en: Yu Zhong died defending Yidao beside Lu Yan and Lu Jing when Jin breached the walls.
entries.literal: When Jin campaigned against Wu, Zhong with Yidao intendant Lu Yan and Yan's younger brother Central Summer Commander Lu Jing held firm and would not yield; when the city broke they were killed.

entries.zh: 忠子谭，字思奥。
entries.en: His son Tan styled Si'ao.
entries.literal: Zhong's son Tan, courtesy name Si'ao.

entries.zh: 《晋阳秋》称谭清贞有检操，外如退弱，内坚正有胆幹。
entries.en: The Jinyang qiu calls Tan reserved yet steel inside—soft-spoken but unbending.
entries.literal: The Jinyang qiu praises Tan as chaste and restrained with disciplined integrity—outwardly seeming yielding and weak, inwardly firm, upright, and bold in capacity.

entries.zh: 仕晋，历位内外，终於卫将军，追赠侍中左光禄大夫，开府仪同三司。〉
entries.en: Under Jin he reached Defender-in-Chief and won posthumous ministerial glory.〉
entries.literal: He served Jin, rose through inner and outer posts, ending as Defender-in-Chief—posthumously honored Palace Attendant, Left Household Grandee with Office Equal to the Three Dukes.〉

entries.zh: 聳，越騎校尉。
entries.en: Yu Song served as Colonel of Agile Cavalry.
entries.literal: Song was Colonel of Agile Cavalry.

entries.zh: 累遷廷尉，湘東、河間太守；
entries.en: He rose to Commandant of Justice and prefect of Xiangdong and Hejian;
entries.literal: He was promoted in stages to Commandant of Justice, Administrator of Xiangdong and Hejian;

entries.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：耸字世龙，翻第六子也。
entries.en: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu names Song as Fan's sixth son, styled Shilong.
entries.literal: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu states: Song, courtesy name Shilong, was Fan's sixth son.

entries.zh: 清虚无欲，进退以礼，在吴历清官，入晋，除河间相，王素闻耸名，厚敬礼之。
entries.en: Ascetic and punctilious in Wu, he became Hejian chancellor under Jin; Prince Su honored his reputation.
entries.literal: Clear, empty of desire, advancing and retreating by ritual—in Wu he passed through pure offices; entering Jin he was appointed Chancellor of Hejian; Prince Su long hearing Song's name treated him with thick courtesy and respect.

entries.zh: 耸抽引人物，务在幽隐孤陋之中。
entries.en: He insisted on lifting talent from hedgerows and hovels.
entries.literal: Song drew forth men of affairs, striving for those hidden in obscurity, orphaned and lowly.

entries.zh: 时王岐难耸，以高士所达，必合秀异，耸书与族子察曰：“世之取士，曾不招未齿於丘园，索良才於总猥，所誉依已成，所毁依已败，此吾所以叹息也。”
entries.en: "Wang Qi argued great names imply genius; Song answered his kinsman Cha that patronage chases winners and shuns unknowns—a vice worth mourning."
entries.literal: At the time Wang Qi challenged Song: men of lofty repute reach only the outstandingly gifted; Song wrote his clansman Cha: "This age's recruitment never summons the toothless recluse from grove and garden nor seeks fine talent from the crude crowd; praise follows what is already made, slander tracks what is already ruined—that is why I sigh."

entries.zh: 耸疾俗丧祭无度，弟昺卒，祭以少牢，酒饭而已，当时族党并遵行之。〉
entries.en: He trimmed funeral feasts to wine and grain when Bing died, and kin copied him.〉
entries.literal: Song loathed vulgar excess in mourning sacrifices; when younger brother Bing died he offered only the lesser beast sacrifice—wine and rice—and kinsmen alike followed the rule.〉

entries.zh: 昺，廷尉尚書，濟陰太守。
entries.en: Bing rose to ministerial rank and governed Jiyin.
entries.literal: Bing was Minister of Justice and Minister over the Masses, Administrator of Jiyin.

entries.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：昺字世文，翻第八子也。
entries.en: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu records Bing, Fan's eighth son, styled Shiwen.
entries.literal: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu states: Bing, courtesy name Shiwen, was Fan's eighth son.

entries.zh: 少有倜傥之志，仕吴黄门郎，以捷对见异，超拜尚书侍中。
entries.en: Wu valued his wit at the Yellow Gates and jumped him to palace minister.
entries.literal: In youth he cherished a free hero's ambition; serving Wu as Gentleman at the Yellow Gates he was singled out for quick repartee and vaulted to Palace Attendant Minister.

entries.zh: 晋军来伐，遣昺持节都督武昌已上诸军事，昺先上还节盖印绶，然后归顺。
entries.en: Facing invasion Bing surrendered credentials above Wuchang before yielding.
entries.literal: When Jin's army came to strike he dispatched Bing with tally as Area Commander-in-Chief for all military affairs from Wuchang upward; Bing first returned tally, canopy, seals and ribbons, then submitted.

entries.zh: 在济阴，抑强扶弱，甚著威风。〉
entries.en: At Jiyin he humbled bullies and shielded commoners—justice visible on the street.〉
entries.literal: In Jiyin he checked the mighty and aided the weak—his martial awe stood renowned.〉

entries.zh: 陸績字公紀，吳郡吳人也。
entries.en: Lu Ji, styled Gongji, hailed from Wu commandery.
entries.literal: Lu Ji, courtesy name Gongji, was a man of Wu in Wu commandery.

entries.zh: 父康，漢末為廬江太守。
entries.en: His father Kang governed Lujiang in Han's twilight.
entries.literal: His father Kang was Administrator of Lujiang at the end of Han.

entries.zh: 〈谢承后汉书曰：康字季宁，少惇孝悌，勤脩操行，太守李肃察孝廉。
entries.en: 〈Xie Cheng's Hou Hanshu says Kang, styled Jining, earned a Flourishing Talent nomination for filial conduct.
entries.literal: 〈Xie Cheng's Later Han History states: Kang, courtesy name Jining, in youth was steeped in filial piety and fraternal duty, diligently cultivated conduct; Administrator Li Su nominated him Flourishing Talent.

entries.zh: 肃后坐事伏法，康敛尸送丧还颍川，行服，礼终，举茂才，历三郡太守，所在称治，后拜庐江太守。〉
entries.en: When Li Su fell to the law Kang bore his body home, mourned fully, then rose through three prefectures to Lujiang.〉
entries.literal: Later Su was executed for an affair; Kang gathered the corpse and escorted the funeral to Yingchuan, observed mourning, finished the rites, was nominated Flourishing Talent, served as Administrator of three commanderies—each place praised his governance—and finally was appointed Administrator of Lujiang.〉

entries.zh: 績年六歲，於九江見袁術。
entries.en: Ji met Yuan Shu in Jiujiang at age six.
entries.literal: At six sui Ji met Yuan Shu on the Jiujiang road.

entries.zh: 術出橘，績懷三枚，去，拜辭墮地，術謂曰：“陸郎作賓客而懷橘乎？”
entries.en: "Shu offered oranges; six-year-old Ji hid three in his sleeve until they spilled at leave-taking—Shu teased him about stealing fruit."
entries.literal: Shu produced oranges; Ji tucked three in his robe; leaving, he bowed in farewell and they fell to the ground; Shu said: "Young Lu, you pocket oranges while a guest?"

entries.zh: 績跪答曰："欲歸遺母。
entries.en: Ji knelt and said he meant them for his mother.
entries.literal: Ji knelt and answered: "I wished to take them home for my mother."

entries.zh: "術大奇之。
entries.en: Shu stared in delight.
entries.literal: Shu greatly marveled at him.

entries.zh: 孫策在吳，張昭、張紘、秦松為上賓，共論四海未泰，須當用武治而平之，績年少末坐，遙大聲言曰："昔管夷吾相齊桓公，九合諸候，一匡天下，不用兵車。
entries.en: At Ce's council on conquering the realm, boy Ji barked from the lowest seat that Guan Zhong unified Qi without war.
entries.literal: When Sun Ce held Wu, Zhang Zhao, Zhang Hong, and Qin Song were chief guests; jointly debating that the four seas were not yet tranquil and arms must rule them, Ji—youngest, seated last—called loudly across the room: "Long ago Guan Zhong ministered Duke Huan of Qi—nine leagues of lords, one restoration under Heaven—without chariot warfare.

entries.zh: 孔子曰：'遠人不服，則修文德以來之。
entries.en: He quoted Confucius—win strangers with culture, not steel.
entries.literal: Confucius said: 'When distant folk do not submit, cultivate civil virtue to draw them.'

entries.zh: '今論者不務道德懷取之術，而惟尚武，績雖童蒙，竊所未安也。
entries.en: He pleaded his youth yet insisted glorifying arms unsettled him.
entries.literal: ' Those who debate today do not labor at virtue and winning hearts but honor force alone—though Ji is a child, privately he cannot rest easy."

entries.zh: "昭等異焉。
entries.en: The elders listened slack-jawed.
entries.literal: Zhao and the others wondered at him.

entries.zh: 績容貌雄壯，博學多識，星歷算數無不該覽。
entries.en: Strapping and encyclopedic, he mastered stars, calendars, and mathematics.
entries.literal: Ji's bearing was heroic and robust; broadly learned and widely informed—astronomy, calendars, reckoning—nothing he failed to survey.

entries.zh: 虞翻舊齒名盛，龐統荊州令士，年亦差長，皆與績友善。
entries.en: Yu Fan and Pang Tong, his elders in fame, counted Ji friend.
entries.literal: Yu Fan by seniority bore famous weight; Pang Tong was Wu's celebrated scholar of Jingzhou; both were somewhat older—all befriended Ji.

entries.zh: 孫權統事，闢為奏曹掾，以直道見憚，出為鬱林太守，加偏將軍，給兵二千人。
entries.en: Quan named him memorial clerk until blunt honesty exiled him to Yulin with rank and two thousand soldiers.
entries.literal: When Sun Quan took charge he summoned Ji as Clerk of Memorial Pillar—straight speaking made men wary—so he went out as Administrator of Yulin with concurrent Lieutenant General and an allotment of two thousand troops.

entries.zh: 績既有躄疾，又意在儒雅，非其志也。
entries.en: Lame and bookish, generalship never suited him.
entries.literal: Ji already suffered lameness and his heart lay with scholar refinement—not his aspiration.

entries.zh: 雖有軍事，著述不廢，作《渾天圖》，注《易》釋《玄》，皆傳於世。
entries.en: Camp life never stopped his brush—his cosmograph and Change commentary survive.
entries.literal: Though military duties pressed he never ceased writing—he composed the Chart of the Encompassing Heavens, annotated the Changes and expounded the Mystery—all handed down.

entries.zh: 豫自知亡日，乃為辭曰："有漢志士吳郡陸績，幼敦《詩》、《書》，長玩《禮》、《易》受命南征，遘疾遇厄，遭命不幸，嗚呼悲隔！
entries.en: Knowing the hour of death he drafted his lament—a scholar's epitaph for a Han heart broken on the Ling frontier.
entries.literal: Yu foreknew his death-day and composed a elegy: "There was a Han loyalist, Lu Ji of Wu commandery—child steeped in Odes and Documents, grown adept at Rites and Changes—received mandate on southern campaign, met illness and hardship, Heaven's lot unkind—alas, sorrow sunders!"

entries.zh: "又曰："從今已去，六十年之外，車同軌，書同文，恨不及見也。
entries.en: He prophesied reunification within sixty years he would not live to witness.
entries.literal: He added: "From now beyond sixty years carts will share gauge and script share form—I regret I shall not see it."

entries.zh: "年三十二卒。
entries.en: He died at thirty-two.
entries.literal: He died at thirty-two sui.

entries.zh: 長子宏，會稽南部都尉，次子睿，長水校尉。
entries.en: Hong commanded southern Kuaiji; Rui led the Long River corps.
entries.literal: Eldest son Hong, Commandant of South Kuaiji; second son Rui, Colonel of Long Rivers.

entries.zh: 绩於鬱林所生女，名曰鬱生，適张温弟白。
entries.en: His Yulin daughter Yusheng wed Zhang Bai, Zhang Wen's brother.
entries.literal: The daughter Ji fathered at Yulin was named Yusheng; she married Zhang Wen's younger brother Bai.

entries.zh: 姚信集有表称之曰：“臣闻唐、虞之政，举善而教，旌德擢异，三王所先，是以忠臣烈士，显名国朝，淑妇贞女，表迹家闾。
entries.en: "Yao Xin petitioned that Tang-Yu governance honored worthy women as much as loyal men.
entries.literal: Yao Xin's collected works preserve a memorial praising her: "Your servant has heard that Tang and Yu's government raised the good and instructed them, hoisted virtue and lifted the unusual—the Three Kings placed this first—therefore loyal ministers and steadfast martyrs shine in court annals, virtuous wives and chaste women leave traces in hamlet gates.

entries.zh: 盖所以阐崇化业，广殖清风，使苟有令性，幽明俱著，苟怀懿姿，士女同荣。
entries.en: Such praise steadies custom for men and women alike.
entries.literal: That widens transformative enterprise and plants pure wind abroad so whoever carries fine nature shows it in light or shade; whoever harbors excellence shares glory between gentlemen and ladies.

entries.zh: 故王蠋建寒松之节而齐王表其里，义姑立殊绝之操而鲁侯高其门。
entries.en: Classic exemplars—Wang Zhuo's lane, the Lu aunt's gate—prove the point.
entries.literal: Hence Wang Zhuo set frost-pine integrity and the Qi king inscribed his lane; the righteous aunt forged unmatched resolve and the Lu marquis raised her gate.

entries.zh: 臣切见故郁林太守陆绩女子郁生，少履贞特之行，幼立匪石之节，年始十三，適同郡张白。
entries.en: The memorial names Yusheng, Lu Ji's girl—betrothed at thirteen to Zhang Bai.
entries.literal: Your servant has personally seen Yusheng, daughter of late Administrator Lu Ji of Yulin—she walked chaste singularity in youth, erected unyielding resolve like undriftable stone; at thirteen sui she married Bai of the same commandery.

entries.zh: 侍庙三月，妇礼未卒，白遭罹家祸，迁死异郡。
entries.en: Three months into marriage Bai died afar in family disaster.
entries.literal: Three months attending the ancestral shrine—wife's rites unfinished—Bai suffered household calamity and died removed to another commandery.

entries.zh: 郁生抗声昭节，义形於色，冠盖交横，誓而不许，奉白姊妹嶮巇之中，蹈履水火，志怀霜雪，义心固於金石，体信贯於神明，送终以礼，邦士慕则。
entries.en: She refused every suitor, nursed Bai's sisters through ruin, and buried him—Wu's matrons took note.
entries.literal: Yusheng raised voice declaring her vow; righteousness shaped her face; coaches crossed pleading remarriage yet she swore refusal; she upheld Bai's sisters through peril, treading flood and fire—mind frost-bright, faith harder than metal or stone, spirit-trust piercing gods—she buried him by ritual so commandery gentlemen took her model.

entries.zh: 臣闻昭德以行，显行以爵，苟非名爵，则劝善不严，故士之有诔，鲁人志其勇，杞妇见书，齐人哀其哭。
entries.en: The memorial cites Lu dirges and Qi's weeping widow—honor needs a title.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard virtue is proclaimed through conduct and conduct displayed through rank—without title or rank encouragement lacks sternness—therefore gentlemen receive dirges: Lu chronicled courage; the Ji wife entered texts and Qi mourned her cry.

entries.zh: 乞蒙圣朝，斟酌前训，上开天聪，下垂坤厚，褒郁生以义姑之号，以厉两髦之节，则皇风穆暢，士女改视矣。”
entries.en: Yao begged the throne to name Yusheng Righteous Aunt and shame faint hearts."
entries.literal: Pray the sacred court weigh ancient precedent—open Heaven's hearing, extend Earth's generosity—award Yusheng the style Righteous Aunt to stiffen young widows' resolve—then royal wind flows serene and gentlemen and ladies revise their gaze."

entries.zh: 赤烏九年，遷驃騎將軍。
entries.en: Chiwu 9 made him agile cavalry general.
entries.literal: Chiwu ninth year—promoted General of Agile Cavalry.

entries.zh: 遭二宮構爭，據擁護太子，言則懇至，義形於色，守之以死，
entries.en: He defended the crown prince unto death—
entries.literal: Met two-palace structure struggle—Ju embraced protected heir apparent—speech then earnest utmost—righteousness shaped face—guarded with death—

entries.zh: 〈殷基《通语》载据争曰：“臣闻太子国之本根，雅性仁孝，天下归心，今卒责之，将有一朝之虑。
entries.en: "〈Tongyu cites Ju’s warning—the heir is the root.
entries.literal: 〈Yin Ji Tongyu records Ju disputed: "Your servant hears heir apparent state root trunk—refined nature benevolent filial—all under Heaven return heart—now suddenly blame him—will have morning's worry.

entries.zh: 昔晋献用骊姬而申生不存，汉武信江充而戾太子冤死。
entries.en: Li Ji and Jiang Chong lessons.
entries.literal: Formerly Jin Xian used Li Ji then Shensheng not preserved—Han Wu trusted Jiang Chong then Crown Prince Li unjust died.

entries.zh: 臣窃惧太子不堪其忧，虽立思子之宫，无所复及矣。”〉
entries.en: Even a repentant hall cannot recall dead heir."〉
entries.literal: Your servant privately fears heir cannot bear that worry—though erect Son-Remembering palace—nothing again reaches."〉

entries.zh: 遂左遷新都郡丞。
entries.en: Quan banished him Xindu assistant.
entries.literal: Thereupon demoted left Administrator Assistant Xindu commandery.

entries.zh: 未到，中書令孫弘譖潤據，因權寢疾，弘為詔書追賜死，時年五十七。
entries.en: Sun Hong whispered poison into a dying Quan's ear and forged an order—Ju never reached his post; they forced him to die at fifty-seven.
entries.literal: Before he arrived, Palace Secretariat Director Sun Hong slandered Zhu Ju with soaking malice; because Quan lay gravely ill, Hong forged an edict commanding him to commit suicide—he was fifty-seven sui.

entries.zh: 孫亮時，二子熊、損各復領兵，為全公主所謂，皆死。
entries.en: Sun Liang restored both sons to commands; Princess Quan framed them and both perished.
entries.literal: Under Sun Liang his two sons Xiong and Sun each again commanded troops—slandered by the Princess of Quan—both died.

entries.zh: 永安中，迫錄前功，以熊子宣襲爵雲陽侯，尚公主。
entries.en: Yong'an auditors remembered old service—Xuan took the Yunyang title and a princess bride.
entries.literal: During Yong'an they posthumously tallied former merit—Xiong's son Xuan inherited the Marquisate of Yunyang and married a princess.

entries.zh: 孫皓時，宣至驃騎將軍。
entries.en: Under Hao he climbed to agile cavalry command.
entries.literal: Under Sun Hao Xuan rose to General of Agile Cavalry.

entries.zh: 評曰：虞翻古之狂直，因難免乎末世，然權不能容，非曠宇也。
entries.en: Chen Shou calls Fan a classical blunt loyalist ill-suited to a fallen age—yet Quan's inability to shelter him betrays a petty court.
entries.literal: The appraisal states: Yu Fan was blunt straightness in the ancient mold—thereby hard to escape harm in a degenerate age—yet that Quan could not tolerate him shows no spacious breadth.

entries.zh: 陸績之於揚《玄》，是仲尼之左丘明，老聘之嚴周矣；
entries.en: Lu Ji stood to Yang Xiong's Taixuan as Confucius to Zuo Qiu or Laozi to Zhuang Zhou—a peer interpreter.
entries.literal: Lu Ji toward Yang Xiong's Mystery parallels Confucius having Zuo Qiuming and Laozi having Zhuang Zhou.

entries.zh: 以瑚璉之器，而作守南越，不亦賊夫人歟！
entries.en: Temple-grade talent parked on a Ling frontier—what misuse of a man!
entries.literal: With talents fit for ritual vessels—yet made guardian of southern Yue—is it not wasting the man!

entries.zh: 張溫才藻俊茂，而智防未備，用致艱患。
entries.en: Zhang Wen blazed with letters but lacked political guardrails—and paid for it.
entries.literal: Zhang Wen's literary brilliance flourished lush—yet wisdom's defenses were not prepared—thereby inviting bitter calamity.

entries.zh: 駱統抗明大義，辭切理至，值權方閉不開。
entries.en: Luo Tong framed the grand moral case with knife-edge clarity—against Quan's deaf door.
entries.literal: Luo Tong upheld and clarified great righteousness—speech cutting, principle utmost—yet met Quan sealed shut and unopening.

entries.zh: 陸瑁篤義規諫，君子有稱焉。
entries.en: Lu Mao's loyal counsel earned gentlemen's praise.
entries.literal: Lu Mao was steadfast in righteousness and remonstrance—gentlemen have praised him for it.

entries.zh: 吾粲、朱據遭罹屯蹇，以正喪身，悲夫！
entries.en: Wu Can and Zhu Ju died for doing right—grief on grief.
entries.literal: Wu Can and Zhu Ju encountered hardship and obstruction—through upright principle lost their lives—alas!

entries.zh: 虞翻字仲翔，會稽餘姚人也。
entries.en: Yu Fan, styled Zhongxiang, came from Yuyao in Kuaiji.
entries.literal: Yu Fan, courtesy name Zhongxiang, was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji commandery.

entries.zh: 〈吴书曰：翻少好学，有高气。
entries.en: 〈The Book of Wu records that as a young man Yu Fan loved scholarship and carried himself with uncommon elevation.
entries.literal: 〈The Book of Wu states: In youth Fan loved learning and bore himself with lofty pride.

entries.zh: 年十二，客有候其兄者，不过翻，翻追与书曰：“仆闻虎魄不取腐芥，磁石不受曲针，过而不存，不亦宜乎！”
entries.en: When he was twelve, a visitor called on his brother but snubbed Yu Fan; Fan sent a letter after him: "They say amber ignores rotten mustard and a lodestone spurns a crooked needle—a slight delivered and unnoticed sits ill with neither party."
entries.literal: At age twelve a guest came to call on his elder brother but passed by without stopping for Fan; Fan pursued him with a letter saying: "I have heard that amber does not pick up rotten mustard and the lodestone does not take a bent needle; to pass by and pay no heed—is that not fitting!"

entries.zh: 客得书奇之，由是见称。〉
entries.en: The guest read the note with admiration, and Fan's reputation began from that hour.〉
entries.literal: When the guest received the letter he marveled at it, and from this Fan was praised.〉

entries.zh: 太守王朗命為功曹。
entries.en: The Administrator Wang Lang named him Clerk of Merit.
entries.literal: Administrator Wang Lang appointed him Clerk of Merit.

entries.zh: 孫策征會稽，翻時遭父喪，衰絰詣府門，朗欲就之，翻乃脫衰入見，勸朗避策。
entries.en: While Sun Ce was marching on Kuaiji, Yu Fan was in mourning for his father; he appeared at the yamen gate in sackcloth. Wang Lang meant to comfort him, but Fan stripped the mourning garb, went inside, and urged Lang to withdraw rather than face Ce.
entries.literal: Sun Ce campaigned against Kuaiji; Fan was then mourning his father and came to the administrator's gate in mourning dress with hemp cord. Lang wished to approach him, but Fan removed his mourning garments and entered to see him, urging Lang to avoid Ce.

entries.zh: 朗不能用。
entries.en: Lang would not follow his counsel.
entries.literal: Lang could not employ him.

entries.zh: 拒戰敗績，亡走浮海。
entries.en: He fought and was routed, then fled by ship onto the open sea.
entries.literal: He resisted in battle and suffered defeat, then fled and went out to sea.

entries.zh: 翻追隨營護，到東部候官，候官長閉城不受，翻往說之，然後見納。
entries.en: Fan stayed with the column as escort until they reached Houguan in the eastern circuit; the county magistrate barred the gates until Fan talked him round and won them entry.
entries.literal: Fan followed to guard the camp; they reached Houguan in the eastern division. The chief of Houguan closed the city and would not receive them; Fan went and persuaded him, and only then were they admitted.

entries.zh: 〈吴书曰：翻始欲送朗到广陵，朗惑王方平记，言“疾来邀我，南岳相求”，故遂南行。
entries.en: 〈The Book of Wu adds that Fan first meant to see Wang Lang safely to Guangling, "but Lang trusted an inscription attributed to Wang Fangping—Hasten and summon me; the Southern Peak calls—and turned his course southward instead."
entries.literal: 〈The Book of Wu states: Fan had first wished to escort Lang to Guangling; Lang was misled by Wang Fangping's inscription, which said Come swiftly and invite me; the Southern Marchmount seeks me, "and therefore went south."

entries.zh: 既至候官，又欲投交州，翻谏朗曰：“此妄书耳，交州无南岳，安所投乎？”
entries.en: At Houguan he planned to bolt for Jiaozhou; Fan warned him: "That text is nonsense—there is no Southern Marchmount in Jiaozhou; what harbor could such a sign point to?"
entries.literal: After reaching Houguan he wished again to flee to Jiaozhou. Fan remonstrated with Lang: "This is a false inscription; Jiaozhou has no Southern Marchmount—where would you go?"

entries.zh: 乃止。〉
entries.en: Lang gave up the idea.
entries.literal: Thereupon he stopped.

entries.zh: 朗謂翻曰："卿有老母，可以還矣。"
entries.en: Lang told him: "You have an old mother at home—you should go back."
entries.literal: Lang said to Fan: "You have an aged mother; you may return."

entries.zh: 〈翻别传曰：朗使翻见豫章太守华歆，图起义兵。
entries.en: 〈Yu Fan's separate biography says Wang Lang dispatched him to Yuzhang's Hua Xin to plan raising loyal troops.
entries.literal: 〈The Separate Biography of Fan states: Lang sent Fan to see Administrator Hua Xin of Yuzhang, plotting to raise troops in righteous revolt.

entries.zh: 翻未至豫章，闻孙策向会稽，翻乃还。
entries.en: Before he reached Yuzhang he learned Sun Ce was bearing down on Kuaiji and wheeled about.
entries.literal: Before Fan reached Yuzhang he heard that Sun Ce was heading for Kuaiji, and Fan then returned.

entries.zh: 会遭父丧，以臣使有节，不敢过家，星行追朗至候官。
entries.en: His father had just died, yet as an accredited envoy he would not detour home; he marched nights until he caught Wang Lang at Houguan.
entries.literal: It happened that he was in mourning for his father; as an envoy under orders he dared not pass his home, but traveled by night and overtook Lang at Houguan.

entries.zh: 朗遣翻还，然后奔丧。
entries.en: Lang released him to return, and only then could Fan observe the funeral rites.
entries.literal: Lang sent Fan back, and only then did Fan go to mourn.

entries.zh: 而传云孙策之来，翻衰绖诣府门，劝朗避策，则为大异。〉
entries.en: The main narrative, however, claims that when Ce approached, Fan appeared at the yamen in mourning bands urging Lang to yield—quite another story.〉
entries.literal: Yet the biography says that when Ce came, Fan in mourning dress went to the gate and urged Lang to avoid Ce—this is a great discrepancy.〉

entries.zh: 翻既歸，策覆命為功曹，待以交友之禮。
entries.en: Once Fan was back, Sun Ce restored him as Clerk of Merit and courted him as an equal.
entries.literal: After Fan returned, Ce again appointed him Clerk of Merit and treated him with the courtesy due a friend.

entries.zh: 身詣翻第。
entries.en: He called at Fan's house himself.
entries.literal: He went in person to Fan's residence.

entries.zh: 〈江表传曰：策书谓翻曰：“今日之事，当与卿共之，勿谓孙策作郡吏相待也。”〉
entries.en: 〈The Jiangbiao zhuan records Ce's letter: "What we face now we shoulder together—do not imagine I would handle you like any county clerk."〉
entries.literal: 〈The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Ce wrote to Fan: "Today's affair I must share with you; do not think Sun Ce means to treat you as a mere clerk of the commandery."〉

entries.zh: 權遷都建業，徵上大將軍陸遜輔登鎮武昌，領宮府留事。
entries.en: When Sun Quan relocated the court to Jianye, he recalled Lu Xun from the field to help Sun Deng hold Wuchang and oversee all residual business of the heir's establishment.
entries.literal: Sun Quan moved the capital to Jianye, summoned Grand Senior General Lu Xun to assist Deng in garrisoning Wuchang, and charged him with the remaining affairs of the palace establishment.

entries.zh: 登或射獵，當由徑道，常遠避良田，不踐苗稼，至所頓息，又擇空閑之地，其不欲煩民如此。
entries.en: On the hunt he kept to byways and gave wide berth to fertile plots so as never to trample crops; when he camped he picked unused ground—such was his care not to burden commoners.
entries.literal: When Deng at times hunted, if he had to take a path he constantly kept far from good fields, not treading on seedlings and crops; when he came to a place to halt and rest, he again chose empty idle ground; his not wishing to trouble the people was like this.

entries.zh: 嘗乘馬出，有彈丸過，左右求之。
entries.en: Once, riding out, a sling pellet whistled past; his escorts set out to find who had fired it.
entries.literal: Once when riding out on horseback, a pellet passed by; his attendants searched for the shooter.

entries.zh: 有一人操彈佩丸，咸以爲是，辭對不服，從者欲捶之，登不聽，使求過丸，比之非類，乃見釋。
entries.en: They seized a man carrying a sling and pellets and assumed he was guilty; he protested his innocence until the escort wanted to thrash him. Sun Deng forbade it, had the actual pellet recovered, and showed it did not match the man's shot—so he was freed.
entries.literal: There was one man who held a pellet-launcher and wore pellets; all thought it was he; he pleaded and answered that he would not submit; the followers wished to beat him; Deng would not listen; he had them seek the passing pellet; comparing it, it was not of the same kind, and only then was the man released.

entries.zh: 又失盛水金馬盂，覺得其主，左右所爲，不忍致罰，呼責數之，長遣歸家，勑親近勿言。
entries.en: When a gilt horse-head basin went missing, he traced it to his own attendants. He could not bring himself to punish them: he scolded them at length, sent them home on extended leave, and told his intimates to keep silent about the affair.
entries.literal: Again he lost a gold horse-head water basin; he perceived who the owner was—it was done by those at his side; he could not bear to impose punishment; he called and rebuked them at length, sent them home for a long period, and ordered those close to him not to speak of it.

entries.zh: 後弟慮卒，權爲之降損，登晝夜兼行，到賴鄉，自聞，即時召見。
entries.en: After his brother Sun Lü died, Sun Quan curtailed court observances in grief. Sun Deng rode night and day to Laixiang, presented himself unbidden, and was admitted at once.
entries.literal: Later when his younger brother Lu died, Sun Quan for his sake lowered and diminished rites; Deng traveled day and night together, arrived at Laixiang, reported himself on hearing the news, and was immediately summoned and received.

entries.zh: 見權悲泣，因諫曰：「慮寢疾不起，此乃命也。
entries.en: He found his father in tears and urged him: "Sun Lü's illness ran its course—that was heaven's decree.
entries.literal: Seeing Sun Quan he wept in grief and therefore remonstrated, saying: "Lü lay ill and did not rise; this is fate.

entries.zh: 方今朔土未一，四海喁喁，天戴陛下，而以下流之念，減損大官殽饌，過於禮制，臣竊憂惶。」
entries.en: The north is still unconquered; the realm hangs on your every word. Yet grief has led you to cut back the imperial kitchen beyond what ritual allows—I cannot help but worry."
entries.literal: At present the northern lands are not unified; within the four seas all look upward; Heaven bears up Your Majesty; yet because of thoughts flowing downstream you reduce and diminish the meats and viands of the great kitchen, exceeding the regulations of ritual; your servant privately is anxious and fearful."

entries.zh: 權納其言，爲之加膳。
entries.en: Sun Quan took the point and restored fuller meals.
entries.literal: Sun Quan accepted his words and for his sake increased the viands.

entries.zh: 住十餘日，欲遣西還，深自陳乞，以乆離定省，子道有闕，又陳陸遜忠勤，無所顧憂，權遂留焉。
entries.en: After ten days Sun Quan meant to send him back to the western command, but Sun Deng begged to stay: he had long neglected his filial duty of visiting his parents, he said, and Lu Xun was loyal and diligent enough that the western front needed no further anxiety from the heir. Sun Quan let him remain.
entries.literal: He stayed more than ten days; Sun Quan wished to send him back west; he deeply stated his own plea that, having long been separated from fixed attendance, there was a gap in the way of a son; he also stated that Lu Xun was loyal and diligent and there was nothing to worry over in looking after affairs; Sun Quan thereupon kept him.

entries.zh: 嘉禾三年，權征新城，使登居守，總知留事。
entries.en: In 234, when Sun Quan marched on Xincheng, he left Sun Deng in charge at the capital with full authority over rear-area administration.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jiahe, Sun Quan campaigned against Xincheng and ordered Deng to remain in guard and overall manage remaining affairs.

entries.zh: 時年穀不豐，頗有盜賊，乃表定科令，所以防禦，甚得止姦之要。
entries.en: Harvests were poor and banditry common, so he memorialized for codified regulations on defense and hit exactly the measures needed to curb crime.
entries.literal: At that time the year's grain was not abundant and there were quite a few bandits; he therefore submitted a memorial fixing statutes and ordinances for purposes of defense, and grasped very well the essentials of stopping wickedness.

entries.zh: 立凡二十一年，年三十三卒。
entries.en: He had been heir for twenty-one years when he died at thirty-three.
entries.literal: Having been established in all twenty-one years, at age thirty-three he died.

entries.zh: 臨終，上疏曰：「臣以無狀，嬰抱篤疾，自省微劣，懼卒隕斃。
entries.en: Near death he addressed a memorial: "I have conducted myself without distinction and now lie gravely ill; knowing my own slight worth, I fear I may suddenly be taken.
entries.literal: At the end of his life he submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant, lacking good form, has been encircled by grave illness; examining himself, he is slight and inferior and fears he will suddenly perish.

entries.zh: 臣不自惜，念當委離供養，埋胔后土，長不復奉望宮省，朝覲日月，生無益於國，死貽陛下重慼，以此爲哽結耳。
entries.en: It is not my own fate I mourn, but that I must leave your service and lie beneath the soil, never again to attend court or behold your radiance. I have done the state little good in life, and my death will only deepen your sorrow—that is what chokes me.
entries.literal: Your servant does not pity himself, but thinks that he must cast off support and bury his flesh in the earth below, long not again to gaze on the palace precincts or court the sun and moon; in life he was of no benefit to the state, in death he leaves Your Majesty heavy grief—on this account it knots his throat.

entries.zh: 臣聞死生有命，長短自天，周晉、顏回有上智之才，而尚夭折，況臣愚陋，年過其壽，生爲國嗣，沒享榮祚，於臣已多，亦何悲恨哉！
entries.en: I know life and death are decreed and longevity is heaven's gift. Prince Jin of Zhou and Yan Hui were men of supreme intellect, yet they died young—how much more I, dull and obscure, who have already outlived my share, lived as your heir, and will depart with honors few could claim? What room is left for regret?
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that death and life have their allotment and length and brevity come from Heaven; Prince Jin of Zhou and Yan Hui had talents of the highest wisdom, yet still met early death—how much more your servant, stupid and mean, his years having passed his allotted span, who in life was heir of the state and in death will enjoy glorious fortune—for your servant it is already much; what grief or resentment is there!

entries.zh: 方今大事未定，逋寇未討，萬國喁喁，係命陛下，危者望安，亂者仰治。
entries.en: The great enterprise is unfinished; rebels still roam. Every corner of the realm looks to you for its very breath—the imperiled seek safety, the chaotic seek order.
entries.literal: At present the great matter is not settled, the fugitive foe is not punished; the myriad regions murmur with upturned mouths; their lives hang on Your Majesty; those in peril look to be secured, those in disorder look up to be governed.

entries.zh: 願陛下棄忘臣身，割下流之恩，脩黃老之術，篤養神光，加羞珍膳，廣開神明之慮，以定無窮之業，則率土幸賴，臣死無恨也。
entries.en: Forget me, I beg you; set aside grief's pull. Practice the quieting arts of Huang-Lao, cherish your vital spirit, take rich nourishment, and broaden your mind for the boundless work ahead. If the realm can lean on you thus, I shall die content.
entries.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to cast off and forget your servant's person, cut away the favor that flows downstream, cultivate the arts of Huang and Lao, earnestly nurture the spirit's radiance, increase and bring forth rare viands, broadly open the considerations of spirit-like clarity, so as to settle the enterprise without end—then within the bounds of the earth all will happily rely, and your servant in death will have no regret.

entries.zh: 皇子和仁孝聦哲，德行清茂，宜早建置，以繫民望。
entries.en: Prince He is humane, filial, and quick of mind; his character is bright and sound. Establish him soon to answer what the people expect.
entries.literal: The imperial son He is humane, filial, keen, and wise; his virtue and conduct are pure and flourishing; he ought early to be established and set in place so as to tie the hopes of the people.

entries.zh: 諸葛恪才略博達，器任佐時。
entries.en: Zhuge Ke combines breadth of talent with strategic depth—he has the capacity to serve the times.
entries.literal: Zhuge Ke's talent and strategy are broad and comprehensive; his capacity fits assisting the age.

entries.zh: 張休、顧譚、謝景，皆通敏有識斷，入宜委腹心，出可爲爪牙。
entries.en: Zhang Xiu, Gu Tan, and Xie Jing are astute men of clear judgment—keep them at your breast in council, send them to the field as your strong arm.
entries.literal: Zhang Xiu, Gu Tan, and Xie Jing are all penetrating and quick and have judgment; within they may be entrusted as heart and belly, without they can serve as claws and fangs.

entries.zh: 范慎、華融矯矯壯節，有國士之風。
entries.en: Fan Shen and Hua Rong carry themselves with the stern dignity of true "knights of the realm.
entries.literal: Fan Shen and Hua Rong, lofty and martial in integrity, have the bearing of men of state.

entries.zh: 羊衜辯捷，有專對之材。
entries.en: Yang Dao is quick-witted and eloquent—material for embassies and set-piece debate.
entries.literal: Yang Dao is eloquent and quick and has the talent for exclusive response.

entries.zh: 刁玄優弘，志履道真。
entries.en: Diao Xuan is large-minded and steady, his aspirations rooted in what is genuine.
entries.literal: Diao Xuan is generous and great; his intent treads the true Way.

entries.zh: 裴欽博記，翰采足用。
entries.en: Pei Qin's memory is encyclopedic and his pen more than adequate to any task.
entries.literal: Pei Qin broadly remembers; his brush splendor suffices for employment.

entries.zh: 蔣脩、虞翻，志節分明。
entries.en: Jiang Xiu and Yu Fan are men of unmistakable principle.
entries.literal: Jiang Xiu and Yu Fan have aims and integrity that are clear and distinct.

entries.zh: 凡此諸臣，或宜廊廟，或任將帥，皆練時事，明習法令，守信固義，有不可奪之志。
entries.en: Each of these men belongs either in the council chamber or at the head of an army. They know the business of government, the letter of the law, and the claims of honor—none of them is easily swayed from his purpose.
entries.literal: All these various ministers, some suitable for hall and temple, some fit to serve as generals and commanders, are all practiced in affairs of the times, clearly versed in statutes and ordinances, keep faith and solidify righteousness, and have aims that cannot be wrested away.

entries.zh: 此皆陛下日月所照，選置臣宮，得與從事，備知情素，敢以陳聞。
entries.en: Your light has fallen on them all; they served in my household and I know their character through and through—I presume to commend them to you.
entries.literal: These all are illumined by Your Majesty's sun and moon; chosen and set in your servant's palace, they obtained to work with him and your servant fully knows their dispositions and past conduct; he dares to set them forth for Your hearing.

entries.zh: 臣重惟當今方外多虞，師旅未休，當厲六軍，以圖進取。
entries.en: Beyond our borders trouble still stirs and the armies never rest. Harden the host and press the advantage while you can.
entries.literal: Your servant further considers that at present beyond the borders there are many alarms, armies and hosts do not rest; one ought to sharpen the six armies to plan advance and seizure.

entries.zh: 軍以人爲衆，衆以財爲寶，竊聞郡縣頗有荒殘，民物凋弊，姦亂萌生，是以法令繁滋，刑辟重切。
entries.en: Soldiers need men, and men need means. I hear that many districts lie waste, the people are exhausted, and crime is spreading—hence the thickening of laws and the severity of punishments.
entries.literal: Armies take men as their multitude, multitudes take wealth as their treasure; your servant has privately heard that commanderies and districts are in many places desolate and ruined, people and goods are withered and exhausted, treachery and disorder sprout and arise; for this reason statutes and ordinances multiply and thrive, punishments and penalties are heavy and keen.

entries.zh: 臣聞爲政聽民，律令與時推移，誠宜與將相大臣詳擇時宜，博采衆議，寬刑輕賦，均息力役，以順民望。
entries.en: Good government heeds the people; laws must move with the times. Counsel with your generals and ministers, gather opinion widely, ease penalties and taxes, and balance labor service—that is how to answer what the people long for.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that in governing one listens to the people; statutes and ordinances shift with the times; truly one ought with generals, ministers, and great officials carefully choose what fits the times, broadly gather the multitude's proposals, relax punishments and lighten levies, evenly still labor and corvée, so as to comply with the people's hopes.

entries.zh: 陸遜忠勤於時，出身憂國，謇謇在公，有匪躬之節。
entries.en: Lu Xun has been loyal and tireless, staking himself on the state's troubles and speaking plainly in its service—the classic minister who forgets self for duty.
entries.literal: Lu Xun is loyal and diligent toward the times; he gives his person in worry for the state; he is outspoken in public service and has the integrity of not sparing his person.

entries.zh: 諸葛瑾、步隲、朱然、全琮、朱據、呂岱、吾粲、闞澤、嚴畯、張承、孫怡忠於爲國，通達治體。
entries.en: Zhuge Jin, Bu Zhi, Zhu Ran, Quan Zong, Zhu Ju, Lü Dai, Wu Can, Kan Ze, Yan Jun, Zhang Cheng, and Sun Yi are steadfast servants of the state who understand how government works.
entries.literal: Zhuge Jin, Bu Zhi, Zhu Ran, Quan Zong, Zhu Ju, Lü Dai, Wu Can, Kan Ze, Yan Jun, Zhang Cheng, and Sun Yi are loyal in acting for the state and comprehend the body of governance.

entries.zh: 可令陳上便宜，蠲除苛煩，愛養士馬，撫循百姓。
entries.en: Charge them to memorialize on practical reforms, strip away vexatious exactions, care for troops and horses, and soothe the common people.
entries.literal: They may be ordered to set forth what is advantageous, remit and remove harsh vexations, cherish and nurture soldiers and horses, comfort and follow the hundred surnames.

entries.zh: 五年之外，十年之內，遠者歸復，近者盡力，兵不血刃，而大事可定也。
entries.en: Within five to ten years the distant will rally, the near will give their all, and you may settle the great enterprise without drawing a sword.
entries.literal: Beyond five years, within ten years, those far will return and restore themselves, those near will exhaust their strength, arms will not blood blades, and the great matter can be settled.

entries.zh: 臣聞『鳥之將死其鳴也哀，人之將死其言也善』，故子囊臨終，遺言戒時，君子以爲忠，豈況臣登，其能已乎？
entries.en: They say a dying bird's cry is sad and a dying man's words are true. Zi-nang's deathbed counsel was judged loyal by every gentleman—how could I, Sun Deng, fall silent?
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that 'when a bird is about to die its cry is mournful; when a man is about to die his words are good'; therefore when Zi-nang faced the end, his dying words warned the times, and the gentleman deemed it loyalty—how much more your servant Deng, could he stop himself?

entries.zh: 願陛下留意聽采，臣雖死之日，猶生之年也。」
entries.en: I beg you to weigh these words: the day I die will still be a day I have lived, if you hear me."
entries.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to heed and listen and gather them in; though it be the day of your servant's death, it is still as the years of his life."

entries.zh: 旣絕而後書聞，權益以摧感，言則隕涕。
entries.en: The memorial reached Sun Quan only after Sun Deng had died. Sun Quan was shattered; whenever he spoke of it, he wept.
entries.literal: After he had expired, only then was the memorial heard; Sun Quan all the more was crushed and moved, and when he spoke tears fell.

entries.zh: 是歲，赤烏四年也。
entries.en: It was the fourth year of the Chiwu era (241).
entries.literal: That year was the fourth year of Chiwu.

entries.zh: 謝景時爲豫章太守，不勝哀情，棄官奔赴，拜表自劾。
entries.en: Xie Jing was prefect of Yuzhang. Overcome by grief, he abandoned his post to hurry to the capital and memorialized for punishment.
entries.literal: Xie Jing at the time was administrator of Yuzhang; unable to overcome grief, he cast aside office and hurried to attend; he submitted a memorial impeaching himself.

entries.zh: 權曰：「君與太子從事，異於他吏。」
entries.en: Sun Quan told him, "Your service to the heir sets you apart from ordinary officials."
entries.literal: Sun Quan said: "You in serving the heir apparent differ from other officials."

entries.zh: 使中使慰勞，聽復本職，發遣還郡。
entries.en: He sent envoys to console Xie Jing, allowed him to resume his post, and sent him back to his commandery.
entries.literal: He sent inner envoys to console and comfort him, permitted him to resume his original office, and issued orders sending him back to his commandery.

entries.zh: 謚登曰宣太子。
entries.en: Sun Deng was canonized as Crown Prince Xuan ("the Expositor").
entries.literal: Deng was given the posthumous title Expositor Heir.

entries.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：初葬句容，置園邑，奉守如法，後三年改葬蔣陵。〉
entries.en: 〈The Wu shu records that he was first interred at Jurong with a funerary estate and guardians as statute required, then, three years later, moved to the Jiang Mausoleum near Zhongshan.〉
entries.literal: 〈The Wu shu states: At first he was buried at Jurong, a park settlement was established, and guardianship was maintained according to law; after three years he was reburied at the Jiang Mausoleum by Bell Mountain.〉

entries.zh: 孫慮字子智，登弟也。
entries.en: Sun Lu, styled Zizhi, was Sun Deng's younger brother.
entries.literal: Sun Lu, courtesy name Zizhi, was Deng's younger brother.

entries.zh: 少敏惠有才藝，權器愛之。
entries.en: Even as a boy he showed quick intelligence and varied gifts; Sun Quan doted on him.
entries.literal: In youth he was keen, clever, and had talents and arts; Sun Quan valued and loved him.

entries.zh: 黃武七年，封建昌侯。
entries.en: In 228 he received the title of marquis of Jianchang.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Huangwu he was enfeoffed as marquis of Jianchang.

entries.zh: 後二年，丞相雍等奏慮性聦體達，所尚日新，比方近漢，宜進爵稱王，權未許。
entries.en: Two years later Chancellor Yong and others urged that Sun Lu was bright, well rounded, and ever improving—comparable to Han princes—and should be promoted to king. Sun Quan refused.
entries.literal: After two years, Chancellor Yong and others memorialized that Lu by nature was intelligent, his person comprehensive, what he esteemed daily renewed, comparing him to the recent Han, he ought to advance in rank and be titled king; Sun Quan did not grant it.

entries.zh: 乆之，尚書僕射存上疏曰：「帝王之興，莫不襃崇至親，以光羣后，故魯衞於周，寵冠諸侯，高帝五王，封列于漢，所以藩屏本朝，爲國鎮衞。
entries.en: Eventually Vice Director of the Secretariat Cun memorialized: "Every founding house exalts its closest kin to shine on the nobility—Lu and Wei stood first among Zhou lords, and Gaozu's five princes secured the Han. Such kin are the screen around the throne and the state's shield.
