entries.literal: After a long time, Vice Director of the Secretariat Cun submitted a memorial saying: "In the rise of emperors and kings there has never been one who did not exalt and honor the utmost kin so as to bring glory to the host of lords; therefore Lu and Wei toward Zhou had favor crowning the feudal lords, the five kings of the Exalted Founder were enfeoffed in array in the Han—these were the means to screen the root court and act as bulwarks and guards for the state.

entries.zh: 建昌侯慮稟性聦敏，才兼文武，於古典制，宜正名號。
entries.en: Marquis Sun Lu of Jianchang is clever by nature and gifted in both civil and military affairs; classical precedent calls for his title to be regularized.
entries.literal: The marquis of Jianchang Lu by endowment is intelligent and keen, his talents embrace both civil and military; according to ancient classical regulations, he ought to have his name and title rectified.

entries.zh: 陛下謙光，未肯如舊，羣寮大小，咸用於邑。
entries.en: Your modesty has held you back from following precedent, and the whole bureaucracy is frustrated.
entries.literal: Your Majesty's modest radiance has not been willing to follow the old pattern; hosts great and small among the host of officials all therefore are pent up.

entries.zh: 方今姦寇恣睢，金鼓未弭，腹心爪牙，惟親與賢。
entries.en: Rebels still swagger and the drums of war have not quieted. For the men at your breast and the arm you strike with, nothing matches kinsmen and proven talent.
entries.literal: At present treacherous foes act as they please; gongs and drums are not stilled; heart-belly and claws and fangs are only kin and worthies.

entries.zh: 輒與丞相雍等議，咸以慮宜爲鎮軍大將軍，授任偏方，以光大業。」
entries.en: We have consulted Chancellor Yong and the rest: all agree that Sun Lu should be named general who stabilizes the army and given a regional command to magnify your great enterprise."
entries.literal: We have then deliberated with Chancellor Yong and others; all consider that Lu ought to be made general who stabilizes the army, grant him appointment on a side quarter, so as to broaden and magnify the great enterprise."

entries.zh: 權乃許之，於是假節開府，治半州。
entries.en: Sun Quan agreed. Sun Lü received the imperial baton, opened his own command, and governed half the province.
entries.literal: Sun Quan thereupon granted it; thereupon Lu was given credentials of authority and opened a general's headquarters, administering half the province.

entries.zh: 〈《吳書》載權詔曰：「期運擾亂，凶邪肆虐，威罰有序，干戈不戢。
entries.en: 〈The Wu shu preserves Sun Quan's edict: "Fortune's course is in turmoil and the wicked hold sway; though justice has its course, the weapons of war have not been stowed away.
entries.literal: 〈The Wu shu records Sun Quan's edict: "The allotted span is troubled and chaotic; the vicious and wicked run rampant; awesome punishments have their order, yet arms are not laid down.

entries.zh: 以慮氣志休懿，武略夙昭，必能爲國佐定大業，故授以上將之位，至以殊特之榮，寵以兵馬之勢，委以偏方之任。
entries.en: Sun Lü's bearing is noble and his military talent proven—he can help secure the great work. So I invest him as a supreme general, grant him extraordinary honor, put troops at his disposal, and charge him with a frontier command.
entries.literal: Because Lu in temper and intent is generous and fine, his martial strategy long manifest, he is sure to be able for the state to assist in settling the great enterprise, therefore We confer on him the position of chief general, reaching to the glory of singular distinction, favor him with the power of arms and horses, and entrust him with responsibility for a side quarter.

entries.zh: 外欲威振敵虜，厭難萬里，內欲鎮撫遠近，慰卹將士，誠慮建功立事竭命之秋也。
entries.en: Without, he shall overawe the foe across a thousand miles; within, he shall steady the realm and hearten the army. This is the season for him to stake everything on achievement.
entries.literal: Without, We desire to awe and shake the enemy barbarians and crush hardship for ten thousand li; within, We desire to pacify and soothe far and near, console and relieve generals and soldiers—truly We consider this the autumn when Lu ought to exhaust his life in establishing merit and accomplishing affairs.

entries.zh: 慮其內脩文德，外經武訓，持盈若沖，則滿而不溢。
entries.en: Let him cultivate civil virtue within and drill the army without; let him keep a full measure as if it were still empty, so that success never spills into arrogance.
entries.literal: Lu ought within to cultivate civil virtue, without to regulate martial training, hold fullness as if it were emptiness, then though full he will not overflow.

entries.zh: 敬慎乃心，無忝所受。」〉
entries.en: Guard your heart with care, and do not shame the trust I place in you."〉"
entries.literal: Be reverent and careful in your heart; do not disgrace what you have received."〉"

entries.zh: 慮以皇子之尊，富於春秋，遠近嫌其不能留意。
entries.en: As a prince in the bloom of youth, he was thought too young to handle real responsibility.
entries.literal: Lu, by the dignity of an imperial son, being rich in the spring and autumn of years, those near and far suspected that he could not attend to business with care.

entries.zh: 及至臨事，遵奉法度，敬納師友，過於衆望。
entries.en: When power actually came to him, he followed statute, heeded his tutors, and surpassed what anyone had expected.
entries.literal: But when it came to facing affairs, he observed and upheld the laws, respectfully received masters and friends, and exceeded the multitude's expectations.

entries.zh: 年二十，嘉禾元年卒。
entries.en: He died in 232, aged twenty.
entries.literal: At age twenty, in the first year of Jiahe, he died.

entries.zh: 無子，國除。
entries.en: He left no heir, and the marquisate was abolished.
entries.literal: He had no son; the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 孫和字子孝，慮弟也。
entries.en: Sun He, styled Zixiao, was Sun Lü's younger brother.
entries.literal: Sun He, courtesy name Zixiao, was Lu's younger brother.

entries.zh: 少以母王有寵見愛，年十四，爲置宮衞，使中書令闞澤教以書藝。
entries.en: His mother Lady Wang was in favor, so he was doted on from boyhood. At fourteen he received a princely guard, and Kan Ze of the Secretariat was ordered to tutor him in letters and the arts.
entries.literal: In youth because his mother Lady Wang had favor he was loved; at age fourteen a palace guard was established for him, and Sun Quan ordered Director of the Secretariat Kan Ze to teach him writing and arts.

entries.zh: 好學下士，甚見稱述。
entries.en: He loved books and treated men of learning with deference, and won wide praise.
entries.literal: He loved learning and humbled himself before scholars; he was much praised in report.

entries.zh: 赤烏五年，立爲太子，時年十九。
entries.en: In 242, at nineteen, he was named crown prince.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Chiwu he was established as heir apparent; at the time he was nineteen.

entries.zh: 闞澤爲太傅，薛綜爲少傅，而蔡穎、張純、封俌、嚴維等皆從容侍從。
entries.en: Kan Ze was made grand tutor and Xue Zong junior tutor; Cai Ying, Zhang Chun, Feng Fu, Yan Wei, and others formed his leisurely circle of attendants.
entries.literal: Kan Ze became grand tutor, Xue Zong junior tutor, while Cai Ying, Zhang Chun, Feng Fu, Yan Wei, and others all attended him at ease in following service.

entries.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：和少岐嶷有智意，故權尤愛幸，常在左右，衣服禮秩雕玩珍異之賜，諸子莫得比焉。
entries.en: 〈The Wu shu says Sun He was precocious and clever, so Sun Quan favored him above the rest, kept him always at his side, and showered him with gifts no other son received.
entries.literal: 〈The Wu shu states: He in youth was precocious and had intelligent purpose, therefore Sun Quan especially loved and favored him, constantly kept him at his right and left, and in gifts of clothing, ritual rank, carved playthings, and rare treasures none of the other sons could compare.

entries.zh: 好文學，善騎射，承師涉學，精識聦敏，尊敬師傅，愛好人物。
entries.en: He cultivated literature, excelled at riding and archery, studied under masters, showed sharp wit, honored his tutors, and cherished worthy men.
entries.literal: He loved literary learning, was good at riding and archery, received teachers and crossed into study, was keen in perception and quick and clever, respected masters and tutors, and loved and esteemed men of note.

entries.zh: 穎等每朝見進賀，和常降意，歡以待之。
entries.en: When Cai Ying and his fellows came to court to offer congratulations, Sun He always humbled himself and welcomed them warmly.
entries.literal: Whenever Ying and the others at court audience advanced congratulations, He always lowered his intent and received them with joy.

entries.zh: 講校經義，綜察是非，及訪諮朝臣，考績行能，以知優劣，各有條貫。
entries.en: He discussed the Classics, weighed right and wrong, questioned ministers about policy, and assessed their performance so that merit and fault each had its place.
entries.literal: He lectured and collated canonical meanings, comprehensively examined right and wrong, and when he visited and consulted court ministers, examined their conduct and ability so as to know excellence and inferiority, each having its systematic order.

entries.zh: 後諸葛壹僞叛以誘魏將諸葛誕，權潛軍待之。
entries.en: Later Zhuge Yi pretended to defect to lure Zhuge Dan of Wei; Sun Quan hid an army to spring the trap.
entries.literal: Later Zhuge Yi feigned rebellion to lure the Wei general Zhuge Dan; Sun Quan secretly stationed troops awaiting him.

entries.zh: 和以權暴露外次，又戰者凶事，常憂勞憯怛，不復會同飲食，數上諫，戒令持重，務在全勝，權還，然後敢安。
entries.en: With his father camped in the field and war—a thing of ill omen—hanging over the state, Sun He could not bring himself to feast; he remonstrated again and again that Sun Quan hold steady and aim at total victory, and only when the sovereign returned did he rest easy.
entries.literal: He because Sun Quan was exposed in camp outside, and moreover warfare is an inauspicious matter, constantly worried and grieved in bitter distress, no longer joined in common drinking and eating, several times submitted remonstrance, enjoining him to be steady and weighty, striving for complete victory; only when Sun Quan returned did he dare be at ease.

entries.zh: 張純字元基，敦之子。
entries.en: Zhang Chun, courtesy name Yuanji, was the son of Zhang Dun.
entries.literal: Zhang Chun, courtesy name Yuanji, was the son of Dun.

entries.zh: 《吳錄》曰：純少厲操行，學博才秀，切問捷對，容止可觀。
entries.en: The Wu lu records that Zhang Chun disciplined himself young, was widely read and talented, asked sharp questions and answered crisply, and carried himself with presence.
entries.literal: The Wu lu states: Chun in youth hardened his conduct, his learning was broad and his talent outstanding, he pressed questions and answered swiftly, and his bearing was worth viewing.

entries.zh: 拜郎中，補廣德令，治有異績，擢爲太子輔義都尉。〉
entries.en: He served as a gentleman of the palace, then as magistrate of Guangde with a distinguished record, and rose to capital commandant assisting the heir.〉
entries.literal: He was appointed gentleman of the palace, supplemented as magistrate of Guangde, his rule had unusual traces of success, and he was promoted to capital commandant who aids righteousness for the heir.〉

entries.zh: 是後王夫人與全公主有隙。
entries.en: Afterward Lady Wang and the Princess of Quan fell out.
entries.literal: After this Lady Wang and the Princess of Quan had a rift.

entries.zh: 權嘗寢疾，和祠祭於廟，和妃叔父張休居近廟，邀和過所居。
entries.en: When Sun Quan fell seriously ill, Sun He sacrificed at the ancestral temple. His consort's uncle Zhang Xiu lived nearby and asked the heir to stop at his house.
entries.literal: Sun Quan once lay ill; He performed sacrifice and prayer in the temple; He's consort's paternal uncle Zhang Xiu dwelt near the temple and invited He to pass his dwelling.

entries.zh: 全公主使人覘視，因言太子不在廟中，專就妃家計議；
entries.en: The Princess of Quan had him watched, then reported that the crown prince had skipped the temple to plot at his in-laws' house;
entries.literal: The Princess of Quan had people spy and watch, and on that account said the heir apparent was not in the temple but had gone specially to the consort's kin to plot counsel;

entries.zh: 又言王夫人見上寢疾，有喜色。
entries.en: she added that Lady Wang had looked pleased when the sovereign took to his bed.
entries.literal: she also said that when Lady Wang saw the sovereign lying ill, she had a joyful expression.

entries.zh: 權由是發怒，夫人憂死，而和寵稍損，懼於廢黜。
entries.en: Sun Quan exploded with rage. Lady Wang died of grief, Sun He's favor waned, and he began to fear deposition.
entries.literal: Sun Quan for this reason gave vent to anger; the lady died in worry, and He's favor was gradually diminished; he feared deposition.

entries.zh: 魯王霸覬覦滋甚，陸遜、吾粲、顧譚等數陳適庶之義，理不可奪，全寄、楊笁爲魯王霸支黨，譖愬日興。
entries.en: Prince Sun Ba of Lu eyed the throne more openly. Lu Xun, Wu Can, and Gu Tan repeatedly argued the law of legitimate heir versus younger sons, but Quan Ji and Yang Zhu backed Sun Ba, and slander flew daily.
entries.literal: The Prince of Lu Ba gazed with ever greater covetousness; Lu Xun, Wu Can, Gu Tan, and others several times set forth the righteousness that separates heir and concubine's son, the principle being that it could not be wrested away; Quan Ji and Yang Zhu became partisan supporters of the Prince of Lu Ba, and slander and complaint rose daily.

entries.zh: 粲遂下獄誅，譚徙交州。
entries.en: Wu Can was jailed and killed; Gu Tan was banished to Jiaozhou.
entries.literal: Can thereupon went down to prison and was executed; Tan was banished to Jiaozhou.

entries.zh: 權沈吟者歷年，
entries.en: For years Sun Quan wavered,
entries.literal: Sun Quan hesitated for successive years,

entries.zh: 〈殷基《通語》曰：初權旣立和爲太子，而封霸爲魯王，初拜猶同宮室，禮秩未分。
entries.en: 〈Yin Ji's Tong yu records that when Sun He was made heir and Sun Ba prince of Lu, they at first still shared quarters and equal ceremony.
entries.literal: 〈Yin Ji's Tong yu states: At first, after Sun Quan had established He as heir apparent and enfeoffed Ba as Prince of Lu, at first investiture they still shared the same palace quarters and ritual rank was not divided.

entries.zh: 羣公之議，以爲太子、國王上下有序，禮秩宜異，於是分宮別僚，而隙端開矣。
entries.en: Ministers argued that crown prince and feudal prince must observe rank; separate households and staffs were ordered, and the split began.
entries.literal: The host of dukes' deliberation held that heir apparent and prince of the state, superior and inferior, had an order, and ritual rank ought to differ; thereupon they divided palaces and separated staffs, and the crack of rift opened.

entries.zh: 自侍御賔客造爲二端，仇黨疑貳，滋延大臣。
entries.en: Attendants and guests chose sides; suspicion spread through the high ministers.
entries.literal: From attendants, imperial companions, and guests they fashioned two ends; factions of enmity and suspicion in two minds spread and extended among great ministers.

entries.zh: 丞相陸遜、大將軍諸葛恪、太常顧譚、驃騎將軍朱據、會稽太守滕胤、大都督施績、尚書丁密等奉禮而行，宗事太子，驃騎將軍步隲、鎮南將軍呂岱、大司馬全琮、左將軍呂據、中書令孫弘等附魯王，中外官僚將軍大臣舉國中分。
entries.en: Chancellor Lu Xun, Grand General Zhuge Ke, Grand Master of Ceremonies Gu Tan, Cavalry General Zhu Ju, Administrator of Kuaiji Teng Yin, Grand Commander Shi Ji, Minister Ding Mi, and others acted according to ritual and treated the heir apparent as principal. Cavalry General Bu Zhi, General Who Guards the South Lü Dai, Grand Marshal Quan Zong, Left General Lü Ju, Director of the Secretariat Sun Hong, and others attached themselves to the Prince of Lu. Officials inside and outside court, generals, and great ministers were divided throughout the state.
entries.literal: Chancellor Lu Xun, Grand General Zhuge Ke, Grand Master of Ceremonies Gu Tan, Cavalry General Zhu Ju, Administrator of Kuaiji Teng Yin, Area Commander Shi Ji, Minister Ding Mi, and others upheld ritual and acted accordingly, making the heir apparent their clan concern; Cavalry General Bu Zhi, General Who Stabilizes the South Lü Dai, Grand Marshal Quan Zong, General of the Left Lü Ju, Director of the Secretariat Sun Hong, and others attached to the Prince of Lu; inner and outer clerks, generals, and great ministers split the whole state down the middle.

entries.zh: 權患之，謂侍中孫峻曰：「子弟不睦，臣下分部，將有袁氏之敗，爲天下笑。
entries.en: Sun Quan told Sun Jun, "My sons feud and my servants take sides—we risk the Yuan brothers' disaster and the world's mockery.
entries.literal: Sun Quan worried over it and said to Palace Attendant Sun Jun: "The sons and younger brothers are not harmonious; the subordinates divide into factions—there will be the Yuan clan's defeat and We shall be laughed at by the world.

entries.zh: 一人立者，安得不亂？」
entries.en: How can the realm stay calm when two heirs are in play?"
entries.literal: When one man is established, how can there not be chaos?"

entries.zh: 於是有改嗣之規矣。
entries.en: He began to consider replacing the heir.
entries.literal: Thereupon there was a plan to change the successor.

entries.zh: 臣松之以爲袁紹、劉表謂尚、琮爲賢，本有傳後之意，異於孫權旣以立和而復寵霸，坐生亂階，自構家禍，方之袁、劉，昏悖甚矣。
entries.en: Pei Songzhi comments: Yuan Shao and Liu Biao held Shang and Cong worthy and originally meant to pass the succession to them—unlike Sun Quan, who had already named an heir yet doted on Sun Ba, inviting ruin at home. Beside Yuan and Liu, Sun Quan looks far more blind.
entries.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that Yuan Shao and Liu Biao held Shang and Cong worthy and originally had intent to transmit the succession—this differed from Sun Quan, who having already established He again favored Ba, thereby sitting and producing the steps of disorder and for himself constructing family calamity; compared to Yuan and Liu, his benighted perversity was extreme.

entries.zh: 步隲以德度著稱，爲吳良臣，而阿附於霸，事同楊笁，何哉？
entries.en: Bu Zhi was celebrated as a worthy Wu minister—why did he cling to Sun Ba like Yang Zhu?
entries.literal: Bu Zhi was famed for virtue and measure, was a good minister of Wu, yet he fawned and attached to Ba—the affair being the same as Yang Zhu's—how could it be?

entries.zh: 和旣正位，適庶分定，就使才德不殊，猶將義不黨庶，況霸實無聞，而和爲令嗣乎？
entries.en: Once the rightful heir was fixed, the line between legitimate son and younger brother was clear. Even had their talents been equal, duty forbids siding with the lesser son—and Sun Ba had no reputation beside Sun He.
entries.literal: He having already taken correct position, legitimate heir and concubine's son were divided and fixed; granting that talents and virtues were not different, still the righteousness would not favor the concubine's son—how much more when Ba in truth had no reputation, while He was the lawful successor?

entries.zh: 夫邪僻之人，豈其舉體無善，但一爲不善，衆美皆亡耳。
entries.en: A wicked man is not all vice—but one wrong act cancels every virtue.
entries.literal: As for depraved and crooked men, how can their whole persons lack good?—yet once they do one ungood thing, all their beauties perish.

entries.zh: 隲若果有此事，則其餘不足觀矣！
entries.en: If Bu Zhi really did that, nothing else he did deserves our respect!
entries.literal: If Zhi truly had this affair, then the rest is not worth viewing!

entries.zh: 呂岱、全琮之徒，蓋所不足論耳。〉
entries.en: Lü Dai, Quan Zong, and their like scarcely merit discussion.〉
entries.literal: As for Lü Dai, Quan Zong, and their sort, they are probably not worth discussing.〉

entries.zh: 後遂幽閉和。
entries.en: Sun He was then placed under house arrest.
entries.literal: Afterward they thereupon confined He in seclusion.

entries.zh: 於是驃騎將軍朱據、尚書僕射屈晃率諸將吏泥頭自縛，連日詣闕請和。
entries.en: Zhu Ju and Vice Director Qu Huang led officers to the gates with heads smeared with mud and ropes on their wrists, day after day begging Sun Quan to forgive Sun He.
entries.literal: Thereupon Cavalry General Zhu Ju, Vice Director of the Secretariat Qu Huang, leading the host of generals and clerks with mud on their heads and binding themselves, for successive days went to the palace gates requesting reconciliation for He.

entries.zh: 權登白爵觀見，甚惡之，勑據、晃等無事忩忩。
entries.en: From the White Heron Watch Sun Quan saw the demonstration and was furious; he ordered Zhu Ju and Qu Huang to stop their clamor.
entries.literal: Sun Quan ascended the White Heron Watch and saw them; he greatly hated it and ordered Ju, Huang, and the others to have no business in frantic haste.

entries.zh: 權欲廢和立亮，無難督陳正、五營督陳象上書，稱引晉獻公殺申生，立奚齊，晉國擾亂，又據、晃固諫不止。
entries.en: When Sun Quan meant to depose Sun He for Sun Liang, colonels Chen Zheng and Chen Xiang cited Duke Xian of Jin, who killed Shen Sheng to install Xi Qi and threw the state into chaos; Zhu Ju and Qu Huang still would not let the matter drop.
entries.literal: Sun Quan wished to depose He and establish Liang; the Colonel of the Garrison Without Difficulty Chen Zheng and the Colonel of the Five Camps Chen Xiang submitted memorials, citing Duke Xian of Jin who killed Shen Sheng and established Xi Qi, whereby Jin was thrown into turmoil; again Ju and Huang firmly remonstrated without ceasing.

entries.zh: 權大怒，族誅正、象，據、晃牽入殿，杖一百，
entries.en: Sun Quan raged, executed Chen Zheng and Chen Xiang root and branch, had Zhu Ju and Qu Huang dragged into court, and gave them a hundred strokes,
entries.literal: Sun Quan was greatly angry, exterminated the clans of Zheng and Xiang, dragged Ju and Huang into the hall, and caned them one hundred strokes,

entries.zh: 〈《吳歷》曰：晃入，口諫曰：「太子仁明，顯聞四海。
entries.en: 〈The Wu li says Qu Huang entered and cried, "The crown prince is humane and wise, known throughout the realm.
entries.literal: 〈The Wu li states: When Huang entered, he remonstrated with his mouth: "The heir apparent is humane and enlightened, renowned within the four seas.

entries.zh: 今三方鼎跱，實不宜搖動太子，以生衆心。
entries.en: The three kingdoms stand like a tripod; you must not unsettle the heir and sow doubt among the people.
entries.literal: Now the three sides stand like tripods; it is truly not fitting to shake the heir apparent so as to give birth to the multitude's doubts.

entries.zh: 願陛下少垂聖慮，老臣雖死，猶生之年。」
entries.en: I beg you reconsider—though this old minister die, he will count his life well spent."
entries.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty slightly to let fall sagely consideration; though your aged servant die, it would still count as years of life."

entries.zh: 叩頭流血，辭氣不撓。
entries.en: He beat his head on the floor until the blood flowed and never softened his tone.
entries.literal: He knocked his head until it bled; his words and temper did not bend.

entries.zh: 權不納晃言，斥還田里。
entries.en: Sun Quan refused to hear him and sent Qu Huang home to his lands.
entries.literal: Sun Quan did not accept Huang's words and dismissed him to return to his fields.

entries.zh: 孫皓即位，詔曰：「故僕射屈晃，志匡社稷，忠諫亡身。
entries.en: When Sun Hao came to the throne he decreed, "The late Vice Director Qu Huang gave his life in loyal remonstrance for the altars of state.
entries.literal: When Sun Hao assumed the throne, he issued an edict: "The former Vice Director of the Secretariat Qu Huang, his aim was to rectify the altars of soil and grain, and he loyally remonstrated unto death.

entries.zh: 封晃子緒爲東陽亭侯，弟幹、恭爲立義都尉。」
entries.en: He enfeoffed Qu Huang's son Qu Xu as village marquis of Dongyang and his brothers Qu Gan and Qu Gong as capital commandants for upholding righteousness."
entries.literal: He enfeoffed Huang's son Xu as village marquis of Dongyang, younger brothers Gan and Gong as capital commandants who uphold righteousness."

entries.zh: 緒後亦至尚書僕射。
entries.en: Qu Xu later rose to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Xu later also reached the office of Vice Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 晃，汝南人，見胡沖荅問。
entries.en: Qu Huang was from Runan; see Hu Chong's Questions and Answers.
entries.literal: Huang was a man of Runan; see Hu Chong's Questions and Answers.

entries.zh: 《吳書》曰：張純亦盡言極諫，權幽之，遂棄市。〉
entries.en: The Wu shu adds that Zhang Chun remonstrated to the limit; Sun Quan jailed him and had him executed in the marketplace.〉
entries.literal: The Wu shu states: Zhang Chun also spoke exhaustively in extreme remonstrance; Sun Quan confined him, then cast him aside in the market.〉

entries.zh: 竟徙和於故鄣，羣司坐諫誅放者十數。
entries.en: Sun He was banished to Guchang, and a dozen or more officials who had pleaded for him were killed or exiled.
entries.literal: In the end He was moved to Guchang; hosts of officials who sat for remonstrance were executed or banished in numbers of ten and more.

entries.zh: 衆咸冤之。
entries.en: Public opinion held him wronged.
entries.literal: The multitude all held it unjust.

entries.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：權寢疾，意頗感寤，欲徵和還立之，全公主及孫峻、孫弘等固爭之，乃止。〉
entries.en: 〈The Wu shu says that when Sun Quan fell ill he nearly recalled Sun He as heir, but the Princess of Quan and Sun Jun and Sun Hong blocked it.〉
entries.literal: 〈The Wu shu states: When Sun Quan lay ill with a sleeping sickness, his mind was quite moved to enlightenment and he wished to summon He back and establish him; the Princess of Quan and Sun Jun, Sun Hong, and others firmly contested it, and only then he stopped.〉

entries.zh: 孫休立，封和子皓爲烏程侯，自新都之本國。
entries.en: When Sun Xiu took the throne he enfeoffed Sun He's son Sun Hao as marquis of Wucheng, who traveled from Xindu to his fief.
entries.literal: When Sun Xiu was established, he enfeoffed He's son Hao as marquis of Wucheng, who went from Xindu to his own state.

entries.zh: 休薨，皓即阼，其年追謚父和曰文皇帝，改葬明陵，置園邑二百家，令、丞奉守。
entries.en: After Sun Xiu died Sun Hao succeeded; the same year he posthumously titled his father Sun He as Emperor Wen, reinterred him at Ming Mausoleum with a two-hundred-household funerary estate under magistrate and assistant.
entries.literal: When Xiu died, Hao succeeded to the throne; that year he posthumously honored his father He with the title Emperor Wen, reburied him at Ming Mausoleum, established a park settlement of two hundred households, and ordered a magistrate and assistant to maintain guardianship.

entries.zh: 後年正月，又分吳郡、丹楊九縣爲吳興郡，治烏程，置太守，四時奉祠。
entries.en: The next New Year he carved nine counties from Wu and Danyang into a new Wu Xing commandery based at Wucheng, appointed a grand administrator, and ordered sacrifices each season.
entries.literal: In the first month of the following year, again he divided nine counties of Wu commandery and Danyang to make Wu Xing commandery, with its seat at Wucheng, and established a grand administrator, with seasonal sacrifice in the four seasons.

entries.zh: 有司奏言，宜立廟京邑。
entries.en: Officials memorialized for an ancestral temple in the capital.
entries.literal: The responsible officials submitted saying that a temple ought to be established in the capital city.

entries.zh: 寶鼎二年七月，使守大匠薛珝營立寢堂，號曰清廟。
entries.en: In the seventh month of 267 he had Guardian Grand Engineer Xue Xu build a spirit hall styled the Pure Temple.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Baoding, he ordered the Guardian Grand Engineer Xue Xu to build a hall for the resting spirit, styled the Pure Temple.

entries.zh: 十二月，遣守丞相孟仁、太常姚信等備官寮中軍步騎二千人，以靈輿法駕，東迎神於明陵。
entries.en: In the twelfth month he sent Acting Chancellor Meng Ren, Grand Master Yao Xin, a full retinue, and two thousand guards with the imperial bier east to Ming Mausoleum to fetch the spirit.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month he sent Acting Chancellor Meng Ren, Grand Master of Ceremonies Yao Xin, and others with full complement of officials and followers, two thousand foot and horse of the central army, with the spirit carriage and statutory equipage, to go east and welcome the spirit at Ming Mausoleum.

entries.zh: 皓引見仁，親拜送於庭。
entries.en: Sun Hao received Meng Ren in audience and bowed him off in the courtyard himself.
entries.literal: Hao led Ren in audience and personally bowed in sending off at the courtyard.

entries.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：比仁還，中使手詔，日夜相繼，奉問神靈起居動止。
entries.en: 〈The Wu shu says that while Meng Ren was returning, couriers with the emperor's own edicts followed one another night and day asking after the spirit's progress.
entries.literal: 〈The Wu shu states: When Ren returned, inner envoys with autograph edicts succeeded one another day and night, conveying inquiries after the spirit's rest and rise, movement and stillness.

entries.zh: 巫覡言見和被服，顏色如平生日，皓悲喜涕淚，悉召公卿尚書詣闕門下受賜。〉
entries.en: Mediums claimed Sun He appeared in court dress, his face as in life; Sun Hao wept for joy and sorrow and summoned the high ministers to the gate to receive blessings.〉
entries.literal: Witches and shamans said they saw He in robes and caps, his complexion as on ordinary days of life; Hao was moved between joy and sorrow to tears and mucus, and summoned all dukes, ministers, and directors of departments to the gates below the palace to receive bestowal.〉

entries.zh: 靈輿當至，使丞相陸凱奉三牲祭於近郊，皓於金城外露宿。
entries.en: As the bier neared, he told Chancellor Lu Kai to sacrifice the three victims in the near suburb while he himself camped in the open outside the Metal Wall.
entries.literal: When the spirit carriage was about to arrive, he ordered Chancellor Lu Kai to offer the three sacrificial victims in sacrifice at the near suburbs, while Hao lodged in the open outside the Metal Wall.

entries.zh: 明日，望拜於東門之外。
entries.en: The next day he bowed toward the east outside the city gate.
entries.literal: The next day he gazed and bowed outside the eastern gate.

entries.zh: 其翌日，拜廟薦祭，歔欷悲感。
entries.en: The following day he worshiped at the temple, offered sacrifice, and wept aloud.
entries.literal: The day after that he bowed in the temple, presented sacrifice, sighed and wept, moved and grieved.

entries.zh: 比七日三祭，倡技晝夜娛樂。
entries.en: For seven days and three services, musicians and dancers entertained without cease.
entries.literal: For seven days with three sacrifices, singing girls and performers by day and night provided entertainment.

entries.zh: 有司奏言「祭不欲數，數則黷，宜以禮斷情」，然後止。
entries.en: The responsible officials memorialized, "Sacrifices should not be too frequent; if they are frequent, they become profane. Emotion should be restrained by ritual." Only then did the observances stop.
entries.literal: The responsible officials submitted saying "Sacrifice ought not to be frequent; if frequent then it is profane; one ought to cut off feeling by ritual"—only then did it stop.

entries.zh: 〈《吳歷》曰：和四子：皓、德、謙、俊。
entries.en: 〈The Wu li lists four sons of Sun He: Sun Hao, Sun De, Sun Qian, and Sun Jun.
entries.literal: 〈The Wu li states: He had four sons: Hao, De, Qian, and Jun.

entries.zh: 孫休即位，封德錢唐侯，謙永安侯，俊拜騎都尉。
entries.en: When Sun Xiu came to the throne he enfeoffed Sun De at Qiantang, Sun Qian at Yongan, and appointed Sun Jun cavalry commandant.
entries.literal: When Sun Xiu assumed the throne, he enfeoffed De as marquis of Qiantang, Qian as marquis of Yongan, and Jun was appointed cavalry commandant.

entries.zh: 皓在武昌，吳興施但因民之不堪命，聚萬餘人，劫謙，將至秣陵，欲立之。
entries.en: While Sun Hao was at Wuchang, Shi Dan of Wu Xing, claiming the people could not endure his rule, raised over ten thousand men, seized Sun Qian, and marched on Moling intending to enthrone him.
entries.literal: When Hao was at Wuchang, Shi Dan of Wu Xing, because the people could not bear their commands, gathered more than ten thousand men, seized Qian, and was about to reach Moling, intending to establish him.

entries.zh: 未至三十里住，擇吉日，但遣使以謙命詔丁固、諸葛靚。
entries.en: They halted thirty li short, picked an auspicious day, and sent envoys in Sun Qian's name to summon Ding Gu and Zhuge Jing.
entries.literal: Before reaching thirty li they halted, chose an auspicious day, and Dan sent envoys with Qian's order to summon Ding Gu and Zhuge Jing.

entries.zh: 靚即斬其使。
entries.en: Zhuge Jing beheaded the messenger at once.
entries.literal: Jing thereupon beheaded his envoy.

entries.zh: 但遂前到九里，固、靚出擊，大破之。
entries.en: Shi Dan pushed on to Jiuli; Ding Gu and Zhuge Jing sallied forth and crushed him.
entries.literal: Dan thereupon advanced to Jiuli; Gu and Jing came out and attacked, greatly defeating him.

entries.zh: 但兵裸身無鎧甲，臨陣皆披散。
entries.en: Shi Dan's soldiers were naked, without armor; when they faced the battle line they all scattered.
entries.literal: Dan's soldiers were naked without armor; facing battle they all scattered.

entries.zh: 謙獨坐車中，遂生獲之。
entries.en: Sun Qian alone sat in a carriage and was taken alive.
entries.literal: Qian alone sat in a carriage; thereupon he was captured alive.

entries.zh: 固不敢殺，以狀告皓，皓酖之，母子皆死。
entries.en: Ding Gu dared not execute him and reported to Sun Hao, who poisoned him with wine; mother and son both died.
entries.literal: Gu did not dare kill him but reported the situation to Hao; Hao poisoned him with ale, and mother and son both died.

entries.zh: 俊，張承外孫，聦明辨惠，爲遠近所稱，皓又殺之。〉
entries.en: Sun Jun was Zhang Cheng's grandson by a daughter—clever and praised far and wide—and Sun Hao killed him too.〉
entries.literal: Jun was Zhang Cheng's maternal grandson, clever in discrimination and quick in wisdom, praised by far and near, and Hao again killed him.〉

entries.zh: 霸二子，基、壹。
entries.en: Sun Ba had two sons, Ji and Yi.
entries.literal: Ba had two sons, Ji and Yi.

entries.zh: 五鳳中，封基爲吳侯，壹宛陵侯。
entries.en: During the Wufeng era, Ji was made Marquis of Wu and Yi Marquis of Wanling.
entries.literal: In the Wufeng era, Ji was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wu and Yi as Marquis of Wanling.

entries.zh: 基侍孫亮在內，太平二年257年，盜乘御馬，收付獄。
entries.en: Ji served Sun Liang in the inner palace. In 257 (the second year of Taiping) he stole and rode an imperial horse and was imprisoned.
entries.literal: Ji attended Sun Liang within the inner palace; in the second year of Taiping (257) he stole and rode an imperial horse and was taken into custody.

entries.zh: 亮問侍中刁玄曰：「盜乘御馬罪云何？」
entries.en: Sun Liang asked Attendant-in-Ordinary Diao Xuan, "What is the penalty for stealing and riding an imperial horse?"
entries.literal: Liang asked Attendant-in-Ordinary Diao Xuan, saying: "What is the penalty for stealing and riding an imperial horse?"

entries.zh: 玄對曰：「科應死。
entries.en: Diao Xuan replied, "By statute the penalty is death.
entries.literal: Xuan replied, saying: "By statute the penalty is death.

entries.zh: 然魯王早終，惟陛下哀原之。」
entries.en: Yet the Prince of Lu died young; I beg Your Majesty to show pity and pardon him."
entries.literal: Yet the Prince of Lu died young; I beg Your Majesty to show pity and pardon him."

entries.zh: 亮曰：「法者，天下所共，何得阿以親親故邪？
entries.en: Sun Liang said, "Law belongs to all under Heaven—how can one show favoritism because of kinship?
entries.literal: Liang said: "Law is what all under Heaven share; how can one show favoritism because of kinship?

entries.zh: 當思惟可以釋此者，柰何以情相迫乎？」
entries.en: One ought to think of what could release him—why press me with personal sentiment?"
entries.literal: One ought to think of what could release this case—why press me with personal sentiment?"

entries.zh: 玄曰：「舊赦有大小，或天下，亦有千里、五百里赦，隨意所及。」
entries.en: Diao Xuan said, "Amnesties of old came in great and small forms—sometimes for the whole realm, sometimes for a radius of a thousand or five hundred li, as far as the sovereign wished to extend mercy."
entries.literal: Xuan said: "Amnesties of old came in great and small forms—sometimes for all the realm, sometimes for a radius of a thousand or five hundred li, according to what the sovereign wished to reach."

entries.zh: 亮曰：「解人不當爾邪！」
entries.en: Sun Liang said, "Should not someone who understands matters act thus!"
entries.literal: Liang said: "Should not someone who understands matters act thus!"

entries.zh: 乃赦宮中，基以得免。
entries.en: He then proclaimed an amnesty within the palace, and Ji was spared.
entries.literal: Thereupon he proclaimed an amnesty within the palace, and Ji thereby escaped punishment.

entries.zh: 孫皓即位，追和、霸舊隙，削基、壹爵土，與祖母謝姬俱徙會稽烏傷縣。
entries.en: When Sun Hao succeeded, he revived the old feud between Sun He and Sun Ba, stripped Ji and Yi of their titles and fiefs, and exiled them with their grandmother Lady Xie to Wushang in Kuaiji.
entries.literal: When Sun Hao took the throne, he revived the old enmity between He and Ba, stripped Ji and Yi of their titles and fiefs, and together with their grandmother Lady Xie exiled them to Wushang county in Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 評曰：孫登居心所存，足爲茂美之德。
entries.en: The appraiser says: Sun Deng's inner life was the stuff of true nobility.
entries.literal: The appraisal states: What Sun Deng stored in his heart was enough to be luxuriant and beautiful virtue.

entries.zh: 慮、和並有好善之姿，規自砥礪，或短命早終，或不得其死，哀哉！
entries.en: Sun Lü and Sun He both loved the good and strove to better themselves—one died young, the other was destroyed; how pitiful!
entries.literal: Lu and He together had the bearing that loves the good; they regulated and sharpened themselves—some met early death with short fate, some did not obtain natural death—alas!

entries.zh: 霸以庶干適，奮不遵軌度，固取危亡之道也。
entries.en: Sun Ba, a younger son, muscled against the heir; Sun Fen scorned the rules—each courted ruin by a clear road.
entries.literal: Ba by a concubine's son meddled with the heir; Fen did not follow track and measure—solidly they took the path of danger and ruin.

entries.zh: 然奮之誅夷，橫遇飛禍矣。
entries.en: Yet Sun Fen's slaughter was sheer mischance, a bolt from the blue.
entries.literal: Yet Fen's execution and extermination met calamity that flew from nowhere.

entries.zh: 孫登字子高，權長子也。
entries.en: Sun Deng, whose courtesy name was Zigao, was Sun Quan's firstborn son.
entries.literal: Sun Deng, courtesy name Zigao, was the eldest son of Sun Quan.

entries.zh: 魏黃初二年，以權爲吳王，拜登東中郎將，封萬戶侯，登辭疾不受。
entries.en: In 221, the Wei court invested Sun Quan as King of Wu and named Sun Deng General of the Household for All Purposes of the East with a fief of ten thousand households; Sun Deng pleaded ill health and refused the appointment and title.
entries.literal: In the second year of Huangchu of Wei, Sun Quan was made King of Wu; Sun Deng was appointed General of the Household for All Purposes of the East and enfeoffed as marquis of ten thousand households, but Sun Deng declined citing illness and did not accept.

entries.zh: 是歲，立登爲太子，選置師傅，銓簡秀士，以爲賔友，於是諸葛恪、張休、顧譚、陳表等以選入，侍講詩書，出從騎射。
entries.en: The same year Sun Deng was made crown prince. Tutors were appointed and talented men chosen as his companions, so Zhuge Ke, Zhang Xiu, Gu Tan, Chen Biao, and others joined his household by competitive selection—indoors they expounded the Classics; outdoors they rode and shot with him.
entries.literal: That year he was established as heir apparent; masters and tutors were chosen and set in place, and outstanding scholars were screened and selected to be guests and companions; thereupon Zhuge Ke, Zhang Xiu, Gu Tan, Chen Biao, and others entered by selection, lecturing him on the Classics and histories indoors and accompanying him in riding and archery when he went out.

entries.zh: 權欲登讀《漢書》，習知近代之事，以張昭有師法，重煩勞之，乃令休從昭受讀，還以授登。
entries.en: Sun Quan wanted his heir to read the Han shu and learn recent history. Zhang Zhao was the acknowledged master teacher, but Sun Quan hesitated to burden him, so he had Zhang Xiu study under Zhang Zhao and then pass the lessons on to Sun Deng.
entries.literal: Sun Quan wished Sun Deng to read the Han shu and become familiar with affairs of recent times; because Zhang Zhao had proper methods of instruction and Sun Quan shrank from wearying him excessively, he ordered Zhang Xiu to receive instruction in reading from Zhang Zhao and return to teach Sun Deng.

entries.zh: 登待接寮屬，略用布衣之禮，與恪、休、譚等或同輿而載，或共帳而寐。
entries.en: With his staff Sun Deng kept to plain, almost commoner-level courtesy: he shared a carriage with Zhuge Ke, Zhang Xiu, Gu Tan, and the like, or slept in the same tent with them.
entries.literal: In receiving his subordinate officials Sun Deng broadly used the rites of a commoner, and with Ke, Xiu, Tan, and others he sometimes rode in the same carriage or slept in the same tent.

entries.zh: 太傅張溫言於權曰：「夫中庶子官最親密，切問近對，宜用儁德。」
entries.en: Grand Tutor Zhang Wen urged Sun Quan: "Palace attendants stand closest to the heir; they field urgent questions at his side. The posts demand men of exceptional moral stature."
entries.literal: Grand Tutor Zhang Wen spoke to Sun Quan, saying: "The office of palace attendant is the most intimate; it answers pressing questions at close quarters; outstanding virtue ought to be employed."

entries.zh: 於是乃用表等爲中庶子。
entries.en: Sun Quan then appointed Chen Biao and others palace attendants.
entries.literal: Thereupon Chen Biao and others were employed as palace attendants.

entries.zh: 後又以庶子禮拘，復令整巾侍坐。
entries.en: Later the formal etiquette for attendants proved awkwardly stiff, so he told them to straighten their caps and take seats while on duty.
entries.literal: Later, because the rites for palace attendants were restrictive, he again ordered them to arrange their headcloths and attend seated.

entries.zh: 黃龍元年，權稱尊號，登爲皇太子，以恪爲左輔，休右弼，譚爲輔正，表爲翼正都尉，是爲四友，而謝景、范慎、刁玄、羊衜等皆爲賔客，
entries.en: In 229 Sun Quan took the imperial style; Sun Deng became crown prince. Zhuge Ke was named left support, Zhang Xiu right support, Gu Tan rectifier of the heir, and Chen Biao capital commandant who wings the rectifier—the group known as the Four Friends—while Xie Jing, Fan Shen, Diao Xuan, Yang Dao, and others served as his guests.
entries.literal: In the first year of Huanglong, when Sun Quan assumed the exalted title, Sun Deng became imperial heir; Ke was made left support, Xiu right support, Tan rectifier of the heir, Biao capital commandant who wings the rectifier—these were called the Four Friends—while Xie Jing, Fan Shen, Diao Xuan, Yang Dao, and others all became guests,

entries.zh: 〈衜音道。〉
entries.en: 〈The gloss reads the character with the same sound as dao, 'way.'〉
entries.literal: 〈The note glosses the character as pronounced dao, like the word for 'way."

entries.zh: 於是東宮號爲多士。
entries.en: The heir's establishment was soon renowned for the density of talent around him.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Eastern Palace was styled as abounding in worthy men.

entries.zh: 〈《吳錄》曰：慎字孝敬，廣陵人，竭忠知己之君，纏綿三益之友，時人榮之。
entries.en: 〈According to the Wu lu, Fan Shen, styled Xiaojing, came from Guangling. He gave his whole loyalty to a sovereign who truly knew him, and he clung to friendships that enriched character in the classical "three ways"—contemporaries held him in high esteem. )
entries.literal: 〈The Wu lu states: Fan, courtesy name Xiaojing, was a man of Guangling; he exhausted loyalty toward a ruler who knew him, and clung to friends who brought the three benefits; people of the time honored him for it. )

entries.zh: 著論二十篇，名曰《矯非》。
entries.en: He wrote twenty essays collected under the title Rectifying Error.
entries.literal: He composed twenty treatises, entitled Rectifying Error.

entries.zh: 後爲侍中，出補武昌左部督，治軍整頓。
entries.en: He later served as palace attendant, then transferred to command the left wing at Wuchang, where he ran a tight, disciplined camp.
entries.literal: Later he became palace attendant, went out to fill the post of commander of the left division at Wuchang, and governed the army in good order.

entries.zh: 孫皓移都，甚憚之，詔曰：「慎勳德俱茂，朕所敬憑，宜登上公，以副衆望。」
entries.en: After Sun Hao shifted the capital he grew wary of Fan Shen's stature and issued an edict: "Fan's achievements and character alike command respect; I lean on him with reverence. He should be raised to the highest ducal rank to satisfy public expectation."
entries.literal: When Sun Hao moved the capital he greatly feared him and issued an edict saying: "Fan's merit and virtue are both flourishing; he is one on whom We rely in reverence; he ought to be raised to the highest duke rank to answer the hopes of the multitude."

entries.zh: 以爲太尉。
entries.en: He was appointed grand commandant.
entries.literal: He was made grand commandant.

entries.zh: 慎自恨久爲將，遂託老耄。
entries.en: Fan Shen had wearied of life in the field and pleaded senility to step down.
entries.literal: Fan Shen himself resented having long been a general and therefore pleaded extreme old age.

entries.zh: 軍士戀之，舉營爲之隕涕。
entries.en: The troops loved him; an entire camp shed tears at his departure.
entries.literal: The soldiers were attached to him; the whole camp wept tears for him.

entries.zh: 鳳凰三年卒，子耀嗣。
entries.en: He died in 274; his son Fan Yao inherited his rank.
entries.literal: He died in the third year of Fenghuang; his son Yao succeeded.

entries.zh: 玄，丹楊人。
entries.en: Diao Xuan was from Danyang.
entries.literal: Xuan was a man of Danyang.

entries.zh: 衜，南陽人。
entries.en: Yang Dao came from Nanyang.
entries.literal: Dao was a man of Nanyang.

entries.zh: 《吳書》曰：衜初爲中庶子，年二十。
entries.en: The Wu shu records that Yang Dao began as a palace attendant at the age of twenty.
entries.literal: The Wu shu states: Dao at first was a palace attendant; he was twenty years of age.

entries.zh: 時廷尉監隱蕃交結豪傑，自衞將軍全琮等皆傾心敬待，惟衜及宣詔郎豫章楊迪拒絕不與通，時人咸怪之。
entries.en: The court jailer Yin Fan was courting powerful men, and even Guard General Quan Zong courted his favor—yet Yang Dao and the edict herald Yang Di of Yuzhang would have nothing to do with him, which contemporaries found inexplicable.
entries.literal: At that time the jail overseer of the commandant of justice, Yin Fan, cultivated ties with bold spirits; from Guard General Quan Zong downward all inclined their hearts and treated him with respect; only Dao and the edict announcer of Yuzhang, Yang Di, refused and would not associate with him; people of the time all thought it strange.

entries.zh: 而蕃後叛逆，衆乃服之。
entries.en: When Yin Fan later turned traitor, everyone conceded that Yang Dao and Yang Di had been right.
entries.literal: But when Fan later rebelled, the crowd then admired them.

entries.zh: 《江表傳》曰：登使侍中胡綜作賔友目曰：「英才卓越，超踰倫匹，則諸葛恪。
entries.en: The Jiangbiao zhuan says Sun Deng had Palace Attendant Hu Zong draft appraisals of his companions: "For brilliance that towers above ordinary men, there is Zhuge Ke.
entries.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Deng ordered Palace Attendant Hu Zong to compose a catalogue of guests and companions, saying: "In outstanding talent that transcends the common run, surpassing peers, there is Zhuge Ke.

entries.zh: 精識時機，達幽究微，則顧譚。
entries.en: For sharp judgment of timing and insight into hidden motives, there is Gu Tan.
entries.literal: In keen perception of the opportune moment, penetrating the obscure and investigating the subtle, there is Gu Tan.

entries.zh: 凝辨宏達，言能釋結，則謝景。
entries.en: For steady judgment, breadth of mind, and words that untangle dilemmas, there is Xie Jing.
entries.literal: In concentrated discernment and breadth of vision, in speech able to unravel knots, there is Xie Jing.

entries.zh: 究學甄微，游夏同科，則范慎。」
entries.en: For scholarship that sifts the fine points and rivals the disciples You and Xia, there is Fan Shen."
entries.literal: In exhaustive study and discrimination of the subtle, on a par with You and Xia, there is Fan Shen."

entries.zh: 衜乃私駁綜曰：「元遜才而疏，子嘿精而狠，叔發辯而浮，孝敬深而狹。」
entries.en: Yang Dao quietly contradicted Hu Zong: "Zhuge Ke is gifted but careless; Gu Tan is sharp but ruthless; Xie Jing is fluent but shallow; Fan Shen is deep but narrow-minded."
entries.literal: Dao then privately refuted Zong, saying: "Yuanxun has talent but is careless; Zimo is acute but harsh; Shufa is eloquent but shallow; Xiaojing is profound but narrow."

entries.zh: 所言皆有指趣。
entries.en: Each remark had a clear point behind it.
entries.literal: What he said all had pointed significance.

entries.zh: 而衜卒以此言見咎，不爲恪等所親。
entries.en: Those words earned Yang Dao resentment, and Zhuge Ke's circle never warmed to him.
entries.literal: But Dao in the end because of these words incurred blame and was not treated as intimate by Ke and the others.

entries.zh: 後四人皆敗，吳人謂衜之言有徵。
entries.en: When all four later fell, Wu observers said Yang Dao's verdicts had proved prophetic.
entries.literal: Later when the four men all met ruin, the people of Wu said Dao's words had been verified.

entries.zh: 位至桂陽太守，卒。〉
entries.en: He rose to prefect of Guiyang and died there.〉
entries.literal: He rose to the rank of administrator of Guiyang and died.〉

entries.zh: 赤烏二年，濬卒，子翥嗣。
entries.en: Pan Jun died in the second year of Chiwu (239), and his son Pan Zhu inherited his title.
entries.literal: In the second year of Chiwu, Jun died; his son Zhu succeeded.

entries.zh: 濬女配建昌侯孫慮。
entries.en: Pan Jun's daughter was married to Sun Lü, the marquis of Jianchang.
entries.literal: Jun's daughter was matched in marriage to Sun Lü, marquis of Jianchang.

entries.zh: 〈吴书曰：翥字文龙，拜骑都尉，后代领兵，早卒。
entries.en: 〈The Book of Wu records that Pan Zhu, courtesy name Wenlong, became chief of cavalry, later took over his father's command, and died young.
entries.literal: 〈The Book of Wu states: Zhu, courtesy name Wenlong, was appointed chief of cavalry; afterward he took acting command of troops and died early.

entries.zh: 翥弟祕，权以姊陈氏女妻之，调湘乡令。
entries.en: His younger brother Pan Mi was given a wife from the Chen family on Sun Quan's sister's side and was posted magistrate of Xiangxiang.
entries.literal: Zhu's younger brother Mi—Quan took the daughter of the Chen clan, his elder sister's family, as wife for him, and transferred him to be magistrate of Xiangxiang.

entries.zh: 《襄阳记》曰：襄阳习温为荆州大公平。
entries.en: The Xiangyang ji notes that Xi Wen of Xiangyang served as the great impartial selector for Jing Province.
entries.literal: The Xiangyang ji states: Xi Wen of Xiangyang was great impartial selector of Jing Province.

entries.zh: 大公平，今之州都。
entries.en: That office corresponds to what is now called the provincial marshal.
entries.literal: Great impartial selector is today's provincial marshal.

entries.zh: 祕过辞於温，问曰：「先君昔曰君侯当为州里议主，今果如其言，不审州里谁当复相代者？」
entries.en: Pan Mi called on Xi Wen to bid farewell and asked, "My father once predicted you would become the province's chief arbiter, and he was right—who do you think should succeed you in that role?"
entries.literal: Mi passed by to take leave of Wen and asked, saying: "My late father once said that you, lord, ought to be chief arbiter for the province; now it has indeed been as his words—may I ask who in the province ought next to succeed one another in replacing?"

entries.zh: 温曰：「无过於君也。」
entries.en: No one is better suited than yourself," Xi Wen replied.
entries.literal: Wen said: "None surpasses you."

entries.zh: 后祕为尚书僕射，代温为公平，甚得州里之誉。〉
entries.en: Pan Mi later rose to vice director of the secretariat, succeeded Xi Wen as impartial selector, and won wide acclaim across the province.
entries.literal: Later Mi became vice director of the secretariat, replaced Wen as impartial selector, and greatly obtained the praise of the province.

entries.zh: 陸凱字敬風，吳郡吳人，丞相遜族子也。
entries.en: Lu Kai, styled Jingfeng, came from Wu in Wu commandery, a kinsman of Chancellor Lu Xun.
entries.literal: Lu Kai, courtesy name Jingfeng, was a man of Wu in Wu commandery, a clansman of Chancellor Xun.

entries.zh: 黃武初為永興、諸暨長，所在有治跡，拜建武都尉，領兵。
entries.en: Early in Huangwu he governed Yongxing and Zhuji with a clean record, became Commandant Who Establishes Martiality, and took command of troops.
entries.literal: Early in Huangwu he served as magistrate of Yongxing and Zhuji; wherever he went he left traces of good governance. He was appointed Commandant Who Establishes Martiality and led troops.

entries.zh: 雖統軍眾，手不釋書。
entries.en: Even while commanding armies he never laid books aside.
entries.literal: Though he commanded armies, he never put books aside.

entries.zh: 好《太玄》，論演其意，以筮輒驗。
entries.en: He loved the Taixuan, worked out its doctrines, and his divinations always proved true.
entries.literal: He loved the Taixuan, elaborated its meaning, and whenever he divined by it the results proved true.

entries.zh: 赤烏中，除儋耳太守，討朱崖，斬獲有功，遷為建武校尉。
entries.en: In the Chiwu era he became administrator of Dan'er, campaigned against Zhuya with success, and was promoted to Colonel Who Establishes Martiality.
entries.literal: In Chiwu he was appointed Administrator of Dan'er, campaigned against Zhuya, and for beheading and capture of the enemy was rewarded; he was transferred to Colonel Who Establishes Martiality.

entries.zh: 五鳳二年255年，討山賊陳毖於零陵。
entries.en: In Wufeng 2 (255) he attacked the mountain bandit Chen Bi in Lingling.
entries.literal: In the second year of Wufeng, 255 CE, he campaigned against the mountain bandit Chen Bi in Lingling.

entries.zh: 斬毖克捷，拜巴丘督、偏將軍，封都鄉侯，轉為武昌右部督。
entries.en: He killed Chen Bi in victory, became commander at Baqiu and major general, was enfeoffed as village marquis of Du, and transferred to colonel of the right division at Wuchang.
entries.literal: He beheaded Bi with success, was appointed Commander at Baqiu and Major General, enfeoffed as Village Marquis of Du, and transferred to colonel of the right division at Wuchang.

entries.zh: 與諸將共赴壽春；
entries.en: He marched with other generals to Shouchun;
entries.literal: Together with other generals he went to Shouchun;

entries.zh: 還，累遷蕩魏、綏遠將軍。
entries.en: On return he was promoted repeatedly to General Who Quells Wei and General Who Pacifies the Far.
entries.literal: On return he was promoted repeatedly to General Who Quells Wei and General Who Pacifies the Far.

entries.zh: 孫休即位，拜征北將軍，假節領豫州牧。
entries.en: When Sun Xiu succeeded, Lu Kai was made General Who Conquers the North with acting authority as governor of Yu Province.
entries.literal: When Sun Xiu took the throne, Kai was appointed General Who Conquers the North with acting credentials as Governor of Yu Province.

entries.zh: 孫皓立，遷鎮西大將軍，都督巴丘，領荊州牧，進封嘉興侯。
entries.en: When Sun Hao took the throne, Lu Kai became Grand General Who Guards the West, supervised Baqiu as governor of Jing Province, and was advanced to marquis of Jiaxing.
entries.literal: When Sun Hao succeeded, he was transferred to Grand General Who Guards the West, supervising Baqiu as Governor of Jing Province, and advanced to Marquis of Jiaxing.

entries.zh: 孫皓與晉平，使者丁忠自北還，說皓弋陽可襲，凱諫止，語在《皓傳》。
entries.en: When Sun Hao made peace with Jin, the envoy Ding Zhong returned from the north urging a raid on Yiyang; Lu Kai dissuaded him—the account is in Sun Hao's biography.
entries.literal: When Sun Hao made peace with Jin, the envoy Ding Zhong returned from the north and urged Hao to raid Yiyang; Kai remonstrated and stopped it—the account is in the biography of Hao.

entries.zh: 寶鼎元年，遷左丞相。
entries.en: In Baoding 1 he was transferred to left chancellor.
entries.literal: In the first year of Baoding he was transferred to Left Chancellor.

entries.zh: 臣聞五音令人耳不聰，五色令人目不明，此無益於政，有損於事者也。
entries.en: The classics warn that music dulls the ear and pigments dim the eye; they bring no profit to government, only injury.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that the five sounds make a man's ears not sharp, the five colors make a man's eyes not clear—this is of no benefit to government and has harm for affairs.

entries.zh: 自昔先帝時，後宮列女，及諸織絡，數不滿百，米有畜積，貨財有餘。
entries.en: Under the late emperor the inner palace and weaving halls together held fewer than a hundred women, yet the granaries stayed full and the treasury ran a surplus.
entries.literal: In former times under the late emperor, the palace ladies and all the weaving girls did not number a full hundred; grain had accumulation, goods and wealth were in surplus.

entries.zh: 先帝崩後，幼、景在位，更改奢侈，不蹈先跡。
entries.en: After his death the Young and Jing emperors turned to extravagance and abandoned his frugal example.
entries.literal: After the late emperor's passing, during the reigns of the Young Lord and Jing, they altered toward extravagance and did not tread in the tracks of the former.

entries.zh: 伏聞織絡及諸徒坐，乃有千數，計其所長，不足為國財。
entries.en: I am told the weaving sheds and penal workshops now hold more than a thousand souls, yet their output hardly counts as national income.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that the weaving girls and all those sitting in convict labor now number in the thousands; reckoning what they produce, it is not enough to be wealth for the state.

entries.zh: 然坐食宮廩，歲歲相承，此為無益。
entries.en: They simply consume the palace grain year after year, to no good purpose.
entries.literal: Yet they sit and eat the palace granaries, year after year continuing one another—this is without benefit.

entries.zh: 願陛下料出賦嫁，給與無妻者。
entries.en: Release surplus palace women to wed men who have no wives.
entries.literal: Your servant prays Your Majesty will select out those fit for marriage and bestow them on men without wives.

entries.zh: 如此，上應天心，下合地意，天下幸甚。
entries.en: Heaven will approve, earth will consent, and the realm will be the better for it.
entries.literal: If it is thus, above it will answer the mind of Heaven, below it will match the intent of Earth—great fortune for All-under-Heaven.

entries.zh: 初，皓常銜凱數犯顏忤旨，加何定譖構非-，既以重臣，難繩以法，又陸抗時為大將在疆場，故以計容忍。
entries.en: At first Sun Hao resented Lu Kai for repeatedly speaking bluntly and defying his will, and He Ding piled on slander. Because Kai was a senior minister, Hao could not easily punish him by law; Lu Kang still commanded on the frontier, so Hao endured it by policy.
entries.literal: At first Hao continually harbored resentment because Kai repeatedly offended him and defied his will; moreover He Ding slandered and fabricated charges against him. Since Kai was a high minister, Hao could not easily punish him by law; furthermore Lu Kang then served as Grand General on the frontier, so by policy Hao endured it.

entries.zh: 抗卒後，竟徙凱家於建安。
entries.en: After Lu Kang died, Hao at last moved Lu Kai's household to Jian'an.
entries.literal: After Kang died, Hao at last moved Kai's household to Jian'an.

entries.zh: 或曰寶鼎元年十二月，凱與大司馬丁奉、御史大夫丁固謀，因皓謁廟，欲廢皓立孫休子。
entries.en: Some say that in the twelfth month of Baoding 1 Lu Kai plotted with Grand Marshal Ding Feng and Censor-in-chief Ding Gu to use Sun Hao's temple visit to depose him and install Sun Xiu's son.
entries.literal: Some say in the twelfth month of Baoding 1 Kai plotted with Grand Marshal Ding Feng and Censor-in-chief Ding Gu, taking advantage of Hao's temple visit, to depose Hao and install Sun Xiu's son.

entries.zh: 時左將軍留平領兵先驅，故密語平，平拒而不許，誓以不洩，是以所圖不果。
entries.en: Left General Liu Ping then led the vanguard, so they confided in him; Ping refused and swore not to reveal the plot, and the scheme failed.
entries.literal: At that time Left General Liu Ping led troops as vanguard, so they secretly spoke to Ping; Ping refused and would not assent, swearing not to leak the matter—therefore the plot failed.

entries.zh: 太史郎陳苗奏皓久陰不雨，風氣回逆，將有陰謀，皓深警懼雲。
entries.en: Astronomer Chen Miao reported that Sun Hao's long drought and contrary winds foretold a secret plot, and Sun Hao was deeply alarmed.
entries.literal: Astronomer Chen Miao memorialized that Hao had long lacked rain and winds ran contrary—there would be a secret plot; Hao was deeply alarmed and afraid.

entries.zh: 《吴录》曰：旧拜庙，选兼大将军领三千兵为卫，凯欲因此兵以图之，令选曹白用丁奉。
entries.en: The Wu Lu states: On old temple visits an acting grand general with three thousand troops served as escort; Lu Kai meant to use those troops for the plot and had the selection bureau propose Ding Feng.
entries.literal: The Wu Lu states: When paying temple visits in old practice, they selected an acting Grand General with three thousand troops as escort; Kai wished to use those troops for the plot and had the selection bureau report appointing Ding Feng.

entries.zh: 皓偶不欲，曰：「更选。」
entries.en: Sun Hao happened to refuse and said, "Choose someone else."
entries.literal: Hao happened not to want this and said, "Choose someone else."

entries.zh: 凯令执据，虽蹔兼，然宜得其人。
entries.en: Lu Kai pressed his case; though Feng was temporarily appointed acting commander, the right man still had to be found.
entries.literal: Kai pressed his grounds; though Feng was temporarily appointed acting commander, the right man ought to be found.

entries.zh: 皓曰：「用留平。」
entries.en: Sun Hao said, "Use Liu Ping."
entries.literal: Hao said, "Use Liu Ping."

entries.zh: 凯令其子祎谋语平。
entries.en: Lu Kai had his son Lu Yi plan to speak with Liu Ping.
entries.literal: Kai had his son Yi plan to speak with Ping.

entries.zh: 平素与丁奉有隙，祎未及得宣凯旨，平语祎曰：「闻野猪入丁奉营，此凶徵也。」
entries.en: Ping had long been at odds with Ding Feng; before Yi could deliver Lu Kai's message, Ping told him, "I hear a wild boar entered Ding Feng's camp—a bad omen."
entries.literal: Ping had long been at odds with Ding Feng; Yi had not yet delivered Kai's message when Ping told Yi, "I hear a wild boar entered Ding Feng's camp—this is an ill omen."

entries.zh: 有喜色。
entries.en: He looked pleased.
entries.literal: He wore a look of pleasure.

entries.zh: 祎乃不敢言，还，因具启凯，故辍止。
entries.en: Lu Yi dared not speak further, returned, reported everything to Lu Kai, and the plot was abandoned.
entries.literal: Yi then dared not speak, returned, and fully reported to Kai, so the scheme was stopped.

entries.zh: 臣聞有國以賢為本，夏殺龍逢，殷獲伊摯。
entries.en: They say a state stands on worthy men: Xia slew Long Pang, yet Yin won Yi Yin.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that a state takes worth as its root: Xia killed Longpang, Yin obtained Yi Zhi.

entries.zh: 斯前世之明效，今日之師表也。
entries.en: That is the ancient lesson and our mirror today.
entries.literal: This is the clear effect of former generations, the model for today.

entries.zh: 中常侍王蕃黃中通理，處朝忠謇，斯社稷之重鎮，大吳之龍逢也，而陛下忿其苦辭，惡其直對，梟之殿堂，屍骸暴棄。
entries.en: Wang Fan, the palace attendant, was a man of inner integrity and clear judgment, loyal and blunt in council—the very pillar of Wu, your Long Pang—yet you resented his plain speech, loathed his candor, had him executed in open court, and left his body unburied.
entries.literal: The palace attendant Wang Fan was yellow at the center and comprehended principle; in court he was loyal and outspoken—he was the heavy bulwark of the altars of soil and grain, the Long Pang of great Wu; yet Your Majesty resented his bitter words, hated his straight replies, displayed him in the hall, and his corpse was cast aside exposed.

entries.zh: 邦內傷心，有識悲悼，咸以吳國夫差復存，先帝親賢，陛下反之，是陛下不遵先帝二也；
entries.en: The whole court grieved; men said King Fuchai of Wu had come again. The late emperor cherished worth; you do the opposite—this is the second way you abandon his model;
entries.literal: Within the state hearts were wounded, those with understanding mourned in grief; all thought that Wu's Fuchai had returned to life; the late emperor honored the worthy—Your Majesty does the opposite: this is the second instance of Your Majesty's not following the late emperor;

entries.zh: 今在所監司，民為煩猥，兼有內使，擾亂其中，一民十吏，何以堪命?昔景帝時，交阯反亂，實由茲起，是為遵景帝之闕，不遵先帝十七也；
entries.en: Local inspectors harrow the people, and palace agents stir trouble within—ten clerks for every household. How can the people endure? Jiaozhi rose under Emperor Jing for just such reasons. You copy Jing's error, not the late emperor's way—that is the seventeenth count.
entries.literal: Now the overseers in each place vex the people with fussiness, and moreover there are inner agents who throw them into confusion within—one people, ten clerks—how can they bear the mandate? In the time of Emperor Jing, Jiaozhi rebelled; truly it arose from this: this is following Emperor Jing's fault, not following the late emperor, seventeenth;

entries.zh: 潘濬字承明，武陵漢壽人也。
entries.en: Pan Jun, whose courtesy name was Chengming, came from Hanshou in Wuling commandery.
entries.literal: Pan Jun, courtesy name Chengming, was a man of Hanshou in Wuling.

entries.zh: 弱冠從宋仲子受學。
entries.en: While still in his early twenties he took instruction from Song Zhongzi.
entries.literal: At the capping age he studied under Song Zhongzi.

entries.zh: 〈吴书曰：濬为人聪察，对问有机理，山阳王粲见而贵异之。
entries.en: 〈The Book of Wu records that Pan Jun was sharp and observant, that his replies in conversation were always well ordered, and that Wang Can of Shanyang singled him out for special regard.
entries.literal: 〈The Book of Wu states: Jun was by nature keen and perceptive, and in answering questions he showed a clear pattern of reasoning; Wang Can of Shanyang saw him and honored him as extraordinary.

entries.zh: 由是知名，为郡功曹。〉
entries.en: He soon made a name for himself and was appointed merit clerk of the commandery.〉
entries.literal: By this he became known and was made merit clerk of the commandery.〉

entries.zh: 年未三十，荊州牧劉表辟為部江夏從事。
entries.en: Before he turned thirty, Governor Liu Biao of Jing Province recruited him as an assistant clerk attached to the Jiangxia section of headquarters.
entries.literal: Before he had reached thirty, the Governor of Jing Province, Liu Biao, summoned him and appointed him assistant clerk for Jiangxia in the headquarters staff.

entries.zh: 時沙羨長贓穢不脩，濬按殺之，一郡震竦。
entries.en: The magistrate of Shaxi was lining his pockets and neglecting his duty; Pan Jun had him tried and put to death, and the entire commandery stood in awe.
entries.literal: At that time the magistrate of Shaxi was corrupt and did not regulate himself; Jun investigated and executed him, and the whole commandery trembled with awe.

entries.zh: 後為湘鄉令，治甚有名。
entries.en: He was later named magistrate of Xiangxiang and earned wide renown for how he ran the county.
entries.literal: Later he became magistrate of Xiangxiang, and his administration was very celebrated.

entries.zh: 劉備領荊州，以濬為治中從事。
entries.en: When Liu Bei assumed authority over Jing Province, he made Pan Jun his administrative adjutant.
entries.literal: Liu Bei took charge of Jing Province and appointed Jun as administrative adjutant.

entries.zh: 備入蜀，留典州事。
entries.en: Liu Bei left him behind to manage provincial affairs when he marched into Shu.
entries.literal: When Bei entered Shu, he was left behind to supervise the affairs of the province.

entries.zh: 其一曰：“天綱弛絕，四海分崩，群生憔悴，士人播越，兵寇所加，邑無居民，風塵煙火，往往而處。
entries.en: The first begins: "The cosmic order has snapped; the realm is shattered; the people are worn thin and scholars wander homeless; where armies march, cities stand empty under a haze of war.
entries.literal: The first says: "Heaven's net hangs slack, the four seas split and crumble; the throng of creatures is withered, gentlemen are scattered; where arms and bandits strike, towns lack dwellers; wind-blown dust and smoke of war are the usual sights.

entries.zh: 自三代以來，大亂之極，未有若今時者也。
entries.en: Since the Three Dynasties there has been no chaos to match this age.
entries.literal: Since the Three Dynasties, at the extreme of great chaos, there has been none like the present time.

entries.zh: 臣質志薄，處時無方，繫於土壤，不能翻飛，遂為曹氏執事戎役。
entries.en: I, Wu Zhi, am a man of small ambition, pinned to the north with no way to fly free, and so I serve the Cao house in arms.
entries.literal: Your subject Zhi's aims are slight; placed in the times without method, tied to the soil, unable to soar aloft, thereupon for the Cao clan he holds office in military service.

entries.zh: 遠處河朔，天衢隔絕，雖望風慕義，思托大命，愧無因緣，得展其志。
entries.en: The imperial road is blocked to me on the northern plain; though I long to join your righteous cause, I have had no opening—until now.
entries.literal: Far removed on the northern He, the celestial thoroughfare is cut off; although I admire righteousness from afar and wish to entrust myself to the great mandate, I shamefully lack the connection to unfold my intent.

entries.zh: 每往來者，竊聽風化，伏知陛下齊德乾坤，同明日月，神武之姿，受之自然。
entries.en: From every traveler I glean news of your rule: you match heaven and earth in virtue, share light with the sun and moon, and your martial majesty is nature's own gift.
entries.literal: Whenever travelers come and go, I secretly listen to their tidings of custom; prostrate I know that Your Majesty matches virtue with Qian and Kun, shares brightness with sun and moon, and the bearing of divine martiality is received from nature.

entries.zh: 敷演皇極，流化萬里，自江以南，戶受覆燾。
entries.en: You extend the royal polestar; your civilizing sway runs ten thousand li; south of the river every hearth rests beneath your wing.
entries.literal: You spread the supreme pivot, your transforming influence flows ten thousand li; from south of the Yangzi every household receives your covering shade.

entries.zh: 英雄俊傑，上達之士，莫不心歌腹詠，樂在歸附者也。
entries.en: Every hero and man of note sings your praise in secret and yearns to come over.
entries.literal: Heroes and outstanding men, gentlemen who rise to eminence—none do not sing in heart and chant in belly, rejoicing to attach themselves.

entries.zh: 今年六月末，奉聞吉日，龍興踐阼，恢弘大繇，整理天綱，將使遺民，睹見定主。
entries.en: At the close of the sixth month I learned of your accession: the dragon has mounted the throne, widened the great design, and restored order so that lost folk may at last see their true sovereign.
entries.literal: This year at the end of the sixth month I heard the auspicious day: the dragon rose and ascended the throne, expanding the great plan, setting Heaven's net in order, about to let the surviving people behold a settled lord.

entries.zh: 營武王伐殷，殷氏倒戈；
entries.en: When King Wu marched on Shang, the Shang warriors lowered their blades;
entries.literal: When King Wu of Zhou campaigned against Yin, the Yin clan turned their spears;

entries.zh: 高祖誅項，四面楚歌。
entries.en: Gaozu struck down Xiang Yu while Chu songs rose on every side.
entries.literal: the High Ancestor executed Xiang Yu, and on four sides Chu songs arose.

entries.zh: 方之今日，未足以喻。
entries.en: Those old stories scarcely match the joy of your accession.
entries.literal: Compared to today, they are not enough to serve as likeness.

entries.zh: 臣質不勝吳天至願，謹遣所親同郡黃定恭行奉表，及托降叛，間關求達，其欲所陳，載列於左。”
entries.en: I cannot contain my longing for your mandate; I send my kinsman Huang Ding with this memorial, threading the border by devious routes—my full plea is set out below."
entries.literal: Your subject Zhi cannot overcome his utmost wish toward august Heaven; respectfully he dispatches his intimate, fellow townsman Huang Ding, reverently to present a memorial, and relying on the channel of surrender and rebellion, by perilous paths seeks to reach you—what he wishes to state is arrayed at left."

entries.zh: 二年，青州人隱蕃歸吳。
entries.en: In the second year of that era a Qingzhou adventurer named Yin Fan crossed over to Wu.
entries.literal: In the second year, a man of Qingzhou, Yin Fan, came over to Wu.

entries.zh: 上書曰：“臣聞紂為無道，微子先出。
entries.en: He presented a memorial: "I have heard that when Zhou was cruel, Weizi left the court first.
entries.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject has heard that Zhou was without the Way, and Weizi departed first.

entries.zh: 高祖寬明，陳平先入。
entries.en: When Gaozu showed clemency, Chen Ping was first through the gate.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor was magnanimous and clear-sighted, and Chen Ping entered first.

entries.zh: 臣年二十二，委棄封域，歸命有道，賴蒙天靈，得自全致。
entries.en: At twenty-two I abandoned my fief and came to a righteous sovereign; heaven spared me and I arrived intact.
entries.literal: Your subject, at age twenty-two, cast aside his enfeoffed domain, returned his mandate to the possessor of the Way, and relying on receiving Heaven's numinous favor, was able to preserve himself whole.

entries.zh: 臣至北有日，而主者同之降人，未見精別，使臣徽言妙旨，不得上達。
entries.en: I have been here for days, yet your clerks lump me with common deserters and will not carry my plea upward.
entries.literal: Your subject has been in the north some days, yet those in charge treat him like other defectors and have not discerned fine distinctions, so that your subject's subtle words and excellent points cannot ascend to be heard.

entries.zh: 於邑三歎，曷惟其已。
entries.en: I choke back sob after sob—there is no end to this grief.
entries.literal: I sigh thrice in anguish—how can it be stopped!

entries.zh: 謹詣闕拜章，乞蒙引見。”
entries.en: I therefore present myself at the gate with this memorial and beg for an audience."
entries.literal: Respectfully I have come to the palace gate to bow with a memorial, begging to receive a summons to audience."

entries.zh: 權即召入。
entries.en: Sun Quan had him brought in at once.
entries.literal: Quan immediately summoned him to enter.

entries.zh: 蕃謝答問，及陳時務，甚有辭觀。
entries.en: Yin Fan parried the emperor's questions and discoursed on policy with striking eloquence.
entries.literal: Fan gave thanks, answered questions, and set forth the affairs of the time—very fine in rhetorical display.

entries.zh: 綜時侍坐，權問何如。
entries.en: Hu Zong was present; Sun Quan asked his opinion of the man.
entries.literal: Zong at the time was in attendance at the sitting; Quan asked how he was.

entries.zh: 綜對曰："蕃上書，大語有似東方朔，巧捷詭辯有似彌衡。
entries.en: Hu Zong said, His memorial sounds like Dongfang Shuo at his broadest and like Mi Heng at his sharpest.
entries.literal: Zong replied: Fan's memorial—its grand language resembles Dongfang Shuo; its clever quickness and crafty disputation resembles Mi Heng.

entries.zh: 而才皆不及。
entries.en: But he is not their equal in genius.
entries.literal: Yet in talent he reaches neither."

entries.zh: "權又問可堪何官？
entries.en: The emperor asked what post might suit him.
entries.literal: Quan again asked what office he could bear.

entries.zh: 綜對曰："未可以治民，且試以都輦小職。
entries.en: Hu Zong answered, "Not yet a magistrate—give him a small post around the capital first."
entries.literal: Zong replied: "Not yet fit to govern the people—for now try him in a minor capital conveyance duty."

entries.zh: "權以蕃盛論刑獄，用為廷尉監。
entries.en: Because Yin Fan spoke well of criminal law, Sun Quan made him an assistant in the ministry of justice.
entries.literal: Quan, because Fan discoursed at length on penal cases, employed him as overseer of the commandant of justice.

entries.zh: 左將軍朱據、廷尉郝普稱蕃有王佐之才，普尤與之親善，常怨歎其屈。
entries.en: Zhu Ju, general of the left, and Hao Pu, chief justice, hailed him as ministerial timber; Hao Pu grew especially close and complained that such a man was underemployed.
entries.literal: General of the Left Zhu Ju and Commandant of Justice Hao Pu praised Fan as having the talent of a king's assistant; Pu especially was intimate and friendly with him, often resenting and sighing that he was wronged.

entries.zh: 後蕃謀叛，事覺伏誅，
entries.en: Later Yin Fan plotted treason; when it leaked he was put to death.
entries.literal: Later Fan plotted rebellion; when the affair was discovered he was executed.

entries.zh: 〈吴录曰：蕃有口才，魏明帝使诈叛如吴，令求作廷尉职，重案大臣以离间之。
entries.en: 〈The Wu Records say Cao Rui sent him south as a spy to angle for the post of commandant of justice and use reopened cases against high ministers to sow discord.
entries.literal: 〈The Wu lu states: Fan had rhetorical skill; Emperor Ming of Wei sent him feigning defection to Wu, ordering him to seek the office of commandant of justice and reopen weighty cases against great ministers to sow discord.

entries.zh: 既为廷尉监，众人以据、普与蕃亲善，常车马云集，宾客盈堂。
entries.en: Once he held that office, Zhu Ju and Hao Pu were seen at his door so often that rumor painted a conspiracy.
entries.literal: Once he became overseer of justice, the crowd, because Ju and Pu were intimate with Fan, constantly saw carriages and horses gather like clouds and guests fill the hall.

entries.zh: 及至事觉，蕃亡走，捕得，考问党与，蕃无所言。
entries.en: When the plot broke, Yin Fan ran, was caught, and under torture about accomplices said nothing.
entries.literal: When the affair was discovered, Fan fled; he was captured and examined on accomplices—Fan said nothing.

entries.zh: 吴主使将入，谓曰：“何乃以肌肉为人受毒乎？”
entries.en: Sun Quan sent an officer to ask why he would let his body absorb another man's torture.
entries.literal: The ruler of Wu sent a general in and said to him: "Why would you let your flesh take poison for another?"

entries.zh: 蕃曰：“孙君，丈夫图事，岂有无伴！
entries.en: Yin Fan replied, "My lord, a man who plays for high stakes always has partners.
entries.literal: Fan said: "Lord Sun, when a man plots great things, how can he lack companions!

entries.zh: 烈士死，不足相牵耳。”
entries.en: A man of honor may die; he will not drag others down with him."
entries.literal: When a resolute knight dies, it is not enough to drag others along."

entries.zh: 遂闭口而死。
entries.en: He shut his mouth and died.
entries.literal: Thereupon he closed his mouth and died.

entries.zh: 吴历曰：权问普：“卿前盛称蕃，又为之怨望朝廷，使蕃反叛，皆卿之由。”〉
entries.en: The Wu Calendar records Sun Quan confronting Hao Pu: "You heaped praise on Yin Fan and grumbled against the court until he rebelled—that fault is yours."
entries.literal: The Wu li states: Quan asked Pu: "You earlier lavishly praised Fan, and also on his behalf resented the court—making Fan rebel—all stems from you."

entries.zh: 普見責自殺。
entries.en: Hao Pu killed himself under the reproach.
entries.literal: When Pu saw he was blamed, he committed suicide.

entries.zh: 據禁止，歷時乃解。
entries.en: Zhu Ju was confined for a long stretch before he was cleared.
entries.literal: Ju was placed under confinement; only after a long time was it lifted.

entries.zh: 拜綜偏將軍，兼左執法，領辭訟。
entries.en: Hu Zong was promoted to lieutenant general, left law enforcer, and again put in charge of lawsuits.
entries.literal: Zong was appointed lieutenant general, concurrently left law enforcer, in charge of litigation.

entries.zh: 遼東之事，輔吳將軍張昭以諫權言辭切至，權亦大怒，其和協彼此，使之無隙，綜有力焉。
entries.en: When the Liaodong campaign drove Zhang Zhao, general who assists Wu, to remonstrate in blistering terms and Sun Quan raged, Hu Zong helped heal the rift between sovereign and chief counselor.
entries.literal: In the Liaodong affair, General Who Assists Wu Zhang Zhao in remonstrating with Quan used speech cutting and extreme; Quan also was greatly angry; that he reconciled and harmonized the two sides, causing them to have no rift—Zong had power therein.

entries.zh: 性嗜酒，酒後歡呼極意，或推引杯觴，搏擊左右。
entries.en: He loved wine; drunk, he would whoop with delight, shove the cups about, and even cuff his neighbors.
entries.literal: By nature he loved wine; after wine he shouted for joy to the utmost, sometimes pushing and pulling cups and goblets, striking those to his left and right.

entries.zh: 權愛其才，弗之責也。
entries.en: Sun Quan prized his gifts and overlooked the excess.
entries.literal: Quan loved his talent and did not blame him for it.

entries.zh: 其二曰：“昔伊尹去夏人商，陳平委楚歸漢，書功竹帛，遺名陵後世，世主不謂之背誕者，以為知天命也。
entries.en: The second reads: "Long ago Yi Yin left Xia for Shang and Chen Ping abandoned Chu for Han; their deeds were recorded on bamboo and silk and their names endure for posterity—rulers did not call them traitors, but men who read Heaven's mandate.
entries.literal: The second says: "In olden days Yi Yin left Xia for Shang, and Chen Ping abandoned Chu for Han; their merits were written on bamboo and silk and their names left mounds for later ages—sovereigns did not call them traitorous, deeming them men who knew Heaven's mandate.

entries.zh: 臣昔為曹氏所見交接，外托群臣，內如骨肉，恩義綢繆，有合無離，遂受偏方之任，總河北之軍。
entries.en: I was once taken in by the Cao house—outwardly a minister, inwardly treated like kin; our bond was close and unbroken, and I received a frontier command over the Hebei armies.
entries.literal: Your subject was once received and connected by the Cao clan—outwardly among ministers, inwardly like flesh and bone; grace and duty were close-woven, joined without parting—thereupon he received a regional command and oversaw the armies north of the He.

entries.zh: 當此之時，志望高大，永與曹氏同死懼生。
entries.en: In those days my ambition was high; I meant to live and die with the Cao house.
entries.literal: At that time his aims were lofty; he would forever share death and fear life with the Cao clan.

entries.zh: 惟恐功之不建，事之不成耳。
entries.en: I feared only that our work would fail and our cause come to nothing.
entries.literal: He only feared that merit would not be established and affairs would not succeed.

entries.zh: 及曹氏之亡，後嗣繼位，幼沖統政，讒言彌興。
entries.en: After Cao Cao's death the heir took the throne—a child in power—and slander multiplied.
entries.literal: When the Cao clan's founder died, the successor ascended, a youth holding government; slanderous words spread ever more.

entries.zh: 同儕者以勢相害，異趣者得間其言，而臣受性簡略，素不下人，視彼數子，意實迫之，此亦臣之過也。
entries.en: Colleagues preyed on one another; rivals seized on their talk; and I, blunt by nature and never humble before others, had pressed those men hard—this too was my fault.
entries.literal: Peers harmed one another by power; those of different bent found openings in their words; yet your subject by nature is plain and brief, never deferring to others—looking on those several men, he truly pressed them—this too is your subject's fault.

entries.zh: 遂為邪議所見構會，招至猜疑，誣臣欲叛。
entries.en: Evil counsel framed me, suspicion followed, and I was accused of plotting rebellion.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was framed by evil talk and brought under suspicion, falsely accused of wishing to rebel.

entries.zh: 雖識真者保明其心，世亂讒勝，余嫌猶在，常懼一旦橫受無辜，憂心孔疚，如覆冰炭。
