Wan Yu argued that intimate inner offices should employ good men, so Sun Hao ordered the offices to seek loyal and incorrupt gentlemen and chose Lou Xuan as Colonel Garrisoning the Forbidden Interior below the palace, in charge of affairs within the halls. Ranking with the nine ministers, Lou Xuan carried the blade as an imperial guard, corrected himself and led the others, acted according to law, and answered sharply and directly. He repeatedly crossed Hao’s wishes and gradually drew blame and anger.
entries.literal: By old practice those in charge within the forbidden precincts always used intimate men for the post; Yu presented that intimate near offices ought to employ good men; Hao thereupon ordered the responsible offices to seek loyal and pure gentlemen to meet that selection, and so used Xuan as palace-base colonel who garrisons the forbidden interior, in charge of hall affairs—Xuan, ranking with the nine ministers, bore the blade as bodyguard, corrected his person and led the host, acted by the law, answered cuttingly and straight, repeatedly went against Hao's intent, and gradually met blame and anger.

entries.zh: 後人誣白玄與賀邵相逢，駐共耳語大笑，謗訕政事，遂被詔詰責，送付廣州。
entries.en: Later a informer claimed he had stopped in the road with He Shao, whispered and laughed, and mocked policy; an edict condemned him and he was banished to Guangzhou.
entries.literal: Afterward someone falsely reported that Xuan, meeting He Shao, halted and together whispered in the ear and laughed greatly, slandering and mocking government affairs; thereupon he received an edict of interrogation and blame and was sent off to Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 丞相陸凱上疏曰："常侍王蕃黃中通理，知天知物，處朝忠蹇，斯社稷之重鎮，大吳之龍逢也。
entries.en: Lu Kai memorialized: Wang Fan is the inner integrity and clear judgment of the court—Wu's pillar, your Long Pang.
entries.literal: Chancellor Lu Kai submitted a memorial saying: Regular attendant Wang Fan is yellow within and comprehends principle; he knows Heaven and knows things; in court he is loyal and outspoken—he is the heavy bulwark of the altars of soil and grain, the Long Pang of great Wu.

entries.zh: 昔事景皇，納言左右，景皇欽嘉，歎為異倫。
entries.en: He served Emperor Jing as a candid advisor and won that emperor's open admiration.
entries.literal: In former times he served Emperor Jing, speaking out at the ruler's side; Emperor Jing admired and praised him, sighing that he was of a different class.

entries.zh: 而陛下忿其苦辭，惡其直對，梟之殿堂，屍骸暴棄，邦內傷心，有識悲悼。
entries.en: Yet you resented his blunt speech, executed him in open court, and left his body unburied—the whole court grieves, every thoughtful man mourns.
entries.literal: Yet Your Majesty resented his bitter words, hated his straight replies, displayed him in the hall, and his corpse was cast aside exposed—within the state hearts are wounded, those with understanding mourn in grief.

entries.zh: "其痛蕃如此。
entries.en: Such was Lu Kai's grief for Wang Fan.
entries.literal: Thus he grieved for Fan to this degree.

entries.zh: 蕃死時年三十九，皓徙蕃家屬廣州。
entries.en: Wang Fan died at thirty-nine; Sun Hao banished his kin to Guangzhou.
entries.literal: When Fan died he was thirty-nine years old; Hao moved Fan's family dependants to Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 二弟著、延皆作佳器，郭馬起事，不為馬用，見害。
entries.en: His brothers Wang Zhu and Wang Yan were both promising men; when Guo Ma rose in revolt they refused to serve him and were put to death.
entries.literal: His two younger brothers Zhu and Yan were both fine vessels; when Guo Ma raised an affair, they would not serve Ma and were killed.

entries.zh: 皓話玄名聲，復徙玄及子據，付交阯將張奕，使以戰自效，陰別敕奕令殺之。
entries.en: Sun Hao, resenting Lou Xuan's reputation, again transferred Lou Xuan and his son Lou Ju, handing them to General Zhang Yi in Jiaozhi with orders to prove themselves in battle, while secretly instructing Zhang Yi to kill them.
entries.literal: Hao took account of Xuan's reputation, again transferred Xuan and his son Ju, handed them to Jiao general Zhang Yi, ordered them to prove themselves in battle, and secretly issued a separate edict to Yi ordering him to kill them.

entries.zh: 據到交阯，病死。
entries.en: Lou Ju died of illness on reaching Jiaozhi.
entries.literal: When Ju reached Jiaozhi, he died of illness.

entries.zh: 玄一身隨亦討賊，持刀步涉，見亦輒拜，亦未忍殺。
entries.en: Lou Xuan alone followed Zhang Yi against rebels, sword in hand, wading on foot; whenever he met Zhang Yi he bowed deeply, and Zhang could not bring himself to strike.
entries.literal: Xuan alone followed Yi in campaigning against bandits, carrying a blade and wading on foot; when he saw Yi he always bowed, and Yi could not bear to kill.

entries.zh: 會亦暴卒，玄殯斂亦，於器中見敕書，還便自殺。
entries.en: When Zhang Yi died suddenly, Lou Xuan prepared his body for burial and found the secret order in the baggage; he returned and took his own life.
entries.literal: When Yi also suddenly died, Xuan encoffined Yi; in the coffin gear he saw the secret edict, and on return then killed himself.

entries.zh: 〈江表傳曰：皓遣将张奕追赐玄鸩，奕以玄贤者，不忍即宣诏致药，玄阴知之，谓奕曰：「当早告玄，玄何惜邪？」
entries.en: 〈The Jiangbiao zhuan says Sun Hao sent Zhang Yi after Lou Xuan with poison; Zhang, honoring Lou as a worthy, hesitated to announce the edict; Lou guessed the truth and told him, "Tell me plainly—I do not cling to life."
entries.literal: 〈The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Hao sent general Zhang Yi to pursue and bestow poison on Xuan; Yi, because Xuan was a worthy man, could not bear immediately to proclaim the edict and deliver the drug; Xuan secretly knew it and said to Yi: "You ought early to tell Xuan—what would Xuan grudge?"

entries.zh: 即服药死。
entries.en: He drank the poison at once.
entries.literal: Immediately he took the drug and died.

entries.zh: 臣松之以玄之清高，必不以安危易操，无缘骤拜张奕，以亏其节。
entries.en: Pei Songzhi doubts that so principled a man would suddenly bow repeatedly to Zhang Yi and stain his honor.
entries.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that with Xuan's purity and elevation he surely would not for safety or peril alter his integrity, and had no reason suddenly to bow to Zhang Yi and impair his integrity.

entries.zh: 且祸机既发，岂百拜所免？
entries.en: Nor would a hundred bows avert a plot already sprung.
entries.literal: Moreover once the trap of disaster had sprung, how could a hundred bows avoid it?

entries.zh: 江表传所言，於理为长。〉
entries.en: The Jiangbiao zhuan version is the more plausible.
entries.literal: What the Jiangbiao zhuan says is superior in accord with principle.

entries.zh: 賀邵字興伯，會稽山陰人也，
entries.en: He Shao, courtesy name Xingbo, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji
entries.literal: He Shao, courtesy name Xingbo, was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji,

entries.zh: 〈吴书曰：邵，贺齐之孙，景之子。〉
entries.en: 〈The Book of Wu identifies him as He Qi's grandson and He Jing's son.〉
entries.literal: 〈The Book of Wu states: Shao was grandson of He Qi, son of Jing.〉

entries.zh: 孫休即位，從中郎為散騎中常侍，出為吳郡太守。
entries.en: When Sun Xiu took the throne he rose from gentleman of the palace to attendant at ease and regular palace attendant, then became grand administrator of Wu.
entries.literal: When Sun Xiu ascended the throne, he went from gentleman of the palace to attendant at ease and regular palace attendant, and went out as grand administrator of Wu commandery.

entries.zh: 孫皓時，入為左典軍，遷中書令，領太子太傅。
entries.en: Under Sun Hao he became left army supervisor, then director of the secretariat, while serving as grand tutor to the heir apparent.
entries.literal: In Sun Hao's time he entered as left army supervisor, was transferred to director of the secretariat, and concurrently held grand tutor to the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 臣聞興國之君樂聞其過，荒亂之主樂聞其譽。
entries.en: A rising king loves to hear his faults; a doomed king loves praise.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that the lord who raises a state delights to hear his faults, while the lord of wasteland and chaos delights to hear his praise.

entries.zh: 聞其過者過日消而福臻，聞其譽者譽日損而禍至。
entries.en: Faults heard shrink and fortune grows; praise heard swells and calamity nears.
entries.literal: He who hears his faults—faults daily diminish and blessing arrives; he who hears his praise—praise daily shrinks and disaster comes.

entries.zh: 是以古之人君，捐讓以進賢，虛己以求過，譬天位於乘□，以虎尾為警戒。
entries.en: The ancients yielded to bring forward talent and took the throne as riding rotten wood beside a tiger's tail.
entries.literal: Therefore the lords of old yielded place to advance the worthy, emptied themselves to seek faults, likened the heavenly seat to riding a rotten log, and took the tiger's tail as warning.

entries.zh: 至於陛下，嚴刑法以禁直辭，黜善士以逆諫臣，眩耀毀譽之實，沉淪近習之言。
entries.en: You silence candor with cruel law, exile good men who remonstrate, chase gossip, and drown in favorites' whispers.
entries.literal: As for Your Majesty, you use harsh punishments to forbid straight speech, dismiss good gentlemen to reject remonstrating ministers, dazzle yourself with the reality of slander and praise, and sink in the words of those near at hand.

entries.zh: 昔高宗思佐，夢寐得賢，而陛下求之如忘，忽之如遺。
entries.en: Gaozong dreamed his ministers; you forget yours and toss them aside.
entries.literal: In olden times Gaozong thought on helpers and in dream and sleep obtained the worthy; Your Majesty seeks them as if forgotten, neglects them as if cast away.

entries.zh: 故常侍王蕃忠恪在公，才任輔弼，以醉酒之間加之大戮。
entries.en: Wang Fan was fit to be your pillar—you slew him for a drunken slip.
entries.literal: Therefore regular attendant Wang Fan was loyal and careful in public service, his talent fit to assist and guide—over drunkenness in a feast you added the great execution.

entries.zh: 近鴻臚葛奚，先帝舊臣，偶有逆迕，昏醉之言耳，三爵之後，禮所不諱，陛下猥發雷霆，謂之輕慢，飲之醇酒，中毒隕命。
entries.en: Ge Xi, an elder statesman, misspoke while drunk—rites forgive what follows three cups—yet you called it lese-majesty, forced strong wine on him, and he died of poison.
entries.literal: Recently grand herald Ge Xi, an old minister of the late emperor, once by chance was contrary and disobedient—it was words of muddled drunkenness; after three goblets, what rites do not excuse—Your Majesty rashly loosed thunder, calling it slighting and irreverent, made him drink strong wine, and he was poisoned and lost his life.

entries.zh: 自是之後，海內悼心，朝臣失圖，仕者以退為幸，居者以出為福，誠非所以保光洪緒，臣隆道化也。
entries.en: Officials now count leaving office as luck and staying home as blessing—no way to preserve the dynasty or spread moral rule.
entries.literal: From this time within the seas mourn in heart, court ministers lose their bearings; those in office take retirement as fortune, those at home take going out as blessing—this is truly not the means to preserve the bright great line and extend the transforming Way.

entries.zh: 書奏，皓深恨之。
entries.en: Sun Hao read the memorial and nursed a deep grudge.
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Hao deeply hated him.

entries.zh: 邵奉公貞正，親近所憚。
entries.en: He Shao was incorrupt and upright—the emperor's favorites feared him.
entries.literal: Shao served the public with integrity and uprightness; those intimate with the ruler feared him.

entries.zh: 乃共譖邵與樓玄謗毀國事，俱被詰責。
entries.en: They framed He Shao and Lou Xuan for defaming the state; both were censured.
entries.literal: Thereupon they jointly slandered Shao and Lou Xuan as slandering and ruining state affairs; both received edict interrogation and blame.

entries.zh: 玄見送南州，邵原復職。
entries.en: Lou Xuan went south while He Shao was briefly restored.
entries.literal: Xuan was seen off to the southern province; Shao was originally restored to office.

entries.zh: 後邵中惡風，口不能言，去職數月，皓疑其托疾，收付酒藏，掠考千所，邵卒無一語，竟見殺害，家屬徙臨海。
entries.en: He Shao fell mute with a stroke; Sun Hao called it shamming, jailed him in the wine office, tortured him endlessly—He never spoke and was murdered; his kin were banished to Linhai.
entries.literal: Afterward Shao was struck by evil wind and could not speak; he left office several months; Hao suspected he feigned illness, seized him and handed him to the wine bureau, tortured and examined at a thousand places—Shao to the end had not one word, and in the end was killed; family dependants were moved to Linhai.

entries.zh: 並下詔誅玄子孫，是歲天冊元年也，邵年四十九。
entries.en: The same year Sun Hao ordered Lou Xuan's descendants executed; it was the first year of Tiance; He Shao was forty-nine.
entries.literal: At the same time an edict went down to execute Xuan's sons and grandsons; it was the first year of the Tiance era; Shao was forty-nine years old.

entries.zh: 〈邵子循，字彦先。
entries.en: 〈His son He Xun, courtesy name Yanxian,
entries.literal: 〈Shao's son Xun, courtesy name Yanxian.

entries.zh: 虞预晋书曰：循丁家祸，流放海滨，吴平，还乡里。
entries.en: Yu Yu's Jin History says He Xun suffered family ruin, was exiled to the coast, and returned home when Wu fell.
entries.literal: Yu Yu's Jin shu states: Xun suffered family disaster, was banished to the sea's edge; when Wu was pacified, he returned to his home village.

entries.zh: 节操高厉，童齔不群，言行举动，必以礼让。
entries.en: High-minded from childhood, he stood apart from other boys and was always courteous in word and deed.
entries.literal: His integrity was lofty and stern; from childhood he stood apart from others, and in speech and conduct he always acted with ritual courtesy.

entries.zh: 好学博闻，尤善三礼。
entries.en: He loved books and excelled in the three ritual classics.
entries.literal: He loved learning and read widely, especially skilled in the three ritual canons.

entries.zh: 举秀子，除阳羡、武康令。
entries.en: Recommended as a flourishing talent, he became magistrate of Yangxian and Wukang.
entries.literal: Recommended as flourishing talent, he was appointed magistrate of Yangxian and Wukang.

entries.zh: 顾荣、陆机、陆云表荐循曰：“伏见吴兴武康令贺循德量邃茂，才鉴清远，服膺道素，风操凝峻，历践三城，刑政肃穆，守职下县，编名凡萃，出自新邦，朝无知己，恪居遐外，志不自营，年时倏忽，而邈无阶绪，实州党愚智所为怅然。
entries.en: Gu Rong, Lu Ji, and Lu Yun jointly memorialized: "We humbly see that He Xun of Wukang combines depth of character with clarity of judgment, lives by the plain Way, and has governed three counties with a stern hand. A man of a newly conquered land without patrons at court, he languishes in a minor post while years slip away—the whole province grieves to see talent wasted.
entries.literal: Gu Rong, Lu Ji, and Lu Yun submitted a memorial recommending Xun, saying: We humbly see that He Xun, magistrate of Wukang in Wuxing, has deep and abundant virtue and measure, talent and insight clear and far, embraces the plain of the Way, conduct and integrity stern and lofty; he has passed through three cities in office, punishments and government solemn, guarding duty in a lower county, his name listed among the common mass, coming from a new state, the court without one who knows him, respectfully dwelling far outside, his intent not self-seeking, years and seasons suddenly passing, yet far without ladder or thread—truly what the foolish and wise of the province together feel regret about.

entries.zh: 臣等并以凡才，累授饰进，被服恩泽，忝豫朝末，知良士后时，而守局无言，惧有蔽贤之咎，是以不胜愚管，谨冒死表闻。”
entries.en: We are mediocre men already favored at court; to stay silent while a worthy languishes would be to hide talent from you—we therefore risk death to speak."
entries.literal: We your servants are all with ordinary talent, repeatedly receiving advancement in ornament, clothed in favor and grace, shamefully placed at the court's end; knowing a good gentleman is behind the times yet guarding our posts without speech, we fear the fault of concealing the worthy—therefore, unable to bear our foolish tubes, we respectfully risk death to set forth and be heard.

entries.zh: 久之，召为太子舍人。
entries.en: After long delay he was named attendant to the heir apparent.
entries.literal: After a long time he was summoned to be attendant to the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 石冰破扬州，循亦合众，事平，杜门不出。
entries.en: When Shi Bing ravaged Yangzhou, He Xun raised troops; when peace returned he shut his gates and would not show himself.
entries.literal: When Shi Bing broke Yangzhou, Xun also gathered a host; when the affair was settled, he closed his door and did not go out.

entries.zh: 陈敏作乱，以循为丹杨内史，循称疾固辞，敏不敢逼。
entries.en: Chen Min tried to name him interior administrator of Danyang; He Xun pleaded illness and Chen Min dared not press him.
entries.literal: When Chen Min rebelled, he appointed Xun as interior administrator of Danyang; Xun claimed illness and firmly declined—Min did not dare force him.

entries.zh: 于时江东豪右无不受敏爵位，惟循与同郡硃诞不挂贼网。
entries.en: While every great clan in Jiangdong took Chen Min's commissions, only He Xun and his townsman Zhu Dan refused the rebel's snare.
entries.literal: At that time among the powerful families east of the Yangzi none did not accept titles from Min—only Xun together with Zhu Dan of his commandery did not hang in the rebel's net.

entries.zh: 后除吴国内史，不就。
entries.en: He was later offered interior administrator of Wu but declined.
entries.literal: Afterward he was appointed interior administrator of Wu commandery but did not take up the post.

entries.zh: 元皇帝为镇东将军，请循为军司马，帝为晋王，以循为中书令，固让不受，转太常，领太子太傅。
entries.en: When Sima Rui was general who guards the east he asked He Xun to be his army marshal; as Prince of Jin he offered the secretariat—He Xun refused—and made him grand master of ceremonies and grand tutor to the heir apparent instead.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan was general who guards the east, he requested Xun as army marshal; when the Prince became Prince of Jin, he made Xun director of the secretariat—he firmly declined and would not accept, was transferred to grand master of ceremonies, concurrently grand tutor to the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 时朝廷初建，动有疑议，宗庙制度皆循所定，朝野谘询，为一时儒宗。
entries.en: In the new Jin court he settled every disputed ritual and became the age's leading Confucian authority.
entries.literal: At that time the court was newly established; whenever there was doubt in discussion, the rites of the ancestral temple were all what Xun settled; court and wild consulted him—he was the Confucian leader of the age.

entries.zh: 年六十，太兴二年卒。
entries.en: He died at sixty in the second year of Taixing (319).
entries.literal: At age sixty he died in the second year of Taixing.

entries.zh: 追赠司空，谥曰穆。
entries.en: He was posthumously named minister of works with the posthumous epithet Mu.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was honored as minister of works, posthumous name Mu.

entries.zh: 循诸所著论，并传於世。
entries.en: His essays survive in his collected works.
entries.literal: The various treatises Xun wrote were all transmitted in the world.

entries.zh: 子隰，临海太守。〉
entries.en: His son He Xi became grand administrator of Linhai.
entries.literal: His son Xi was grand administrator of Linhai.

entries.zh: 又北敵注目，伺國盛衰，陛下不恃己之威德；
entries.en: The northern enemy watches our strength; you do not trust your own virtue;
entries.literal: Moreover the northern foe fixes his gaze, watching whether the state waxes or wanes; Your Majesty does not rely on your own awe and virtue;

entries.zh: 而怙敵之不來，忽四海之困窮，而輕虜之不為難，誠非長策廟勝之要也。
entries.en: you bank on their staying away, ignore the empire's misery, and assume they will never strike—no recipe for lasting victory.
entries.literal: yet you rely on the enemy's not coming, neglect the four seas' destitution, and treat the barbarians' not acting as easy—this is truly not the essential of long strategy and temple victory.

entries.zh: 昔大皇帝勤身苦體，創基南夏，割據江山，拓士萬里，雖承天贊，實由人力也。
entries.en: The Grand Emperor built Wu with his own sweat though Heaven smiled on him.
entries.literal: In olden times the Grand Emperor toiled body and suffered flesh, founded the base in southern Xia, carved the rivers and mountains, expanded territory ten thousand li—though he received Heaven's aid, in truth it was by human strength.

entries.zh: 餘慶遺祚，至於陛下，陛下宜勉崇德器，以光前烈。
entries.en: His legacy rests with you—honor his virtue and magnify his deeds.
entries.literal: Remaining blessing and handed-down fortune have reached Your Majesty; Your Majesty ought to strive to honor virtue and capacity, to brighten the former blazing deeds.

entries.zh: 愛民養士，保全先軌，何可忽顯祖之功勤，輕難得之大業。
entries.en: Cherish the people and the scholar-officials; do not squander what he won with such pain.
entries.literal: Cherish the people and nurture scholars, preserve intact the former tracks—how can you neglect the Grand Ancestor's toil and slight a hard-won great enterprise?

entries.zh: 忘天下之不振，替興衰之巨變哉?臣聞否泰無常，吉兇由人，長江限不可久恃，苟我不守，一葦可航也。
entries.en: Will you forget the realm's peril? Fortune turns; the Yangzi is no eternal shield—fail to hold it and a reed boat suffices to cross.
entries.literal: Forget that All-under-Heaven is not rising, replace the great change of rise and fall? Your servant has heard that woe and weal are not constant, fortune and misfortune lie with men; the Yangzi's barrier cannot long be relied on—if we do not guard it, a single reed can be sailed across.

entries.zh: 昔秦建皇帝之號，據殽函之阻，德化不修，法政苛酷，毒流生民，忠臣杜口，是以一夫大呼，社稷傾覆。
entries.en: Qin held the passes yet fell to one cry of revolt when law turned cruel and loyal tongues fell silent.
entries.literal: In olden times Qin assumed the title of emperor, occupied the barrier of Yao and Han, did not cultivate virtue and transformation, law and government were harsh and cruel, poison flowed to the living people, loyal ministers sealed their mouths—therefore one man shouted aloud and the altars overturned.

entries.zh: 近劉氏據三關之險，守重山之固，可謂金城石室，萬世之業，任授失賢，一朝喪沒，君臣系頸，共為羈僕。
entries.en: Liu Shan held impregnable Shu yet lost everything in a day when wrong men held office—ruler and ministers bound like slaves.
entries.literal: Recently the Liu house held the peril of three passes, guarded the solidity of layered mountains—it could be called metal walls and stone chambers, an enterprise for ten thousand generations; appointments lost the worthy, in one morning it was lost and sunk, lord and ministers with cords about their necks together became tethered servants.

entries.zh: 此當世之明鑒，目前之炯戒也。
entries.en: That is the mirror of our age and a warning in plain sight.
entries.literal: This is a clear mirror of the age, a blazing warning before the eyes.

entries.zh: 願陛下遠考前事，近覽世變，豐基強本，割情從道，則成康之治興，而聖祖之祚隆矣。
entries.en: Study past and present, strengthen the foundations, rule by principle, not whim—then you may revive a Cheng-Kang age and honor your ancestor's line.
entries.literal: Your servant prays Your Majesty will examine far the former affairs, look near at the changes of the age, fatten the base and strengthen the root, cut private feeling and follow the Way—then the rule of Cheng and Kang will rise and the Grand Ancestor's fortune will flourish.

entries.zh: 和廢後，為黃門侍郎。
entries.en: After Prince He's deposition Wei Yao became gentleman attendant at the yellow gates.
entries.literal: After He was deposed, he became gentleman attendant at the yellow gates.

entries.zh: 孫亮即位，諸葛恪輔政，表曜為太史令，撰《吳書》，華核、薛瑩等皆與參同，孫休踐阼，為中書郎、博士祭酒。
entries.en: When Sun Liang took the throne, Zhuge Ke as regent recommended Yao as grand astrologer to compile the Book of Wu; Hua He, Xue Ying, and others all took part. When Sun Xiu acceded, Yao became gentleman of the secretariat and libationer of the erudits.
entries.literal: When Sun Liang ascended the throne, Zhuge Ke governed and memorialized Yao as grand astrologer to compose the Book of Wu; Hua He, Xue Ying, and others all joined in the same work; when Sun Xiu mounted the steps, he was gentleman of the secretariat and libationer of erudits.

entries.zh: 命曜依劉向故事，校定眾書。
entries.en: Sun Xiu ordered him to collate the imperial library on Liu Xiang's model.
entries.literal: He ordered Yao according to Liu Xiang's precedent to collate and fix the multitude of books.

entries.zh: 又欲延曜侍講，而左將軍張布近習寵幸，事行多玷，憚曜侍講儒士，又性精確，懼以古今警戒休意，固爭不可。
entries.en: He wished Wei Yao to lecture the throne, but Zhang Bu, the favorite general, blocked it, fearing a scholar would lecture Sun Xiu on moral history.
entries.literal: He also wished to extend Yao as lecturer-in-waiting, but General of the Left Zhang Bu was a near attendant, favored and doted on, his deeds many times stained; he feared Yao as lecturer, a Confucian gentleman, and moreover by nature precise, feared he would use past and present to warn Xiu's intent—therefore he firmly contended that it could not be done.

entries.zh: 休深恨布，語在《休傳》。
entries.en: Sun Xiu came to hate Zhang Bu—the story is told in Sun Xiu's biography.
entries.literal: Xiu deeply hated Bu—the words are in the biography of Xiu.

entries.zh: 然曜竟止不入。
entries.en: Wei Yao never took the lecturer's post.
entries.literal: Yet in the end Yao stopped and did not enter.

entries.zh: 曜運值千載，特蒙哀識，以其儒學，得與史官，貂蟬內侍，承答天問，聖朝仁篤，慎終追遠，迎神之際，垂涕敕曜。
entries.en: Wei Yao’s fortune met a rare age, and he received special pity and recognition. Because of his Confucian learning, he was allowed to join the historians, serve inside as a sable-cicada attendant, and answer the Son of Heaven’s questions. The sage court was humane and earnest, careful at the end and mindful of the distant past; when the spirits were welcomed, the ruler wept and gave Wei Yao his charge.
entries.literal: Yao's fate met a thousand ages, especially receiving pity and recognition; because of his Confucian learning he was allowed to join the historians, sable-collar attendant within, answering Heaven's questions; the sage court is humane and earnest, careful of endings and mindful of the distant; at the meeting to welcome the spirits he wept and ordered Yao.

entries.zh: 曜愚惑不達。
entries.en: He was slow to grasp your intent.
entries.literal: Yao was foolish and confused, not penetrating.

entries.zh: 不能敷宣陛下大舜之美，而拘擊史官，使聖趣不敘，至行不彰，實曜愚蔽當死之罪，然臣慺慺，見曜自少勤學，雖老不倦，探綜墳典，溫故知新，及意所經識古今行事，外吏之中少過曜者。
entries.en: He failed to hymn your Shun-like virtue—yet among field officials none knows the classics like Wei Yao.
entries.literal: He could not spread and proclaim Your Majesty's beauty like great Shun, yet was bound as historian, causing sage intent not to be narrated and utmost conduct not to be displayed—truly Yao's foolish blindness is a crime deserving death; yet your servant earnestly sees that Yao from youth studied diligently, though old not weary, delved into the tomb classics, reviewed the old and knew the new, and in what his mind has passed through, knowledge of past and present deeds—among outer clerks few surpass Yao.

entries.zh: 昔李陵為漢將，軍敗不還而降匈奴，司馬遷不加疾惡，為陵遊說，漢武帝以遷有良史之才，欲使畢成所撰，忍不加誅，書卒成立，垂之無窮。
entries.en: Han Wudi spared Sima Qian so the Records could be finished—Li Ling's fall did not cost the historian his life.
entries.literal: In olden times Li Ling was a Han general; his army was defeated, did not return, and surrendered to the Xiongnu—Sima Qian did not add harsh hatred and spoke for Ling; Han Wudi, because Qian had talent for a good historian, wished to let him complete what he was writing, bore not to add execution—the book in the end was completed and hangs endless.

entries.zh: 今曜在吳，亦漢之史遷也。
entries.en: Wei Yao is Wu's Sima Qian.
entries.literal: Now Yao in Wu is also Han's Sima Qian.

entries.zh: 伏見前後符瑞彰著。
entries.en: I have seen bright omens fore and aft.
entries.literal: Your servant humbly sees that before and after, talisman auspices have been manifest.

entries.zh: 神指天應，繼出累見，一統之期，庶不復久。
entries.en: Heaven answers the throne—the day of unification cannot be far.
entries.literal: The spirit points, Heaven responds; they have come forth repeatedly in succession—the time of unification, perhaps, will not again be long.

entries.zh: 事乎之後，當觀時設制，三王不相因禮，五帝不相沿樂，質文殊塗，損益異體，宜得輩依準古義，有所改立。
entries.en: When peace comes you must reform rites and music as kings of old did—let scholars take the classics as your guide.
entries.literal: After affairs are settled, one ought to observe the times and set institutions; the three kings did not inherit one another's rites, the five emperors did not continue one another's music—substance and pattern differ in path, decrease and increase differ in body—one ought to get a group to take ancient meaning as standard and have places to change and establish.

entries.zh: 漢氏承秦，則有叔孫通定一代之儀，曜之才學亦漢通之次也。
entries.en: Wei Yao could be another Shusun Tong for this dynasty.
entries.literal: The Han house inherited Qin, then there was Shusun Tong who fixed a generation's observances—Yao's talent and learning are next after Han's Tong.

entries.zh: 又《吳書》雖已有頭角，敘贊未述。
entries.en: The Book of Wu has a skeleton but lacks full narrative and appraisal.
entries.literal: Moreover the Book of Wu, though it already has horns and head, narrative and praise are not yet set forth.

entries.zh: 昔班固作《漢書》，文辭典雅，後劉珍，劉毅等作《漢記》，遠不及固，敘傳尤劣。
entries.en: Ban Gu's Han shu towers over the Han ji of Liu Zhen, Liu Yi, and others—the latter's biographies are poor stuff.
entries.literal: In olden times Ban Gu made the Han shu, literary phrasing classic and elegant; afterward Liu Zhen and Liu Yi and others made the Han ji, far not reaching Gu, especially narrative and biography inferior.

entries.zh: 今年《吳書》當垂千載，編次諸吏，後之才士論次善惡，非得良才如曜者，實不可使闕不朽之書。
entries.en: The Wu history must last a millennium—without a talent like Wei Yao it cannot be perfected.
entries.literal: Now this year the Book of Wu is to hang for a thousand ages; compiling and ordering the various clerks, later men of talent ordering good and evil—if one does not get a good talent like Yao, truly one cannot let the book of indestructibility lack.

entries.zh: 如臣頑蔽，誠非其人。
entries.en: I am too dull for the task myself.
entries.literal: As your servant is stubborn and blocked, truly he is not that man.

entries.zh: 今冠虜充斥，征伐未已，居無積年之儲，出無敵之畜，此乃有國者所宣深憂也。
entries.en: Helmets crowd the borders, war never stops, and we keep neither long-term grain nor a war chest—any ruler should tremble at that.
entries.literal: Now cap-and-diadem foes fill every quarter, campaigns and attacks do not cease; within there is no store laid by for years, without there is no hoard against the enemy—this is what those who possess a state ought deeply to worry about.

entries.zh: 夫財谷所生，皆出於民，趨時務農，國之上急。
entries.en: Wealth and grain spring from the people; timely farming is the state's first duty.
entries.literal: Now wealth and grain are born, all come from the people; hastening to the season and devoting effort to farming is the state's highest urgency.

entries.zh: 而都下諸官，所掌別異，各自下調，不計民力，輒與近期。
entries.en: Yet each capital bureau issues its own quotas without regard for peasant strength or realistic deadlines.
entries.literal: Yet the various offices of the capital, what they administer differs each; each on its own sends down demands, not reckoning the people's strength, always setting a near deadline.

entries.zh: 長吏畏罪，晝夜催民，委捨佃事，遑赴會日，定送到都，或蘊積不用，而徒使百姓消力失時。
entries.en: Magistrates, fearing punishment, drive farmers from the fields to meet arbitrary deadlines while grain rots unused in the capital.
entries.literal: Senior officials fear blame, day and night urge the people, cast aside tenancy tasks, hasten to keep the meeting day, fix delivery to the capital—sometimes it piles and is not used, yet vainly makes the hundred surnames waste strength and miss the season.

entries.zh: 到秋收月，督其限入，奪其播殖之時，而責定送其今年之稅，如有逋懸，則籍沒財物，故家戶貧困，衣食不足。
entries.en: In harvest month they demand tax while forbidding sowing; default means confiscation—so families starve.
entries.literal: When the month of autumn harvest comes, they supervise their limit of intake, seize the time for sowing and planting, yet require fixed delivery of this year's tax; if there is default or suspension, then they register and confiscate goods—therefore households are destitute, clothing and food insufficient.

entries.zh: 宜暫息眾役，專心農桑。
entries.en: Suspend corvée and put every hand to tillage and silk.
entries.literal: For the moment one ought to rest the multitude of labor tasks and devote heart to farming and sericulture.

entries.zh: 古人稱一夫不耕，或受其饑。
entries.en: They said one idle husband means hunger for someone.
entries.literal: The ancients said if one husband does not plow, perhaps someone suffers hunger.

entries.zh: 一女不織，或受其寒。
entries.en: One idle loom means someone goes cold.
entries.literal: If one woman does not weave, perhaps someone suffers cold.

entries.zh: 是以先王治國，惟農是務。
entries.en: So the kings of old put farming first.
entries.literal: Therefore former kings in governing states took only farming as the task.

entries.zh: 軍興以來，已向百栽，農人廢南畝之務，女工停機杼之業。
entries.en: A century of war has idled plowmen and stilled shuttles.
entries.literal: Since armies rose, already nearly a hundred years; farming men abandon the work of the southern acres, women's work stops the loom's trade.

entries.zh: 推此揆之，則蔬食而長饑，薄衣而履冰者，固不少矣。
entries.en: Many already live on greens yet starve and wear thin cloth on ice.
entries.literal: Pushing this and measuring it, those who eat vegetables yet long hunger, wear thin clothes yet tread on ice are certainly not few.

entries.zh: 臣聞主之所求於民者二，民之所望於主者三。
entries.en: The ruler asks two things of the people; the people ask three of him.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that what the lord seeks from the people is two, what the people hope from the lord is three.

entries.zh: 二謂求其為己勞也，求其為己死也。
entries.en: Those two are labor and life.
entries.literal: The two mean seeking that they toil for him, seeking that they die for him.

entries.zh: 三謂譏者能食之，勞者能息之，有功者能賞之。
entries.en: The three are food for the hungry, rest for the weary, reward for merit.
entries.literal: The three mean that the hungry can be fed, the weary can rest, the meritorious can be rewarded.

entries.zh: 民以致其二事而主失其三望者，則怨心生而功不建，今帑藏不實，民勞役猥，主之二求已備，民之三望未報。
entries.en: You take their toil and blood yet give no food, rest, or reward—resentment rises and nothing is built.
entries.literal: When the people bring these two tasks yet the lord loses their three hopes, then resentment is born and achievement is not built; now treasury stores are not solid, the people labor and corvée is numerous—the lord's two seeks are already prepared, the people's three hopes are not repaid.

entries.zh: 且饑者不待美饌而後飽，寒者不俟狐貉而後溫，為味者口之奇，文繡者身之飾也。
entries.en: The hungry need no banquet; the cold need no fur coat—spices and embroidery are luxuries, not needs.
entries.literal: Moreover the hungry do not wait for fine viands before being full; the cold do not wait for fox and badger before being warm—making flavors is the mouth's oddity, patterned embroidery is the body's ornament.

entries.zh: 今事多而役繁，民貧而俗奢，百工作無用之器，婦人為綺靡之飾，不勤麻枲，並鄉黼黻，轉相倣傚，恥獨無有。
entries.en: Yet multitudes chase useless crafts and silken finery, shunning hemp until every lane apes brocade.
entries.literal: Now affairs are many and corvée thick, the people are poor yet vulgar ways extravagant; the hundred crafts make useless implements, women make extravagant finery, do not work hemp and ramie, together toward embroidered insignia, turn and imitate one another, ashamed to be alone without having.

entries.zh: 兵民之家，猶復遂俗，內無儋石之儲，而出有綾綺之服，至於富賈商販之家，重以金銀，奢恣尤甚。
entries.en: Even poor soldiers' wives wear silk while cupboards stay empty; merchants heap gold and outdo all in waste.
entries.literal: In soldier and commoner households, still they follow vulgar ways; within they have not a dan or shi of store, yet without they have damask and gauze dress; as for rich merchant peddler households, doubled with gold and silver, extravagance is especially extreme.

entries.zh: 天下未平，百姓不贍，宜一生民之原，豐谷帛之業。
entries.en: The realm is still at war—nurture the people's root and pile up grain and cloth.
entries.literal: All-under-Heaven is not yet settled, the hundred surnames do not have enough; one ought to unify the root of nurturing the living, enrich the enterprise of grain and silk.

entries.zh: 而棄功於浮華之巧，妨日於侈靡之事，上無尊卑等級之差，下有耗財物力之損。
entries.en: Chasing glitter wastes days and erases rank; high and low alike drain coin and strength.
entries.literal: Yet one casts aside achievement on flashy cleverness, wastes days on extravagant matters; above there is no difference of noble and base rank, below there is loss of wealth and material force.

entries.zh: 今吏士之家，少無子女，多者三四，少者一二，通令戶有一女，十萬家則十萬人，人織績一歲一束，則十萬束矣。
entries.en: If every household with daughters put one girl to the loom, a hundred thousand bolts a year would follow.
entries.literal: Now in clerk and soldier households, few lack daughters; many have three or four, few have one or two—suppose by order each household has one daughter, a hundred thousand households then a hundred thousand people; each weaves one bolt in a year, then a hundred thousand bolts.

entries.zh: 使四疆之內同心戮力，數年之間，布帛必積。
entries.en: Let the four quarters weave together and silks will fill the storehouses within a few years.
entries.literal: Make within the four borders hearts join in one effort; within several years cloth and silk must accumulate.

entries.zh: 恣民五色，惟所服用，但禁綺繡無益之飾。
entries.en: Let commoners dye what they need—only ban useless brocade.
entries.literal: Let the people use the five colors as they will for dress, only forbid useless finery of figured silk.

entries.zh: 且美貌者不待華采以祟好，艷姿者不待文綺以致愛，五采之飾，足以麗矣。
entries.en: Beauty needs no brocade; five hues of plain weave suffice for grace.
entries.literal: Moreover one of fine face does not await splendid colors to exalt beauty; one of lovely form does not await patterned silk to bring love—the ornament of five colors is enough to be lovely.

entries.zh: 若極粉黛，窮盛服，未必無醜婦。
entries.en: Heaps of rouge and robes do not banish ugliness.
entries.literal: If one exhausts powder and eyebrow paint, exhausts sumptuous dress, not necessarily is there no ugly woman.

entries.zh: 廢華采，去文繡，未必無美人也。
entries.en: Strip the paint and brocade—beauty does not vanish.
entries.literal: Cast aside splendid colors, remove patterned silk—not necessarily is there no beautiful person.

entries.zh: 若實如論，有之無益廢之無損者，何愛而不斬禁以充府藏之急乎？
entries.en: If finery neither helps nor harms to lose, why not forbid it to fill urgent granaries?
entries.literal: If it is truly as in the discussion—having it has no benefit, abolishing it has no harm—why love and not cut and forbid it to fill the treasury's urgency?

entries.zh: 此救乏之上務，富國之本業也，使管、晏復生，無以易此。
entries.en: This is the highest task of relieving want and the root enterprise of enriching the state; were Guan and Yan born again, they could not change this.
entries.literal: This is the highest task of relieving want, the root enterprise of enriching the state; were Guan and Yan born again, they could not change this.

entries.zh: 漢之文、景，承平繼統，天下已定，四方無虞，猶以雕文之妨農事，錦繡之害女紅，開富國之利，杜饑寒之本。
entries.en: Han Wendi and Jingdi, though the realm was at peace, still banned luxuries that hurt farm and loom to stock the treasury and stop cold and hunger.
entries.literal: Wen and Jing of Han inherited peace in succession, All-under-Heaven was already settled, the four quarters without worry—still they took carved patterns as hindering farming, brocade embroidery as harming women's work, opened profit for enriching the state, blocked the root of hunger and cold.

entries.zh: 況今六台分乖；
entries.en: How much worse now that the realm is split—
entries.literal: How much more now the six terraces split and contrary;

entries.zh: 豺狼充路；
entries.en: jackals block the roads,
entries.literal: jackals and wolves fill the roads;

entries.zh: 兵不離疆；
entries.en: weapons never leave the frontier,
entries.literal: weapons do not leave the border;

entries.zh: 甲不解帶。
entries.en: armor never comes off—
entries.literal: armor is not unbuckled.

entries.zh: 而可以不廣生財之原，充府藏之積哉？
entries.en: —can you refuse to widen the sources of wealth and fill the granaries?
entries.literal: —and can one not broaden the root of producing wealth, fill the accumulation of the treasury?

entries.zh: 湯征諸侯。
entries.en: Tang led punitive expeditions against the regional lords.
entries.literal: Tang campaigned against the lords.

entries.zh: 葛伯不祀，湯始伐之。
entries.en: When the lord of Ge failed to perform the sacrifices, Tang attacked him first.
entries.literal: Lord of Ge did not sacrifice; Tang first attacked him.

entries.zh: 湯曰：「予有言：人視水見形，視民知治不。」
entries.en: Tang said, "Men look into water to see their faces; look to the people to know whether rule is sound."
entries.literal: Tang said, "I have a saying: people look on water and see form; look on the people and know order or not."

entries.zh: 伊尹曰：「明哉！
entries.en: Yi Yin replied: "How clear—
entries.literal: yiyin said, "How clear!

entries.zh: 言能聽，道乃進。
entries.en: when counsel is heard, the Way moves forward.
entries.literal: When words can be heard, the way then advances.

entries.zh: 君國子民，為善者皆在王官。
entries.en: The lord who fathers his people gathers every worthy into his court.
entries.literal: Ruler of the state, father to the people—all who do good are at the royal court.

entries.zh: 勉哉，勉哉！」
entries.en: Strive, my lord—never slacken."
entries.literal: Exert yourself, exert yourself!"

entries.zh: 湯曰：「汝不能敬命，予大罰殛之，無有攸赦。」
entries.en: Tang warned, "Whoever spurns my command I will strike down without mercy."
entries.literal: Tang said, "You who fail to reverence the command—I will greatly punish and kill you, without any sparing."

entries.zh: 作湯征。
entries.en: He composed the Tang Punitive Expeditions.
entries.literal: He made "Tang's Punitive Expeditions."

entries.zh: 伊尹名阿衡。
entries.en: Yi Yin was named Aheng.
entries.literal: yiyin's name was Aheng.

entries.zh: 阿衡欲奸湯而無由，乃為有莘氏媵臣，負鼎俎，以滋味說湯，致于王道。
entries.en: Wishing to serve Tang but lacking an introduction, Aheng joined the Youxin bridal procession as a cook, carried pots and boards, won Tang over through his cooking, and drew him toward the kingly Way.
entries.literal: Wishing to serve Tang but lacking an introduction, Aheng became a attendant in the Youxin bridal train, carried pots and boards, won Tang over through flavor, and led him toward the kingly Way.

entries.zh: 或曰，伊尹處士，湯使人聘迎之，五反然後肯往從湯，言素王及九主之事。
entries.en: Others say yiyin was a recluse whom Tang invited five times before he came, then spoke to him of the model rulers and the Nine Masters.
entries.literal: Others say yiyin was a recluse whom Tang invited five times before he came, then lectured on the model rulers and the Nine Masters.

entries.zh: 湯舉任以國政。
entries.en: Tang handed him the administration of the realm.
entries.literal: Tang raised and entrusted him with state government.

entries.zh: 伊尹去湯適夏。
entries.en: yiyin left Tang and went over to the Xia court.
entries.literal: yiyin left Tang for Xia.

entries.zh: 既醜有夏，復歸于亳。
entries.en: Once he had taken Xia's measure, he returned to Bo.
entries.literal: Having found fault with You-Xia, he returned to Bo.

entries.zh: 入自北門，遇女鳩、女房，作女鳩女房。
entries.en: He entered by the north gate, met the ladies Jiuji and Fang, and composed the pieces Nüjiu and Nüfang.
entries.literal: Entering by the north gate, he met Nüjiu and Nüfang; he made "Nüjiu and Nüfang."

entries.zh: 帝太甲既立三年，不明，暴虐，不遵湯法，亂德，於是伊尹放之於桐宮。
entries.en: After three years Taijia proved dark, violent, and lawless; yiyin banished him to the Tong palace.
entries.literal: Emperor Taijia having been established three years, was not enlightened, cruel and tyrannical, did not follow Tang's laws, disordered virtue; thereupon yiyin banished him to Tong Palace.

entries.zh: 三年，伊尹攝行政當國，以朝諸侯。
entries.en: For three years yiyin ruled as regent and received the lords at court.
entries.literal: Three years yiyin exercised government in proxy and held court over the lords.

entries.zh: 太宗崩，子沃丁立。
entries.en: When the Grand Ancestor died, his son Woding succeeded.
entries.literal: Grand Ancestor passed away; his son Woding established himself.

entries.zh: 帝沃丁之時，伊尹卒。
entries.en: Under Woding, yiyin died.
entries.literal: In Emperor Woding's time, yiyin passed away.

entries.zh: 既葬伊尹於亳，咎單遂訓伊尹事，作沃丁。
entries.en: After Yi Yin had been buried at Bo, Jiu Dan set forth Yi Yin’s deeds in instruction and composed Woding.
entries.literal: After yiyin was buried at Bo, Jiusdan expounded his deeds in the piece called Woding.

entries.zh: 湯歸至于泰卷陶，中壘作誥。
entries.en: On his return Tang halted at Taijuan Tao, where Zhonglei composed the proclamations.
entries.literal: On his return Tang halted at Taijuan Tao, where Zhonglei composed the announcements.

entries.zh: 既絀夏命，還亳，作湯誥：「維三月，王自至於東郊。
entries.en: After ending Xia's mandate he returned to Bo and issued Tang's Announcement: "In the third month the king came in person to the eastern suburbs.
entries.literal: Having ended Xia's mandate, he returned to Bo and made "Tang's Announcement": "It is the third month; the king personally reached the eastern suburbs.

entries.zh: 告諸侯群后：『毋不有功於民，勤力乃事。
entries.en: He told the assembled rulers: None of you may neglect the people; labor diligently at your duties.
entries.literal: He told the lords and host of rulers: 'None shall fail to work for the people; exert yourselves in your tasks.

entries.zh: 予乃大罰殛女，毋予怨。』
entries.en: Or I will punish you severely—do not blame me for it.
entries.literal: I will then greatly punish and kill you—do not blame me.

entries.zh: 曰：『古禹、皋陶久勞于外，其有功乎民，民乃有安。
entries.en: He said: Long ago Yu and Gao Yao worked far from court; they served the people, and the people found peace.
entries.literal: Saying: 'Of old Yu and Gao Yao long toiled outside; they had merit toward the people; the people then had rest.

entries.zh: 東為江，北為濟，西為河，南為淮，四瀆已修，萬民乃有居。
entries.en: East lay the Long River, north the Ji, west the Yellow River, south the Huai—the four streams were tamed, and the people had homes.
entries.literal: East was the Yangtze, north was the Ji, west was the He, south was the Huai—the four channels were repaired; the myriad people then had dwellings.

entries.zh: 后稷降播，農殖百穀。
entries.en: Hou Ji brought down seed and taught farming of every grain.
entries.literal: Prince Millet descended and sowed, farming planted the hundred grains.

entries.zh: 三公咸有功于民，故後有立。
entries.en: The three high ministers all served the people, and their lines were founded in turn.
entries.literal: The three dukes all had merit toward the people; therefore afterward they had establishment.

entries.zh: 昔蚩尤與其大夫作亂百姓，帝乃弗予，有狀。
entries.en: When Chiyou and his officers ravaged the people, Heaven withdrew favor—there was clear cause.
entries.literal: Of old Chiyou with his great officers made disorder among the hundred surnames; the Emperor then did not grant him—there was evidence.

entries.zh: 先王言不可不勉。』
entries.en: The words of the former kings must be heeded.
entries.literal: The former kings' words must not go unheeded.

entries.zh: 曰：『不道，毋之在國，女毋我怨。』」
entries.en: He added: If you stray from the Way, you shall not remain in power—do not resent me for it."
entries.literal: Saying: 'If not the Way, do not let it remain in the state—you must not resent me.'

entries.zh: 以令諸侯。
entries.en: Thus, he charged the regional lords.
entries.literal: Thereby commanding the lords.

entries.zh: 伊尹作咸有一德，咎單作明居。
entries.en: Yi Yin composed All Possess One Virtue, and Jiu Dan composed Bright Dwelling.
entries.literal: yiyin composed All Possess One Virtue; Jiusdan composed Bright Dwelling.

entries.zh: 當是時，夏桀為虐政淫荒，而諸侯昆吾氏為亂。
entries.en: At this time Jie of Xia governed with cruelty and excess, and the lords of Kunwu raised disorder.
entries.literal: In those days Jie of Xia ruled with cruelty and excess while the Kunwu lords stirred rebellion.

entries.zh: 湯乃興師率諸侯，伊尹從湯，湯自把鉞以伐昆吾，遂伐桀。
entries.en: Tang then raised an army of the lords, yiyin at his side, and himself wielded the axe against Kunwu before marching on Jie.
entries.literal: Tang thereupon raised troops leading the lords; yiyin followed Tang; Tang himself grasped the battle-axe to attack Kunwu, then attacked Jie.

entries.zh: 湯曰：「格女眾庶，來，女悉聽朕言。
entries.en: Tang addressed the host: "Come, all of you, and hear my words.
entries.literal: Tang said, "Come you multitude, come, you all listen to my words.

entries.zh: 匪台小子敢行舉亂，有夏多罪，予維聞女眾言，夏氏有罪。
entries.en: It is not I who dare stir revolt; Xia is heavy with crime—I have heard you yourselves say the Xia house is guilty.
entries.literal: It is not I, the little child, who dare raise disorder; You-Xia has many crimes—I only have heard you multitudes speak—the Xia clan has guilt.

entries.zh: 予畏上帝，不敢不正。
entries.en: I fear Heaven and dare not withhold punishment.
entries.literal: I fear Supreme God; I dare not fail to correct.

entries.zh: 今夏多罪，天命殛之。
entries.en: Xia's crimes are many; Heaven has ordered its destruction.
entries.literal: Now Xia has many crimes; Heaven's mandate is to strike it dead.

entries.zh: 今女有眾，女曰：『我君不恤我眾，捨我嗇事而割政』。
entries.en: You say among yourselves: Our king does not pity us—he sets aside our field work and meddles with government.
entries.literal: Now you have a multitude; you say, 'Our lord does not pity us multitudes, casts aside our harvest toil and cuts policy.

entries.zh: 女其曰：『有罪，其柰何』？
entries.en: You ask: If there is fault, what can be done?
entries.literal: You will say, 'If there is guilt, what then shall be done?

entries.zh: 夏王率止眾力，率奪夏國。
entries.en: The king of Xia has drained your strength and plundered the Xia domain.
entries.literal: The Xia king has led astray and exhausted the multitude's strength, led and seized the Xia state.

entries.zh: 有眾率怠不和，曰：『是日何時喪？
entries.en: The people have grown slack and bitter, crying: "When will this sun set?
entries.literal: The multitude has led slackness and discord, saying, 'When will this sun perish?

entries.zh: 予與女皆亡』！
entries.en: I will perish with you!"
entries.literal: I and you will all perish!

entries.zh: 夏德若茲，今朕必往。
entries.en: Xia's conduct is such that I must march against it.
entries.literal: Xia's virtue being thus, now I must go.

entries.zh: 爾尚及予一人致天之罰，予其大理女。
entries.en: Join me, the One Man, in carrying out Heaven's sentence, and I will reward you richly.
entries.literal: You still may join me, the One Man, to inflict Heaven's punishment—I will greatly order you.

entries.zh: 女毋不信，朕不食言。
entries.en: Do not doubt me—I keep my oath.
entries.literal: You must not disbelieve—I do not break my word.

entries.zh: 女不從誓言，予則帑僇女，無有攸赦。」
entries.en: Whoever breaks this oath I will execute, you and your families, without mercy."
entries.literal: You who do not follow the sworn words—I will put you and your kin to death, without any sparing."

entries.zh: 以告令師，作湯誓。
entries.en: He proclaimed this to the host and composed the Oath of Tang.
entries.literal: He reported this to the army and composed the Oath of Tang.

entries.zh: 於是湯曰：「吾甚武」，號曰武王。
entries.en: Tang then said, "I am greatly martial," and took the title Martial King.
entries.literal: Thereupon Tang said, "I am very martial," and styled himself Martial King.

entries.zh: 桀敗於有娀之虛，桀奔於鳴條，夏師敗績。
entries.en: Jie was beaten at Yousong, fled to Mingtiao, and his army was routed.
entries.literal: Jie was defeated at the ruins of Yousong; Jie fled to Mingtiao; Xia's army suffered rout.

entries.zh: 湯遂伐三嵕，俘厥寶玉，義伯、仲伯作典寶。
entries.en: Tang then attacked Sanzong, seized its sacred jades, and the lords Yibo and Zhongbo composed the Canon of the Treasure.
entries.literal: Tang then attacked Sanzong, seized its sacred jades, and Yibo and Zhongbo composed the Canon of the Treasure.

entries.zh: 湯既勝夏，欲遷其社，不可，作夏社。
entries.en: After conquering Xia, Tang wished to relocate its soil altar but could not, and composed Xia's Earth Altar.
entries.literal: Tang having conquered Xia, wished to move its earth altar, could not, and made "Xia's Earth Altar."

entries.zh: 伊尹報。
entries.en: yiyin made his report.
entries.literal: yiyin presented his report.

entries.zh: 於是諸侯畢服，湯乃踐天子位，平定海內。
entries.en: The lords all submitted; Tang took the throne and brought peace within the seas.
entries.literal: The lords all submitted; Tang took the throne and brought peace inside the seas.

entries.zh: 湯崩，太子太丁未立而卒，於是乃立太丁之弟外丙，是為帝外丙。
entries.en: When Tang died, the heir Taiding died before he could rule, so Taiding's brother Waibing became Emperor Waibing.
entries.literal: Tang passed away; heir son Taiding had not been established then died; thereupon they established Taiding's younger brother Waibing—this is Emperor Waibing.

entries.zh: 帝外丙即位三年，崩，立外丙之弟中壬，是為帝中壬。
entries.en: Waibing ruled three years and died; his brother Zhongren succeeded as Emperor Zhongren.
entries.literal: Emperor Waibing having assumed position three years, passed away; they established Waibing's younger brother Zhongren—this is Emperor Zhongren.

entries.zh: 帝中壬即位四年，崩，伊尹乃立太丁之子太甲。
entries.en: Zhongren ruled four years and died; yiyin then set Taiding's son Taijia on the throne.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhongren having assumed position four years, passed away; yiyin then established Taiding's son Taijia.

entries.zh: 太甲，成湯適長孫也，是為帝太甲。
entries.en: Taijia was Cheng Tang's senior great-grandson through the main line—Emperor Taijia.
entries.literal: Taijia, Cheng Tang's eldest great-grandson by the proper line—this is Emperor Taijia.

entries.zh: 帝太甲元年，伊尹作伊訓，作肆命，作徂后。
entries.en: In Emperor Taijia’s first year, Yi Yin composed the Instructions for Taijia, the Broad Commands, and The Departed Sovereign.
entries.literal: In Taijia's first year yiyin composed the Instructions for Taijia, the Loose Commands, and Gone Kings.

entries.zh: 帝太甲居桐宮三年，悔過自責，反善，於是伊尹乃迎帝太甲而授之政。
entries.en: Taijia spent three years in Tong, repented, and mended his ways; yiyin then brought him back and restored the government.
entries.literal: Emperor Taijia dwelling in Tong Palace three years, repented fault and blamed himself, returned to good; thereupon yiyin then welcomed Emperor Taijia and handed him the government.

entries.zh: 帝太甲修德，諸侯咸歸殷，百姓以寧。
entries.en: Taijia cultivated virtue; the lords rallied to Yin again and the people were calmed.
entries.literal: Emperor Taijia cultivated virtue; the lords all returned to Yin; the hundred surnames thereby were tranquil.

entries.zh: 伊尹嘉之，乃作太甲訓三篇，褒帝太甲，稱太宗。
entries.en: yiyin praised him, composed the three Instructions of Taijia, and honored him as Grand Ancestor.
entries.literal: yiyin praised him, composed the three Instructions of Taijia, honored him as Grand Ancestor.

entries.zh: 帝雍己崩，弟太戊立，是為帝太戊。
entries.en: Yongji died; his brother Taiwu became Emperor Taiwu.
entries.literal: Emperor Yongji passed away; younger brother Taiwu established himself—this is Emperor Taiwu.

entries.zh: 帝太戊立伊陟為相。
entries.en: Taiwu appointed Yizhi chief minister.
entries.literal: Emperor Taiwu established Yizhi as minister.

entries.zh: 亳有祥桑谷共生於朝，一暮大拱。
entries.en: At Bo mulberry and grain sprouted together in the courtyard and in one night grew thick as an arm.
entries.literal: At Bo there was an omen: mulberry and grain grew together in the court; in one night they became as thick as a clasped hand.

entries.zh: 帝太戊懼，問伊陟。
entries.en: Taiwu was frightened and asked Yizhi what it meant.
entries.literal: Emperor Taiwu feared and questioned Yizhi.

entries.zh: 伊陟曰：「臣聞妖不勝德，帝之政其有闕與？
entries.en: Yizhi said, "I have heard that portents cannot overcome virtue. Perhaps there is a flaw in your government?
entries.literal: Yizhi said, "I have heard that portents cannot overcome virtue—perhaps there is a flaw in your government?

entries.zh: 帝其修德。」
entries.en: My lord, cultivate your virtue."
entries.literal: The king must cultivate his virtue."

entries.zh: 太戊從之，而祥桑枯死而去。
entries.en: Taiwu listened; the strange mulberry died away.
entries.literal: Taiwu followed it, and the auspicious mulberry withered and departed.

entries.zh: 伊陟贊言于巫咸。
entries.en: Yizhi relayed this counsel to Wuxian.
entries.literal: Yizhi praised the words to Wuxian.

entries.zh: 巫咸治王家有成，作咸艾，作太戊。
entries.en: Wu Xian brought order to the royal house and achieved success; he composed Xian Ai and Taiwu.
entries.literal: Wuxian brought order to the royal house and composed Xian Ai and Taiwu.

entries.zh: 帝太戊贊伊陟于廟，言弗臣，伊陟讓，作原命。
entries.en: Emperor Taiwu praised Yi Zhi in the ancestral temple, speaking of him as more than a mere minister. Yi Zhi declined the honor, and Original Mandate was composed.
entries.literal: Taiwu honored Yizhi in the temple as more than a mere minister; Yizhi declined, and the Original Mandate was composed.

entries.zh: 殷復興，諸侯歸之，故稱中宗。
entries.en: Yin flourished again and the lords rallied—hence he is called the Middle Ancestor.
entries.literal: Yin revived; the lords returned to it; therefore he is called Middle Ancestor.

entries.zh: 中宗崩，子帝中丁立。
entries.en: When the Middle Ancestor died, his son Zhongding succeeded.
entries.literal: Middle Ancestor passed away; his son Emperor Zhongding established himself.

entries.zh: 帝中丁遷于隞。
entries.en: Zhongding moved the capital to Ao.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhongding moved the capital to Ao.

entries.zh: 河亶甲居相。
entries.en: Hedanjia ruled from Xiang.
entries.literal: Hedanjia dwelt at Xiang.

entries.zh: 祖乙遷于邢。
entries.en: Zuyi moved the seat to Xing.
entries.literal: Zuyi moved the capital to Xing.

entries.zh: 帝中丁崩，弟外壬立，是為帝外壬。
entries.en: Zhongding died; his brother Wairen became Emperor Wairen.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhongding passed away; younger brother Wairen established himself—this is Emperor Wairen.

entries.zh: 仲丁書闕不具。
entries.en: The written records for Zhongding are missing and incomplete.
entries.literal: The records of Zhongding are lost and incomplete.

entries.zh: 帝外壬崩，弟河亶甲立，是為帝河亶甲。
entries.en: Wairen died; his brother Hedanjia became Emperor Hedanjia.
entries.literal: Emperor Wairen passed away; younger brother Hedanjia established himself—this is Emperor Hedanjia.

entries.zh: 河亶甲時，殷復衰。
entries.en: Under Hedanjia Yin weakened again.
entries.literal: In Hedanjia's time, Yin again declined.

entries.zh: 帝小乙崩，子帝武丁立。
entries.en: Xiaoyi died and his son Wuding ruled.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaoyi passed away; his son Emperor Wuding established himself.

entries.zh: 帝武丁即位，思復興殷，而未得其佐。
entries.en: Wuding wished to restore Yin but had not yet found the right minister.
entries.literal: Emperor Wuding having assumed the throne, thought to revive Yin but had not yet found his helper.

entries.zh: 三年不言，政事決定於冢宰，以觀國風。
entries.en: For three years he held his tongue while the chief minister decided affairs, the better to read the realm.
entries.literal: For three years he did not speak; government was decided by the chief minister, to observe the customs of the state.

entries.zh: 武丁夜夢得聖人，名曰說。
entries.en: One night Wuding dreamed of a sage named Yue.
entries.literal: Wuding night dreamed he obtained a sage, named Yue.

entries.zh: 以夢所見視群臣百吏，皆非也。
entries.en: He compared the vision to his officers—none fit the dream.
entries.literal: According to the dream's appearance he viewed ministers and hundred clerks—none matched.

entries.zh: 於是乃使百工營求之野，得說於傅險中。
entries.en: He sent artisans to search the wilds and found Yue at Fu ravine.
entries.literal: Thereupon he sent craftsmen to seek in the wilds and obtained Yue at Fu ravine.

entries.zh: 是時說為胥靡，筑於傅險。
entries.en: At that time Yue was a corvée laborer, building at Fu ravine.
entries.literal: At that time Yue was a convict laborer, building at Fu ravine.

entries.zh: 見於武丁，武丁曰是也。
entries.en: When he was brought to Wuding, the king said, This is the man.
entries.literal: Presented to Wuding, Wuding said this is he.

entries.zh: 得而與之語，果聖人，舉以為相，殷國大治。
entries.en: They spoke and found him a sage; he was made minister and Yin was well governed.
entries.literal: Having obtained him and conversed with him, he was indeed a sage; raised to be minister—Yin state was greatly ordered.

entries.zh: 故遂以傅險姓之，號曰傅說。
entries.en: He took his name from Fu ravine and was called Fu Yue.
entries.literal: Therefore, they took Fu ravine as his surname, styled Fu Yue.

entries.zh: 帝武丁崩，子帝祖庚立。
entries.en: Wuding died and his son Zugeng succeeded.
entries.literal: Emperor Wuding passed away; his son Emperor Zugeng established himself.

entries.zh: 祖己嘉武丁之以祥雉為德，立其廟為高宗，遂作高宗肜日及訓。
entries.en: Zu Ji praised Wu Ding for turning the auspicious pheasant omen into virtue; his temple was established as Gaozong, and Gaozong’s Rong Day and its instruction were composed.
entries.literal: Zuji praised Wuding for turning the pheasant omen to good; his temple was titled Gaozong, and the Congratulatory Day of Gaozong and related texts were composed.

entries.zh: 帝武丁祭成湯，明日，有飛雉登鼎耳而呴，武丁懼。
entries.en: Wuding sacrificed to Tang; the next day a pheasant lit on the cauldron's ear and cried; the king was afraid.
entries.literal: Emperor Wuding sacrificed to Cheng Tang; next day a flying pheasant perched on the tripod ear and crowed; Wuding feared.

entries.zh: 祖己曰：「王勿憂，先修政事。」
entries.en: Zuji said, "Do not fear, my king. Set your government in order first."
entries.literal: Zuji said, "Do not fear, my king—set your government in order first."

entries.zh: 祖己乃訓王曰：「唯天監下典厥義，降年有永有不永，非天夭民，中絕其命。
entries.en: Zuji lectured the king: "Heaven looks down and grounds its justice in right conduct; it grants long or short life, not to cut men off in youth but to end those who stray mid-course.
entries.literal: Zuji lectured the king: Heaven looks down and grounds its justice in right conduct; it grants long or short life—not to cut men off in youth but to end those who stray mid-course.

entries.zh: 民有不若德，不聽罪，天既附命正厥德，乃曰其奈何。
entries.en: When men lack fitting virtue and ignore their faults, Heaven attaches a charge to straighten their conduct—then we ask what is to be done.
entries.literal: When the people lack virtue fitting them, refuse to hear their guilt, Heaven having attached mandate corrects their virtue—then it says what can be done.

entries.zh: 鳴呼！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 王嗣敬民，罔非天繼，常祀毋禮于棄道。」
entries.en: The king's heir must honor the people. All live under Heaven's succession; in your regular rites never carelessly abandon the Way."
entries.literal: The king's heir must honor the people—all live under Heaven's succession; in your regular rites never carelessly abandon the Way."

entries.zh: 武丁修政行德，天下咸驩，殷道復興。
entries.en: Wuding set his house in order and practiced virtue; the realm rejoiced and Yin flourished again.
entries.literal: Wuding cultivated government and practiced virtue; all under Heaven rejoiced; Yin's way again revived.

entries.zh: 西伯歸，乃陰修德行善，諸侯多叛紂而往歸西伯。
entries.en: The Western Earl went home and quietly built virtue; many lords forsook Zhou for him.
entries.literal: Western Earl returning secretly cultivated virtue doing good; many lords rebelled against Zhou and went to join Western Earl.

entries.zh: 西伯滋大，紂由是稍失權重。
entries.en: As the Western Earl grew mighty, Zhou's grip slackened.
entries.literal: Western Earl grew greater; Zhou thereby gradually lost weight of power.

entries.zh: 王子比干諫，弗聽。
entries.en: Prince Bigan remonstrated; Zhou would not hear him.
entries.literal: Prince Bigan remonstrated; he would not listen.

entries.zh: 商容賢者，百姓愛之，紂廢之。
entries.en: Shang Rong was worthy and beloved; Zhou dismissed him.
entries.literal: Shang Rong was a worthy; the hundred surnames loved him; Zhou cast him aside.

entries.zh: 及西伯伐饑國，滅之，紂之臣祖伊聞之而咎周，恐，奔告紂曰：「天既訖我殷命，假人元龜，無敢知吉，非先王不相我後人，維王淫虐用自絕，故天棄我，不有安食，不虞知天性，不迪率典。
entries.en: When the Western Earl destroyed Ji, Zuyi, a minister of Zhou, heard of it, was alarmed by the Zhou state's rise, and rushed in fear to warn King Zhou, saying, "Heaven has ended Yin's mandate; even the great tortoise cannot show good fortune. It is not that the former kings have forsaken us, but that the king's cruelty has cut us off from Heaven, so we lack peace, ignore Heaven's will, and spurn the statutes.
entries.literal: When the Western Earl destroyed the state of Ji, Zuyi, a minister of Zhou, heard of it, was alarmed at the Zhou state's rise, and in fear rushed to report to King Zhou, saying, "Heaven has already ended the mandate of Yin; when we consult the great tortoise, none dare pronounce good fortune. It is not that the former kings do not aid us their descendants, but that the king by dissolute cruelty has cut himself off, so Heaven abandons us. We lack secure food, do not heed Heaven's mind, and do not follow the statutes.

entries.zh: 今我民罔不欲喪，曰『天曷不降威，大命胡不至』？
entries.en: Now none of your people but wishes this house to fall, crying, "When will Heaven strike—why does the great mandate not come?"
entries.literal: Now none of your people but wishes this house to perish, crying, "When will Heaven send down its terrors—why does the great mandate not come?"

entries.zh: 今王其柰何？」
entries.en: What will you do now, my king?"
entries.literal: What will you do now, my king?"

entries.zh: 紂曰：「我生不有命在天乎！」
entries.en: Zhou said, "Was I not born with Heaven’s mandate?"
entries.literal: Zhou said, "Was I not born with a mandate from Heaven?"

entries.zh: 祖伊反，曰：「紂不可諫矣。」
entries.en: Zu Yi returned and said, "Zhou can no longer be remonstrated with."
entries.literal: Zuyi returned and said, "Zhou cannot be admonished."

entries.zh: 西伯既卒，周武王之東伐，至盟津，諸侯叛殷會周者八百。
entries.en: After the Western Earl died, King Wu marched east to Mengjin; eight hundred lords who had turned from Yin rallied to him.
entries.literal: Western Earl having passed away, King Wu of Zhou campaigned east, reaching Mengjin; lords rebelling against Yin who met Zhou were eight hundred.

entries.zh: 諸侯皆曰：「紂可伐矣。」
entries.en: The feudal lords all said, "Zhou can be attacked now."
entries.literal: The lords all said, "Zhou may be attacked."

entries.zh: 武王曰：「爾未知天命。」
entries.en: King Wu said, "You do not yet understand Heaven’s mandate."
entries.literal: King Wu said, "You do not yet know Heaven's mandate."

entries.zh: 乃復歸。
entries.en: So he marched home.
entries.literal: Thereupon he returned.

entries.zh: 紂愈淫亂不止。
entries.en: Zhou sank deeper into vice without end.
entries.literal: Zhou further dissolute and chaotic without stop.

entries.zh: 微子數諫不聽，乃與大師、少師謀，遂去。
entries.en: Weizi remonstrated repeatedly but was not heard; he then consulted with the Grand Master and Junior Master and departed.
entries.literal: Weizi pleaded again and again in vain, then conspired with the grand and junior masters and left.

entries.zh: 比干曰：「為人臣者，不得不以死爭。」
entries.en: Bigan said, "A minister who will not risk death is no minister."
entries.literal: Bigan said, "Being someone's minister, one cannot but contend with death."

entries.zh: 乃彊諫紂。
entries.en: He then rebuked Zhou bluntly.
entries.literal: Thereupon he strongly remonstrated Zhou.

entries.zh: 紂怒曰：「吾聞聖人心有七竅。」
entries.en: Zhou raged, "I hear a sage's heart has seven chambers."
entries.literal: Zhou angrily said, "I have heard the sage's heart has seven openings."

entries.zh: 剖比干，觀其心。
entries.en: He cut Bigan open to look at his heart.
entries.literal: He cut open Bigan and viewed his heart.

entries.zh: 箕子懼，乃詳狂為奴，紂又囚之。
entries.en: Jizi feigned madness as a slave in terror; Zhou jailed him too.
entries.literal: Jizi feared, then feigned madness as a slave; Zhou again imprisoned him.

entries.zh: 殷之大師、少師乃持其祭樂器奔周。
entries.en: The Grand Master and Junior Master of Yin then took the sacrificial and musical vessels and fled to Zhou.
entries.literal: Yin's grand and junior masters fled to Zhou carrying the ritual vessels.

entries.zh: 周武王於是遂率諸侯伐紂。
entries.en: King Wu then led the host against Zhou.
entries.literal: King Wu of Zhou thereupon then led the lords to attack Zhou.

entries.zh: 紂亦發兵距之牧野。
entries.en: Zhou sent an army to meet him at Muye.
entries.literal: Zhou also raised troops to resist him at Muye.

entries.zh: 甲子日，紂兵敗。
entries.en: On the jiazi day, Zhou’s army was defeated.
entries.literal: On the jiazi day, Zhou's army was defeated.

entries.zh: 紂走入，登鹿臺，衣其寶玉衣，赴火而死。
entries.en: Zhou fled inside, climbed the Deer Terrace, put on his robe of precious jades, and threw himself into the flames.
entries.literal: Zhou fled within, climbed Lutai in his jeweled robes, and burned himself to death.

entries.zh: 周武王遂斬紂頭，縣之［大］白旗。
entries.en: King Wu of Zhou then cut off Zhou’s head and hung it from the great white banner.
entries.literal: King Wu struck off his head and raised it on the great white standard.

entries.zh: 殺妲己。
entries.en: He executed Daji.
entries.literal: He killed Daji.

entries.zh: 釋箕子之囚，封比干之墓，表商容之閭。
entries.en: He freed Jizi, sealed Bigan's grave, and honored Shang Rong's lane.
entries.literal: He released Jizi from prison, sealed Bigan's tomb, marked Shang Rong's lane.

entries.zh: 封紂子武庚、祿父，以續殷祀，令修行盤庚之政。
entries.en: He enfeoffed Zhou's son Wugeng—Lufu—to keep Yin sacrifices and follow Pangeng's rule.
entries.literal: He enfeoffed Zhou's son Wugeng, Lufu, to continue Yin sacrifices, ordering him to practice Pangeng's government.

entries.zh: 殷民大說。
entries.en: The Yin people rejoiced.
entries.literal: Yin people greatly rejoiced.

entries.zh: 於是周武王為天子。
entries.en: King Wu then became Son of Heaven.
entries.literal: Thereupon King Wu of Zhou became Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 其後世貶帝號，號為王。
entries.en: Later Zhou dropped the title emperor and called its rulers kings.
entries.literal: His later generations lowered the title emperor, styling them kings.

entries.zh: 而封殷後為諸侯，屬周。
entries.en: Yin's descendants were enfeoffed as lords under Zhou.
entries.literal: And he enfeoffed Yin's posterity as lords, subordinate to Zhou.

entries.zh: 周武王崩，武庚與管叔、蔡叔作亂，成王命周公誅之，而立微子於宋，以續殷後焉。
entries.en: When King Wu died, Wugeng and the lords of Guan and Cai rebelled; King Cheng ordered the Duke of Zhou to crush them and set Weizi in Song to carry on Yin's line.
entries.literal: When King Wu of Zhou died, Wugeng rebelled with the lords of Guan and Cai; King Cheng ordered the Duke of Zhou to execute them and established Weizi in Song to continue Yin's line.

entries.zh: 殷契，母曰簡狄，有娀氏之女，為帝嚳次妃。
entries.en: Xie of Yin was born to Jiandi, a woman of the Yousong clan and secondary consort of Emperor Ku.
entries.literal: Xie of Yin had a mother named Jiandi, of the Yousong clan, who was Di Ku's secondary consort.

entries.zh: 三人行浴，見玄鳥墮其卵，簡狄取吞之，因孕生契。
entries.en: While Jiandi bathed with two companions, a dark bird dropped an egg; she took it, swallowed it, and conceived Xie.
entries.literal: The three of them went to bathe; seeing the dark bird drop its egg, Jiandi took and swallowed it; thereby pregnant she bore Xie.

entries.zh: 契長而佐禹治水有功。
entries.en: When Xie came of age he helped Yu manage the flood and earned distinction.
entries.literal: Xie grew up and assisted Yu in regulating the waters with merit.

entries.zh: 帝舜乃命契曰：「百姓不親，五品不訓，汝為司徒而敬敷五教，五教在寬。」
entries.en: Emperor Shun appointed Xie and said, "The people are estranged, and the five relationships are not guided. As Minister of Education, spread the five teachings with generous patience."
entries.literal: Emperor Shun then charged Xie, saying, "The people lack affection; the five relationships lack instruction. You shall be Minister of Education and reverently spread the five teachings—the five teachings lie in generosity."

entries.zh: 封于商，賜姓子氏。
entries.en: He received the fief of Shang and the clan name Zi.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed at Shang and granted the surname Zi.

entries.zh: 契興於唐、虞、大禹之際，功業著於百姓，百姓以平。
entries.en: He rose in the age of Yao, Shun, and Yu the Great; his achievements won renown among the people, and the realm was at peace.
entries.literal: He flourished in the time of Yao, Shun, and Great Yu; his deeds won renown among the people and kept the realm at peace.

entries.zh: 太后欲王呂氏，先立孝惠後宮子彊為淮陽王，子不疑為常山王，子山為襄城侯，子朝為軹侯，子武為壺關侯。
entries.en: Empress Lü wished to make Lü clan kings. She first established Emperor Xiaohui's rear palace son Qiang as the King of Huaiyang, son Buyi as the King of Changshan, son Shan as Lord Xiangcheng, son Zhao as Lord Zhi, son Wu as Lord Huguan.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager wished to make Lü clan kings. She first established Emperor Xiaohui's rear palace son Qiang as King of Huaiyang, son Buyi as King of Changshan, son Shan as Lord Xiangcheng, son Zhao as Lord Zhi, son Wu as Lord Huguan.

entries.zh: 太后風大臣，大臣請立酈侯呂臺為呂王，太后許之。
entries.en: Empress Lü hinted to the ministers. The ministers requested to establish Lord Li Lü Tai as King Lü. Empress Lü permitted it.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager hinted to the ministers. The ministers requested to establish Lord Li Lü Tai as King Lü. The Empress Dowager permitted it.

entries.zh: 建成康侯釋之卒，嗣子有罪，廢，立其弟呂祿為胡陵侯，續康侯後。
entries.en: Marquis Kang of Jiancheng, Lü Shizhi, died. His heir committed crimes and was stripped of rank, so she established his younger brother Lü Lu as Marquis of Huling to continue the line.
entries.literal: Lord Kang of Jiancheng Lü Shizhi passed. His heir son had crime. He was abolished. She established his younger brother Lü Lu as Lord Hu Ling to continue the Lord Kang's posterity.

entries.zh: 二年，常山王薨，以其弟襄城侯山為常山王，更名義。
entries.en: In the second year, the King of Changshan died. She made his younger brother, the Marquis of Xiangcheng, king of Changshan, changing his name to Yi.
entries.literal: In the second year, King of Changshan passed. She made his younger brother Lord Xiangcheng Shan the King of Changshan. She changed his name to Yi.

entries.zh: 十一月，呂王臺薨，謚為肅王，太子嘉代立為王。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, King Lü Tai died. He was given the posthumous title King Su, and Crown Prince Jia succeeded him as king.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, King Lü Tai passed. He was given the posthumous title King Su. Crown prince Jia was established to substitute as king.

entries.zh: 三年，無事。
entries.en: In the third year, nothing of note occurred.
entries.literal: In the third year, there were no events.

entries.zh: 四年，封呂媭為臨光侯，呂他為俞侯，呂更始為贅其侯，呂忿為呂城侯，及諸侯丞相五人。
entries.en: In the fourth year, she enfeoffed Lü Xu as Marquis of Linguang, Lü Ta as Marquis of Yu, Lü Gengshi as Marquis of Zhuiji, Lü Fen as Marquis of Lücheng, and also enfeoffed five chancellors as marquises.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, she enfeoffed Lü Xu as Lord Lin Guang, Lü Ta as Lord Yu, Lü Gengshi as Lord Zhui Qi, Lü Fen as Lord Lü Cheng, and five chancellors of the various marquises.

entries.zh: 宣平侯女為孝惠皇后時，無子，詳為有身，取美人子名之，殺其母，立所名子為太子。
entries.en: When the daughter of Marquis Xuanping became Emperor Xiaohui's empress, she bore no sons. She feigned pregnancy, took a handsome woman's son and claimed him as her own, killed the mother, and established the child as crown prince.
entries.literal: When the daughter of Marquis Xuanping was Emperor Xiaohui's empress, she had no sons. She feigned pregnancy. She took a beautiful woman's son and named him as her own. She killed the mother. She established the named son as crown prince.

entries.zh: 孝惠崩，太子立為帝。
entries.en: After Emperor Xiaohui died, the crown prince was enthroned.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaohui passed. The crown prince was established as emperor.

entries.zh: 帝壯，或聞其母死，非真皇后子，乃出言曰：「后安能殺吾母而名我？
entries.en: When the emperor grew older, he learned that his mother had died and that he was not truly the empress's son. He then said aloud, "How could the empress have killed my mother and called me her son?
entries.literal: When the emperor grew older, he heard that his mother had died and that he was not truly the empress's son. He then spoke out, saying: "How could the empress have killed my mother and called me her son?

entries.zh: 我未壯，壯即為變。」
entries.en: When I come of age, there will be a reckoning."
entries.literal: When I am grown, there will be a reckoning."

entries.zh: 太后聞而患之，恐其為亂，乃幽之永巷中，言帝病甚，左右莫得見。
entries.en: Empress Lü heard and was worried by it. She feared he would cause disorder. She imprisoned him in the Yongxiang. She said the emperor's illness was severe. His attendants could not see him.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager heard and was worried by it. She feared he would cause disorder. She then imprisoned him in the Yongxiang. She said the emperor's illness was severe. His attendants could not see him.

entries.zh: 太后曰：「凡有天下治為萬民命者，蓋之如天，容之如地，上有歡心以安百姓，百姓欣然以事其上，歡欣交通而天下治。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager said, "Whoever holds the realm and governs for the myriad people covers them as heaven does and bears them as earth does. The ruler above has a joyful heart to settle the people; the people below gladly serve their ruler. Joy flows between them and the realm is governed.
entries.literal: The empress dowager said: "Whoever holds the realm and governs for the myriad people covers them as heaven does and bears them as earth does. Above, there is a joyful heart to settle the people; below, the people gladly serve their ruler. Joy flows between them and the realm is governed.

entries.zh: 今皇帝病久不已，乃失惑惛亂，不能繼嗣奉宗廟祭祀，不可屬天下，其代之。」
entries.en: Now the emperor has long been ill, confused, and delirious, unable to continue the succession and tend the ancestral temples and sacrifices. He cannot be entrusted with the realm. Let another replace him."
entries.literal: Now the emperor has long been ill, confused and delirious, unable to continue the succession and tend the ancestral temples and sacrifices. He cannot be entrusted with the realm. Let another replace him."

entries.zh: 群臣皆頓首言：「皇太后為天下齊民計所以安宗廟社稷甚深，群臣頓首奉詔。」
entries.en: The ministers all bowed and said, "The Empress Dowager, for the sake of the realm and the people, has deeply considered how to secure the ancestral temples and altars of state. We bow and accept the decree."
entries.literal: The ministers all bowed their heads and said: "The empress dowager, for the sake of the realm and the people, has deeply considered how to secure the ancestral temples and altars of state. We bow our heads and accept the decree."

entries.zh: 帝廢位，太后幽殺之。
entries.en: The emperor's position was abolished. Empress Lü imprisoned and killed him.
entries.literal: The emperor's position was abolished. The Empress Dowager imprisoned and killed him.

entries.zh: 五月丙辰，立常山王義為帝，更名曰弘。
entries.en: In the fifth month, on the bingchen day, King Yi of Changshan was enthroned as emperor under the personal name Hong.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, bingchen day, King Yi of Changshan was established as emperor. His name was changed to Hong.

entries.zh: 不稱元年者，以太后制天下事也。
entries.en: It was not called the first year because the empress dowager controlled state affairs.
entries.literal: He did not call it the first year because the Empress Dowager controlled world affairs.

entries.zh: 以軹侯朝為常山王。
entries.en: Lord Zhi Zhao became the King of Changshan.
entries.literal: Lord Zhi Zhao became King of Changshan.

entries.zh: 置太尉官，絳侯勃為太尉。
entries.en: The office of Grand Commandant was created, and Zhou Bo, Marquis of Jiang, was appointed to it.
entries.literal: The office of Grand Commandant was established, and Bo, Marquis of Jiang, became Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 五年八月，淮陽王薨，以弟壺關侯武為淮陽王。
entries.en: In the fifth year, eighth month, the King of Huaiyang passed. His younger brother Lord Huguan Wu became the King of Huaiyang.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, eighth month, King of Huaiyang passed. His younger brother Lord Huguan Wu became King of Huaiyang.

entries.zh: 六年十月，太后曰呂王嘉居處驕恣，廢之，以肅王臺弟呂產為呂王。
entries.en: In the sixth year, tenth month, the empress dowager said King Lü Jia was arrogant and lawless in his residence and conduct, deposed him, and made Lü Chan, younger brother of King Su Lü Tai, King of Lü.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, tenth month, the Empress Dowager said King Lü Jia's dwelling and conduct were arrogant and unrestrained. She abolished him. King Su Tai's younger brother Lü Chan became King Lü.

entries.zh: 夏，赦天下。
entries.en: In summer, there was a general amnesty throughout the realm.
entries.literal: In summer, there was an amnesty for the world.

entries.zh: 封齊悼惠王子興居為東牟侯。
entries.en: Xingju, another son of King Daohui of Qi, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongmou.
entries.literal: Xingju, son of King Daohui of Qi, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongmou.

entries.zh: 呂祿、呂產欲發亂關中，內憚絳侯、朱虛等，外畏齊、楚兵，又恐灌嬰畔之，欲待灌嬰兵與齊合而發，猶豫未決。
entries.en: Lü Lu and Lü Chan wished to raise rebellion in Guanzhong. Within they feared the Marquis of Jiang and the Marquis of Zhuxu; without they feared the troops of Qi and Chu; they also feared Guan Ying would turn against them. They wished to wait until Guan Ying's troops joined Qi before acting, but hesitated and could not decide.
entries.literal: Lü Lu and Lü Chan wished to raise rebellion in Guanzhong. Within they feared the Marquis of Jiang and the Marquis of Zhuxu; without they feared the troops of Qi and Chu; they also feared that Guan Ying would turn against them. They wished to wait until Guan Ying's troops joined with Qi before acting, but hesitated and could not decide.

entries.zh: 當是時，濟川王太、淮陽王武、常山王朝名為少帝弟，及魯元王呂后外孫，皆年少未之國，居長安。
