entries.en: At this time the kings of Jichuan, Huaiyang, and Changshan—named as the Young Emperor's younger brothers—and the King of Lu, the Empress Dowager's grandson by a daughter, were all young and had not gone to their states; they lived in Chang'an.
entries.literal: At this time the kings of Jichuan, Huaiyang, and Changshan, named as the younger brothers of the Young Emperor, and the King of Lu, the empress dowager's grandson by a daughter, were all young and had not gone to their states; they dwelt in Chang'an.

entries.zh: 趙王祿、梁王產各將兵居南北軍，皆呂氏之人。
entries.en: The King of Zhao, Lu, and the King of Liang, Chan, each commanded troops and held the northern and southern armies—all were of the Lü clan.
entries.literal: The King of Zhao, Lu, and the King of Liang, Chan, each commanded troops and held the northern and southern armies; all were men of the Lü clan.

entries.zh: 列侯群臣莫自堅其命。
entries.en: None of the marquises or ministers felt his life was safe.
entries.literal: None of the ranked marquises and ministers could make his own life secure.

entries.zh: 呂太后者，高祖微時妃也，生孝惠帝、女魯元太后。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Lü was Gaozu's consort from his humble days. She bore Emperor Xiaohui and a daughter, Princess Yuan of Lu.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Lü was Gaozu's consort during his humble times. She gave birth to Emperor Xiaohui and a daughter, Princess Yuan of Lu.

entries.zh: 及高祖為漢王，得定陶戚姬，愛幸，生趙隱王如意。
entries.en: When Gaozu became King of Han, he took Consort Qi of Dingtao into favor. He doted on her, and she bore Ruyi, later King Yin of Zhao.
entries.literal: When Gaozu became Han King, he obtained Concubine Qi from Dingtao. He loved and favored her. She gave birth to King Yin of Zhao, Ruyi.

entries.zh: 孝惠為人仁弱，高祖以為不類我，常欲廢太子，立戚姬子如意，如意類我。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaohui was benevolent and weak. Gaozu considered him unlike himself. He often wished to abolish the crown prince and establish Concubine Qi's son Ruyi, for Ruyi was like him.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaohui was benevolent and weak as a person. Gaozu considered him unlike himself. He often wished to abolish the crown prince and establish Concubine Qi's son Ruyi, for Ruyi was like him.

entries.zh: 戚姬幸，常從上之關東，日夜啼泣，欲立其子代太子。
entries.en: Concubine Qi was in high favor and regularly accompanied the emperor east of the passes. She wept day and night, pleading for her son to replace the crown prince.
entries.literal: Concubine Qi was favored. She often followed the emperor to Guandong. Day and night she wept and cried, wishing to establish her son to replace the crown prince.

entries.zh: 呂后年長，常留守，希見上，益疏。
entries.en: Empress Lü was older and was frequently left behind to guard the capital, so she rarely saw the emperor and grew increasingly estranged.
entries.literal: Empress Lü was older. She often stayed to defend. She rarely saw the emperor. She became increasingly distant.

entries.zh: 如意立為趙王後，幾代太子者數矣，賴大臣爭之，及留侯策，太子得毋廢。
entries.en: After Ruyi was made King of Zhao, he came close several times to replacing the crown prince. Only the ministers' resistance and Marquis of Liu's strategy kept the crown prince from being deposed.
entries.literal: After Ruyi was established as King of Zhao, he nearly replaced the crown prince several times. It relied on ministers contending against it, and Marquis Liu's strategy, that the crown prince was not abolished.

entries.zh: 昌至渭橋，丞相以下皆迎。
entries.en: When Song Chang reached the Wei Bridge, the chancellor and all below him came to welcome him.
entries.literal: When Chang reached the Wei Bridge, the Chancellor and all below him came to welcome him.

entries.zh: 宋昌還報。
entries.en: Song Chang returned and reported.
entries.literal: Song Chang returned and reported.

entries.zh: 代王馳至渭橋，群臣拜謁稱臣。
entries.en: The King of Dai rode swiftly to Wei Bridge, where the ministers bowed before him and acknowledged themselves as his subjects.
entries.literal: The King of Dai hurried to Wei Bridge, where the ministers bowed in audience and called themselves his subjects.

entries.zh: 代王下車拜。
entries.en: The King of Dai dismounted from his carriage and returned the bow.
entries.literal: The King of Dai got down from his carriage and bowed.

entries.zh: 太尉勃進曰：「願請閒言。」
entries.en: Grand Marshal Bo stepped forward and said: 'I wish to speak with you privately.'
entries.literal: Grand Marshal Bo stepped forward and said: 'I wish to request a private word.'

entries.zh: 宋昌曰：「所言公，公言之。
entries.en: Song Chang said: 'If it's a public matter, speak it openly.
entries.literal: Song Chang said: 'If what is spoken is public, let the gentleman speak it openly.

entries.zh: 所言私，王者不受私。」
entries.en: If it's a private matter, kings do not accept private communications.'
entries.literal: If what is spoken is private, a king does not accept private communications.'

entries.zh: 太尉乃跪上天子璽符。
entries.en: The Grand Marshal knelt and offered him the imperial seal and tally.
entries.literal: The Grand Marshal then knelt and presented the Son of Heaven's seal and tally.

entries.zh: 代王謝曰：「至代邸而議之。」
entries.en: The King of Dai refused for the moment: "We can discuss this once we reach the Dai residence."
entries.literal: The King of Dai declined, saying, "We will discuss this when we reach the Dai residence."

entries.zh: 遂馳入代邸。
entries.en: He galloped into the Dai residence.
entries.literal: He then galloped into the Dai residence.

entries.zh: 群臣從至。
entries.en: The ministers followed and arrived.
entries.literal: The ministers followed and arrived.

entries.zh: 丞相陳平、太尉周勃、大將軍陳武、御史大夫張蒼、宗正劉郢、朱虛侯劉章、東牟侯劉興居、典客劉揭皆再拜言曰：「子弘等皆非孝惠帝子，不當奉宗廟。
entries.en: Chancellor Chen Ping, Grand Marshal Zhou Bo, General-in-Chief Chen Wu, Grandee Secretary Zhang Cang, Imperial Clan Administrator Liu Ying, Marquis Zhu Xu Liu Zhang, Marquis Dong Mou Liu Xingju, and Court Guests Receptionist Liu Jie all bowed twice and said: 'Zi Hong and the others are not sons of Emperor Xiaohui and should not serve at the ancestral temple.
entries.literal: Chancellor Chen Ping, Grand Marshal Zhou Bo, General-in-Chief Chen Wu, Grandee Secretary Zhang Cang, Imperial Clan Administrator Liu Ying, Marquis Zhu Xu Liu Zhang, Marquis Dongmou Liu Xingju, and Court Receptionist Liu Jie all bowed twice and said: 'Zi Hong and the others are not sons of Emperor Xiaohui and ought not serve at the ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 臣謹請（與）陰安侯列侯頃王后與瑯邪王、宗室、大臣、列侯、吏二千石議曰：『大王高帝長子，宜為高帝嗣。』
entries.en: We ministers respectfully request that this be discussed with the Marquis of Yin'an, the ranked marquises, the Queen Dowager of King Qing, the King of Langye, the imperial clan, the great ministers, marquises, and officials of 2,000 shi. They have said: 'Your Majesty is Emperor Gao's eldest son and should succeed Emperor Gao.'
entries.literal: We ministers respectfully request to discuss this with the Marquis of Yin'an, the ranked marquises, the Queen Dowager of King Qing, the King of Langye, the imperial clan, the great ministers, marquises, and officials of two thousand shi, who have said: 'Your Majesty is Emperor Gao's eldest son and ought to succeed Emperor Gao.'

entries.zh: 願大王即天子位。」
entries.en: We wish Your Majesty to immediately ascend the imperial throne.'
entries.literal: We wish Your Majesty to immediately ascend the Son of Heaven's position.'

entries.zh: 代王曰：「奉高帝宗廟，重事也。
entries.en: The King of Dai said: 'Serving at Emperor Gao's ancestral temple is a grave matter.
entries.literal: The King of Dai said: 'To serve at Emperor Gao's ancestral temple is a grave matter.

entries.zh: 寡人不佞，不足以稱宗廟。
entries.en: I am unworthy and cannot bear the charge of serving the ancestral temple.
entries.literal: I am untalented and insufficient to serve at the ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 願請楚王計宜者，寡人不敢當。」
entries.en: I wish to request that the King of Chu be consulted on what is appropriate. I do not dare to accept.'
entries.literal: I wish to request that the King of Chu be consulted on what is fitting; I do not dare accept.'

entries.zh: 群臣皆伏固請。
entries.en: All the court ministers prostrated themselves and pressed their request hard.
entries.literal: All the ministers prostrated themselves and firmly requested.

entries.zh: 代王西鄉讓者三，南鄉讓者再。
entries.en: The King of Dai declined three times while facing west and twice while facing south.
entries.literal: The King of Dai declined three times while facing west, and declined twice while facing south.

entries.zh: 丞相平等皆曰：「臣伏計之，大王奉高帝宗廟最宜稱，雖天下諸侯萬民以為宜。
entries.en: Chancellor Ping and the others said: 'We ministers have considered this carefully. Your Majesty is the proper and worthy one to serve at Emperor Gao's ancestral temple, and the feudal lords and people throughout the realm all agree.
entries.literal: Chancellor Ping and the others all said: 'We ministers have prostrated ourselves and considered the matter: Your Majesty is most fitting and worthy to serve at Emperor Gao's ancestral temple, and though the feudal lords and the myriad people of the realm all consider it fitting.

entries.zh: 臣等為宗廟社稷計，不敢忽。
entries.en: For the sake of the ancestral temple and the state, we ministers dare not be negligent.
entries.literal: We ministers, for the sake of the ancestral temple and the state, dare not be negligent.

entries.zh: 願大王幸聽臣等。
entries.en: We beg Your Majesty to hear your ministers.
entries.literal: May Your Majesty graciously listen to us, your ministers.

entries.zh: 臣謹奉天子璽符再拜上。」
entries.en: We ministers respectfully present the imperial seal and tally, bowing twice in offering.'
entries.literal: We ministers respectfully present the Son of Heaven's seal and tally, bowing twice in offering.'

entries.zh: 代王曰：「宗室將相王列侯以為莫宜寡人，寡人不敢辭。」
entries.en: The King of Dai said: 'If the imperial clan, generals, chancellors, kings, and marquises all consider me the most suitable, I dare not decline.'
entries.literal: The King of Dai said: 'The imperial clan, generals, chancellors, kings, and marquises all consider none more fitting than I; I do not dare decline.'

entries.zh: 遂即天子位。
entries.en: He immediately ascended the imperial throne.
entries.literal: He then immediately ascended the imperial throne.

entries.zh: 濟北王興居聞帝之代，欲往擊胡，乃反，發兵欲襲滎陽。
entries.en: When Xingju, King of Jibei, heard of the emperor’s succession, he used the campaign against the Hu as a pretext to rebel, raising troops to strike Xingyang.
entries.literal: Jibei King Xingju heard of the emperor's succession, desired to go attack the Hu, then rebelled, raising troops desiring to attack Xingyang.

entries.zh: 於是詔罷丞相兵，遣棘蒲侯陳武為大將軍，將十萬往擊之。
entries.en: At that point an edict dismissed the Chancellor's troops and dispatched the Marquis of Jipu, Chen Wu, as General-in-Chief, leading 100,000 troops to attack them.
entries.literal: Thereupon an edict dismissed the Chancellor's troops and dispatched the Marquis of Jipu, Chen Wu, as General-in-Chief, leading 100,000 troops to attack them.

entries.zh: 祁侯賀為將軍，軍滎陽。
entries.en: The Marquis of Qi, he, became general and was stationed at Xingyang.
entries.literal: The Marquis of Qi, He, became general and was stationed at Xingyang.

entries.zh: 七月辛亥，帝自太原至長安。
entries.en: On the xinhai day of the seventh month, the emperor went from Taiyuan to Chang'an.
entries.literal: Seventh month Xinhai, emperor from Taiyuan to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 乃詔有司曰：「濟北王背德反上，詿誤吏民，為大逆。
entries.en: Then an edict to the officials said: 'The King of Jibei has turned his back on virtue and rebelled against the emperor, deceiving and misleading officials and people, committing great rebellion.
entries.literal: Then edict officials said: 'Jibei King turned virtue rebelled emperor, deceived misled officials people, became great rebellion.

entries.zh: 濟北吏民兵未至先自定，及以軍地邑降者，皆赦之，復官爵。
entries.en: Jibei officials, and people, and troops who settled themselves before the army arrived, and those who surrendered with army lands and towns, shall all be pardoned and have their offices and nobility restored.
entries.literal: Jibei officials, people, and troops who settled themselves before the army arrived, and those who surrendered with army lands and towns, shall all be pardoned and have their offices and nobility restored.

entries.zh: 與王興居去來，亦赦之。」
entries.en: Those who came and went with King Xingju shall also be pardoned.'
entries.literal: With king Xingju come and go, also pardon them.'

entries.zh: 八月，破濟北軍，虜其王。
entries.en: In the eighth month, the Jibei army was defeated, and their king was captured.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, the Jibei army was defeated and their king captured.

entries.zh: 赦濟北諸吏民與王反者。
entries.en: The officials and people of Jibei who had joined the king in rebellion were pardoned.
entries.literal: Pardon the officials and people of Jibei who rebelled with the king.

entries.zh: 孝文皇帝，高祖中子也。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowen was Gaozu's middle son.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaowen was Gaozu's middle son.

entries.zh: 高祖十一年春，已破陳豨軍，定代地，立為代王，都中都。
entries.en: In the spring of Gaozu's eleventh year, after defeating Chen Xi's army and pacifying the Dai region, he was made King of Dai with his capital at Zhongdu.
entries.literal: In the spring of Gaozu's eleventh year, after defeating Chen Xi's army and pacifying the Dai region, he was established as King of Dai with his capital at Zhongdu.

entries.zh: 太后薄氏子。
entries.en: His mother was Empress Dowager Bo.
entries.literal: He was the son of Empress Dowager Bo.

entries.zh: 即位十七年，高后八年七月，高后崩。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year of his reign as king, in the seventh month of Empress Gao's eighth year, Empress Gao died.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year after he took the throne, in the seventh month of Empress Gao's eighth year, Empress Gao passed away.

entries.zh: 九月，諸呂呂產等欲為亂，以危劉氏，大臣共誅之，謀召立代王，事在呂后語中。
entries.en: In the ninth month, Lü clansmen led by Lü Chan plotted rebellion against the Liu house. The ministers executed them and then planned to summon and enthrone the King of Dai; details are in the Annals of Empress Dowager Lü.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, the Lü clansmen led by Lü Chan plotted rebellion to endanger the Liu clan. The ministers executed them together and plotted to summon and establish the King of Dai. This matter is detailed in the Lü Empress Dowager's biography.

entries.zh: 孝景皇帝者，孝文之中子也。
entries.en: Emperor Jing was the middle son of Emperor Wen.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaojing was the middle son of Emperor Xiaowen.

entries.zh: 母竇太后。
entries.en: His mother was Empress Dowager Dou.
entries.literal: His mother was Empress Dowager Dou.

entries.zh: 孝文在代時，前后有三男，及竇太后得幸，前后死，及三子更死，故孝景得立。
entries.en: While Emperor Wen was still in Dai, he had three sons by his former consort. After Lady Dou won his favor, that consort died, and the three sons died in turn as well. This was how Emperor Jing came to be named heir.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen was in Dai, he had three sons by his former queen. After Empress Dowager Dou gained his favor, the former queen died, and the three sons also died one after another. Therefore, Emperor Xiaojing was able to be established.

entries.zh: 後三年十月，日月皆（食）赤五日。
entries.en: In the tenth month of the third year of the later period, both the sun and the moon appeared red for five days.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of the later period, the sun and moon were both red for five days.

entries.zh: 十二月晦，雷。
entries.en: There was thunder on the last day of the twelfth month.
entries.literal: Twelfth month last day, thunder.

entries.zh: 日如紫。
entries.en: The sun appeared purple.
entries.literal: Sun like purple.

entries.zh: 五星逆行守太微。
entries.en: The five planets moved in retrograde motion and lingered near Taiwei.
entries.literal: The five planets moved retrograde and guarded Taiwei.

entries.zh: 月貫天廷中。
entries.en: The moon passed through the center of the Heavenly Court constellation.
entries.literal: The moon passed through the center of the Heavenly Court.

entries.zh: 正月甲寅，皇太子冠。
entries.en: On the jiayin day of the first month, the crown prince underwent his coming-of-age capping ceremony.
entries.literal: In the first month, on the jiayin day, the imperial crown prince underwent the capping ceremony.

entries.zh: 甲子，孝景皇帝崩。
entries.en: On the jiazi day, Emperor Jing passed away.
entries.literal: On the jiazi day, Emperor Xiaojing died.

entries.zh: 遺詔賜諸侯王以下至民為父後爵一級，天下戶百錢。
entries.en: In his final edict, he granted one grade of noble rank to feudal kings and everyone below them, down to commoners who inherited their fathers' households, and gave one hundred cash to every household in the empire.
entries.literal: His testamentary edict bestowed one grade of noble rank on feudal kings and those below them, down to commoners who were heirs to their fathers, and gave one hundred cash to each household under Heaven.

entries.zh: 出宮人歸其家，復無所與。
entries.en: He released palace women to return to their homes, exempting them from further obligations.
entries.literal: He released palace women to return to their homes, restoring the households that had no one to depend on.

entries.zh: 太子即位，是為孝武皇帝。
entries.en: The crown prince ascended the throne; this was Emperor Wu.
entries.literal: The crown prince ascended the throne; this was Emperor Xiaowu.

entries.zh: 三月，封皇太后弟蚡為武安侯，弟勝為周陽侯。
entries.en: In the third month, he enfeoffed Tian Fen, the Empress Dowager's younger brother, as Marquis of Wuan, and Tian Sheng, another younger brother, as Marquis of Zhouyang.
entries.literal: In the third month, he enfeoffed Fen, younger brother of the Empress Dowager, as Marquis of Wuan, and her younger brother Sheng as Marquis of Zhouyang.

entries.zh: 置陽陵。
entries.en: He established Yangling.
entries.literal: He established Yangling.

entries.zh: 三年正月乙巳，赦天下。
entries.en: In the first month of his third year, on the yisi day, he granted a general amnesty throughout the empire.
entries.literal: In the first month of the third year, on the yisi day, he granted amnesty to all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 長星出西方。
entries.en: A comet appeared in the west.
entries.literal: A long star appeared in the west.

entries.zh: 天火燔雒陽東宮大殿城室。
entries.en: A fire from the sky consumed the great hall and other buildings in Luoyang's Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: Heavenly fire burned the great hall and buildings of the Eastern Palace at Luoyang.

entries.zh: 吳王濞、楚王戊、趙王遂、膠西王卬、濟南王辟光、菑川王賢、膠東王雄渠反，發兵西鄉。
entries.en: The Kings Bi of Wu, Wu of Chu, Sui of Zhao, Ang of Jiaoxi, Piguang of Jinan, Xian of Zichuan, and Xiongqu of Jiaodong rebelled, raised armies, and marched west.
entries.literal: King Bi of Wu, King Wu of Chu, King Sui of Zhao, King Ang of Jiaoxi, King Piguang of Jinan, King Xian of Zichuan, and King Xiongqu of Jiaodong rebelled, raised troops, and faced west.

entries.zh: 天子為誅晁錯，遣袁盎諭告，不止，遂西圍梁。
entries.en: The emperor executed Chao Cuo on their account and sent Yuan Ang to explain his decision and admonish them. They still did not stop, and went west to besiege Liang.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven executed Chao Cuo for their sake and sent Yuan Ang to explain and admonish them, but they did not stop, and then went west to besiege Liang.

entries.zh: 上乃遣大將軍竇嬰、太尉周亞夫將兵誅之。
entries.en: The emperor then sent Grand General Dou Ying and Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu to lead troops and suppress the rebellion.
entries.literal: The emperor then sent Grand General Dou Ying and Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu to lead troops and punish them.

entries.zh: 六月乙亥。
entries.en: On yihai in the sixth month.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on the yihai day.

entries.zh: 赦亡軍及楚元王子藝等與謀反者。
entries.en: He pardoned deserters, along with Yi, son of King Yuan of Chu, and others who had taken part in the conspiracy.
entries.literal: He granted amnesty to deserters and to Yi, son of King Yuan of Chu, and the others who had conspired in rebellion.

entries.zh: 封大將軍竇嬰為魏其侯。
entries.en: He enfeoffed Grand General Dou Ying as the Marquis of Weiqi.
entries.literal: Enfeoffed Grand General Dou Ying as Marquis of Weiqi.

entries.zh: 立楚元王子平陸侯禮為楚王。
entries.en: He installed Li, son of King Yuan of Chu and Marquis of Pinglu, as King of Chu.
entries.literal: He established Li, son of King Yuan of Chu and Marquis of Pinglu, as King of Chu.

entries.zh: 立皇子端為膠西王，子勝為中山王。
entries.en: He installed his son Duan as the King of Jiaoxi and his son Sheng as the King of Zhongshan.
entries.literal: Installed imperial son Duan as the King of Jiaoxi, son Sheng as the King of Zhongshan.

entries.zh: 徙濟北王志為菑川王，淮陽王餘為魯王，汝南王非為江都王。
entries.en: He transferred King Zhi of Jibei to Zichuan, King Yu of Huaiyang to Lu, and King Fei of Runan to Jiangdu.
entries.literal: He transferred King Zhi of Jibei to be King of Zichuan, King Yu of Huaiyang to be King of Lu, and King Fei of Runan to be King of Jiangdu.

entries.zh: 齊王將廬、燕王嘉皆薨。
entries.en: King Jianglu of Qi and King Jia of Yan both passed away.
entries.literal: King Jianglu of Qi and King Jia of Yan both died.

entries.zh: 元年四月乙卯，赦天下。
entries.en: In the fourth month of his first year, on the yimao day, he granted a general amnesty throughout the empire.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the first year, on the yimao day, he granted amnesty to all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 乙巳，賜民爵一級。
entries.en: On the yisi day, he granted the common people one grade of noble rank.
entries.literal: On the yisi day, he bestowed one grade of noble rank on the people.

entries.zh: 五月，除田半租，為孝文立太宗廟。
entries.en: In the fifth month, he abolished the half-tax on agricultural land and established the Taizong temple for Emperor Wen.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, he abolished the half land tax and established the Taizong temple for Emperor Xiaowen.

entries.zh: 令群臣無朝賀。
entries.en: He ordered the ministers to dispense with the court congratulations ceremony.
entries.literal: He ordered the assembled ministers not to offer court congratulations.

entries.zh: 匈奴入代，與約和親。
entries.en: The Xiongnu invaded Dai, and he made peace with them through a heqin marriage alliance.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu entered Dai, and he made a treaty of heqin with them.

entries.zh: 二年春，封故相國蕭何孫系為武陵侯。
entries.en: In the spring of his second year, he enfeoffed Xi, grandson of the former Chancellor Xiao He, as Marquis of Wuling.
entries.literal: In spring of the second year, he enfeoffed Xi, grandson of the former Chancellor Xiao He, as Marquis of Wuling.

entries.zh: 男子二十而得傅。
entries.en: Men became liable for service registration at age twenty.
entries.literal: Males received service registration at twenty.

entries.zh: 四月壬午，孝文太后崩。
entries.en: On the renwu day of the fourth month, Empress Dowager Xiaowen passed away.
entries.literal: In the fourth month, on the renwu day, Empress Dowager Xiaowen died.

entries.zh: 廣川、長沙王皆之國。
entries.en: The Kings of Guangchuan and Changsha both went to their fiefs.
entries.literal: The Kings of Guangchuan and Changsha both went to their states.

entries.zh: 丞相申屠嘉卒。
entries.en: Chancellor Shentu Jia passed away.
entries.literal: Chancellor Shentu Jia died.

entries.zh: 八月，以御史大夫開封陶青為丞相。
entries.en: In the eighth month, he appointed Tao Qing of Kaifeng, the Grandee Secretary, as Chancellor.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, he made Tao Qing of Kaifeng, the Grandee Secretary, Chancellor.

entries.zh: 彗星出東北。
entries.en: A comet appeared in the northeast.
entries.literal: A comet appeared in the northeast.

entries.zh: 秋，衡山雨雹，大者五寸，深者二尺。
entries.en: In autumn, hail fell in Hengshan, with the largest stones five cun across and accumulations two chi deep.
entries.literal: In autumn, hail fell in Hengshan; the largest stones were five cun, and the deepest accumulation was two chi.

entries.zh: 熒惑逆行，守北辰。
entries.en: Mars moved in retrograde motion and lingered near Beichen.
entries.literal: Mars moved retrograde and guarded Beichen.

entries.zh: 月出北辰閒。
entries.en: The moon appeared near Beichen.
entries.literal: The moon appeared among Beichen.

entries.zh: 歲星逆行天廷中。
entries.en: Jupiter moved in retrograde motion within the Heavenly Court constellation.
entries.literal: Jupiter moved retrograde within the Heavenly Court.

entries.zh: 置南陵及內史、祋祤為縣。
entries.en: He established Nanling, Neishi, and Duiyu as counties.
entries.literal: He established Nanling, and also Neishi and Duiyu, as counties.

entries.zh: 四年夏，立太子。
entries.en: In the summer of his fourth year, he established the crown prince.
entries.literal: Fourth year summer, established crown prince.

entries.zh: 立皇子徹為膠東王。
entries.en: He installed his son Che as King of Jiaodong.
entries.literal: Installed imperial son Che as King of Jiaodong.

entries.zh: 六月甲戌，赦天下。
entries.en: On the jiaxu day of the sixth month, he granted a general amnesty throughout the empire.
entries.literal: Sixth month jiaxu, granted amnesty to all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 後九月，更以（弋）［易］陽為陽陵。
entries.en: In the intercalary ninth month, he renamed Yiyang as Yangling.
entries.literal: In the intercalary ninth month, he changed Yiyang to Yangling.

entries.zh: 復置津關，用傳出入。
entries.en: He reestablished the ferry checkpoints and required travel passes for entry and exit.
entries.literal: He reestablished the ferry checkpoints and used travel passes for entry and exit.

entries.zh: 冬，以趙國為邯鄲郡。
entries.en: In winter, he converted the state of Zhao into Handan commandery.
entries.literal: Winter, made Zhao state into Handan commandery.

entries.zh: 五年三月，作陽陵、渭橋。
entries.en: In the third month of his fifth year, he built Yangling and the Wei Bridge.
entries.literal: In the third month of the fifth year, he built Yangling and the Wei Bridge.

entries.zh: 五月，募徙陽陵，予錢二十萬。
entries.en: In the fifth month, he recruited settlers for Yangling and gave them 200,000 cash.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, he recruited people to move to Yangling and gave them 200,000 cash.

entries.zh: 江都大暴風從西方來，壞城十二丈。
entries.en: At Jiangdu, a great gale came from the west and damaged twelve zhang of the city wall.
entries.literal: At Jiangdu, a great violent wind came from the west and damaged twelve zhang of the city wall.

entries.zh: 丁卯，封長公主子蟜為隆慮侯。
entries.en: On dingmao, he made Qiao, the eldest princess's son, Marquis of Longlu.
entries.literal: On the dingmao day, he enfeoffed Qiao, son of the eldest princess, as Marquis of Longlu.

entries.zh: 徙廣川王為趙王。
entries.en: He transferred the King of Guangchuan to become King of Zhao.
entries.literal: Transferred King of Guangchuan to be King of Zhao.

entries.zh: 六年春，封中尉（趙）綰為建陵侯，江都丞相嘉為建平侯，隴西太守渾邪為平曲侯，趙丞相嘉為江陵侯，故將軍布為鄃侯。
entries.en: In the spring of his sixth year, he enfeoffed Zhao Wan, the Commandant, as Marquis of Jianling; Jia, Chancellor of Jiangdu, as Marquis of Jianping; Hunye, Governor of Longxi, as Marquis of Pingqu; Jia, Chancellor of Zhao, as Marquis of Jiangling; and Bu, a former general, as Marquis of Shu.
entries.literal: In spring of the sixth year, he enfeoffed Commandant Zhao Wan as Marquis of Jianling, Jia the Chancellor of Jiangdu as Marquis of Jianping, Hunye the Governor of Longxi as Marquis of Pingqu, Jia the Chancellor of Zhao as Marquis of Jiangling, and Bu the former general as Marquis of Shu.

entries.zh: 梁楚二王皆薨。
entries.en: The Kings of Liang and Chu both passed away.
entries.literal: The two kings of Liang and Chu both passed away.

entries.zh: 後九月，伐馳道樹，殖蘭池。
entries.en: In the intercalary ninth month, he had trees cut down along the imperial highways and replanted by Orchid Pond.
entries.literal: In the intercalary ninth month, he cut down trees along the imperial highways and planted them by Orchid Pond.

entries.zh: 七年冬，廢栗太子為臨江王。
entries.en: In the winter of his seventh year, he deposed Crown Prince Li and made him King of Linjiang.
entries.literal: In winter of the seventh year, he deposed Crown Prince Li and made him King of Linjiang.

entries.zh: （一）十（二）［一］月晦，日有食之。
entries.en: On the last day of the eleventh month, there was a solar eclipse.
entries.literal: The eleventh month last day, the sun was eclipsed.

entries.zh: 春，免徒隸作陽陵者。
entries.en: In spring, he pardoned the convicts and bondservants working on the Yangling tomb.
entries.literal: In spring, he pardoned the convicts and bondservants working on Yangling.

entries.zh: 丞相青免。
entries.en: Chancellor Qing was dismissed from office.
entries.literal: Chancellor Qing was dismissed.

entries.zh: 二月乙巳，以太尉條侯周亞夫為丞相。
entries.en: On the yisi day of the second month, he appointed Zhou Yafu, Grand Commandant and Marquis of Tiao, as Chancellor.
entries.literal: In the second month, on the yisi day, he made Zhou Yafu, Grand Commandant and Marquis of Tiao, Chancellor.

entries.zh: 四月乙巳，立膠東王太后為皇后。
entries.en: On the yisi day of the fourth month, he established the mother of the King of Jiaodong as Empress.
entries.literal: In the fourth month, on the yisi day, he established the mother of the King of Jiaodong as Empress.

entries.zh: 丁巳，立膠東王為太子。
entries.en: On dingsi, he named the King of Jiaodong crown prince.
entries.literal: On the dingsi day, he established the King of Jiaodong as crown prince.

entries.zh: 名徹。
entries.en: His name was Che.
entries.literal: Named Che.

entries.zh: 中元年，封故御史大夫周苛孫平為繩侯，故御史大夫周昌（子）［孫］左車為安陽侯，四月乙巳，赦天下，賜爵一級。
entries.en: In the first year of the middle period, he enfeoffed Ping, grandson of the former Grandee Secretary Zhou Ke, as Marquis of Sheng, and Zuoju, grandson of the former Grandee Secretary Zhou Chang, as Marquis of Anyang. On the yisi day of the fourth month, he granted a general amnesty throughout the empire and bestowed one grade of noble rank.
entries.literal: In the first year of the middle period, he enfeoffed Ping, grandson of the former Grandee Secretary Zhou Ke, as Marquis of Sheng, and Zuoju, grandson of the former Grandee Secretary Zhou Chang, as Marquis of Anyang. In the fourth month, on the yisi day, he granted amnesty to all under Heaven and bestowed one grade of noble rank.

entries.zh: 除禁錮。
entries.en: He lifted the restrictions imposed by legal disabilities.
entries.literal: He abolished legal disabilities.

entries.zh: 地動。
entries.en: There was an earthquake.
entries.literal: Earth moved.

entries.zh: 衡山、原都雨雹，大者尺八寸。
entries.en: Hail fell at Hengshan and Yuandu, with the largest stones measuring one chi and eight cun across.
entries.literal: Hail fell at Hengshan and Yuandu, with the largest stones measuring one chi and eight cun.

entries.zh: 中二年二月，匈奴入燕，遂不和親。
entries.en: In the second month of the second year of the middle period, the Xiongnu invaded Yan, and he therefore abandoned heqin relations.
entries.literal: In the second month of the second year of the middle period, the Xiongnu entered Yan, and thereafter he did not maintain heqin relations.

entries.zh: 三月，召臨江王來。
entries.en: In the third month, he summoned the King of Linjiang to court.
entries.literal: In the third month, he summoned the King of Linjiang to come.

entries.zh: 即死中尉府中。
entries.en: He died there in the Commandant's office.
entries.literal: He then died in the Commandant's office.

entries.zh: 夏，立皇子越為廣川王，子寄為膠東王。
entries.en: That summer, he made his son Yue King of Guangchuan and his son Ji King of Jiaodong.
entries.literal: In summer, he established his son Yue as King of Guangchuan and his son Ji as King of Jiaodong.

entries.zh: 封四侯。
entries.en: He enfeoffed four marquises.
entries.literal: He enfeoffed four marquises.

entries.zh: 九月甲戌，日食。
entries.en: On the jiaxu day of the ninth month, there was a solar eclipse.
entries.literal: Ninth month jiaxu, solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 中三年冬，罷諸侯御史中丞。
entries.en: In the winter of the third year of the middle period, he abolished the office of Censor-in-Chief in the feudal states.
entries.literal: In winter of the third year of the middle period, he abolished the feudal lords' Censor-in-Chief offices.

entries.zh: 春，匈奴王二人率其徒來降，皆封為列侯。
entries.en: In spring, two Xiongnu kings led their followers in surrendering, and both were enfeoffed as full marquises.
entries.literal: In spring, two Xiongnu kings led their followers and came to surrender; both were enfeoffed as full marquises.

entries.zh: 中四年三月，置德陽宮。
entries.en: In the third month of the fourth year of the middle period, he established the Deyang Palace.
entries.literal: Middle fourth year third month, established Deyang Palace.

entries.zh: 大蝗。
entries.en: There was a great locust plague.
entries.literal: Great locusts.

entries.zh: 秋，赦徒作陽陵者。
entries.en: In autumn, he granted amnesty to convicts working on the Yangling tomb.
entries.literal: Autumn, granted amnesty to convicts working on Yangling.

entries.zh: 中五年夏，立皇子舜為常山王。
entries.en: In the summer of the fifth year of the middle period, he established his son Shun as King of Changshan.
entries.literal: Middle fifth year summer, established imperial son Shun as King of Changshan.

entries.zh: 封十侯。
entries.en: He enfeoffed ten marquises.
entries.literal: Enfeoffed ten marquises.

entries.zh: 六月丁巳，赦天下，賜爵一級。
entries.en: On the dingsi day of the sixth month, he granted a general amnesty throughout the empire and bestowed one grade of noble rank.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on the dingsi day, he granted amnesty to all under Heaven and bestowed one grade of noble rank.

entries.zh: 天下大潦。
entries.en: There were great floods throughout the empire.
entries.literal: All under Heaven great floods.

entries.zh: 更命諸侯丞相曰相。
entries.en: He changed the title of the feudal lords' chancellors, calling them simply xiang.
entries.literal: He changed the title of the feudal lords' chancellors to xiang.

entries.zh: 秋，地動。
entries.en: In autumn, there was an earthquake.
entries.literal: Autumn, earth moved.

entries.zh: 中六年二月己卯，行幸雍，郊見五帝。
entries.en: On the jimao day of the second month of the sixth year of the middle period, he traveled in imperial progress to Yong and performed the suburban sacrifices to the Five Emperors.
entries.literal: In the second month of the sixth year of the middle period, on the jimao day, he went in imperial progress to Yong and performed the suburban audience sacrifices to the Five Emperors.

entries.zh: 三月，雨雹。
entries.en: In the third month, it rained hail.
entries.literal: Third month, rained hail.

entries.zh: 四月，梁孝王、城陽共王、汝南王皆薨。
entries.en: In the fourth month, King Xiao of Liang, King Gong of Chengyang, and the King of Runan all passed away.
entries.literal: In the fourth month, King Xiao of Liang, King Gong of Chengyang, and the King of Runan all died.

entries.zh: 立梁孝王子明為濟川王，子彭離為濟東王，子定為山陽王，子不識為濟陰王。
entries.en: He established Ming, son of King Xiao of Liang, as King of Jichuan; Pengli as King of Jidong; Ding as King of Shanyang; and Bushi as King of Jiyin.
entries.literal: He established Ming, son of King Xiao of Liang, as King of Jichuan; his son Pengli as King of Jidong; his son Ding as King of Shanyang; and his son Bushi as King of Jiyin.

entries.zh: 梁分為五。
entries.en: The kingdom of Liang was divided into five parts.
entries.literal: Liang was divided into five.

entries.zh: 封四侯。
entries.en: He enfeoffed four marquises.
entries.literal: Enfeoffed four marquises.

entries.zh: 更命廷尉為大理，將作少府為將作大匠，主爵中尉為都尉，長信詹事為長信少府，將行為大長秋，大行為行人，奉常為太常，典客為大行，治粟內史為大農。
entries.en: He renamed several offices: the Commandant of Justice became Grand Judge; the Chamberlain for the Palace Buildings became Grand Artisan; the Commandant in Charge of Noble Ranks became Commandant; the Chamberlain for Changxin became Lesser Chamberlain of Changxin; the Jiangxing became Grand Changqiu; the Grand Herald became Traveller; the Fengchang became Grand Constant; the Superintendent of Guests became Grand Herald; and the Grain Intendant of the Capital became Grand Minister of Agriculture.
entries.literal: He changed the title of the Commandant of Justice to Grand Judge, the Chamberlain for the Palace Buildings to Grand Artisan, the Commandant in Charge of Noble Ranks to Commandant, the Chamberlain for Changxin to Lesser Chamberlain of Changxin, the Jiangxing to Grand Changqiu, the Grand Herald to Traveller, the Fengchang to Grand Constant, the Superintendent of Guests to Grand Herald, and the Grain Intendant of the Capital to Grand Minister of Agriculture.

entries.zh: 以大內為二千石，置左右內官，屬大內。
entries.en: He made the Grand Interior a two-thousand-shi office and established left and right interior officials under it.
entries.literal: He made the Grand Interior a two-thousand-shi office, and established left and right interior officials subordinate to the Grand Interior.

entries.zh: 七月辛亥，日食。
entries.en: On the xinhai day of the seventh month, there was a solar eclipse.
entries.literal: Seventh month xinhai, solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 八月，匈奴入上郡。
entries.en: In the eighth month, the Xiongnu invaded Shangjun commandery.
entries.literal: Eighth month, Xiongnu entered Shangjun.

entries.zh: 後元年冬，更命中大夫令為衛尉。
entries.en: In the winter of the first year of the later period, he renamed the Commander of the Palace Gentlemen as Commandant of the Guards.
entries.literal: In winter of the first year of the later period, he changed the title of Commander of the Palace Gentlemen to Commandant of the Guards.

entries.zh: 三月丁酉，赦天下，賜爵一級，中二千石、諸侯相爵右庶長。
entries.en: On the dingyou day of the third month, he granted a general amnesty throughout the empire and bestowed one grade of noble rank. Officials of middle two-thousand-shi rank and the chancellors of feudal lords received the rank of Right Shuzhang.
entries.literal: In the third month, on the dingyou day, he granted amnesty to all under Heaven and bestowed one grade of noble rank. Officials of middle two-thousand-shi rank and feudal lords' chancellors received the noble rank of Right Shuzhang.

entries.zh: 四月，大酺。
entries.en: In the fourth month, there was a great public celebration with drinking.
entries.literal: Fourth month, great assembly.

entries.zh: 五月丙戌，地動，其蚤食時復動。
entries.en: On the bingxu day of the fifth month, there was an earthquake, and it shook again at breakfast time.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, on the bingxu day, the earth moved, and it moved again at early-meal time.

entries.zh: 上庸地動二十二日，壞城垣。
entries.en: In Shangyong, the earth shook for twenty-two days and damaged the city walls.
entries.literal: Shangyong earth moved twenty-two days, damaged city walls.

entries.zh: 七月乙巳，日食。
entries.en: On the yisi day of the seventh month, there was a solar eclipse.
entries.literal: Seventh month yisi, solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 丞相劉舍免。
entries.en: Chancellor Liu She was dismissed from office.
entries.literal: Chancellor Liu She dismissed.

entries.zh: 八月壬辰，以御史大夫綰為丞相，封建陵侯。
entries.en: On the renchen day of the eighth month, he appointed Wan, the Grandee Secretary, as Chancellor and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Jianling.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, on the renchen day, he made Wan, the Grandee Secretary, Chancellor and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Jianling.

entries.zh: 後二年正月，地一日三動。
entries.en: In the first month of the second year of the later period, the earth shook three times in one day.
entries.literal: In the first month of the second year of the later period, the earth moved three times in one day.

entries.zh: 郅將軍擊匈奴。
entries.en: General Zhi attacked the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: General Zhi attacked the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 酺五日。
entries.en: There was a public drinking celebration for five days.
entries.literal: Drinking celebration five days.

entries.zh: 令內史郡不得食馬粟，沒入縣官。
entries.en: He ordered the Interior commanderies not to feed grain to horses; any such grain was to be confiscated for government use.
entries.literal: He ordered that the commanderies under the Interior not feed grain to horses, and that such grain be confiscated into government stores.

entries.zh: 令徒隸衣七緵布。
entries.en: He ordered convicts and bondservants to be dressed in seven-zong cloth.
entries.literal: He ordered convicts and bondservants to wear clothing made of seven-zong cloth.

entries.zh: 止馬舂。
entries.en: He ended the practice of using horses to pound grain.
entries.literal: He stopped the use of horses for pounding grain.

entries.zh: 為歲不登，禁天下食不造歲。
entries.en: Because the harvest had failed, he forbade people throughout the empire from eating grain that was not from the current year.
entries.literal: Because the harvest did not mature, he forbade all under Heaven from eating grain not produced in the current year.

entries.zh: 省列侯遣之國。
entries.en: He reduced the number of marquises at court and sent them back to their fiefs.
entries.literal: He reduced the marquises and sent them to their states.

entries.zh: 三月，匈奴入雁門。
entries.en: In the third month, the Xiongnu invaded Yanmen commandery.
entries.literal: Third month, Xiongnu entered Yanmen.

entries.zh: 十月，租長陵田。
entries.en: In the tenth month, he leased out the Changling fields for rent.
entries.literal: In the tenth month, he collected rent from the Changling fields.

entries.zh: 大旱。
entries.en: There was a great drought.
entries.literal: Great drought.

entries.zh: 衡山國、河東、雲中郡民疫。
entries.en: An epidemic struck the people of Hengshan state and the Hedong and Yunzhong commanderies.
entries.literal: The people of Hengshan state and of Hedong and Yunzhong commanderies suffered an epidemic.

entries.zh: 太史公曰：漢興，孝文施大德，天下懷安，至孝景，不復憂異姓，而晁錯刻削諸侯，遂使七國俱起，合從而西鄉，以諸侯太盛，而錯為之不以漸也。
entries.en: The Grand Historian says: When Han arose, Emperor Wen practiced great virtue, and the realm rested in peace. By Emperor Jing's time, there was no longer any fear of kings from other surnames. But Chao Cuo cut sharply into the power of the feudal lords, causing the seven states to rise together, join in alliance, and march west. The problem was that the feudal lords had grown too powerful, and Cuo did not proceed gradually.
entries.literal: The Grand Historian said: When the Han arose, Emperor Xiaowen practiced great virtue, and all under Heaven cherished peace. By Emperor Xiaojing, there was no longer anxiety over rulers of different surnames, but Chao Cuo sharply curtailed the feudal lords, and so caused the seven states to rise together, unite in alliance, and face west. This was because the feudal lords were too powerful, and Cuo acted without gradual steps.

entries.zh: 及主父偃言之，而諸侯以弱，卒以安。
entries.en: When Zhufu Yan later proposed his policy, the feudal lords were weakened, and the realm was finally at peace.
entries.literal: When Zhufu Yan spoke of it, the feudal lords were thereby weakened, and in the end there was peace.

entries.zh: 安危之機，豈不以謀哉？
entries.en: Surely the turning point between security and peril lies in policy and planning?
entries.literal: The pivot of safety and danger, is it not in planning?

entries.zh: 帝廑
entries.en: Emperor Jin
entries.literal: Emperor Jin

entries.zh: 文王昌生武王發。
entries.en: King Wen Chang fathered King Wu Fa.
entries.literal: King Wen Chang begot King Wu Fa.

entries.zh: 周武王代殷，從黃帝至武王十九世。
entries.en: When King Wu of Zhou replaced Yin, it was nineteen generations from the Yellow Emperor to King Wu.
entries.literal: King Wu of Zhou replaced Yin; from the Yellow Emperor to King Wu, nineteen generations.

entries.zh: 成王誦
entries.en: King Cheng (Song)
entries.literal: King Cheng Song

entries.zh: 魯周公旦，武王弟。初封。
entries.en: Lu: Zhou Gong Dan, younger brother of King Wu. First enfeoffment.
entries.literal: Lu Zhou Gong Dan, Wu Wang younger brother. First enfeoffed.

entries.zh: 齊太公尚，文王、武王師。初封。
entries.en: Qi: Tai Gong Shang, teacher of King Wen and King Wu. First enfeoffment.
entries.literal: Qi Tai Gong Shang, Wen Wang, Wu Wang teacher. First enfeoffed.

entries.zh: 晉唐叔虞，武王子。初封。
entries.en: Jin: Tang Shu Yu, son of King Wu. First enfeoffment.
entries.literal: Jin Tang Shu Yu, Wu Wang son. First enfeoffed.

entries.zh: 秦惡來，助紂。父飛廉，有力。
entries.en: Qin: E Lai, assisted King Zhou. Father Fei Lian, who was strong.
entries.literal: Qin E Lai, assisted Zhou. Father Fei Lian, had strength.

entries.zh: 楚熊繹。繹父鬻熊，事文王。初封。
entries.en: Chu: Xiong Yi. Yi's father Yu Xiong, who served King Wen. First enfeoffment.
entries.literal: Chu: Xiong Yi. Yi's father Yu Xiong served King Wen. First enfeoffment.

entries.zh: 宋微子啟，紂庶兄。初封。
entries.en: Song: Wei Zi Qi, elder brother of King Zhou by a concubine. First enfeoffment.
entries.literal: Song Wei Zi Qi, Zhou elder brother by concubine. First enfeoffed.

entries.zh: 衛康叔，武王弟。初封。
entries.en: Wei: Kang Shu, younger brother of King Wu. First enfeoffment.
entries.literal: Wei Kang Shu, Wu Wang younger brother. First enfeoffed.

entries.zh: 陳胡公滿，舜之後。初封。
entries.en: Chen: Hu Gong Man, descendant of Shun. First enfeoffment.
entries.literal: Chen Hu Gong Man, Shun's descendant. First enfeoffed.

entries.zh: 蔡叔度，武王弟。初封。
entries.en: Cai: Shu Du, younger brother of King Wu. First enfeoffment.
entries.literal: Cai Shu Du, Wu Wang younger brother. First enfeoffed.

entries.zh: 曹叔振鐸，武王弟。初封。
entries.en: Cao: Shu Zhen Duo, younger brother of King Wu. First enfeoffment.
entries.literal: Cao Shu Zhen Duo, Wu Wang younger brother. First enfeoffed.

entries.zh: 燕召公奭，周同姓。初封。
entries.en: Yan: Zhao Gong Shi, of the same surname as Zhou. First enfeoffment.
entries.literal: Yan Zhao Gong Shi, Zhou same surname. First enfeoffed.

entries.zh: 帝太甲，故太子太丁子。淫，伊尹放之桐宮。三年，悔過自責，伊尹乃迎之復位。
entries.en: Emperor Taijia, son of the former heir Taiding, was dissolute. Yi Yin confined him in the Tong Palace; after three years of repentance Yi Yin restored him.
entries.literal: Emperor Taijia, son of the former heir Taiding. He was dissolute; Yi Yin confined him in the Tong Palace. After three years he repented and blamed himself, and Yi Yin welcomed him back to the throne.

entries.zh: 帝沃丁。伊尹卒。
entries.en: Emperor Woding. Yi Yin died.
entries.literal: Emperor Woding. Yi Yin died.

entries.zh: 帝太戊，雍己弟。以桑穀生，稱中宗。
entries.en: Emperor Taiwu, Yongji's younger brother, was called Zhongzong because mulberry and grain grew together.
entries.literal: Emperor Taiwu, younger brother of Yongji. Because mulberry and grain grew together, he was called Zhongzong.

entries.zh: 帝武丁。雉升鼎耳雊。得傅說。稱高宗。
entries.en: Emperor Wuding. A pheasant perched on the tripod ear and crowed; he obtained Fuyue and was called Gaozong.
entries.literal: Emperor Wuding. A pheasant perched on the tripod ear and crowed. He obtained Fuyue. He was called Gaozong.

entries.zh: 康王釗，刑錯四十餘年。
entries.en: King Kang (Zhao): for more than forty years punishments were laid aside.
entries.literal: King Kang (Zhao); punishments were laid aside for more than forty years.

entries.zh: 魯公伯禽
entries.en: Lu: Duke Bo Qin
entries.literal: Lu Gong Bo Qin

entries.zh: 丁公呂伋
entries.en: Qi: Duke Ding, Lü Ji
entries.literal: Ding Gong Lü Ji

entries.zh: 晉侯燮
entries.en: Jin: Marquis Xie
entries.literal: Jin Hou Xie

entries.zh: 女防
entries.en: Nu Fang
entries.literal: Nu Fang

entries.zh: 熊乂
entries.en: Xiong Yi
entries.literal: Xiong Yi

entries.zh: 微仲，啟弟。
entries.en: Wei Zhong, younger brother of Qi.
entries.literal: Wei Zhong, Qi younger brother.

entries.zh: 康伯
entries.en: Kang Bo
entries.literal: Kang Bo

entries.zh: 申公
entries.en: Duke Shen
entries.literal: Shen Gong

entries.zh: 蔡仲
entries.en: Cai Zhong
entries.literal: Cai Zhong

entries.zh: 九世至惠侯。
entries.en: Nine generations to Marquis Hui.
entries.literal: Nine generations to Hui Hou.

entries.zh: 曰：「傳云天下之君王為萬夫之黔首請贖民之命者帝，有福萬世。
entries.en: He said, "The traditions say that the ruler of the world who, on behalf of the multitude, pleads to redeem the lives of the common people becomes an emperor and has good fortune for ten thousand generations.
entries.literal: He said: "The traditions say that the ruler of the world who pleads to redeem the lives of the common people on behalf of the masses becomes emperor and has good fortune for ten thousand generations.

entries.zh: 黃帝是也。
entries.en: The Yellow Emperor was such a one.
entries.literal: Yellow Emperor was such.

entries.zh: 五政明則修禮義，因天時舉兵征伐而利者王，有福千世。
entries.en: When the five forms of government are clear, one cultivates ritual and righteousness. Those who raise armies for campaigns in accord with Heaven's timing and thereby gain advantage become kings and have good fortune for a thousand generations.
entries.literal: When the five forms of government are clear, one cultivates ritual and righteousness; those who raise troops for campaigns according to Heaven's timing and gain advantage become kings and have good fortune for a thousand generations.

entries.zh: 蜀王，黃帝後世也，至今在漢西南五千里，常來朝降，輸獻於漢，非以其先之有德，澤流後世邪？
entries.en: The King of Shu was also a descendant of the Yellow Emperor. Even now, though he is five thousand li southwest of Han, he regularly comes to court, submits, and presents tribute to Han. Is this not because his ancestor possessed virtue and his grace flowed down to later generations?
entries.literal: The King of Shu was also a descendant of the Yellow Emperor. Even now, five thousand li southwest of Han, he regularly comes to court, submits, and offers tribute to Han. Is this not because his ancestors had virtue and their grace flowed to later generations?

entries.zh: 行道德豈可以忽乎哉！
entries.en: To practice morality and virtue—how can one neglect it!
entries.literal: To practice morality and virtue—how can one lightly neglect it!

entries.zh: 人君王者舉而觀之。
entries.en: Rulers and kings should take up this matter and examine it.
entries.literal: Rulers and kings should take this up and examine it.

entries.zh: 漢大將軍霍子孟名光者，亦黃帝後世也。
entries.en: Huo Zimeng, the Han General-in-Chief whose given name was Guang, was also a descendant of the Yellow Emperor.
entries.literal: The Han General-in-Chief Huo Zimeng, named Guang, was also a descendant of the Yellow Emperor.

entries.zh: 此可為博聞遠見者言，固難為淺聞者說也。
entries.en: This can be discussed with people of broad learning and far sight, but it is certainly difficult to explain to those whose knowledge is shallow.
entries.literal: This can be spoken of to those with broad learning and far sight, but it is certainly difficult to explain to those of shallow knowledge.

entries.zh: 何以言之？
entries.en: Why do I say this?
entries.literal: Why speak thus?

entries.zh: 古諸侯以國為姓。
entries.en: In ancient times the feudal lords took their state as surname.
entries.literal: Ancient feudal lords took state as surname.

entries.zh: 霍者，國名也。
entries.en: Huo was a state name.
entries.literal: Huo, state name.

entries.zh: 武王封弟叔處於霍，後世晉獻公滅霍公，後世為庶民，往來居平陽。
entries.en: King Wu enfeoffed his younger brother Shuchu at Huo. In a later generation, Duke Xian of Jin destroyed Duke Huo, and his descendants became commoners, moving back and forth until they settled at Pingyang.
entries.literal: King Wu enfeoffed his younger brother Shuchu at Huo. In a later generation, Duke Xian of Jin destroyed Duke Huo; his descendants became commoners and moved back and forth, living at Pingyang.

entries.zh: 平陽在河東，河東晉地，分為衛國。
entries.en: Pingyang lies in Hedong. Hedong was Jin territory, and was later partitioned into the state of Wei.
entries.literal: Pingyang is in Hedong. Hedong was Jin territory and was later divided to become part of the state of Wei.

entries.zh: 以詩言之，亦可為周世。
entries.en: If one speaks in terms of the Poetry, this too may be regarded as belonging to the Zhou lineage.
entries.literal: Speaking in terms of the Poetry, this too can be treated as part of the Zhou lineage.

entries.zh: 周起后稷，后稷無父而生。
entries.en: The Zhou arose from Hou Ji, Hou Ji was born without a father.
entries.literal: Zhou arose from Hou Ji, Hou Ji without father born.

entries.zh: 以三代世傳言之，后稷有父名高辛；
entries.en: Speaking in terms of the Three Dynasties genealogical transmissions, Hou Ji had a father named Gaoxin;
entries.literal: Speaking in terms of the Three Dynasties genealogical transmissions, Hou Ji had a father named Gaoxin;

entries.zh: 高辛，黃帝曾孫。
entries.en: Gaoxin was the great-grandson of the Yellow Emperor.
entries.literal: Gaoxin was the Yellow Emperor's great-grandson.

entries.zh: 黃帝終始傳曰：『漢興百有餘年，有人不短不長，出（自）［白］燕之鄉，持天下之政，時有嬰兒主，欲行車。』
entries.en: The Yellow Emperor's Chronicles of Beginning and End says, "More than a hundred years after the Han arises, there will be a man neither short nor tall, from the region of Baiyan, who holds the government of all under Heaven at a time when there is an infant ruler who wishes to ride in a carriage."
entries.literal: The Yellow Emperor's Chronicles of Beginning and End say: "More than a hundred years after the Han arose, there will be a man neither short nor tall, coming from the region of Baiyan, holding the government of all under Heaven, at a time when there is an infant ruler who wishes to ride in a carriage."

entries.zh: 霍將軍者，本居平陽（自）［白］燕。
entries.en: General Huo Guang originally lived at Pingyang in Baiyan.
entries.literal: General Huo originally lived at Pingyang in Baiyan.

entries.zh: 臣為郎時，與方士考功會旗亭下，為臣言。
entries.en: When I was a gentleman-attendant, I met the alchemist Kaogong under the Banner Pavilion, and he told me.
entries.literal: When I was a gentleman-attendant, I met the alchemist Kaogong under the Banner Pavilion, and he spoke to me.

entries.zh: 豈不偉哉！」
entries.en: Is this not magnificent!"
entries.literal: Is this not magnificent!"

entries.zh: 太史公曰：五帝、三代之記，尚矣。
entries.en: The Grand Historian says: The records of the Five Emperors and Three Dynasties go back to great antiquity.
entries.literal: Grand Historian says: Five Emperors, Three Dynasties records, remote.

entries.zh: 自殷以前諸侯不可得而譜，周以來乃頗可著。
entries.en: Before the Yin dynasty, the genealogies of the feudal lords cannot be fixed; only from the Zhou dynasty onward can they be recorded with confidence.
entries.literal: From Yin before feudal lords cannot be obtained to arrange genealogy, Zhou since then considerably can be recorded.

entries.zh: 孔子因史文次春秋，紀元年，正時日月，蓋其詳哉。
entries.en: Confucius followed the historical texts to arrange the Spring and Autumn Annals, recording the first year and correcting the seasons, days, and months—how detailed it is!
entries.literal: Confucius followed historical texts arranged Spring and Autumn, recorded first year, corrected seasons days months, indeed detailed.

entries.zh: 至於序尚書則略，無年月；
entries.en: As for arranging the Shangshu, it is brief, without years or months;
entries.literal: As for arranging Shangshu then brief, without years months;

entries.zh: 或頗有，然多闕，不可錄。
entries.en: Some have quite a bit, but many are deficient and cannot be recorded.
entries.literal: Some considerably have, yet many deficient, cannot record.

entries.zh: 故疑則傳疑，蓋其慎也。
entries.en: Therefore, where there is doubt, transmit the doubt—that is how cautious he was.
entries.literal: Therefore, doubt then transmit doubt, indeed cautious.

entries.zh: 帝王世國號
entries.en: Imperial reigns and state designations
entries.literal: Imperial age and state title

entries.zh: 顓頊屬
entries.en: Line of Zhuanxu
entries.literal: Zhuanxu line

entries.zh: 俈屬
entries.en: Line of Ku
entries.literal: Ku line

entries.zh: 堯屬
entries.en: Line of Yao
entries.literal: Yao line

entries.zh: 舜屬
entries.en: Line of Shun
entries.literal: Shun line

entries.zh: 夏屬
entries.en: Line of Xia
entries.literal: Xia line

entries.zh: 殷屬
entries.en: Line of Yin
entries.literal: Yin line

entries.zh: 周屬
entries.en: Line of Zhou
entries.literal: Zhou line

entries.zh: 周衰，禮廢樂壞，大小相踰，管仲之家，兼備三歸。
entries.en: When the Zhou declined, rites were abandoned and music was ruined. Great and small overstepped each other. Guan Zhong's household combined and equipped the three gui reception halls.
entries.literal: When the Zhou declined, rites were abandoned and music was ruined; great and small mutually overstepped each other. In Guan Zhong's household, he combined and equipped the three gui.

entries.zh: 循法守正者見侮於世，奢溢僭差者謂之顯榮。
entries.en: Those who follow the law and guard uprightness are mocked by the world, while those who are extravagant, excessive, and presumptuous are called illustrious and glorious.
entries.literal: Following law guarding upright ones seen insulted by the world, extravagant overflowing presumptuous differing ones called manifest glory.

entries.zh: 自子夏，門人之高弟也，猶云「出見紛華盛麗而說，入聞夫子之道而樂，二者心戰，未能自決」，而況中庸以下，漸漬於失教，被服於成俗乎？
entries.en: Even Zi Xia, the highest disciple among the disciples, still said: 'Going out I see variegated splendor and flourishing beauty and am pleased; entering I hear the Master's Dao and am happy. These two things battle in my heart, and I cannot decide for myself.' How much more so for those of middle and ordinary ability and below, who are gradually immersed in lost teaching and clothed in established customs?
entries.literal: Even Zi Xia, disciples' high disciple, still said "Going out seeing variegated splendor flourishing beauty and pleased, entering hearing Master Dao and happy, two things heart battle, unable self-decide", moreover middle ordinary and below, gradually immersed in lost teaching, clothed in established customs?

entries.zh: 孔子曰「必也正名」，於衛所居不合。
entries.en: Confucius said: 'It must be rectifying names.' In Wei, however, this did not fit where he was staying.
entries.literal: Confucius said "It must be rectifying names", at Wei his residence not harmonious.

entries.zh: 仲尼沒後，受業之徒沈湮而不舉，或適齊、楚，或入河海，豈不痛哉！
entries.en: After Zhongni passed away, his disciples who received his teachings sank into obscurity and were not raised up. Some went to Qi and Chu, others entered the rivers and seas. How could this not be painful!
entries.literal: Zhong Ni passed away after, received teachings disciples sunken submerged not raised, some went to Qi, Chu, some entered rivers seas, how not painful!

entries.zh: 至秦有天下，悉內六國禮儀，采擇其善，雖不合聖制，其尊君抑臣，朝廷濟濟，依古以來。
entries.en: When Qin possessed the realm, it entirely took in the rites and ceremonies of the six states, selecting what was good from them. Though they did not match the sage system, they honored the ruler and suppressed ministers, and the court was flourishing and orderly, following ancient practices.
entries.literal: Until Qin possessed the realm, entirely took in six states' rites ceremonies, selected their good, though not matching sage system, their honoring ruler suppressing minister, court flourishing flourishing, following ancient since.

entries.zh: 至于高祖，光有四海，叔孫通頗有所增益減損，大抵皆襲秦故。
entries.en: As for Gaozu, who shone over All under Heaven, Shusun Tong made considerable additions and subtractions, but in broad outline he still followed the old Qin practices.
entries.literal: As for Gaozu, illuminated possessed four seas, Shusun Tong considerably had additions subtractions, generally all followed Qin old.

entries.zh: 自天子稱號下至佐僚及宮室官名，少所變改。
entries.en: From the Son of Heaven's titles down to assistants and palace office names, little was changed.
entries.literal: From Son of Heaven titles down to assistants and palace room official names, little changed.

entries.zh: 孝文即位，有司議欲定儀禮，孝文好道家之學，以為繁禮飾貌，無益於治，躬化謂何耳，故罷去之。
entries.en: When Filial Wen ascended the throne, the officials discussed and wished to establish ceremony and rites. But Filial Wen was fond of Daoist learning and considered that elaborate rites and decorated appearances were of no benefit to governing—what mattered was personal transformation—so he dismissed them.
entries.literal: Filial Wen ascended throne, officials discussed wished establish ceremony rites, Filial Wen fond Daoist learning, considered elaborate rites decorated appearances, no benefit to governing, personal transformation is what mattered, therefore dismissed them.

entries.zh: 孝景時，御史大夫晁錯明於世務刑名，數干諫孝景曰：「諸侯藩輔，臣子一例，古今之制也。
entries.en: During Emperor Jing's time, Imperial Secretary Chao Cuo was clear about worldly affairs and penal names. He several times earnestly admonished Emperor Jing, saying: 'The feudal lords are screens and auxiliaries; ministers and sons are one rule—this is the system of ancient and present times.
entries.literal: During Filial Jing's time, Imperial Secretary Chao Cuo was clear about worldly affairs and penal names. He several times earnestly admonished Filial Jing, saying: "The feudal lords are screens and auxiliaries; ministers and sons are one rule—this is the system of ancient and present times.

entries.zh: 今大國專治異政，不稟京師，恐不可傳後。」
entries.en: Now the great states monopolize governance with different administrations and do not report to the capital. I fear this cannot be transmitted to posterity.'
entries.literal: Now great states monopolize governance different administration, not report capital, fear cannot transmit posterity."

entries.zh: 孝景用其計，而六國畔逆，以錯首名，天子誅錯以解難。
entries.en: Emperor Jing used his plan, and then the six states rebelled. Making Cuo the pretext, the Son of Heaven executed Cuo to resolve the difficulty.
entries.literal: Filial Jing used his plan, and then the six states rebelled. Making Cuo the pretext, the Son of Heaven executed Cuo to resolve the difficulty.

entries.zh: 事在袁盎語中。
entries.en: The details appear in the account of Yuan Ang's words.
entries.literal: The matter is set forth in Yuan Ang's account.

entries.zh: 是後官者養交安祿而已，莫敢復議。
entries.en: After this, officials only nourished connections and secured their stipends. None dared discuss the matter again.
entries.literal: After this officials nourished connections secured stipends only, none dared again discuss.

entries.zh: 今上即位，招致儒術之士，令共定儀，十餘年不就。
entries.en: When the present Majesty ascended the throne, he summoned scholars of Confucian arts and ordered them to establish the ceremonies together. After more than ten years, the work was still not complete.
entries.literal: Present Majesty ascended throne, summoned Confucian arts scholars, ordered together establish ceremonies, ten several years not completed.

entries.zh: 或言古者太平，萬民和喜，瑞應辨至，乃采風俗，定制作。
entries.en: Some said that in ancient times, when there was great peace and the ten thousand people were harmonious and happy, and auspicious responses clearly arrived, then customs were collected and creations established.
entries.literal: Some said ancient ones great peace, ten thousand people harmonious happy, auspicious responses clearly arrived, then collected customs, established creations.

entries.zh: 上聞之，制詔御史曰：「蓋受命而王，各有所由興，殊路而同歸，謂因民而作，追俗為制也。
entries.en: The emperor heard this and formulated an edict to the imperial secretary, saying: 'Generally those who received the mandate and became kings each had their origin of rising. Though by different roads, they return to the same place. This means following the people to make things and pursuing customs as the system.
entries.literal: The emperor heard this and formulated an edict to the imperial secretary, saying: "Generally those who received the mandate and became kings each had their origin of rising. Though by different roads, they return to the same place. This means following the people to make things and pursuing customs as the system.

entries.zh: 議者咸稱太古，百姓何望？
entries.en: The discussers all praise great antiquity—what hope do the common people have?
entries.literal: Discussers all praised great antiquity, common people what hope?

entries.zh: 漢亦一家之事，典法不傳，謂子孫何？
entries.en: The Han is also the matter of one family. If the classical laws are not transmitted, what will we tell our descendants?
entries.literal: Han also one family's matter, classical laws not transmitted, what tell descendants?

entries.zh: 化隆者閎博，治淺者褊狹，可不勉與！」
entries.en: Those whose transforming power flourishes are vast and broad; those whose governance is shallow are narrow and cramped. Can we not strive toward this!'
entries.literal: Those whose transforming power flourishes are vast and broad; those whose governance is shallow are narrow and cramped. Can we not strive toward this!"

entries.zh: 乃以太初之元改正朔，易服色，封太山，定宗廟百官之儀，以為典常，垂之於後云。
entries.en: Then, taking the origin of Taichu as their starting point, they corrected the calendar, changed the garment colors, and conducted the Feng sacrifice at Mount Tai. They also established the ceremonies for the ancestral temple and the hundred officials, making them classical constants to be handed down to posterity.
entries.literal: Then with Tai Chu's origin corrected calendar, changed garment colors, sealed Taishan, established ancestral temple hundred officials' ceremonies, as classical constant, handed down to posterity cloud.

entries.zh: 太史公曰：洋洋美德乎！
entries.en: The Grand Historian says: How vast and beautiful is this virtue!
entries.literal: The Grand Historian said: How vast and beautiful is virtue!

entries.zh: 宰制萬物，役使群眾，豈人力也哉？
entries.en: It controls the ten thousand things and directs the multitudes. How could this be accomplished by human power alone?
entries.literal: Controlling ten thousand things, employing the multitudes, how is it human power?

entries.zh: 余至大行禮官，觀三代損益，乃知緣人情而制禮，依人性而作儀，其所由來尚矣。
entries.en: I went to the rites office of the Grand Lineage and observed the gains and losses of the Three Dynasties. Only then did I understand that rites are established in accord with human feeling, and ritual implements are made in accord with human nature; their origin is already ancient.
entries.literal: I went to the rites office of the Grand Lineage, observed the Three Dynasties' additions and subtractions, then knew that rites are established following human feelings, ritual implements are made relying on human nature, and their origins are already ancient.

entries.zh: 武王伐紂，吹律聽聲，推孟春以至于季冬，殺氣相并，而音尚宮。
entries.en: When King Wu campaigned against Zhou, he blew the pitch-pipes and listened to the sounds, extending this from the first month of spring to the last month of winter. The killing qi joined together, but the sound still favored gong.
entries.literal: Wu King attacked Zhou, blew pitchpipes listened sound, extended first spring to last winter, killing qi mutually joined, but sound still palace.

entries.zh: 同聲相從，物之自然，何足怪哉？
entries.en: Like sounds mutually follow each other; this is the natural way of things. What is there to be surprised about?
entries.literal: Same sound mutually follow, things natural, what sufficient strange?

entries.zh: 高祖有天下，三邊外畔；
entries.en: When Gaozu possessed all under Heaven, the three borders rebelled on the outside.
entries.literal: Gaozu possessed realm, three borders external rebelled.

entries.zh: 大國之王雖稱蕃輔，臣節未盡。
entries.en: The kings of the great states, though called screen auxiliaries, did not complete their ministerly conduct.
entries.literal: Great states kings though called screen auxiliaries, minister conduct not complete.

entries.zh: 會高祖厭苦軍事，亦有蕭、張之謀，故偃武一休息，羈縻不備。
entries.en: By then Gaozu was weary of military affairs, and he also had the advice of Xiao He and Zhang Liang. So he set aside military force for a time, keeping restraint and control but not yet fully completing them.
entries.literal: Met Gaozu tired bitter military affairs, also had Xiao, Zhang plans, therefore rested martial one rest, restraint bridle not complete.

entries.zh: 歷至孝文即位，將軍陳武等議曰：「南越、朝鮮自全秦時內屬為臣子，後且擁兵阻阸，選蠕觀望。
entries.en: By the time Emperor Wen ascended the throne, General Chen Wu and others deliberated, saying, "Nanyue and Joseon had been subjects within the realm since the unified Qin. Later, they held troops, blocked the passes, and lingered in hesitation, watching from the sidelines.
entries.literal: When it came to Emperor Wen's accession, General Chen Wu and others deliberated, saying: "Nanyue and Chaoxian, from the time of unified Qin, were subjects within the realm. Later they moreover held troops and blocked the passes, hesitating and watching from the sidelines.

entries.zh: 高祖時天下新定，人民小安，未可復興兵。
entries.en: In Gaozu's time, the realm was newly settled; the people were slightly peaceful. It was not possible to again raise weapons.
entries.literal: Gaozu time realm newly settled, people slightly peaceful, not able again raise weapons.

entries.zh: 今陛下仁惠撫百姓，恩澤加海內，宜及士民樂用，征討逆黨，以一封疆。」
entries.en: Now Your Majesty is benevolent and kind, bringing comfort to the common people, and your grace reaches everywhere within the seas. We should act while scholars and commoners are eager to serve, campaign against the rebellious factions, and bring the frontiers into unity."
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty is benevolent and kind, comforting the common people; grace and favor pervade within the seas. It is fitting to take advantage while scholars and the people are glad to serve, to campaign and attack the rebellious faction, and unify the borders."

entries.zh: 孝文曰：「朕能任衣冠，念不到此。
entries.en: Emperor Wen said, "I am able to wear the cap and gown, but my thoughts had not gone this far.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen said: "I can bear the cap and gown, but my thoughts did not reach this.

entries.zh: 會呂氏之亂，功臣宗室共不羞恥，誤居正位，常戰戰慄慄，恐事之不終。
entries.en: When the turmoil of the Lü clan arose, I and the meritorious ministers and the imperial clan together held the throne without shame; we mistakenly occupied the legitimate position, constantly trembling in fear that the affair would not succeed.
entries.literal: Met Lü clan chaos, meritorious ministers imperial clan together without shame, mistakenly occupied correct position, constantly trembling fearful, feared affairs not end.

entries.zh: 且兵凶器，雖克所願，動亦秏病，謂百姓遠方何？
entries.en: Besides, weapons are ominous tools. Even if one obtains what one wants, mobilization still exhausts and harms the people. What then of the common people and distant places?
entries.literal: Moreover, weapons ominous tools, though overcome wished, move also consume illness, say common people distant places what?

entries.zh: 又先帝知勞民不可煩，故不以為意。
entries.en: The former emperor also knew that the people could not bear further labor, and therefore gave no thought to such a plan.
entries.literal: Moreover, the former emperor knew the people could not be harassed with labor, and therefore gave no thought to this.

entries.zh: 朕豈自謂能？
entries.en: How can I myself say I am able?
entries.literal: I how self say able?

entries.zh: 今匈奴內侵，軍吏無功，邊民父子荷兵日久，朕常為動心傷痛，無日忘之。
entries.en: Now the Xiongnu internally invade; the military officials have no merit; the border people, fathers and sons, carry weapons for days long. I am constantly moved in heart and pained; there is no day I forget it.
entries.literal: Now Xiongnu internally invade, military officials no merit, border people fathers sons carry weapons days long, I constantly for moved heart pained, no day forget it.

entries.zh: 今未能銷距，願且堅邊設候，結和通使，休寧北陲，為功多矣。
entries.en: Since I cannot yet drive them back, for now I wish to strengthen the borders, establish watchposts, make peace, maintain envoys, and let the northern frontier rest in calm. That would already be a great achievement.
entries.literal: Now unable to repel them, I wish for the present to strengthen the borders and set watchposts, form peace and maintain envoys, and let the northern frontier rest and settle; that would already be a great achievement.

entries.zh: 且無議軍。」
entries.en: And do not discuss military affairs."
entries.literal: Moreover, do not discuss military affairs."

entries.zh: 故百姓無內外之繇，得息肩於田畝，天下殷富，粟至十餘錢，鳴雞吠狗，煙火萬里，可謂和樂者乎！
entries.en: Therefore, the common people had no labor service inside or outside the borders; they could rest their shoulders in the fields and on the farms. The realm was abundant and rich; millet sold for only ten or so cash. Roosters crowed and dogs barked, and smoke and hearthfires stretched for ten thousand li. Can this not be called harmonious and happy?
entries.literal: Therefore, common people no internal external corvee, obtain rest shoulders in fields acres, realm abundant rich, millet reach ten several cash, crowing roosters barking dogs, smoke fires ten thousand li, can call harmonious happy ones!

entries.zh: 王者制事立法，物度軌則，壹稟於六律，六律為萬事根本焉。
entries.en: Kings establish institutions and laws; all measures and norms derive from the six pitch-pipes. The six pitch-pipes are the root of all affairs.
entries.literal: Kings establish affairs make laws, things measure tracks rules, one receive from six pitchpipes, six pitchpipes are ten thousand affairs root there.

entries.zh: 漢興，高祖曰「北畤待我而起」，亦自以為獲水德之瑞。
entries.en: When Han rose, Gaozu said, “The northern altar waited for me before it arose,” and he too took himself to have received the auspicious sign of water virtue.
entries.literal: When Han rose, Gaozu said, “The northern altar awaited me and rose with me,” and he also took himself to have received the auspicious sign of water virtue.

entries.zh: 雖明習歷及張蒼等，咸以為然。
entries.en: Even Zhang Cang and the others who understood the calendar clearly all took this to be correct.
entries.literal: Even those who were skilled in the calendar, including Zhang Cang and others, all agreed.

entries.zh: 是時天下初定，方綱紀大基，高后女主，皆未遑，故襲秦正朔服色。
entries.en: At that time the realm had only just been settled and the great foundation of order was being laid. Empress Gao, ruling as a woman, had no leisure for the matter, so the Qin calendar, monthly beginnings, and clothing colors were retained.
entries.literal: At that time the realm had only just been settled and the great foundation of order was being laid. Empress Gao, as a female ruler, had no leisure for it, so the Qin calendar, new moon, and clothing colors were retained.

entries.zh: 至今上即位，招致方士唐都，分其天部；
entries.en: When the present emperor came to the throne, he summoned the fangshi Tang Du to divide the celestial sectors;
entries.literal: When the current emperor ascended the throne, he summoned the fangshi Tang Du and had him apportion the heavenly divisions;

entries.zh: 而巴落下閎運算轉歷，然後日辰之度與夏正同。
entries.en: then Luoxia Hong of Ba calculated the rotating calendar, and only afterward did the sun’s degrees and the days correspond with the Xia calendar.
entries.literal: and when Luoxia Hong of Ba calculated the revolving calendar, the degrees of the sun and the days then matched the Xia calendar.

entries.zh: 乃改元，更官號，封泰山。
entries.en: The emperor then changed the era name, revised the official titles, and performed the Feng sacrifice at Mount Tai.
entries.literal: He then changed the era name, altered the office titles, and sacrificed at Mount Tai.

entries.zh: 因詔御史曰：「乃者，有司言星度之未定也，廣延宣問，以理星度，未能詹也。
entries.en: He therefore issued an edict to the imperial secretary, saying: “Recently the relevant officials reported that the stellar degrees had not yet been fixed. I have widely extended inquiry to rectify the stellar degrees, but have not yet gained full clarity.
entries.literal: He therefore issued an edict to the imperial secretary, saying: “Recently the relevant officials reported that the stellar degrees had not yet been fixed. I have widely extended inquiry to set right the stellar degrees, but have not yet fully attained clarity.

entries.zh: 蓋聞昔者黃帝合而不死，名察度驗，定清濁，起五部，建氣物分數。
entries.en: I have heard that in antiquity the Yellow Emperor joined with the Way and did not die; he named, examined, and verified the degrees, fixed the clear and the turbid, established the five divisions, and set up the numerical measures of qi and things.
entries.literal: I have heard that in antiquity the Yellow Emperor attained unity and did not die; he named, examined, and verified the degrees, fixed the clear and turbid, established the five divisions, and set up the measures and proportions of qi and things.

entries.zh: 然蓋尚矣。
entries.en: But this is still very remote indeed.
entries.literal: But this is still very remote indeed.

entries.zh: 書缺樂弛，朕甚閔焉。
entries.en: The records are incomplete and music has slackened into decay; this deeply grieves me.
entries.literal: The records are incomplete and music has fallen into decay; I am deeply distressed by this.

entries.zh: 朕唯未能循明也，紬績日分，率應水德之勝。
entries.en: I alone have not yet been able to follow and clarify the established calendar, but have only carried forward the daily divisions, broadly conforming to the ascendancy of water virtue.
entries.literal: I alone have not yet been able to follow and clarify the way, but have only continued the daily divisions, broadly conforming to the predominance of water virtue.

entries.zh: 今日順夏至，黃鐘為宮，林鐘為徵，太蔟為商，南呂為羽，姑洗為角。
entries.en: Now, in accord with the summer solstice, Huangzhong serves as gong, Linzhong as zhi, Taicu as shang, Nanlu as yu, and Guxi as jue.
entries.literal: Today, in accordance with the summer solstice, Huangzhong is gong, Linzhong is zhi, Taicu is shang, Nanlü is yu, and Guxi is jue.

entries.zh: 自是以後，氣復正，羽聲復清，名復正變，以至子日當冬至，則陰陽離合之道行焉。
entries.en: From this point on, the qi again became correct, the yu pitch again became clear, and the names again returned to their proper alternation. When the zi day coincides with the winter solstice, the way of yin and yang separating and joining is put into practice.
entries.literal: From this point on, the qi again became correct, the yu pitch again became clear, and the names again returned to proper alteration. By the time the zi day coincides with the winter solstice, the way of yin and yang separating and joining is put into practice.

entries.zh: 十一月甲子朔旦冬至已詹，其更以七年為太初元年。
entries.en: When the eleventh month, the jiazi day, the new moon, dawn, and the winter solstice all coincided, they changed the calendar so that the seventh year became the first year of Taichu.
entries.literal: By the time the eleventh month, Jiazi, new moon, and winter solstice were all reached, they changed it so that the seventh year became the first year of Taichu.

entries.zh: 年名『焉逢攝提格』，月名『畢聚』，日得甲子，夜半朔旦冬至。」
entries.en: The year was named “Yanfeng Shetige”; the month was named “Biju”; the day was Jiazi; and at midnight the new moon, dawn, and winter solstice coincided.”
entries.literal: The year was named “Yanfeng Shetige”; the month was named “Biju”; the day was Jiazi; and at midnight came the new moon, dawn, and winter solstice.”

entries.zh: 歷術甲子篇太初元年，歲名「焉逢攝提格」，月名「畢聚」，日得甲子，夜半朔旦冬至。
entries.en: The calendar method of the Jiazi chapter for the first year of Taichu: the year was named “Yanfeng Shetige”; the month was named “Biju”; the day was Jiazi; at midnight the new moon, dawn, and winter solstice coincided.
entries.literal: The calendar method of the Jiazi chapter for the first year of Taichu: the year was named “Yanfeng Shetige”; the month was named “Biju”; the day obtained Jiazi; at midnight came the new moon, dawn, and winter solstice.

entries.zh: 昔自在古，歷建正作於孟春。
entries.en: In ancient times, the calendar was set to begin in the first month of spring.
entries.literal: In ancient times, the proper beginning of the calendar was fixed in the first month of spring.

entries.zh: 於時冰泮發蟄，百草奮興，秭鳺先滜。
entries.en: At that time, the ice melts and the hibernating creatures stir; the hundred grasses flourish, and the cuckoo calls first.
entries.literal: At that time the ice melts and the hibernating creatures stir, the hundred grasses flourish, and the cuckoo is first to call.

entries.zh: 物乃歲具，生於東，次順四時，卒于冬分。
entries.en: Things then complete the year, springing from the east, moving in order through the four seasons, and ending at the winter solstice.
entries.literal: Things then complete the year, spring from the east, follow the four seasons in order, and end at the winter solstice.

entries.zh: 時雞三號，卒明。
entries.en: At the third crowing of the rooster, daylight finally arrives.
entries.literal: When the rooster crows three times, dawn arrives.

entries.zh: 撫十二［月］節，卒于丑。
entries.en: It passes through the twelve monthly nodes and comes to completion at Chou.
entries.literal: It runs through the twelve monthly divisions and ends in Chou.

entries.zh: 日月成，故明也。
entries.en: When the sun and moon are in order, brightness results.
entries.literal: When the sun and moon are complete, there is brightness.

entries.zh: 明者孟也，幽者幼也，幽明者雌雄也。
entries.en: Bright means the elder; dark means the younger. Together, dark and bright mean female and male.
entries.literal: Bright means the elder; dark means the younger. Dark and bright together mean female and male.

entries.zh: 雌雄代興，而順至正之統也。
entries.en: Female and male rise in alternation, following the proper succession of the correct order.
entries.literal: Female and male alternate in succession, thus following the right order.

entries.zh: 日歸于西，起明於東；
entries.en: The sun returns to the west, then brings light forth in the east;
entries.literal: The sun returns to the west and rises in the east.

entries.zh: 月歸於東，起明于西。
entries.en: the moon returns to the east, then brings light forth in the west.
entries.literal: The moon returns to the east and rises in the west.

entries.zh: 正不率天，又不由人，則凡事易壞而難成矣。
