entries.en: If the calendar neither follows Heaven nor rests on human ordering, then every undertaking becomes easy to ruin and difficult to complete.
entries.literal: If the calendar does not follow heaven or derive from human ordering, then all affairs are easy to ruin and hard to complete.

entries.zh: 其後四十有餘年，今天子元光之中，而河決於瓠子，東南注鉅野，通於淮、泗。
entries.en: More than forty years later, in the middle years of the present emperor's Yuanguang era, the Yellow River burst at Huzi, flowed southeast into Juye, and joined the Huai and Si rivers.
entries.literal: More than forty years later, in the middle of the present emperor’s Yuanguang era, the Yellow River burst at Huzi, flowed southeast into Juye, and joined the Huai and Si rivers.

entries.zh: 於是天子使汲黯、鄭當時興人徒塞之，輒復壞。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven accordingly sent Ji An and Zheng Dangshi to raise laborers and block the breach, but each repair broke open again.
entries.literal: Accordingly, the Son of Heaven sent Ji An and Zheng Dangshi to raise laborers to block it, but each time it broke again.

entries.zh: 是時武安侯田蚡為丞相，其奉邑食鄃。
entries.en: At the time, Tian Fen, the Marquis of Wu'an, was serving as chancellor, and his appanage lay at Shu.
entries.literal: At that time the Marquis of Wu’an, Tian Fen, was chancellor, and his appanage was at Shu.

entries.zh: 鄃居河北，河決而南則鄃無水菑，邑收多。
entries.en: Shu lay north of the Yellow River. If the river breached and ran south, Shu would suffer no flooding, and the estate's revenues would be large.
entries.literal: Shu lay north of the Yellow River; if the river breached and flowed south, Shu would suffer no flood damage, and the estate’s revenues would be large.

entries.zh: 蚡言於上曰：「江河之決皆天事，未易以人力為彊塞，塞之未必應天。」
entries.en: Fen said to the emperor, “Breaches in the Jiang and Yellow River are all matters of Heaven. Human effort cannot easily force them shut, and sealing them may not accord with Heaven's will.”
entries.literal: Fen said to the emperor: “Breaks in the Jiang and the Yellow River are all matters of Heaven. They are not easily forced shut by human effort, and sealing them may not accord with Heaven.”

entries.zh: 而望氣用數者亦以為然。
entries.en: Those who observed qi and made calculations also agreed.
entries.literal: Those who observed qi and used calculations also thought this was so.

entries.zh: 於是天子久之不事復塞也。
entries.en: For a long time after that, the Son of Heaven made no further attempt to close the breach.
entries.literal: For a long time, the Son of Heaven made no further attempt to block it.

entries.zh: 自河決瓠子後二十餘歲，歲因以數不登，而梁楚之地尤甚。
entries.en: More than twenty years after the Yellow River breached at Huzi, harvests failed repeatedly, and the lands of Liang and Chu suffered especially badly.
entries.literal: More than twenty years after the Yellow River breached at Huzi, harvests repeatedly failed, and the lands of Liang and Chu suffered especially severely.

entries.zh: 天子既封禪巡祭山川，其明年，旱，乾封少雨。
entries.en: After the Son of Heaven performed the fengshan rites, inspected the mountains and rivers, and offered sacrifices to them, drought came the following year, and the sealed altar was dry with little rain.
entries.literal: After the Son of Heaven had performed the fengshan rites and inspected and sacrificed to the mountains and rivers, the following year brought drought, and the sealed altar was dry with little rain.

entries.zh: 天子乃使汲仁、郭昌發卒數萬人塞瓠子決。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven then sent Ji Ren and Guo Chang to mobilize tens of thousands of soldiers and close the breach at Huzi.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven then sent Ji Ren and Guo Chang to mobilize tens of thousands of soldiers to block the Huzi breach.

entries.zh: 於是天子已用事萬里沙，則還自臨決河，沈白馬玉璧于河，令群臣從官自將軍已下皆負薪窴決河。
entries.en: When the Son of Heaven had performed the rites at Wanli Sha, he returned and personally inspected the breached river, sank a white horse and a jade bi into it, and ordered all the officials and attendants, from the generals down, to carry firewood and fill the breach.
entries.literal: After the Son of Heaven had performed the rites at Wanli Sha, he returned and personally inspected the breached river, sank a white horse and a jade bi into it, and ordered all the officials and attendants, from the generals down, to carry firewood and fill the breach.

entries.zh: 是時東郡燒草，以故薪柴少，而下淇園之竹以為楗。
entries.en: At that time Dongjun had burned off the grass, and because firewood was scarce, bamboo from the Qi garden was felled and used as stakes.
entries.literal: At that time, Dongjun had burned off the grass, and because firewood was scarce, bamboo from the Qi garden was cut down and used as stakes.

entries.zh: 漢興三十九年，孝文時河決酸棗，東潰金隄，於是東郡大興卒塞之。
entries.en: In the thirty-ninth year after the Han rose, during Emperor Xiaowen's reign, the Yellow River burst at Suanzao and broke through the Eastern Golden Dike. Dong Commandery was then mobilized on a large scale to close the breach.
entries.literal: In the thirty-ninth year after Han’s rise, during Emperor Xiaowen’s reign, the Yellow River burst at Suanzao and broke through the Eastern Golden Dike, whereupon Dong Commandery was mobilized on a large scale to seal it.

entries.zh: 是時鄭當時為大農，言曰：「異時關東漕粟從渭中上，度六月而罷，而漕水道九百餘里，時有難處。
entries.en: At this time Zheng Dangshi was superintendent of agriculture. He said, “In earlier times, grain transport from east of the passes went up through the Wei. It took six months to complete the journey, and the route was more than nine hundred li long.
entries.literal: At this time Zheng Dangshi was superintendent of agriculture. He said: “In earlier times, grain transport from east of the passes went up through the Wei; it took six months to complete, and the water route was more than nine hundred li, with difficult stretches along the way.

entries.zh: 引渭穿渠起長安，并南山下，至河三百餘里，徑，易漕，度可令三月罷；
entries.en: If water from the Wei is drawn off and a canal is cut from Chang'an along the foot of the Southern Mountains to the Yellow River, a distance of more than three hundred li, the route will be direct, transport will be easy,
entries.literal: If the Wei is drawn off and a canal is cut from Chang’an along the foot of the Southern Mountains to the Yellow River, more than three hundred li, the route will be direct, transport will be easy, and it can probably be completed in three months;

entries.zh: 而渠下民田萬餘頃，又可得以溉田：此損漕省卒，而益肥關中之地，得穀。」
entries.en: and more than ten thousand qing of the people's fields below the canal can also be irrigated. This would reduce transport costs, spare soldiers, and enrich the soil of Guanzhong."
entries.literal: and more than ten thousand qing of the people’s fields below the canal can also be irrigated. This would reduce transport costs and save soldiers, while enriching the soil of Guanzhong and producing grain.”

entries.zh: 天子以為然，令齊人水工徐伯表，悉發卒數萬人穿漕渠，三歲而通。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven approved. He ordered Xu Bo, a water engineer from Qi, to mark out the route, and mobilized tens of thousands of soldiers to cut the transport canal for more than three years.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven thought this was right. He ordered Xu Bo, a water engineer from Qi, to mark out the route, and mobilized tens of thousands of soldiers to cut the transport canal; after three years it was opened.

entries.zh: 通，以漕，大便利。
entries.en: Once opened for transport, it proved extremely convenient.
entries.literal: Once opened and used for transport, it proved highly convenient.

entries.zh: 其後漕稍多，而渠下之民頗得以溉田矣。
entries.en: Thereafter, transport gradually increased, and the people below the canal were able to irrigate their fields.
entries.literal: Thereafter transport gradually increased, and the people below the canal were able to irrigate their fields.

entries.zh: 其後河東守番系言：「漕從山東西，歲百餘萬石，更砥柱之限，敗亡甚多，而亦煩費。
entries.en: Later Fan Xi, governor of Hedong, said, “Transport moving west from east of the mountains amounts to more than a million shi each year. It must pass the hazards of Dizhu, where much is lost and costs are burdensome.
entries.literal: Later Fan Xi, governor of Hedong, said: “Transport goes westward from east of the mountains, more than a million shi each year. It must pass through the hazards of Dizhu, where much is lost and ruined, and it is also troublesome and costly.

entries.zh: 穿渠引汾溉皮氏、汾陰下，引河溉汾陰、蒲阪下，度可得五千頃。
entries.en: If canals are cut to draw the Fen River down to irrigate the land below Pishi and Fenyin, and to draw the Yellow River down to irrigate the land below Fenyin and Puban, we estimate that five thousand qing of fields can be obtained.
entries.literal: If canals are cut to draw the Fen River to irrigate the land below Pishi and Fenyin, and to draw the Yellow River to irrigate the land below Fenyin and Puban, we estimate that five thousand qing can be obtained.

entries.zh: 五千頃故盡河壖棄地，民茭牧其中耳，今溉田之，度可得穀二百萬石以上。
entries.en: All five thousand qing are abandoned riverbank lands, where the people do little more than cut fodder and pasture animals. If irrigated and farmed, we estimate they could yield more than two million shi of grain.
entries.literal: These five thousand qing are all abandoned riverbank lands, where the people merely cut fodder and pasture animals. If they are irrigated and farmed, we estimate that more than two million shi of grain can be obtained.

entries.zh: 穀從渭上，與關中無異，而砥柱之東可無復漕。」
entries.en: The grain could travel up the Wei like grain from Guanzhong, and east of Dizhu there would no longer be any need for transport.”
entries.literal: The grain can go up the Wei, just like grain from Guanzhong, and east of Dizhu there will no longer be any need for transport.”

entries.zh: 天子以為然，發卒數萬人作渠田。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven approved and mobilized tens of thousands of soldiers to create canal-irrigated fields.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven thought this was right and mobilized tens of thousands of soldiers to make canal-fields.

entries.zh: 數歲，河移徙，渠不利，則田者不能償種。
entries.en: After several years, the Yellow River shifted, the canal became useless, and the farmers could not recover their seed grain.
entries.literal: After several years, the Yellow River shifted, the canal lost its usefulness, and the farmers could not recover the seed grain.

entries.zh: 久之，河東渠田廢，予越人，令少府以為稍入。
entries.en: After a long interval, the Hedong canal-fields were abandoned and assigned to people from Yue, and the Privy Treasury was ordered to count them as added revenue.
entries.literal: After a long time, the Hedong canal-fields were abandoned and given to people from Yue, and the Privy Treasury was ordered to count them as incremental revenue.

entries.zh: 其後人有上書欲通褒斜道及漕事，下御史大夫張湯。
entries.en: Later, someone submitted a memorial proposing that the Bao-Xie road be opened and transport arranged through it. The matter was referred to Imperial Counselor Zhang Tang.
entries.literal: Later someone submitted a memorial proposing to open the Bao-Xie road and arrange transport; the matter was referred to Imperial Counselor Zhang Tang.

entries.zh: 湯問其事，因言：「抵蜀從故道，故道多阪，回遠。
entries.en: Tang investigated and said, “To reach Shu by the old route, one must cross many slopes, and the way is long and winding.
entries.literal: Tang asked about the matter and said: “To reach Shu by the old route, one must cross many slopes, and it is long and circuitous.

entries.zh: 今穿褒斜道，少阪，近四百里；
entries.en: If the Bao-Xie road is cut through now, there will be fewer slopes, and the route will be nearly four hundred li shorter.
entries.literal: Now, if the Bao-Xie road is cut through, there will be fewer slopes and the route will be nearly four hundred li shorter;

entries.zh: 而褒水通沔，斜水通渭，皆可以行船漕。
entries.en: The Bao River connects with the Mian, and the Xie River connects with the Wei, so both can be used for boat transport.
entries.literal: and the Bao River connects with the Mian, while the Xie River connects with the Wei, so both can be used for boat transport.

entries.zh: 漕從南陽上沔入褒，褒之絕水至斜，閒百餘里，以車轉，從斜下下渭。
entries.en: Transport from Nanyang would go up the Mian River and enter the Bao. From the Bao's headwaters across to the Xie is more than a hundred li, where carts would transfer the cargo; from there it would descend the Xie into the Wei.
entries.literal: Transport from Nanyang would go up the Mian River and enter the Bao. From the Bao’s headwaters across to the Xie is more than a hundred li, where carts would transfer the cargo; from the Xie it would then go down to the Wei.

entries.zh: 如此，漢中之穀可致，山東從沔無限，便於砥柱之漕。
entries.en: In this way, the grain of Hanzhong can be brought in, and shipments from east of the mountains by way of the Mian will be without limit. It will be more convenient than transport through Dizhu.
entries.literal: In this way the grain of Hanzhong can be brought in, and shipments from east of the mountains by way of the Mian will have no limit; it will be more convenient than transport through Dizhu.

entries.zh: 且褒斜材木竹箭之饒，擬於巴蜀。」
entries.en: Moreover, Bao-Xie has timber, bamboo, and arrow bamboo in abundance, just as Ba and Shu do.”
entries.literal: Moreover, the timber, bamboo, and arrow bamboo of Bao-Xie are as abundant as those of Ba and Shu.”

entries.zh: 天子以為然，拜湯子卬為漢中守，發數萬人作褒斜道五百餘里。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven approved. He appointed Tang's son Ang as governor of Hanzhong and mobilized tens of thousands of men to build the Bao-Xie road for more than five hundred li.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven thought this was right. He appointed Tang’s son Ang governor of Hanzhong and mobilized tens of thousands of men to build the Bao-Xie road, more than five hundred li.

entries.zh: 道果便近，而水湍石，不可漕。
entries.en: The road was indeed convenient and shorter, but the water was swift and full of rocks, so it could not be used for transport.
entries.literal: The road was indeed convenient and shorter, but the water was swift and rocky and could not be used for transport.

entries.zh: 天子既臨河決，悼功之不成，乃作歌曰：「瓠子決兮將柰何？
entries.en: When the Son of Heaven came to the breached Yellow River, he grieved that the work was not complete and composed a song: “The Huzi breach! What can be done?
entries.literal: When the Son of Heaven came to the breached Yellow River and grieved that the work had not been completed, he composed a song: “The Huzi breach, ah! What can be done?

entries.zh: 皓皓旰旰兮閭殫為河！
entries.en: Brightly shining, the embankment itself becomes the river!
entries.literal: Brightly shining, the embankment becomes the river!

entries.zh: 殫為河兮地不得寧，功無已時兮吾山平。
entries.en: The river floods the land and gives it no peace; the labor never ends, and my mountain is leveled.
entries.literal: The river overflows the land and gives it no peace; the work has no end, and my mountain is leveled.

entries.zh: 吾山平兮鉅野溢，魚沸郁兮柏冬日。
entries.en: My mountain is leveled, and Juye overflows; the fish surge and churn like cypress in the winter sun.
entries.literal: My mountain is leveled, and Juye overflows; the fish surge and churn like cypress in winter sunlight.

entries.zh: 延道弛兮離常流，蛟龍騁兮方遠遊。
entries.en: The dikes break loose, the channel leaves its old course, and the dragons and serpents gallop off to roam far away.
entries.literal: The dikes loosen, the channel leaves its old course, and the dragons and serpents gallop off to roam far away.

entries.zh: 歸舊川兮神哉沛，不封禪兮安知外！
entries.en: Return to the old channel, ah, and the spirit flourishes! Without feng and shan, how can one know the wider world?
entries.literal: Return to the old channel, ah, and the spirit flourishes! Without feng and shan, how can one know the world beyond?

entries.zh: 為我謂河伯兮何不仁，泛濫不止兮愁吾人？
entries.en: For my sake, tell the River Lord: why are you so cruel, flooding without end and grieving us people?
entries.literal: For my sake, say to the River Lord: why are you so cruel, flooding without end and grieving us people?

entries.zh: 齧桑浮兮淮、泗滿，久不反兮水維緩。」
entries.en: When the mulberry banks are gnawed away and float, the Huai and Si are full; when it has been away for some time, the water level falls slack.”
entries.literal: When the mulberry banks are gnawed away and float, the Huai and Si are full; when it has not returned for long, the water level is slack.”

entries.zh: 一曰：「河湯湯兮激潺湲，北渡污兮浚流難。
entries.en: "The river surges and roars, rushing and rippling; crossing north through the foul current makes dredging hard.
entries.literal: The river surges and roars, rushing and rippling; crossing north through the foul current is hard to dredge.

entries.zh: 搴長茭兮沈美玉，河伯許兮薪不屬。
entries.en: Raise the long cattails and sink the jade; if the River Lord agrees, the firewood will not be lacking.
entries.literal: Raise the long cattails and sink the jade; if the River Lord assents, the firewood will not be lacking.

entries.zh: 薪不屬兮衛人罪，燒蕭條兮噫乎何以御水！
entries.en: If firewood is not lacking, then the fault lies with the people of Wei; if the withered reeds are burned bare, ah, how can one hold back the water!
entries.literal: If the firewood is not lacking, then the fault is with the people of Wei; if the withered reeds are burned bare, ah, how can one hold back the water!

entries.zh: 穨林竹兮楗石菑，宣房塞兮萬福來。」
entries.en: Pile up the forest bamboo and stake the stone dike; once Xuanfang is sealed, ten thousand blessings will surely come.”
entries.literal: Pile up the forest bamboo and stake the stone dike; once Xuanfang is sealed, ten thousand blessings will come.”

entries.zh: 於是卒塞瓠子，筑宮其上，名曰宣房宮。
entries.en: They finally blocked the Huzi breach, built a palace over it, and named it Xuanfang Palace.
entries.literal: They finally blocked the Huzi breach and built a palace over it, naming it Xuanfang Palace.

entries.zh: 而道河北行二渠，復禹舊跡，而梁、楚之地復寧，無水災。
entries.en: Thereafter, they diverted the Yellow River into two channels to the north, restored Yu’s old traces, and the lands of Liang and Chu again became peaceful and free of flood disaster.
entries.literal: Thereafter they diverted the Yellow River into two channels to the north, restored Yu’s old traces, and the lands of Liang and Chu again became peaceful, free of flood disaster.

entries.zh: 太史公曰：余南登廬山，觀禹疏九江，遂至于會稽太湟，上姑蘇，望五湖；
entries.en: The Grand Historian says: I myself climbed the south face of Mount Lu, observed Yu’s diversion of the Nine Rivers, then went on to Kuaiji and Taihuang, ascended Gusu, and looked out over the Five Lakes;
entries.literal: The Grand Historian says: I myself climbed Mount Lu in the south, observed Yu’s diversion of the Nine Rivers, then went on to Kuaiji and Taihuang, ascended Gusu, and looked out over the Five Lakes;

entries.zh: 東闚洛汭、大邳，迎河，行淮、泗、濟、漯洛渠；
entries.en: to the east, I gazed upon Luorui and Dapi, met the Yellow River, and followed the Huai, Si, Ji, Ta, and Luo waterways;
entries.literal: to the east, I gazed upon Luorui and Dapi, met the Yellow River, and followed the Huai, Si, Ji, Ta, and Luo canals;

entries.zh: 西瞻蜀之岷山及離碓；
entries.en: To the west, I looked upon the Min Mountains of Shu and upon Lidui;
entries.literal: to the west, I looked upon the Min Mountains of Shu and upon Lidui;

entries.zh: 北自龍門至于朔方。
entries.en: to the north, I traveled from Longmen to Shuofang.
entries.literal: to the north, I went from Longmen to Shuofang.

entries.zh: 曰：甚哉，水之為利害也！
entries.en: How great indeed are the benefits and harms of water!
entries.literal: How great are the benefits and harms of water!

entries.zh: 余從負薪塞宣房，悲瓠子之詩而作河渠書。
entries.en: I followed the men carrying firewood to block Xuanfang, grieved over the poem of the Huzi breach, and thus wrote the Book of Rivers and Canals.
entries.literal: I followed the men carrying firewood to block Xuanfang, grieved over the poem of the Huzi breach, and so wrote the Book of Rivers and Canals.

entries.zh: 《夏書》曰：禹抑洪水十三年，過家不入門。
entries.en: The Xia Shu says that Yu controlled the floods for thirteen years and passed his home without entering.
entries.literal: The Xia Shu says: Yu controlled the floods for thirteen years and passed his home without entering.

entries.zh: 陸行載車，水行載舟，泥行蹈毳，山行即橋。
entries.en: On land, he used carts; on water, boats; in mud, rush mats; and in the mountains, bridges.
entries.literal: He used carts on land, boats on water, rush matting in mud, and bridges in the mountains.

entries.zh: 以別九州，隨山浚川，任土作貢。
entries.en: He set apart the Nine Provinces, dredged the rivers along the mountains, and assigned tribute according to the soil.
entries.literal: He distinguished the nine provinces, dredged the rivers along the mountains, and assigned tribute according to the soil.

entries.zh: 通九道，陂九澤，度九山。
entries.en: He opened the Nine Roads, embanked the Nine Marshes, and surveyed the Nine Mountains.
entries.literal: He opened the nine roads, banked the nine marshes, and measured the nine mountains.

entries.zh: 然河菑衍溢，害中國也尤甚。
entries.en: But the Yellow River’s flood damage was especially severe in the Central States.
entries.literal: Yet the Yellow River’s flood disasters were especially severe in the Central States.

entries.zh: 唯是為務。
entries.en: That was his only task.
entries.literal: This alone was his task.

entries.zh: 故道河自積石歷龍門，南到華陰，東下砥柱，及孟津、雒汭，至于大邳。
entries.en: So he traced the Yellow River from Jishi through Longmen, south to Huayin, then east down Dizhu, through Mengjin and Luorui, and on to Dapi.
entries.literal: Therefore, he guided the Yellow River from Jishi through Longmen, south to Huayin, then east down Dizhu, through Mengjin and Luorui, and on to Dapi.

entries.zh: 於是禹以為河所從來者高，水湍悍，難以行平地，數為敗，乃二渠以引其河。
entries.en: Believing the river’s source was high and its current swift and violent, he found it hard to channel across level ground and often failed, so he split it into two channels to divert it.
entries.literal: He thought the river’s source was high and its current swift and violent, so it was difficult to channel across level ground and often failed; he therefore divided it into two channels to lead it off.

entries.zh: 北載之高地，過降水，至于大陸，播為九河，同為逆河，入于勃海九川既疏，九澤既灑，諸夏艾安，功施于三代。
entries.en: He led it north to higher ground, crossed Jiangshui, reached the Great Plain, spread it into the Nine Rivers, turned them all into reverse-flowing channels, and sent them into the Bohai Sea. Once the Nine Rivers had been dredged and the Nine Marshes drained, the Xia states were at peace, and his achievement endured through the Three Dynasties.
entries.literal: He diverted it north to high ground, crossed Jiangshui, reached the Great Plain, spread it into the nine rivers, made them all reverse-flowing channels, and sent them into the Bohai Sea. After the nine rivers had been dredged and the nine marshes drained, the various Xia states were at peace, and his achievement extended through the Three Dynasties.

entries.zh: 天下已平，高祖乃令賈人不得衣絲乘車，重租稅以困辱之。
entries.en: After the realm was pacified, Emperor Gaozu then ordered that merchants could not wear silk or ride carriages and imposed heavy taxes to disgrace them.
entries.literal: World already pacified, Gao Zu then ordered merchants not wear silk ride carriages, heavy taxes to distress humiliate them.

entries.zh: 孝惠、高后時，為天下初定，復弛商賈之律，然市井之子孫亦不得仕宦為吏。
entries.en: During the time of Emperor Xiaohui and Empress Dowager Gao, since the realm had only just been settled, they again relaxed the laws on merchants, yet the sons and grandsons of the marketplace still could not serve as officials or clerks.
entries.literal: Xiao Hui, Gao Hou time, because world initially settled, again relaxed merchant laws, yet marketplace sons grandsons also not allowed serve as officials be clerks.

entries.zh: 量吏祿，度官用，以賦於民。
entries.en: They measured clerk salaries and estimated official expenses, then levied them on the people.
entries.literal: Measured clerk salaries, estimated official expenses, to levy on people.

entries.zh: 而山川園池市井租稅之入，自天子以至于封君湯沐邑，皆各為私奉養焉，不領於天下之經費。
entries.en: Revenues from mountains, rivers, parks, ponds, and marketplaces, from the Son of Heaven down to the enfeoffed lords and their maintenance estates, were all reserved for private support and not counted among the realm's ordinary expenses.
entries.literal: And mountains rivers parks ponds marketplace tax incomes, from Son of Heaven down to sealed lords hot bath towns, all each for private support, not included in world regular expenses.

entries.zh: 漕轉山東粟，以給中都官，歲不過數十萬石。
entries.en: Grain from Shandong was transported to supply the central offices, and the yearly total did not exceed several hundred thousand shi.
entries.literal: Shandong grain was transported by canal to supply the central government offices, no more than several hundred thousand shi per year.

entries.zh: 至孝文時，莢錢益多，輕，乃更鑄四銖錢，其文為「半兩」，令民縱得自鑄錢。
entries.en: By the time of Emperor Xiaowen, elm-seed tokens had grown numerous and light, so they cast new four-zhu coins bearing the inscription “half liang,” and allowed the people to cast coins freely.
entries.literal: To Xiaowen’s time, elm-seed tokens grew many and light; then they recast four-zhu money, its inscription “half liang,” and ordered the people freely to cast money.

entries.zh: 故吳諸侯也，以即山鑄錢，富埒天子，其後卒以叛逆。
entries.en: Therefore, the feudal lord of Wu cast coins near the mountains, became as rich as the Son of Heaven, and later finally rebelled.
entries.literal: Therefore, Wu feudal lord, by near mountain cast money, rich equal Son of Heaven, his after finally with rebellion.

entries.zh: 鄧通，大夫也，以鑄錢財過王者。
entries.en: Deng Tong, a grand master, grew richer than kings by casting money.
entries.literal: Deng Tong, grand master, with casting money wealth exceeded kings.

entries.zh: 故吳、鄧氏錢布天下，而鑄錢之禁生焉。
entries.en: Thus, the coinage of Wu and the Deng clan spread throughout the realm, and the prohibition on casting money arose from it.
entries.literal: Therefore, Wu, Deng clan money spread world, and casting money prohibition born there.

entries.zh: 至今上即位數歲，漢興七十餘年之閒，國家無事，非遇水旱之災，民則人給家足，都鄙廩庾皆滿，而府庫餘貨財。
entries.en: By the time the present emperor had been on the throne for several years, in the more than seventy years since Han rose, the nation had no affairs. When they did not encounter water or drought disasters, the people then had each person supplied and each house sufficient, the granaries of cities and towns were all full, and the treasuries had surplus goods and wealth.
entries.literal: To now emperor ascended throne several years, Han rise seventy more years between, nation no affairs, not encounter water drought disasters, people then person supplied house sufficient, cities towns granaries all full, and treasuries surplus goods wealth.

entries.zh: 京師之錢累巨萬，貫朽而不可校。
entries.en: The money in the capital accumulated in enormous quantities, until the strings rotted, and the coins could no longer be counted.
entries.literal: Capital money accumulated huge ten thousand, strings rotted and could not be counted.

entries.zh: 太倉之粟陳陳相因，充溢露積於外，至腐敗不可食。
entries.en: The grain in the great granary, old grain following old grain, was full and overflowed, exposed and piled outside, until it rotted and could not be eaten.
entries.literal: Great granary grain old old mutually followed, full overflowed exposed piled outside, to rotten could not be eaten.

entries.zh: 眾庶街巷有馬，阡陌之閒成群，而乘字牝者儐而不得聚會。
entries.en: Commoners in streets and alleys had horses, and along the paths and crossroads they formed groups; those who rode government-branded mares were shunned and could not gather for meetings.
entries.literal: The masses in streets and alleys had horses, and between paths and crossroads they formed groups; those who rode government-branded mares were shunned and could not gather for meetings.

entries.zh: 守閭閻者食粱肉，為吏者長子孫，居官者以為姓號。
entries.en: Those who guarded the alley gates ate fine grain and meat, those who served as clerks extended their sons and grandsons, and those who resided as officials took it as their surname and appellation.
entries.literal: Guarded alley gates ate fine grain meat, served as clerks extended sons grandsons, resided as officials took as surname appellation.

entries.zh: 故人人自愛而重犯法，先行義而後絀恥辱焉。
entries.en: Therefore, each person loved themselves and valued not violating the law, first practiced righteousness, and then shrank from shame and humiliation.
entries.literal: Therefore, each person self loved and valued not violate law, first practiced righteousness then shrank from shame humiliation.

entries.zh: 當此之時，網疏而民富，役財驕溢，或至兼并豪黨之徒，以武斷於鄉曲。
entries.en: At this time, the net of law was loose, and the people were wealthy. Some became arrogant and extravagant in their use of wealth, even annexing land and gathering powerful retainers, using force to dominate local affairs.
entries.literal: At this time, the legal net was loose and the people were wealthy. Some grew arrogant and extravagant in their use of wealth, even annexing land and gathering powerful followers, and settled affairs in the countryside by force.

entries.zh: 宗室有土公卿大夫以下，爭于奢侈，室廬輿服僭于上，無限度。
entries.en: The imperial clan, territorial lords, high ministers, and officials below them competed in extravagance, and their houses, carriages, and clothing exceeded the privileges allowed by their rank.
entries.literal: The imperial clan, territorial lords, high ministers, and officials below them competed in extravagance, and their houses, carriages, and clothing overstepped the privileges of their superiors without limit.

entries.zh: 物盛而衰，固其變也。
entries.en: When things flourish, they then decline; this is certainly their change.
entries.literal: Things flourish then decline, certainly their change.

entries.zh: 其後四年，而漢遣大將將六將軍，軍十餘萬，擊右賢王，獲首虜萬五千級。
entries.en: Four years later, the Han sent a great general with six generals and an army of more than a hundred thousand to attack the Right Worthy King, and took fifteen thousand heads and captives.
entries.literal: Its after four years, and Han sent great general led six generals, army ten more thousand, attacked right worthy king, obtained heads captives ten five thousand ranks.

entries.zh: 明年，大將軍將六將軍仍再出擊胡，得首虜萬九千級。
entries.en: The next year, the great general again led the six generals out against the Hu and took nineteen thousand heads and captives.
entries.literal: Next year, great general led six generals still again went out attacked Hu, got heads captives ten nine thousand ranks.

entries.zh: 捕斬首虜之士受賜黃金二十餘萬斤，虜數萬人皆得厚賞，衣食仰給縣官；
entries.en: The soldiers who captured and beheaded the enemy received more than two hundred thousand jin of yellow gold, and the captives, numbering tens of thousands, all received generous rewards; their clothing and food were supplied by the county officials.
entries.literal: Captured beheaded heads captives soldiers received rewarded yellow gold twenty more ten thousand jin, captives several ten thousand people all got thick reward, clothing food looked up supplied county officials;

entries.zh: 而漢軍之士馬死者十餘萬，兵甲之財轉漕之費不與焉。
entries.en: The dead soldiers and horses of the Han army numbered more than a hundred thousand, and the cost of armor and transport is not included.
entries.literal: And Han army soldiers horses dead ones ten more thousand, weapons armor wealth transported expenses not included there.

entries.zh: 於是大農陳藏錢經秏，賦稅既竭，猶不足以奉戰士。
entries.en: By then, the Grand Farmer's cash reserves had been depleted and tax revenues exhausted, yet there was still not enough to support the soldiers.
entries.literal: By then, the Grand Farmer's cash reserves had been depleted and tax revenues exhausted, yet there was still not enough to support the soldiers.

entries.zh: 有司言：「天子曰『朕聞五帝之教不相復而治，禹湯之法不同道而王，所由殊路，而建德一也。
entries.en: The officials said: “The Son of Heaven has said, ‘I have heard that the teachings of the Five Emperors were not repeated, yet they governed; the laws of Yu and Tang were different, yet they both became kings. What they came from was different, but the virtue they established was the same.
entries.literal: Officials spoke: 'Son of Heaven said 'I heard five emperors teachings not repeated and governed, Yu Tang laws different ways and kinged, what from different roads, but established virtue one also.

entries.zh: 北邊未安，朕甚悼之。
entries.en: The northern frontier is not at peace, and I am deeply troubled by it.
entries.literal: North border not peaceful, I very mourn it.

entries.zh: 日者，大將軍攻匈奴，斬首虜萬九千級，留蹛無所食。
entries.en: Recently, the great general attacked the Xiongnu, taking nineteen thousand heads and captives, but the detained prisoners were left with nothing to eat.
entries.literal: Recently the great general attacked the Xiongnu, beheaded nineteen thousand heads and captives, and left the detained captives with nothing to eat.

entries.zh: 議令民得買爵及贖禁錮免減罪』。
entries.en: We ask that people be allowed to buy ranks and redeem penalties and confinement, and thereby reduce crimes.'
entries.literal: Discuss ordered people could buy nobility rank and redeem prohibitions imprisonments exempt reduce crimes.'

entries.zh: 請置賞官，命曰武功爵。
entries.en: We request the establishment of reward offices, to be called martial merit ranks.
entries.literal: Request establish reward officials, named martial merit nobility ranks.

entries.zh: 級十七萬，凡直三十餘萬金。
entries.en: There were 170,000 ranks in all, worth more than 300,000 in gold.
entries.literal: There were 170,000 ranks in all, worth more than 300,000 in gold.

entries.zh: 諸買武功爵官首者試補吏，先除；
entries.en: Those who buy the martial merit rank first are tested for office and given priority in exemption;
entries.literal: Various buy martial merit nobility rank officials first ones tested filled clerks, first exempted;

entries.zh: 千夫如五大夫；
entries.en: a thousand-man commander is treated like a fifth-grade grand master;
entries.literal: Thousand leader like five grand masters;

entries.zh: 其有罪又減二等；
entries.en: if they have committed crimes, their sentence is reduced by two grades;
entries.literal: Their had crimes moreover reduced two grades;

entries.zh: 爵得至樂卿：以顯軍功。」
entries.en: and the rank can rise as high as Leqing, all to display military merit.”
entries.literal: Nobility rank could reach music minister: to display military merit.'

entries.zh: 軍功多用越等，大者封侯卿大夫，小者郎吏。
entries.en: Military merit often leapt past the ordinary ranks: the greatest were enfeoffed as marquises, ministers, and grandees, while lesser men became palace gentlemen and clerks.
entries.literal: Military merit often bypassed the usual ranks, with the greatest being enfeoffed as marquises, ministers, and grandees, and the lesser as palace gentlemen and clerks.

entries.zh: 吏道雜而多端，則官職秏廢。
entries.en: When the paths of official advancement become mixed and too many, the offices are worn down and ruined.
entries.literal: Clerk ways mixed and many branches, then official duties expended abolished.

entries.zh: 天子為伐胡，盛養馬，馬之來食長安者數萬匹，卒牽掌者關中不足，乃調旁近郡。
entries.en: For the campaign against the Hu, the Son of Heaven greatly raised horses. Tens of thousands of horses came to feed at Chang’an, but Guanzhong did not have enough men to tend them, so they requisitioned from nearby commanderies.
entries.literal: Son of Heaven for attacked Hu, greatly raised horses, horses that came ate Chang An several ten thousand horses, soldiers led cared ones Guan Zhong insufficient, then transferred nearby commanderies.

entries.zh: 而胡降者皆衣食縣官，縣官不給，天子乃損膳，解乘輿駟，出御府禁藏以贍之。
entries.en: All the surrendered Hu had to be fed and clothed by the government, but the government could not meet the demand. The Son of Heaven therefore reduced his own meals, released horses from the imperial carriage teams, and drew on the palace storehouses to support them.
entries.literal: And Hu surrendered ones all clothed fed county officials, county officials not supplied, Son of Heaven then reduced meals, released carriage teams, took out imperial storehouse forbidden stores to support them.

entries.zh: 其明年，山東被水菑，民多饑乏，於是天子遣使者虛郡國倉廥以振貧民。
entries.en: The next year, Shandong suffered flooding and many people were hungry and destitute. The Son of Heaven therefore sent messengers to empty the commanderies’ and kingdoms’ granaries to relieve the poor.
entries.literal: Its next year, Shan Dong suffered water disaster, people many hungry lacking, therefore Son of Heaven sent messengers emptied commandery kingdom granaries to relieve poor people.

entries.zh: 猶不足，又募豪富人相貸假。
entries.en: Even so it was still not enough, so they recruited wealthy men to lend to the poor.
entries.literal: Still it was insufficient; moreover they recruited wealthy men to lend to the poor.

entries.zh: 尚不能相救，乃徙貧民於關以西，及充朔方以南新秦中，七十餘萬口，衣食皆仰給縣官。
entries.en: Still this was not enough to save them all, so the poor were moved west of the pass and into the newly settled Qin region south of Shuofang, more than seven hundred thousand people in all, with food and clothing supplied by the government.
entries.literal: Still could not mutually save, then moved poor people to pass west, and filled Shuo Fang south new Qin middle, seventy more ten thousand mouths, clothing food all looked up supplied county officials.

entries.zh: 數歲，假予產業，使者分部護之，冠蓋相望。
entries.en: For several years they were given land and property, and the messengers were assigned in districts to protect them, with official canopies and banners appearing everywhere.
entries.literal: Several years, lent gave properties, messengers divided sections protected them, official hats canopies mutually gazed.

entries.zh: 其費以億計，不可勝數。
entries.en: The expense was counted in hundreds of millions and could not be measured.
entries.literal: Its expenses counted in hundred million, could not be completely counted.

entries.zh: 於是縣官大空。
entries.en: Thus, the county offices were left greatly depleted.
entries.literal: Therefore, county officials greatly empty.

entries.zh: 而富商大賈或蹛財役貧，轉轂百數，廢居居邑，封君皆低首仰給。
entries.en: Rich merchants and great traders either hoarded wealth and employed the poor, rotated wagon hubs by the hundreds, hoarded goods and waited in towns, and the enfeoffed lords all bowed their heads and relied on them for supplies.
entries.literal: The rich merchants and great traders either hoarded wealth and employed the poor, rotated axles by the hundreds, hoarded goods and resided in towns, and the enfeoffed lords all lowered their heads and looked up to them for supply.

entries.zh: 冶鑄煮鹽，財或累萬金，而不佐國家之急，黎民重困。
entries.en: Through smelting, casting, and boiling salt, wealth accumulated to tens of thousands of gold, but it did not help the state’s urgent needs, and the common people were heavily burdened.
entries.literal: Smelted cast boiled salt, wealth or accumulated ten thousand gold, but not assisted nation urgent, common people heavily distressed.

entries.zh: 於是天子與公卿議，更錢造幣以贍用，而摧浮淫并兼之徒。
entries.en: Therefore, the Son of Heaven discussed the matter with the dukes and ministers, remade the currency to supply public use, and checked the men who grew fat on floating gains and monopoly.
entries.literal: Therefore, Son of Heaven with dukes ministers discussed, changed money made currency to support use, and crushed floating lewd annexed merged followers.

entries.zh: 是時禁苑有白鹿而少府多銀錫。
entries.en: At this time the forbidden park had white deer and the Shaofu had abundant silver and tin.
entries.literal: This time forbidden park had white deer and Shao Fu much silver tin.

entries.zh: 自孝文更造四銖錢，至是歲四十餘年，從建元以來，用少，縣官往往即多銅山而鑄錢，民亦閒盜鑄錢，不可勝數。
entries.en: From the time Emperor Xiaowen cast the four-zhu coin, more than forty years had passed by this year. Since Jianyuan, coinage was scarce, and the county officials often took the copper from many mountains to cast money; the people also secretly cast coins in great numbers.
entries.literal: From Xiao Wen moreover made four zhu money, to this year forty more years, from Jian Yuan since, use few, county officials often took many copper mountains and cast money, people also secretly stole cast money, could not be completely counted.

entries.zh: 錢益多而輕，物益少而貴。
entries.en: Money became more numerous and lighter, while goods became scarcer and dearer.
entries.literal: Money moreover many and light, goods moreover few and expensive.

entries.zh: 有司言曰：「古者皮幣，諸侯以聘享。
entries.en: The officials said: “In ancient times there was leather currency, which the feudal lords used for presenting gifts and making offerings.
entries.literal: Officials spoke: 'Ancient ones leather currency, feudal lords with presented enjoyed.

entries.zh: 金有三等，黃金為上，白金為中，赤金為下。
entries.en: Gold had three grades: yellow gold as the highest, white gold as the middle, and red gold as the lowest.
entries.literal: Gold had three grades, yellow gold as upper, white gold as middle, red gold as lower.

entries.zh: 今半兩錢法重四銖，而姦或盜摩錢裏取鋊，錢益輕薄而物貴，則遠方用幣煩費不省。」
entries.en: Now the half-liang coin weighs four zhu, but corrupt men grind the inside of the coins and take out filings, so money becomes thinner and lighter while goods grow dearer; thus currency used in distant places becomes troublesome and costly.”
entries.literal: Now half liang money method heavy four zhu, but evil ones or stole ground money inside took filings, money moreover light thin and goods expensive, then distant places used currency troublesome costly not economical.'

entries.zh: 乃以白鹿皮方尺，緣以藻繢，為皮幣，直四十萬。
entries.en: Then they took a square foot of white deer skin, edged it with embroidered ornament, and made leather currency worth four hundred thousand.
entries.literal: Then with a square foot of white deer skin, edged with embroidered ornament, they made leather currency worth four hundred thousand.

entries.zh: 王侯宗室朝覲聘享，必以皮幣薦璧，然後得行。
entries.en: When kings, marquises, and the imperial clan had audiences or made offerings, they had to present jade bi with leather currency and only then could proceed.
entries.literal: Kings marquises imperial clan morning audiences presented enjoyed, must with leather currency presented jade bi, then could proceed.

entries.zh: 大農上鹽鐵丞孔僅、咸陽言：「山海，天地之藏也，皆宜屬少府，陛下不私，以屬大農佐賦。
entries.en: The Great Farmer submitted a proposal from the salt and iron assistants Kong Jin and Xianyang: 'The mountains and seas are the storehouses of heaven and earth, and should all belong to the Privy Treasurer. Your Majesty does not keep them for private use, but assigns them to the Great Farmer to support public revenues.
entries.literal: Great Farmer submitted salt iron assistant Kong Jin, Xian Yang spoke: 'Mountains seas, heaven earth stores also, all should belong Shao Fu, Your Majesty not private, to belong Great Farmer assist taxes.

entries.zh: 願募民自給費，因官器作煮鹽，官與牢盆。
entries.en: We ask to recruit people who will cover their own expenses and use official equipment to boil salt, with the government providing the iron pans.
entries.literal: Wish recruit people self supply expenses, using official tools make boil salt, officials give iron pans.

entries.zh: 浮食奇民欲擅管山海之貨，以致富羨，役利細民。
entries.en: Idlers and speculators wish to monopolize the products of the mountains and seas, enrich themselves, and exploit the common people for profit.
entries.literal: Floating eating strange people wish monopolize control mountains seas goods, to become rich abundant, employ profit small people.

entries.zh: 其沮事之議，不可勝聽。
entries.en: Their obstructionist arguments are too many to listen to.
entries.literal: Their obstructed affairs discussions, could not be completely heard.

entries.zh: 敢私鑄鐵器煮鹽者，釱左趾，沒入其器物。
entries.en: Anyone who dares privately to cast iron tools or boil salt shall have the left toe fettered and all tools and goods confiscated.
entries.literal: Dare privately cast iron tools boil salt ones, branded left toe, confiscated their tools goods.

entries.zh: 郡不出鐵者，置小鐵官，便屬在所縣。」
entries.en: In commanderies that do not produce iron, establish minor iron offices and attach them to the local counties.'
entries.literal: Commanderies not produce iron ones, establish small iron officials, conveniently belong local counties.'

entries.zh: 使孔僅、東郭咸陽乘傳舉行天下鹽鐵，作官府，除故鹽鐵家富者為吏。
entries.en: They sent Kong Jin and Dongguo Xianyang by relay carriage to inspect salt and iron operations throughout the empire, establish government offices, and appoint wealthy men from the former salt and iron families as officials.
entries.literal: Made Kong Jin, Dongguo Xian Yang ride post carriages toured world salt iron, established official offices, removed former salt iron family rich ones served as clerks.

entries.zh: 吏道益雜，不選，而多賈人矣。
entries.en: The ranks of officials became increasingly mixed and were no longer carefully selected; many were merchants.
entries.literal: Clerk ways moreover mixed, not selected, and many merchants.

entries.zh: 其明年，驃騎仍再出擊胡，獲首四萬。
entries.en: The next year, the swift cavalry again went out to attack the Hu and took forty thousand heads.
entries.literal: Its next year, super cavalry still again went out attacked Hu, obtained heads forty thousand.

entries.zh: 其秋，渾邪王率數萬之眾來降，於是漢發車二萬乘迎之。
entries.en: That autumn, the Hunye King led tens of thousands to surrender, and Han accordingly sent twenty thousand carriages to welcome them.
entries.literal: Its autumn, Hun Ye king led several ten thousand crowd came surrendered, therefore Han sent carriages twenty thousand teams welcomed them.

entries.zh: 既至，受賞，賜及有功之士。
entries.en: Once they arrived, rewards were bestowed, and the meritorious soldiers received their share.
entries.literal: Having arrived, received rewards, bestowed reached meritorious warriors.

entries.zh: 是歲費凡百餘巨萬。
entries.en: That year’s expenses altogether amounted to more than a hundred huge ten-thousands.
entries.literal: This year expenses altogether hundred more huge ten thousand.

entries.zh: 又造銀錫為白金。
entries.en: They also made silver and tin into white gold.
entries.literal: Moreover, made silver tin as white gold.

entries.zh: 以為天用莫如龍，地用莫如馬，人用莫如龜，故白金三品：其一曰重八兩，圜之，其文龍，名曰「白選」，直三千；
entries.en: They held that for heaven nothing was better than the dragon, for earth nothing better than the horse, and for man nothing better than the turtle. Therefore, there were three grades of white gold: the first weighed eight liang, was round, bore a dragon, and was called “White Selection,” worth three thousand;
entries.literal: Considered heaven use nothing like dragon, earth use nothing like horse, person use nothing like turtle, therefore white gold three kinds: its one said heavy eight liang, rounded it, its inscription dragon, named 'white select', worth three thousand;

entries.zh: 二曰以重差小，方之，其文馬，直五百；
entries.en: the second had a slightly lighter weight, was square, bore a horse, and was worth five hundred;
entries.literal: Two said with weight difference small, squared it, its inscription horse, worth five hundred;

entries.zh: 三曰復小，撱之，其文龜，直三百。
entries.en: the third was smaller still, was made oval, bore a turtle, and was worth three hundred;
entries.literal: The third was smaller still, made oval, bore a turtle, and was worth three hundred.

entries.zh: 令縣官銷半兩錢，更鑄三銖錢，文如其重。
entries.en: They ordered the county officials to melt down the half-liang coins and cast new three-zhu coins with inscriptions matching their weight.
entries.literal: Ordered county officials melted half liang money, moreover cast three zhu money, inscription like its weight.

entries.zh: 盜鑄諸金錢罪皆死，而吏民之盜鑄白金者不可勝數。
entries.en: Those who privately cast gold coins were all liable to death, yet the clerks and commoners who secretly cast white gold coins were too many to count.
entries.literal: Stole cast various gold money crimes all death, but clerks people stole cast white gold ones could not be completely counted.

entries.zh: 於是以東郭咸陽、孔僅為大農丞，領鹽鐵事；
entries.en: Therefore, they made Dongguo Xianyang and Kong Jin the Great Farmer Assistant, to lead salt and iron affairs;
entries.literal: Therefore, with Dongguo Xian Yang, Kong Jin as Great Farmer Assistant, led salt iron affairs;

entries.zh: 桑弘羊以計算用事，侍中。
entries.en: Sang Hongyang handled financial calculations as a Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: Sang Hong Yang with calculations handled affairs, Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 咸陽，齊之大煮鹽，孔僅，南陽大冶，皆致生累千金，故鄭當時進言之。
entries.en: Xianyang was a major salt producer from Qi, and Kong Jin was a major iron smelter from Nanyang. Both had amassed fortunes of thousands of gold, and therefore Zheng Dangshi recommended them.
entries.literal: Xianyang was a major salt producer from Qi, and Kong Jin a major iron smelter from Nanyang; both had amassed fortunes of several thousand in gold, so Zheng Dangshi recommended them.

entries.zh: 弘羊，雒陽賈人子，以心計，年十三侍中。
entries.en: Hongyang was the son of a merchant from Luoyang. Because of his skill at mental calculation, he became a Palace Attendant at the age of thirteen.
entries.literal: Hong Yang, Luo Yang merchant son, with mental calculations, year thirteen Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 故三人言利事析秋豪矣。
entries.en: Thus, when these three men discussed matters of profit, they analyzed them down to the finest detail.
entries.literal: Therefore, three people spoke profit affairs analyzed autumn down.

entries.zh: 天子乃思卜式之言，召拜式為中郎，爵左庶長，賜田十頃，布告天下，使明知之。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven then recalled Bu Shi's words, summoned and appointed Shi as Palace Attendant, granted him the rank of Left Chief of the Multitude, granted ten qing of fields, and proclaimed it to the realm, so all would know.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven then recalled Bu Shi's words, summoned and appointed Shi as Palace Attendant, granted him the rank of Left Chief of the Multitude, granted ten qing of fields, and proclaimed it to the realm so all would know.

entries.zh: 初，卜式者，河南人也，以田畜為事。
entries.en: Initially, Bu Shi was a person from Henan, and he took farming and livestock as his affairs.
entries.literal: Initially, Bu Shi was, He Nan person also, with farming livestock as affairs.

entries.zh: 親死，式有少弟，弟壯，式脫身出分，獨取畜羊百餘，田宅財物盡予弟。
entries.en: When his parents died, Shi had a young brother. When the brother grew up, Shi separated himself and divided the property, taking alone more than a hundred livestock sheep, and giving all the fields, houses, wealth, and goods to his brother.
entries.literal: Parents died, Shi had young brother, brother grew up, Shi separated body out divided, alone took livestock sheep hundred more, fields houses wealth goods all gave brother.

entries.zh: 式入山牧十餘歲，羊致千餘頭，買田宅。
entries.en: Shi entered the mountains and pastured for more than ten years, and the sheep brought more than a thousand heads, so he bought fields and houses.
entries.literal: Shi entered mountain pastured ten more years, sheep brought thousand more heads, bought fields houses.

entries.zh: 而其弟盡破其業，式輒復分予弟者數矣。
entries.en: Whenever his brother squandered his property, Bu Shi again divided off part of his own property and gave it to him.
entries.literal: When his brother squandered his property, Bu Shi repeatedly divided off shares of his own property and gave them to him.

entries.zh: 是時漢方數使將擊匈奴，卜式上書，願輸家之半縣官助邊。
entries.en: At this time, Han was just frequently sending generals to attack the Xiongnu, and Bu Shi submitted a memorial, wishing to transport half of his family's wealth to the county officials to assist the border.
entries.literal: This time Han just frequently sent generals attacked Xiongnu, Bu Shi memorialed, wished transport family half county officials assist border.

entries.zh: 天子使使問式：「欲官乎？」
entries.en: The Son of Heaven sent a messenger to ask Shi, “Do you want an official post?”
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven sent a messenger to ask Shi: “Do you wish for office?”

entries.zh: 式曰：「臣少牧，不習仕宦，不願也。」
entries.en: Shi said, “Your servant has herded animals since youth and does not understand official service. I do not want it.”
entries.literal: Shi said: “Your servant has herded since youth and is not versed in official service; I do not wish it.”

entries.zh: 使問曰：「家豈有冤，欲言事乎？」
entries.en: The messenger asked, “Does your household perhaps have some grievance you wish to report?”
entries.literal: The messenger asked: “Does your household perhaps have a grievance you wish to report?”

entries.zh: 式曰：「臣生與人無分爭。
entries.en: Shi said, “Your servant has lived his life without quarreling with others.
entries.literal: Shi said: “Your servant has gone through life without quarreling with others.

entries.zh: 式邑人貧者貸之，不善者教順之，所居人皆從式，式何故見冤於人！
entries.en: I lend to the poor in my village and teach and guide the unruly. Everyone where I live follows me, so why would I suffer grievance from others?
entries.literal: I lend to the poor among my townspeople and teach and guide those who are unruly; those where I live all follow me—why should I suffer grievance from others!

entries.zh: 無所欲言也。」
entries.en: There is nothing I wish to say.”
entries.literal: There is nothing I wish to say.”

entries.zh: 使者曰：「茍如此，子何欲而然？」
entries.en: The messenger said, “If that is so, sir, what do you want, and why are you acting this way?”
entries.literal: The messenger said: “If it is so, sir, what do you want, and why act thus?”

entries.zh: 式曰：「天子誅匈奴，愚以為賢者宜死節於邊，有財者宜輸委，如此而匈奴可滅也。」
entries.en: Shi said, “The Son of Heaven is punishing the Xiongnu. Your foolish servant thinks that the worthy should die loyally at the frontier and the wealthy should contribute their goods. In this way the Xiongnu can be destroyed.”
entries.literal: Shi said: “The Son of Heaven is punishing the Xiongnu. I, your foolish servant, think the worthy should die loyally at the border and the wealthy should contribute their goods; in this way the Xiongnu can be destroyed.”

entries.zh: 使者具其言入以聞。
entries.en: The messenger completed his words and entered to report.
entries.literal: Messenger complete his words entered to report.

entries.zh: 天子以語丞相弘。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven spoke of it to Chancellor Hong.
entries.literal: Son of Heaven with spoke Chancellor Hong.

entries.zh: 弘曰：「此非人情。
entries.en: Hong said: “This is not human feeling.
entries.literal: Hong said: “This is not human feeling.

entries.zh: 不軌之臣，不可以為化而亂法，願陛下勿許。」
entries.en: Such lawless subjects cannot be held up as models without undermining the law. I beg Your Majesty not to permit it.”
entries.literal: Such lawless subjects cannot be held up as models without subverting the law. I beg Your Majesty not to permit it.”

entries.zh: 於是上久不報式，數歲，乃罷式。
entries.en: The emperor therefore gave Shi no reply for a long time, and after several years he let the matter drop.
entries.literal: Thereupon the emperor long gave no reply to Shi; after several years he set the matter aside.

entries.zh: 式歸，復田牧。
entries.en: Shi returned and again farmed and pastured.
entries.literal: Shi returned, again farmed pastured.

entries.zh: 歲餘，會軍數出，渾邪王等降，縣官費眾，倉府空。
entries.en: More than a year later, with the army frequently in the field and the Hunye king and others having surrendered, government expenses mounted and the granaries and treasuries were empty.
entries.literal: Year more, met army frequently went out, Hun Ye king etc. surrendered, county officials expenses many, granaries treasuries empty.

entries.zh: 其明年，貧民大徙，皆仰給縣官，無以盡贍。
entries.en: The next year, large numbers of poor people migrated. They all depended on the government for support, but there was no way to provide fully for them.
entries.literal: Its next year, poor people greatly moved, all looked up supplied county officials, no with completely support.

entries.zh: 卜式持錢二十萬予河南守，以給徙民。
entries.en: Bu Shi brought 200,000 cash and gave it to the Governor of Henan to supply the relocated people.
entries.literal: Bu Shi held money twenty ten thousand gave He Nan governor, to supply moved people.

entries.zh: 河南上富人助貧人者籍，天子見卜式名，識之，曰「是固前而欲輸其家半助邊」，乃賜式外繇四百人。
entries.en: Henan submitted a register of wealthy men who had aided the poor. When the Son of Heaven saw Bu Shi's name, he recognized him and said, “This is the man who earlier wished to contribute half his property to aid the frontier,” and granted Shi the commutation payments for four hundred men's frontier service.
entries.literal: Henan submitted a register of wealthy men who had aided the poor. The Son of Heaven saw Bu Shi's name, recognized him, and said, “This is the man who earlier wished to contribute half his property to aid the frontier,” then granted Shi the commutation payments for four hundred men's frontier service.

entries.zh: 式又盡復予縣官。
entries.en: Shi then gave the county officials additional funds in full.
entries.literal: Shi moreover completely again gave county officials.

entries.zh: 是時富豪皆爭匿財，唯式尤欲輸之助費。
entries.en: At this time, the rich and powerful all competed to conceal their wealth, but Bu Shi alone was eager to send his wealth in to help meet state expenses.
entries.literal: At this time, the rich and powerful all competed to hide their wealth, but Bu Shi alone was eager to send his wealth in to help meet state expenses.

entries.zh: 天子於是以式終長者，故尊顯以風百姓。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven therefore considered Shi as a worthy elder, and therefore honored and displayed him to influence the hundred surnames.
entries.literal: Son of Heaven therefore with Shi as worthy elder, therefore honored displayed to influence hundred surnames.

entries.zh: 商賈以幣之變，多積貨逐利。
entries.en: The merchants, because of the currency changes, accumulated many goods and pursued profit.
entries.literal: Merchants with currency changes, many accumulated goods pursued profit.

entries.zh: 於是公卿言：「郡國頗被菑害，貧民無產業者，募徙廣饒之地。
entries.en: Therefore, the dukes and ministers said: 'The commanderies and kingdoms have rather suffered disasters, and the poor people who have no property should be recruited and moved to broad and fertile lands.
entries.literal: Therefore, dukes ministers spoke: 'Commanderies kingdoms rather suffered disasters, poor people no property ones, recruit move broad fertile lands.

entries.zh: 陛下損膳省用，出禁錢以振元元，寬貸賦，而民不齊出於南畝，商賈滋眾。
entries.en: Your Majesty reduced meals and economized use, took out forbidden money to relieve the common people, and leniently lent taxes, but the people did not uniformly go out to the south fields, and merchants increased greatly.
entries.literal: Your Majesty reduced meals economized use, took out forbidden money to relieve common people, leniently lent taxes, but people not uniformly went out to south fields, merchants increased many.

entries.zh: 貧者畜積無有，皆仰縣官。
entries.en: The poor had no reserves, and all depended on the county officials.
entries.literal: Poor ones stored accumulated none had, all looked up county officials.

entries.zh: 異時算軺車賈人緡錢皆有差，請算如故。
entries.en: At earlier times, taxes on light carriages, merchants, and registered cash holdings were all graded. We request that they be taxed as before.
entries.literal: Different times taxed light carriages merchants string money all had differences, request tax as before.

entries.zh: 諸賈人末作貰貸賣買，居邑稽諸物，及商以取利者，雖無市籍，各以其物自占，率緡錢二千而一算。
entries.en: Merchants engaged in secondary occupations, borrowing and lending, buying and selling, living in towns, hoarding goods, and taking profit from trade, even if they had no market registration, were each to register themselves and their goods. The rate was one tax for every two thousand strings of cash.
entries.literal: Various merchants end business borrowed lent bought sold, resided towns delayed various goods, and merchants to take profit ones, although no market registration, each with their goods self registered, rate string money two thousand and one tax.

entries.zh: 諸作有租及鑄，率緡錢四千一算。
entries.en: For rented enterprises and casting operations, the rate was one assessment for every four thousand strings of cash.
entries.literal: Various works had rent and cast, rate string money four thousand one tax.

entries.zh: 非吏比者三老、北邊騎士，軺車以一算；
entries.en: For those not of clerk rank, the three elders and north border cavalry, light carriages were taxed at one tax;
entries.literal: Not clerk rank ones three elders, north border cavalry, light carriages with one tax;

entries.zh: 商賈人軺車二算；
entries.en: merchant people's light carriages were taxed at two taxes;
entries.literal: Merchant people light carriages two taxes;

entries.zh: 船五丈以上一算。
entries.en: boats of five zhang or above were taxed at one tax.
entries.literal: Boats five zhang above one tax.

entries.zh: 匿不自占，占不悉，戍邊一歲，沒入緡錢。
entries.en: Those who concealed their holdings and did not register, or registered incompletely, were sent to garrison the frontier for one year, and their cash holdings were confiscated.
entries.literal: Concealed not self registered, registered not complete, garrisoned border one year, confiscated string money.

entries.zh: 有能告者，以其半畀之。
entries.en: Those who were able to report were given half of it.
entries.literal: Had could report ones, with their half gave them.

entries.zh: 賈人有市籍者，及其家屬，皆無得籍名田，以便農。
entries.en: Merchants registered in the market rolls, and their dependents, could not register titled land, to favor farming.
entries.literal: Merchants had market registration ones, and their family dependents, all not got registered named fields, to facilitate farming.

entries.zh: 敢犯令，沒入田僮。」
entries.en: Those who dare to violate the command will have their fields and servants confiscated.'
entries.literal: Dare violate command, confiscated fields servants.'

entries.zh: 初，式不願為郎。
entries.en: Initially, Shi did not wish to be a lang.
entries.literal: Initially, Shi not wished be lang.

entries.zh: 上曰：「吾有羊上林中，欲令子牧之。」
entries.en: The emperor said, “I have sheep in Shanglin Park, and I want you, sir, to herd them.”
entries.literal: The emperor said: “I have sheep in Shanglin Park and wish you, sir, to herd them.”

entries.zh: 式乃拜為郎，布衣屩而牧羊。
entries.en: Shi was then appointed as lang, and wearing cloth clothes and sandals, he pastured sheep.
entries.literal: Shi then appointed lang, cloth clothes sandals and pastured sheep.

entries.zh: 歲餘，羊肥息。
entries.en: More than a year later, the sheep became fat and increased.
entries.literal: Year more, sheep fat increased.

entries.zh: 上過見其羊，善之。
entries.en: The emperor passed by and saw his sheep, and approved of them.
entries.literal: Emperor passed saw his sheep, good them.

entries.zh: 式曰：「非獨羊也，治民亦猶是也。
entries.en: Shi said, “This applies not only to sheep; governing the people is also like this.
entries.literal: Shi said: “It is not only sheep; governing the people is also like this.

entries.zh: 以時起居；
entries.en: Rise and reside according to the time.
entries.literal: By time rise reside;

entries.zh: 惡者輒斥去，毋令敗群。」
entries.en: Drive out the bad ones at once, and do not let them ruin the flock.”
entries.literal: Drive out the bad at once and do not let them ruin the flock.”

entries.zh: 上以式為奇，拜為緱氏令試之，緱氏便之。
entries.en: The emperor considered Shi remarkable and, to test him, appointed him magistrate of Goushi, whose people found his administration beneficial.
entries.literal: The emperor considered Shi remarkable and appointed him magistrate of Goushi to test him; the people of Goushi found his administration beneficial.

entries.zh: 遷為成皋令，將漕最。
entries.en: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Chenggao, where his supervision of grain transport received the highest rating.
entries.literal: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Chenggao, where his supervision of grain transport received the highest rating.

entries.zh: 上以為式樸忠，拜為齊王太傅。
entries.en: The emperor considered Shi simple and loyal, and appointed him as grand tutor to the king of Qi.
entries.literal: Emperor considered Shi simple loyal, appointed Qi king grand tutor.

entries.zh: 而大農顏異誅。
entries.en: The Grand Minister of Agriculture Yan Yi was executed.
entries.literal: And great farmer Yan Yi executed.

entries.zh: 初，異為濟南亭長，以廉直稍遷至九卿。
entries.en: Initially, Yi was a pavilion chief in Jinan, and with integrity and straightness, he gradually moved to the nine ministers.
entries.literal: Initially, Yi was Ji Nan pavilion chief, with integrity straight gradually moved to nine ministers.

entries.zh: 上與張湯既造白鹿皮幣，問異。
entries.en: The emperor, with Zhang Tang, having made white deer skin currency, asked Yi.
entries.literal: Emperor with Zhang Tang having made white deer skin currency, asked Yi.

entries.zh: 異曰：「今王侯朝賀以蒼璧，直數千，而其皮薦反四十萬，本末不相稱。」
entries.en: Yi said: 'Now kings and marquises offer morning congratulations with blue jade bi, worth several thousand, but the skin presented instead is worth four hundred thousand. The root and tip do not match.'
entries.literal: Yi said: 'Now kings marquises morning congratulations with blue jade bi, worth several thousand, but its skin presented instead forty ten thousand, root tip not match.'

entries.zh: 天子不說。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven was not pleased.
entries.literal: Son of Heaven not pleased.

entries.zh: 張湯又與異有卻，及有人告異以它議，事下張湯治異。
entries.en: Zhang Tang also had a grudge against Yi. When someone accused Yi over other remarks, the matter was sent down to Zhang Tang to handle.
entries.literal: Zhang Tang moreover with Yi had grudge, and someone accused Yi with other discussions, matter sent down Zhang Tang governed Yi.

entries.zh: 異與客語，客語初令下有不便者，異不應，微反脣。
entries.en: Yi spoke with a guest, and the guest spoke of the initial command that had been issued and had inconvenient aspects. Yi did not respond, but slightly turned his lips.
entries.literal: Yi with guest spoke, guest spoke initial command issued had inconvenient ones, Yi not responded, slightly turned lips.

entries.zh: 湯奏當異九卿見令不便，不入言而腹誹，論死。
entries.en: Tang memorialized that Yi, as one of the nine ministers, saw the command as inconvenient, did not enter and speak, but slandered in his abdomen, and sentenced him to death.
entries.literal: Tang memorialed should Yi nine ministers saw command inconvenient, not entered spoke but abdomen slandered, sentenced death.

entries.zh: 自是之後，有腹誹之法（以此）［比］，而公卿大夫多諂諛取容矣。
entries.en: After this, the law against inner slander was extended by analogy, and many high ministers and officials gained favor through flattery.
entries.literal: After this, the law against inner slander was applied by analogy, and many high ministers and officials won favor through flattery.

entries.zh: 天子既下緡錢令而尊卜式，百姓終莫分財佐縣官，於是（楊可）告緡錢縱矣。
entries.en: After the Son of Heaven issued the cash-registration order and honored Bu Shi, the common people still did not contribute their wealth to assist the government. Yang Ke was then allowed to proceed with reports on concealed cash holdings.
entries.literal: Son of Heaven having issued string money command and honored Bu Shi, hundred surnames finally none divided wealth assisted county officials, therefore (Yang Ke) accused string money let go.

entries.zh: 初，大農筦鹽鐵官布多，置水衡，欲以主鹽鐵；
entries.en: Initially, the Great Farmer managed the salt and iron officials, whose numbers had grown large. The Water Balance was established with the intention of taking charge of salt and iron;
entries.literal: Initially, great farmer managed salt iron officials spread many, established water balance, wanted to master salt iron;

entries.zh: 及楊可告緡錢，上林財物眾，乃令水衡主上林。
entries.en: When Yang Ke's reports on concealed cash holdings brought large quantities of wealth and goods into Shanglin, they ordered the Water Balance to take charge of Shanglin.
entries.literal: And Yang Ke accused string money, Shang Lin wealth goods many, then ordered water balance master Shang Lin.

entries.zh: 上林既充滿，益廣。
entries.en: Once Shanglin was full, they expanded it further.
entries.literal: Shang Lin already filled full, moreover broadened.

entries.zh: 是時越欲與漢用船戰逐，乃大修昆明池，列觀環之。
entries.en: At this time, Yue wanted to use boats with Han to battle and pursue, so they greatly repaired the Kunming Pool and arranged towers to surround it.
entries.literal: This time Yue wanted with Han used boats battled pursued, then greatly repaired Kunming Pool, arranged towers surrounded it.

entries.zh: 治樓船，高十餘丈，旗幟加其上，甚壯。
entries.en: They made tower boats, more than ten zhang high, with the flags and banners added on them, and they were very strong.
entries.literal: Made tower boats, high ten more zhang, flags banners added on it, very strong.

entries.zh: 於是天子感之，乃作柏梁臺，高數十丈。
entries.en: Therefore, the Son of Heaven sensed it, and then made the Boliang Terrace, several tens of zhang high.
entries.literal: Therefore, Son of Heaven sensed it, then made Bo Liang Terrace, high several ten zhang.

entries.zh: 宮室之修，由此日麗。
entries.en: The repair of palace rooms, from this time, became daily more beautiful.
entries.literal: Palace rooms repair, from this daily beautiful.

entries.zh: 是時山東被河菑，及歲不登數年，人或相食，方一二千里。
entries.en: At this time, Shandong suffered a Yellow River disaster, and for several years the harvests were not abundant. The people sometimes ate each other, in an area of one to two thousand li.
entries.literal: This time Shan Dong suffered Yellow River disaster, and years not abundant several years, people or mutually ate, area one two thousand li.

entries.zh: 天子憐之，詔曰：「江南火耕水耨，令饑民得流就食江淮閒，欲留，留處。」
entries.en: The Son of Heaven pitied them and issued an edict: “In Jiangnan they burn fields and weed by water. Let the hungry people move to seek food between the Jiang and Huai; those who wish to remain may remain where they are.”
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven pitied them and issued an edict: “In Jiangnan they burn off fields and weed by water; let the hungry people move to seek food between the Jiang and Huai; those who wish to stay may remain there.”

entries.zh: 遣使冠蓋相屬於道，護之，下巴蜀粟以振之。
entries.en: They sent messengers in a continuous stream along the roads to protect them, and sent grain down from Bashu to relieve them.
entries.literal: Sent messengers official hats continuously connected on road, protected them, sent down Ba Shu grain to relieve them.

entries.zh: 其明年，天子始巡郡國。
entries.en: The next year, the Son of Heaven began to tour the commanderies and kingdoms.
entries.literal: Its next year, Son of Heaven began toured commanderies kingdoms.

entries.zh: 東度河，河東守不意行至，不辨，自殺。
entries.en: Going east, they crossed the Yellow River, and the governor of Hedong did not expect the travel to arrive and was not prepared, so he committed suicide.
entries.literal: East crossed Yellow River, He Dong governor not expected travel arrived, not prepared, committed suicide.

entries.zh: 行西踰隴，隴西守以行往卒，天子從官不得食，隴西守自殺。
entries.en: Traveling west, the imperial party crossed Long. The governor of Longxi was caught unprepared by the tour's sudden arrival; the Son of Heaven's attendants had no food, and the governor committed suicide.
entries.literal: Traveling west, the imperial party crossed Long. The governor of Longxi was caught unprepared by the tour's sudden arrival; the Son of Heaven's attendants had no food, and the governor committed suicide.

entries.zh: 於是上北出蕭關，從數萬騎，獵新秦中，以勒邊兵而歸。
entries.en: Therefore, the emperor went north and exited Xiaoguan, followed by several tens of thousands of cavalry, hunted in the new Qin middle, and restrained the border troops and returned.
entries.literal: Therefore, emperor north exited Xiao Guan, followed several ten thousand cavalry, hunted new Qin middle, to restrain border troops and return.

entries.zh: 新秦中或千里無亭徼，於是誅北地太守以下，而令民得畜牧邊縣，官假馬母，三歲而歸，及息什一，以除告緡，用充仞新秦中。
entries.en: In the New Qin region, there were stretches of a thousand li without watch stations. Therefore, the Grand Administrator of Beidi and his subordinates were executed, and the people were ordered to raise livestock in the border counties. The officials lent out breeding mares; after three years the borrowers returned them with one-tenth of the increase. This replaced the concealed-cash reporting system and was used to fill and populate the New Qin region.
entries.literal: New Qin middle or thousand li no watch stations, therefore executed Bei Di grand administrator below, and ordered people could raise livestock border counties, officials lent mare mothers, three years and return, and increased one tenth, to remove accuse string money, used fill populate new Qin middle.

entries.zh: 自造白金五銖錢後五歲，赦吏民之坐盜鑄金錢死者數十萬人。
entries.en: Five years after creating white gold and five-zhu coins, he pardoned the officials and commoners, numbering in the tens of thousands, who had been sentenced to death for illicitly casting gold coins.
entries.literal: From made white gold five zhu money after five years, pardoned clerks people sat stole cast gold money died ones several ten thousand people.

entries.zh: 其不發覺相殺者，不可勝計。
entries.en: Those who killed one another without being discovered were beyond counting.
entries.literal: Their not discovered mutually killed ones, could not be completely counted.

entries.zh: 赦自出者百餘萬人。
entries.en: More than a million people came forward voluntarily and were pardoned.
entries.literal: Pardoned self came out ones hundred more ten thousand people.

entries.zh: 然不能半自出，天下大抵無慮皆鑄金錢矣。
entries.en: Yet not even half came forward voluntarily, and people throughout the empire generally went on casting gold coins without concern.
entries.literal: Yet could not half self came out, world generally without worry all cast gold money.

entries.zh: 犯者眾，吏不能盡誅取，於是遣博士褚大、徐偃等分曹循行郡國，舉兼并之徒守相為（吏）［利］者。
entries.en: There were so many violators that the officials could not punish and confiscate from them all. The court therefore sent the erudites Chu Da, Xu Yan, and others in separate groups to inspect the commanderies and kingdoms and expose those who enriched themselves as governors or ministers by joining with powerful annexers.
entries.literal: Violators many, clerks could not completely execute take, therefore sent erudites Chu Da, Xu Yan etc. divided sections followed toured commanderies kingdoms, raised annexed merged followers governors ministers for (clerks) [benefit] ones.

entries.zh: 而御史大夫張湯方隆貴用事，減宣、杜周等為中丞，義縱、尹齊、王溫舒等用慘急刻深為九卿，而直指夏蘭之屬始出矣。
entries.en: At this time, Imperial Censor Zhang Tang was rising in power and controlling affairs. Jian Xuan, Du Zhou, and others were appointed assistant censors; Yi Zong, Yin Qi, Wang Wenshu, and others used cruel, urgent, harsh, and searching methods as ministers among the Nine Ministers. Officials such as the Direct Commissioner Xia Lan began to appear.
entries.literal: At this time, Censor-in-Chief Zhang Tang was at the height of his influence. Jian Xuan, Du Zhou, and others became assistant censors; Yi Zong, Yin Qi, Wang Wenshu, and others rose to the Nine Ministers through cruel, harsh, and exacting methods; and special commissioners such as Xia Lan began to be sent out.

entries.zh: 是歲也，張湯死而民不思。
entries.en: That year, Zhang Tang died, and the people did not think of him.
entries.literal: This year also, Zhang Tang died and people not thought of.

entries.zh: 所忠言：「世家子弟富人或鬬雞走狗馬，弋獵博戲，亂齊民。」
entries.en: Suo Zhong said, “Sons of eminent houses and the wealthy sometimes fight cocks, race dogs and horses, hunt and shoot, gamble and play, thereby disordering the common people.”
entries.literal: Suo Zhong said: “Sons of eminent houses and the wealthy sometimes fight cocks, run dogs and horses, hunt and shoot, gamble and play—disordering the common people.”

entries.zh: 乃徵諸犯令，相引數千人，命曰「株送徒」。
entries.en: They then summoned those who had violated the edict. Mutual denunciations implicated several thousand people, who were called “convicts sent off in chains.”
entries.literal: Then they summoned those who violated the edict; mutual denunciations implicated several thousand people, whom they named “convicts sent off in chains.”

entries.zh: 入財者得補郎，郎選衰矣。
entries.en: Those who entered wealth got to supplement lang, and lang selections declined.
entries.literal: Entered wealth ones got supplemented lang, lang selections declined.

entries.zh: 既得寶鼎，立后土、太一祠，公卿議封禪事，而天下郡國皆豫治道橋，繕故宮，及當馳道縣，縣治官儲，設供具，而望以待幸。
entries.en: After obtaining the precious ding, they established sacrifices to Houtu and Taiyi. The dukes and ministers discussed the feng and shan sacrifices, and the commanderies and kingdoms throughout the realm all prepared by repairing roads and bridges and restoring former palaces. Counties along the imperial roads managed official stores, prepared supplies, and waited expectantly for an imperial visit.
entries.literal: Having got precious ding, established Hou Tu, Tai Yi sacrifices, dukes ministers discussed feng shan affairs, and world commanderies kingdoms all prepared repaired roads bridges, mended former palaces, and should gallop road counties, counties administered official stores, set up supplies, and gazed to await favor.

entries.zh: 其明年，南越反，西羌侵邊為桀。
entries.en: The next year, Nanyue rebelled, and the Xiqiang invaded the border and became rebellious.
entries.literal: Its next year, Nan Yue rebelled, Xi Qiang invaded border became rebellious.

entries.zh: 於是天子為山東不贍，赦天下［囚］，因南方樓船卒二十餘萬人擊南越，數萬人發三河以西騎擊西羌，又數萬人度河筑令居。
entries.en: Therefore, because resources east of the mountains were insufficient, the Son of Heaven pardoned prisoners throughout the realm. More than two hundred thousand tower-ship troops from the south were used to attack Nanyue. Several tens of thousands of cavalry were sent west of Sanhe to attack the Xiqiang, and several tens of thousands more crossed the Yellow River and built Lingju.
entries.literal: Therefore, Son of Heaven for Shan Dong not sufficient, pardoned world [prisoners], using south tower boat troops twenty more ten thousand attacked Nan Yue, several ten thousand sent San He west cavalry attacked Xi Qiang, moreover several ten thousand crossed Yellow River built Ling Ju.

entries.zh: 初置張掖、酒泉郡，而上郡、朔方、西河、河西開田官，斥塞卒六十萬人戍田之。
entries.en: They first established the commanderies of Zhangye and Jiuquan, and in Shangjun, Shuofang, Xihe, and Hexi they opened agricultural offices. They expanded the frontier garrisons, and six hundred thousand soldiers guarded and farmed the land.
entries.literal: Initially established Zhang Ye, Jiu Quan commanderies, and Shang Jun, Shuo Fang, Xi He, He Xi opened field officials, expanded border troops sixty ten thousand garrisoned farmed them.

entries.zh: 中國繕道餽糧，遠者三千，近者千餘里，皆仰給大農。
entries.en: The central states repaired roads and transported grain. The farthest routes were three thousand li and the nearest more than a thousand li, and all supplies came from the Grand Minister of Agriculture.
entries.literal: Central states repaired roads sent grain, far ones three thousand, near ones thousand more li, all looked up supplied great farmer.

entries.zh: 邊兵不足，乃發武庫工官兵器以贍之。
entries.en: The frontier troops lacked equipment, so weapons from the imperial armory and workshops were issued to supply them.
entries.literal: Border troops insufficient, then issued martial storehouse craftsmen official weapons to support them.

entries.zh: 車騎馬乏絕，縣官錢少，買馬難得，乃著令，令封君以下至三百石以上吏，以差出牝馬天下亭，亭有畜牸馬，歲課息。
entries.en: Horses for chariots and cavalry were exhausted, government funds were low, and horses were hard to buy. A decree was therefore issued ordering everyone from enfeoffed lords down to officials of three hundred shi and above to contribute mares according to rank to the post stations throughout the empire. The stations raised the mares and assessed their yearly increase.
entries.literal: Chariot cavalry horses lacked exhausted, county officials money few, buy horses difficult got, then established command, ordered sealed lords below to three hundred shi above clerks, by differences sent out female horses world pavilions, pavilions had raised female horses, yearly assessed interest.

entries.zh: 齊相卜式上書曰：「臣聞主憂臣辱。
entries.en: The chancellor of Qi, Bu Shi, submitted a memorial saying: 'I, your minister, have heard that when the lord worries, the minister is shamed.
entries.literal: Qi chancellor Bu Shi memorialed said: 'Minister heard lord worries minister shames.

entries.zh: 南越反，臣願父子與齊習船者往死之。」
entries.en: Nanyue has rebelled, and I, your minister, ask that my son and I, together with those in Qi skilled with boats, go and die in the campaign.'
entries.literal: Nan Yue rebelled, minister wishes father son with Qi practiced boat ones go die for it.'

entries.zh: 天子下詔曰：「卜式雖躬耕牧，不以為利，有餘輒助縣官之用。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven issued an edict saying: 'Bu Shi personally farms and herds, yet does not pursue profit; whenever he has a surplus, he assists government expenses.
entries.literal: Son of Heaven issued edict said: 'Bu Shi although personally farmed pastured, not took as profit, had surplus then assisted county officials use.

entries.zh: 今天下不幸有急，而式奮願父子死之，雖未戰，可謂義形於內。
