entries.en: Now the world has unfortunately met an emergency, and Shi has roused himself and asked that he and his son die in the campaign. Although they have not yet fought, this may be called righteousness taking form within.
entries.literal: Now world unfortunately has urgency, and Shi aroused wished father son die for it, although not yet battled, can be called righteousness shaped within.

entries.zh: 賜爵關內侯，金六十斤，田十頃。」
entries.en: I grant him the nobility of Guannei Hou, sixty jin of gold, and ten qing of fields.'
entries.literal: Granted nobility Guan Nei Hou, gold sixty jin, fields ten qing.'

entries.zh: 布告天下，天下莫應。
entries.en: The proclamation went out to the realm, but no one responded.
entries.literal: It was proclaimed to the realm, but none in the realm responded.

entries.zh: 列侯以百數，皆莫求從軍擊羌、越。
entries.en: The ranked marquises numbered in the hundreds, yet none asked to accompany the army in attacking the Qiang and Yue.
entries.literal: Arranged marquises by hundred counted, all none sought follow army attack Qiang, Yue.

entries.zh: 至酎，少府省金，而列侯坐酎金失侯者百餘人。
entries.en: At the libation ceremony, the Shaofu inspected the gold, and more than a hundred ranked marquises were convicted over their libation gold and stripped of their marquisates.
entries.literal: At the libation ceremony, the Shaofu inspected the gold, and more than a hundred ranked marquises were convicted over their libation gold and lost their marquisates.

entries.zh: 乃拜式為御史大夫。
entries.en: Then they appointed Shi as Imperial Censor.
entries.literal: Then appointed Shi as Imperial Censor.

entries.zh: 其明年，元封元年，卜式貶秩為太子太傅。
entries.en: The next year, in the first year of Yuanfeng, Bu Shi was demoted in rank and became grand tutor to the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: Its next year, Yuan Feng first year, Bu Shi demoted rank became Crown Prince grand tutor.

entries.zh: 而桑弘羊為治粟都尉，領大農，盡代僅筦天下鹽鐵。
entries.en: Sang Hongyang became Colonel for the Management of Grain, took charge of the Great Farmer's office, and took over from Kong Jin in managing the empire's salt and iron.
entries.literal: And Sang Hong Yang became Governing Grain colonel, led great farmer, completely replaced Jin managed world salt iron.

entries.zh: 弘羊以諸官各自市，相與爭，物故騰躍，而天下賦輸或不償其僦費，乃請置大農部丞數十人，分部主郡國，各往往縣置均輸鹽鐵官，令遠方各以其物貴時商賈所轉販者為賦，而相灌輸。
entries.en: Hongyang observed that because officials each bought goods on their own and competed with one another, prices rose sharply, and the empire's taxes and transport levies sometimes did not cover their hired expenses. He therefore requested the establishment of several dozen divisional assistants under the Great Farmer, assigned by region to oversee the commanderies and kingdoms. Equal transport, salt, and iron offices were commonly established in the counties. Distant regions were ordered, when their local goods were expensive, to use what merchants transported and sold as tax payments, so that the regions could supply one another.
entries.literal: Hongyang observed that because the various offices each made their own purchases, they competed with one another and drove prices sharply upward, while taxes shipped from across the empire sometimes did not cover their freight costs. He therefore requested the appointment of several dozen regional assistants to the Grand Farmer, each responsible for a group of commanderies and kingdoms. Equal-transport and salt-and-iron offices were established in selected counties, and distant regions were ordered to pay their taxes in local goods of the kinds merchants normally transported for sale when prices were high, so that goods could be transferred and supplied among the regions.

entries.zh: 置平準于京師，都受天下委輸。
entries.en: They established the Equalization Office at the capital, where transported goods from throughout the empire were received.
entries.literal: Established level standard at capital, capital received world entrusted transports.

entries.zh: 召工官治車諸器，皆仰給大農。
entries.en: They summoned artisan officials to repair carriages and equipment, all supplied by the Grand Minister of Agriculture.
entries.literal: Summoned craftsmen officials repaired carriages various tools, all looked up supplied great farmer.

entries.zh: 大農之諸官盡籠天下之貨物，貴即賣之，賤則買之。
entries.en: The Great Farmer's officials brought the empire's goods under their control, selling when prices were high and buying when prices were low.
entries.literal: Great farmer various officials completely contained world goods, expensive then sold them, cheap then bought them.

entries.zh: 如此，富商大賈無所牟大利，則反本，而萬物不得騰踴。
entries.en: In this way, rich merchants and great traders had no way to pursue enormous profits, so they returned to basic occupations, and prices no longer surged wildly.
entries.literal: Like this, rich merchants great traders nowhere sought great profits, then returned to fundamentals, and myriad things not got to leap jump.

entries.zh: 故抑天下物，名曰「平準」。
entries.en: Therefore, they stabilized prices throughout the realm, and the policy was named “Equalization.”
entries.literal: Therefore, they stabilized goods throughout the realm, and the policy was named “Equalization.”

entries.zh: 天子以為然，許之。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven considered it so and permitted it.
entries.literal: Son of Heaven considered it so, permitted it.

entries.zh: 於是天子北至朔方，東到太山，巡海上，并北邊以歸。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven then went north to Shuofang and east to Taishan, toured the coast, and returned along the northern frontier.
entries.literal: Therefore, Son of Heaven north to Shuo Fang, east to Tai Shan, toured sea above, along north border to return.

entries.zh: 所過賞賜，用帛百餘萬匹，錢金以巨萬計，皆取足大農。
entries.en: Wherever he passed, he distributed rewards and gifts, spending more than a million bolts of silk and money and gold counted in the tens of thousands. All of it was drawn from the Great Farmer.
entries.literal: Passed places rewarded bestowed, used silk hundred more ten thousand bolts, money gold counted in huge ten thousands, all took sufficient great farmer.

entries.zh: 式既在位，見郡國多不便縣官作鹽鐵，鐵器苦惡，賈貴，或彊令民賣買之。
entries.en: Once Shi was in office, he saw that many commanderies and kingdoms found government salt and iron production inconvenient. The iron tools were poor, prices were high, and in some places the people were forced to buy and sell them.
entries.literal: Shi already in position, saw commanderies kingdoms many inconvenient county officials made salt iron, iron tools bitter bad, merchants expensive, or strongly ordered people bought sold them.

entries.zh: 而船有算，商者少，物貴，乃因孔僅言船算事。
entries.en: Because boats were taxed, merchants were few and goods were expensive. Through Kong Jin, he reported on the boat tax.
entries.literal: And boats had tax, merchants few, goods expensive, then through Kong Jin spoke boat tax affairs.

entries.zh: 上由是不悅卜式。
entries.en: The emperor therefore was not pleased with Bu Shi.
entries.literal: Emperor therefore not pleased Bu Shi.

entries.zh: 是歲小旱，上令官求雨，卜式言曰：「縣官當食租衣稅而已，今弘羊令吏坐市列肆，販物求利。
entries.en: That year there was a slight drought, and the emperor ordered officials to pray for rain. Bu Shi said, “Officials should live on rents and dress themselves from taxes alone; now Sang Hongyang has made them sit in the market and sell goods.
entries.literal: That year there was a slight drought; the emperor ordered officials to pray for rain. Bu Shi said: “The officials should live on rents and dress on taxes alone; now Sang Hongyang has clerks sit in market rows and shops, peddling goods for profit.

entries.zh: 亨弘羊，天乃雨。」
entries.en: Execute Sang Hongyang, and Heaven will send rain.”
entries.literal: Execute Sang Hongyang, and heaven will then rain.”

entries.zh: 漢連兵三歲，誅羌，滅南越，番禺以西至蜀南者置初郡十七，且以其故俗治，毋賦稅。
entries.en: Han kept troops in the field for three years, punished the Qiang, and extinguished Nanyue. From Panyu westward to the south of Shu, it established seventeen new commanderies, governed them according to local customs, and imposed no taxes.
entries.literal: Han connected troops three years, executed Qiang, extinguished Nan Yue, Pan Yu west to Shu south ones established initial commanderies seventeen, moreover with their former customs governed, no taxes.

entries.zh: 南陽、漢中以往郡，各以地比給初郡吏卒奉食幣物，傳車馬被具。
entries.en: The commanderies beyond Nanyang and Hanzhong, each according to its land resources, supplied the clerks and troops of the new commanderies with provisions, food, money, goods, relay carriages, horses, and transport equipment.
entries.literal: Nan Yang, Han Zhong past commanderies, each with land proportion supplied initial commanderies clerks troops provisions food currency goods, relay carriages horses covered equipment.

entries.zh: 而初郡時時小反，殺吏，漢發南方吏卒往誅之，閒歲萬餘人，費皆仰給大農。
entries.en: The new commanderies sometimes had minor rebellions in which officials were killed. Han sent southern officials and troops to punish them, with more than ten thousand people mobilized every other year. All the expenses were supplied by the Grand Minister of Agriculture.
entries.literal: And initial commanderies sometimes small rebelled, killed clerks, Han sent southern clerks troops went executed them, between years ten thousand more people, expenses all looked up supplied great farmer.

entries.zh: 大農以均輸調鹽鐵助賦，故能贍之。
entries.en: Through equal transport and control of salt and iron, the Great Farmer supplemented tax revenues and could therefore support these expenses.
entries.literal: Great farmer with equal transport regulated salt iron assisted taxes, therefore could support them.

entries.zh: 然兵所過縣，為以訾給毋乏而已，不敢言擅賦法矣。
entries.en: Yet the counties through which the troops passed merely drew on their own resources to prevent shortages, and no one dared call this unauthorized taxation.
entries.literal: Yet the counties through which the troops passed drew on their own resources to prevent shortages, and no one dared call this unauthorized taxation.

entries.zh: 太史公曰：農工商交易之路通，而龜貝金錢刀布之幣興焉。
entries.en: The Grand Historian said: When the roads of exchange for farming, commerce, and artisans were connected, the currencies of turtle shells, cowries, gold, money, knives, and cloth arose.
entries.literal: Grand Historian said: farming commerce artisans exchange roads connected, and turtle shells cowries gold money knives cloth currencies arose there.

entries.zh: 所從來久遠，自高辛氏之前尚矣，靡得而記云。
entries.en: Its origins lay in the remote past, even before the age of Gaoxin, and cannot be recorded.
entries.literal: Its origins lay in remote antiquity, even before the age of Gaoxin, and could not be recorded.

entries.zh: 故書道唐虞之際，詩述殷周之世，安寧則長庠序，先本絀末，以禮義防于利；
entries.en: Therefore, the writings spoke of the time of Tang and Yu, and the poems described the age of Yin and Zhou. When peaceful, they grew schools, put fundamentals first and reduced ends, and with rites and righteousness guarded against profits;
entries.literal: Therefore, writings spoke Tang Yu time, poems described Yin Zhou age, peaceful then grew schools, first fundamentals reduced ends, with rites righteousness guarded against profits;

entries.zh: 事變多故而亦反是。
entries.en: When affairs changed and had many troubles, they also reversed this.
entries.literal: Affairs changed many troubles and also reversed this.

entries.zh: 是以物盛則衰，時極而轉，一質一文，終始之變也。
entries.en: Therefore, when things flourish, they then decline. When time reaches an extreme, it then turns. One solid, one pattern—this is the change of beginning and end.
entries.literal: Therefore, things flourish then decline, time extreme then turn, one solid one pattern, beginning end change also.

entries.zh: 禹貢九州，各因其土地所宜，人民所多少而納職焉。
entries.en: In Yu's tribute system, the nine provinces paid their levies according to what their lands produced and the size of their populations.
entries.literal: Yu tribute nine provinces, each according to their land suitable, people more less and paid duties there.

entries.zh: 湯武承獘易變，使民不倦，各兢兢所以為治，而稍陵遲衰微。
entries.en: Tang and Wu inherited worn-out systems and changed them with ease, so that the people were not exhausted. Each governed with anxious care, yet over time their houses gradually declined and weakened.
entries.literal: Tang Wu inherited exhaustion easily changed, made people not weary, each earnestly so governed, but gradually declined weakened.

entries.zh: 齊桓公用管仲之謀，通輕重之權，徼山海之業，以朝諸侯，用區區之齊顯成霸名。
entries.en: Duke Huan of Qi used Guan Zhong's strategy, mastered the balance of light and heavy, controlled the industries of mountains and seas, and brought the feudal lords to court. With the small state of Qi, he made his name as hegemon shine.
entries.literal: Qi Huan duke used Guan Zhong strategy, connected light heavy power, cornered mountain sea industries, to make audience feudal lords, used small small Qi displayed became hegemon name.

entries.zh: 魏用李克，盡地力，為彊君。
entries.en: Wei employed Li Ke, fully developed the productive capacity of its land, and became powerful.
entries.literal: Wei employed Li Ke, fully developed the productive capacity of its land, and became powerful.

entries.zh: 自是以後，天下爭於戰國，貴詐力而賤仁義，先富有而後推讓。
entries.en: From this time on, the world contended through the Warring States, valuing deceit and force while slighting benevolence and righteousness; wealth came first, and deference came afterward.
entries.literal: From this after, world contended in Warring States, valued deceit force but cheapened benevolence righteousness, first rich had then afterward yielded.

entries.zh: 故庶人之富者或累巨萬，而貧者或不厭糟糠；
entries.en: Therefore, some wealthy commoners accumulated fortunes of many tens of thousands, while some poor people could not even fill themselves with bran and husks;
entries.literal: Therefore, commoners rich ones or accumulated huge ten thousand, but poor ones or not satisfied with bran husks;

entries.zh: 有國彊者或并群小以臣諸侯，而弱國或絕祀而滅世。
entries.en: Some powerful states annexed clusters of smaller ones and reduced other lords to submission, while weak states saw their sacrifices cut off and their lines extinguished.
entries.literal: Had states strong ones or annexed groups small to serve feudal lords, but weak states or cut sacrifices extinguished generations.

entries.zh: 以至於秦，卒并海內。
entries.en: This continued down to Qin, which finally united all within the seas.
entries.literal: To arrived at Qin, finally united within seas.

entries.zh: 虞夏之幣，金為三品，或黃，或白，或赤；
entries.en: In the currencies of Yu and Xia, gold was of three kinds: either yellow, or white, or red;
entries.literal: Yu Xia currencies, gold as three kinds, or yellow, or white, or red;

entries.zh: 或錢，或布，或刀，或龜貝。
entries.en: or coins, or cloth, or knives, or turtle shells and cowries.
entries.literal: Or coins, or cloth, or knives, or turtle shells cowries.

entries.zh: 及至秦，中一國之幣為（三）［二］等，黃金以溢名，為上幣；
entries.en: By the time of Qin, the currency of the unified state was divided into two grades: yellow gold, measured by the yi, served as the higher currency;
entries.literal: And to Qin, unifying one state currencies as (three) [two] grades, yellow gold with yi named, as upper currency;

entries.zh: 銅錢識曰半兩，重如其文，為下幣。
entries.en: copper coins bore the inscription 'half liang', weighed what the inscription stated, and served as the lower currency.
entries.literal: Copper coins inscription said half liang, heavy like its writing, as lower currency.

entries.zh: 而珠玉、龜貝、銀錫之屬為器飾寶藏，不為幣。
entries.en: Pearls, jade, turtle shells, cowries, silver, tin, and the like were used for vessels, ornaments, and stored treasure, but not as currency.
entries.literal: And pearls jade, turtle shells cowries, silver tin kind as vessel decorations treasure stores, not as currency.

entries.zh: 然各隨時而輕重無常。
entries.en: Yet each changed with the times, and their relative value was never fixed.
entries.literal: Yet each followed time and light heavy no constant.

entries.zh: 於是外攘夷狄，內興功業，海內之士力耕不足糧馕，女子紡績不足衣服。
entries.en: Abroad they drove back the Yi and Di, while at home they undertook great works. Men throughout the realm farmed with all their strength yet had too little grain to eat, and women spun and wove yet had too little clothing to wear.
entries.literal: Thus, abroad they repelled the Yi and Di, and at home they launched great undertakings; yet the men of the realm could not produce enough provisions however hard they farmed, nor could its women weave enough cloth for clothing.

entries.zh: 古者嘗竭天下之資財以奉其上，猶自以為不足也。
entries.en: People of old could exhaust the resources and wealth of the world to support those above them and still think it insufficient.
entries.literal: Ancient ones often exhausted world resources wealth to support their superiors, still self considered insufficient also.

entries.zh: 無異故云，事勢之流，相激使然，曷足怪焉。
entries.en: There is no special reason for this. The momentum of affairs, each force driving the next, made it so. Why should it be surprising?
entries.literal: No different therefore speak, affairs situations flow, mutually stimulated made so, why sufficient strange there.

entries.zh: 漢興，接秦之獘，丈夫從軍旅，老弱轉糧馕，作業劇而財匱，自天子不能具鈞駟，而將相或乘牛車，齊民無藏蓋。
entries.en: When Han rose, it inherited Qin’s exhaustion. Men followed military campaigns, and the old and infirm transported grain and food. Labor was heavy and wealth scarce; even the Son of Heaven could not equip matched horses, while generals and ministers sometimes rode ox carts and commoners had nothing in reserve.
entries.literal: Han rose, connected Qin exhaustion, men followed military campaigns, old weak transported grain food, work intense and wealth scarce, from Son of Heaven could not equip matched horses, and generals ministers or rode ox carts, common people no stored covers.

entries.zh: 於是為秦錢重難用，更令民鑄錢，一黃金一斤，約法省禁。
entries.en: Therefore, because Qin coinage was heavy and hard to use, they further ordered the people to cast money, fixing the value at one catty of gold per jin, and regulated the laws while reducing prohibitions.
entries.literal: Therefore, because Qin coinage was heavy and hard to use, they further ordered the people to cast money, with one catty of gold to one jin, and regulated the laws while reducing prohibitions.

entries.zh: 而不軌逐利之民，蓄積餘業以稽市物，物踴騰糶，米至石萬錢，馬一匹則百金。
entries.en: People who broke the rules to pursue profit hoarded surplus goods to control the market, driving prices up. Rice reached ten thousand cash per shi, and a single horse cost a hundred gold.
entries.literal: And lawless profit-seeking people accumulated surplus stock to control market goods; goods leaped in price, rice reached ten thousand cash per shi, and one horse then cost a hundred gold.

entries.zh: 周章卒，子熊遂立，熊遂卒，子柯相立。
entries.en: When Zhouzhang died, his son Xiongsui was established. When Xiongsui died, his son Kexiang was established.
entries.literal: Zhou Zhang died, son Xiong Sui established, Xiong Sui died, son Ke Xiang established.

entries.zh: 柯相卒，子彊鳩夷立。
entries.en: When Kexiang died, his son Qiang Jiuyi was established.
entries.literal: Ke Xiang died, son Qiang Jiu Yi established.

entries.zh: 彊鳩夷卒，子餘橋疑吾立。
entries.en: When Qiang Jiuyi died, his son Yuqiaoyiwu was established.
entries.literal: Qiang Jiu Yi died, son Yu Qiao Yiwu established.

entries.zh: 餘橋疑吾卒，子柯盧立。
entries.en: When Yuqiaoyiwu died, his son Kelu was established.
entries.literal: Yu Qiao Yiwu died, son Ke Lu established.

entries.zh: 柯盧卒，子周繇立。
entries.en: When Kelu died, his son Zhouyu was established.
entries.literal: Ke Lu died, son Zhou You established.

entries.zh: 周繇卒，子屈羽立。
entries.en: When Zhouyu died, his son Quyu was established.
entries.literal: Zhou You died, son Qu Yu established.

entries.zh: 屈羽卒，子夷吾立。
entries.en: When Quyu died, his son Yiwu was established.
entries.literal: Qu Yu died, son Yiwu established.

entries.zh: 夷吾卒，子禽處立。
entries.en: When Yiwu died, his son Qinchu was established.
entries.literal: Yiwu died, son Qin Chu established.

entries.zh: 禽處卒，子轉立。
entries.en: When Qinchu died, his son Zhuan was established.
entries.literal: Qin Chu died, son Zhuan established.

entries.zh: 轉卒，子頗高立。
entries.en: Zhuan died, and his son Pogao was established.
entries.literal: Zhuan died, son Po Gao established.

entries.zh: 頗高卒，子句卑立。
entries.en: Pogao died, and his son Goubei was established.
entries.literal: Po Gao died, son Gou Bei established.

entries.zh: 是時晉獻公滅周北虞公，以開晉伐虢也。
entries.en: At this time, Duke Xian of Jin extinguished the Duke of Yu north of Zhou, in order to open the way for Jin to attack Guo.
entries.literal: This time Jin Xian Gong extinguished Zhou north Yu Gong, to open Jin attack Guo also.

entries.zh: 句卑卒，子去齊立。
entries.en: Goubei died, and his son Quqi was established.
entries.literal: Gou Bei died, son Qu Qi established.

entries.zh: 去齊卒，子壽夢立。
entries.en: Quqi died, and his son Shoumeng was established.
entries.literal: Qu Qi died, son Shou Meng established.

entries.zh: 壽夢立而吳始益大，稱王。
entries.en: When Shoumeng was established, Wu began to grow even greater and called itself king.
entries.literal: Shou Meng established and Wu began moreover great, called king.

entries.zh: 太伯卒，無子，弟仲雍立，是為吳仲雍。
entries.en: Taibo died without a son, and his younger brother Zhongyong was established as Wu Zhongyong.
entries.literal: Tai Bo died, no son, younger brother Zhong Yong established, this was Wu Zhong Yong.

entries.zh: 仲雍卒，子季簡立。
entries.en: When Zhongyong died, his son Jijian was established.
entries.literal: Zhong Yong died, son Ji Jian established.

entries.zh: 季簡卒，子叔達立。
entries.en: When Jijian died, his son Shuda was established.
entries.literal: Ji Jian died, son Shu Da established.

entries.zh: 叔達卒，子周章立。
entries.en: When Shuda died, his son Zhouzhang was established.
entries.literal: Shu Da died, son Zhou Zhang established.

entries.zh: 是時周武王克殷，求太伯、仲雍之後，得周章。
entries.en: At this time, King Wu of Zhou conquered Yin and sought the descendants of Taibo and Zhongyong, and found Zhouzhang.
entries.literal: This time Zhou Wu Wang conquered Yin, sought Tai Bo, Zhong Yong descendants, got Zhou Zhang.

entries.zh: 周章已君吳，因而封之。
entries.en: Zhouzhang was already ruling Wu, so Zhou enfeoffed him there.
entries.literal: Zhou Zhang already ruled Wu, therefore sealed him.

entries.zh: 乃封周章弟虞仲於周之北故夏虛，是為虞仲，列為諸侯。
entries.en: Then they enfeoffed Zhouzhang’s younger brother Yuzhong in the former Xia capital north of Zhou, and he became Yuzhong, one of the feudal lords.
entries.literal: Then sealed Zhou Zhang younger brother Yu Zhong at Zhou north former Xia capital, this was Yu Zhong, listed as feudal lord.

entries.zh: 吳太伯，太伯弟仲雍，皆周太王之子，而王季歷之兄也。
entries.en: Taibo and his younger brother Zhongyong were both sons of King Tai of Zhou and elder brothers of King Jili.
entries.literal: Wu Tai Bo, Tai Bo younger brother Zhong Yong, all Zhou Tai Wang sons, and Wang Ji Li brothers also.

entries.zh: 季歷賢，而有聖子昌，太王欲立季歷以及昌，於是太伯、仲雍二人乃奔荊蠻，文身斷髮，示不可用，以避季歷。
entries.en: Jili was worthy and had the sage son Chang, so King Tai wanted to establish Jili and then Chang. Taibo and Zhongyong therefore fled to the Jing Man, tattooed their bodies, and cut their hair to show they could not be used, thereby yielding the succession to Jili.
entries.literal: Jili was worthy and had the sage son Chang, so King Tai wanted to establish Jili and then Chang; therefore Taibo and Zhongyong fled to the Jing Man, tattooed their bodies, and cut their hair, showing that they could not be used, in order to avoid Jili.

entries.zh: 季歷果立，是為王季，而昌為文王。
entries.en: Jili was indeed established, and he became King Ji, while Chang became King Wen.
entries.literal: Ji Li indeed established, this was Wang Ji, and Chang became Wen Wang.

entries.zh: 太伯之奔荊蠻，自號句吳。
entries.en: When Taibo fled to the Jing Man, he called himself Gouwu.
entries.literal: Tai Bo fled Jing Man, self named Gou Wu.

entries.zh: 荊蠻義之，從而歸之千餘家，立為吳太伯。
entries.en: The Jing Man considered him righteous, and more than a thousand families followed and submitted to him, so he was established as Wu Taibo.
entries.literal: Jing Man considered righteous, followed and submitted thousand more families, established as Wu Tai Bo.

entries.zh: 召公奭與周同姓，姓姬氏。
entries.en: The Duke of Shao, Shi, shared the Zhou surname, the Ji clan.
entries.literal: Duke of Shao Shi shared the same surname with Zhou, surname Ji clan.

entries.zh: 周武王之滅紂，封召公於北燕。
entries.en: When King Wu of Zhou destroyed King Zhou, he enfeoffed the Duke of Shao in Northern Yan.
entries.literal: When King Wu of Zhou destroyed Zhou, he enfeoffed the Duke of Shao at Northern Yan.

entries.zh: 其在成王時，召王為三公：自陜以西，召公主之；
entries.en: During King Cheng's reign, the Duke of Shao served as one of the Three Ducal Ministers: west of Shan, the Duke of Shao administered it;
entries.literal: During King Cheng's time, the Duke of Shao was one of the three dukes: from Shan westwards, the Duke of Shao governed it;

entries.zh: 自陜以東，周公主之。
entries.en: The Duke of Zhou governed the territory east of Shan.
entries.literal: From Shan eastwards, the Duke of Zhou governed it.

entries.zh: 成王既幼，周公攝政，當國踐祚，召公疑之，作君奭。
entries.en: King Cheng was still young, so the Duke of Zhou acted as regent and took charge of the state. The Duke of Shao suspected him and wrote the Jun Shi.
entries.literal: King Cheng was still young; the Duke of Zhou acted as regent, held charge of the state, and exercised the royal position. The Duke of Shao suspected him and composed the Jun Shi.

entries.zh: 君奭不說周公。
entries.en: The Jun Shi expressed displeasure with the Duke of Zhou.
entries.literal: Jun Shi was not pleased with the Duke of Zhou.

entries.zh: 周公乃稱「湯時有伊尹，假于皇天；
entries.en: The Duke of Zhou then said, "In the time of Tang there was Yi Yin, who relied upon August Heaven;
entries.literal: The Duke of Zhou then said: "In Tang's time there was Yi Yin, who relied on the August Heaven;

entries.zh: 在太戊時，則有若伊陟、臣扈，假于上帝，巫咸治王家；
entries.en: In Tai Wu’s time there were Yi Zhi and Chen Hu, who relied on the Supreme Deity. Wu Xian governed the royal house;
entries.literal: In Tai Wu's time, there were Yi Zhi and Chen Hu, who relied on the Supreme Deity. Wu Xian governed the royal house;

entries.zh: 在祖乙時，則有若巫賢；
entries.en: In Zu Yi’s time there was another Wu Xian, the preceding minister's son;
entries.literal: In Zu Yi's time, there was another Wu Xian, son of the preceding Wu Xian;

entries.zh: 在武丁時，則有若甘般：率維茲有陳，保乂有殷」。
entries.en: In Wu Ding's time, there was Gan Ban, who led and maintained these arrangements, protecting and governing the state of Yin."
entries.literal: In Wu Ding's time, there was Gan Ban: leading and maintaining these arrangements, protecting and governing Yin."

entries.zh: 於是召公乃說。
entries.en: The Duke of Shao was then pleased.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Duke of Shao was pleased.

entries.zh: 燕見秦且滅六國，秦兵臨易水，禍且至燕。
entries.en: Yan saw that Qin was about to destroy the six states. Qin’s army had reached the Yi River, and disaster was about to reach Yan.
entries.literal: Yan saw that Qin was about to destroy the six states. Qin's army reached the Yi River, and disaster was about to come to Yan.

entries.zh: 太子丹陰養壯士二十人，使荊軻獻督亢地圖於秦，因襲刺秦王。
entries.en: The heir apparent Dan secretly raised twenty brave men and sent Jing Ke to present the map of Dukang to Qin, then took advantage of this to assassinate the King of Qin.
entries.literal: The heir apparent Dan secretly raised twenty brave men and sent Jing Ke to present the Dukang map to Qin, then took advantage of this to assassinate the King of Qin.

entries.zh: 秦王覺，殺軻，使將軍王翦擊燕。
entries.en: The King of Qin discovered the plot, killed Ke, and sent General Wang Jian to attack Yan.
entries.literal: The King of Qin detected it, killed Ke, and sent General Wang Jian to attack Yan.

entries.zh: 二十九年，秦攻拔我薊，燕王亡，徙居遼東，斬丹以獻秦。
entries.en: In the twenty-ninth year, Qin attacked and captured our Ji. The Yan king fled and moved to Liaodong, then beheaded Dan and presented his head to Qin.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, Qin attacked and captured our Ji. The Yan king fled, moved to Liaodong, and beheaded Dan to present to Qin.

entries.zh: 三十年，秦滅魏。
entries.en: In the thirtieth year, Qin destroyed Wei.
entries.literal: In the thirtieth year, Qin destroyed Wei.

entries.zh: 管叔鮮、蔡叔度者，周文王子而武王弟也。
entries.en: Guan Shu Xian and Cai Shu Du were both sons of King Wen of Zhou and younger brothers of King Wu.
entries.literal: Guan Shu Xian and Cai Shu Du were sons of King Wen of Zhou and younger brothers of King Wu.

entries.zh: 武王同母兄弟十人。
entries.en: King Wu and nine other brothers shared the same mother.
entries.literal: King Wu was one of ten brothers born to the same mother.

entries.zh: 母曰太姒，文王正妃也。
entries.en: Their mother was Tai Si, King Wen’s principal consort.
entries.literal: Their mother was called Tai Si, King Wen's principal consort.

entries.zh: 其長子曰伯邑考，次曰武王發，次曰管叔鮮，次曰周公旦，次曰蔡叔度，次曰曹叔振鐸，次曰成叔武，次曰霍叔處，次曰康叔封，次曰冉季載。
entries.en: Her eldest son was called Bo Yi Kao; next came King Wu Fa, then Guan Shu Xian, the Duke of Zhou Dan, Cai Shu Du, Cao Shu Zhen Duo, Cheng Shu Wu, Huo Shu Chu, Kang Shu Feng, and Ran Ji Zai.
entries.literal: Their eldest son was called Bo Yi Kao, next was King Wu Fa, next was Guan Shu Xian, next was the Duke of Zhou Dan, next was Cai Shu Du, next was Cao Shu Zhen Duo, next was Cheng Shu Wu, next was Huo Shu Chu, next was Kang Shu Feng, next was Ran Ji Zai.

entries.zh: 冉季載最少。
entries.en: Ran Ji Zai was the youngest.
entries.literal: Ran Ji Zai was the youngest.

entries.zh: 同母昆弟十人，唯發、旦賢，左右輔文王，故文王舍伯邑考而以發為太子。
entries.en: Of the ten brothers from the same mother, only Fa and Dan were worthy. They assisted King Wen on left and right, so King Wen passed over Bo Yi Kao and made Fa his crown prince.
entries.literal: The ten brothers from the same mother, only Fa and Dan were worthy. They assisted King Wen on left and right, so King Wen abandoned Bo Yi Kao and made Fa his crown prince.

entries.zh: 及文王崩而發立，是為武王。
entries.en: When King Wen passed away, Fa ascended the throne and became King Wu.
entries.literal: When King Wen passed away, Fa ascended and became King Wu.

entries.zh: 伯邑考既已前卒矣。
entries.en: Bo Yi Kao had already died previously.
entries.literal: Bo Yi Kao had already died previously.

entries.zh: 武王已克殷紂，平天下，封功臣昆弟。
entries.en: After King Wu conquered King Zhou of Shang and pacified the world, he enfeoffed meritorious ministers and his brothers.
entries.literal: King Wu had already conquered King Zhou of Shang and pacified the world, enfeoffing meritorious ministers and his brothers.

entries.zh: 於是封叔鮮於管，封叔度於蔡：二人相紂子武庚祿父，治殷遺民。
entries.en: Therefore, he enfeoffed Shu Xian at Guan and Shu Du at Cai. These two men assisted Wu Geng Lu Fu, son of King Zhou, in governing the remnant people of Yin.
entries.literal: He therefore enfeoffed Shu Xian at Guan and Shu Du at Cai. The two men assisted Wu Geng Lufu, son of King Zhou of Shang, in governing the remnant people of Yin.

entries.zh: 封叔旦於魯而相周，為周公。
entries.en: He enfeoffed Shu Dan at Lu, and Shu Dan assisted Zhou, becoming the Duke of Zhou.
entries.literal: He enfeoffed Shu Dan at Lu and he assisted Zhou, becoming the Duke of Zhou.

entries.zh: 封叔振鐸於曹，封叔武於成，封叔處於霍。
entries.en: He enfeoffed Shu Zhen Duo at the state of Cao, Shu Wu at the state of Cheng, and Shu Chu at the state of Huo.
entries.literal: He enfeoffed Shu Zhen Duo at Cao, Shu Wu at Cheng, and Shu Chu at Huo.

entries.zh: 康叔封、冉季載皆少，未得封。
entries.en: Kang Shu Feng and Ran Ji Zai were both young and had not yet received enfeoffments.
entries.literal: Kang Shu Feng and Ran Ji Zai were both young and had not yet obtained enfeoffments.

entries.zh: 武王既崩，成王少，周公旦專王室。
entries.en: After King Wu passed away, King Cheng was young, and the Duke of Zhou Dan took charge of the royal house.
entries.literal: King Wu had already passed away. King Cheng was young, and the Duke of Zhou Dan monopolized the royal chamber.

entries.zh: 管叔、蔡叔疑周公之為不利於成王，乃挾武庚以作亂。
entries.en: Guan Shu and Cai Shu suspected that the Duke of Zhou's actions were not in King Cheng's interest, so they joined with Wu Geng and raised a rebellion.
entries.literal: Guan Shu and Cai Shu suspected that the Duke of Zhou's conduct was not to King Cheng's benefit, so they took Wu Geng and raised a rebellion.

entries.zh: 周公旦承成王命伐誅武庚，殺管叔，而放蔡叔，遷之，與車十乘，徒七十人從。
entries.en: The Duke of Zhou Dan received King Cheng's command, attacked and executed Wu Geng, killed Guan Shu, and banished Cai Shu. He relocated Cai Shu with ten chariots and seventy followers.
entries.literal: The Duke of Zhou Dan received King Cheng's command to attack and execute Wu Geng, kill Guan Shu, and banish Cai Shu. He moved him and gave him ten chariots with seventy followers.

entries.zh: 而分殷餘民為二：其一封微子啟於宋，以續殷祀；
entries.en: He divided the remnant people of Yin into two groups: over one group he enfeoffed Wei Zi Qi at Song, to continue the sacrifices of Yin;
entries.literal: And divided Yin remnant people into two: one enfeoffed Wei Zi Qi at Song, to continue Yin sacrifices;

entries.zh: 其一封康叔為衛君，是為衛康叔。
entries.en: Over the other group he enfeoffed Kang Shu as lord of Wei, thereafter known as Kang Shu of Wei.
entries.literal: The other he enfeoffed Kang Shu as lord of Wei, who became Wei Kang Shu.

entries.zh: 封季載於冉。
entries.en: He enfeoffed Ji Zai at Ran.
entries.literal: He enfeoffed Ji Zai at Ran.

entries.zh: 冉季、康叔皆有馴行，於是周公舉康叔為周司寇，冉季為周司空，以佐成王治，皆有令名於天下。
entries.en: Ran Ji and Kang Shu were both disciplined and mild in conduct. Therefore, the Duke of Zhou promoted Kang Shu to be Zhou's Minister of Crime and Ran Ji to be Zhou's Minister of Works, assisting King Cheng in government. Both had good reputations throughout the realm.
entries.literal: Ran Ji and Kang Shu both had gentle conduct. Therefore, the Duke of Zhou raised Kang Shu to be Zhou's Minister of Crime, and Ran Ji to be Zhou's Minister of Works, to assist King Cheng in governing. They all had good reputations throughout the world.

entries.zh: 伯邑考，其後不知所封。
entries.en: Bo Yi Kao—it is not known where his descendants were enfeoffed.
entries.literal: Bo Yi Kao—his descendants are not known where they were enfeoffed.

entries.zh: 武王發，其後為周，有本紀言。
entries.en: King Wu Fa—his descendants became Zhou, and their story is told in the basic annals.
entries.literal: King Wu Fa—his descendants became Zhou, and there are basic annals that speak of this.

entries.zh: 管叔鮮作亂誅死，無後。
entries.en: Guan Shu Xian rebelled and was executed, leaving no descendants.
entries.literal: Guan Shu Xian rebelled and was executed. He had no descendants.

entries.zh: 周公旦，其後為魯，有世家言。
entries.en: The Duke of Zhou Dan—his descendants became Lu, and their story is told in the hereditary houses.
entries.literal: The Duke of Zhou Dan—his descendants became Lu, and there are hereditary houses that speak of this.

entries.zh: 蔡叔度，其後為蔡，有世家言。
entries.en: Cai Shu Du—his descendants became Cai, and their story is told in the hereditary houses.
entries.literal: Cai Shu Du—his descendants became Cai, and there are hereditary houses that speak of this.

entries.zh: 曹叔振鐸，有後為曹，有世家言。
entries.en: Cao Shu Zhen Duo had descendants who became Cao, and their story is told in the hereditary houses.
entries.literal: Cao Shu Zhen Duo had descendants who became Cao, and there are hereditary houses that speak of this.

entries.zh: 成叔武，其後世無所見。
entries.en: Cheng Shu Wu—his later generations are nowhere to be seen.
entries.literal: Cheng Shu Wu—his later generations are nowhere seen.

entries.zh: 霍叔處，其後晉獻公時滅霍。
entries.en: Huo Shu Chu—his descendants were destroyed at Huo during the time of Duke Xian of Jin.
entries.literal: Huo Shu Chu—his descendants were extinguished at Huo during Jin's Duke Xian's time.

entries.zh: 康叔封，其後為衛，有世家言。
entries.en: Kang Shu Feng—his descendants became Wei, and their story is told in the hereditary houses.
entries.literal: Kang Shu Feng—his descendants became Wei, and there are hereditary houses that speak of this.

entries.zh: 冉季載，其後世無所見。
entries.en: Ran Ji Zai—his later generations are nowhere to be seen.
entries.literal: Ran Ji Zai—his later generations are nowhere seen.

entries.zh: 太史公曰：管蔡作亂，無足載者。
entries.en: The Grand Historian says: Guan and Cai rebelled, and there was little worth recording.
entries.literal: The Grand Historian said: Guan and Cai rebelled, and there was little worth recording.

entries.zh: 然周武王崩，成王少，天下既疑，賴同母之弟成叔、冉季之屬十人為輔拂，是以諸侯卒宗周，故附之世家言。
entries.en: However, when King Wu of Zhou died, King Cheng was young, and the world was already suspicious. The royal house relied on King Wu's younger brothers by the same mother, Cheng Shu, Ran Ji, and the rest of the ten brothers, to assist and protect it, and thus the feudal lords ultimately honored Zhou. Therefore, this account is attached to the hereditary houses.
entries.literal: However, when King Wu of Zhou died, King Cheng was young, and the world was already suspicious. They relied on the same mother's younger brothers Cheng Shu, Ran Ji and their group of ten to assist and protect, thus the feudal lords ultimately honored Zhou. Therefore, it is attached to the hereditary houses account.

entries.zh: 曹叔振鐸者，周武王弟也。
entries.en: Cao Shu Zhen Duo was the younger brother of King Wu of Zhou.
entries.literal: Cao Shu Zhen Duo was Zhou King Wu's younger brother.

entries.zh: 武王已克殷紂，封叔振鐸於曹。
entries.en: After King Wu defeated King Zhou of Shang, he enfeoffed Shu Zhenduo at Cao.
entries.literal: King Wu had already defeated King Zhou of Shang and enfeoffed Shu Zhen Duo at Cao.

entries.zh: 陳胡公滿者，虞帝舜之後也。
entries.en: Chen Hu Gong, Man, was a descendant of Emperor Shun of Yu.
entries.literal: Chen Hu Gong Man was a descendant of Emperor Shun of Yu.

entries.zh: 昔舜為庶人時，堯妻之二女，居于媯汭，其後因為氏姓，姓媯氏。
entries.en: When Shun was still a commoner, Yao gave him his two daughters in marriage, and they lived at Gui Rui. Their descendants therefore took Gui as their clan surname.
entries.literal: Formerly when Shun was a commoner, Yao married him two daughters, and they resided at Gui Rui. Their descendants therefore became the clan surname, the Gui clan.

entries.zh: 舜已崩，傳禹天下，而舜子商均為封國。
entries.en: After Shun died and transmitted the realm to Yu, Shun's son Shang Jun was given a fief.
entries.literal: Shun had already passed away and transmitted the world to Yu, while Shun's son Shang Jun was made an enfeoffed state.

entries.zh: 夏后之時，或失或續。
entries.en: During the Xia rulers, some lines were lost and some continued.
entries.literal: During the time of the Xia rulers, some were lost and some continued.

entries.zh: 至于周武王克殷紂，乃復求舜後，得媯滿，封之於陳，以奉帝舜祀，是為胡公。
entries.en: When King Wu of Zhou conquered King Zhou of Yin, he again sought out Shun's descendants, found Gui Man, and enfeoffed him at Chen to continue the sacrifices of Emperor Shun. This was Duke Hu.
entries.literal: When Zhou's King Wu conquered Yin Zhou, he then again sought Shun's descendants, obtained Gui Man, and enfeoffed him at Chen to continue Emperor Shun's sacrifices. This was Duke Hu.

entries.zh: 三十七年，齊桓公伐蔡，蔡敗；
entries.en: In the thirty-seventh year, Duke Huan of Qi attacked Cai, and Cai was defeated;
entries.literal: Thirty-seventh year, Qi Huan Gong attacked Cai, Cai defeated;

entries.zh: 南侵楚，至召陵，還過陳。
entries.en: He marched south against Chu, reached Shaoling, and passed through Chen on his return.
entries.literal: He invaded south against Chu, reached Shao Ling, and on his return passed through Chen.

entries.zh: 陳大夫轅濤涂惡其過陳，詐齊令出東道。
entries.en: The Chen grand officer Yuan Taotu disliked Qi's passage through Chen, so he tricked Qi into leaving by the eastern route.
entries.literal: Chen's grand officer Yuan Taotu disliked his passing through Chen and tricked Qi into sending them out by the eastern route.

entries.zh: 東道惡，桓公怒，執陳轅濤涂。
entries.en: The eastern route was poor, and Duke Huan was angered, so he seized Yuan Taotu of Chen.
entries.literal: The eastern route was poor. Duke Huan was angered and seized Yuan Taotu of Chen.

entries.zh: 是歲，晉獻公殺其太子申生。
entries.en: That year, Duke Xian of Jin killed his crown prince, Shen Sheng.
entries.literal: In this year, Duke Xian of Jin killed his crown prince Shen Sheng.

entries.zh: 三十四年，初，哀公娶鄭，長姬生悼太子師，少姬生偃。
entries.en: In the thirty-fourth year, initially Duke Ai married a woman from Zheng. His elder wife gave birth to Crown Prince Dao Shi, and his younger wife gave birth to Yan.
entries.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, initially Duke Ai married a woman from Zheng. His elder wife gave birth to Crown Prince Dao Shi, his younger wife gave birth to Yan.

entries.zh: 二嬖妾，長妾生留，少妾生勝。
entries.en: He had two favored concubines: the elder concubine gave birth to Liu, and the younger concubine gave birth to Sheng.
entries.literal: Two favored concubines: the elder concubine gave birth to Liu, the younger concubine gave birth to Sheng.

entries.zh: 留有寵哀公，哀公屬之其弟司徒招。
entries.en: Liu was favored by Duke Ai. Duke Ai entrusted him to his younger brother, Steward Zhao.
entries.literal: Liu was favored by Duke Ai. Duke Ai entrusted him to his younger brother Situ Zhao.

entries.zh: 哀公病，三月，招殺悼太子，立留為太子。
entries.en: Duke Ai was ill. In the third month, Zhao killed Crown Prince Dao and established Liu as crown prince.
entries.literal: Duke Ai was ill. In the third month, Zhao killed the Dao crown prince and established Liu as crown prince.

entries.zh: 哀公怒，欲誅招，招發兵圍守哀公，哀公自經殺。
entries.en: Duke Ai was angered and wanted to execute Zhao. Zhao raised troops and surrounded Duke Ai, and Duke Ai hanged himself.
entries.literal: Duke Ai was angered and desired to execute Zhao. Zhao raised troops and surrounded Duke Ai. Duke Ai hanged himself.

entries.zh: 招卒立留為陳君。
entries.en: Zhao at last set up Liu as lord of Chen.
entries.literal: Zhao finally established Liu as lord of Chen.

entries.zh: 四月，陳使使赴楚。
entries.en: In the fourth month, Chen dispatched an envoy to Chu.
entries.literal: In the fourth month, Chen sent an envoy to Chu.

entries.zh: 楚靈王聞陳亂，乃殺陳使者，使公子棄疾發兵伐陳，陳君留奔鄭。
entries.en: When King Ling of Chu heard of Chen’s disorder, he killed the Chen envoy and ordered Prince Qiji to raise troops against Chen. Liu, the lord of Chen, fled to Zheng.
entries.literal: King Ling of Chu heard of Chen's chaos and killed the Chen envoy. He had Prince Qi Ji raise troops to attack Chen. Chen's lord Liu fled to Zheng.

entries.zh: 九月，楚圍陳。
entries.en: In the ninth month, Chu surrounded Chen.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, Chu surrounded Chen.

entries.zh: 十一月，滅陳。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, Chu destroyed Chen.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, they extinguished Chen.

entries.zh: 使棄疾為陳公。
entries.en: Chu made Qi Ji the Duke of Chen.
entries.literal: They made Qi Ji the Duke of Chen.

entries.zh: 杞東樓公者，夏后禹之後苗裔也。
entries.en: Qi Dong Lou Gong was a descendant of Yu of the Xia rulers.
entries.literal: Qi Dong Lou Gong was a descendant of Yu of the Xia rulers.

entries.zh: 殷時或封或絕。
entries.en: During the Yin times, they were sometimes enfeoffed and sometimes ended.
entries.literal: During Yin times, they were sometimes enfeoffed and sometimes ended.

entries.zh: 周武王克殷紂，求禹之後，得東樓公，封之於杞，以奉夏后氏祀。
entries.en: King Wu of Zhou conquered Yin Zhou and sought Yu's descendants. He obtained Duke Dong Lou and enfeoffed him at Qi to continue the Xiahou clan's sacrifices.
entries.literal: Zhou's King Wu conquered Yin Zhou and sought Yu's descendants. He obtained Duke Dong Lou and enfeoffed him at Qi to continue the Xiahou clan's sacrifices.

entries.zh: 舜之後，周武王封之陳，至楚惠王滅之，有世家言。
entries.en: Shun's descendants were enfeoffed by King Wu of Zhou in the state of Chen, until King Hui of Chu destroyed them. Their story is told in the hereditary houses.
entries.literal: Shun's descendants—Zhou's King Wu enfeoffed them at Chen, until King Hui of Chu extinguished them. There are hereditary houses that speak of this.

entries.zh: 禹之後，周武王封之杞，楚惠王滅之，有世家言。
entries.en: Yu's descendants were enfeoffed by King Wu of Zhou in the state of Qi, until King Hui of Chu destroyed them. Their story is told in the hereditary houses.
entries.literal: Yu's descendants—Zhou's King Wu enfeoffed them at Qi, until King Hui of Chu extinguished them. There are hereditary houses that speak of this.

entries.zh: 契之後為殷，殷有本紀言。
entries.en: Xie's descendants became Yin. Yin has basic annals that speak of this.
entries.literal: Xie's descendants became Yin. Yin has basic annals that speak of this.

entries.zh: 殷破，周封其後於宋，齊湣王滅之，有世家言。
entries.en: When Yin fell, Zhou enfeoffed its descendants in the state of Song. King Min of Qi destroyed them. Their story is told in the hereditary houses.
entries.literal: Yin was broken. Zhou enfeoffed their descendants at Song. King Min of Qi extinguished them. There are hereditary houses that speak of this.

entries.zh: 后稷之後為周，秦昭王滅之，有本紀言。
entries.en: Hou Ji's descendants became the state of Zhou. King Zhao of Qin destroyed them. Their story is told in the basic annals.
entries.literal: Hou Ji's descendants became Zhou. King Zhao of Qin extinguished them. There are basic annals that speak of this.

entries.zh: 皋陶之後，或封英、六，楚穆王滅之，無譜。
entries.en: Gao Yao's descendants were sometimes enfeoffed at the states of Ying and Liu. King Mu of Chu destroyed them. There is no genealogy.
entries.literal: Gao Yao's descendants were sometimes enfeoffed at Ying and Liu. King Mu of Chu extinguished them. There is no genealogy.

entries.zh: 伯夷之後，至周武王復封於齊，曰太公望，陳氏滅之，有世家言。
entries.en: Bo Yi's descendants were again enfeoffed at Qi by King Wu of Zhou, under the name Tai Gong Wang. The Chen clan destroyed them. Their story is told in the hereditary houses.
entries.literal: Bo Yi's descendants were again enfeoffed at Qi by Zhou's King Wu, called Tai Gong Wang. The Chen clan extinguished them. There are hereditary houses that speak of this.

entries.zh: 伯翳之後，至周平王時封為秦，項羽滅之，有本紀言。
entries.en: Bo Yi's descendants were enfeoffed as Qin during the time of King Ping of Zhou. Xiang Yu destroyed them. Their story is told in the basic annals.
entries.literal: Bo Yi's descendants were enfeoffed as Qin during King Ping of Zhou's time. Xiang Yu extinguished them. There are basic annals that speak of this.

entries.zh: 垂、益、夔、龍，其後不知所封，不見也。
entries.en: Chui, Yi, Kui, and Long—it is not known where their descendants were enfeoffed, and they are not seen in the records.
entries.literal: Chui, Yi, Kui, and Long—their descendants are not known where they were enfeoffed and are not seen.

entries.zh: 右十一人者，皆唐虞之際名有功德臣也；
entries.en: The eleven people above were all famous ministers with merit and virtue during the time of Tang and Yu;
entries.literal: Right eleven people, all Tang Yu time famous meritorious virtue ministers;

entries.zh: 其五人之後皆至帝王，餘乃為顯諸侯。
entries.en: The descendants of five of them all became emperors and kings, while the rest became prominent feudal lords.
entries.literal: Their five people's descendants all became emperor kings, remainder became illustrious feudal lords.

entries.zh: 滕、薛、騶，夏、殷、周之閒封也，小，不足齒列，弗論也。
entries.en: Teng, Xue, and Zou were enfeoffed between Xia, Yin, and Zhou. They were small and too slight to rank among the others, so they are not discussed.
entries.literal: Teng, Xue, and Zou were enfeoffed between Xia, Yin, and Zhou. They were small and insufficient to rank with the teeth. They are not discussed.

entries.zh: 周武王時，侯伯尚千餘人。
entries.en: During the time of King Wu of Zhou, there were still over a thousand marquises and earls.
entries.literal: During Zhou's King Wu's time, there were still over a thousand hou and bo.

entries.zh: 及幽、厲之後，諸侯力攻相并。
entries.en: After Kings You and Li, the feudal lords attacked one another by force and annexed one another’s lands.
entries.literal: And after You and Li, the feudal lords attacked each other with force and annexed one another.

entries.zh: 江、黃、胡、沈之屬，不可勝數，故弗采著于傳（上）［云］。
entries.en: Jiang, Huang, Hu, Shen, and the like are too numerous to count exhaustively, so they are not collected and recorded in these traditions.
entries.literal: Jiang, Huang, Hu, Shen and such, cannot exhaust count, therefore not collected recorded in transmissions (upper) [cloud].

entries.zh: 太史公曰：舜之德可謂至矣！
entries.en: The Grand Historian says: Shun's virtue can be called the utmost!
entries.literal: Grand Historian said: Shun virtue can be called utmost!

entries.zh: 禪位於夏，而後世血食者歷三代。
entries.en: He yielded the throne to Xia, yet his descendants continued to receive blood sacrifices through three dynasties.
entries.literal: He yielded the throne to Xia, and his later generations' blood sacrifices spanned three dynasties.

entries.zh: 及楚滅陳，而田常得政於齊，卒為建國，百世不絕，苗裔茲茲，有土者不乏焉。
entries.en: When Chu destroyed Chen, Tian Chang took power in Qi and ultimately founded a state whose line endured for a hundred generations. His descendants flourished, and many of them held land.
entries.literal: And when Chu extinguished Chen, Tian Chang obtained government in Qi. He finally established a state that has not ended for a hundred generations. His descendants flourish and flourish. Those with land are not lacking.

entries.zh: 至禹，於周則杞，微甚，不足數也。
entries.en: As for Yu's line, under the Zhou it survived as Qi, but it was so diminished that it scarcely counted.
entries.literal: As for Yu, in Zhou it was Qi. It was extremely tiny and insufficient to count.

entries.zh: 楚惠王滅杞，其後越王句踐興。
entries.en: King Hui of Chu destroyed Qi. Later, King Gou Jian of Yue rose.
entries.literal: King Hui of Chu extinguished Qi. Later, King Gou Jian of Yue rose.

entries.zh: 太史公曰：余讀世家言，至於宣公之太子以婦見誅，弟壽爭死以相讓，此與晉太子申生不敢明驪姬之過同，俱惡傷父之志。
entries.en: The Grand Historian said: I read the hereditary houses' accounts, and arrived at Duke Xuan's crown prince who was executed because of his wife, and his younger brother Shou contended to die to yield to each other. This is the same as Jin's crown prince Shen Sheng, who dared not clarify Li Ji's transgression. Both disliked injuring their father's intention.
entries.literal: The Grand Historian said: I read the hereditary-house accounts, and when I reached Duke Xuan's crown prince who was executed because of his wife, and the younger brother Shou who contended over dying in mutual yielding, this was the same as Jin's crown prince Shen Sheng not daring to make clear Li Ji's fault; both disliked injuring their father's will.

entries.zh: 然卒死亡，何其悲也！
entries.en: Yet they finally died. How sad it is!
entries.literal: Yet in the end they died. How sad it is!

entries.zh: 或父子相殺，兄弟相滅，亦獨何哉？
entries.en: Some fathers and sons kill each other, and brothers extinguish each other. Why is this the case?
entries.literal: Some father son mutually kill, brothers mutually extinguish, also only what?

entries.zh: 衛康叔名封，周武王同母少弟也。
entries.en: Wei Kang Shu, named Feng, was a younger full brother of King Wu of Zhou.
entries.literal: Wei Kang Shu, named Feng, was King Wu of Zhou's younger brother by the same mother.

entries.zh: 其次尚有冉季，冉季最少。
entries.en: After him came Ran Ji, who was the youngest.
entries.literal: Next there was still Ran Ji, who was the youngest.

entries.zh: 越王謂范蠡曰：「以不聽子故至於此，為之柰何？」
entries.en: The king of Yue said to Fan Li, “Because I did not listen to you, I have reached this pass. What should be done?”
entries.literal: The king of Yue said to Fan Li, “Because I did not listen to you, I have come to this point. What is to be done?”

entries.zh: 蠡對曰：「持滿者與天，定傾者與人，節事者以地。
entries.en: Fan Li replied, “When something is full, one should accord with Heaven; when something has overturned, one should accord with people; when regulating affairs, one should accord with the earth.
entries.literal: Fan Li replied: “When something is full, one should align with Heaven; when something is overturned, one should align with people; when regulating affairs, one should accord with the land.

entries.zh: 卑辭厚禮以遺之，不許，而身與之市。」
entries.en: Send them humble words and generous gifts. If they do not permit it, then you yourself must go and bargain with the Wu king in person.”
entries.literal: Humble words thick gifts to send them, if not permitted, then body with them bargain.'

entries.zh: 句踐曰：「諾。」
entries.en: Goujian said: “Yes.”
entries.literal: Gou Jian said: 'Yes.'

entries.zh: 乃令大夫種行成於吳，膝行頓首曰：「君王亡臣句踐使陪臣種敢告下執事：句踐請為臣，妻為妾。」
entries.en: He then ordered Grandee Zhong to go and make peace with Wu. Zhong walked on his knees, kowtowed, and said: “Goujian, fugitive servant of Your Majesty, sends his attendant minister Zhong to address those below you: Goujian asks to become your minister, and his wife your concubine.”
entries.literal: He then ordered Grandee Zhong to go and make peace with Wu. Zhong walked on his knees, knocked his head to the ground, and said: “Goujian, fugitive servant of Your Majesty, sends his attendant minister Zhong to address those below you: Goujian asks to become your minister, and his wife your concubine.”

entries.zh: 吳王將許之。
entries.en: The Wu king was about to permit it.
entries.literal: The Wu wang was about to permit it.

entries.zh: 子胥言於吳王曰：「天以越賜吳，勿許也。」
entries.en: Zixu spoke to the Wu king, saying: “Heaven grants Yue to Wu. Do not permit it.”
entries.literal: Zi Xu spoke to Wu wang said: 'Heaven with Yue grants Wu, do not permit.'

entries.zh: 種還，以報句踐。
entries.en: Zhong returned to report to Gou Jian.
entries.literal: Zhong returned to report to Gou Jian.

entries.zh: 句踐欲殺妻子，燔寶器，觸戰以死。
entries.en: Goujian wanted to kill his wife and children, burn his treasure vessels, and fight to the death.
entries.literal: Gou Jian desired to kill his wife and children, burn the treasure vessels, and fight to the death.

entries.zh: 種止句踐曰：「夫吳太宰嚭貪，可誘以利，請閒行言之。」
entries.en: Zhong stopped Goujian and said, “The Grand Administrator Pi of Wu is greedy and can be tempted by profit. Please allow me to go secretly and speak with him.”
entries.literal: Zhong stopped Goujian and said: “The Grand Administrator Pi of Wu is greedy and can be tempted with profit. Please let me go secretly and speak with him.”

entries.zh: 於是句踐以美女寶器令種閒獻吳太宰嚭。
entries.en: Goujian then commanded Zhong to secretly offer beautiful women and treasure vessels to Pi, the Grand Administrator of Wu.
entries.literal: Thereupon Gou Jian commanded Zhong to secretly offer beautiful women and treasure vessels to Wu's grand administrator Pi.

entries.zh: 嚭受，乃見大夫種於吳王。
entries.en: Pi accepted and then presented Grandee Zhong to the Wu king.
entries.literal: Pi accepted and then presented Grandee Zhong to the Wu wang.

entries.zh: 種頓首言曰：「願大王赦句踐之罪，盡入其寶器。
entries.en: Zhong kowtowed and said: “I hope Your Majesty will pardon Goujian’s offense and accept all his precious vessels.
entries.literal: Zhong knocked his head to the ground and said: “I hope Your Majesty will pardon Goujian’s offense and accept all his precious vessels.

entries.zh: 不幸不赦，句踐將盡殺其妻子，燔其寶器，悉五千人觸戰，必有當也。」
entries.en: If you do not pardon him, Goujian will kill his wife and children to the last, burn his treasure vessels, and send all five thousand men into a fight to the death. They will certainly resist fiercely.”
entries.literal: If you do not pardon him, Gou Jian will kill his wife and children to the last, burn his treasure vessels, and all five thousand men will fight to the death. There will certainly be stiff resistance.'

entries.zh: 嚭因說吳王曰：「越以服為臣，若將赦之，此國之利也。」
entries.en: Pi then persuaded the king of Wu, saying, “Yue has submitted as your minister. If you pardon it, the state will profit.”
entries.literal: Pi then persuaded the king of Wu: “Yue has submitted as your minister. If you pardon it, this will profit the state.”

entries.zh: 吳王將許之。
entries.en: The Wu king was about to permit it.
entries.literal: The Wu wang was about to permit it.

entries.zh: 子胥進諫曰：「今不滅越，後必悔之。
entries.en: Zixu advanced and admonished, saying: “If we do not extinguish the state of Yue now, we will certainly regret it later.
entries.literal: Zi Xu advanced admonished said: 'Now not extinguish Yue, later certainly regret it.

entries.zh: 句踐賢君，種、蠡良臣，若反國，將為亂。」
entries.en: Goujian is a worthy lord, and Zhong and Li are good ministers. If they return to their country, they will stir up trouble.”
entries.literal: Gou Jian worthy lord, Zhong, Li good ministers, if return country, will cause chaos.'

entries.zh: 吳王弗聽，卒赦越，罷兵而歸。
entries.en: The Wu king did not listen. He finally pardoned Yue, dismissed the troops, and returned.
entries.literal: The Wu wang did not listen. He finally pardoned Yue, dismissed the troops, and returned.

entries.zh: 范蠡遂去，自齊遺大夫種書曰：「蜚鳥盡，良弓藏；
entries.en: Fan Li then departed. From Qi he sent Grandee Zhong a letter, saying, “When the flying birds are gone, the fine bow is put away;
entries.literal: Fan Li then left. From Qi he sent Grandee Zhong a letter, saying: “When the flying birds are gone, the fine bow is stored away;

entries.zh: 狡兔死，走狗烹。
entries.en: when the cunning rabbit is dead, the swift hound is cooked.
entries.literal: when the cunning rabbit is dead, the running hound is cooked.

entries.zh: 越王為人長頸鳥喙，可與共患難，不可與共樂。
entries.en: The king of Yue has a long neck and a beak like a bird's. One can share hardship and danger with him, but not joy.
entries.literal: The king of Yue has a long neck and a bird’s beak. One can share hardship and danger with him, but not joy.

entries.zh: 子何不去？」
entries.en: Why do you not leave?”
entries.literal: Why do you not leave?”

entries.zh: 種見書，稱病不朝。
entries.en: When Zhong saw the letter, he claimed illness and stopped attending court.
entries.literal: When Zhong saw the letter, he claimed illness and did not attend court.

entries.zh: 人或讒種且作亂，越王乃賜種劍曰：「子教寡人伐吳七術，寡人用其三而敗吳，其四在子，子為我從先王試之。」
entries.en: Someone slandered Zhong, saying that he was about to rebel. The king of Yue then bestowed a sword on Zhong and said, “You taught me seven strategies for attacking Wu. I used three of them and defeated Wu; the remaining four are still with you. Follow the former king and test them for me.”
entries.literal: Someone slandered Zhong, saying that he was about to start a rebellion. The king of Yue then bestowed a sword on Zhong and said: “You taught me seven strategies for attacking Wu. I used three of them and defeated Wu; the remaining four are still with you. Follow the former king and test them for me.”

entries.zh: 種遂自殺。
entries.en: Zhong then committed suicide.
entries.literal: Zhong then committed suicide.

entries.zh: 句踐之困會稽也，喟然嘆曰：「吾終於此乎？」
entries.en: When Goujian was trapped at Kuaiji, he sighed deeply and said, “Is this where I end?”
entries.literal: When Goujian was trapped at Kuaiji, he sighed deeply and said, “Will I end here?”

entries.zh: 種曰：「湯系夏臺，文王囚羑里，晉重耳奔翟，齊小白奔莒，其卒王霸。
entries.en: Zhong said, “Tang was bound at Xiatai, King Wen was imprisoned at Youli, Chong’er of Jin fled to the Di, and Xiaobai of Qi fled to Ju, yet in the end they became kings and hegemons.
entries.literal: Zhong said: “Tang was bound at Xiatai, King Wen was imprisoned at Youli, Chong’er of Jin fled to the Di, and Xiaobai of Qi fled to Ju, yet in the end they became kings and hegemons.

entries.zh: 由是觀之，何遽不為福乎？」
entries.en: Seen in this light, how do we know that this will not become a blessing?”
entries.literal: Seen from this, how do we know this will not quickly become a blessing?”

entries.zh: 吳既赦越，越王句踐反國，乃苦身焦思，置膽於坐，坐臥即仰膽，飲食亦嘗膽也。
entries.en: After Wu pardoned Yue, King Goujian of Yue returned to his state. He hardened his body and brooded bitterly, placing gall by his seat; whenever he sat or lay down he looked up at it, and whenever he ate or drank he tasted it.
entries.literal: After Wu pardoned Yue, King Goujian of Yue returned to his state. He then tormented his body and strained his thoughts, placing gall at his seat; whenever he sat or lay down he looked up at the gall, and when eating and drinking he tasted it.

entries.zh: 曰：「女忘會稽之恥邪？」
entries.en: He would say, “Have you forgotten the humiliation at Kuaiji?”
entries.literal: He would say, “Have you forgotten the shame of Kuaiji?”

entries.zh: 身自耕作，夫人自織，食不加肉，衣不重采，折節下賢人，厚遇賓客，振貧弔死，與百姓同其勞。
entries.en: He personally tilled the fields, and his wife personally wove. His food had no extra meat, and his clothing no layered colors. He humbled himself before worthy men, treated guests generously, helped the poor, mourned the dead, and shared the labor of the common people.
entries.literal: He personally tilled the fields, and his wife personally wove. His food had no added meat, his clothing no layered colors. He lowered himself before worthy men, treated guests generously, aided the poor, mourned the dead, and shared the people’s labors.

entries.zh: 欲使范蠡治國政，蠡對曰：「兵甲之事，種不如蠡；
entries.en: He wanted Fan Li to govern the affairs of the state. Fan Li replied, “In matters of armor and weapons, Zhong is not equal to me;
entries.literal: He wanted Fan Li to govern the affairs of the state. Fan Li replied: “In matters of armor and weapons, Zhong is not as good as I am;

entries.zh: 填撫國家，親附百姓，蠡不如種。」
entries.en: but in pacifying the state and drawing the people close, I am not equal to Zhong.”
entries.literal: but in pacifying the state and drawing the people close, I am not as good as Zhong.”

entries.zh: 於是舉國政屬大夫種，而使范蠡與大夫柘稽行成，為質於吳。
entries.en: Goujian then entrusted state affairs to Grandee Zhong, and sent Fan Li and Grandee Zheji to make peace and serve as hostages in Wu.
entries.literal: Thereupon he entrusted the affairs of the state to Grandee Zhong, and sent Fan Li and Grandee Zheji to make peace and serve as hostages in Wu.

entries.zh: 二歲而吳歸蠡。
entries.en: After two years, Wu returned Li.
entries.literal: After two years, Wu returned Li.

entries.zh: 居二年，吳王將伐齊。
entries.en: After two years, the Wu king was about to attack Qi.
entries.literal: After two years, the Wu wang was about to attack Qi.

entries.zh: 子胥諫曰：「未可。
entries.en: Wu Zixu remonstrated: “Not yet.
entries.literal: Wu Zixu remonstrated: “It is not yet possible.

entries.zh: 臣聞句踐食不重味，與百姓同苦樂。
entries.en: I have heard that Goujian does not eat richly varied dishes and shares hardship and joy with the common people.
entries.literal: I have heard that Gou Jian eats no repeated flavors and shares bitterness and joy with the common people.

entries.zh: 此人不死，必為國患。
entries.en: If this man does not die, he will certainly become a danger to the state.
entries.literal: If this person does not die, he will certainly become a state calamity.

entries.zh: 吳有越，腹心之疾，齊與吳，疥癬也。
entries.en: For Wu, Yue is a disease in its very vitals; Qi is only a skin ailment.
entries.literal: For Wu, Yue is a disease of the heart and belly; Qi is only scabies and ringworm.

entries.zh: 願王釋齊先越。」
entries.en: I hope the king will set Qi aside and deal with Yue first.”
entries.literal: I hope the king will leave Qi aside and deal with Yue first.”

entries.zh: 吳王弗聽，遂伐齊，敗之艾陵，虜齊高、國以歸。
entries.en: The Wu king did not listen. He then attacked Qi, defeated them at Ai Ling, captured Gao and Guo of Qi, and returned.
entries.literal: The Wu wang did not listen. He then attacked Qi, defeated them at Ai Ling, captured Qi Gao and Guo, and returned.

entries.zh: 讓子胥。
entries.en: He reproached Wu Zixu.
entries.literal: He reproached Zi Xu.

entries.zh: 子胥曰：「王毋喜！」
entries.en: Zixu said: “King, do not rejoice!”
entries.literal: Zi Xu said: 'Wang do not rejoice!'

entries.zh: 王怒，子胥欲自殺，王聞而止之。
entries.en: The king was angered. Zi Xu desired to commit suicide. The king heard and stopped him.
entries.literal: The wang was angered. Zi Xu desired suicide. The wang heard and stopped him.

entries.zh: 越大夫種曰：「臣觀吳王政驕矣，請試嘗之貸粟，以卜其事。」
entries.en: Grandee Zhong of Yue said: “I observe that the king of Wu’s government has grown arrogant. Let us test him by asking to borrow grain, and thereby read how matters stand.”
entries.literal: Grandee Zhong of Yue said: “I observe that the king of Wu’s government has grown arrogant. Please let us test him by asking to borrow grain, so that we can divine how matters stand.”

entries.zh: 請貸，吳王欲與，子胥諫勿與，王遂與之，越乃私喜。
entries.en: They requested to borrow. The Wu king desired to give. Zi Xu admonished not to give. The king then gave it. Yue then privately rejoiced.
entries.literal: They requested to borrow. The Wu wang desired to give. Zi Xu admonished not to give. The wang then gave it. Yue then privately rejoiced.

entries.zh: 子胥言曰：「王不聽諫，後三年吳其墟乎！」
entries.en: Wu Zixu said, “If the king does not listen to remonstrance, within three years Wu may lie in ruins!”
entries.literal: Wu Zixu said, “If the king does not listen to remonstrance, in three years Wu may be ruins!”

entries.zh: 太宰嚭聞之，乃數與子胥爭越議，因讒子胥曰：「伍員貌忠而實忍人，其父兄不顧，安能顧王？
entries.en: The Grand Administrator Pi heard this and repeatedly argued with Wu Zixu over Yue policy. He then slandered Wu Zixu, saying, “Wu Yuan appears loyal, but in truth he is cruel. He disregarded his own father and elder brother; how can he care for Your Majesty?
entries.literal: The Grand Administrator Pi heard this and repeatedly disputed Yue policy with Wu Zixu. He then slandered Wu Zixu, saying: “Wu Yuan appears loyal, but in truth he is cruel. He did not care for his own father and elder brother; how can he care for the king?

entries.zh: 王前欲伐齊，員彊諫，已而有功，用是反怨王。
entries.en: Earlier, when the king wished to attack Qi, Wu Yuan forcefully remonstrated. After the campaign succeeded, he took this as a reason to resent the king.
entries.literal: When the king previously wanted to attack Qi, Wu Yuan strongly remonstrated. After the campaign succeeded, he used this as a reason to resent the king.

entries.zh: 王不備伍員，員必為亂。」
entries.en: If the king does not guard against Wu Yuan, Yuan will certainly rebel.”
entries.literal: Wang not prepare Wu Yuan, Yuan certainly causes chaos.'

entries.zh: 與逢同共謀，讒之王。
entries.en: Together with Feng Tong they plotted and slandered to the king.
entries.literal: Together with Feng Tong they plotted and slandered to the wang.

entries.zh: 王始不從，乃使子胥於齊，聞其託子於鮑氏，王乃大怒，曰：「伍員果欺寡人！」
entries.en: The king at first did not follow this advice, and later sent Zixu to Qi. When he heard that Zixu had entrusted his son to the Bao clan, the king became furious and said: “Wu Yuan has indeed deceived me!”
entries.literal: Wang at first not followed, then sent Zi Xu to Qi, heard he entrusted son to Bao clan, wang then greatly angered, said: 'Wu Yuan indeed deceives I!'

entries.zh: 役反，使人賜子胥屬鏤劍以自殺。
entries.en: When the campaign returned, the king sent someone to present Wu Zixu with the Zhulou sword and order him to kill himself.
entries.literal: When the mission returned, the king sent someone to bestow on Wu Zixu the Zhulou sword, with which he was to kill himself.

entries.zh: 子胥大笑曰：「我令而父霸，我又立若，若初欲分吳國半予我，我不受，已，今若反以讒誅我。
entries.en: Wu Zixu laughed loudly and said: “I made your father hegemon, and I established you as well. At first, you wished to divide the state of Wu in half and give it to me, but I did not accept it. Now you instead execute me on slander.
entries.literal: Zi Xu laughed loudly and said: 'I made your father hegemon, and I moreover established you. You at first wished to divide the Wu state in half and give it to me. I did not accept it. And now you instead use slander to execute me.

entries.zh: 嗟乎，嗟乎，一人固不能獨立！」
entries.en: Alas, alas—a lone man truly cannot stand alone!”
entries.literal: Alas, alas—a lone man truly cannot succeed alone!'

entries.zh: 報使者曰：「必取吾眼置吳東門，以觀越兵入也！」
entries.en: He told the envoy, “Take my eyes and set them on Wu’s eastern gate, so that I may watch the Yue army enter!”
entries.literal: He told the envoy, “You must take my eyes and place them on Wu’s eastern gate, so that I may watch the Yue army enter!”

entries.zh: 於是吳任嚭政。
entries.en: Wu then entrusted the government to Pi.
entries.literal: Thereupon Wu entrusted the government to Pi.

entries.zh: 越王句踐，其先禹之苗裔，而夏后帝少康之庶子也。
entries.en: King Goujian of Yue descended from Yu, through a younger son of Emperor Shaokang of the Xia royal house.
entries.literal: King Goujian of Yue was descended from Yu and from a younger son of Emperor Shaokang of the Xia royal house.

entries.zh: 封於會稽，以奉守禹之祀。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed at Kuaiji so that he could maintain Yu’s sacrifices.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed at Kuaiji to maintain the sacrifices to Yu.

entries.zh: 文身斷發，披草萊而邑焉。
entries.en: His people tattooed their bodies, cut their hair short, cleared the wild grasslands, and established settlements there.
entries.literal: His people tattooed their bodies, cut their hair short, cleared the grassy wilderness, and founded settlements there.

entries.zh: 後二十餘世，至於允常。
entries.en: After more than twenty generations, the line came down to Yunchang.
entries.literal: After more than twenty generations, it reached Yun Chang.

entries.zh: 允常之時，與吳王闔廬戰而相怨伐。
entries.en: In Yunchang’s time, he fought King Helü of Wu, and the two states repeatedly attacked each other out of mutual resentment.
entries.literal: In Yunchang’s time, he fought King Helü of Wu, and the two states attacked one another in mutual resentment.

entries.zh: 允常卒，子句踐立，是為越王。
entries.en: When Yunchang died, his son Goujian came to the throne as king of Yue.
entries.literal: Yunchang died, and his son Goujian came to the throne as king of Yue.

entries.zh: 十八年，齊、魏伐我，我決河水灌之，兵去。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year, Qi and Wei attacked Zhao. The Zhao forces breached the river dikes and flooded the invaders, forcing them to withdraw.
entries.literal: Eighteenth year, Qi, Wei attacked us, we broke river water flooded them, troops left.

entries.zh: 二十二年，張儀相秦。
entries.en: In the twenty-second year, Zhang Yi became chancellor of Qin.
entries.literal: Twenty-second year, Zhang Yi became prime minister of Qin.

entries.zh: 趙疵與秦戰，敗，秦殺疵河西，取我藺、離石。
entries.en: Zhao Ci fought against Qin and was defeated. Qin killed Ci west of the Yellow River and seized the Zhao cities of Lin and Lishi.
entries.literal: Zhao Ci with Qin battled, defeated, Qin killed Ci river west, took our Lin, Li Shi.

entries.zh: 二十三年，韓舉與齊、魏戰，死于桑丘。
entries.en: In the twenty-third year, Han Ju fought against Qi and Wei and was killed at Sangqiu.
entries.literal: Twenty-third year, Han Ju with Qi, Wei battled, died at Sang Qiu.

entries.zh: 趙文、趙造、周袑、趙俊皆諫止王毋胡服，如故法便。
entries.en: Zhao Wen, Zhao Zao, Zhou Shao, and Zhao Jun all remonstrated with the king, urging him to abandon the Hu dress and retain the old ways as more fitting.
entries.literal: Zhao Wen, Zhao Zao, Zhou Shan, Zhao Jun all advised stop wang not barbarian clothing, like old law convenient.

entries.zh: 王曰：「先王不同俗，何古之法？
entries.en: The king replied, "The former kings did not share the same customs — so which antiquity should serve as our model?
entries.literal: The king said: 'Former kings had different customs, what ancient laws exist?

entries.zh: 帝王不相襲，何禮之循？
entries.en: The emperors and kings did not follow one another's practices — so which rites should we adhere to?
entries.literal: Emperors and kings do not imitate each other, what rituals should be followed?

entries.zh: 虙戲、神農教而不誅，黃帝、堯、舜誅而不怒。
entries.en: Fuxi and Shennong taught the people without resorting to punishment; the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun punished without anger.
entries.literal: Fuxi and Shennong taught without punishing, Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun punished without anger.

entries.zh: 及至三王，隨時制法，因事制禮。
entries.en: When it came to the Three Kings, they fashioned their laws to suit the times and shaped their rituals to match the circumstances.
entries.literal: When it came to the Three Kings, they made laws according to the times, created rituals according to circumstances.

entries.zh: 法度制令各順其宜，衣服器械各便其用。
entries.en: Their statutes, measures, and decrees each conformed to what was fitting, and their clothing and implements each served a practical purpose.
entries.literal: Laws, measures, decrees, and commands each followed what was appropriate, clothing and implements each suited their use.

entries.zh: 故禮也不必一道，而便國不必古。
entries.en: Therefore, ritual need not follow a single path, and what benefits the state need not derive from antiquity.
entries.literal: Therefore, ritual does not necessarily follow one path, and what benefits the state does not necessarily come from antiquity.

entries.zh: 聖人之興也不相襲而王，夏、殷之衰也不易禮而滅。
entries.en: The sages who rose to kingship did not do so by imitating their predecessors, and the Xia and Yin dynasties did not perish because they changed their rites.
entries.literal: The rise of sages does not imitate predecessors to become kings, the decline of Xia and Yin did not change rituals to perish.

entries.zh: 然則反古未可非，而循禮未足多也。
entries.en: It follows, then, that a departure from antiquity cannot in itself be condemned, and that merely adhering to ritual does not in itself deserve praise.
entries.literal: Thus, returning to antiquity cannot be criticized, but following ritual is not sufficient praise.

entries.zh: 且服奇者志淫，則是鄒、魯無奇行也；
entries.en: If it were true that wearing strange attire leads to a licentious spirit, then Zou and Lu would never have produced men of exceptional conduct.
entries.literal: Moreover, those who wear strange clothing have licentious ambitions, but this means that Zou and Lu have no exceptional conduct;

entries.zh: 俗辟者民易，則是吳、越無秀士也。
entries.en: If it were true that unorthodox customs make the people fickle, then Wu and Yue would never have produced outstanding scholars.
entries.literal: Customs that are eccentric make the people fickle, but this means that Wu and Yue have no outstanding scholars.

entries.zh: 且聖人利身謂之服，便事謂之禮。
entries.en: The sages called that which benefits the body 'clothing,' and that which facilitates affairs 'ritual.'
entries.literal: Moreover, the sages called benefiting the body 'clothing', and what facilitates affairs 'ritual'.

entries.zh: 夫進退之節，衣服之制者，所以齊常民也，非所以論賢者也。
entries.en: The rules for propriety in conduct and the regulations for dress are meant to keep the common people in order — they are not the standard by which the worthy are judged.
entries.literal: Indeed, the regulations for advancing and retreating, the systems for clothing, these are to regulate the common people, not to judge the worthy.

entries.zh: 故齊民與俗流，賢者與變俱。
entries.en: The common people drift with the current of custom, but the worthy move with the tide of change.
entries.literal: Therefore, regulate the people to flow with customs, the worthy accompany changes.

entries.zh: 故諺曰『以書御者不盡馬之情，以古制今者不達事之變』。
entries.en: As the proverb says, 'He who drives a horse by the book will never master the horse's true nature, and he who governs the present by the standards of antiquity will never grasp the changing nature of affairs.'
entries.literal: Therefore, the proverb says: 'One who drives a horse by the book does not understand the horse's temperament, one who applies ancient systems to today does not comprehend changes in affairs.'

entries.zh: 循法之功，不足以高世；
entries.en: The merit of merely following established law is not enough to rise above one's age.
entries.literal: The merit of following the law is not sufficient to stand above the world;

entries.zh: 法古之學，不足以制今。
entries.en: And the learning of those who merely imitate antiquity is not enough to master the present.
entries.literal: Studying the laws of antiquity is not sufficient to govern the present.

entries.zh: 子不及也。」
entries.en: You, sirs, do not measure up to this."
entries.literal: You are not equal to it.'

entries.zh: 遂胡服招騎射。
entries.en: And so the king adopted Hu dress and began training a force of mounted archers.
entries.literal: Thus, he adopted barbarian clothing and recruited cavalry archers.

entries.zh: 王還，不聽秦，秦圍邯鄲。
entries.en: The king returned to Handan and refused Qin's terms. Qin then laid siege to the capital.
entries.literal: The king returned, did not heed Qin, Qin besieged Handan.

entries.zh: 武垣令傅豹、王容、蘇射率燕眾反燕地。
entries.en: The magistrate of Wuyuan, Fu Bao, along with Wang Rong and Su She, led the Yan garrison in a revolt and returned to Yan territory.
entries.literal: The magistrate of Wuyuan, Fu Bao, Wang Rong, and Su She led Yan troops to rebel in Yan territory.

entries.zh: 趙以靈丘封楚相春申君。
entries.en: Zhao enfeoffed the Lord of Chunshen, the chancellor of Chu, with the city of Lingqiu.
entries.literal: Zhao enfeoffed Lingqiu to Chu's chancellor Lord Chunshen.

entries.zh: 七年，秦人攻趙，趙大將李牧、將軍司馬尚將，擊之。
entries.en: In the seventh year, Qin launched a major assault on Zhao. The great general Li Mu and General Sima Shang took command of the defense.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, Qin attacked Zhao, Zhao's great general Li Mu and general Sima Shang commanded, attacked them.

entries.zh: 李牧誅，司馬尚免，趙怱及齊將顏聚代之。
entries.en: Li Mu was executed, and Sima Shang was dismissed. Zhao Cong and the Qi general Yan Ju were appointed in their place.
entries.literal: Li Mu was executed, Sima Shang dismissed, Zhao Cong and Qi general Yan Ju replaced them.

entries.zh: 趙怱軍破，顏聚亡去。
entries.en: Zhao Cong's army was shattered. Yan Ju fled.
entries.literal: Zhao Cong's army was broken, Yan Ju fled.

entries.zh: 以王遷降。
entries.en: King Qian was taken and surrendered.
entries.literal: King Qian surrendered.

entries.zh: 趙氏之先，與秦共祖。
entries.en: The Zhao clan's forebears shared an ancestor with Qin.
entries.literal: Zhao clan's forebears, together with Qin shared ancestor.

entries.zh: 至中衍，為帝大戊御。
entries.en: Reaching Zhong Yan, he was Emperor Da Wu's charioteer.
entries.literal: Reached Zhong Yan, was Emperor Da Wu's charioteer.

entries.zh: 其後世蜚廉有子二人，而命其一子曰惡來，事紂，為周所殺，其後為秦。
entries.en: In his later generations, Feilian had two sons, and named one of them Elai. Elai served King Zhou and was killed by the Zhou. His descendants became Qin.
entries.literal: His later generations Feilian had sons two, and named his one son said Elai, served Zhou, was by Zhou killed, his descendants became Qin.

entries.zh: 惡來弟曰季勝，其後為趙。
entries.en: Elai's younger brother was named Jisheng. His descendants became Zhao.
entries.literal: Elai's younger brother named Jisheng, his descendants became Zhao.

entries.zh: 十二年，楚敗我襄陵。
entries.en: In the twelfth year, Chu defeated our forces at Xiangling.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year, Chu defeated our Xiang Ling.

entries.zh: 諸侯執政與秦相張儀會齧桑。
entries.en: The chief ministers of the feudal states met with Zhang Yi, the chancellor of Qin, at Niesang.
entries.literal: The feudal lords' chief ministers met with Qin chancellor Zhang Yi at Nie Sang.

entries.zh: 十三年，張儀相魏。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year, Zhang Yi became the chancellor of Wei.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year, Zhang Yi became chancellor of Wei.

entries.zh: 魏有女子化為丈夫。
entries.en: In Wei, a woman transformed into a man.
entries.literal: Wei had a woman who transformed into a man.

entries.zh: 秦取我曲沃、平周。
entries.en: Qin seized our cities of Quwo and Pingzhou.
entries.literal: Qin took our Qu Wo and Ping Zhou.

entries.zh: 十六年，襄王卒，子哀王立。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year, King Xiang died. His son ascended the throne as King Ai.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year, Xiang Wang died. His son Ai Wang was established.

entries.zh: 張儀復歸秦。
entries.en: Zhang Yi returned once more to Qin.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi again returned to Qin.

entries.zh: 九年，與秦王會臨晉。
entries.en: In the ninth year, Wei met with the King of Qin at Linjin.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, they met with the Qin wang at Lin Jin.

entries.zh: 張儀、魏章皆歸于魏。
entries.en: Zhang Yi and Wei Zhang both returned to Wei.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi and Wei Zhang all returned to Wei.

entries.zh: 魏相田需死，楚害張儀、犀首、薛公。
entries.en: The Wei chancellor Tian Xu died. Chu feared the influence of Zhang Yi, Xishou, and the Lord of Xue.
entries.literal: The Wei chancellor Tian Xu died. Chu feared Zhang Yi, Xishou, and the Lord of Xue.

entries.zh: 楚相昭魚謂蘇代曰：「田需死，吾恐張儀、犀首、薛公有一人相魏者也。」
entries.en: The Chu chancellor Zhao Yu said to Su Dai, 'Now that Tian Xu is dead, I fear that one of those three — Zhang Yi, Xishou, or the Lord of Xue — will become chancellor of Wei.'
entries.literal: Chu chancellor Zhao Yu told Su Dai said: 'Tian Xu died, I fear Zhang Yi, Xi Shou, Xue Gong have one chancellor Wei.'

entries.zh: 代曰：「然相者欲誰而君便之？」
entries.en: Su Dai replied, 'Then whom would you prefer as chancellor? Tell me, and I will make arrangements.'
entries.literal: Dai said: 'So chancellor want who and lord convenient it?'

entries.zh: 昭魚曰：「吾欲太子之自相也。」
entries.en: Zhao Yu said, 'I would prefer the crown prince himself to serve as chancellor.'
entries.literal: Zhao Yu said: 'I want crown prince self chancellor.'

entries.zh: 代曰：「請為君北，必相之。」
