entries.en: Su Dai said, 'Allow me to go north on your behalf. I will see to it that he is made chancellor.'
entries.literal: Dai said: 'Please for lord north, certainly chancellor it.'

entries.zh: 昭魚曰：「柰何？」
entries.en: Zhao Yu asked, 'How will you manage it?'
entries.literal: Zhao Yu said: 'How?'

entries.zh: 對曰：「君其為梁王，代請說君。」
entries.en: Su Dai replied, 'Play the role of the King of Liang, and let me practice my argument on you.'
entries.literal: Replied: 'Lord become Liang wang, Dai please persuade lord.'

entries.zh: 昭魚曰：「柰何？」
entries.en: Zhao Yu asked, 'How will you manage it?'
entries.literal: Zhao Yu said: 'How?'

entries.zh: 對曰：「代也從楚來，昭魚甚憂，曰：『田需死，吾恐張儀、犀首、薛公有一人相魏者也。』
entries.en: Su Dai began, "I have just come from Chu. Zhao Yu is deeply worried. He said, 'Now that Tian Xu is dead, I fear that Zhang Yi, Xishou, or the Lord of Xue will become chancellor of Wei.'
entries.literal: Replied: 'Dai from Chu come, Zhao Yu very worried, said: 'Tian Xu died, I fear Zhang Yi, Xi Shou, Xue Gong have one chancellor Wei.'

entries.zh: 代曰：『梁王，長主也，必不相張儀。
entries.en: I told him, 'The King of Liang is an experienced ruler. He will certainly not appoint Zhang Yi as chancellor.
entries.literal: Dai said: 'Liang wang, senior lord, certainly not chancellor Zhang Yi.

entries.zh: 張儀相，必右秦而左魏。
entries.en: If Zhang Yi were made chancellor, he would surely favor Qin at Wei's expense.
entries.literal: If Zhang Yi is chancellor, he will certainly favor Qin and slight Wei.

entries.zh: 犀首相，必右韓而左魏。
entries.en: If Xishou were made chancellor, he would favor Han at Wei's expense.
entries.literal: If Xi Shou is chancellor, he will certainly favor Han and slight Wei.

entries.zh: 薛公相，必右齊而左魏。
entries.en: If the Lord of Xue were made chancellor, he would favor Qi at Wei's expense.
entries.literal: If Xue Gong is chancellor, he will certainly favor Qi and slight Wei.

entries.zh: 梁王，長主也，必不便也。』
entries.en: The King of Liang is a seasoned ruler—he would surely find none of these acceptable.'
entries.literal: Liang wang, senior lord, certainly not convenient.'

entries.zh: 王曰：『然則寡人孰相？』
entries.en: The King said, 'Then whom should I appoint as chancellor?'
entries.literal: Wang said: 'So then I who chancellor?'

entries.zh: 代曰：『莫若太子之自相。
entries.en: Su Dai said, 'Nothing would be better than making the Crown Prince chancellor himself.
entries.literal: Dai said: 'Nothing better than crown prince self chancellor.

entries.zh: 太子之自相，是三人者皆以太子為非常相也，皆將務以其國事魏，欲得丞相璽也。
entries.en: If the Crown Prince serves as chancellor, all three men will regard him as merely a temporary appointment. Each will then strive to devote his state's resources to serving Wei, hoping to obtain the chancellor's seal for himself.
entries.literal: If the crown prince chancellors himself, these three will all consider the crown prince an extraordinary chancellor. They will all strive to have their states serve Wei in order to obtain the chancellor seal.

entries.zh: 以魏之彊，而三萬乘之國輔之，魏必安矣。
entries.en: With Wei's own strength, and three great powers of ten thousand chariots rallying behind it, Wei will surely be secure.
entries.literal: With Wei's strength, and three ten-thousand-chariot states assisting it, Wei will certainly be peaceful.

entries.zh: 故曰莫若太子之自相也。』」
entries.en: That is why I say nothing would be better than the Crown Prince serving as chancellor himself.'"
entries.literal: Therefore, said nothing better than crown prince self chancellor.'"

entries.zh: 遂北見梁王，以此告之。
entries.en: He then traveled north to see the King of Liang and presented this argument to him.
entries.literal: He then went north and saw the Liang wang, telling him this.

entries.zh: 太子果相魏。
entries.en: The crown prince did in fact become chancellor of Wei.
entries.literal: The crown prince indeed became chancellor of Wei.

entries.zh: 十年，張儀死。
entries.en: In the tenth year, Zhang Yi died.
entries.literal: In the tenth year, Zhang Yi died.

entries.zh: 十一年，與秦武王會應。
entries.en: In the eleventh year, the King met with King Wu of Qin at Ying.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, they met with Qin Wu Wang at Ying.

entries.zh: 十二年，太子朝於秦。
entries.en: In the twelfth year, the Crown Prince traveled to Qin for an audience.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year, the crown prince went for audience in Qin.

entries.zh: 秦來伐我皮氏，未拔而解。
entries.en: Qin attacked our city of Pishi but failed to take it and withdrew.
entries.literal: Qin came and attacked our Pi Shi, but did not capture it and retreated.

entries.zh: 十四年，秦來歸武王后。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year, Qin sent back the queen of King Wu.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year, Qin came and returned the Wu Wang queen.

entries.zh: 十六年，秦拔我蒲反、陽晉、封陵。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year, Qin captured our cities of Pufan, Yangjin, and Fengling.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year, Qin captured our Pu Fan, Yang Jin, and Feng Ling.

entries.zh: 十七年，與秦會臨晉。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year, the King met with Qin at Linjin.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year, they met with Qin at Lin Jin.

entries.zh: 秦予我蒲反。
entries.en: Qin returned Pufan to us.
entries.literal: Qin gave us Pu Fan.

entries.zh: 十八年，與秦伐楚。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year, Wei joined Qin in attacking Chu.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, they attacked Chu with Qin.

entries.zh: 二十一年，與齊、韓共敗秦軍函谷。
entries.en: In the twenty-first year, Wei joined with Qi and Han to defeat the Qin army at Hangu Pass.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year, with Qi and Han they together defeated the Qin army at Han Gu.

entries.zh: 魏之先，畢公高之後也。
entries.en: The forebears of the Wei clan were descendants of Duke Gao of Bi.
entries.literal: The ancestors of Wei were descendants of Bi Gong Gao.

entries.zh: 畢公高與周同姓。
entries.en: Duke Gao of Bi shared the same surname as the royal house of Zhou.
entries.literal: Bi Gong Gao shared the same surname with Zhou.

entries.zh: 武王之伐紂，而高封於畢，於是為畢姓。
entries.en: When King Wu conquered the tyrant Zhou, Gao was enfeoffed at Bi, and his descendants took Bi as their surname.
entries.literal: When Wu Wang attacked Zhou, Gao was enfeoffed at Bi, thus becoming the Bi surname.

entries.zh: 其後絕封，為庶人，或在中國，或在夷狄。
entries.en: In later generations the line lost its fief, and its descendants became commoners, scattered across the Central States and among the barbarian lands.
entries.literal: His descendants lost their enfeoffment and became commoners, some in the central states, some among the barbarians.

entries.zh: 其苗裔曰畢萬，事晉獻公。
entries.en: A distant descendant named Bi Wan entered the service of Duke Xian of Jin.
entries.literal: His descendant was called Bi Wan and served Jin Xian Gong.

entries.zh: 宣惠王五年，張儀相秦。
entries.en: In the fifth year of King Xuan Hui, Zhang Yi became chancellor of Qin.
entries.literal: In Xuan Hui Wang's fifth year, Zhang Yi became chancellor of Qin.

entries.zh: 八年，魏敗我將韓舉。
entries.en: In the eighth year, Wei defeated Han forces under the general Han Ju.
entries.literal: In the eighth year, Wei defeated our general Han Ju.

entries.zh: 十一年，君號為王。
entries.en: In the eleventh year, the lord assumed the title of king.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, the lord was titled wang.

entries.zh: 與趙會區鼠。
entries.en: He met with Zhao at Qushu.
entries.literal: They met with Zhao at Qu Shu.

entries.zh: 十四，秦伐敗我鄢。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year, Qin attacked Han and defeated its army at Yan.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year, Qin attacked and defeated us at Yan.

entries.zh: 十六年，秦敗我修魚，虜得韓將鯁、申差於濁澤。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year, Qin defeated Han at Xiuyu and captured the Han generals Geng and Shen Chai at Zhuoze.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year, Qin defeated us at Xiu Yu and captured the Han generals Geng and Shen Chai at Zhu Ze.

entries.zh: 韓氏急，公仲謂韓王曰：「與國非可恃也。
entries.en: The state of Han was in dire straits. Gong Zhong said to the King of Han, "Our allies cannot be relied on.
entries.literal: The Han clan was in dire straits. Gong Zhong said to the King of Han, "Allied states cannot be relied upon.

entries.zh: 今秦之欲伐楚久矣，王不如因張儀為和於秦，賂以一名都，具甲，與之南伐楚，此以一易二之計也。」
entries.en: Qin has long wished to attack Chu. Your Majesty would do better to make peace with Qin through Zhang Yi, offer them one great city, prepare our armor, and join them in a southern campaign against Chu. This is the strategy of trading one to gain two."
entries.literal: Qin has long wished to attack Chu. Your Majesty would do better to make peace with Qin through Zhang Yi, offer one famous city as tribute, prepare armor, and join them in a southern campaign against Chu—this is the strategy of trading one to gain two."

entries.zh: 韓王曰：「善。」
entries.en: The King of Han said, "Very well."
entries.literal: The King of Han said, "Good."

entries.zh: 乃警公仲之行，將西購於秦。
entries.en: They then prepared Gong Zhong's mission, intending to negotiate terms with Qin in the west.
entries.literal: Thus, they prepared Gong Zhong's journey, about to negotiate with Qin in the west.

entries.zh: 楚王聞之大恐，召陳軫告之。
entries.en: When the King of Chu learned of this, he was greatly alarmed. He summoned Chen Zhen and informed him.
entries.literal: The King of Chu heard this and was greatly alarmed. He summoned Chen Zhen and told him of it.

entries.zh: 陳軫曰：「秦之欲伐楚久矣，今又得韓之名都一而具甲，秦韓并兵而伐楚，此秦所禱祀而求也。
entries.en: Chen Zhen said, "Qin has long desired to attack Chu. Now they have also obtained a great city from Han and armed their forces. If Qin and Han combine their armies to invade Chu, it will be the very thing Qin has prayed to the gods for.
entries.literal: Chen Zhen said, "Qin has long wished to attack Chu. Now they have also obtained one famous city from Han and equipped their armor. If Qin and Han combine their troops to attack Chu, this is what Qin has prayed for at the altars.

entries.zh: 今已得之矣，楚國必伐矣。
entries.en: Now that they have obtained it, Chu will certainly be invaded.
entries.literal: Now they have already obtained it. Chu will certainly be attacked.

entries.zh: 王聽臣為之警四境之內，起師言救韓，命戰車滿道路，發信臣，多其車，重其幣，使信王之救己也。
entries.en: If Your Majesty heeds my counsel, alert the troops within our borders, raise an army under the banner of rescuing Han, fill the roads with war chariots, and dispatch trusted envoys with lavish gifts, so that Han will believe Your Majesty intends to come to their aid.
entries.literal: Your Majesty listen to this minister and for it alert within the four borders, raise troops saying they save Han, order chariots to fill the roads, send trusted ministers with many chariots and heavy gifts, making them believe the wang will save them.
